schoolClusters.note: The densest concentration of British-curriculum provision in Dubai, and where most option-block conversations about applied subjects start. Option sheets differ school by school and year by year, so check your own school's published list rather than assuming 0471 is available.

schoolClusters.city: Schools serving Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais
schoolClusters.note: Larger cohorts, broader option blocks and a higher share of students sitting nine or ten IGCSE subjects. Applied subjects appear here more often than in the smaller western schools, usually in a block against a second science.

sections.heading: What Cambridge 0471 support costs in Dubai, and why applied subjects price differently
paragraphs: Market rates for one-to-one tuition in Dubai in October 2026 run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the budget online end to AED 650 for a named premium tutor. Travel and Tourism 0471 sits unusually high inside that spread for a subject that is not considered academically difficult, and the reason is not difficulty. It is that very few tutors in this city have taught the syllabus to a series. A parent is paying for scarcity, and should know that is what they are paying for.

The table below sets out the bands as the market publishes them, with the source of each range. Read the right-hand column before the left: a budget hour and a specialist hour are different products, and the difference matters more on an applied subject than on Mathematics, where a competent generalist can carry a student a long way. On 0471, a generalist can teach the content and still leave the student writing four-mark answers worth two marks, because the mark scheme language is subject-specific and has to be taught deliberately.

None of these figures is IB Gram's price. Our model is a free trial lesson followed by a consultation that puts a number on the specific gap in front of your child, because an honest quote needs the diagnosis first. What this page can tell you is the band you should expect to be quoted in Dubai by anybody, so that a figure far below it or far above it prompts a question rather than a signature.

One further note on monthly packages, which is how a lot of Dubai tutoring is sold. Online monthly packages advertised in this market have been seen at AED 799 for eight sessions, and in-home packages at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Divide before you compare: eight short online sessions and four long in-home visits are not the same amount of teaching, and the per-hour figures are further apart than the monthly headline suggests.

sections.heading: The home-tutor question answered: Dubai traffic, travel time and what it adds to the hour
paragraphs: Parents search for a home tutor because the mental model is simple: somebody competent arrives, your child sits down, and nobody drives anywhere. It is a reasonable thing to want. The problem in Dubai is arithmetic. A tutor who takes a 5pm session in Jumeirah and a 7pm session in Mirdif spends roughly as long in the car as in the two lessons combined, and that time is not free. It is recovered as a higher hourly rate, a minimum booking length, a travel surcharge, or a tutor who is quietly late and quietly tired.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE. Home visits are a service we offer only in India, and every country page on this site says the same thing. For a UAE family, 0471 is taught one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, and the case for that is not convenience. It is the tutor pool. A family in Al Warqa searching for a 0471 specialist within a twenty-minute drive is choosing from almost nobody. The same family on video is choosing from every specialist available in that time slot.

The comparison below is the one worth making before you decide. It is not online versus the idea of in-home tuition; it is online versus what an in-home arrangement in Dubai actually involves on a Tuesday in February. The travel column is the one most quotes leave out, and the substitution column is the one families discover in week six, when the tutor who knows 0471 is unavailable and a replacement who does not is sent instead.

A fair point against online delivery deserves stating. A tutor in the room can see a bored fourteen-year-old faster than a tutor on a screen, and a student who will not keep a camera on is harder to teach. Our answer is structural rather than rhetorical: screen-shared source material both parties annotate live, written work submitted and returned marked, and session notes to the parent. A student who disengages on video shows up in the written work within a fortnight.

sections.heading: The five units of 0471, and which ones a paid hour should buy
paragraphs: Travel and Tourism 0471 is built from five units: the travel and tourism industry, features of worldwide destinations, customer care and working procedures, travel and tourism products and services, and marketing and promotion. Confirm the current component structure, durations and weightings on the syllabus page at cambridgeinternational.org for your child's examination year, because Cambridge revises specifications and a tutor working from an old printout is a real risk on a minority subject.

Where a paid hour earns its money varies sharply by unit. The first unit is largely structural knowledge and most students can learn it from the textbook with supervision. The second rewards specific destinations described with real detail, which is the single biggest opportunity a Dubai candidate has and the one most waste. The third and fourth are scored on application to a scenario, which is a technique rather than a body of knowledge. The fifth, marketing and promotion, is where borderline candidates most often lose a grade, because it asks for justified recommendations and students supply descriptions.

That distribution should shape where you spend. A family with eight sessions of budget should not divide them equally across five units. Two on destination detail, three on scenario application, two on marketing justification and one on timed practice will move more marks than an even split, and a tutor who cannot tell you which unit your child is weakest in after one marked paper has not diagnosed anything.

The table maps each unit to the kind of loss we see in Dubai students' scripts and to the hours a repair typically takes. Treat the hour counts as planning estimates from marked work, not promises: a student who writes fluently and knows no destinations needs a different plan from one who knows Dubai inside out and cannot structure a paragraph.

sections.heading: Source booklets and case studies: the technique that separates grades in 0471
paragraphs: 0471 is an applied subject, which means the examination gives students material and asks them to do something with it. That is the whole game. A candidate who reads a case study about a resort, extracts three relevant facts and uses them to justify an answer will out-score a candidate who has memorised more content and writes it out untethered. Dubai students are frequently the second kind, because a lot of classroom teaching here is content delivery under timetable pressure.

The repair is mechanical and teachable. Read the question stem for the command word and the mark allocation before reading the source material. Mark up the source for facts that connect to the stem. Write one developed point per two marks available, each carrying a fact from the source and a consequence. Say what follows from the fact rather than restating it. Students who practise this with a tutor watching them do it, rather than being told about it, change their scripts in three or four sessions.

The second technique is a destination bank, and it is where a Dubai candidate has an unfair advantage nobody uses. A student here can write about an airline hub, a cruise terminal, a desert excursion market, a shoulder season driven by summer heat, inbound business tourism and the effect of Ramadan on hotel occupancy, all from observation. Three or four destinations known in genuine detail — including one in the UAE, one long-haul and one that depends on a single attraction — will answer most destination questions a paper can ask.

The third is time. Applied papers punish over-writing more than under-writing, because a student who spends twelve minutes on a four-mark question has stolen the time from a ten-mark one. We teach the arithmetic explicitly: minutes available divided by marks available, rounded down, written on the top of the paper before the first answer. It is unglamorous and it recovers marks in every series.

sections.heading: Counting back from a Cambridge series, and the money that moves first
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every examination centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used. In practical terms: ask your child's school or examination centre which zone it sits in, and work from that timetable only.

The deadline structure is the part families underestimate, so here is a worked example from Cambridge's own published key dates for the March 2027 series. Final entries are due 27 November 2026. The examination period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027. Forecast grades are due 27 February 2027, results are released on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. Read it backwards and the shape is clear: the money and the paperwork move about ten weeks before the first paper, and a tutoring plan that starts after entries close has lost its cheapest weeks.

For families sitting Pearson Edexcel International GCSE instead, the pattern is comparable but the dates are not. Pearson runs May/June and November series; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so check the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

The table below is the calendar as a budget document rather than an examination document. Each row names who sets the deadline, because that determines whether it can move. A school's internal mock date can shift. A Cambridge entry deadline cannot.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: Dubai fees, the 2026-27 freeze and the private-candidate route
paragraphs: Tutoring spend only makes sense next to the rest of a Dubai education budget. The private school sector here enrolled 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with UK-curriculum provision taking the largest share of enrolment at 37 per cent, Indian curricula 26 per cent, American 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate 7 per cent. That is the market a parent is buying inside, and it is dense enough that option blocks, teaching quality and subject availability vary considerably between two schools five minutes apart.

On fees, there is a specific and useful fact. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family planning tutoring, that removes one variable from next year's budget. Separately, Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent.

Against that, a tutoring plan is a modest line. Bestimate's 2026 monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. A single-subject 0471 plan of one session a week for two terms sits in the middle band. Where cost escalates is the late pre-series intensive, which is why the cheapest intervention in this subject is an honest conversation in Year 10.

If your child is sitting 0471 as a private candidate because the school does not offer it, there is an additional cost nobody mentions on a tutoring page: the examination centre's own entry fee, which varies by centre and is paid directly to them. Ask for it in writing, ask what it includes, and ask what the centre's internal deadline is, which is always earlier than Cambridge's.

sections.heading: Is the person you are paying legally permitted to tutor in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and a surprising number of families paying for it have never asked the question. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced private tuition work permits, administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service is listed as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, with a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system.

Two things follow that are worth a parent's attention. First, because the permit costs nothing, any tutor who tells you the fee is why they do not hold one is telling you something else. Second, individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, and figures circulating online could not be verified, so this page quotes none.

There is a separate and often confused category. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor: a training institute needs an Educational Services Permit from KHDA, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no centre or office in the UAE, and makes no claim of approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge International or Pearson. Any tutoring page claiming otherwise should be asked for the permit number.

In Abu Dhabi there is an extra rule parents should know even when they live in Dubai, because families move. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. This is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document, so verify it against the current ADEK text before relying on it. The practical point stands: your child's own classroom teacher, privately, is not the arrangement to seek.

sections.heading: What a 0471 tutor does with marked work, and the line nobody should cross
paragraphs: Travel and Tourism 0471 is assessed by written examination, which removes a temptation that exists on coursework-bearing subjects. It does not remove it entirely: students build case-study notes, write practice answers and sometimes produce portfolio-style tasks for school. The boundary is the same in every subject. A tutor teaches, questions, models and gives feedback. The script that goes to Cambridge, and any piece of assessed school work, must be the student's own from first word to last.

In practice that means a tutor may read a student's practice answer and mark it against the published criteria, explain why a point scored two rather than four, model an answer to a different question so the student can see the structure, and ask the questions that make the student find the weakness themselves. What a tutor may not do is supply sentences for the student to copy, rewrite a draft into something the student could not have produced, or hand over a finished piece of work. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments. That is a malpractice trigger for the student and a liability for whoever bought it.

Material is the other boundary. Cambridge, Pearson and the IB own their syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables. We reference them and link to the official source. We do not reproduce them as downloads, and any tutor offering you a bundle of mark schemes to keep is distributing somebody else's copyright. The official syllabus for 0471, including current component structure and assessment weightings, lives on cambridgeinternational.org, and that is where a parent should read it.

The last boundary is the honest one about outcomes. No tutor can promise a grade. What a plan can promise is a diagnosis you can read, written work marked against the criteria, and a session-by-session record of what changed. If a provider promises your family a specific grade on an applied subject with five units and a written examination, the only safe response is to ask how, in writing.

process.description: A checkpoint timed to the centre's entry deadline rather than to our invoicing. Either the plan is working and continues, or the diagnosis was wrong and it changes. Families who review late pay for repair hours they did not need.

faqs.question: How much does a Cambridge IGCSE Travel and Tourism 0471 tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates collected in October 2026 put qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150-300 an hour and examination-year specialists at AED 200-450 or more. In-home one-to-one sits at AED 180-350 per Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, with independent home tutors quoting up to AED 500 once travel is absorbed. 0471 tends to price in the upper half of those bands because very few Dubai tutors have taught the syllabus to a series. Those are market figures rather than IB Gram's price list; our model is a free trial lesson and then a written plan with the total stated before you commit.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a 0471 tutor to our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Cambridge 0471 is taught one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. The reason is the tutor pool rather than cost: a family in Mirdif or Dubai South looking for a 0471 specialist within driving distance is choosing from almost nobody, while the same family on video is choosing from every specialist free in that slot. If you want a tutor physically in the room, a Dubai agency can arrange that and this page sets out what the market charges for it.

faqs.question: Why is 0471 more expensive to tutor than Mathematics in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Scarcity, not difficulty. Dubai has a deep pool of Maths tutors and a very shallow one for Travel and Tourism, so the few people who have taught 0471 to a Cambridge series can quote at the top of the band. There is a second reason worth knowing: a generalist can teach 0471 content competently and still leave a student writing four-mark answers worth two, because the mark scheme language on an applied subject has to be taught deliberately. You are paying for someone who knows how the marks are split, not just what the topics are.

faqs.question: Is a two-hour minimum booking normal for in-home 0471 tuition in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It is rarely itemised, which is the problem. A tutor taking a 5pm session in Jumeirah and a 7pm session in Mirdif spends about as long driving as teaching, and that time is recovered somewhere: a higher hourly figure, a two-hour minimum booking, a travel surcharge, or a tutor who arrives late and leaves early. Comparing the in-home band of AED 180-500 with the online band of AED 150-450 understates the gap, because the in-home hour usually comes with a minimum length attached. Ask any in-home quote three questions: minimum booking, travel charge, and what happens if the tutor is delayed.

faqs.question: Which of the five 0471 units should we spend tutoring hours on first?
faqs.answer: Start with a marked past-paper question rather than a guess. Across the Dubai scripts we see, the recurring losses are in features of worldwide destinations, where answers are generic and carry no named example, and in marketing and promotion, where students describe rather than justify a recommendation. The industry-structure unit is the one most students can learn from the textbook with supervision. A sensible eight-session split is two sessions on destination detail, three on applying content to a scenario, two on justified recommendations and one on timed practice, adjusted once the first marked paper comes back.

faqs.question: Can my child sit 0471 as a private candidate if their Dubai school does not offer it?
faqs.answer: Yes, through an approved examination centre in Dubai that accepts private candidates. The centre handles the entry, the invigilation and the zone timetable, and charges its own fee directly to the family. This is how a good share of Dubai 0471 candidates actually sit the paper, because the subject is often squeezed out of an option block. Three questions before you count on it: which series the centre is entering, what its internal deadline is, and what the fee includes. The centre's own deadline is always earlier than Cambridge's, and it is the one families miss.

faqs.question: What is a Cambridge administrative zone, and why does it matter for a Dubai candidate?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and publishes a different timetable version for each. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong timetable was used. For a Dubai family the practical step is small and important: ask the school or examination centre which zone it sits in, then work only from that timetable. A revision schedule built from a timetable found online is a schedule built on somebody else's zone.

faqs.question: How far before the papers do Cambridge entries actually close?
faqs.answer: Months, and this is the deadline that costs families money. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series show final entries due 27 November 2026 against an examination period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. Read backwards, the paperwork and the money move roughly ten weeks before the first paper. Tutoring arranged after entries close is repair work at the most expensive hourly rate available, which is why the cheapest intervention is a conversation in Year 10.

faqs.question: Are monthly tutoring packages in Dubai better value than paying per session?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but only after you divide. Packages advertised in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Those headline figures hide very different amounts of teaching and very different session lengths, so convert both to an hourly figure before comparing. Then ask what the package does with unused sessions, whether marking time is inside the price, and whether the rate is held if you pause during examination weeks. A package that cannot be paused is a discount you pay for in wasted sessions.

faqs.question: Do private tutors working with Dubai students need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced private tuition work permits through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a MoHRE permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you. Because the permit costs nothing, a tutor citing the fee as a reason for not holding one is telling you something else.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre group class a sensible way to cover 0471 cheaply?
faqs.answer: It is the cheapest hour available and usually the wrong one for this subject. Centres roster classes around demand, and 0471 rarely generates enough enrolment in one Dubai community to fill a class, so a family is often sold a general business or geography class instead. Where group teaching does work is a pair or a group of two to four students on the same unit at a similar level, which costs roughly a third to a half of the one-to-one rate per student. Ask the centre directly which syllabus code the class teaches before enrolling.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education lessons affect when a 0471 session can run?
faqs.answer: They do, and families underestimate it. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit. That lands as a fuller timetable and, for many students, additional Arabic homework on weekday evenings. In practice the workable 0471 slots in Dubai are straight after school or after 7pm, and the 7pm-to-9pm window is heavily contested. Booking a fixed weekly slot early in the term is worth more than negotiating a lower rate for a slot that keeps moving.

faqs.question: Can a 0471 tutor help with case-study notes and practice answers?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary is worth stating. A tutor may mark a student's practice answer against the published criteria, explain why a point scored two rather than four, model an answer to a different question so the structure is visible, and ask the questions that make the student find the weakness. A tutor may not supply sentences to copy or hand over finished work. Anything submitted to Cambridge or to the school must be the student's own throughout. One operator in this market sells completed assessments outright; that is a malpractice trigger for the student, not a shortcut.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a 0471 student in Dubai usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends on what the gap is, which is why the first session is a diagnosis rather than a lesson. Patterns we see: a student with solid content and weak examination technique typically needs six to eight sessions concentrated on applied answers; a student who has missed a unit needs two to three on that unit plus timed practice; a student starting Year 10 from scratch is better served by weekly sessions across two terms, which costs less per mark than any intensive. Bestimate's 2026 monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240-600 at the budget end and AED 600-1,200 mid-market.

faqs.question: Should a 0471 quote state whether marking sits inside the hourly rate?
faqs.answer: Ask, because in this market it varies and it is the most common hidden extra. Marking a full 0471 past paper properly against the mark scheme takes a tutor 30 to 45 minutes, and some providers bill that separately, some fold it into the rate, and some simply do not do it. A rate that excludes marking is not cheaper; it is a different product, and on an applied subject the marked script is where the improvement comes from. Get the answer in writing alongside the minimum booking length and the cancellation terms.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-travel-and-tourism.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Cambridge IGCSE Travel and Tourism 0471 to examination and mark against the published assessment criteria. In the trial lesson they will tell you which kind of session your child needs first, which is usually not the one a parent expects to buy.

intro.heading: Five kinds of 0471 hour, and why they are not the same purchase
paragraphs: Parents ask what an online 0471 tutor costs in Dubai as though there were a single answer. There is a market band — roughly AED 150-300 an hour for a qualified online subject tutor and AED 200-450 or more for an examination-year specialist, from rate cards collected in October 2026 — but the band hides the more useful question, which is what kind of hour you are buying. A diagnostic session, a content session, a destination-building session, a marked-paper session and a timed-practice session cost similar amounts and do completely different work. Buying four of the wrong one is how families spend AED 1,200 and see nothing move.

The first hour should always be a diagnosis. A tutor gives your child a past-paper question, watches them write it, marks it live against the criteria and says which of the five syllabus units is leaking marks. That hour produces a plan rather than teaching, and it is the only hour we would ask a family to buy before knowing anything else. Our version of it is the free trial lesson, one per family, booked before any payment is taken.

Content hours are the cheapest per mark and the ones families skip. A student who has missed the products and services unit needs it taught, and a generalist tutor can do that competently. Destination-building hours are different and are where a Dubai candidate has an advantage nobody uses: the syllabus asks repeatedly about destination appeal, access, climate and attractions, and a student living in this city can describe an airline hub, a cruise terminal, a desert excursion market and a season shaped by summer heat from observation rather than from a revision guide.

Marked-paper hours are the expensive ones that actually move grades late in the course. Marking a full 0471 paper properly against the mark scheme takes a tutor 30 to 45 minutes before the lesson even starts, so ask any provider whether that time is inside the rate. Timed-practice hours are the last stage, and they are cheap to run and brutal to sit: a student writes under examination conditions while the tutor watches the clock and the structure, and nothing is explained until the pen goes down.

What this page will not do is invent an IB Gram price list. The figures here are the Dubai market's, attributed where they came from, published because three of the six competitor pages researched for this market quote no price at all and the two that do quote in US dollars. After a free trial lesson you get a written plan naming the kind of sessions, how many, and the total in AED. A quote without a diagnosis attached is a guess with a decimal point.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-travel-and-tourism.subjectsIntro: 0471 sits in an option block with other Cambridge subjects, and some of them share skills so directly that one teaching move pays into two papers. These are the pairings Dubai families ask about most.

subjects.name: Travel and Tourism (0471)
subjects.description: Five units, written examination, applied marking. The recurring diagnosis in a first session is not missing knowledge: it is a student writing everything they know instead of the two developed points a four-mark question asks for.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Shares segmentation, the marketing mix and customer service with 0471's later units. Teach a student to justify a recommendation once and both papers improve, which makes this the most efficient pairing in the block.

subjects.name: Enterprise (0454)
subjects.description: Practical business planning and pitching, assessed partly on applying ideas to a scenario. Students who take it alongside 0471 are usually comfortable with applied questions and weak on precise industry vocabulary.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Explains tourism seasonality properly. A student who can talk about elasticity writes a far better answer on why a Dubai hotel discounts in August than one working from a textbook sentence about low season.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Destination geography plus data-response technique. Climate graphs and arrival tables are read the same way in both subjects, and a geographer usually arrives at 0471 already able to extract a fact from a source.

subjects.name: Environmental Management (0680)
subjects.description: Sustainability answers in 0471 are frequently vague. Students carrying this subject can name an actual impact and an actual management response, which is exactly what the evaluation marks are looking for.

subjects.name: Global Perspectives (0457)
subjects.description: Research, evidence and perspective, assessed in part through coursework. The transferable habit is attributing evidence, which lifts a 0471 answer on responsible tourism out of generalities.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: Most Dubai 0471 candidates write the paper in their second language. Industry vocabulary and the phrasing of a justification have to be taught explicitly, or applied marks earned in the student's head never reach the script.

subjects.name: Accounting (0452)
subjects.description: Rarely paired, occasionally decisive. A student who reads figures confidently handles 0471's revenue, occupancy and pricing data without the hesitation that costs time on the paper.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Foreign Language (0544)
subjects.description: Present in almost every Dubai timetable because Arabic is mandatory in the emirate's private schools whatever curriculum the school is licensed for. It matters here as a scheduling constraint on when a 0471 session can happen.

sections.heading: What each kind of 0471 session is worth in AED, and which one to buy first
paragraphs: The useful way to price 0471 tuition in Dubai is by the job the hour does. The market band for a qualified online subject tutor sits around AED 150-300, and an examination-year specialist at AED 200-450 or more, from rate cards collected in October 2026. Inside that band, a diagnostic hour and a timed-practice hour cost roughly the same and are worth wildly different amounts depending on when in the course you buy them.

Order matters more than rate. A family that buys six content hours when the student already knows the content has bought nothing; a family that buys six marked-paper hours before the content is in place has bought frustration. The sequence that works on this syllabus is diagnose, fill the content gaps, build the destination bank, mark papers, then practise against the clock. Each stage ends when the written work says it has, not when a package runs out.

The table prices each type and names what should come out of it. Read the last column hardest: a session with no defined output is the one that quietly repeats itself for eight weeks. On a minority subject where a specialist is charging at the top of the band, a parent is entitled to know what the hour produces.

One note on marking, which is the hidden line in this market. A 0471 paper marked properly against the mark scheme takes a tutor 30 to 45 minutes before the lesson begins. Some providers include that, some bill it, some skip it and call the result feedback. A rate that excludes marking is not a cheaper version of the same product; it is a different product, and on an applied subject the marked script is where the improvement lives.

sections.heading: Dubai is the case study the syllabus keeps asking for
paragraphs: 0471 asks candidates to write about destination appeal, access and transport, accommodation types, attractions, seasonality, customer types and the economic effects of tourism. A student in Birmingham learns those from a textbook. A student in Dubai can look out of a window. Almost no Dubai candidate uses this, because classroom teaching under timetable pressure defaults to the resort examples printed in the revision guide.

Work through the syllabus with the emirate as the worked example and the answers change character. Access and transport: an international airline hub, a metro line that runs to the mall and the airport, a cruise terminal, a road network built around a single arterial highway. Accommodation: beach resorts, serviced apartments, free-zone business hotels, desert camps. Attractions: natural, built, and the whole category of manufactured attraction that this city specialises in. Seasonality: an inverted season driven by summer heat rather than winter cold, plus demand shifts around Ramadan and around the European school year.

Customer types are the part students find easiest once it is pointed out. A Dubai candidate has watched business travellers, family tourists, stopover passengers, visiting relatives of residents, cruise passengers ashore for nine hours, and the domestic staycation market that fills hotels on a long weekend. Each of those has different needs, which is exactly what the customer care and products units are testing. A student who can name the segment and its need writes a two-mark point instead of a one-mark observation.

The discipline is specificity. An examiner cannot award marks for a destination described in words that would fit anywhere. The habit we teach is three concrete facts per destination — one about access, one about the main appeal, one about a constraint or risk — written in a notebook and learnt. Three or four destinations held that way, with one of them in the UAE and one long-haul, will answer almost any destination question a paper can set.

sections.heading: Where marks actually leak on an applied paper, and how a lesson fixes it
paragraphs: The most common 0471 script we see from Dubai students is not ignorant. It is undirected. The student knows the material, reads the question quickly, and writes everything adjacent to the topic in the hope that the marks are in there somewhere. Applied papers do not reward that. They reward a developed point per two marks available, anchored to the material the paper supplied, with the consequence stated rather than implied.

The second leak is the command word. Identify, state, describe, explain, justify and evaluate ask for different things and carry different marks, and a student who explains when asked to identify has spent four minutes earning one mark. We teach the student to circle the command word and write the mark total at the top of the answer space before writing a single sentence. It looks trivial and it changes scripts within a month.

The third leak is timing, and the arithmetic is simple enough to teach in ten minutes. Total minutes divided by total marks gives a minute-per-mark figure; round down, write it on the paper, and check it at the halfway question. Students who over-write early answers steal the time from the high-mark questions at the end, which is where the grade actually sits. This single habit recovers marks for students whose content knowledge has not changed at all.

The fourth leak is evaluation. The marketing and promotion unit, and the higher-mark questions elsewhere, ask for a recommendation with a reason and usually a counterweight. Students supply the recommendation and stop. The teachable move is a sentence pattern: the recommendation, the reason tied to the customer or operator in the question, and one limitation. Taught explicitly, practised four or five times, marked each time, it is the single biggest grade-mover on this syllabus.

sections.heading: What a live online 0471 lesson actually looks like, minute by minute
paragraphs: Parents reasonably want to know what they are paying for when nobody is in the room. A 0471 session is well suited to video because the subject is built on documents: source material, case studies, mark schemes and the student's own written answers. All of those are better shared on a screen both people can annotate than passed across a table. What online removes is travel time; what it demands is structure, because a session with no agenda is more obviously aimless on video than in a living room.

A sixty-minute session runs to a shape. Five minutes reviewing the written work set last time, with the marks explained rather than announced. Ten minutes teaching or re-teaching the specific thing the marks showed was missing. Fifteen minutes of guided practice where the student writes and the tutor interrupts. Twenty minutes of independent writing under something close to examination conditions, camera on, tutor silent. Ten minutes taking the answer apart against the criteria and setting the next piece of work.

The practicalities are modest. A laptop or tablet with a working microphone, a quiet room with a door, a table, pen and paper, and a way to photograph or scan a handwritten answer. Handwriting matters: the examination is written by hand, so practice answers should be too, then photographed and submitted. A student who only ever types practice answers will be slower and messier on the paper than their knowledge deserves.

What a parent should receive is a short note after each session saying what was taught, what was set, and what the last piece of work scored against which criteria. That note is the thing to ask any provider for before paying, because it is the only evidence a family outside the room can actually read. A provider who will not write three sentences after a lesson is a provider whose sessions you cannot audit.

sections.heading: Choosing a series, and what each choice costs in preparation weeks
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Which series a Dubai student sits is usually decided by the school, but private candidates and retake students genuinely choose, and the choice is a planning decision with a price attached. June gives a full academic year of teaching before the paper. November gives roughly a term and a half, in a period broken by a long summer and by the start-of-year settling that eats September.

Every examination centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge publishes a separate timetable version for each. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used. Ask your school or centre which zone it sits in, then build the revision plan from that timetable only. A plan built from a timetable found in a search result is a plan built on somebody else's zone.

Entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers, which is the fact that costs families the most money. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series are the clearest worked example: final entries due 27 November 2026, examination period 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Cambridge Direct 13 May and certificates in late June. Whichever series your child sits, assume the paperwork and the money move about ten weeks ahead of the first paper and confirm the actual dates with the centre.

For families sitting Pearson Edexcel International GCSE instead, series run in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also issues provisional timetables ahead of each series, so work from the live official document rather than a restated date.

sections.heading: Where a 0471 grade actually counts, and where it does not
paragraphs: Applied subjects carry a reputation in Dubai staffrooms, and parents hear it. The accurate position is narrower than the gossip. A good 0471 grade is a good IGCSE grade and sits on the certificate like any other. What varies is how a particular sixth form or university route weighs it, and that is a question to ask admissions in writing rather than to infer from a rumour at the school gate.

For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One competitor page ranking for these queries states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced position is five. Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs, not something a tutoring service performs, and it should be verified on the Ministry's own channel.

For sixth-form entry, the honest answer is that a Business or Economics A Level teacher will care more about a student's English and Mathematics grades than about which applied subject they took. 0471 helps as evidence of interest in a hospitality or tourism pathway, and some UAE hospitality management degrees treat it as directly relevant. It is not a substitute for the core grades a sixth form sets as conditions, and it does not block anything either.

The practical advice for a Year 11 family is unglamorous. Get the sixth form's offer conditions in writing. Count your five equivalency subjects and check Arabic and Islamic Education are not among them. Then decide how many tutoring hours 0471 deserves relative to the subjects the offer actually names. Spending specialist rates on 0471 while a conditional Mathematics grade goes unaddressed is the most common misallocation we see in this market.

sections.heading: The honest limits of this page, and of any 0471 tutor
paragraphs: IB Gram teaches UAE students one-to-one over live video. We do not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India, and the same statement appears on every country page on this site. If your family wants somebody physically in the room, Dubai agencies arrange that and the market band for it is AED 180-500 an hour depending on the tutor and the distance. We would rather name that than pretend the option does not exist.

We hold no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, Cambridge International or Pearson, and we operate no office, centre or branch in the UAE. Those are specific things issued to specific entities: a training institute with premises in Dubai needs an Educational Services Permit from KHDA, and an individual tutor needs a private tuition work permit through MoHRE, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Any tutoring page claiming regulator approval should be asked for the permit number.

On assessed work, the boundary is fixed. A tutor teaches, questions, models and marks. The answers that go to Cambridge, and anything submitted to the school, must be the student's own throughout. We do not supply sentences to copy, rewrite a draft into something a student could not have produced, or hand over finished pieces of work. One operator in this market sells completed assessments; for the student that is a malpractice trigger, not a shortcut. We also do not reproduce Cambridge syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads, because they belong to Cambridge. We reference and link them.

On outcomes, no tutor can promise a grade and this page does not. What a plan can offer is a diagnosis written down, work marked against the published criteria, a record of what changed week by week, and a review timed to the entry deadline rather than to our invoicing. If that is not what a provider is selling you, the AED figure is not the thing to negotiate.

process.description: Syllabus code 0471, the school or examination centre, which series your child is entered for, and the last marked piece of work. On a minority subject the precision matters: it is what allows a match to a tutor who has taught 0471 to examination rather than one prepared to read ahead.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson first
process.description: One free trial lesson per family, before any payment. The tutor sets a past-paper question, marks it live, and names which of the five units is costing marks. If the match is wrong you say so and nothing is owed. The output is a plan you can compare against any other quote in the market.

process.title: Buy the right kind of hour, in the right order
process.description: Diagnose, teach the content gaps, build the destination bank, mark papers, then practise against the clock. The written plan says which kind of session, how many of each, and the total in AED, so nobody is paying for content hours a student did not need.

process.title: Work between sessions, marked before the next one
process.description: Answers are written by hand, photographed and submitted, then marked against the published criteria before the lesson. A short note goes to the parent after every session saying what was taught, what was set and what the last piece scored.

process.title: Review against the centre's deadline
process.description: A checkpoint timed to the examination centre's entry deadline rather than to a billing cycle. Either the evidence says the plan is working and it continues, or the diagnosis was wrong and it changes. The centre's internal deadline is earlier than Cambridge's, so it is the one in the plan.

whyPoints.title: Priced by the job, not by the hour alone
whyPoints.description: Five kinds of 0471 session, each with a market figure and a defined output. A family can see which hour they are buying and what should come out of it, which is more useful than a single rate quoted with no plan attached.

whyPoints.title: Dubai used as the case study
whyPoints.description: The syllabus asks about destinations, access, accommodation, seasonality and customer types. Your child lives inside working examples of all five. We teach them to use it, which is a marks advantage almost no Dubai candidate currently takes.

whyPoints.title: Marking is part of the lesson, not an extra
whyPoints.description: A 0471 paper marked properly against the mark scheme takes 30 to 45 minutes before the session begins. That time is stated in the plan rather than hidden, because the marked script is where an applied subject actually improves.

whyPoints.title: A specialist, not the nearest available person
whyPoints.description: Very few tutors in Dubai have taught 0471 to a series. Online delivery means the match is to someone who has, wherever they are, instead of whoever lives within a tolerable drive of your community.

whyPoints.description: The AED bands here come from published rate cards and a dated market rate table, labelled as the market's rather than ours. No star ratings, no satisfaction percentages, no student counts we cannot evidence.

whyPoints.description: No regulator approval, no UAE office, no promised grade, and no home visits in the UAE. Knowing what a provider will not do is worth as much to a parent as the list of what it will.

faqs.question: What should a single diagnostic session on Cambridge 0471 cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates for a qualified online subject tutor in Dubai run about AED 150-300 an hour, and a diagnostic session sits inside that band because it takes the same hour of a specialist's time. The difference is the output: a diagnostic should end with a named weak unit, a session count and a written note, not a lesson. Many providers waive it as a trial, and ours is free, one per family, before any payment is taken. If a provider charges for a diagnosis, ask what document you receive at the end of it before agreeing.

faqs.question: Can my child use Dubai itself as a destination case study in the 0471 examination?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the advantage almost nobody uses. The syllabus asks about destination appeal, access, accommodation types, attractions, seasonality and customer types, and a student living here can describe an international hub airport, a cruise terminal, free-zone business hotels, desert camps, an inverted peak season driven by summer heat, and visitor segments from stopover passengers to the domestic staycation market. What matters is specificity: three concrete facts per destination, one about access, one about appeal and one about a constraint. Examiners cannot award marks for a description that would fit any city.

faqs.question: How many destinations does a 0471 candidate actually need to know properly?
faqs.answer: Three or four, known in real detail, beats a dozen known vaguely. The working set we build is one UAE or Gulf destination the student can describe from observation, one long-haul destination with a different climate and access profile, one destination dependent on a single major attraction, and optionally one mass-market beach destination. For each, the student learns three facts: how visitors get there, the main appeal, and one constraint or risk. That structure answers most destination questions a paper can ask, and it fits on two sides of a notebook.

faqs.question: What does an online 0471 lesson actually look like from start to finish?
faqs.answer: A sixty-minute session runs to a shape: five minutes on last week's marked work with the marks explained, ten minutes teaching the specific gap the marks revealed, fifteen minutes of guided practice where the student writes and the tutor interrupts, twenty minutes of independent writing under timed conditions with the tutor silent, then ten minutes taking the answer apart against the criteria and setting the next piece. Source material and the student's script are shared on screen and annotated by both. A short note goes to the parent afterwards saying what was taught and what the last work scored.

faqs.question: Is the November Cambridge series a sensible choice for a 0471 retake?
faqs.answer: It can be, and the deciding factor is weeks rather than preference. Cambridge runs June and November series, so a student who misses a grade in June can sit again in November if the centre enters them in time. November gives roughly a term and a half of preparation, broken by the summer and by September settling, so the plan has to be tighter than a June plan. Ask the examination centre two things first: whether it enters the November series for 0471, and what its own internal deadline is, which is always earlier than Cambridge's.

faqs.question: Does 0471 count towards the five subjects the UAE Ministry of Education asks for?
faqs.answer: On the British track, the published equivalency requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. A 0471 grade counts as an accredited IGCSE subject on the same basis as any other. Equivalency is run by the Ministry, not by any tutoring service, so verify the current rule on the Ministry's own channel before planning a subject count around it.

faqs.question: Will a 0471 grade help with a hospitality or tourism degree application in the UAE?
faqs.answer: It is relevant and sometimes explicitly welcomed, and it is not decisive. UAE hospitality and tourism management programmes care about the overall profile and the English language requirement first. Where 0471 helps is as evidence that a stated interest is real, which matters in a personal statement and in an interview. Where families get it wrong is spending specialist tutoring rates on 0471 while a conditional Mathematics or English grade named in an offer goes unaddressed. Read the university's published admission requirements and allocate hours to what the offer actually names.

faqs.question: How do we practise 0471 source questions online without printing papers?
faqs.answer: The source material is shared on screen and both tutor and student annotate it live, which is closer to how an examiner expects it to be used than passing a printout across a table. The answer itself should be written by hand, because the examination is handwritten, then photographed and submitted for marking. A student who only ever types practice answers writes slower and messier on the day than their knowledge deserves. The only equipment needed is a device with a microphone, a quiet room with a door, a table, and a phone camera.

faqs.question: My child writes long 0471 answers and still scores badly. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost always the command word and the mark allocation. Identify, describe, explain and justify ask for different things and carry different marks, and a student who explains when asked to identify has spent four minutes earning one. Long answers also steal time from the high-mark questions at the end, which is where the grade sits. The fix is mechanical: circle the command word, write the mark total at the top of the answer space, aim at one developed point per two marks, and calculate minutes-per-mark before the first sentence. Scripts change within a month of practising that.

faqs.question: Is Travel and Tourism treated as an easy IGCSE by Dubai schools?
faqs.answer: It carries that reputation in some staffrooms and the reputation is not accurate. 0471 is content-light compared with a science and writing-heavy compared with most option subjects, so it rewards students who can structure an applied answer and punishes those who cannot. Many students who choose it expecting an easier ride are surprised by how much extended writing it demands. A good grade is a good IGCSE grade. What varies is how a particular sixth form weighs an applied subject, which is a question for that admissions team in writing.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover 0471 and Business Studies 0450 in the same session?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is often the efficient choice, because the marketing, segmentation and customer service content overlaps and the evaluation technique is identical. What makes it work is honesty about time: ninety minutes split across two syllabuses is not two lessons, and a student with a gap in both subjects usually needs separate sessions for a few weeks before the shared work pays off. Ask the tutor to state in the plan which syllabus gets which minutes, and to mark work from both against the right criteria rather than blending them.

faqs.question: What setup does a 0471 online lesson need at our end in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Less than most families expect. A laptop or tablet with a working microphone and camera, a quiet room with a door that closes, a table, pen and paper, and a phone to photograph handwritten answers. A wired or reliable home connection matters more than speed; dropped audio mid-explanation wastes more of the hour than low resolution does. One practical note for apartment communities: a student writing a timed answer on a sofa is practising the wrong posture and the wrong attention. A table is part of the equipment list.

faqs.question: How do we check which version of the 0471 syllabus my child is sitting?
faqs.answer: Ask the school or examination centre for the syllabus year they have entered, then read that version on cambridgeinternational.org. Cambridge revises specifications, and on a minority subject an out-of-date printout circulating in a department is a genuine risk. The syllabus page states the current components, durations and weightings, which is why this page points you there rather than restating them. Do the same for the timetable: ask which of Cambridge's six administrative zones your centre sits in, because each zone has its own timetable version and Cambridge will not accept responsibility for a paper missed using the wrong one.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change a 0471 revision schedule in Dubai?
faqs.answer: School days shorten, energy patterns shift, and evening availability changes for many families. In practice we move sessions earlier in the afternoon or to after Iftar, depending on the household, and we shorten them. Forty-five focused minutes during Ramadan is worth more than a ninety-minute session nobody is present for. For students sitting a spring or early-summer series, the planning point is that Ramadan usually falls in the weeks when timed practice should be ramping up, so the practice schedule needs building around it in advance rather than being abandoned and resumed.

faqs.question: Does an online tutor need the same UAE permit as one who visits homes?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit regardless of delivery. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a MoHRE permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-travel-and-tourism.closingBody: If your child is sitting Cambridge IGCSE Travel and Tourism 0471 at a Dubai school or through an examination centre, the first hour to buy is the one that tells you which of the five units is actually costing marks. Ours is free: one trial lesson per family, a past-paper question marked live, and a written note on what the repair involves and roughly how many sessions it needs. After that the AED figures on this page stop being a band and start being a plan. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, built around your child's centre, their zone timetable and the series they are entered for.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-travel-and-tourism.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Cambridge IGCSE Travel and Tourism over live video to students in Dubai. Each works from the student's own school scheme of work and the current syllabus document, and each spends session time on stimulus-anchored written answers rather than on retelling industry content a student already has in their notes.

intro.heading: The subject reads easily, which is exactly why it is mismarked
paragraphs: Travel and Tourism is chosen by students who find it accessible, and they are right that it is accessible. The content makes sense on first reading, the examples are familiar, and nothing in it is conceptually hard in the way that organic chemistry is hard. That accessibility is precisely why the subject produces so many disappointed results. A student who understands the material assumes understanding is what is being marked, and writes accordingly.

What the paper actually rewards is specificity. Asked to describe the appeal of a destination, a candidate who writes that it has beautiful beaches and many attractions has written nothing an examiner can credit; one who names the airport, the type of accommodation, a specific attraction and the market it serves has written an answer. Asked how an organisation could improve its customer care, a candidate who offers general good advice scores far below one who uses the organisation described in the stimulus material by name and responds to its particular problem.

Then there is data. Applied subjects put charts, tables and tourism figures in front of candidates and ask them to describe a trend or make a comparison. The mark goes to the student who states the trend and quotes a figure from the source, and it is withheld from the student who describes every number in the table in sequence. This is a technique, not knowledge, and it takes about one session to install.

For a student in Dubai the subject comes with an unusual advantage. The emirate is a functioning worked example of nearly every topic on an applied tourism course: a global hub airport, a flag carrier and a low-cost carrier, a second airport in the south, a large hotel inventory across several market segments, purpose-built attractions, a cruise terminal, a government department responsible for economy and tourism, and visible tension between development and sustainability. A student who learns to describe what is around them in the paper's language has a case study nobody can take away.

On delivery: lessons are one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, since that is a service offered only in India. For 0471 this matters more than for a core subject. Travel and Tourism is taught in a minority of Dubai schools, which makes the number of tutors who have taken a cohort through the syllabus genuinely small, and selecting from that group by who can drive to a particular address would usually mean not selecting a 0471 tutor at all. Everything on this page that is sourced is attributed, and everything that must be checked against the syllabus for a particular examination year is flagged as such. No grade is predicted and no figure quoted here is an IB Gram price.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-travel-and-tourism.programmesIntro: Travel and Tourism runs from an IGCSE option through to degree level, and the UAE has an unusually direct route from one end to the other. These are the stages a Dubai student might pass through.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Travel and Tourism
programmes.description: An applied Cambridge Upper Secondary course covering the structure of the industry, destinations and their appeal, customer care and working procedures, products and services, marketing, and the economic, social and environmental impacts of tourism. The assessment style rewards specific, stimulus-anchored writing, which is a different habit from the discursive style that works in some other humanities subjects.
programmes.countryNote: Confirm with the school's exams officer which components your child is entered for and which syllabus version applies to their examination year. Cambridge revises syllabuses on a cycle and applied subjects can change their component structure between versions, which makes revision material found online a genuine risk rather than a minor inconvenience.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS & A Level Travel and Tourism
programmes.description: The sixth-form continuation, treating the industry at a management level: destination planning, marketing strategy, visitor management and sustainable development. Extended responses grow considerably and candidates are expected to evaluate business decisions rather than describe practice. The IGCSE habits that transfer best are data handling and stimulus discipline; the habit that must be built is sustained argument.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Dubai school running 0471 continues it to AS and A Level, because a small Year 12 group is harder to timetable than a Year 10 option. Ask whether the group actually ran in the current academic year, and ask how many students were in it, rather than relying on a prospectus listing.

programmes.name: Applied and vocational hospitality routes
programmes.description: Several Dubai schools and colleges offer applied qualifications in hospitality, travel or business as an alternative to a second A Level. Assessment is typically more coursework-weighted, which suits students who work steadily and struggle with a single examination window. The 0471 content maps across directly; the assessment habits do not, because the demand shifts from timed writing to sustained portfolio work.
programmes.countryNote: Equivalency rules differ by qualification type, and a vocational qualification is not automatically treated like an A Level for UAE attestation. Check the specific qualification with the Ministry of Education or the emirate attestation authority before assuming a route, and ask the receiving university what it accepts in writing.

programmes.name: Hospitality and tourism management degrees
programmes.description: The UAE hosts several hospitality and tourism management programmes, and the sector itself is one of the larger graduate employers in the country. Entry rarely requires school Travel and Tourism, but the subject does three things that help: it supplies industry vocabulary, it builds comfort with tourism data, and it gives a candidate something specific to say at interview about a destination they actually know.
programmes.countryNote: On the British track, UAE equivalency requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE passes at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, alongside one Advanced Level pass at grade E or above or two Advanced Subsidiary passes at the same grade. Verify the current wording with the Ministry rather than with any tutoring website.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-travel-and-tourism.subjectsIntro: These are the content areas commonly taught on an applied tourism course at this level, with what each one demands in an answer. Confirm the exact content and component list in the syllabus document for your child's examination year.

subjects.name: Structure of the travel and tourism industry
subjects.description: Sectors and organisations, from carriers and accommodation providers to tour operators, travel agents and tourist boards, and how they relate to one another. Marks go to using the correct term for the correct organisation, so vocabulary accuracy matters more here than explanation.

subjects.name: Features of worldwide destinations
subjects.description: What makes a destination appealing, and to which market. The examinable skill is naming features with precision, gateway airports, accommodation types, natural and built attractions, climate patterns and accessibility, rather than praising a place in general terms.

subjects.name: Customer care and working procedures
subjects.description: What good service consists of, how organisations handle complaints, and the procedures staff follow. Deceptively simple and heavily mismarked, because candidates write common-sense advice instead of responding to the specific organisation and problem in the stimulus material.

subjects.name: Travel and tourism products and services
subjects.description: Packages, ancillary products, transport options, itineraries and the way products are combined for a market segment. Questions often supply a customer with stated needs, so the answer has to match products to that customer rather than list what exists.

subjects.name: Destination management and appeal
subjects.description: How destinations are developed, managed and promoted, including visitor management, infrastructure and carrying capacity. Dubai supplies abundant material here, from airport capacity to purpose-built attraction districts, all of it checkable rather than imagined.

subjects.name: Marketing and promotion
subjects.description: Market research, segmentation, the promotional mix and how a destination or product is positioned. Candidates do well to name a real campaign or a real market segment, because a specific example separates a creditable answer from a textbook definition.

subjects.name: Sustainable tourism and environmental impact
subjects.description: The environmental consequences of tourism development, approaches to managing them, and the tension between growth and conservation. The highest-tariff questions live here, and they want a weighted judgement about a trade-off rather than a list of pros and cons.

subjects.name: Economic and socio-cultural impacts
subjects.description: Employment, income, leakage, seasonality, cultural change and the effects on host communities. The discipline is to attribute an effect to a mechanism: tourism raises employment through specific activity, not simply because visitors arrive.

subjects.name: Interpreting tourism data
subjects.description: Reading charts and tables of arrivals, spend or capacity, describing a trend and quoting a figure from the source. A technique rather than content, worth a reliable share of the paper, and installable in roughly one session of focused work.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-travel-and-tourism.regionsIntro: Dubai has a feature no other case study offers a student: the industry is in the neighbourhood. These notes cover both what a community can supply as evidence and when a session can realistically start.

regions.name: Deira
regions.note: The oldest commercial district, close to the creek, the souks and the abra crossings. Students here can describe heritage and cultural tourism as something observed rather than read about, which is exactly the specificity a destination question rewards.

regions.name: Al Garhoud
regions.note: Next to the main airport, with aviation and hotel employment visible in daily life. A student from this area can talk about hub operations and airport-adjacent accommodation with detail that reads as genuine rather than assembled from a textbook.

regions.name: Dubai Festival City
regions.note: A mixed retail, hotel and residential development beside the creek, and a usable local example of how a single site combines accommodation, retail and attraction functions. Journey times to school vary, so an evening slot generally holds better than an after-school one.

regions.name: Dubai South
regions.note: Built around the second airport and the exhibition legacy site in the south of the emirate. Students here live inside a worked example of planned tourism infrastructure, which is a strong source of named detail for development questions.

regions.name: Jebel Ali
regions.note: Port, free zone and a cruise and logistics corridor. Maritime tourism and the relationship between freight and passenger infrastructure are observable here, and both come up in questions about transport and access.

regions.name: Al Qusais
regions.note: Dense residential district with long school journeys in several directions. Arrival times vary considerably day to day, so a fixed weekend session holds across a term more reliably than a weekday one.

regions.name: Muhaisnah
regions.note: Residential area with students travelling to schools across the northern and eastern districts. Evening sessions after the commute has been absorbed work better than anything attempted immediately on arrival home.

schoolClusters.city: Deira, Al Qusais and Muhaisnah
schoolClusters.note: Long-established schools with large cohorts and mixed boards. Applied subjects such as Travel and Tourism often run here where a smaller academic option would not, because the cohort size supports a viable group, though the teacher may carry Business Studies as their main load.

schoolClusters.city: Jebel Ali and the southern corridor
schoolClusters.note: Schools serving the port, free-zone and Dubai South communities, where many families work directly in aviation, logistics or hospitality. Students here frequently arrive with industry knowledge from home, which helps the content and does nothing for the writing technique.

modes.title: Stimulus-drill session
modes.description: Sixty minutes built around stimulus material: a described organisation, a customer with stated needs, or a data table. The student writes short answers anchored to the material, and the marking checks one thing above all, whether the organisation or person in the stimulus actually appears in the answer.

sections.heading: What 0471 asks a candidate to do
paragraphs: Applied subjects are assessed by demand type rather than by topic, which is why a student can revise every content area and still write mid-range answers. There are six demands on a paper of this kind, and each has its own shape, its own length and its own characteristic failure. Teaching them separately is faster than teaching the content again, because the content is usually already there.

The pattern is consistent across cohorts. Naming questions get over-written, costing time that the extended response later needs. Destination questions get adjectives instead of named features. Applied questions about an organisation get general good advice that would be true of any hotel or any airline. Data questions get a recitation of the table rather than a trend and a figure. Evaluation questions get a list of positives followed by a list of negatives and then a stop.

The table sets each demand against what earns the mark and the error that most often replaces it. Read the final row twice. The highest-tariff question on an applied tourism paper usually asks for a judgement about a development or a policy, and the answer has to commit to a position with a stated reason for the weighting. A conclusion saying that it depends on circumstances is a true statement and an uncreditable one, and students write it constantly because it feels balanced. The practical use of this table is as a self-check before an answer is written rather than after it is marked. A student who identifies the demand type in the first ten seconds has already made the two decisions that matter, how long the answer should be and whether a judgement is owed.

sections.heading: Dubai as a live case study, used properly
paragraphs: Examiners can tell the difference between a case study a student owns and one they borrowed. Owned case studies contain the kind of detail nobody puts in a revision guide: how a particular district is reached, which market segment a hotel strip serves, what happens to visitor numbers in August, which part of a development came first. Dubai students can produce that detail from observation, and it reads as authentic because it is.

The way to build it is to take one destination and run it through every content area deliberately. Industry structure: which carriers, which terminals, which accommodation groups, which government body does what. Destination appeal: the specific attractions and the segments they target, business and leisure, stopover and long-stay. Customer care: what a service standard looks like in a sector where it is a competitive variable. Marketing: how the destination positions itself and to whom. Impacts: employment, seasonality, cultural change, construction and water use.

Two disciplines keep it honest. First, every detail must be checkable; nothing invented, no estimated figures, no visitor numbers the student cannot source. An invented statistic in an answer is worse than no statistic, and it is a habit that becomes expensive at AS Level. Second, the case study must be tested cold rather than reread, because a case study recognised on a page is not one available under timed conditions. A second, contrasting destination is worth building as well, since comparison questions are common and a student with one example can only answer half of them.
