sections.heading: The components your school enters, and what to confirm
paragraphs: This is the dullest section on the page and the one that saves the most wasted effort. Applied Cambridge syllabuses are revised on a cycle and component structures can change between versions, so revision material found online may describe a different assessment from the one your child will sit. A family that confirms five facts with the school at the start of Year 10 removes the whole category of risk.

The five are the exact syllabus code on the entry, the series the school enters, whether any non-examined component applies to that cohort, which Cambridge administrative zone the centre sits in, and whether any specified destination or content list applies to the examination year. None of these is difficult to obtain; all of them require asking the exams officer rather than a subject teacher, because the entry is an administrative fact rather than a teaching one.

The zone question is worth particular attention. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after working from the wrong version. A timetable downloaded from a search result is therefore not a safe document. Take the dates from the centre, and treat any date restated on a tutoring website, this one included, as something to verify at source. One further point belongs here, and it is about copyright rather than logistics. Syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes are published by the awarding body and should be obtained from cambridgeinternational.org or through the school. A provider offering to supply them as downloads is distributing material that is not theirs to distribute.

sections.heading: Customer care: the hardest easy topic on the paper
paragraphs: Every teacher of applied tourism knows this pattern. Customer care looks like the topic a sensible 15-year-old could answer without studying, and it reliably produces the weakest answers on the paper. The reason is that the questions supply a specific organisation with a specific problem, and candidates respond with general principles of good service that would apply equally to a dentist.

The repair is a rule rather than more content. Any answer about an organisation named in stimulus material must use that organisation by name, and must respond to the detail the stimulus supplied. If the material says the hotel receives complaints about check-in queues at peak arrival times, the answer is about check-in queues at peak arrival times, not about the importance of friendly staff. The detail is in the question because the examiner put it there to be used.

A second habit helps: separating what an organisation should do from why it matters commercially. Many questions want both, and candidates supply one. Reducing check-in queues matters because arrival experience affects review scores and repeat custom, and saying so turns a procedural answer into one that reaches the higher band. Practised on five short stimulus items in a single session, this is one of the faster improvements available in the subject, and it transfers directly to the applied questions in Business Studies for students taking both. Dubai students have an advantage worth using here as well. Many live in households where a parent works in aviation, hospitality or retail, and service standards are a real topic at home rather than an abstraction. A specific observation about how a complaint was actually handled is far stronger evidence than a sentence about the importance of customer satisfaction.

sections.heading: Sustainability and the judgement nobody commits to
paragraphs: The highest-tariff questions on an applied tourism paper tend to concern sustainability, development or impact, and they ask for a judgement. This is where the largest single block of marks sits and where the most consistent failure occurs: candidates produce a competent list of environmental, economic and social considerations, arrange them into positives and negatives, and then decline to decide anything.

A creditable answer names the trade-off explicitly and then weights it. A development may create employment and raise local income while increasing water consumption and pressure on a coastal habitat. The judgement is not that both matter; it is which matters more in this case and on what grounds, with the grounds stated. Timescale is often the most useful ground available: a cost borne immediately against a benefit accruing over decades, or the reverse, gives a student a defensible basis for weighting that does not depend on opinion.

Dubai supplies rich material for this, and it should be used carefully. Coastal development, water use in a desert climate, construction cycles and the carbon cost of long-haul aviation are all genuine considerations and all observable. What a student must not do is attach invented numbers to them. A judgement supported by a named mechanism and a stated timescale is stronger than one propped up by a figure the candidate could not source, and the second is a habit that becomes a serious problem in a sixth-form course where sources are expected.

State the ground for the weighting, not just the conclusion

A judgement that commits beats a balanced non-answer every time

sections.heading: Where 0471 marks are actually lost
paragraphs: Across marked scripts the losses concentrate in six places, none of which is a gap in industry knowledge. Each has a specific repair and each repair is short, which is why diagnosis before teaching matters so much in this subject. A tutor who begins by reteaching the structure of the industry to a student whose problem is adjectives has spent a session on something that was not broken.

The largest loss is the adjective problem, and it is the easiest to see on a page. A student describing a destination writes words like stunning, popular, modern and well-connected, none of which names anything. Circling every adjective in one of the student's own answers and asking them to replace each with a named feature is a ten-minute exercise that changes how they write permanently. The second largest is the stimulus-free answer described earlier.

The table lists all six with the session that fixes each. Note the last row. Timing in applied subjects fails in a particular way: candidates over-write the short recall questions because they feel confident on them, and then meet the extended judgement question with eight minutes left. That is a timing problem, not a sustainability problem, and it will look like a content weakness on any report that only records the mark. The six losses also tend to arrive together, which is encouraging rather than depressing. A student who writes in adjectives usually also ignores the stimulus and recites the data table, because all three are the same underlying habit of writing about the subject rather than answering the question in front of them. Repair one and the others move with it.

sections.heading: Cambridge series and the entry lag for a 0471 candidate
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Most Dubai schools enter the June series. The dates that actually govern a family's planning are not the examination dates but the entry deadlines, which sit months earlier and are submitted by the school rather than by the family.

The published March 2027 series shows the size of that lag clearly. Its examination period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades due on 27 February 2027, results reaching centres on Direct on 13 May and certificates following in late June. The entry deadline therefore precedes the first paper by more than two months. A student who decides in January that they would like to sit a subject has already missed the entry, and the same structural gap applies to the June and November series.

For a candidate considering a retake, the practical consequence is that the decision has to be made before the previous results feel settled. Pearson, used by some Dubai schools for other subjects, publishes an International GCSE November series whose 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with June 2026 results reaching centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, and November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. Those dates illustrate how a retake can fit inside one school year, and they should still be confirmed on the board's own timetable page.

sections.heading: Where 0471 leads in the UAE, and what equivalency asks
paragraphs: The UAE is one of the few places where an applied tourism qualification sits next to the industry it describes. The sector employs at scale across aviation, accommodation, attractions, events and retail, and a student who understands how those parts connect has something concrete to say in an interview at eighteen. That is a genuine argument for the subject, separate from whether a university asks for it.

The administrative layer needs stating plainly. On the British track, UAE equivalency requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count of five, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at grade E or above or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. An applied subject can form part of the five where it is among the accredited subjects submitted. One ranking competitor page states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced figure is five.

Equivalency and attestation sit with the Ministry of Education and the emirate authority. Across the UAE, Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain by ADEK, Sharjah by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the federal Ministry of Education. IB Gram describes these processes and does not perform, expedite or guarantee any part of them, and no tutoring is required for equivalency, admission or progression. Verify any requirement at the authority's own source before acting on it.

sections.heading: Getting started with 0471 in Dubai, and the availability position
paragraphs: Starting takes three facts and one hour. The three facts are the syllabus code and board from the school entry form, the series the school enters, and the most recent real mark with the paper it came from. The hour is a free trial lesson, one per subject, with no payment details taken beforehand, built around a short stimulus item so that the first thing produced is an answer rather than a conversation about the industry.

The disclosure concerns supply, and in this subject it is more acute than in most. Travel and Tourism is taught in a minority of Dubai schools and entered by a small number of candidates relative to the sciences or Mathematics, so the number of tutors in the region who have taken a cohort through the syllabus to examination is genuinely limited. On a week when none is free, we will say so and set out the alternatives: a specialist in another time zone whose availability suits a Dubai evening, a start date a few weeks out, or a short diagnostic engagement now with the main block beginning when a specialist is available.

What we will not do is present a Business Studies or Geography tutor as a 0471 specialist. The content overlap is real and tempting, and it is not the same thing. An applied tourism paper rewards a particular style of stimulus-anchored, named-feature writing, and a capable teacher who has never marked to that scheme will produce lessons that feel useful and scripts that stay in the middle band. A marked stimulus answer makes that visible in the first session, which is why the trial exists.

All five come from the exams officer rather than the subject teacher, because an entry is an administrative fact. Doing this in Year 10 removes an entire category of wasted revision.

What the student writes in those fifteen minutes identifies whether the problem is adjectives, stimulus discipline, data handling or timing, and those need different sessions.

whyPoints.description: The content of 0471 is accessible and the marks are not, so sessions go on stimulus-anchored writing rather than on retelling industry structure. A student who already owns the notes does not need them read aloud at an hourly rate.

whyPoints.description: Observation-level detail about a real destination reads as authentic because it is, and it cannot be taken away in an examination. Every fact is checkable and nothing is invented, which also builds the sourcing habit a sixth-form course will require.

Cambridge states that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who works from the wrong zone timetable, which makes this a real risk rather than paperwork.

faqs.question: What does Cambridge IGCSE Travel and Tourism 0471 cover?
faqs.answer: The structure of the travel and tourism industry and its organisations, the features that make destinations appealing and to which markets, customer care and working procedures, products and services, destination management, marketing and promotion, and the economic, social and environmental impacts of tourism including sustainability. Running through all of it is a data-handling element, since questions supply charts and tables of arrivals, spend or capacity. Confirm the exact content and component list in the syllabus document for your child's examination year, because applied syllabuses are revised on a cycle.

faqs.question: Is 0471 an easier IGCSE than Geography or Business Studies?
faqs.answer: The content is more accessible and the marking is not more forgiving, which is why the subject produces so many surprised results. Nothing in it is conceptually difficult, so students assume understanding is what is assessed. What is actually assessed is specificity: named features instead of adjectives, the organisation in the stimulus used by name, a trend with a figure quoted from the source, and a judgement that commits. Those are techniques rather than knowledge, and a student who has not been shown them will write fluently and score in the middle.

faqs.question: Which components does my child's school enter for 0471?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer rather than the subject teacher, because the entry is an administrative fact. Five things are worth confirming at the same time: the exact syllabus code on the entry, the series the school enters, whether any non-examined component applies to that cohort, which of Cambridge's six administrative zones the centre sits in, and whether any specified destination or content list applies to the examination year. Applied syllabuses can change component structure between versions, so material found online may describe a different assessment from the one your child will sit.

faqs.question: Can my child use Dubai as a case study in 0471 answers?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the strongest positions a candidate anywhere can be in. Dubai supplies a working example of nearly every content area: hub and secondary airports, carriers, a large hotel inventory across market segments, purpose-built attractions, a cruise terminal, a government department responsible for economy and tourism, and visible tension between development and environmental limits. Two rules keep it creditable. Every detail must be checkable, with no invented figures. And the case study must be tested cold, because one recognised on a page is not one available under timed conditions.

faqs.question: Where do 0471 candidates lose the most marks?
faqs.answer: Six places, none of them industry knowledge. Adjectives where named features were wanted. Applied answers that ignore the organisation described in the stimulus and offer advice that would suit any business. Data answers that recite the table instead of stating a trend and quoting one figure. Impacts asserted with no mechanism attached. Judgement questions answered with a pros list, a cons list and no decision. And time spent over-writing short recall questions, leaving the highest-tariff question rushed. Each repair is short, which is why diagnosis should come before any reteaching.

faqs.question: Does 0471 count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: An applied subject can form part of the required count where it is among the accredited subjects submitted. The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from those five, alongside one accredited Advanced Level subject at grade E or above or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. One ranking competitor states six subjects are required; the sourced figure is five. Verify current requirements with the Ministry or the emirate attestation authority directly.

faqs.question: Will 0471 help my child get into a hospitality degree in the UAE?
faqs.answer: It helps as preparation more than as a formal requirement. Most hospitality and tourism management programmes do not demand the school subject, and entry turns on attested certificates and the programme's own criteria. What 0471 supplies is industry vocabulary, comfort with tourism data, and something concrete to say at interview about a destination the student genuinely knows. Ask the admissions office what it accepts in writing rather than inferring it, and remember that no tutoring is required for admission or progression anywhere in this process.

faqs.question: How much tourism data does a 0471 candidate have to interpret?
faqs.answer: Enough that the technique is worth a session on its own. Questions supply charts and tables of visitor arrivals, spend, capacity or market share, and ask for a trend, a comparison or a calculation. The mark goes to the answer that states the trend and quotes one figure from the source. It is withheld from the answer that describes every number in sequence, which is what most candidates do unprompted. The technique is installable in roughly one session of focused work on real chart material and pays back on every paper afterwards.

faqs.question: Does 0471 lead to Cambridge A Level Travel and Tourism?
faqs.answer: It leads there naturally where a school offers the continuation, which is code 9395 at AS and A Level. The sixth-form course treats the industry at management level, covering destination planning, marketing strategy, visitor management and sustainable development, with considerably longer extended responses and an expectation that candidates evaluate business decisions. Data handling and stimulus discipline transfer unchanged from the IGCSE. Sustained argument has to be built. Ask whether the group actually ran in the current year, because a small Year 12 cohort is harder to timetable than a Year 10 option block.

faqs.question: How many 0471 sessions a week does a Dubai student need?
faqs.answer: One weekly session of sixty minutes suits most students through Years 10 and 11, provided the student writes between sessions. In an applied subject improvement comes from producing stimulus-anchored answers rather than from contact hours, so a second weekly session with nothing written in between usually adds cost rather than marks. Families commonly move to two sessions in the final eight to twelve weeks, with one spent writing under timed conditions and the other on the marking. A short case-study block during a school holiday is often better value than either.

faqs.question: Will a 0471 tutor come to our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, as that service exists only in India. Travel and Tourism sessions run one-to-one over live video, with stimulus material and the student's own written answers screen-shared so both sides annotate the same page. For this subject the trade is clearly favourable. 0471 is taught in a minority of Dubai schools, so specialists are few, and filtering an already small group by who can reach one address in traffic would usually mean not getting a 0471 specialist at all.

faqs.question: When are 0471 exams held, and when do entries close?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and the entry deadlines sit months before the papers. The published March 2027 series shows the scale of that gap: examinations from 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries due 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Direct 13 May and certificates in late June. Take your own dates from the school, because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong zone timetable.

faqs.question: How does a 0471 tutor help with customer-care questions?
faqs.answer: By replacing general good advice with a rule. Any answer about an organisation named in stimulus material must use that organisation by name and respond to the detail the stimulus supplied. If the material describes complaints about check-in queues at peak arrival times, the answer addresses check-in queues at peak arrival times rather than the importance of friendly staff. A second habit separates what the organisation should do from why it matters commercially, since many questions want both and candidates supply one. Five short stimulus items in a session covers it.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting 0471 support in the final term?
faqs.answer: Yes, because the available marks in this subject sit in technique rather than in content, and technique moves faster than knowledge. A final term can realistically fix the adjective habit, install stimulus discipline, teach the trend-plus-figure data answer and build three judgement paragraphs. What it cannot do is construct a case study from nothing or recover a content area never taught. Nobody can promise a grade from a final term, and a provider who does should be treated with real scepticism. A marked stimulus answer in week one tells you which problem you have.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-travel-and-tourism.closingBody: The quickest diagnostic in this subject takes four minutes. Ask your child to describe the appeal of a destination they know in five sentences, then count the adjectives and count the named features. If adjectives outnumber features, you have found the first session and it is a short one. Send the syllabus code, the series and the last marked paper, take the free trial lesson, one per subject with no payment details taken beforehand, and the hour will produce a stimulus answer marked on screen rather than a conversation about the industry.

intro.heading: The code on the statement of entry decides everything else
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE is not one qualification. It is a large family of separate syllabuses, each with its own four-digit code, its own paper set, and its own rules about tiering and practical assessment. Mathematics 0580 and Additional Mathematics 0606 are different courses that a Dubai student may sit together. Physics 0625, Coordinated Sciences 0654 and Combined Science 0653 cover overlapping content to different depths and are assessed quite differently. English First Language 0500 and English as a Second Language 0510 reward different things entirely.

This matters because almost every tutoring conversation in this market starts at the wrong level of detail. A parent asks for a science tutor; the useful request is a tutor for Cambridge 0620 Extended who has taught Paper 4 and Paper 6. A parent asks for maths help; the useful request names 0580 Extended or 0606, which are not interchangeable and rarely suit the same tutor. The code is printed on your child's statement of entry and the school's exams officer can confirm it in a sentence, and it is the single most useful piece of information you can bring to a first conversation.

The second thing the code brings with it is the tier. On most Cambridge IGCSE syllabuses, candidates are entered for either the Core paper set or the Extended paper set, and the Core papers cap the available grade at C. That is an administrative ceiling rather than a judgement about ability, and because Dubai entries are submitted months ahead of the papers, it is often fixed before a family realises it exists. Any conversation about tier belongs in the autumn term of Year 10, with evidence from marked work behind it.

The third is the assessment shape. Cambridge sciences separate multiple-choice, theory and practical assessment into distinct components, and candidates lose marks in different ways on each. The practical component rewards skills that are rarely taught explicitly: labelling axes, keeping significant figures consistent between a table and a conclusion, naming a control rather than gesturing at one, and describing what is being measured rather than what is being done. A tutor who has worked on those answers knows things a theory-only teacher does not.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Cambridge's school-age programmes run in a sequence, and the IGCSE year sits at the point where the assessment demand changes character. These are the stages a Dubai family encounters and what each is actually assessed on.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary, before IGCSE
programmes.description: The stage that builds what IGCSE will assume: algebraic manipulation, scientific vocabulary, and written accuracy. Cambridge offers Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests, which run in March, May and October, and they give a school and a family a structured reading before the IGCSE course begins rather than after it.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools admit new arrivals across the year, so Year 9 classes hold children from CBSE, American and other British schemes. Checkpoint results, where a school uses them, are a useful independent indicator of which specific topics were never taught in a child's previous sequence. The gaps at this stage are almost always specific rather than general, which makes short diagnostic work better value than a long weekly commitment.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Core tier
programmes.description: Core candidates sit the Core paper set, assessed on the Core subject content, with the available grade capped at C. The command terms are identical to Extended, so the marks still turn on reading the question properly, and the content is narrower rather than easier in style. Tutoring at this tier is largely about securing the grades in reach and testing honestly whether Extended is reachable.
programmes.countryNote: Because Cambridge entries in Dubai are submitted months before the papers, a tier change requested in the spring is usually an administrative impossibility rather than a teaching decision. Where a child needs a subject at A Level or at Higher Level in the Diploma, a Core entry can close that route. Take marked evidence to the head of department in the autumn term of Year 10.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE, Extended tier
programmes.description: Extended carries the full syllabus content and the full grade range. The additional content is where the marks concentrate: non-linear algebra and transformations in 0580, moles and electrolysis in 0620, momentum and electromagnetic induction in 0625. Papers are longer, method marks carry more weight, and the practical components demand a skill set of their own.
programmes.countryNote: Extended dominates in Dubai schools feeding sixth forms that run A Level or the IB Diploma, because both post-16 routes assume the Extended content as a floor. Dubai sixth forms publish their own per-subject entry requirements rather than working to a national standard, and on campuses running both routes the same Extended grade can satisfy one and fall short for the other.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level, after IGCSE
programmes.description: The route many Dubai Cambridge students take at 16, and the reason Extended content matters. International A Level exams run in the same June and November series as IGCSE, so a household can find two children sitting different qualifications to the same calendar. The content gap from Extended IGCSE to AS is specific and nameable rather than general.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Dubai campus runs both A Level and the IB Diploma, the IGCSE grades that open each route differ by subject and are published by the school. Ask for that document before setting a target grade, because working backwards from a published threshold produces a tuition plan with a defined finish rather than an open-ended one.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the Cambridge IGCSE syllabuses Dubai schools most commonly enter, with the code, the tiering position and the specific place the marks go. Confirm the code against your child's statement of entry, since schools occasionally change syllabus between cohorts.

subjects.name: Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Core and Extended sit different paper sets, and the Extended papers reward visible method. The reliable losses are algebraic fraction manipulation, transformations, and multi-step problems where a correct first step is followed by an unexplained jump to an answer.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: A separate syllabus taken alongside 0580, not instead of it, and it assumes fluency that 0580 only introduces. Losses sit in prerequisite algebra and trigonometry rather than in the topic being examined, which is why diagnosing it properly saves more hours than teaching it faster.

subjects.name: Physics 0625
subjects.description: Assessment separates multiple choice, theory and practical skills into distinct components. Theory losses cluster in momentum, circuits and electromagnetic induction, where a stated relationship before substitution is worth marks. Practical losses are about axes, significant figures and controls.

subjects.name: Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: The mole determines the Extended grade more than any other single idea. A candidate who cannot move between mass, moles and concentration unprompted loses marks in several components at once. Electrolysis, rates of reaction and the organic topics at the end are the other predictable losses.

subjects.name: Biology 0610
subjects.description: Content-rich and marked strictly against command terms. Candidates who know the material still score half marks by describing where the question says explain, and by using everyday vocabulary where the syllabus specifies a precise term. The fix is a rule, not more revision.

subjects.name: Coordinated Sciences 0654 and Combined Science 0653
subjects.description: Three disciplines assessed together, so a weakness in one strand pulls the aggregate down invisibly. A diagnostic that reports performance separately by discipline is worth the first hour, because the real fix is almost always narrower than the overall grade suggests.

subjects.name: English First Language 0500 and English as a Second Language 0510
subjects.description: 0500 rewards controlled purposeful writing and precise reading response; 0510 rewards accuracy and task completion. The consequential issue in Dubai cohorts is children entered for the wrong one of the two, which is a conversation with the school rather than a tutoring task.

subjects.name: Economics 0455 and Business Studies 0450
subjects.description: Both are lost on the longer questions, where a correct definition is never connected to the data or the case study and the application and evaluation marks go unclaimed. Because those marks are large and few, individual paper scores are noisy and a trend needs more data points.

subjects.name: Computer Science 0478
subjects.description: Algorithms must be expressed in the published pseudocode conventions, and students fluent in Python routinely lose marks writing Python instead. The theory component on data representation and networks rewards exact vocabulary, which responds to structured recall testing.

subjects.name: Arabic First Language 0508 and Arabic Foreign Language 0544
subjects.description: Arabic runs alongside the international curriculum in Dubai private schools under KHDA requirements, and the two Cambridge routes are different courses with different demands. Children are sometimes placed by nationality rather than competence, and that placement is worth checking first.

subjects.name: Geography 0460 and History 0470
subjects.description: Source-and-skills subjects presented as content subjects. History candidates lose marks narrating instead of arguing from the source; Geography candidates lose them on case-study specificity and on the data-response and fieldwork components, where general answers earn nothing.

subjects.name: Accounting 0452 and Art and Design 0400
subjects.description: Accounting rewards exact format and layout as much as understanding, and marks go on presentation conventions. Art and Design is assessed through work produced over time, which places it under the academic-honesty rules discussed later on this page.

sections.heading: Which Cambridge IGCSE codes Dubai schools actually enter
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE syllabuses are identified by a four-digit code, and the code is the unit of work for a tutor. It determines the paper set, whether tiering applies, how practical skills are assessed, and which published mark scheme the work should be judged against. A request for a science tutor is therefore under-specified in a way that costs real time: Physics 0625, Coordinated Sciences 0654 and Combined Science 0653 overlap in content and differ substantially in assessment.

The table below lists the codes most commonly entered by Dubai schools, with the tiering position and the assessment shape for each. Two cautions on using it. First, schools occasionally change syllabus between cohorts, so confirm the code against your child's own statement of entry rather than against a sibling's experience. Second, syllabus content is revised periodically, and a tutor whose experience is of an earlier version is teaching to a specification your child is not sitting. Both checks take one message to the school's exams officer.

What this page does not do is reproduce Cambridge material. Syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes are published by Cambridge International under its own terms, and the right practice is to reference them and link to cambridgeinternational.org rather than to supply them as downloads. A tutor who works from the published criteria and sends you the official link is doing it properly; one who offers a private library of papers and mark schemes is doing something else.

sections.heading: Core and Extended: what the tier actually decides
paragraphs: Tiering is the most consequential decision in a Cambridge IGCSE course and the one parents understand least. On most tiered syllabuses a candidate is entered either for the Core paper set or for the Extended paper set, and the Core papers cap the highest available grade at C. That ceiling exists regardless of how well a candidate performs, which means the entry decision rather than the examination decides the top of the range.

The content difference is not simply more of the same. Extended adds the material that carries the hardest marks: non-linear algebra and transformations in Mathematics, the quantitative mole chemistry in 0620, momentum and electromagnetic induction in 0625. The command terms are identical across tiers, so a Core candidate loses marks for exactly the same reasons an Extended candidate does, which is worth knowing because it means tier does not change what good tutoring looks like, only how much ground it covers.

The timing is the part that catches families. Cambridge entries in Dubai are submitted months before the papers are sat, and a tier change requested in the spring term of Year 11 is usually administratively closed rather than educationally refused. The conversation therefore belongs in the autumn term of Year 10, and it belongs there with evidence: marked timed work showing whether the Extended content is reachable from where the child currently stands, and an estimate of the hours it would take. That is a concrete, bounded use of tuition money with a checkable outcome.

sections.heading: How each Cambridge component is assessed, and where the marks go
paragraphs: Cambridge separates assessment into components with different jobs, and candidates lose marks in component-specific ways. Multiple-choice papers punish misread stems and rushed elimination rather than lack of knowledge. Structured theory papers award method and intermediate steps, so an answer that is right but unexplained can score less than one that is wrong but well set out. Practical and alternative-to-practical papers assess handling of data, apparatus and method description, which is a separate skill set from the theory.

The table that follows maps that component by component. It deliberately does not publish percentage weightings, for a reason worth stating: weightings vary by syllabus and are revised between versions, and a number restated on a tutoring page is exactly the kind of figure that becomes wrong without anyone noticing. The syllabus document for your child's exam year carries the authoritative weighting, and a tutor should be working from that document rather than from memory.

What the table is for is sequencing. If you know which component is carrying your child's largest pool of recoverable marks, the order of work chooses itself. A Chemistry candidate losing heavily on the practical paper and moderately on theory should start with the practical, because those losses are checklist-fixable and the evidence arrives within weeks. A candidate losing everywhere on the theory paper needs the content diagnosis first, and the practical checklist will not rescue the grade on its own. Ask a tutor to state that ordering explicitly in the first week, in one sentence per component, so the plan can be judged later against what it said it would do.

sections.heading: Command terms: the vocabulary that awards the marks
paragraphs: More Cambridge IGCSE marks are lost to command terms than to any single topic, and the loss is invisible to the student. A candidate who answers describe when the question says explain believes they have answered it. They have written true, relevant, well-expressed content and earned none of the available application marks, because the question was asking for a mechanism and they supplied an observation. Revision does not touch this, because nothing the student knows is missing.

The fix is a rule, taught once and tested repeatedly on marked work. Each command term implies a shape of answer: a cause-and-effect chain, a comparison with both sides stated, a judgement with criteria, a figure read from a graph with units. Once a student can name the shape required before writing, the mark follows from content they already had. This is why a short block aimed at command-term discipline often moves more marks per dirham than a term of content revision in a subject like Biology.

The table below sets out the terms that recur most across Cambridge IGCSE papers, with what each requires and the characteristic loss. It is deliberately usable by a parent: you can read a returned script against it and see the pattern yourself, without knowing the subject. If the same term is being mishandled in week two and week ten, that is a question for the tutor rather than for the child, because it means a rule was never installed.

sections.heading: The practical papers, and why they are the cheapest marks to recover
paragraphs: Cambridge science syllabuses assess practical skills through either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper, and this is where otherwise strong Dubai candidates leak marks most predictably. The losses are not knowledge failures. They are habits: axes left unlabelled or scaled awkwardly, significant figures inconsistent between a table and a conclusion, a control mentioned rather than named, a method described without saying what is being measured, and a conclusion that restates the data instead of answering the question asked.

Because they are habits, they are the cheapest marks in the subject to recover. A short block aimed at one component, with a repeatable checklist applied to past questions until it becomes automatic, often moves more marks than the same hours spent on theory. It also produces evidence quickly, which matters if a family is deciding whether tuition is worth continuing. A tutor who has worked extensively on these answers knows the patterns; one who has taught only theory will teach the content again instead.

For students studying online there is a reasonable question about how practical skills can be developed without a laboratory. The honest answer is that the paper does not assess laboratory manipulation; it assesses recording, plotting, interpreting and describing method, all of which are written skills practised on past questions and real data sets. Where a child sits the practical test rather than the alternative paper, the hands-on work belongs to the school's laboratory sessions, and a tutor's role is preparing the recording and analysis that surround them.

sections.heading: Three series, six zones, and the deadlines that sit months early
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with a March series as well, and Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. For Dubai families this means two children in the same year group can be working to deadlines months apart, and that a resit route may be available sooner than the next summer.

The administrative detail that matters most is zoning. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for that zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask your child's exams officer which zone the centre sits in, and build any revision plan against that timetable rather than against a generic one found online.

The March 2027 series is the clearest worked example of how far ahead the real deadlines sit. The exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries are due 27 November 2026, forecast grades are due 27 February 2027, results reach centres on Direct on 13 May 2027, and certificates follow in late June. An entry deadline three months before the first paper is the reason a tier conversation has to happen in the autumn, and the reason booking a scarce specialist late is both dearer and less likely to succeed.

sections.heading: Grade reporting, and what a Dubai sixth form reads
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE results arrive in a form that confuses families, partly because schools in Dubai report in different conventions and partly because the grade on a certificate is doing several jobs at once. It signals attainment, it records which tier was sat, and it functions as an admissions threshold for a post-16 route. Those three uses pull in different directions, which is why a grade that feels acceptable at home can be insufficient for a particular subject at a particular school.

What a Dubai sixth form actually reads is its own published entry requirement for the specific subject. Those requirements are set by the school rather than nationally, they differ between A Level and the IB Diploma even on one campus, and they are usually stricter for the sciences and Mathematics. A family working backwards from a published threshold has a target; one working from a general wish to improve has a monthly payment. Ask the school for the document in writing, in Year 10 rather than Year 11.

The other reader is the Ministry of Education, for equivalency. On the British track, the published requirement counts five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among those five, alongside one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. That is a different standard from a sixth form's and should be checked on the Ministry's own pages rather than inferred from a tutoring page.

sections.heading: Coursework, academic honesty and what a tutor will not do
paragraphs: Some Cambridge IGCSE syllabuses include work produced over time rather than only timed papers, and that work must be the student's own. A tutor teaches the skills, explains how the published criteria award marks, gives feedback on drafts the student has written, and coaches planning and revision of their own text. A tutor does not supply wording for a submission and does not edit a piece to completion on a student's behalf. No qualification, rate or relationship changes that.

The boundary matters because the consequence falls on the student. A submission that is not the candidate's own work is a malpractice matter for the candidate, and the sanction attaches to them rather than to whoever helped. One operation found in research for these pages sells completed Internal Assessments outright at a published price, which is precisely the practice this boundary exists to exclude. Ask any prospective tutor the question directly and listen for a clear answer rather than a comfortable one.

There is a parallel limit on materials. Cambridge publishes syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes under its own terms, and supplying them as downloads is not something a tutor should offer. Reference them, cite the official page, and link to cambridgeinternational.org. A tutor who marks your child's work against the published criteria and sends you the official link is working correctly; one who offers a private archive of papers and mark schemes is offering something with a different set of problems attached.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge IGCSE syllabus code is my child in Dubai actually entered for?
faqs.answer: It is printed on the statement of entry, and the school's exams officer can confirm it in one message. The code matters more than the subject name because it determines the paper set, whether tiering applies and how practical skills are assessed. Physics 0625, Coordinated Sciences 0654 and Combined Science 0653 overlap in content and are assessed quite differently; Mathematics 0580 and Additional Mathematics 0606 are separate courses often taken together. Confirm it against your own child's entry rather than a sibling's, because schools occasionally change syllabus between cohorts.

faqs.question: Does Core tier really limit the grade my child can get?
faqs.answer: Yes. On Cambridge tiered syllabuses the Core paper set caps the highest available grade at C, regardless of how well a candidate performs. That is an administrative ceiling set by the entry rather than a judgement about ability. Because entries in Dubai are submitted months before the papers, the ceiling is often fixed before parents realise it exists. If your child needs a subject at A Level or at Higher Level in the Diploma, the tier conversation belongs in the autumn term of Year 10, supported by marked timed work showing whether the Extended content is reachable.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge Physics 0625 and Coordinated Sciences 0654?
faqs.answer: 0625 is a single-subject syllabus assessed on its own paper set, with its own practical assessment. 0654 assesses biology, chemistry and physics together across combined components, covering overlapping content to a different depth. The practical implication for tutoring is that a weakness in one discipline inside 0654 drags the overall grade while remaining invisible in the result, so a diagnostic that reports performance separately by discipline is worth the first hour. Confirm which your child is entered for before booking, because the paper set and the past-paper practice differ.

faqs.question: How are Cambridge IGCSE practical skills assessed if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: The written practical component does not assess laboratory manipulation. It assesses recording, plotting, interpreting data and describing method, all of which are written skills practised on past questions and real data sets. Where a school enters candidates for the practical test rather than the alternative paper, the hands-on work belongs to the school's laboratory sessions and a tutor's role is the recording and analysis around them. These are also the cheapest marks in the subject to recover, because the losses are habits: unlabelled axes, inconsistent significant figures, controls named vaguely.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks on answers that look correct?
faqs.answer: Usually command terms or unwritten method. A candidate who answers describe when the question says explain has written true, relevant content and earned none of the available application marks, because the question asked for a mechanism and received an observation. Revision does not fix it, since nothing the student knows is missing. The other common case is Mathematics method marks: working done mentally and never recorded means the marks for the route to the answer were never available. Both are rules, taught once and tested repeatedly on marked work rather than revised.

faqs.question: Can my child sit Cambridge IGCSE in March rather than waiting until June?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a March series alongside June and November, so for many Dubai candidates an earlier route exists. The constraint is the entry deadline rather than readiness: for the March 2027 series, final entries are due 27 November 2026 for an exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027, with results on Direct from 13 May 2027. Whether your centre offers the March series for a given syllabus is a question for the exams officer, and the answer should be obtained well before the November deadline rather than in January.

faqs.question: What is a Cambridge administrative zone and why should we care in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and each zone has its own version of the exam timetable. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. The practical step is to ask your child's exams officer which zone the centre sits in and to build any revision plan against that timetable, rather than against a generic timetable found online or restated on a tutoring page.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics 0606 worth taking alongside 0580?
faqs.answer: It depends on the post-16 plan rather than on general ability. 0606 is a separate syllabus taken alongside 0580, and it assumes fluency that 0580 only introduces, which is why its losses sit in prerequisite algebra and trigonometry rather than in the topic being examined. For a student heading towards A Level Mathematics or Higher Level Analysis and Approaches, it closes a real gap. For a student who will not continue with Mathematics, the hours are usually better spent elsewhere. Ask the school why it is being offered to your child specifically.

faqs.question: Should a Cambridge IGCSE tutor follow our Dubai school's teaching order?
faqs.answer: In term time, yes. The value of weekly one-to-one is fixing this week's lesson while the homework is still open and the content is fresh, and a tutor running a parallel syllabus at their own pace creates a second set of deadlines while leaving the school's work untouched. Ask them to work from the scheme of work, the syllabus code on the statement of entry and the school's assessment calendar. In the eight to ten weeks before a series the order should change, following the mark distribution of the papers instead.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge component should we work on first?
faqs.answer: Whichever carries the largest pool of recoverable marks for your child, which is not always the one with the lowest score. In the sciences that is usually the practical or alternative-to-practical paper, because the losses are habits and a checklist fixes them within weeks, producing evidence quickly. In Mathematics it is usually method marks, recoverable on the very next paper sat. Content diagnosis comes second unless the theory paper is weak across the board. A tutor should be able to name the component and the loss pattern in the trial lesson.

faqs.question: Where can we get Cambridge past papers and mark schemes properly?
faqs.answer: From Cambridge itself, through cambridgeinternational.org and through your child's school, which has access to material for its own candidates. A tutor should reference and link those sources rather than supply a private archive, because Cambridge publishes syllabuses, papers and mark schemes under its own terms and redistributing them is not something a tutoring provider should be doing. A tutor who marks your child's work against the published criteria and sends you the official link is working correctly, and that is also the practice that keeps the marking honest.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a Cambridge IGCSE coursework component?
faqs.answer: With the skills, the criteria and feedback on drafts the student has written, yes. With producing any part of the submission, no. A tutor explains how the published criteria award marks, coaches planning and redrafting, and comments on what the student has already produced. They supply no wording and do not edit a piece to completion. Malpractice sanctions attach to the candidate rather than to whoever helped, which is why the boundary matters to your child specifically. Ask the question directly; a vague answer is itself informative.

faqs.question: Does a Cambridge IGCSE tutor come to our address in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Tuition for families in the UAE is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, and home visiting is a service offered only in India. The in-home market in Dubai does exist, at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel inside the fee. What online delivery changes for a Cambridge family is access to code-level experience: a tutor who has taught 0606 or 0478 across several series is available at a workable Gulf Standard Time hour rather than only if they happen to live nearby.

faqs.question: How many Cambridge IGCSE subjects should my child take in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The school decides the offer and the number, and the useful question is what the grades are for. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, the published rule counts five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among those five. One page ranking for these queries states six subjects are required, which does not match the published rule. For a Dubai sixth form, the binding constraint is its own published per-subject entry grades, which differ between the A Level and Diploma routes.

faqs.question: Are Cambridge grades reported as letters or numbers in Dubai schools?
faqs.answer: Both conventions appear, depending on the syllabus and the school's reporting practice, which is a frequent source of confusion when families compare children across schools. What matters is not the convention but the standard being applied by whoever reads the grade. A Dubai sixth form applies its own published per-subject entry requirement; the Ministry of Education applies the equivalency rule of five accredited subjects at no less than E or grade 3. Ask the school for its own threshold document in Year 10 and work the tuition plan backwards from that number.

dubai/cambridge-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the code, then the component
dubai/cambridge-igcse-tutor.closingBody: Ask the school's exams officer for the four-digit syllabus code, the tier and the series, and ask which of the six Cambridge administrative zones your centre sits in. Then ask a prospective tutor which component carries your child's largest pool of recoverable marks and why. Those four pieces of information turn a vague request for a Cambridge IGCSE tutor into a plan with a sequence and a deadline. A free trial lesson comes first, with no card details and no commitment, and every weighting or date should be confirmed in the syllabus document for your child's own exam year.

intro.heading: The word 'certified' does a lot of work in this search, so let us pin it down
paragraphs: There is no single badge that makes someone a certified IB tutor in Dubai. The International Baccalaureate authorises schools, not freelance tutors, and it runs professional development for teachers employed by those schools. So when a listing says 'certified', the honest follow-up question is: certified by whom, in what, and can you show me the document? Almost every useful answer falls into one of four buckets: a degree in the subject, a teaching qualification, a record of having taught or marked the course, or a government permit to tutor privately in the UAE. Each of those is checkable. Nothing else on a tutoring profile is.

The one piece of paper that is genuinely compulsory is the UAE private tuition work permit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. According to u.ae, the permit is granted free of charge for two years, and the people eligible to hold one include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone giving private lessons without that permit is, in the government's own words, subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so nobody should be quoting you an amount.

Dubai adds a second layer that catches parents out. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority regulates private schools in the emirate, and it issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes that operate from premises with staff. That permit belongs to a building and a business, not to an individual on a laptop. A tutoring brand that holds it can say so and show the number. A brand that does not hold it should never imply otherwise, and a parent who sees a regulator's logo on a tutoring site is entitled to ask for the permit number before anything else.

IB Gram is a matching platform, not a school and not a training institute with a Dubai address. We hold no board accreditation and we do not claim any. What we do is read your child's situation, put forward a tutor whose subject background fits it, let you test that tutor in a free trial lesson, and change the match if the first one does not work. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on a shared screen, scheduled around a Dubai school week. We do not send anyone to a UAE address; in-home visits are a service we run only in India.

The rest of this page is a verification manual. It lists the credentials that exist in this market, what each one tells you about teaching quality, how to check it without taking anyone's word, and the three questions that separate a subject specialist from a generalist who has read the syllabus once. It also covers the things certification cannot tell you, because the gap between a qualified teacher and the right teacher for your child is where most tutoring money is wasted.

dubai/certified-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: Certification questions change shape depending on which IB programme your child is in. A PYP parent is asking about generalist primary teaching; a DP parent is asking whether someone has taught a specific HL syllabus to examination. Here is how each programme sits in Dubai.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, normally three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. Assessment is a mix of externally marked papers and internally assessed work that the school marks and the IB moderates. This is the programme where subject specialism matters most, because a tutor who has taught Chemistry HL to examination knows things about the Paper 2 markscheme that no generalist does.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the DP is concentrated in a set of IB World Schools in Emirates Hills, Al Barsha, Al Sufouh, Nad Al Sheba and Dubai Festival City, while the majority of the emirate's secondary cohort sits IGCSE then A Level instead. That makes DP subject teachers a smaller pool locally than the raw school count suggests, and it is why verifying a specialism matters more here than in a city where every school runs the Diploma.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, with command terms and task-specific clarifications doing most of the work. Reports arrive as criterion letters and numbers rather than percentages, which is why parents often cannot tell whether a 5 is a problem. A tutor who has written MYP task sheets can read that report; one who has not will guess.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools run MYP to Year 11 and then offer a choice between the Diploma and a British sixth form, so a Dubai MYP 5 student is often preparing for two different destinations at once. A tutor working with that student needs to know which criteria carry into DP internal assessment and which drop away, and should be able to name the MYP eAssessment option the school has chosen.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry rather than discrete subject syllabuses, ending in the Year 6 Exhibition. Credentials here look different: a primary teaching qualification and experience of inquiry-led planning matter more than a subject degree. Most useful tutoring at this stage is literacy fluency, number sense and the research habits the Exhibition rewards.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai PYP cohorts are unusually mobile, with children arriving mid-unit from British, Indian and American systems. A tutor's job is often to close a specific gap created by that move rather than to follow the school's inquiry cycle. Arabic as an additional language also starts early in Dubai schools under KHDA's mandatory-subject requirements, and it is the most commonly requested primary support in the emirate.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller IB route combining at least two DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, personal and professional skills, service learning and language development. Students take DP subject papers alongside a vocational qualification, so tutoring demand is usually for the DP components and for the reflective project's research structure.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is offered by only a handful of UAE schools, which means local tutor coverage for it is thin. A parent asking about certification for CP support should expect the honest answer to be about the DP courses inside it, because that is where documented subject teaching experience actually exists. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the match may come from our wider pool and the lesson still runs over video.

dubai/certified-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: Subject by subject, certification means something slightly different. Below is what to look for in a tutor for each of the subjects Dubai families ask about most, with the part of the course where an unqualified tutor is exposed fastest.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Ask which syllabus version the tutor last taught and whether they have supervised a Maths exploration through to submission. The exposure point is HL Paper 3: an extended problem-solving paper that rewards structured investigation rather than recall, and a tutor who has never set one cannot model the thinking.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The statistics and modelling content differs enough from AA that teaching one does not qualify someone for the other. Ask about graphical-display-calculator fluency and regression work. Students lose marks presenting a model without justifying its fit, which a tutor who knows the markscheme flags immediately.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The current syllabus is organised around structure and reactivity with a single scientific investigation as internal assessment. Ask whether the tutor has marked that investigation against its criteria. Organic mechanisms and energetics calculations are where Dubai students most often lose marks they could have kept.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Check that the tutor can talk about uncertainty treatment, not just equations. Paper 2 extended-response questions punish answers that quote a law without applying it to the stated situation, and HL fields and nuclear content is where a generalist's limits show within one session.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term discipline decides most grades here: outline, explain, discuss and evaluate carry different mark expectations. Ask the tutor to show how they would mark a six-mark answer. Statistical handling in the investigation is the other common weak point for Dubai cohorts.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the use of real-world material decide the grade, and HL adds a quantitative paper that catches students who have only revised theory. Ask whether the tutor has supervised the internal assessment commentaries and can name the criteria used to mark them.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Verify experience of the individual oral and of unseen textual analysis, which are different skills taught by different kinds of teacher. Students lose marks by summarising rather than analysing, and HL candidates need a separate essay on a studied work that many tutors have never set.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Ask which case-study material the tutor has worked from and how they teach tool selection under exam pressure. Answers that describe a concept without applying it to the stimulus lose the application marks, and the internal assessment's research-question framing is where most projects go wrong early.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: A programming background does not automatically cover the paper-based theory, and the reverse is also true. Ask about the internal assessment solution-development documentation, which is marked on process evidence rather than on whether the program works.

subjects.name: Arabic as an Additional Language
subjects.description: KHDA requires Dubai private schools to teach Arabic regardless of the licensed curriculum, and requires that schools ensure teachers of Arabic have the authority's approval to teach it. For tutoring, ask about experience with the specific school stream your child sits, since Arab and non-Arab classes follow different expectations.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: TOK is assessed by an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title. A tutor's role is questioning and feedback on the student's own thinking, never drafting. Ask how they coach the choice of prescribed title, because a poor title choice costs marks that no amount of later work recovers.

subjects.name: Extended Essay supervision support
subjects.description: The school supervises the Extended Essay; a tutor can support research method, structure and the reflective process around it. Ask how they handle the boundary between coaching and authorship, and expect a clear answer. A tutor who is vague about that boundary is a risk to your child's candidature.

dubai/certified-ib-tutor.regionsTitle: Where in Dubai families ask these questions
dubai/certified-ib-tutor.regionsIntro: Verification questions arrive differently across the emirate. In the IB-dense communities parents are comparing a tutor against the subject teacher they already have; in the British-curriculum belts they are often checking whether a tutor understands the Diploma at all.

regions.name: Al Barsha
regions.note: Dense with large through-schools running both IB and British routes. Parents here frequently ask whether a tutor has taught the Diploma specifically, because their own school offers two post-16 paths and advice gets mixed.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and The Meadows
regions.note: Long-established IB Diploma catchment. Requests concentrate on HL sciences and Maths AA HL, and parents tend to arrive with a mock paper already marked, asking whether the tutor can read it properly.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: A cluster of senior schools within a short radius, which means families often know several tutors by reputation. The verification question here is usually about permit status rather than subject depth.

regions.name: Oud Metha
regions.note: Older established schools with large cohorts and strong Indian-curriculum presence alongside IGCSE. Parents comparing a Diploma tutor with a CBSE-trained one need the difference in assessment style spelled out.

regions.name: Al Qusais
regions.note: High demand for maths and science support at middle-school level, often for siblings at the same time. Scheduling two consecutive online sessions after the school run is the practical constraint families raise first.

regions.name: Mirdif
regions.note: Villa communities feeding a mix of British and American schools, with MYP families asking how criterion grades translate into something they can act on.

regions.name: Nad Al Sheba
regions.note: Newer senior provision and a fast-growing DP intake. Families here are often in their first year of the Diploma and want to know which credential signals actual DP teaching experience.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis
regions.note: A large student population across several schools, with a lot of mid-year arrivals. Tutoring requests are commonly about closing a syllabus gap created by a move rather than about long-term weakness.

schoolClusters.city: IB World Schools in western Dubai
schoolClusters.note: These schools sit within a short radius of each other and between them cover PYP, MYP and the Diploma. Students from them make up a large share of DP tutoring requests in the emirate, and their internal assessment deadline calendars differ by several weeks, which matters when planning a block of sessions.

schoolClusters.city: IB and dual-route schools in eastern and central Dubai
schoolClusters.note: East of the creek the mix is broader, with Diploma provision alongside large British and Indian cohorts. Families here often need a tutor who can hold two assessment systems in mind at once, because siblings in the same household sit different qualifications.

schoolClusters.city: British-curriculum schools whose students move into the Diploma
schoolClusters.note: A significant number of Dubai DP candidates arrive from an IGCSE background at these schools, either by transferring at 16 or by choosing the Diploma inside the same group. The transition gap is the reason many first tutoring enquiries are made in DP1 term one.

sections.heading: What a certified IB tutor in Dubai can and cannot hold
paragraphs: A certified IB tutor in Dubai can hold four kinds of credential that are real and checkable: an academic qualification in the subject, a teaching qualification such as a PGCE or an equivalent licence from another jurisdiction, a documented history of teaching or examining the course, and a UAE private tuition work permit. Everything else you will see advertised is either a restatement of one of those four or a claim about something that does not exist.

What nobody can hold is a licence from the International Baccalaureate to tutor privately. The IB authorises schools to deliver its programmes and runs professional development workshops for teachers at those schools. A teacher who has completed a category one workshop in Chemistry has evidence of training; they do not have a tutoring licence, and the distinction matters because the second claim is the one that gets used to justify a higher rate.

The other thing nobody holds is regulator endorsement of a tutoring service by name. KHDA regulates private schools in Dubai and issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises and staff. That permit process begins with initial approval, allows a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and is renewed annually with the request filed at least thirty days before expiry. It is a real, specific thing, and a platform without it cannot borrow it.

The practical consequence is simple. When a profile says 'certified', read it as a prompt to ask which of the four real credentials is behind the word. A tutor who answers precisely, names the subject and level they taught and the years they taught it, is giving you more than a logo ever could. A tutor who repeats the word without a document is telling you something too.

sections.heading: The UAE private tuition permit, in the government's own words
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted, and it is regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The federal portal u.ae states that the permit is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone quoting you a permit fee is either confusing it with something else or inventing it.

Eligibility is wider than most parents expect. The published list of people who may apply includes teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in both the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page is titled 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', lists no fees, gives a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

There are conditions attached to holding one. The permit carries a code of conduct, and in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school. Press reporting of those rules describes the permit's code of conduct as barring the same thing. Treat that as reported rather than quoted, and verify it against the current ADEK document if your situation depends on it. Either way, the principle is sound: a parent should not be arranging private lessons with their child's own classroom teacher.

On enforcement, the official position is that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE will be subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts has been published. A figure circulating online could not be verified against any ministry source, which is why you will not find one on this page.

sections.heading: A thirty-minute verification routine any parent can run
paragraphs: You do not need to be an educationalist to check a tutor. You need a marked piece of your child's work and four questions. The marked work does most of the job, because reading a script accurately is a skill that cannot be faked for twenty minutes by someone who has not taught the course.

Start by asking which syllabus version the tutor last taught and in which year. IB subject guides change, and a tutor whose knowledge stops at a superseded guide will teach content your child is not assessed on. Then ask them to look at the marked script and tell you where the marks went. A specialist will talk about command terms, about an answer that described when it should have evaluated, about a method mark lost for an unjustified step. A generalist will talk about confidence and revision technique.

The third question is about internal assessment. Ask what the tutor will and will not do with a draft. The only acceptable answer involves reading what the student has already written and asking questions about it. Any offer to restructure, rewrite or supply content is an academic-honesty problem for your child, not a service, and the IB treats it as malpractice. The fourth question is the permit: ask to see it, and note that it is free, so there is no reason for anyone to be coy.

Run the free trial lesson after those four answers, not before. Sit within earshot for the first ten minutes. You are listening for whether the tutor asks your child to do something within the first five minutes, or whether they explain for twenty. The second pattern is the single most reliable sign that a tutor has not taught one-to-one before, whatever their certificates say.
