sections.heading: What certification cannot tell you, and what to use instead
paragraphs: The limits of certification are not a reason to ignore it. They are a reason to pair it with evidence. A fully qualified teacher with fifteen years in a classroom may be poor at one-to-one work, because the two jobs reward different instincts. Classroom teaching rewards explanation to a group; one-to-one rewards diagnosis of one person, and silence while that person works.

Subject fit is the second thing paper cannot capture. A Maths teacher who has spent a decade on Analysis and Approaches is not automatically right for an Applications and Interpretation student, because the statistics and modelling emphasis is genuinely different. A Physics graduate may be excellent on mechanics and weak on the uncertainty treatment that the internal assessment is marked on. Ask about the specific part of the course where your child is stuck.

Temperament is third, and it decides more outcomes than either of the others. A DP2 student six weeks from final examinations needs someone who will cut the syllabus down to what can still move marks. A DP1 student who has lost confidence after a bad first term needs someone who will rebuild the basics without making the student feel remedial. Those are different people, and no certificate distinguishes them.

This is why a free trial lesson is the centre of our process rather than a marketing device. Credentials narrow the field; the trial picks from it. If the trial does not work, you say so and we match again, and nothing has been spent. That is a more honest offer than any badge, and it is the part of the process parents in Dubai tell us actually changed their decision.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges, and what certification does to the number
paragraphs: Rates in Dubai sort themselves by what a tutor can demonstrate, and the spread is wide. Published figures across the market show budget online tutoring, often delivered by university students, starting around AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits roughly between AED 150 and 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200.

Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutoring runs higher, in the region of AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table reaching AED 450 and beyond for exam-year specialists. The top of the market, where a named or examiner-experienced tutor is advertised, reaches AED 650 at BartyED. In-home visits carry their own band, roughly AED 180 to 500 once travel is included, because somebody is paying for the car.

Those are market figures published by other providers, with their names attached so you can check them. They are not IB Gram's price list. What they tell you is the shape of the market: the single biggest driver of rate is demonstrated specialism at the level being taught, and the second biggest is format, because travel is expensive in a city this spread out. A permit, being free, moves the rate not at all.

Monthly packages advertised in the emirate include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Use those as a sanity check on any quote you are given.

sections.heading: The academic-honesty line a credentialled tutor will not cross
paragraphs: Every piece of internally assessed IB work has to be the student's own. That covers the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge, every subject's internal assessment and the MYP personal project. A tutor's legitimate role is to teach the skills, ask questions about the student's existing material, and give feedback against the published criteria. The student types every word that is submitted.

This is not a soft boundary. The IB treats the submission of work that is not the candidate's own as malpractice, and the consequences land on the student, not on the tutor who helped. In this market that matters, because at least one site competing for these searches openly sells finished internal assessments at a fixed price. A parent who buys that is buying a risk to their child's entire candidature.

So the honest version of coursework support looks slower than the advertised version. A tutor reads a research question and asks whether it can actually be answered in the word limit. They look at a method and ask what the uncontrolled variable is. They read a paragraph and ask what the evidence is for its claim. They hand it back. The student fixes it. Then the school supervisor, who is the person formally responsible, sees the next draft.

Ask any tutor you are considering what they would refuse to do. The answer tells you more about their professionalism than a certificate scan. A tutor who says they will not restructure a draft, will not supply paragraphs and will not work on anything the school has not seen is a tutor who understands the rules your child is bound by.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies sit alongside the IB in Dubai
paragraphs: Dubai parents often discover partway through the Diploma that the subjects their child must take are not only the IB ones. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were set to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. This is a federal principle applied by the emirate: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must follow the ministry's general regulations.

The organisational detail matters for tutoring. KHDA requires schools to organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and the guidance advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Schools are also required to ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have the appropriate approval from KHDA to teach those subjects, which is a concrete credential point a parent can ask about at school level.

For tutoring, the practical rule is to match the stream. A non-Arab student in Arabic as an additional language is assessed differently from an Arab student in Arabic as a first language, and a tutor needs to know which one your child sits before the first session. One more constraint: for the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the ministry is prohibited, so tutoring here follows the school's material rather than importing a parallel course.

sections.heading: Who regulates what, across the seven emirates
paragraphs: A Dubai parent moving within the UAE, or comparing schools across emirates, quickly finds that the authority in charge changes. Dubai private schools answer to KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain answer to the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. ADEK is named by effectively none of the competing tutoring pages in this market, which is an odd gap given how many families move between the two emirates.

Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate. Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, which does the same there. For Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools directly. Those five bodies are the complete regulator map for UAE private schools.

The scope differs in ways that affect parents. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum and fee approval sits with the emirate regulator rather than only inspection. In Dubai, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under the second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total.

Why this belongs on a page about tutor credentials: the regulator that matters for your child's school is not the body that permits your tutor. The school answers to KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the RAK Department of Knowledge or the ministry. The individual tutor answers to MoHRE. Conflating the two is how 'regulator-approved tutor' claims get made, and it is why a parent who understands the split is much harder to mislead.

sections.heading: Honest coverage: what happens when no specialist is free
paragraphs: Availability is the thing tutoring sites hide, and hiding it wastes a fortnight of a parent's time. The real position in Dubai is that common subjects at common levels can usually be matched quickly, and that narrow combinations cannot. Maths AA SL has depth. Chemistry HL in the eight weeks before final examinations does not, because every family in the emirate wants the same slot at the same time.

When we cannot put forward a UAE-based specialist for your subject and level, we say so, and the match comes from our wider pool of IB subject teachers working in other time zones. The lesson still runs one-to-one over live video at a Dubai-friendly time, because Gulf Standard Time overlaps comfortably with both South Asia and Europe. What changes is the tutor's location, not the format or the subject depth.

There are also requests we should decline. If a student needs a diagnosed learning-support intervention, a tutor is not the right answer and a specialist assessment is. If a family wants finished coursework, the answer is no. If a DP2 student has four subjects collapsing at once and three weeks left, the honest conversation is about which two can still move and which cannot, not about selling eight sessions a week.

The reason to publish this is that a coverage limit disclosed in advance is a smaller problem than one discovered in week three. Ask any platform you are considering the same question: what happens if you cannot find someone for my subject? An answer that includes a fallback and a timescale is worth more than a promise that it never happens.

faqs.question: What does 'certified IB tutor' actually mean in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It has no single official meaning, because the International Baccalaureate authorises schools rather than licensing individual tutors. In practice the word stands in for one of four checkable things: a degree in the subject, a teaching qualification, a documented record of teaching or examining the course, or the UAE private tuition work permit. Ask which one is meant. A tutor who answers by naming the subject and level they taught, the years they taught it and the type of school is giving you real information. A tutor who repeats the word without a document is not, and in a market this large that distinction is worth thirty seconds of your time.

faqs.question: Which permit must a private IB tutor in Dubai hold?
faqs.answer: A private tuition work permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. According to u.ae it is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's service page gives a two-working-day completion time via its smart app, website or e-services system. Eligible applicants include school and sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The official position is that anyone giving private lessons without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no schedule of amounts has been published.

faqs.question: How can I check that a tutor's IB teaching experience is real?
faqs.answer: Hand them a marked script from your child and ask where the marks went. Someone who has taught the course will talk about command terms, about an answer that described where it should have evaluated, about a method mark lost to an unjustified step. Someone who has not will talk about revision technique and confidence. Then ask which syllabus version they last taught and in which year, because subject guides change and a tutor working from a superseded one will teach content your child is not assessed on. Those two checks take twenty minutes and are more revealing than any certificate.

faqs.question: Is there such a thing as an official IB tutor qualification?
faqs.answer: No. The IB authorises schools to deliver its programmes and runs professional development workshops for teachers working at those schools. A teacher who has completed a subject workshop has evidence of programme-specific training, which is genuinely useful, but it is training rather than a tutoring licence. Nobody holds a licence from the IB to tutor privately, so any profile implying one is describing something that does not exist. Ask instead for the workshop category, the subject and the year, alongside the teaching history. That combination tells you what the person has actually been trained on.

faqs.question: Can a teacher at my child's Dubai school tutor my child privately?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a problem rather than a shortcut. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and press reporting describes the MoHRE permit's code of conduct as barring the same arrangement. Verify the current wording against the authority's own document if it matters to your decision. The underlying principle holds across the UAE: the person who assesses your child's internal work should not also be paid privately to prepare it. An independent tutor avoids that conflict entirely.

faqs.question: Does KHDA issue a licence to individual private tutors?
faqs.answer: No. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, and it issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes that operate from premises with staff. That process starts with initial approval, allows a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and is renewed annually with the request filed at least thirty days before expiry. It attaches to a business and an address, not to a person teaching from a laptop. Individual tutors are covered by the MoHRE permit instead, and the two are frequently conflated in advertising.

faqs.question: What documents should I ask a certified IB tutor in Dubai to show me?
faqs.answer: Four things, in this order. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free to hold so there is no reason for reluctance. A degree certificate or transcript for the subject, with the institution and year. A teaching qualification or licence, with the issuing jurisdiction and year. And a teaching history naming subject, level, years and school type, which is the item that most predicts whether a session will be useful. If someone declines all four, that is your answer. If they supply all four, you still run the free trial lesson before deciding.

faqs.question: Do university students in Dubai qualify for a private tuition permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The published eligibility list on u.ae includes university students, alongside teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals and school students aged 15 to 18. Holding the permit makes the arrangement lawful; it says nothing about subject depth. A second-year undergraduate may be excellent for MYP maths homework support and quite unsuitable for Chemistry HL eight weeks before final papers. Market rates reflect that: published budget bands featuring student tutors sit far below the specialist bands, which is a rational pricing signal rather than a judgement.

faqs.question: Is a subject degree more useful than a teaching qualification for IB tutoring?
faqs.answer: They answer different questions and the better tutor usually has evidence of both plus course-specific experience. A degree shows content knowledge above syllabus level, which matters for HL extension work and for explaining why a method works. A teaching qualification shows trained pedagogy and assessed practice, which matters for sequencing and for diagnosing a misconception rather than re-explaining. Neither tells you whether the person knows this syllabus version, how its internal assessment is marked, or where candidates habitually drop marks. That comes from having taught the course to examination, which is the credential to ask about last and weight most.

faqs.question: How long does a UAE private tuition work permit stay valid?
faqs.answer: Two years, and u.ae states that it is granted free of charge. MoHRE's own service page for it is titled 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', lists no fees, and gives a two-working-day completion time through the smart app, website and e-services system. When you ask to see a permit, check the issue date rather than only the document itself, since a lapsed permit is the same position as no permit. The permit also carries a code of conduct, so it is reasonable to ask the tutor what conditions they understand themselves to be working under.

faqs.question: What should I do if a tutoring website says a regulator has endorsed it?
faqs.answer: Ask for the permit number and the licensed address, then check them. The only Dubai permit that could support such a claim is a KHDA Educational Services Permit held by a training institute with premises, and it is specific enough to be verified. If a site cannot produce a number, the claim is decoration. The same test applies to board names: the IB, Cambridge and Pearson do not accredit tutoring platforms, so a logo on a website proves nothing about teaching quality. IB Gram holds no such permit and makes no such claim, which is why this page explains the difference rather than borrowing the authority.

faqs.question: Does a certified tutor still need to know my child's exact subject guide?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is where most mismatches happen. IB subject guides are revised, and a revision can change the number of papers, the internal assessment task and the content that is examinable. A tutor who last taught a superseded guide will teach accurately and uselessly. Before the first session, send the tutor the school's course outline and the assessment calendar, and ask them to confirm which guide version your child is sitting. A specialist will already be asking you that question. It takes one message and it prevents a term of well-delivered lessons aimed at the wrong target.

faqs.question: How do I verify a tutor's identity before a first online lesson?
faqs.answer: Ask for the lesson to begin with camera on and for the tutor to confirm their full name, the subject and level they are teaching and their teaching background in the first minute, with you present. Match that against what you were sent in writing beforehand. Keep the first session in a shared room rather than a bedroom, and keep the lesson on the platform's own link rather than a personal channel. For a child, the practical safeguarding rules matter as much as the credential: a named adult in the house knows when the session runs and can see the screen.

faqs.question: Can one verified tutor cover both Maths AA and Physics for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth testing rather than assuming. Plenty of physics teachers are strong on the mechanics and calculus overlap, and a single tutor reduces scheduling friction and gives one person the whole picture of a student's week. The limits appear at Higher Level, where Maths AA Paper 3 and the physics internal assessment reward quite different skills. Our usual approach is to try one tutor for both in the trial, look at how they handle the weaker of the two subjects, and split into two specialists if that answer is thin. The decision is made on the trial, not on the CV.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor we start with turns out to be the wrong match?
faqs.answer: You tell us and we match again at no additional cost. It is worth distinguishing two situations, because they need different responses. If the subject knowledge is thin, change tutor. If the subject knowledge is fine but the student is not engaging, the issue may be session design rather than the person, and a change of format or time often fixes it. We review at the fourth session for exactly this reason: four sessions is enough to see whether technique is moving, even before a grade does, and early enough that a term has not been lost.

Tell us the subject, the level and the school, and we will tell you honestly what we can cover.

dubai/certified-igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE one-to-one, working from the specification your child's school entered them for. Each holds qualifications they can describe precisely, and where a permit or a teaching credential is relevant, this page explains what it covers and how you can check it for yourself.

intro.heading: Two questions hiding inside one word
paragraphs: Certified is doing a lot of work in this search, and it is worth pulling apart before anything else. One meaning is legal: the UAE regulates private tuition through a work permit, and a tutor operating without one is in breach of it. The other meaning is professional: whether this person has a teaching qualification, a relevant degree, and real familiarity with the specification your child will sit. Those are separate things. A tutor can hold the permit and have never taught Cambridge Chemistry 0620, or hold a doctorate in chemistry and no permit at all.

The legal position is clear and worth stating in full. Private tuition in the UAE is covered by the private tutor work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers working in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to you by anyone.

The professional position is where most of a parent's money is decided, and it is less tidy. There is no single IGCSE tutoring certificate. What exists is a set of credentials, each of which evidences something narrow: a degree evidences subject knowledge, a teaching qualification evidences training in instruction, school employment evidences that an institution made a hiring judgement, and specification experience evidences familiarity with the papers themselves. Parents frequently buy the first and need the last. The tables below map which is which and how each can be checked.

IB Gram is an independent IB and IGCSE tutor-matching platform. It does not hold or claim approval, accreditation or licensing from KHDA, from the Ministry of Education, from Cambridge International or from Pearson, has no partnership with any school named on this page, and operates no office in the UAE. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific thing issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, and IB Gram does not hold one. Saying so plainly is more useful to you than the phrase this market overuses.

Because the brief for this page is what the papers assess and where marks are lost, the second half goes there. A credential tells you what someone has done; it does not tell you that Extended Mathematics awards marks for working your child is not writing down, that Physics Paper 6 loses candidates marks on graph axes and controls, or that a correct Economics definition earns nothing if it is never applied to the stimulus material. Those are the things a session fixes, and they are the reason certification is a floor rather than an answer. Tuition for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video; IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and home visiting is offered only in India.

dubai/certified-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Credentials matter differently at each stage of a British-curriculum school career in Dubai, and the certificate a family is ultimately working towards is the IGCSE itself rather than anything a tutor holds. These are the stages and what each one is assessed on.

programmes.name: IGCSE Core tier
programmes.description: Core candidates sit the Core paper set and are assessed on a narrower band of syllabus content. On Cambridge syllabuses the Core papers cap the available grade at C, which means the tier itself limits what the eventual certificate can show. The assessment demand is lower but the command terms are identical, so the marks still turn on reading the question properly.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools finalise entries months before the papers are sat, so the Core-or-Extended decision stops being a live choice partway through Year 10. Where a child needs a subject at A Level or Higher Level in the Diploma, a Core entry can close that door administratively. A diagnostic session can tell you whether the Extended content is reachable from where your child is, which is the evidence that conversation with the school needs.

programmes.name: IGCSE Extended tier
programmes.description: Extended carries the full syllabus and the full grade range, reported as A* to G or 9 to 1 depending on the syllabus and the school's convention. The additional content is where most marks are lost: non-linear algebra and transformations in Maths, moles and electrolysis in Chemistry, momentum and electromagnetic induction in Physics. The papers are longer and the method marks are worth more.
programmes.countryNote: Extended dominates in the Dubai schools feeding sixth forms that run A Level or the IB Diploma, because both post-16 routes assume the Extended content. Dubai sixth forms publish their own per-subject entry thresholds rather than working to a national standard, and because many campuses run both routes, the same Extended grade can be enough for one and short for the other.

programmes.name: Mandatory UAE subjects alongside the curriculum
programmes.ageRange: All year groups in Dubai private schools
programmes.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the licensed international curriculum in Dubai private schools under KHDA requirements, regardless of which curriculum the school is licensed for. These are separate courses with their own requirements rather than a cultural add-on, and they occupy real timetable hours that families planning tuition should account for.
programmes.countryNote: KHDA requires schools to organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and for any mandatory subject it is advised that a lesson runs at least 25 minutes.

programmes.name: Ministry of Education equivalency at 16 to 18
programmes.description: For UAE university entry, the certificate that matters is the Ministry of Education equivalency attestation rather than anything a tutor holds. On the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.
programmes.countryNote: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. One page ranking for these queries states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published rule. IB Gram does not perform or guarantee equivalency; the process belongs to the Ministry and its figures should be verified on the Ministry's own pages before any family plans around them.

dubai/certified-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: A credential does not tell you where the marks go. For each subject below, the specific loss is named: that is what a session fixes, and it is the thing to test a prospective tutor on rather than their certificate.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Extended candidates lose method marks for working done mentally and never written. Transformations, algebraic fraction manipulation and multi-step problems are the reliable losses. A session fixes the habit of recording a line of working before an answer, which is worth marks on every paper.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Assumes fluency that 0580 only introduces, so the losses are not carelessness but genuine gaps in prerequisite algebra and trigonometry. A session fixes the prerequisite rather than the topic in front of the student, which is why diagnosing it properly saves hours.

subjects.name: Physics (0625)
subjects.description: Two distinct losses. In the theory papers, momentum, circuits and electromagnetic induction demand exact formula use and a stated relationship before substitution. In Paper 6, candidates lose marks on graph axes, significant figures, and describing a control instead of naming one.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: The mole is the single biggest determinant of an Extended grade. Candidates who cannot move between mass, moles and concentration unprompted lose marks across several papers at once. Electrolysis, rates of reaction and the final organic topics are the other predictable losses.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Marked strictly against command terms. Students who know the content still score half marks by describing where the question says explain, and by using everyday words where the specification has a precise term. A session fixes command-term discipline, which is a rule rather than revision.

subjects.name: English Language (0500) and English as a Second Language (0510)
subjects.description: The reading-response marks are among the most teachable on any IGCSE paper because they reward a specific technique rather than general flair. The more consequential issue in Dubai cohorts is children entered for the wrong one of the two routes, which is a question for the school.

subjects.name: Economics (0455) and Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Lost on the long questions. Candidates define terms accurately, then never connect them to the data or the case study, so application and evaluation marks go unclaimed. A session fixes answer structure and the discipline of quoting the stimulus material.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Paper 2 requires algorithms in the published pseudocode conventions, and students fluent in Python lose marks writing Python instead. Paper 1 theory on data representation and networks rewards exact vocabulary, which responds well to a structured list and short recall testing.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (0508) and Foreign Language (0544)
subjects.description: Arabic runs alongside the international curriculum in Dubai private schools under KHDA requirements, and the first-language and additional-language routes are different courses with different demands. Children are sometimes placed by nationality rather than competence, and the placement is worth checking before tuition starts.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Sciences (0654, 0653)
subjects.description: Three disciplines compressed into one or two grades, so a weakness in one pulls the result down invisibly. A diagnostic that reports performance separately by discipline is worth the first hour, because the actual fix is almost always narrower than the overall grade suggests.

dubai/certified-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: Where a family lives in Dubai changes when a session can start and which regulator governs the school, but not which credentials a tutor needs. These are the areas families ask about most, with the practical detail that affects scheduling.

regions.name: Dubai Marina, JBR and Al Sufouh
regions.note: Apartment living with school buses arriving late, so sessions realistically start from 17:00. All private schools here fall under KHDA, which publishes each school's inspection rating and fee on its own profile, and those profiles are the place to check what a school actually offers.

regions.name: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Mizhar
regions.note: Villa communities with nearby schools and early home times, supporting 16:00 starts. Large IGCSE cohorts and heavy demand for Maths and the sciences, which is where credential questions most often turn into specification questions.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate and Arabian Ranches
regions.note: Wide catchments feeding the Al Qudra and Umm Suqeim school corridors, with several campuses running both A Level and the IB Diploma. Families here often need to know which post-16 route they are targeting before setting an IGCSE grade target.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1, 2 and 3
regions.note: Short school runs, early session starts, and long-established British-curriculum schools with published KHDA inspection histories. Mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education provision varies in quality between these schools, and that is visible in inspection reports.

regions.name: Business Bay, Downtown and DIFC
regions.note: Tower living where the practical constraint is a room with a door that shuts. Session timing here often works better before parents are home rather than after, and online delivery makes that slot available without a second journey.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle, Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens
regions.note: School runs crossing Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, where afternoon journeys double. A 17:30 start is realistic. These are also the areas where a visiting tutor's travel time would be charged for and buy nothing a parent wants.

regions.name: Deira, Bur Dubai and Al Qusais
regions.note: British and Indian-curriculum schools side by side, with strong IGCSE Maths and science demand. Session timing is usually built around Maghrib and family dinner rather than around traffic, and shifts again through Ramadan.

regions.note: Outlying communities where the local pool of specification-specific tutors is thinnest. Credentials are easy to find; experience of 0606 or 0478 within driving distance is not, which is the clearest practical argument for an online match.

sections.heading: What certified can and cannot mean for an IGCSE tutor in Dubai
paragraphs: There is no IGCSE tutoring certificate. No examination board issues one, no UAE regulator issues one, and any provider implying otherwise is describing something that does not exist. What exists is a set of separate credentials, each evidencing a narrow thing, plus one legal requirement that applies to the activity rather than the person's teaching ability. Knowing which is which turns a vague reassurance into a checkable list.

The distinction that matters most is between permission and competence. The MoHRE private tuition work permit is permission: it says the holder may lawfully provide private lessons in the UAE. It says nothing about whether they can teach Cambridge Physics 0625. A PGCE or equivalent teaching qualification evidences training in instruction. A degree evidences subject knowledge at a level above the syllabus. School employment evidences that an institution made a hiring judgement about that person. Specification experience, which is what most parents actually need, is evidenced by nothing except a track record someone can describe in detail.

The table below is the map. Use it as a question list rather than a demand: a tutor who can tell you which of these they hold, and what each one covers, is already more transparent than most profiles in this market. IB Gram holds no regulator or board approval of its own, does not operate a UAE office, and does not hold a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is the specific permit issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai. Where a credential matters to you, the last column is how to check it without taking anyone's word.

sections.heading: The UAE private tuition permit, by category of tutor
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers working in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, available through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published anywhere official. A figure circulating online could not be verified against any ministry source, and Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties. Any provider quoting a specific fine to you is repeating an unverified number, which is itself a useful signal about the rest of their claims.

One condition deserves emphasis because it affects a very common request. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the holder's own school. This is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document itself, so verify it against current ADEK material before relying on it. The practical point stands in any emirate: your child's own classroom teacher, privately, is not a request to make.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and why it matters to tuition
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and each school's rating and published fee sit on its own KHDA profile. That profile, rather than a school's prospectus, is the place to check what a school actually offers and how it was last judged.

Across the rest of the country the picture differs, and almost no competitor page says so. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education there. Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same, and the Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval and not only inspection sits with the emirate.

For a Dubai family the practical use of this is twofold. First, inspection reports are a free, independent read on the department teaching your child, and a school rated well overall can still have a weak department. Second, if you relocate within the UAE, the regulator changes and so do some of the rules around tuition and school transfer. Context on Dubai specifically: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, and Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools creating 16,846 new places.

sections.heading: What no certificate tells you: how IGCSE papers award marks
paragraphs: IGCSE grades are produced by papers marked to published criteria, and the criteria are specific. That specificity is the whole opportunity. A candidate does not lose a grade because they are weak at Chemistry; they lose it because they cannot move between mass, moles and concentration without prompting, and that single inability costs marks in three separate papers. Diagnosing at that level of detail is a skill, and it is one no credential on the previous tables evidences.

Command terms are the clearest case. Describe, explain and suggest ask for different things, and a student who answers all three as if they said describe loses application and evaluation marks consistently, on every paper, in every series. Content revision does not touch it, because the student believes they answered the question. The fix is a rule, taught once and tested repeatedly on marked work, and it is usually worth more marks in a term than any amount of re-teaching the syllabus.

Method marks are the second case. Extended Mathematics awards marks for working; candidates who compute mentally and write only a result lose marks on answers that were substantially correct. Physics awards a mark for stating the relationship before substituting into it. Paper 6 in the sciences awards marks for labelling axes properly, quoting significant figures consistently and naming a control rather than gesturing at one. None of this is secret. It is published structure, and the value a tutor adds is knowing which of it is costing your child the most and teaching that first.
bullets: Grades turn on patterned, diagnosable losses rather than general weakness

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks actually go missing, by subject and component
paragraphs: The table in this section is the practical centre of the page. Each row names a subject, the component where marks are most often lost, the specific failure behind that loss, and what a session does about it. It is also a useful test of a prospective tutor: read them a row for your child's subject and ask whether they agree and what they would add. A tutor with real specification experience will immediately qualify or extend it; one without will agree pleasantly.

Two patterns run through every row. The first is that the loss is almost always narrower than the grade implies. A grade 5 across a science subject usually traces to two or three recurring failures, not to a general deficit, which is why a diagnostic hour is worth more than a term of coverage. The second is that a large share of the losses are about how an answer is written rather than what the student knows, which is why marked written work between sessions matters more than lesson time.

What a session cannot do is also worth stating. It cannot install content that was never taught, in the weeks before a paper, across a whole syllabus. Where a child arrives eight weeks out with large content gaps, the honest plan is triage: pick the two or three topics carrying the most available marks for that child and say explicitly which parts of the specification are being left alone. A tutor unwilling to name what they are not covering is not planning, and the result is thin coverage of everything.

sections.heading: The certificate that actually matters: Ministry of Education equivalency
paragraphs: For families intending a UAE university, the document that decides things is not a tutor's credential but the Ministry of Education's equivalency attestation of your child's qualifications. On the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That five-subject rule is worth holding onto, because at least one page ranking for UAE tutoring queries states that candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB, no points threshold is published in the source this page relies on, so none is quoted here: verify any IB figure on the Ministry's own pages or with the emirate attestation authority.

Two cautions. IB Gram does not perform, expedite or guarantee equivalency; it is a Ministry process and families should use the official channel. And tuition is not required for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression, so treat any provider framing it that way as applying false urgency to a regulatory process. What tuition can legitimately do is help a child reach the grades that the rule counts, which is a different and more honest claim.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the IGCSE
paragraphs: Dubai private schools teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside whichever international curriculum they are licensed for, and these are not optional enrichment. KHDA's mandatory-subject requirements apply regardless of the licensed curriculum, and the authority stated that its requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year starts in April. The federal baseline behind this is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

The organisational rules are specific and worth knowing, because they explain a good deal of what parents observe. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, and Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Two further details matter for planning. Instructional time for the mandatory subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Schools are also required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach these subjects. For the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited, which is a real constraint on how tutoring material for these subjects can be described.

sections.heading: The boundary no credential removes: assessed work
paragraphs: Some IGCSE subjects carry assessed components that must be the student's own, and no qualification a tutor holds changes what may be done with them. A tutor teaches, explains the criteria, gives feedback on what a student has already produced, and coaches planning and redrafting. They do not supply text for a submission and do not edit a piece to completion on the student's behalf. The consequence of crossing that line lands on the child, as a malpractice matter, rather than on the person who crossed it.

This boundary is not hypothetical in the UAE market. One operation found in research for these pages sells completed Internal Assessments outright at a published price, which is an academic-integrity breach and, for the student, an expulsion risk. The reason to state the boundary on a page like this rather than in small print is that parents are entitled to know where a provider stands before a tutor is in a room with their child, and a provider vague about it has answered the question.

There is a related limit on materials. Boards publish syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes under their own terms, and reproducing or supplying them as downloads is not something a tutor should offer. The right practice is to reference them, cite the official source, and point families to the board's own pages: cambridgeinternational.org for Cambridge syllabuses and timetables, qualifications.pearson.com for Pearson International GCSE material. A tutor who works from the published criteria and sends you the link is doing it properly.

process.title: Ask for the permit and the specification in the same message
process.description: Two questions settle most of this page. Does the tutor hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit, and which specification codes and tiers have they taught? The first is permission, the second is competence, and a tutor who answers both precisely has saved you a week of profile reading.

process.title: A free trial lesson, with no card details taken
process.description: One session before any payment. Use it as a test rather than an introduction: hand the tutor a piece of your child's returned work and ask where the marks went. The specificity of that answer in the first few minutes tells you more about competence than any certificate.

process.title: A diagnostic from timed written work
process.description: The first working session uses a past-paper section under timed conditions, and the output is a named list of causes, an hour estimate and a review date. Expect the causes to be narrow and checkable, in the language of the table above rather than in general terms.

process.title: Weekly sessions with marked work between them
process.description: A timed set at consistent difficulty, marked against the published criteria before each session, plus a short note on what changed. The tutor should be working from the specification code on your child's statement of entry and the school's own assessment calendar.

process.title: Verify anything that matters to you yourself
process.description: Permits, inspection ratings and equivalency rules are all published by the body responsible. KHDA holds each Dubai school's rating and fee, MoHRE administers the tuition permit, and the Ministry of Education publishes equivalency requirements. Nothing on this page is a substitute for those sources.

whyPoints.title: The permit position stated with its source
whyPoints.description: Private tuition in the UAE sits under the MoHRE permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. This page names the resolution, the eligible categories and the official application route, and quotes no fine figure, because none is published.

whyPoints.title: No claimed regulator or board approval
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. It does not hold or claim approval from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge International or Pearson, holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, and operates no UAE office. Where a credential matters, this page says how to check it.

whyPoints.title: Credentials mapped to what they actually evidence
whyPoints.description: A permit evidences permission. A degree evidences subject knowledge. A teaching qualification evidences training. Specification experience evidences familiarity with the papers your child will sit. Conflating them is how families pay for the wrong thing, so the page separates them.

whyPoints.title: The equivalency rule published correctly
whyPoints.description: Five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels. At least one competing page publishes a six-subject requirement. No IB points figure is quoted here, because the source used does not publish one.

whyPoints.title: Stated limits on assessed work
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, reviews and gives feedback on work the student produced. No text is supplied for a submission and no piece is edited to completion. Board materials are referenced and linked rather than redistributed, because both boundaries protect the student rather than the provider.

whyPoints.title: Mandatory UAE subjects treated as real courses
whyPoints.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies run alongside the licensed curriculum in Dubai private schools under KHDA requirements, with specific rules on class organisation and language of instruction. Almost no competing page mentions them, and they occupy real timetable hours.

faqs.question: Is there such a thing as a certified IGCSE tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Not as a single qualification. No examination board or UAE regulator issues an IGCSE tutoring certificate, so any provider implying one exists is describing something that does not. What exists is a legal permission and several separate credentials. The permission is the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The credentials are a teaching qualification, a subject degree, school employment history, and a describable track record on the specification your child is entered for. Ask which of those a tutor holds, and treat the last as the one that most affects the teaching.

faqs.question: Do private tutors working with Dubai families need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tuition in the UAE is covered by the private tutor work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Applications go through MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, via the smart app, website or e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time. Anyone telling you the permit carries a fee is mistaken, and anyone quoting a fine amount is repeating an unverified figure.

faqs.question: Can my child's own schoolteacher tutor them privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: That is the arrangement to avoid. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the holder's own school. This is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document, so verify it against current ADEK material if it affects you directly. The principle holds in any emirate: a teacher who assesses your child's school work should not also be paid privately to prepare it.

faqs.question: What qualifications should I actually ask an IGCSE tutor for?
faqs.answer: Four things, in this order. Whether they hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit, because that is the legal position. Which specification codes and tiers they have taught, and how many cohorts, because that is the competence closest to what you need. What teaching qualification they hold and from where. And whether they can read one of your child's returned scripts and name where the marks went, which is a test rather than a credential and is available to you free in a trial lesson. The fourth usually tells you more than the first three combined.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need to be approved by KHDA to teach IGCSE in Dubai?
faqs.answer: KHDA's permits concern institutions rather than individual private tutors. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. An individual providing private lessons needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit instead. IB Gram holds no KHDA permit and does not describe itself as approved by KHDA, because it is not a training institute with premises in the emirate. Any provider using that phrase should be asked which permit it holds and for what.

faqs.question: Which five subjects count towards UAE equivalency for an IGCSE student?
faqs.answer: The published British-track rule requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. That sits alongside one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One page ranking for UAE tutoring queries states six subjects are required, which does not match the published rule. Verify the current requirement on the Ministry of Education's own pages, because IB Gram does not perform or guarantee equivalency.

faqs.question: Does a teaching certificate mean a tutor knows my child's exam papers?
faqs.answer: No, and conflating the two is the most expensive mistake on this page. A PGCE or equivalent evidences training in instruction and assessment generally. It does not evidence familiarity with Cambridge 0620 Paper 4 or Pearson 4PH1 Paper 2, and the paper-level knowledge is what moves marks in Year 11. A qualified teacher whose experience is on a different board will be learning your child's specification while teaching it. Ask which codes, which tier and how many cohorts, then ask what candidates at your child's grade most reliably lose marks on in that paper.

faqs.question: What does Core tier do to the grade on an IGCSE certificate?
faqs.answer: On Cambridge syllabuses the Core paper set caps the available grade at C, so the tier your child is entered for sets a ceiling on what the certificate can show regardless of performance. Because Dubai entries are submitted months before the papers, that ceiling is often fixed before parents realise it exists. If your child needs a subject at A Level or at Higher Level in the Diploma, the tier conversation belongs in the autumn term of Year 10, with evidence. A diagnostic session can establish whether the Extended content is reachable and roughly what it would cost in hours.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education compulsory in a Dubai IGCSE school?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements that the authority stated must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes for both groups strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with at least 25 minutes advised for any mandatory subject lesson.

faqs.question: Where do Extended Mathematics candidates in Dubai most reliably lose marks?
faqs.answer: On working they never wrote down. Extended papers award method marks for a visible route to an answer, and candidates who compute mentally lose marks on questions that were substantially correct. Beyond that habit, the consistent topic losses are algebraic fraction manipulation, transformations, and multi-step problems where a correct first step is followed by an unexplained jump. None of this is about ability. A session fixes the habit first, because writing one line of method before any answer recovers marks across every paper, and then addresses the topics in order of how many marks each is costing.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE Physics Paper 6 assess that the theory papers do not?
faqs.answer: Practical skills, and it is where otherwise strong candidates leak marks. The losses are patterned: axes unlabelled or scaled awkwardly, significant figures inconsistent between a table and a conclusion, a control mentioned rather than named, and descriptions of method that omit the measurement being taken. These are not knowledge failures, which is why revising the theory does not touch them. A session fixes them with a short checklist applied to past practical questions until it becomes automatic, and it is the component where a tutor who has marked those answers is worth most.

faqs.question: Can a certified tutor help with IGCSE coursework components?
faqs.answer: They can teach the skills, explain the criteria and give feedback on what the student has written. They cannot supply text for a submission or edit a piece to completion on the student's behalf, and no qualification changes that. The consequence of crossing the line is a malpractice matter that falls on the child rather than on the tutor. One operation researched for these pages sells completed Internal Assessments outright, which is exactly the practice this boundary exists to exclude. Ask any prospective tutor the question directly and listen for a clear answer rather than a comfortable one.

faqs.question: Will a certified tutor come to our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Tuition for families in the UAE is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, and in-home visiting is offered only in India. The in-home market in Dubai does exist, at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel inside the fee. What online delivery changes is which credentials and which specification experience are actually available to you: the pool becomes everyone who teaches your child's specification at a workable hour in Gulf Standard Time, rather than everyone willing to drive to your community.

faqs.question: How can I check a Dubai school's inspection rating for myself?
faqs.answer: Through KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai and publishes each school's rating and fee on its own profile. Ratings run on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. Two things are worth knowing when you read one. A school rated well overall can have a weak department, and the report usually says which. And the fee shown there is the authoritative figure: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year.

faqs.question: Does my child need tutoring to get Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider implying otherwise is applying false urgency to a regulatory process. Equivalency is a Ministry assessment of qualifications already obtained, and it is the Ministry's process rather than a tutor's. What tuition can honestly do is help a child reach the grades that the rule counts: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education. IB Gram does not perform, expedite or guarantee equivalency, and recommends checking the current requirement directly with the Ministry or the emirate attestation authority.

dubai/certified-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Two questions, asked in the right order
dubai/certified-igcse-tutor.closingBody: Ask whether the tutor holds a MoHRE private tuition work permit, and ask which specification codes and tiers they have taught and for how many cohorts. The first is the legal floor and the second is the thing that moves marks. Then use the free trial lesson as a test: hand them one of your child's returned scripts and ask where the marks went. A specific answer about method marks, command terms or a practical checklist tells you what no certificate can. Everything on this page that matters to you is published by KHDA, MoHRE or the Ministry of Education, and worth checking there.

dubai/city-walk.tutorsIntro: Tutors matched for City Walk households are chosen for catch-up rather than enrichment: a Year 10 arrival who has missed two terms of a Cambridge specification, a student moving from an American high school into the Diploma, or a Year 11 student whose option block was decided before they landed.

intro.heading: City Walk has no school, which tells you who lives here
paragraphs: City Walk is a low-rise district on Al Wasl Road between Jumeirah 1 and Al Safa, a grid of apartment buildings over retail streets with Coca-Cola Arena on one edge and Al Safa Park a short drive away. It was built as a walkable urban quarter rather than as a family suburb, and the housing stock shows it: a high proportion of one- and two-bedroom apartments, serviced and corporate leases alongside family tenancies, and a steady churn of arrivals and departures. The newer buildings and the central park have brought more families in, but there is still no school inside the development.

That single fact explains most of the tutoring demand from this postcode. Children here are driven or bussed out, usually to Al Safa, Jumeirah or Al Barsha, and the choice of school was frequently made in a hurry from abroad on the basis of which campus had a seat free in the right year group. A seat free in March in Year 10 is a different proposition from a place secured in the previous September, and nobody explains the difference at the point of acceptance.

The specific, practical problem of a mid-year arrival is that a school teaches a syllabus in an order, and it does not go back. A Year 10 student joining in January walks into a Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel specification one and a half terms in. The class has done the topics it has done. The teacher will support an individual as far as a full timetable allows, which is usually a conversation, a set of past topic sheets and an invitation to catch up. The content is not re-taught, and nobody is checking whether the catching up happened until a mock exam makes the answer visible.

There is a second version of this problem that is less obvious and more expensive. A student moving from an American high school, a CBSE school or a British Year 11 into a new programme does not arrive behind so much as sideways. Their prior learning does not map cleanly. An American Algebra 2 student has met functions but perhaps not formal proof; a CBSE Class 10 student has met far more trigonometry than a Cambridge 0580 student but less statistics; a British Year 11 student entering DP1 has the content but not the habit of criterion-based work. Each of those gaps is specific, nameable and closable in a known number of hours, which is the whole point of mapping them.

What follows is that map. Where City Walk children actually go to school and by which route, what has usually been taught by each common mid-year entry point, how each prior system lines up against IGCSE and the Diploma, which IGCSE content cannot be inferred and must be taught, how a short tenancy interacts with a two-year Diploma, what the Jumeirah and Al Wasl market charges in AED, and what the Ministry of Education's equivalency rules require from a family that may not stay in the UAE.

dubai/city-walk.programmesIntro: City Walk children are spread across more systems than a single-school community would be, because the school was chosen on availability. These are the four that matter for arrivals and transfers.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four published criteria marked out of eight and converted to a grade from 1 to 7. For an arriving student the difficulty is rarely content. It is that the grade depends on strands such as investigating patterns or communicating, which are practised habits rather than knowledge, and a student arriving from a content-and-test system has never been asked to demonstrate them.
programmes.countryNote: Several campuses within reach of City Walk run the Middle Years Programme, including the IB continuum schools in Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim. A student joining MYP 4 or MYP 5 from an examination-based system usually needs the criteria explained explicitly in the first fortnight, not in the term the first summative task is returned.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, usually three Higher and three Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Forty-two points from the subjects and up to three from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix. Internal assessment carries 20% in the sciences and both mathematics courses. Entering DP1 late is survivable; entering DP2 late is close to impossible because the internal assessments and the Extended Essay are already in train.
programmes.countryNote: For a City Walk family on a two or three year posting, the Diploma's two-year structure is the single biggest planning consideration. Transferring a Diploma student between schools mid-programme means matching six subjects at matching levels, and a school that cannot offer the same Higher Level combination forces a subject change that costs a year of content.

programmes.name: IGCSE at Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel
programmes.description: Cambridge splits most subjects into Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C and Extended running A* to E. Pearson Edexcel tiers mathematics as Foundation and Higher with a grade 9 ceiling, and runs some subjects on a modular basis where units can be sat in different series. Those structural differences decide what a mid-year arrival has missed and whether any of it can be sat later.
programmes.countryNote: Ask the admissions office two questions at the point of accepting a seat: which board the subject is entered with, and which topics the class has already completed. The second question is the one nobody asks and the one that determines how many hours of catch-up the next three months contain.

programmes.name: A Level, as the post-16 alternative
programmes.description: Three or four linear subjects with no core, assessed almost entirely through terminal written papers. For a transferring family the advantage is portability within the British system and the smaller number of components to match. The disadvantage is depth: a student arriving into the second year of a linear A Level has missed content that is examined in full at the end and never revisited in class.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools reachable from City Walk offer A Level alongside or instead of the Diploma. For a family unsure of how long they will stay, the question worth asking is which route the next likely destination recognises most easily, because that decision is easier to make at sixteen than to unwind at seventeen.

dubai/city-walk.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects that cause the most difficulty for arriving students, with the specific gap each one tends to contain rather than a general description of the course.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 and 0607)
subjects.description: Cambridge 0580 and the International Mathematics syllabus 0607 are different courses with different papers, and 0607 includes an investigation component that 0580 does not. An arriving student entered for the wrong one in their head will practise the wrong papers for a term. Confirm the code, not the subject name.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Pearson Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.description: Two papers, calculator permitted in both, tiered Foundation and Higher with a grade 9 ceiling on Higher. Students arriving from systems with a non-calculator tradition often over-rely on written methods and lose time. The content order differs from Cambridge, so a mid-year transfer between the two boards creates gaps in both directions.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Cambridge 0625 assesses practical skills through either a practical test or a written alternative paper, and which one a school enters for changes how the laboratory work matters. At Diploma level the gap for arrivals is uncertainty handling and graph interpretation for gradient meaning, neither of which most prior systems assess.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The quantitative core, moles, concentration and yield, is where arriving students most often sit behind, because the amount of calculation expected varies widely between systems. At Diploma level the scientific investigation carries 20% at both levels and is marked on design, analysis, conclusion and evaluation, and arrivals rarely have a comparable prior task.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-dense and decided by command terms. Students who come from a system that rewards complete answers tend to over-write short questions and run out of time. The statistical treatment expected in a Diploma investigation is a specific and teachable gap for anyone arriving from a double award science background.

subjects.name: English as a first or second language
subjects.description: Schools sometimes place an arriving bilingual student in the wrong route. First Language English and English as a Second Language are different specifications with different papers, and some sixth forms set First Language as the entry requirement for literature courses. This decision is far easier to get right in Year 9 or at the point of entry than in Year 11.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Usually new subjects for an arriving student, which is an advantage: there is no prior learning to unpick. The marks are decided by diagram accuracy, correct axis labelling and giving a justified recommendation where the question asks for one rather than a list of advantages and disadvantages.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Every student in a Dubai private school takes Arabic regardless of curriculum, and an arriving non-Arabic speaker joins a class that has been running for years. The realistic aim in the first year is script fluency and core vocabulary rather than parity with the class, and support has to work from the school's own material.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Cambridge 0478 separates theory from practical problem-solving, and the programming element is where students arriving from block-based environments struggle hardest. At Diploma level the internal assessment is a developed solution whose documentation carries much of the mark, so planning on paper before coding is the habit worth installing early.

subjects.name: History and Geography
subjects.description: Both depend on named, specific evidence rather than general narrative, and arrivals frequently bring strong general knowledge with no case-study discipline. IGCSE geography answers lose marks without a named place and a named figure; Diploma history rests on comparative argument and a historical investigation with a strict word limit.

dubai/city-walk.regionsIntro: City Walk sits in the middle of the Jumeirah and Al Wasl school corridor, and the practical distinction between its neighbours is journey time at half past three in the afternoon.

regions.name: Al Safa 1 and Al Safa 2
regions.note: Immediately inland across Al Wasl Road, and where a large share of City Walk children are schooled. Journeys are short in distance and unpredictable in time, because the Al Wasl and Al Safa junctions queue heavily at both ends of the school day.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1, 2 and 3
regions.note: The coastal strip running north-west, with several primary and all-through British and IB campuses. Low-rise and villa stock, long-settled families, and school waiting lists that explain why so many City Walk arrivals end up at a campus further out.

regions.name: Al Wasl
regions.note: The corridor City Walk effectively belongs to, running from Jumeirah towards Al Safa Park. Sports clubs, clinics and after-school activity providers concentrate here, which is the real competitor for a weekday evening study slot.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Further along the coast, home to several large all-through campuses including IB continuum provision. The run from City Walk is quick on Al Wasl Road outside peak and considerably slower on Jumeirah Beach Road at the wrong hour.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai and Business Bay
regions.note: A short hop inland, with apartment-living families on similarly short tenancies and the same mid-year arrival pattern. Several City Walk households have an older child at a campus reached through this side of the city.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Quoz
regions.note: Where several of the larger campuses and most of the city's tuition centres sit. The eastbound run along Sheikh Zayed Road at five in the afternoon is the reason in-home evening arrangements in this corridor rarely start on time.

regions.name: La Mer and Pearl Jumeira
regions.note: Coastal developments near City Walk with the same short-lease profile and no schools of their own. Families here and in City Walk frequently share school routes, buses and the same question about how long they will be in Dubai.

schoolClusters.city: Al Safa and Al Wasl campuses
schoolClusters.note: The closest cluster to City Walk, reached in minutes outside peak hours and considerably longer at the school gates. A mixture of British-curriculum primaries and all-through schools, which is where most mid-year Year 7 to Year 10 placements from this postcode land.

sections.heading: Where City Walk children actually go to school
paragraphs: Because the development contains no school, every family here has made a decision about which direction to travel in, and the answers cluster rather than scatter. The nearest cluster is Al Safa and Al Wasl, a few minutes away outside peak hours, which absorbs a large share of primary and lower-secondary placements. The next ring is Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim along the coast, where several all-through campuses and the area's IB continuum provision sit. The third is Al Barsha and Al Quoz inland, which is where families end up when the first two rings are full in the year group they need.

Journey time matters here more than distance, and not in the way a map suggests. Al Wasl Road is quick at ten in the morning and slow at both ends of the school day. The junctions around Al Safa queue, and the Sheikh Zayed Road crossings towards Al Barsha are unreliable enough that families with children at those campuses treat any weekday arrangement before five in the afternoon as optimistic. That is a scheduling fact rather than a complaint, and it is why the first question about an evening session should be when the child is actually through the door.
