sections.heading: Arriving mid-year: what the school will not re-teach
paragraphs: A school teaches a specification in an order and moves forward. That is the correct way to run a class of thirty and it is the whole of the arriving student's problem. A child joining in January has not been taught the first half of the year, and the class will not revisit it, because doing so would penalise everybody else. What the student will be offered is a conversation, access to past topic materials, and the goodwill of a teacher with a full timetable. That is not neglect. It is simply not sufficient on its own.

The gap is also invisible for a while, which is the dangerous part. An arriving student does well enough on current topics, because those are being taught now, and the missing earlier material does not surface until a cumulative assessment or a mock. By then it is often two or three months of content, there is less time left, and the student has acquired the belief that they are weak at the subject rather than that they missed six weeks of it. Separating those two explanations early is one of the most useful things a tutor does for a City Walk family.

sections.heading: Mapping a prior system onto IGCSE or the Diploma
paragraphs: Families moving into Dubai from another system are usually told their child will adapt, which is true and unhelpful. Adaptation has content. A student arriving from an American high school has typically met functions, probability and a good deal of statistics, and may not have met formal proof or the algebraic manipulation speed a Cambridge Extended paper assumes. A student from a CBSE background often arrives with stronger trigonometry and weaker data handling than their new classmates, and with a writing style built for complete answers rather than for command terms with mark allocations attached.

The reverse direction has its own pattern. A British Year 11 student entering DP1 has the content and lacks the habit: nothing in GCSE or IGCSE requires a criterion-based piece of independent work, so the exploration and the Extended Essay are genuinely new activities rather than harder versions of familiar ones. A Middle Years student moving into a British sixth form has the independent habits and may lack specific examined content, particularly in mathematics where the Diploma and A Level diverge early.

None of this is mysterious once it is written down, and writing it down is the job. The table below maps the five transitions we see most often from this part of Dubai, with the gap that genuinely matters in each and roughly how long it takes to close with focused one-to-one work. The point of the table is to turn a vague worry into a finite list, because a finite list can be finished and a vague worry cannot.

sections.heading: The option block you inherit, and the content you cannot infer
paragraphs: A mid-year arrival does not choose their options; they inherit them. The school fits the new student into the blocks that have space, which may mean a subject nobody in the family would have selected and the absence of one that mattered. This is worth raising early rather than accepting silently, because a block that looks fixed in February is sometimes movable in April, and because the alternative is two years of a subject chosen by a timetable. Ask what the constraint actually is, and whether it is a room, a teacher or a rule.

There is also content in these syllabuses that a bright student cannot work out from first principles, and this is where arriving families most often misjudge what tutoring is needed for. Cambridge 0580 and the International Mathematics syllabus 0607 are different courses, and 0607 includes an investigation component that 0580 does not have at all. Cambridge physics 0625 assesses practical skills either through a practical test or through a written alternative paper, and which route the school has entered changes what laboratory experience matters. Pearson Edexcel runs some subjects modularly, where units can be sat in different series, which occasionally gives an arriving student an option a linear course would not.

The practical instruction is narrow and it matters: get the syllabus code from the school in writing, together with the tier where one exists and the practical arrangement where one applies. Cambridge 0580 Extended, Cambridge 0607, Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Higher and Pearson Edexcel 4MB1 are all called IGCSE Maths in conversation, and a tutor working from the wrong one does accurate teaching against a specification the student will never sit. That mistake costs more in a catch-up situation than in any other, because there is no slack to absorb it.

Get the code, the tier and the practical arrangement in writing

sections.heading: A short tenancy against a two-year Diploma
paragraphs: City Walk leases are frequently shorter than the programmes its teenagers are enrolled in, and that mismatch is a real planning problem rather than a theoretical one. The Diploma is a two-year structure in which six subjects, their levels, the Extended Essay subject and the internal assessment work are all locked in early. Moving a Diploma student between schools means finding a school that offers the same six subjects at the same levels, and a single mismatch in a Higher Level subject forces a change that can cost most of a year's content.

IGCSE is more forgiving but not free. Boards differ, entry deadlines sit months before the papers, and a student who moves between Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel part-way through Year 10 arrives with content gaps running in both directions. The modular structure some Pearson Edexcel subjects use occasionally helps here, because units already sat can count, but that depends entirely on what was entered and when. A family who may move should ask about board and entry structure before accepting a place rather than after.

The table below sets out the scenarios we see from this postcode and what reduces the damage in each. Two general rules emerge from it. First, decisions that are cheap to make early become expensive to make late, which argues for asking awkward questions at the point of admission. Second, an online tutoring arrangement survives a move in a way a local one does not: the same tutor, the same slot and the same plan continue from a new city, which for a transient household is a practical advantage rather than a marketing line.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs in the Jumeirah and Al Wasl corridor
paragraphs: Catch-up tutoring is bought in blocks rather than open-endedly, so the useful number for a City Walk family is not only the hourly rate but what a block costs in total. The table below gives published Dubai market bands per hour, the monthly figure at one session a week, and who published each number. These are market rates surveyed in October 2026 from published platform and agency rate pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table. They are not an IB Gram price list and no figure here is a quote.

For a catch-up block the arithmetic is straightforward and worth doing before committing. A Year 10 arrival with sixteen to twenty-four hours of gap in one examined subject, at the qualified subject tutor band, is a defined and finite cost; the same gap left to surface in a Year 11 mock becomes two subjects and a longer programme. Published package offers in this market include around AED 799 per month online for eight sessions, and published monthly estimates for a single weekly hour run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work.

Three questions to ask any provider, including us, before paying anything. Is the figure per hour or per session, and how long is a session. Does it include VAT, and will that be stated on the invoice. What happens to a prepaid balance if you stop after one lesson or leave the country. For context on the wider household budget, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under an economic incentives package the emirate valued at AED 1.5 billion, which makes the tutoring line the variable one this year.

sections.heading: Equivalency for a family that may not stay
paragraphs: A mobile family has one extra piece of paperwork to understand, and almost no competing page in this market mentions it. UAE Ministry of Education equivalency is the process by which a foreign secondary qualification is recognised for use here, and it matters if a child might apply to a UAE university, or if the family stays longer than the current posting. It is a Ministry process. No tutoring provider performs it, guarantees it or speeds it up, and anyone suggesting otherwise should be treated with scepticism.

The British-track requirements, as reported in July 2026, are specific. A student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects, which is a detail at least one ranking competitor gets wrong by stating that six subjects are required. For the American track, English proficiency is shown by a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Math.

For the IB Diploma this page deliberately publishes no points threshold, because the figures circulating online could not be verified against the Ministry's own pages during research for this project. Check moe.gov.ae or the relevant attestation authority directly. The practical advice for a City Walk family is unglamorous: keep every statement of results, keep certificates rather than photographs of them, and begin the attestation conversation in the term before leaving rather than from the next country.

sections.heading: Why these searches say home tutor, and what is actually delivered
paragraphs: Parents who have just moved countries search for a home tutor because it is the arrangement they know. In most of the world a tutor arrives, sits down and works through the material, and after a relocation there is real comfort in a known quantity. In a City Walk apartment there is also a practical argument: the flat is small, the family may not yet have a car, and having somebody come to the building removes a journey from a week that already contains too many.

The honest market picture is this. Published in-home rates in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with the tutor's travel inside that figure, against AED 200 to 450 for an online subject specialist. The people available to visit are those willing to drive into the Al Wasl corridor in the evening, which skews towards generalists rather than specialists in a particular board and level. And a catch-up block is the case where specialisation matters most, because the work is closing a named list of topics from a specific specification rather than general support with homework.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home visits are a service we provide only in India, and nobody will be sent to a City Walk address. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, with screen sharing for past papers and a document camera for written working. For a family who may move again, that has a side benefit that matters more than it sounds: the arrangement is portable. The same tutor and slot continue from the next city, which is not true of anybody who had to drive to the building.

sections.heading: Starting from City Walk, with the limits and the rules stated
paragraphs: The first message should contain facts rather than worries: the school, the year group, the board and syllabus code, the term the child joined, and the topic list from the school if you have been able to get it. If you have a transcript or report from the previous system, send it, because the gap map is built from that document more than from anything a first session can reveal. We then name the tutor, where they are based and what they have taught at that level, before any payment, and a trial session follows at a time set around the actual arrival home.

Two sets of limits are worth stating in advance. Coverage is uneven in narrow Higher Level subjects, in less common languages and in uncommon Pearson Edexcel options, and the honest answer is one of three things: a different hour where the right specialist is free, an adjacent board or level where the overlap is real and the gap can be named, or a plain statement that we cannot cover it. Timing is the other limit. A Year 11 arrival one term before a series, with most of a specification missing, is a triage exercise and we will describe it as one rather than sell a programme that cannot work.

On assessed work the rule does not bend. An internal assessment, an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay must be the student's own work, authenticated by a school supervisor and declared by the school; a malpractice finding falls on the student. A tutor teaches the criteria, reads a draft the student produced and gives written feedback on it, and asks the questions that expose a method the student cannot yet explain. Nobody here authors any part of a submission, and we do not hand over board syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes, because those belong to the boards and the official source is the right place to get them.

process.title: Send the school, the term of entry and the board
process.description: The three facts that determine everything else. A Year 10 student who joined in January on a Cambridge entry has a different problem from one who joined in September on a Pearson Edexcel entry, even in the same subject at the same school. Add the syllabus code from the entry confirmation if you have it.

process.title: Get the topic list from the school in writing
process.description: Ask the head of year or the subject teacher which topics the class has already completed. This is a reasonable request that almost nobody makes, and it converts a vague fear of being behind into a finite list. The list becomes the plan, and the block ends when the list is closed.

process.title: We name the tutor before anything is paid
process.description: You are told who would teach, where they are based, which board and level they cover and what they have taught at it. If nobody suitable is free at the hour your child is actually home, you hear that rather than being matched to a generalist working against the wrong specification.

process.title: A written gap map after the first session
process.description: For a transition case the first session is diagnostic and produces a written list: what transfers from the previous system, what is missing, what has to be unlearned, and the order it will be worked in. For a catch-up block it produces a sequence against the school's topic list with an estimated number of hours.

process.title: Close the block and stop
process.description: A catch-up block has an end. When the topic list is closed, the sensible question is whether weekly teaching is still needed or whether the student is now simply in the class like everybody else. We will say which we think it is. Rolling arrangements that nobody reviews are how tutoring becomes an unexamined line in a household budget.

whyPoints.title: Built around the arrival problem
whyPoints.description: Most tutoring in this market is sold as ongoing support. A City Walk family usually needs something finite: a named list of topics the class covered before the child landed, closed in a known number of hours. That is a different product, it has an end point, and it should be priced and planned as a block.

whyPoints.title: Specification accuracy over proximity
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0580, Cambridge 0607, Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 and Pearson Edexcel 4MB1 are all called IGCSE Maths in conversation. A catch-up block has no slack to absorb a tutor working from the wrong papers, which is why we ask for the code, the tier and the practical arrangement before teaching starts.

whyPoints.title: Portable across a move
whyPoints.description: Tenancies here are often shorter than the programmes the children are enrolled in. Because lessons are delivered online over live video, the same tutor, the same slot and the same plan continue from a new city. An arrangement that depended on somebody driving to the building ends at the airport.

whyPoints.title: Equivalency and paperwork explained, not performed
whyPoints.description: The Ministry of Education's equivalency requirements for the British and American tracks are set out on this page with the detail one ranking competitor gets wrong. We describe the process and point to the official channel. No tutoring provider performs equivalency or attestation, and none should imply that tutoring is required for it.

whyPoints.title: Stated limits on coverage and on timing
whyPoints.description: Some subjects are thinly covered and some arrivals are too late in the course for the work to succeed. You get the real position first, including a plain no, rather than a programme that looks like a solution. A Year 11 arrival one term from a series will be described as triage, because that is what it is.

faqs.question: Which school should we choose if we live in City Walk?
faqs.answer: There is no school inside the development, so every family here chooses a direction. The nearest cluster is Al Safa and Al Wasl, which absorbs most primary and lower-secondary placements and is a few minutes away outside peak hours. The next ring is Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim along the coast, including the area's IB continuum provision. Al Barsha and Al Quoz inland is where families land when the closer schools are full in the required year group. Journey time at half past three, not distance on a map, is the figure that should decide it.

faqs.question: My child joined Year 10 in January. How far behind are they really?
faqs.answer: Usually a third to a half of the IGCSE specification in each examined subject, which is roughly sixteen to twenty-four hours of focused one-to-one work per subject. The important point is that it will not feel like that for months: current topics are being taught now, so performance looks acceptable until a cumulative assessment or a mock exposes the earlier material. Ask the school in writing which topics the class has already completed. That list turns an open-ended worry into a finite piece of work with an end point.

faqs.question: Will the school re-teach what my child missed before they arrived?
faqs.answer: No, and it should not be expected to. A class of thirty moves forward through a specification in order, and going back would penalise everybody else. What a school reasonably offers is a conversation, access to past topic materials and the goodwill of a teacher with a full timetable. That is genuine support and it is not sufficient on its own for two terms of missed content. The gap closes through one-to-one work against the school's own topic list, which is exactly the job a catch-up block is for.

faqs.question: We are moving from an American high school into the IB Diploma. What transfers?
faqs.answer: More than families expect on content and less than they expect on habits. Functions, probability and statistics usually transfer well, as do coursework culture and research skills. The real gaps are command terms and criterion-based marking: a Diploma paper awards marks calibrated to whether it asked you to state, explain, discuss or evaluate, and an American transcript rarely reflects practice at that. Formal proof and non-calculator algebraic speed are the other common gaps. Six to ten weeks of focused work before the first internal assessment usually closes the set.

faqs.question: How does CBSE compare with IGCSE for a child arriving mid-year?
faqs.answer: A CBSE student typically arrives with stronger trigonometry, mechanics and calculation fluency than their new classmates and weaker data handling and extended written answers. The writing style is the bigger adjustment: CBSE rewards complete answers, while IGCSE allocates marks to command terms, so a full paragraph on a two-mark state question earns nothing and costs time elsewhere. Eight to twelve weeks of one-to-one work on data handling, structured written responses and timed paper technique is the usual requirement, and the mathematics content gap is often smaller than the family fears.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge 0580 and 0607 maths?
faqs.answer: They are different courses rather than variants of one. Cambridge 0580 is the mainstream International Mathematics route, split into Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C. Cambridge 0607 is International Mathematics with a different content emphasis and an investigation component that 0580 does not contain at all. A student entered for one and practising past papers from the other is doing accurate work against a specification they will never sit, which matters most in a catch-up situation where there is no slack. Get the code in writing from the school.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our apartment in City Walk?
faqs.answer: Not through us. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs only in India. Tuition for City Walk families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, with screen sharing for past papers and a document camera for written working. Published Dubai market rates for an in-home visit run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with the tutor's travel inside the fee, against AED 200 to 450 for an online specialist. For catch-up work the specialist match matters more than physical presence, because the task is a named topic list from a specific specification.

faqs.question: How much does a catch-up block cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Work from the hours rather than the hourly rate. Published Dubai market bands, surveyed October 2026, put a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to 300 an hour and an IB or IGCSE specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more; generalists are quoted from AED 45 to 150 and in-home visits at AED 180 to 500 with travel included. A Year 10 arrival needing sixteen to twenty-four hours in one subject is therefore a finite, calculable cost. Those figures come from published platform and agency rate pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table.

faqs.question: Our posting may end during the Diploma. What should we decide now?
faqs.answer: Choose a subject combination at DP1 selection that other schools commonly offer, because moving a Diploma student means matching six subjects at matching levels and a single mismatch in a Higher Level subject can cost most of a year's content. Keep the Extended Essay in a widely taught subject for the same reason. And because lessons here are delivered online, a tutoring arrangement continues from the next city with the same tutor and slot, which removes one variable from a move that will already contain plenty.

faqs.question: What does my child need for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track, as reported in July 2026, five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no lower than grade E or grade 3, plus either one accredited Advanced Level subject at E or better or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five, and one ranking competitor incorrectly states six subjects are needed. For the American track, English proficiency is shown by IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT 450 in reading and writing, with SAT Math at 450 or above. Verify current requirements on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: Can we change the option block our child was placed into?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking what the constraint actually is. A mid-year arrival is fitted into the blocks that have space, which can mean a subject nobody would have chosen and the absence of one that mattered. Ask whether the obstacle is a room, a teacher or a rule, because the first two sometimes change at the start of a new term and the third does not. Raise it in the first weeks rather than in the following year, when an inherited choice has become two years of a subject selected by a timetable.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring a problem if our apartment is small and busy?
faqs.answer: It is manageable with three cheap decisions made once. Over-ear headphones with a boom microphone so the student can be heard without competing with the room. A wired connection or the 5 GHz band rather than whatever the laptop joins by default. A second phone or tablet propped as a document camera so the tutor sees the working rather than the face, which changes mathematics and physics sessions more than any other single thing. A one-bedroom apartment with those three in place works better than a study with none of them.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Dubai need a permit, and can we check it?
faqs.answer: Yes to the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE operates under a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications are made through MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, via the smart app, website or e-services system. Tutoring without one brings fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published, so treat quoted amounts sceptically.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start if the exam series is one term away?
faqs.answer: It depends on what is missing rather than on the calendar alone. A student with most of a specification in place who is losing marks in execution can gain a great deal in a term, because timed papers marked against the published mark scheme move grades faster than anything else at that stage. A Year 11 arrival with most of a specification never taught is a triage exercise: choose the subjects where the return is highest, confirm the entries and tiers with the school immediately, and accept that not everything can be rescued. We will say which case you are in.

dubai/city-walk.closingHeading: Turn the worry into a list
dubai/city-walk.closingBody: The useful next step for a City Walk family is to get one document: the list of topics the class has already covered. Send that, with the school, the year group and the syllabus code, and you will get back the name of someone who teaches that exact specification and an estimate of how many hours the gap represents. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video, and they continue from wherever you are if the posting moves. If the honest answer is that the timing makes the job triage rather than catch-up, you will hear that first rather than after four paid sessions.

dubai/culture-village.tutorsIntro: These tutors cover the IB continuum, both IGCSE boards and the transition work a newly arrived student needs. Before matching anybody, tell us which system your child left and which year group the new school placed them in, because those two facts explain most of what a first report will say.

intro.heading: What actually happens when a child joins in February
paragraphs: Culture Village sits on the Dubai Creek between Al Jaddaf and the older districts, a waterfront development of apartments and towers with an unusually high share of households that arrived recently. Professional families relocating to Dubai take apartments here because the location works, the buildings are new and the commute into Downtown, DIFC and the healthcare district is short. A high proportion of the children in these buildings started their current school partway through a year.

A mid-year arrival is not a milder version of a September start. It is a different event with its own difficulties. The class has already covered half a syllabus the student has not seen, or has covered the same material in a different order and in different notation. Friendship groups are formed. The coursework cycle is partly complete. The school has placed the child in a year group based on age and on whatever documents arrived with them, and that placement is sometimes not quite right.

The first report is where this surfaces, and it almost always reads worse than the child's ability. A student who was strong in their previous system produces middling marks because they are being assessed on content taught in October, in a question style nobody has explained, under a reporting format the family has never seen. Parents reasonably conclude there is an academic problem. Usually there is a transition problem, and the two need different responses.

The second thing specific to this district is language. Many households here speak two or three languages, with English as the language of school and something else at home. Dubai private schools must also run Arabic for every student, in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab learners, because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ between the two. A newly arrived student can be enrolled in the wrong stream, and that takes a term to surface and a conversation with the school to correct.

Third, mobility. Families who moved once often move again, within Dubai or out of it, and that changes what matters now. Documents that are easy to obtain while a child is enrolled become difficult later. Subject choices that keep options open are worth more to a mobile family than to a settled one. A decision that looks harmless at fourteen can close a route at seventeen when the family is in a different country.

So this page covers the mid-year transfer properly: how year groups map across systems, what a transfer costs academically subject by subject, the Arabic stream question, coursework already started elsewhere, what a first term of support costs in dirhams, and which documents to collect while you can. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every Culture Village lesson is one-to-one over live video.

dubai/culture-village.programmesIntro: Three systems account for almost every enquiry from this district, and for each the relevant question is what a student joining partway through has missed and what simply looks different.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four lettered criteria using task-specific descriptors rather than percentages. There is no single syllabus to catch up on in the way a national curriculum has one, which helps a transferring student, but the criteria are a new language and the reporting looks nothing like a percentage.
programmes.countryNote: For a mid-year arrival this is the most forgiving programme academically and the most confusing administratively. The content gaps matter less than families fear; the criterion descriptors matter far more, and they can be taught explicitly in three or four sessions rather than absorbed over two reporting cycles.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Terminal papers at sixteen on one of two boards, with Cambridge examining in June and November series and tiering many subjects into Core and Extended, and Pearson Edexcel examining in May/June and November on a 9-1 scale. Entries are made months before the papers.
programmes.countryNote: This is the hardest point at which to arrive mid-year, because the entry decisions have often already been made. A student joining in Year 11 may find the tier, the subject set and the series already fixed. The first conversation with the school should be about entries, not about catching up.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internally assessed components run across both years on school deadlines set well before any board date, so a student arriving midway has coursework partly complete and partly not started.
programmes.countryNote: Arriving mid-Diploma is the most complicated transfer in school education. Subject availability, Higher and Standard Level combinations, coursework already begun at a previous school and CAS evidence all have to be reconciled. The school's IB coordinator holds the authoritative answers and should be the first appointment.

programmes.name: System-to-system bridging
programmes.description: A defined block of work rather than a subject. The content overlap between most systems is higher than parents expect in mathematics and the sciences and lower in English and the humanities, while the assessment conventions differ everywhere. The work is front-loaded on question style and marking conventions.
programmes.countryNote: In Culture Village this is the most requested piece of work, and we plan it as six to twelve weeks with an end point rather than as an open arrangement. A transfer block that runs for a year has stopped being a transfer block and become a dependency.

dubai/culture-village.subjectsIntro: Requests from newly arrived families concentrate on the subjects where assessment conventions differ most between systems, which is not the same list as the subjects students find hardest.

subjects.name: Mathematics 0580 and 4MA1
subjects.levels: Cambridge IGCSE Extended and Pearson Edexcel
subjects.description: Content transfers well across systems; marking does not. A student arriving from a tradition that rewards the correct final answer has to learn that method marks exist for reasoning written on the page, and that single change is usually worth a grade.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic Diploma route. Notation differs noticeably between education systems, and a transferring student can lose marks for writing something correct in an unfamiliar form before anybody explains the convention.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with heavy calculator use. Students from systems where calculators were restricted often arrive underpowered on the technology and lose time rather than marks, which is quick to fix with targeted practice.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The science where topic order varies most between systems, so a mid-year arrival may have met organic chemistry and not electrolysis, or the reverse. Mapping what has actually been covered is the first session's job rather than a guess.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Units, symbols and formula conventions differ between systems more than the physics does. The practical write-up style is usually entirely new, and it carries marks that have nothing to do with understanding the experiment.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The most vocabulary-dependent science and therefore the one most affected by a change of language of instruction. A student who knows a process in another language has to relearn the terms a mark scheme requires, which is work but is predictable work.

subjects.name: English A and English B
subjects.description: Two different courses frequently confused at enrolment, and a mid-year arrival is when the confusion happens. English B is a language-acquisition course; English A treats literature and language analytically. Placement in the wrong one costs a term and should be checked immediately.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language 0510
subjects.description: Accuracy, register and task fulfilment rather than literary analysis. For students arriving from a non-English-medium system this is often the correct placement, and it is one a family should discuss rather than accept by default.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Compulsory in all Dubai private schools, in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because expectations and the language of instruction differ. Newly arrived students are the group most often enrolled in the wrong stream, and the error takes a term to show.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies, History and Geography
subjects.description: The widest gap in any transfer. A student who learned history as narrative meets source evaluation and provenance questions worth a large share of the paper, and can be fluent while scoring poorly for two terms before anybody identifies the cause.

dubai/culture-village.regionsTitle: Culture Village and the creek-side districts
dubai/culture-village.regionsIntro: These are the neighbourhoods around Culture Village sharing its schools and its high proportion of recently arrived households.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf
regions.note: Immediately adjacent, with an IB school inside the district and the healthcare cluster nearby. Many households here work shifts, which changes which evening hours are usable.

regions.name: Dubai Creek Harbour
regions.note: Down the creek, newer apartment towers with a similar resident profile: recent arrivals, young families, short commutes. Schooling options are largely the same.

regions.name: Business Bay
regions.note: North-west along the water, dense apartment living with working parents commuting locally. Sessions are often placed later to overlap with a parent arriving home.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai

sections.heading: Which year group should a child actually be in?
paragraphs: This is the first question and it is frequently settled too quickly. Schools place by age against their own cut-off dates, and the systems do not line up neatly: a child who was in Grade 9 in an American school is usually, though not always, placed in Year 10 in a British-curriculum school, and a child whose birthday falls either side of a cut-off can reasonably go into either of two years.

Getting it wrong in either direction costs something. Placed a year ahead, a student is academically stretched and socially fine, and the pressure appears at the first set of real examinations. Placed a year behind, the student is comfortable, bored and a year older than their classmates by the time they reach the Diploma or A Levels, which matters more at seventeen than it does at twelve.

The table below is the mapping families most often need. It is indicative: every school applies its own cut-off and its own judgement, and the authoritative answer comes from the admissions team with the child's documents in front of them. Use it to ask a better question, not to argue with a decision.

The second part of this question is the examination year, which is what makes placement consequential rather than administrative. A student placed in Year 11 is in an examination year immediately, with entries possibly already submitted. A student placed in Year 10 has a full year before that. The difference between those two placements is not one year of schooling; it is whether the family is managing a transition or managing a transition and a public examination at the same time.

sections.heading: What a mid-year transfer costs, subject by subject
paragraphs: Families arriving mid-year usually ask how far behind their child is, and the honest answer is that behind is the wrong frame. The student is not behind; they are differently prepared. Some of what they know will not be examined here, some of what will be examined has not been taught to them, and a good deal of what they know is fine but has to be expressed differently.

The gap splits into three types and they close at different speeds. Content gaps, where a topic simply has not been taught, are the most visible and the easiest to close: the topic is finite and can be taught. Convention gaps, where the student knows the material and writes it in an unfamiliar form, close faster still once named. Skill gaps, where a question type has never been asked of the student, take the longest, because a new skill has to be built rather than transferred.

The practical sequence is therefore the reverse of what most families expect. Address the conventions first, in the first two or three weeks, because they produce immediate visible improvement and restore a student's confidence after a bad first report. Then the skill gaps, which take the longest and should start early. Content gaps last, because they are finite and can be scheduled.

The table gives honest ranges. They assume a student who was performing well in their previous system; where that was not the case the figures are longer and we will say so after the mapping block rather than before it.

sections.heading: A household speaking three languages, and the Arabic stream question
paragraphs: Many Culture Village households use English at school, another language at home and sometimes a third with grandparents or in the community. That is an asset and it also creates one specific administrative risk at enrolment, which newly arrived families are the most likely to hit.

Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. KHDA also requires Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

The risk for a newly arrived family is placement in the wrong stream. A child from an Arabic-speaking household with limited formal Arabic literacy, or a child with an Arab parent and schooling entirely in another language, can end up in a stream whose expectations do not match their actual starting point. The consequence is a poor report in a compulsory subject, and it takes a term to surface because the subject is rarely the one a family is watching.

The action is simple and should happen in the first fortnight: ask the school which stream your child has been enrolled in for each of these subjects, and what the expectations of that stream are. If the answer does not match the child's background, that is a conversation to have immediately rather than after a report. For these subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, so tutoring works strictly from the school's own material and cannot substitute a different scheme.

sections.heading: Coursework already started at another school
paragraphs: A student who arrives mid-Diploma, or partway through an IGCSE year with non-examined assessment underway, brings unfinished assessed work with them. This is the single most complicated part of a mid-year transfer and it is one where family and tutor both have less authority than the school.

The first appointment should be with the IB coordinator or the examinations officer, not with a tutor. Questions to ask: which components transfer, which must be restarted, what the new school's internal deadlines are, whether the subject and level combination can be timetabled, and whether entries for the series have already been made. The answers determine everything else, and a tutoring plan built before them is guesswork.

What a tutor can usefully do once those answers exist is specific. Explain the criteria of the new school's system, which may differ from the old one in language even where the content is similar. Review what the student has already produced and say which criterion it under-serves. Advise whether a research question that worked under one set of expectations still works under another. Help the student plan a realistic sequence against deadlines that are now compressed.

What a tutor cannot do, on any route and under any time pressure, is supply text, rewrite sections, generate data, choose the question or edit a draft into a finished state. A newly arrived student under deadline pressure with a parent still unpacking is precisely the target for the worst offers in this market, and one provider found in this search sells completed Internal Assessments outright. The malpractice consequence falls on the candidate who declares the work, which is the student.

sections.heading: What a first term of support costs, in dirhams
paragraphs: Relocation is expensive and tutoring arrives as one more line in a month that already contains deposits, furniture and school fees. The figures below are market rates attributed to the providers that published them, in dirhams, and they describe the market rather than an IB Gram price list. Most pages in this market publish no figure at all and two of those that do quote US dollars.

The market separates into four tiers once the published figures are lined up. Budget online help from university students or generalists is advertised from roughly AED 45 to AED 65 an hour, one platform quoting from about AED 33. Qualified subject tutors online sit between about AED 150 and AED 300, with one agency publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits run roughly AED 180 to AED 350 on one published index and AED 200 to AED 500 among independent tutors, travel inside the rate. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutors are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, one agency at AED 270, and one premium provider at AED 650.

For a transition the shape of the spend matters more than the rate. A mapping block of three or four sessions, followed by a finite transition block of six to twelve weeks, is a defined cost with an end. An open weekly arrangement started in a panic in February and still running the following December is a much larger total that nobody ever decided to spend. We quote the block, not the term.

Monthly figures circulating in this market include about AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. One published index estimates weekly one-hour tutoring at roughly AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not increase for 2026-27.

sections.heading: An in-home tutor for a Culture Village apartment against online
paragraphs: In-home tutoring is available in this market and a newly arrived family may well want it: an adult in the room, a visible routine, something solid in a month where everything else is unfamiliar. Those are real benefits and other providers arrange it.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video. For a transition specifically there is a strong argument for the online format that has nothing to do with cost. The work a transferring student needs is unusual: somebody who knows both the system the child left and the system they have joined well enough to name the differences in notation, marking convention and question type. That person is rare and is unlikely to live within a short drive of the creek.

There is also a practical apartment point. A waterfront tower apartment often has one usable desk and no spare room, and a visiting tutor needs a space for the hour. Two children taking consecutive online slots at the same desk costs the household one quiet block instead of two disrupted ones, which matters more than usual while a family is still settling in.

What online gives up: unprompted sight of the page, which we replace with a phone or tablet camera over the working and a tutor who insists on seeing method; and the physical presence of an adult, which for a younger child in an unfamiliar country can genuinely matter more than the precision of the subject match. We will say so where we think it does.

sections.heading: Documents to collect while your child is enrolled
paragraphs: Families who have moved once frequently move again, and the paperwork that is routine to obtain while a child is enrolled becomes awkward afterwards. This is the least interesting section on this page and the one newly arrived parents thank us for most often, because it costs nothing now and saves a great deal later.

Collect the transcript or report history from the previous school in the format it was issued, not a summary. Keep the syllabus codes for every examined subject, because a future school or a university will ask which specification was sat. Get the school's own statement of which programme and stream the child was enrolled in, including the mandatory UAE subjects. Keep examination certificates and statements of results as they arrive rather than trusting that a board will reissue them conveniently.

Attestation and equivalency are separate matters handled by the authorities, not by a school or a tutoring service, and they have their own requirements that change. The relevant published rule for the British track is that five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3 are required, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among those five, alongside one Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Verify the current position with the Ministry of Education or the emirate's attestation authority; we describe the process and never perform it.

The tutoring-relevant consequence of all this is about subject choice. A mobile family should be slower than a settled one to drop a subject, because a dropped subject can close a route in a country you have not moved to yet. Where a student is choosing options at thirteen or fourteen, that is worth an explicit conversation rather than a default.

sections.heading: The first fortnight: what to do before you book a tutor
paragraphs: A newly arrived family is usually advised to get a tutor immediately, and that is often premature. There are four things worth doing first, all free, and they frequently change what tutoring is needed or whether it is needed at all.

Ask the school's admissions or pastoral team which year group placement was made and on what basis, and whether it is reviewable. Ask the head of year or subject teachers what the class has covered so far this year in each examined subject, which is a short list and immediately shows where the content gaps are. Ask which Arabic and Islamic Education stream your child has been placed in. And ask for one marked piece of work in each of two or three subjects, which gives you evidence rather than impressions.

That package of four answers is what a good first tutoring session is built on. Without it, the first paid session becomes a discovery exercise at a specialist rate, and the family pays somebody to find out things a school would have provided for free in two emails.

Then, if a tutor is needed, start with a mapping block of three or four sessions rather than an open weekly arrangement. It produces a written map of what is actually missing, split into conventions, skills and content, with an honest estimate of the weeks each takes. From that map a transition block with a defined end date can be planned. And if the map concludes that the first report was a transition artefact rather than an academic problem, which it sometimes does, we will write that and the family can stop there.

process.description: Which year group, on what basis, and what each class has covered so far this year. Both answers come from the school and are free, and they decide whether the issue is content, conventions or simply the calendar the child arrived on.

process.description: Ask which stream your child was enrolled in and what it assumes. Newly arrived students are the group most often placed in a stream that does not match their background, and it takes a term to surface in a report nobody was watching.

faqs.question: My child joined a Dubai school in February and the first report was poor. Should I be worried?
faqs.answer: Usually less worried than the report suggests. A mid-year arrival is assessed on content taught in October, in a question style nobody has explained, under a reporting format the family has not seen before. A student who was strong elsewhere can produce middling marks for entirely structural reasons. The way to tell is evidence: ask for one marked script in two or three subjects and look at whether the losses are content, notation, mark-scheme vocabulary or an unfamiliar question type. Those four mean different things.

faqs.question: How do year groups map between American, British and IB schools?
faqs.answer: Roughly, a British year number is one higher than the American grade number: Year 10 corresponds to Grade 9, Year 11 to Grade 10, Year 12 to Grade 11. The IB Middle Years Programme runs across Years 7 to 11, and the Diploma occupies Years 12 and 13. Every school applies its own cut-off date and its own judgement, so this is a guide for asking a better question rather than a rule. The decision that matters is whether the placement puts your child into an examination year immediately.

faqs.question: Is it worse to be placed a year ahead or a year behind after a move?
faqs.answer: They fail differently. Placed ahead, a student is stretched and socially fine, and the pressure appears at the first set of real examinations rather than immediately. Placed behind, they are comfortable and often bored, and by the Diploma or A Level years they are a year older than their classmates, which matters more at seventeen than at twelve. Ask the school what the placement was based on and whether it is reviewable, and ask early rather than after a first report.

faqs.question: What transfers between education systems and what does not?
faqs.answer: In mathematics almost all the content transfers and the marking does not: method marks are awarded for reasoning written on the page, which a student trained towards clean final answers forfeits silently. In physics and chemistry the content mostly transfers in a different order, while practical write-up style and unit conventions are new. In biology the processes transfer and the mark-scheme vocabulary does not. English and the humanities are the widest gaps, because extended response structure and source evaluation are question types rather than knowledge.

faqs.question: In what order should a transferring student's gaps be addressed?
faqs.answer: Conventions first, skills second, content last, which is the reverse of what most plans do. Convention gaps, notation, method marks, write-up style, close in a few weeks once named and produce visible improvement that restores confidence after a bad report. Skill gaps, such as source evaluation or extended response structure, take eight to sixteen weeks and should therefore start early. Content gaps are finite and schedulable, so they can wait. Doing content first feels productive and leaves the real losses in place.

faqs.question: How do I check my child is in the right Arabic stream?
faqs.answer: Ask the school directly, in the first fortnight. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Newly arrived students are the group most often placed in a stream that does not match their actual background and literacy level. Ask which stream, what it assumes and how it is assessed, before a report arrives.

faqs.question: Can tutoring use a different Arabic or Islamic Education scheme from the school's?
faqs.answer: No, and this is a genuine constraint rather than a preference. For the mandatory UAE subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited. Tutoring therefore works from the school's own material and the stream the child is enrolled in. A provider offering a separate Arabic programme that will raise a school grade is describing something that does not fit the rules these subjects operate under, which is worth knowing before paying for it.

faqs.question: We arrived mid-Diploma with coursework partly done. Who do we talk to first?
faqs.answer: The new school's IB coordinator, before any tutor. The questions are: which components transfer, which must be restarted, what the new internal deadlines are, whether the subject and level combination can be timetabled, and whether entries have already been made. Those answers determine everything else, and a tutoring plan built before them is guesswork. Once they exist, a tutor can explain the new system's criteria, review what the student has produced and name which criterion is under-served.

faqs.question: Can a tutor finish an Internal Assessment my child started at another school?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody legitimately can. A tutor may teach the content the assessment rests on, explain each criterion and what its marks reward, say whether a research question still works under the new school's expectations, warn that a method will not generate usable data and review a draft to name the weak criterion. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite sections, generate data, choose the question or edit a draft into a finished state. One provider in this market sells completed assessments; the malpractice consequence falls on your child.

faqs.question: How much should a transition cost rather than a full term of tutoring?
faqs.answer: Price the block, not the term. A mapping block of three or four sessions plus a finite transition block of six to twelve weeks is a defined spend with an end point. Published market figures put qualified subject tutors online at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with one agency publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, and specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. The expensive outcome is an open arrangement begun in a panic that nobody ever decides to end.

faqs.question: Do you provide home tutoring for apartments in Culture Village?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video. For a transferring student the argument is about matching rather than cost: the useful tutor knows both the system your child left and the one they joined well enough to name the differences in notation and marking, and that person is unlikely to live within a short drive of the creek.

faqs.question: Which documents should we collect while our child is at this school?
faqs.answer: The full transcript or report history in its original format rather than a summary. The syllabus codes for every examined subject, each year, because future schools and universities ask which specification was sat. A school statement of the programme and the Arabic and Islamic Education stream your child was enrolled in. And every examination certificate and results statement as it arrives, since reissues are slow and sometimes chargeable. All of this is routine now and awkward once you have left.

faqs.question: Should a family that might move again be careful about dropping subjects?
faqs.answer: Yes, more careful than a settled family. A subject dropped at fourteen can close a route in a country you have not moved to yet, and option choices made for convenience in one system occasionally look costly in another. The published British-track equivalency rule in the UAE requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus an Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects. Verify current requirements with the ministry.

faqs.question: What should we do in the first fortnight after arriving, before booking anything?
faqs.answer: Four free things. Ask which year group placement was made, on what basis, and whether it is reviewable. Ask each subject teacher what the class has covered so far this year, which is a short list that immediately shows the content gaps. Ask which Arabic and Islamic Education stream your child is in. And ask for one marked piece of work in two or three subjects. That package is what a useful first tutoring session is built on, and sometimes it shows no tutor is needed.

dubai/culture-village.closingHeading: Map the gap before you buy the hours
dubai/culture-village.closingBody: A child who joined a Dubai school in February is not behind; they are differently prepared, and the first report rarely says which. Before booking anything, ask the school four free questions: the basis of the year-group placement, what each class has covered this year, which Arabic and Islamic Education stream your child is in, and whether you can see one marked piece of work per subject. Then start with a mapping block of three or four sessions that produces a written list of what is actually missing, split into conventions, skills and content, with honest timescales. Build a transition block with an end date from that. Every lesson is one-to-one over live video, and it continues if you move again.

dubai/damac-hills.tutorsIntro: The profiles below are the ones DAMAC Hills families book most: IGCSE Mathematics and the separate sciences, Diploma Higher Level subjects, and the scarcer options that no tutor within driving distance covers. Each teaches a named specification.

intro.heading: Distance quietly chooses the tutor before you do
paragraphs: A DAMAC Hills parent looking for a tutor is making a choice they are probably not aware of making. The practical set of tutors available to a household this far down Umm Suqeim Road is not the set of good tutors in Dubai; it is the much smaller set who are willing to drive out here, at the hour your child is free, for a single lesson. Everything else about the decision - subject knowledge, board, level, experience with the specific paper - gets applied to whatever is left after that filter.

The filter is tighter than it feels. A tutor who lives in Barsha or Jumeirah and charges by the hour has to spend forty minutes or more each way to reach a DAMAC Hills address at five o'clock. That journey is unpaid time unless it is priced into the rate, which it is, and it also limits them to one or at most two households in an evening. Rational tutors respond by declining the trip, charging a premium for it, or stacking families in the same community into consecutive slots that may not suit either.

So the figures parents compare are not comparing the same thing. A quoted in-home rate contains tutor time plus journey time plus the opportunity cost of the lesson they could not take. That is why market in-home rates in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online - figures read from provider listings and a published Dubai rate survey in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list. The gap is mostly geography.

Removing the journey does two things, and the second matters more than the first. It takes the travel premium out of the price. More importantly, it replaces a selection filter based on driving distance with one based on who actually teaches your child's specification. For a core subject at IGCSE that may not change much. For Higher Level Physics, Pearson Further Pure Mathematics or a smaller Diploma option, it is the difference between a specialist and whoever was available.

On delivery, plainly: lessons run one-to-one over live video with screen sharing. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. If a family's judgement is that a particular child needs an adult physically in the room, an in-home tutor is the right answer for that child and this page sets out what that choice costs so the decision can be made with the numbers visible.

Nothing here promises a grade. The rest of this page covers what the radius actually costs, when a session can start from each route out of the community, which subjects are genuinely unavailable locally, and the boundary a tutor has to keep on assessed work.

dubai/damac-hills.programmesIntro: All four programmes appear in this community, with the school inside DAMAC Hills and others reached along Umm Suqeim and Al Qudra Roads. Each note below includes the part of the programme where a specialist match matters most, because that is where distance costs the most.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years of specification-led courses examined at the end of Year 11, with the syllabus code deciding the papers, the tiering and the formula sheet. Cambridge runs Core and Extended routes on several subjects with different grade ceilings; Pearson generally runs a single tier. Eight or nine subjects compete for the same evenings.
programmes.countryNote: For the core IGCSE subjects a local tutor is usually findable, so distance costs money rather than quality. Where it starts costing quality is the less common entries - Further Pure Mathematics, Additional Mathematics, a second language - which a tutor willing to drive to DAMAC Hills may well not teach at all.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internally assessed work in each subject is marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB. The specialist requirement is sharper here: Higher Level teaching is paper-specific, and a general subject tutor at that level is doing something different from what the student needs.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the radius bites hardest. The number of Higher Level Physics or Chemistry specialists who will drive to DAMAC Hills on a weekday evening is small, and in the February to May window it is smaller still. Online delivery is not a convenience here; it is what makes the match possible at all.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject group, each marked out of eight and converted to a 1-7 grade, with no external papers until optional eAssessment at the end of Year 11. Marks come from interim tasks, so a weak criterion can sit inside a respectable grade for a long time without anybody naming it.
programmes.countryNote: MYP work is usually best bought as a short block aimed at one criterion rather than as a standing slot. That shape is awkward for an in-home arrangement, because a tutor who has committed to a weekly drive wants a weekly booking, and online delivery makes a six-week block with an endpoint straightforward.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units with reporting against outcomes rather than marks. Reading fluency, number-fact recall and written stamina decide how Year 7 goes, and a prose report can hide all three. Short frequent sessions beat long infrequent ones at this age.
programmes.countryNote: Primary is the one stage where a parent might reasonably prefer someone in the room, and it is also the stage where a thirty-minute session makes most sense. Paying an in-home travel premium for half an hour of teaching is the worst value in this market, which is worth knowing before arranging it.

dubai/damac-hills.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones DAMAC Hills families request most, with a note on how hard each is to find locally. The pattern is consistent: core subjects are findable nearby, and everything else is not.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: Findable locally and the subject that responds best to a weekly hour, because the failures are visible in the script. Extended candidates lose marks on multi-step problems mixing two topics with no signposted method. Check the tier before booking: a Core entry caps the grade.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics
subjects.description: Generally findable, though board-specific experience is not. The written practical paper tests reading an unfamiliar method and finding its weakness, and a tutor who only knows the other board's paper structure will teach the content well and the paper badly.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles calculations and organic chemistry decide the grade and both reward drill. Available locally, but the pool narrows sharply if you also want someone who knows the specific practical paper your child sits.

subjects.name: IGCSE Biology
subjects.description: Widely available. Marks turn on terminology precision and answering the command term used rather than on content volume, which also makes this a subject a disciplined student can lift substantially alone with past papers.

subjects.name: IGCSE Further Pure Mathematics
subjects.description: A separate qualification from International GCSE Mathematics, taken alongside it at some schools. Almost never covered by a tutor whose selling point is proximity, because the cohort is small and the content is distinct. This is a clear case for a wider pool.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof and calculus are the Higher Level pressure points, and the exploration moves whole grades because it is marked against five lettered criteria. Higher Level specialists who will drive this far on a weekday are a short list, and shorter from February.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and heavy graphical-calculator work. Calculator technique is genuinely teachable and routinely neglected; interpretation carries marks students expect for the calculation alone.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The scarcest of the Higher Level sciences in this market. Marks are lost in algebra rather than physics, and the data-analysis component is barely practised. For a DAMAC Hills household this is the subject where a driving radius and a good match are least compatible.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the Higher Level papers. The internally assessed investigation loses marks on uncertainty handling and on conclusions that outrun the data, both of which need someone who has marked the component.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry the marks and unlabelled diagrams lose them. The internally assessed commentaries are built on published articles, so article choice sets the ceiling before any analysis is written. Moderately available, and better online than locally.

subjects.name: Psychology and the smaller Diploma options
subjects.description: Psychology, Global Politics, Computer Science and similar options draw on a much shorter list than the headline subject grids suggest. Within a thirty-minute radius of DAMAC Hills the realistic answer is often nobody, which is the whole argument for removing the radius.

sections.heading: What a driving radius does to the choice of tutor
paragraphs: Start with the direct answer: for a household in DAMAC Hills, insisting on a tutor who comes to the house reduces the available pool by a large and unmeasured proportion, and the reduction is not random. It removes specialists first. A tutor whose subject is in demand across the whole city has no reason to spend ninety minutes in a car for one lesson, so the people who accept the journey are disproportionately those with spare capacity.

That is not an argument that local tutors are weak. Plenty are excellent, and for a core IGCSE subject the pool within a reasonable radius is deep enough that a good match exists. The argument is narrower and more specific: the scarcer the requirement, the more the radius costs. Higher Level Physics, Pearson Further Pure Mathematics, Psychology, a second language, or a specific practical paper on a specific board - for each of those, the number of people inside a thirty-minute drive who genuinely teach it may be zero.

Families rarely see this happening because the filter is applied before they get a shortlist. An agency with a travel radius presents the tutors who will travel; the ones who will not never appear. The parent then chooses the best of what is shown and reasonably concludes they chose well. The counterfactual - the Higher Level specialist twenty-five kilometres away who would have taken the lesson online - is invisible.

The table makes the trade explicit by radius. The point of the last column is that each ring costs something specific rather than something vague. Deciding to pay that cost is entirely legitimate; for a nine-year-old who needs an adult in the room it may be the right call. Paying it unknowingly for a Diploma Higher Level subject is the version worth avoiding.

sections.heading: The travel premium, decomposed
paragraphs: An in-home hour is not an hour. It is the taught hour plus the journey each way plus the lesson the tutor could not take instead, and all three are inside the number you are quoted. Nobody itemises this, which is why a parent comparing AED 250 for an in-home lesson with AED 220 online concludes the difference is small. For a household this far from where most tutors live, the difference is most of the gap.

Market rates make the shape visible. In-home one-to-one in Dubai runs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, according to a published Dubai rate survey giving 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertising 200 to 500. A qualified subject tutor online is AED 150 to 300, and an IB or IGCSE specialist AED 200 to 450 or more. Monthly packages in this market are advertised at around AED 799 online for eight sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 in-home for four two-hour sessions. Those figures were read in October 2026 and are market rates, not ours.

Compare the monthly packages carefully, because they are the clearest illustration. Eight online sessions against four in-home sessions of twice the length is the same nominal teaching time for roughly double the money, and the in-home version concentrates it into half as many contacts. For most subjects, eight shorter contacts produce more than four long ones, because spacing beats duration for retention. So the premium buys fewer, longer sessions as well as costing more.

The table below separates what the money is actually for. The last column is specific to this community: from a DAMAC Hills address, the journey component is at the upper end of what it would be anywhere in Dubai. If physical presence is what a family wants, that is a reasonable thing to buy - but it should be bought knowingly, with the arithmetic above visible rather than folded into a single hourly figure.

sections.heading: The Umm Suqeim and Al Qudra routes, and when a session can start
paragraphs: The second thing distance does is set the earliest useful session time, and it does so differently for each child in a household. A child at the school inside DAMAC Hills can be home by about half past three. A sibling bussed from the Arabian Ranches cluster or Dubai Hills is typically back between half past four and half past five. A student travelling from Dubai Investments Park or further west can be later still.

This matters because the useful hour is the one before fatigue, not the one after dinner. A session at eight in the evening with a student who left the house at six thirty in the morning is an hour of attendance. The same hour at half past four, for a child who arrived home at four, does several times the work. Where an earlier slot exists for a particular child, it is worth rearranging the rest of the household to protect it.

The table maps the main routes against a realistic arrival window and the earliest start we would recommend. These are operational figures from scheduling families in the southern communities rather than published survey data, and yours will differ by fifteen minutes in one direction or the other. Tell us the school and the route and the slot is set from that rather than from an average.

One more consequence of the geography is worth naming. Because the roads out of this community feed into a small number of junctions, a delay affects every child in the household at once rather than one of them. That is the practical case for agreeing a single named fallback slot for the whole house instead of per-child rearrangements, and for putting the latest-arriving child's work into a weekend block where the road has no vote.

sections.heading: What a wider pool actually buys, subject by subject
paragraphs: It is easy to make the online argument abstractly and harder to make it concretely, so here it is concretely. For some subjects a wider pool buys very little, because the local supply is adequate and a competent tutor is a competent tutor. For others it buys the difference between a specialist and a substitute. Knowing which category your request falls into is the whole decision.

Core IGCSE subjects sit in the first category. Mathematics, Biology, Chemistry and English are taught by enough people in Dubai that a household in the southern communities can find a good local match, and the main cost of insisting on a visit is money rather than quality. Even there, one caveat applies: board-specific experience is scarcer than subject experience, and a tutor who knows the other board's practical paper will teach content well and the paper badly.

The second category is where the radius genuinely hurts. Higher Level Physics is the clearest case - it is the scarcest of the Diploma sciences in this market and it tightens from February. Pearson Further Pure Mathematics, Cambridge Additional Mathematics, Psychology, Global Politics, Computer Science and the less common languages all draw on short lists city-wide, and within half an hour of DAMAC Hills the honest count is often zero.

The table sets this out request by request. Where a UAE-based specialist is not free, the fallback is a specialist based outside the UAE, most often in India, teaching the same specification online, with the base and the time difference stated before anything is confirmed. That is disclosed in advance rather than discovered later, which is a different thing from routing a Dubai parent to a foreign number and letting them assume local delivery.
