sections.heading: The school inside the community and the schools outside it
paragraphs: DAMAC Hills has a school inside it, which changes household logistics more than fees do. A child attending it is home by mid-afternoon, with the best study window of the day still ahead of them. A sibling at a school in the Ranches or Dubai Hills is home an hour or more later with that window largely gone. In a household with both, those two children should not be treated as having the same evening.

The board question still applies. Schools around the southern communities choose examination boards subject by subject, so a student can sit Cambridge in the sciences and Pearson in Mathematics, and two siblings at different schools can be on different boards in the same subject. The subject name on both reports looks identical; the paper structure, tiering and formula sheet are not. Ask each school's examinations officer for the board, the syllabus code and the tier, in writing.

A note on inspection ratings, since families in a newer community often ask. KHDA licenses and inspects Dubai private schools and publishes inspection outcomes on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. Those bands describe the school, and they are published on the regulator's own site, which is the only place to read them. They say nothing about whether your particular child is on top of the independent half of their course, which is the thing tutoring addresses.

For market context: KHDA counted 227 private schools and 387,441 pupils in Dubai in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, and confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under an economic incentives package. Dubai is adding seven new private schools for 2026-27, four British and three IB, creating 16,846 places - and new capacity in the southern communities is part of why the school list here keeps changing.

sections.heading: Group classes and tuition centres: the second commute
paragraphs: The alternative to bringing a tutor out is taking the student in, and from DAMAC Hills that means a drive to a licensed centre in Barsha, Jumeirah or one of the newer commercial clusters. On paper the class rate looks attractive. Counted properly, it rarely is, because the cost includes two journeys at the worst hours of the day and a parent's evening alongside the fee.

There is also a question about what a class delivers. Group teaching covers content at a pace set by the group, which suits a student who needs the whole topic again. It does not suit a student whose losses are specific and individual, because the tutor cannot stop and watch one student attempt thirty unprompted questions while the rest wait. Most students who have reached the point of paying for help are in the second category rather than the first.

Where a class genuinely works is revision of a shared syllabus close to an examination, for a student who is broadly on track and needs structure and company. In that narrow case the pace problem matters less and the social effect helps. Even then, the two journeys have to be counted, and from this community they are substantial enough to turn a ninety-minute class into a three-hour commitment.

The sibling-shared session is the version of this idea that does work here. Two children at genuinely the same point in the same subject on the same specification take one hour together, online, at roughly half the one-to-one rate each. It halves the cost per child and halves the number of slots an evening has to hold, without adding a journey. It fails when children two years apart are put together to save money, because the tutor ends up teaching one and occupying the other.

sections.heading: Coursework support and the line a tutor cannot cross
paragraphs: There are providers ranking for these searches that sell finished internal assessments at a fixed price. The arithmetic is worth stating plainly: a student who submits purchased work faces their school's academic honesty process and, under IB rules, a malpractice finding that can cost the entire diploma. The provider keeps the fee. The exposure is entirely the student's, and it follows them.

Legitimate support is narrower and genuinely more useful. A tutor teaches the criteria by letter and the marks attached to each. A tutor interrogates a research question until it is answerable inside the word limit. A tutor questions the method, the sample, the data and the reasoning. A tutor reads a draft and replies with questions - why this comparison, what does this graph show that the table does not, which limitation would an examiner notice first. The student then decides, in their own words.

What a tutor must not do is supply text, restructure an argument on the student's behalf, or hand back a rewritten version to be retyped. The test is whether the student can defend every decision in the work under questioning, without notes, because every decision was theirs. That standard is what protects them, and it does not relax because a deadline is close or because a family is paying a premium rate.

The same boundary covers the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay, the MYP Personal Project and IGCSE coursework. One practical point for this community in particular: a tutor working online leaves a written trail of feedback, which is easier to show a school than a verbal conversation in a living room if a question about authorship ever arises. That is a small advantage of the format and worth knowing about.

sections.heading: The permit, the regulator, and what IB Gram does not claim
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and this is a reasonable thing for a parent to ask about before letting anyone teach their child. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen.

MoHRE's own service page lists the permit as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount appears here; a figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source.

Two conditions matter for anyone considering a visiting tutor. The permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. So engaging your child's own teacher privately is not the convenient shortcut it appears to be, regardless of who offers it.

Separately, a tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific authorisation with an initial approval stage and annual renewal. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no office, centre or branch in the UAE, and delivers lessons online. Nothing on this site claims approval, accreditation or licensing by KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, because none is held.

sections.heading: Judging whether the arrangement is working
paragraphs: A household that has solved the geography problem still has to answer the ordinary one, which is whether the tutoring is doing anything. This is unusually easy to lose track of, because a session that happens reliably and pleasantly feels like progress, and in a community where arranging anything is effortful, reliability can be mistaken for effectiveness.

The evidence that counts is narrow. Marks on your child's own returned work. Scores on whole timed papers marked against the published scheme. And whether the specific failure named in the diagnostic has stopped appearing - if the finding was that the student cannot begin an unprompted question, the test is whether they now begin unprompted questions. School report grades move too slowly and confidence is not evidence at all.

Set the review point before the first session rather than when doubt arrives. Six to eight weeks suits a weekly slot: long enough for a habit to change, short enough that a wrong match is not carried through a term. Three outcomes are legitimate at that point - continue, change tutor, or stop - and stopping should be a normal result. Tutoring that has done its job should end rather than become a standing arrangement.

Ask for the written record too. Each session should produce a short note naming what was worked on and the next target, and four consecutive notes on the same topic mean something is not landing. A provider who cannot produce that is asking you to take a term's benefit on trust in a market where an hour costs AED 150 to 450, and for a household that has already paid a premium in logistics, that is the wrong thing to be asked.

process.title: Tell us the school, the route and the arrival time
process.description: For each child: school, route and roughly when they walk through the door. From DAMAC Hills that varies by more than an hour between a child at the local school and one bussed from the Ranches, and the slot is set from the real figure rather than an average.

process.title: Send the syllabus code, level and tier
process.description: Ask the examinations officer in writing for the board, the code and, on Cambridge subjects, the tier. That is what determines the match, and it matters more here than elsewhere because the scarce requests are exactly the ones a local tutor is least likely to cover.

process.title: One diagnostic hour on marked work
process.description: The first session works on returned scripts and a short set of unprompted questions rather than teaching, and you get the finding in writing. It also establishes whether the request is a core subject where local supply would have been fine or a scarce one where it would not.

process.title: See the match before you commit
process.description: You are told who the tutor is, which specification they teach, where they are based and what time zone they are in before anything is booked. If no UAE-based specialist is free for a scarce subject, that is said at this stage rather than after the first invoice.

process.title: Fix the slot and one household fallback
process.description: A protected weekly time per child, timed from their arrival, with a single named fallback slot for the whole house. Because the roads out of this community feed a few junctions, a delay affects every child at once, and one agreed catch-up time is easier to hold than several.

process.title: Review on marks at six to eight weeks
process.description: We compare the plan against marked work and decide to continue, change tutor or stop. Stopping is a normal outcome. Reliability is not the same as effectiveness, and in a community where arranging anything takes effort the two are especially easy to confuse.

whyPoints.title: No travel filter applied before you see a match
whyPoints.description: The tutor is chosen because they teach your child's specification, not because they will drive to Al Qudra Road at five o'clock. For a Higher Level subject or a less common entry that filter is the difference between a specialist and whoever had capacity.

whyPoints.title: The travel premium is shown, not absorbed
whyPoints.description: Market in-home rates of AED 180-500 against AED 150-300 online are mostly geography, and the monthly packages make it starker: eight online sessions at around AED 799 against four in-home at AED 1,599-1,799. Those figures are published by others and dated to October 2026.

whyPoints.title: Start times mapped per route, per child
whyPoints.description: A child at the school inside the community and a sibling bussed from the Ranches do not have the same evening. Both slots are set from their own arrival time, which is only possible when nothing has to travel between them.

whyPoints.title: Scarce subjects named honestly
whyPoints.description: Higher Level Physics, Pearson Further Pure Mathematics, Psychology and the smaller options have short lists city-wide and often none within half an hour of here. Where no UAE-based specialist is free you are told, with the fallback tutor's base and time zone stated.

whyPoints.title: Spacing over duration
whyPoints.description: Eight shorter contacts beat four long ones for retention in most subjects, which is the second thing an in-home package costs besides money. The session length is set by what the subject needs rather than by what justifies a journey.

whyPoints.title: A coursework line that does not move
whyPoints.description: Criteria taught by letter, method and reasoning questioned, drafts answered with questions. No text supplied and no section rewritten. The test is whether your child can defend every choice unaided, and online work leaves a written feedback trail if authorship is ever queried.

faqs.question: How far will a tutor actually travel to DAMAC Hills?
faqs.answer: Further than you would expect for a weekly booking at a good rate, and not as far as you need for a scarce subject. A tutor living in Barsha or Jumeirah faces forty minutes or more each way to reach an address here at five o'clock, which is unpaid time unless it is priced into the rate, and it limits them to one or two households in an evening. The people who accept that journey are disproportionately those with spare capacity, which means the radius filters out specialists first rather than at random.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send tutors to DAMAC Hills villas?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide in-home tutoring anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service offered only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video with screen sharing, which is how a tutor and a student work through a marked script together. For a household this far down Umm Suqeim Road the practical gain is twofold: no travel premium inside the rate, and a tutor chosen because they teach your child's specification rather than because they are willing to make the drive.

faqs.question: What does the travel premium actually add to an hour?
faqs.answer: Most of the gap between the two rates. Market in-home one-to-one in Dubai runs roughly AED 180-500 an hour including travel, with a published Dubai rate survey giving 180-350 and independent home tutors advertising 200-500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online and AED 200-450 or more for a specialist. The monthly packages make it clearer still: around AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those figures were read in October 2026 and are market rates, not ours.

faqs.question: What time can a session start for a DAMAC Hills family?
faqs.answer: It depends on the child rather than the community. A child at the school inside DAMAC Hills is often home by about half past three, so a four o'clock start is realistic and worth protecting. A sibling bussed from the Arabian Ranches cluster or Dubai Hills is typically back between half past four and half past five, which puts the floor at about half past five. A student travelling from the western schools may be later still, and for them a weekend block is usually better value than a late weekday hour.

faqs.question: Which schools do DAMAC Hills children attend?
faqs.answer: There is a school inside the community, which a good number of local children attend, and beyond that families travel north to the Arabian Ranches and Dubai Hills schools, north-west to the Motor City and Sports City cluster, or west towards Dubai Investments Park. Those schools choose examination boards subject by subject, so one student can sit Cambridge in the sciences and Pearson in Mathematics, and two siblings at different schools can be on different boards in the same subject. Ask each examinations officer for the board, code and tier in writing.

faqs.question: Is it worth driving to a tuition centre in Barsha from here?
faqs.answer: Rarely, once the journey is counted on both sides. From DAMAC Hills a ninety-minute class becomes a three-hour commitment at the worst hours of the day, plus a parent's evening, on top of the fee. The deeper problem is pace: group teaching covers content at the group's speed, which suits a student who needs a whole topic again but not one whose losses are specific and individual - and most families who have reached the point of paying for help are in the second category.

faqs.question: We want someone physically in the room. Is online a compromise?
faqs.answer: For some children, yes, and it is worth saying so rather than arguing. A young primary child who needs an adult present to stay on task is better served by someone in the room, and if that is your judgement an in-home tutor is the right choice. What this page asks is that the choice is made with the numbers visible: from DAMAC Hills it costs a substantial travel premium and it narrows the pool, which matters little for Year 4 reading and a great deal for Higher Level Physics.

faqs.question: Which subjects are effectively impossible to find locally?
faqs.answer: Within about thirty minutes of here, the honest list is longer than most families expect: Higher Level Physics, Pearson Further Pure Mathematics, Cambridge Additional Mathematics, Psychology, Global Politics, Computer Science and the less common languages. These draw on short lists across the whole city, and inside a driving radius from the southern communities the realistic count is often zero. Higher Level Mathematics is findable with early booking and tightens sharply from February onwards, which is when most families start looking.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two children in a DAMAC Hills household?
faqs.answer: Across two slots, yes, and it often works well. In a single shared session, only when the two children are genuinely at the same point in the same subject on the same specification - in which case it costs roughly half the one-to-one rate each and halves the number of slots the evening has to hold. Two children even two years apart cannot share usefully: the tutor teaches one and occupies the other. Review any shared arrangement after four sessions, because a mismatch shows up quickly.

faqs.question: How do we judge whether the arrangement is working?
faqs.answer: On three things, none of which is confidence. Marks on your child's own returned work. Scores on whole timed papers marked against the published scheme. And whether the specific failure named in the diagnostic has stopped appearing. Set the review point before the first session - six to eight weeks suits a weekly slot - with continue, change tutor or stop as the three legitimate outcomes. In a community where arranging anything is effortful, a session that happens reliably is especially easy to mistake for one that is working.

faqs.question: Does a tutor who lives nearby know our school better?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth less than it sounds. Local knowledge of a school's culture is pleasant but it is not what moves a grade; knowledge of the specific paper is. What actually matters is the syllabus code, the tier and the component where marks are being lost, and a tutor who has taught that exact specification for years will diagnose faster than one who knows the building. Where local familiarity genuinely helps is with a school's internal coursework deadlines, and those can simply be sent to any tutor.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help my child finish an internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Help them finish it, yes; finish it for them, no. A tutor can teach the criteria by letter and the marks attached to each, identify which criterion is currently scoring nothing, question the method, data and reasoning, and respond to a draft with questions rather than corrections. What a tutor must not do is supply text, restructure the argument or hand back a rewritten version to retype. The test is whether your child can defend every choice unaided, and purchased coursework risks a malpractice finding that can cost the whole diploma.

faqs.question: Do tutors visiting DAMAC Hills need a permit?
faqs.answer: Any individual providing private tutoring in the UAE does. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE lists the application with no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. Since the permit costs nothing, not holding it usually means the rules were never checked.

faqs.question: What happens if a session has to move at short notice?
faqs.answer: It is rescheduled within the same week, which is one of the less obvious advantages of removing the journey. A visiting tutor who has built an evening around one trip to this community cannot usually offer an alternative slot that week, so a cancelled lesson becomes a lost lesson. Agree a single named fallback time for the whole household rather than one per child: the roads out of here feed a small number of junctions, so a delay tends to affect every child at once rather than one of them.

faqs.question: Is a tutor based outside the UAE a downgrade?
faqs.answer: Not for subject teaching, provided the specification matches and the time zone works - and both are stated before you book rather than discovered afterwards. For a scarce request such as Higher Level Physics in February, the realistic comparison is not a UAE specialist against a non-UAE one; it is a non-UAE specialist against nobody, or against a general science tutor teaching above their level. What we will not do is conceal the tutor's base, which two providers in this market effectively do by routing UAE parents to foreign numbers.

dubai/damac-hills.closingHeading: Decide what you are buying before you compare rates
dubai/damac-hills.closingBody: From DAMAC Hills the first question is not which tutor but which constraint you want to accept: a driving radius that filters specialists out, or a wider pool with nobody in the room. For core IGCSE subjects either works and the difference is mostly price. For Higher Level sciences and the scarcer entries, the radius is the whole decision. Send the school, the route, the arrival time, and the syllabus code or IB subject and level with the last marked work. You will get a written diagnostic, the named tutor with their specification, base and time zone, the rate in AED, one household fallback slot and a review date. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video.

intro.heading: The part of the course your child has to carry alone
paragraphs: A DAMAC Hills 2 family almost never needs a tutor because a school is teaching badly. The schools this community buses into are inspected annually and most teach the specification competently. The problem is structural: both the Diploma Programme and IGCSE hand a large, graded portion of the course to the student to complete outside lesson time, and nothing in the school day is designed to supervise that part. A Chemistry teacher with twenty-two students has four lessons a week to cover a two-year specification. The exploration, the forty hours of independent practice, the past-paper discipline and the reading that turns a six into a seven happen at a desk in Dubailand, alone, at eight in the evening.

That is where the gap opens, and it opens quietly. Class marks stay respectable because class tasks are scaffolded. Mock marks fall because mock papers are not. Parents see a report that says 'working at expected level' in March and a mock grade two bands lower in December, and conclude something changed. Nothing changed. The assessment simply stopped carrying the student and started testing them.

Measuring that gap is the useful thing a tutor does first. An hour of diagnosis on an unseen paper tells you which of four failure modes you are dealing with: content never secured, content secured but not retrievable under time, command terms misread, or working shown so thinly that method marks are lost on correct answers. Those four problems need four different remedies, and buying generic weekly tutoring for the wrong one wastes a term. A student who loses marks on presentation does not need more content; they need six supervised papers with a marker sitting beside them pointing at the line where a mark went.

DAMAC Hills 2 adds a practical constraint on top. The community sits out on the Al Qudra side of Dubailand, and the schools its children attend are in Dubai Investments Park, Motor City, Arabian Ranches, Dubai Sports City and The Sustainable City. A secondary bus route home is rarely under forty minutes and frequently longer in term time. A 16:00 session that would work in Jumeirah does not work here, and a tutor driving out from Deira makes it worse rather than better. Online delivery removes the whole problem: the lesson starts when the child is through the door and fed, not when a car finishes a journey.

IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform, not a centre. There is no IB Gram building in Dubai, and lessons for UAE families are delivered as one-to-one online tuition over live video with a shared whiteboard and a recording the student keeps. Home visits are a service we offer only in India; we do not send a tutor to any UAE address. What that buys a DAMAC Hills 2 family is choice of specialist rather than choice of whoever lives within a twenty-minute drive of Al Qudra Road, which on a Physics HL or Economics HL request is the difference between a subject teacher and a generalist.

dubai/damac-hills-2.programmesIntro: DAMAC Hills 2 children sit three broad routes, and the tutoring each one needs differs more than the brochures suggest. The notes below say what each programme actually assesses and what a student in this community typically carries home.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an internal assessment worth roughly 20 to 25 per cent of the final grade, written by the student over several months. The external papers are sat in a single session, which means two years of content is examined across a fortnight. Grades run 1 to 7 per subject with a maximum of 45 points including three bonus points from TOK and the Extended Essay.
programmes.countryNote: DAMAC Hills 2 students reach the DP mostly through Greenfield International School in Dubai Investments Park and Jumeirah English Speaking School in Arabian Ranches, with others moving across from British-track schools after IGCSE. That second group starts DP1 having never written an internal assessment and often needs the first term purely on research method and criterion language rather than on subject content.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked 0 to 8, with teacher judgement converted to a 1 to 7 grade. There is no external paper until the optional eAssessment at the end of MYP 5. The criteria reward inquiry, communication and reflection as much as right answers, which is a genuine shift for a child arriving from a British primary where accuracy was most of the mark.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP question that recurs in this part of Dubailand is whether to continue into the DP or move to IGCSE at 14. Families weigh the bus distance to an IB continuum school against the British schools nearer Motor City and Sports City. Tutoring in MYP 4 and 5 is most useful when it builds the algebraic fluency and the lab-write-up discipline that the DP assumes already exists.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Typically eight to ten subjects examined at the end of Year 11, graded 9 to 1 or A* to G depending on the board and subject. Cambridge offers Core and Extended tiers in several subjects, where Core caps at grade C and Extended runs to A*. Papers are short, numerous and heavily pattern-based, which makes past-paper discipline the single highest-return activity in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: Most DAMAC Hills 2 children in Years 10 and 11 attend British-curriculum schools around Dubai Investments Park, Motor City and Dubai Sports City. The practical risk here is tier: a child entered for Core Mathematics cannot be awarded above a C, and a UAE Ministry of Education equivalency file needs five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, so a tier decision taken in Year 10 constrains options years later.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry with no external examinations, ending in the Year 6 Exhibition. Reporting is descriptive rather than numerical, which is why parents moving in from a graded system often cannot tell whether their child is behind. Reading fluency, number bonds and written stamina are the three things worth checking independently.
programmes.countryNote: Primary provision is the part DAMAC Hills 2 feels most, because the youngest children take the longest bus ride relative to their day. Tutoring at this stage is short and infrequent by design: two twenty-five to thirty-minute sessions a week on reading or number, placed before dinner rather than after it.

dubai/damac-hills-2.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects DAMAC Hills 2 families ask for most, with the specific place each one usually goes wrong. A tutor who cannot name that place is guessing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which exposes any weakness in algebraic manipulation that a graphing display has been hiding. HL adds proof by induction, complex numbers and a far heavier calculus load. Most marks are lost on unjustified steps rather than wrong answers.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-permitted throughout, with statistics, modelling and financial mathematics carrying the weight. Students who chose it to avoid algebra are caught by the HL statistics content and by the need to interpret output in words rather than just produce it.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms account for most lost marks. The data booklet is permitted but rarely practised with, so students waste minutes hunting values. HL organic requires mechanism arrows drawn precisely enough to earn the mark, which is a drawing skill as much as a chemistry one.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields are usually secure; thermal physics, waves and the HL option paper are not. The recurring failure is treating a derivation as a formula to recall rather than a chain to reconstruct, which collapses as soon as the examiner changes the variable being solved for.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A content-heavy course where the marks sit in command terms. 'Outline', 'explain' and 'evaluate' demand different structures, and a student who writes everything they know about a topic will score below one who answers the verb asked. HL biochemistry and plant science are the usual weak zones.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides Paper 1. Axes mislabelled, a shift drawn without a new equilibrium marked, or a welfare area left unshaded all lose marks that the written analysis cannot recover. HL adds quantitative Paper 3, where the arithmetic is easy but the interpretation is not.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is an unseen guided analysis under timed conditions, and the Individual Oral is internally assessed against a global issue the student chooses. Most students can analyse; fewer can structure an argument in seventy-five minutes without a plan they have practised.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: Extended tier questions in the last third of each paper combine two topics, usually geometry inside algebra. Students lose marks by abandoning a question after one line instead of extracting the method marks available for a correct start.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and the alternative-to-practical paper cause most of the damage. Circuit questions require reading a diagram carefully before calculating; the practical paper requires knowing how a named apparatus is used, which cannot be revised from a textbook alone.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles calculations, qualitative analysis tests and electrolysis products are the three reliable mark-losers. The qualitative tests are pure recall and are worth drilling to automaticity, which is an efficient use of early sessions.

subjects.name: IGCSE Biology
subjects.description: Transport in plants, homeostasis and genetics crosses. The genetic-cross questions are procedural and highly scorable once the layout is fixed; students lose marks by omitting gamete rows or failing to state the ratio asked for.

subjects.name: IGCSE Business Studies
subjects.description: Case-study application is the whole paper. A technically correct definition scores one mark; the remaining marks require the answer to refer to the named business in the insert, which students consistently forget under time pressure.

sections.heading: What a DAMAC Hills 2 parent is actually buying
paragraphs: Searching for IB and IGCSE tutors in DAMAC Hills 2 returns pages that talk about passion and commitment. What a parent in this community needs is narrower: someone who will take over the part of the course the school cannot supervise, and who can be reached at 18:30 on a weekday without anyone driving on Al Qudra Road. That is the whole proposition, and it is worth stating before the marketing starts.

Both qualifications are built on the same assumption, which is that a motivated student will do substantial independent work. The IGCSE assumption is past papers: the papers are formulaic, the mark schemes are public, and a Year 11 student who has worked through six series properly will outperform an equally able student who has worked through none. The Diploma assumption is heavier still, because the internal assessment in each subject is a multi-month research task carried out largely outside lesson time, and Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay sit on top of six subjects.

No school timetable in Dubai supervises that work closely, because no timetable can. A teacher with four lessons a week and a two-year specification to deliver has to choose, and they choose content delivery. The student is left with the practice, the drafting and the revision. For a self-organising sixteen-year-old that is fine. For most, it is the point at which the grade separates from the ability.

sections.heading: The four places the gap opens in the Diploma
paragraphs: A Diploma grade that sits below a student's apparent ability almost always traces to one of four causes, and they are distinguishable within a single marked paper. The first is content never secured. A topic was taught in DP1, understood at the time, and never retrieved since. The student recognises the question and cannot produce the method. The remedy is cheap and boring: a reteach of the topic followed by spaced retrieval over a fortnight.

The second is content secured but not retrievable under time. The student can do every question given twenty minutes and none given eight. This is the most common cause in Dubai cohorts and the most frequently misdiagnosed, because the student honestly believes they do not understand the material. They do. What they lack is automaticity, which only comes from timed practice with a stopwatch running and someone enforcing the stop.

The third is misread command terms. The Diploma uses a published list of command terms with precise meanings, and the mark schemes follow them literally. A student asked to 'outline' who 'explains' wastes four minutes and gains nothing; a student asked to 'evaluate' who 'describes' loses most of the marks on an eight-mark question. This is a vocabulary problem masquerading as a subject problem and can be fixed in two sessions of sorting past questions by verb.

The fourth is thin working. Correct answers lose method marks when the intermediate steps are absent, and in Mathematics Paper 1 that can cost several marks across a paper without a single wrong answer. Diagnosis here needs someone to mark the student's actual script against the actual mark scheme, line by line, which is precisely what a school teacher with twenty-two scripts to return cannot do at that resolution.
bullets: Content never secured: reteach plus spaced retrieval, two to three weeks

sections.heading: IGCSE in Years 10 and 11: where independent practice decides the grade
paragraphs: The IGCSE is a pattern-recognition examination, and this is not a criticism of it. Each paper has a stable structure, a published mark scheme and a question bank that recycles the same assessment objectives in different clothing. A student who has worked through several past series under timed conditions, marked them honestly and logged their errors, walks into the real paper having already met every question type. A student who has revised by rereading notes has not.

Board and syllabus code matter more than parents expect, because the same subject is assessed differently by Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel. Cambridge tiers several subjects into Core and Extended, and the Core tier caps the available grade; Pearson generally does not tier the same way and uses different paper structures. Buying a tutor who teaches 'IGCSE Maths' without knowing whether the child sits 0580 Extended or 4MA1 is how a family ends up paying for practice on the wrong paper format.

A second, quieter issue is tier placement. Schools set tiers in Year 10 on the basis of Year 9 attainment, and the decision is reversible only within a window. A child capped at Core Mathematics cannot be awarded above a grade C, which has consequences for A Level and Diploma entry and for the five-subject count a UAE Ministry of Education equivalency file requires. If there is a case for moving tier, it has to be made with evidence early in Year 10, not argued in Year 11.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs around Dubailand, and who charges what
paragraphs: Most pages competing for this search publish no price at all, and two of the larger ones quote in US dollars, a currency no Dubai family pays school fees in. The figures below are market rates in AED, taken from providers' own published pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, read in October 2026. They are the market, not an IB Gram price list.

The pattern across providers is consistent. Online lessons with a qualified subject specialist cluster between AED 150 and AED 300 an hour. In-home visits carry a travel premium and sit between AED 180 and AED 500, with the upper end reflecting distance as much as expertise. IB and IGCSE specialists command AED 200 to AED 450 and above; one premium provider publishes AED 650. At the budget end, platforms advertise from AED 33 to AED 65 an hour, which generally buys a university student working from a textbook rather than a subject specialist working from a mark scheme.

For a DAMAC Hills 2 family the travel premium is the number worth attending to. The community is far enough out that an in-home tutor is pricing a round trip of well over an hour into the fee, and is drawn from whoever is willing to make that trip. That is a small pool, and it is selected for geography rather than for subject. Online delivery removes the premium and widens the pool to anyone who teaches the specification, which is why an HL Physics or HL Economics request is answerable here at all.

Set the rate against the rest of the bill before deciding what is reasonable. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, so a tutoring budget is the variable part of an otherwise fixed education cost. One session a week for a school year is a different financial object from two sessions a week plus an exam-run intensive, and it is worth modelling both before committing.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the exam instead of forwards from today
paragraphs: Families plan tutoring from the date they decide to start. Examination boards plan from entry deadlines, which sit months before the papers. The two calendars do not meet, and the result is a family booking in February for a session whose entry closed in November. Working backwards from the exam is the single most useful planning habit available, and no competing page in this market does it.

The sourced Cambridge example makes the point. For the March 2027 series, Cambridge publishes an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Direct from 13 May and certificates in late June. The entry deadline is ten weeks before the first paper. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct zone timetable, noting that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version.

Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May or June and again in November. Its November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so the live official PDF is the only version worth planning from.

IB session dates are the exception on this page. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no IB examination or results date here has been confirmed from the IB itself. UAE schools sit the May session; for the exact window, the school's IB coordinator and ibo.org are the only sources worth relying on, and both should be checked before a revision plan is fixed.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch on an internal assessment
paragraphs: This is the section the essay mills in this search result hope nobody reads. One provider in the researched set sells finished Internal Assessments outright. That is academic malpractice under IB rules, it is an expulsion risk for the student, and it is the opposite of tutoring. A family paying for coursework support deserves a plain account of where the line sits, because the student is the one who signs the authenticity declaration.

The permitted territory is wide and genuinely valuable. A tutor may teach research method, interrogate a research question until it is narrow enough to answer, explain what each assessment criterion is actually asking for, read a draft the student has written and say which criterion is underserved and why, teach the statistics or the referencing conventions the task needs, and ask the questions that make a student notice a flaw in their own argument. All of that is teaching.

The prohibited territory is narrow and absolute. A tutor does not supply sentences for inclusion, does not restructure a draft by rewriting it, does not provide data the student did not collect, and does not produce any part of a submitted document. The student's work must be the student's own, and the distinction is not a matter of degree: feedback describes what is wrong; authorship fixes it for them.

There is a related constraint worth knowing in Abu Dhabi, reported by Gulf News: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that also restricts serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it, but the direction of travel is clear enough that 'your child's own teacher, privately' should never be the proposition.

sections.heading: KHDA, the inspection bands and what a school report really tells you
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a judgement on a six-band scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are regulated by ADEK, Sharjah by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the federal Ministry of Education.

The scale of the Dubai market explains why the inspection report matters. Government figures for 2024-25 record 387,441 pupils across 227 private schools offering seventeen different curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26 per cent, American at 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. KHDA has also confirmed seven new private schools for the 2026-27 intake, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places.

What a band does not tell you is how your child is doing. An Outstanding school contains students who are struggling and a Good school contains students achieving sevens. The useful reading of an inspection report is diagnostic rather than evaluative: look at the judgement for the specific phase and subject your child sits, because a school can be strong in primary and merely acceptable in post-16 science, and that distinction is what determines whether a tutor is worth hiring.

Two structural points follow from this for DAMAC Hills 2 families. First, read the report for the school, phase and subject, not the headline band. Second, no tutoring provider holds KHDA approval in any meaningful sense. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, with initial approval, a six-month window to complete the steps and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram has no Dubai premises and holds no such permit, and any provider describing its tutors as carrying KHDA approval is making a claim worth checking.

sections.heading: Mandatory UAE subjects the tutoring budget usually forgets
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of which international curriculum it is licensed for. KHDA's mandatory-subjects guidelines required implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. These subjects appear on the report card and consume timetable hours, and families focused on Chemistry and Mathematics routinely discover the Arabic grade late.

The organisational rules are specific. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language is used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. Schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least twenty-five minutes. There is also a content constraint that matters for tutoring: for these subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, so support here means helping a student with the school's own material rather than introducing an alternative course.

Schools must also ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a checkable credential and a reasonable question to ask the school. For a DAMAC Hills 2 family the practical planning point is simple: when you build an evening timetable around two tutored subjects, leave a slot for Arabic rather than discovering in May that it needed one.

sections.heading: When no local tutor covers the subject, and what happens then
paragraphs: Every tutoring provider has coverage limits and almost none publish them. The honest position for a DAMAC Hills 2 request is that common subjects at common levels are matched quickly, and narrow combinations are not. IGCSE Mathematics, the three separate sciences and English are deep pools. Diploma Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Economics, Higher Level Psychology, Business Management, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and second languages at Higher Level are thin pools everywhere, not only in Dubai.

Because lessons are delivered online over live video rather than at an address, the pool is not restricted to tutors living within driving distance of Al Qudra Road. That is the practical argument for the format. A DAMAC Hills 2 family requesting Higher Level Chemistry is choosing from specialists who teach that specification, instead of from the small set of people willing to drive out to the far side of Dubailand on a Tuesday evening.

When a specialist genuinely is not available for a requested slot, the useful response is to say so and offer the alternatives rather than fill the slot with a generalist. The alternatives are usually a different time with the right tutor, a short diagnostic block with a related-subject specialist to establish exactly what is needed, or a wait with a stated date. A family that is told the truth can plan; a family given a generalist discovers the mismatch three weeks later, having lost three weeks.

One further point on legality, because it bears on availability. Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen and university students. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its app, website or e-services. Those offering private tuition without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anyone.

process.title: Tell us the syllabus, not just the subject
process.description: The first message should name the school, the year group, the board and the code if you have it, and the two or three specific topics where marks are being lost. A request that says 'IGCSE Chemistry 0620 Extended, Year 11, struggling with moles and electrolysis' is matched accurately. One that says 'science help' is not.

process.title: One diagnostic session on real work
process.description: The first session is spent on an unseen paper or a marked school assessment rather than on teaching. The tutor marks it against the official criteria and reports which of the four failure modes is in play. That single hour usually changes the plan a parent arrived with, and it is the cheapest useful thing available.

process.title: Fix the slot around the Dubailand bus
process.description: Sessions are agreed in Gulf Standard Time around the actual arrival of the school bus in DAMAC Hills 2, not around a nominal school finish time. Most families here settle on 17:30 or 18:30 on weekdays, with weekend mornings used for longer internal assessment or exam-paper blocks.

process.title: Work a plan built backwards from the exam
process.description: The tutor builds the term plan from the entry deadline and exam window backwards, interleaved with the school's own assessment dates. Content work front-loads; timed practice takes over in the final eight to ten weeks. The plan is rewritten after each school assessment rather than followed blindly.

process.title: Review the evidence, not the feeling
process.description: Every six to eight weeks the question is whether marks on comparable tasks have moved. If they have not, the diagnosis was wrong and the plan or the tutor changes. A free trial session is available before any commitment so a family can test the match before spending; the trial length and terms are stated when it is booked.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus code
whyPoints.description: A tutor is assigned against the specification your child's school entered them for, including the Core or Extended tier and the board. Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 are not the same paper, and practising the wrong format is a term wasted on something that looks like progress.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery, stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons for UAE families run one to one over live video with a shared whiteboard and a recording the student keeps. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The format is published here so nobody books expecting a car.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before scheduling
whyPoints.description: The first session establishes whether the problem is content, speed, command terms or presentation. Those four need different remedies, and selling weekly tutoring for an undiagnosed problem is how families spend a year on the wrong intervention.

whyPoints.title: Prices in AED with sources

whyPoints.title: Coursework support that keeps the student safe
whyPoints.description: Internal assessment and Extended Essay work is teaching, questioning and criterion-referenced feedback on the student's own drafts. Nothing is supplied for submission. The student signs the authenticity declaration, and our role has to be compatible with that signature.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed
whyPoints.description: When no specialist is free for a requested subject and slot, we say so and give the options rather than placing a generalist. Thin-pool Higher Level subjects are named on this page so a family can plan around availability instead of discovering it later.

faqs.question: Can a DAMAC Hills 2 family book an in-home tutor through IB Gram?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits in DAMAC Hills 2 or anywhere else in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Lessons for Dubai families are delivered one to one over live video, with a shared whiteboard and a session recording the student keeps. For a community this far out on the Al Qudra side of Dubailand, the online format is also the better deal: it removes the travel premium an in-home tutor prices into the fee, and it widens the choice from whoever will drive to DAMAC Hills 2 to any specialist who teaches your child's syllabus.

faqs.question: How much do IB and IGCSE tutors cost for a DAMAC Hills 2 family?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Dubai, read in October 2026, run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor online and AED 200 to AED 450 and above for an IB or IGCSE specialist. In-home visits sit higher, at AED 180 to AED 500, because travel is priced in. Budget platforms advertise from AED 33 to AED 65, which usually buys a university student rather than a specialist. Those figures are the market, taken from providers' own pages and Bestimate's 2026 rate table, not an IB Gram price list. Ask for the trial session before fixing a budget.

faqs.question: Which schools do DAMAC Hills 2 children usually travel to?
faqs.answer: The nearest provision sits in Dubai Investments Park and the inner Dubailand corridor: Greenfield International School, Durham School Dubai, South View School, The Aquila School and Jebel Ali School in neighbouring DAMAC Hills, with Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City. A second corridor runs north to Motor City and Dubai Sports City for GEMS Metropole, Victory Heights Primary and Bradenton Preparatory, and to Arabian Ranches for Jumeirah English Speaking School and Ranches Primary. These names are local context only; IB Gram has no relationship with any of them.

faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start in DAMAC Hills 2?
faqs.answer: Most families here settle on 17:30 or 18:30 on weekdays. The secondary bus run from Dubai Investments Park, Motor City or Arabian Ranches rarely takes under forty minutes and often longer in term time, so a 16:00 slot that suits an inner-city community does not work in DAMAC Hills 2. Because lessons are online, the session begins when the child is home and fed rather than when a car completes a journey. Weekend mornings are the usual choice for longer internal assessment or full timed-paper blocks.

faqs.question: My child's class marks are fine but mocks are poor. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly the difference between scaffolded and unscaffolded assessment. Class tasks come with structure, hints and a known topic; mock papers come with none of those. The most common cause in Dubai cohorts is content that is understood but not retrievable under time pressure, which feels to the student like not understanding the material. It is fixed by timed practice with an enforced stop, not by reteaching. A single marked unseen paper will usually distinguish this from the three other causes: unsecured content, misread command terms, or working shown too thinly to earn method marks.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's Diploma internal assessment without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor may teach research method, narrow an over-broad research question, explain what each assessment criterion is asking for, read a draft the student has written and name which criterion is underserved, and teach the statistics or referencing the task requires. A tutor may not supply sentences for inclusion, rewrite a draft, provide data the student did not collect, or produce any part of what is submitted. The student signs an authenticity declaration, and any provider offering a finished assessment is creating an expulsion risk for your child.

faqs.question: Does my child's IGCSE syllabus code actually matter when choosing a tutor?
faqs.answer: It matters more than the subject name. Cambridge 0620 Chemistry and Pearson Edexcel 4CH1 assess the same discipline with different paper structures, different practical arrangements and different question styles. Cambridge also tiers several subjects into Core and Extended, where Core caps the grade at C. A tutor working from the wrong specification will teach competent chemistry and the wrong exam. The code is on the school's entry sheet or available from the examinations officer, and it is the first thing worth establishing before any booking.

faqs.question: Why does the entry deadline matter if the exam is months away?
faqs.answer: Because the entry deadline, not the exam, is the point after which choices close. Cambridge publishes final entries for the March 2027 series as due 27 November 2026, with the exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027 and forecast grades due 27 February. That is an entry deadline ten weeks before the first paper. Tier changes, subject changes and private-candidate arrangements all have to be settled before it. Working backwards from the exam window rather than forwards from today is the planning habit that prevents a family discovering a closed door in February.

faqs.question: Are there Arabic and Islamic Education requirements my child has to meet in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, and KHDA required implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA mandates separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibits combined classes. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. For these subjects, additional or different content without Ministry of Education permission is prohibited, so support means working with the school's own material.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram approved by KHDA to tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider claiming that status is worth questioning. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, involving initial approval, a six-month window to complete the steps and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram has no Dubai premises and holds no such permit. Separately, individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need a MoHRE private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is granted free of charge for two years.

faqs.question: What do the KHDA inspection bands tell me about whether my child needs a tutor?
faqs.answer: Less than parents assume. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually and publishes a judgement across six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. That band describes the school, not your child: Outstanding schools contain students who are struggling and Good schools produce sevens. The useful reading is granular. Look at the judgement for the specific phase and subject your child sits, because a school can be strong in primary and merely acceptable in post-16 sciences, and that gap is where tutoring either earns its fee or does not.

faqs.question: Which Higher Level subjects are hardest to find a tutor for?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Economics, Higher Level Psychology, Business Management, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and second languages at Higher Level are thin pools everywhere, not only in Dubai. IGCSE Mathematics, the three separate sciences and English are deep pools and are matched quickly. When a specialist is not free for a requested slot, the options are a different time with the right tutor, a short diagnostic block with a related-subject specialist, or a wait with a stated date. We say which applies rather than placing a generalist.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week should a Year 11 student in DAMAC Hills 2 have?
faqs.answer: One session a week per weak subject through most of Year 11, rising to two or three a week in the final six to eight weeks when the work shifts to timed papers. More than that early in the year usually reduces the student's own independent practice, which is the activity that actually moves an IGCSE grade. The honest sequencing is one diagnostic hour, then weekly work on the diagnosed problem, then an exam-run intensive. Reviewing marks on comparable tasks every six to eight weeks tells you whether the cadence is right.

faqs.question: Does the UAE Ministry of Education equivalency process affect IGCSE subject choices?
faqs.answer: It can. For the British track, the Ministry requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. That makes a Core-tier cap or a dropped subject a decision with later consequences. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong. Verify your own case with the Ministry rather than with any tutoring page.

faqs.question: What happens in the very first session, and is there a trial?
faqs.answer: The first session is diagnostic rather than instructional. The student works an unseen paper or brings a marked school assessment, and the tutor marks it against the official criteria and reports which failure mode is in play: unsecured content, poor retrieval under time, misread command terms or thin working. A free trial session is available before any commitment, with its length and conditions stated at the time of booking so there is nothing to discover afterwards. Most families change the plan they arrived with after that hour.

dubai/damac-hills-2.closingHeading: Start with the gap, not with the timetable
dubai/damac-hills-2.closingBody: The useful first step for a DAMAC Hills 2 family is not booking a weekly slot. It is finding out, from one marked piece of real work, which part of the course your child is carrying alone and failing to carry. Send the school, the year group, the board and the syllabus code if you have it, plus the two or three topics where marks are going. We will match a specialist who teaches that exact specification and run a diagnostic session over live video at a time that works after the Dubailand bus. Pick by subject and level first, by availability second: the constraint in this neighbourhood is almost never the tutor, it is the hour between the school run and dinner.

intro.heading: Why the Deira afternoon decides the tutoring plan
paragraphs: Deira is one of the few parts of Dubai where almost nobody attends school inside the neighbourhood. The private secondary schools that Deira families use sit in Al Garhoud, Dubai Festival City, Oud Metha, Al Mamzar, Al Qusais and Muhaisnah. That means the day ends with a journey, and the journey crosses one of a small number of pinch points: Al Maktoum Bridge, Al Garhoud Bridge, Al Shindagha Tunnel, or the Red Line between Union and Salah Al Din. The journey is short in kilometres and long in minutes, and it lands in the exact window when every other school in the city is emptying.

This matters more than it sounds. A family that books a lesson at 4:00pm and finds the child walks in at 3:55pm has not bought an hour of teaching; it has bought an hour of a tired child being asked questions. A family that books at 5:30pm has bought a usable hour but has pushed homework to 7:00pm and reading to 9:00pm. The difference between those two bookings is not the tutor's quality. It is whether anyone thought about the drive.

The second thing that shapes Deira is the mix of boards. In one apartment block you will find a Year 11 student sitting Cambridge IGCSE, a Year 11 student sitting Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, a Grade 10 student on CBSE, and a DP1 student who moved up through the Middle Years Programme. Those four children have different papers, different command terms, different coursework deadlines and different exam months. A tutor who treats them as one cohort will teach to the middle and help none of them.

Third, Deira households are frequently multi-generational and often multilingual, with Arabic, Malayalam, Urdu, Tagalog or Russian spoken at home alongside English. Dubai private schools must run Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in those subjects because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. For a Deira family that is not a footnote. It is three or four extra lessons a week sitting on top of a full IGCSE or Diploma load.

What follows is written for that reality. We start with the clock, because the clock is what ends most tutoring arrangements in this part of Dubai. Then session length, then what the market charges in dirhams, then the honest comparison between a tutor who has to drive here and a specialist who appears on screen at the agreed minute. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India, and every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video. That constraint is also the reason a Deira family can work with a Chemistry Higher Level specialist rather than whoever happens to live twenty minutes away.

dubai/deira.programmesIntro: Deira students sit across the IB continuum and both IGCSE boards, often inside the same family. These are the programmes we cover and what each one asks of a student living on this side of the creek.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an internally assessed component marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB. The workload is not evenly spread: the first half of DP1 is content, the second half of DP1 and the start of DP2 is coursework, and the final six months is past-paper technique under time pressure.
programmes.countryNote: For Deira families the Diploma usually means a commute to Dubai Festival City or Oud Metha, which puts the end of the school day close to 3:30pm. We hold Diploma slots from 4:15pm so that a Higher Level session is not the first thing a student does after a bridge crossing, and we keep a second weekly slot free in coursework months.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, lettered A to D, with task-specific descriptors rather than percentage marks. Students who have come from a national board often lose marks on criterion D, which asks for reflection and evaluation, simply because no previous school asked them to write in that register.
programmes.countryNote: Deira's MYP students are frequently mid-continuum transfers who joined from a CBSE or a national-curriculum school. The gap is rarely content. It is the criterion language, the research expectations and the Personal Project in the final year, which is self-managed and lands in the same term as mock examinations.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two boards, two sets of syllabus codes, two different habits. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series with Core and Extended tiers in many subjects. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November and uses a 9-1 grade scale on most specifications. The paper structures differ enough that past-paper practice on the wrong board is close to wasted time.
programmes.countryNote: Deira families should confirm the board before booking anything. Two schools in the same district can teach the same subject under different codes, and the Core and Extended decision in Cambridge subjects caps the achievable grade. We ask for the syllabus code at the enquiry stage for exactly this reason.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry rather than discrete subjects, with no external examinations. Tutoring at this stage is about reading fluency, number sense and the writing stamina that the Middle Years Programme will assume. Short sessions work better than long ones, and progress is measured by what the child can do unaided.
programmes.countryNote: Primary-age Deira children are often the easiest to schedule and the hardest to schedule around siblings. We keep PYP sessions to 30 or 45 minutes and place them before the older child's slot, so one device and one quiet room can serve two children in the same evening.

dubai/deira.subjectsIntro: Subject choice in Deira skews towards the sciences, mathematics and business, partly because of the engineering, trade and medical professions the district's working parents come from. These are the subjects we are asked for most often here.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic route. Higher Level adds proof, complex numbers and a substantially harder calculus strand. Marks are lost on unjustified steps rather than wrong answers: an examiner awards method marks for reasoning that is written down, not reasoning that happened in the student's head.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling route, with statistics, finance and the graphical display calculator doing real work. Students arriving from a traditional algebra-heavy background often underestimate it, then lose marks on interpretation questions that ask what a number means in context.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and electricity dominate the marks and the losses. At IGCSE the recurring failure is circuit analysis under exam conditions; at Higher Level it is the mathematical fluency needed to turn a physical situation into an equation quickly enough to finish the paper.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and the quantitative paper are where grades move. The internally assessed investigation rewards a narrow, well-controlled question with honest uncertainty treatment, which is the opposite of the ambitious project most students first propose.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A vocabulary subject disguised as a science. Students who write fluent prose still lose marks by answering around a command term rather than inside it. Higher Level adds depth in biochemistry and physiology that cannot be revised late.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools, theory and a real organisation. The internally assessed research project needs a focused question and genuine source material, and students in trading families often have better access to that material than they realise. Higher Level adds extension topics and a case-study paper.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the fastest grade gain available. A correctly labelled diagram with axes, curves and shifts earns marks that prose cannot. Higher Level adds quantitative questions and a policy paper that rewards precise use of real examples.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Two external papers and oral assessment. The individual oral asks the student to connect a global issue to two texts, one of them in translation, and it is prepared work rather than improvisation. Structure and evidence selection carry more weight than style.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic as a first language
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must run Arabic for all students, in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab learners. The two streams have different expectations and different languages of instruction, and a tutor who teaches the wrong stream will produce work the school cannot use.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Taken alongside Extended Mathematics by students heading for Higher Level maths or engineering. It covers calculus, vectors and trigonometric identities a year early, and it is the single best preparation for Analysis and Approaches available at age sixteen.

dubai/deira.regionsTitle: Deira and the surrounding districts we cover
dubai/deira.regionsIntro: These are the neighbourhoods either side of Deira whose families share the same school belt and the same afternoon traffic. The detail matters because the start time that works in Al Mamzar does not work in Al Qusais.

regions.name: Bur Dubai
regions.note: Across the creek through Al Shindagha Tunnel. Families here reach the Oud Metha school belt faster than Deira families do, which usually buys a 3:45pm slot rather than a 4:15pm one.

regions.name: Karama
regions.note: Dense apartment living with the Oud Metha schools within a short drive. The constraint is rarely travel and often study space: one quiet room shared between siblings sets the realistic session length.

regions.name: Oud Metha
regions.note: The school belt itself, with several long-established British and Indian-curriculum schools inside walking distance of each other. Early slots are possible here in a way they are not elsewhere in old Dubai.

regions.name: Al Mankhool
regions.note: Apartment blocks with a mix of British-curriculum and Indian-curriculum families. Afternoon arrivals are early, so a 3:45pm session holds without pushing homework into the evening.

regions.name: Al Garhoud
regions.note: Close to the airport and to Dubai Festival City. The Al Garhoud Bridge approach is the pinch point, and families who miss the early window often find 4:30pm is the first honest slot.

regions.name: Al Mamzar
regions.note: Coastal and quieter, with schools on the Sharjah side of the district within reach. Shorter journeys mean an earlier start, which is useful for students carrying both a full IGCSE load and the mandatory Arabic stream.

regions.name: Hor Al Anz
regions.note: Adjacent to Deira proper and served by the same roads. Multi-generational households are common, and sessions placed before the evening meal are more reliable than sessions placed after it.

regions.name: Al Muteena
regions.note: Central Deira, walking distance from the Red Line at Salah Al Din. Students who travel to school by metro arrive home later than their classmates, and the lesson slot has to reflect that.

regions.name: Al Qusais
regions.note: A long corridor along Damascus Street with several large schools. The afternoon traffic here is the heaviest in the district, and 4:30pm is a more realistic first slot than 4:00pm.

regions.name: Al Nahda
regions.note: On the Dubai-Sharjah boundary, where some families attend schools regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority rather than KHDA. The regulator differs, and so do the term dates to plan revision around.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai Festival City, Al Garhoud and Al Mamzar
schoolClusters.note: The school belt most Deira secondary students travel to. It spans an IB continuum school, long-standing British-curriculum schools and Indian-curriculum schools, which is why four exam boards appear in one Deira apartment block. Students we support attend schools in this belt.
schools: Al Ittihad Private School, Al Mamzar

schoolClusters.city: Oud Metha, Al Mankhool and the Bur Dubai side
schoolClusters.note: Reached through Al Shindagha Tunnel or over Al Maktoum Bridge. These schools run IGCSE and A Level, or CBSE to Grade 12, and the mix means a single tutor rarely covers two children in the same household without checking the syllabus codes first.
schools: The Indian High School, Oud Metha

schoolClusters.city: Al Qusais and Muhaisnah
schoolClusters.note: The eastern end of the Deira school run, along Damascus Street and Algeria Street. Large cohorts, strong science uptake, and the heaviest afternoon traffic of any direction out of Deira. Session timing here is set by the road, not by the school bell.
