dubai/deira.modesIntro: Three formats work for Deira households, and the choice is usually dictated by how many children are being taught and how much of the week is already committed to the mandatory UAE subjects.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, fixed slot
modes.description: One subject, one tutor, the same time each week over live video. This is the format that holds across a term because it becomes part of the household routine rather than something negotiated weekly. For Deira families the fixed slot is usually placed fifteen to thirty minutes after the realistic arrival time, not at the school bell.
bullets: Same tutor, same hour, same subject each week
Slot set after arrival, with a fifteen-minute buffer
Written note to the parent after each session
Reviewed against school assessment data every six weeks

modes.title: Two shorter sessions in a coursework term
modes.description: During the months when an internally assessed investigation, a research project or a Personal Project is live, a single long session is the wrong shape. Two shorter sessions in the same week give the student time to act on feedback between them, which is what the assessment criteria actually reward.
bullets: Two 45-minute slots rather than one 90-minute slot
The student does the work between sessions, not during them
Feedback against the published criteria, by letter
No part of the assessed work is written by the tutor

modes.title: Intensive block before a paper
modes.description: A short, dense sequence in the four to six weeks before an exam series, built around past papers and mark schemes rather than new content. It suits students who are already close to a grade boundary and need technique, timing and command-term discipline rather than teaching.
bullets: Built from the correct board's papers, not a generic set
Timed conditions from the second session onwards
Marked against the official scheme, with the student marking too
Finishes when the series starts, not before

sections.heading: What a search for IB and IGCSE tutors in Deira usually means
paragraphs: Parents in Deira who search for a tutor are nearly always solving one of four problems, and they are different problems with different answers. The first is a grade that has slipped on a school report and nobody can say exactly why. The second is a specific topic that has defeated a child for months, usually electricity in physics, organic chemistry, or the move from arithmetic to algebraic reasoning in mathematics. The third is coursework: an internally assessed investigation or a research project that has a school deadline the family only learned about last week. The fourth is time, not understanding, where the child knows the material and cannot finish a paper.

Each of those needs a different first session. A slipped grade needs diagnosis before teaching, because the cause is often two topics back from where the symptom appeared. A single hard topic needs direct instruction and then independent practice. Coursework needs process coaching against the published criteria, with the student doing every piece of the writing. A timing problem needs past papers under the clock and almost no explanation at all.

The honest answer to "how many sessions will this take" depends entirely on which of the four it is. A timing problem can move inside three weeks. A two-year gap in algebraic fluency cannot. Anyone who quotes a number of sessions before looking at a marked script is guessing, and the guess is usually optimistic because an optimistic guess closes the sale.

What we do first is ask for a marked paper or a school report, and we ask which board and which syllabus code. In Deira that question does real work, because two children on the same street may be sitting the same subject under Cambridge and Pearson specifications that mark differently. Starting without that detail wastes the first two sessions on discovery that a document would have answered.
bullets: A slipped grade is a diagnostic problem, not a teaching problem
A hard topic needs instruction then unaided practice
Coursework needs criteria coaching, never written help
A timing problem needs the clock, not more explanation

sections.heading: The Deira afternoon, bridge by bridge
paragraphs: Deira sits on the wrong side of the creek from much of the school belt, and the crossing points are few: Al Maktoum Bridge, Al Garhoud Bridge, Al Shindagha Tunnel, Floating Bridge during its operating hours, and the Red Line underneath. Every one of those is busiest between 2:00pm and 4:00pm because that is when the schools empty, and the time penalty is not evenly distributed. A family whose school sits in Al Mamzar may be home in fifteen minutes. A family whose school sits in Al Qusais may take fifty.

The practical consequence is that there is no single correct start time for Deira. There is a correct start time for your journey. We ask three questions at the enquiry stage: which school, how the child travels, and what time they actually walked in last Tuesday. The third question is the one that matters, because the school bus timetable and the school bus reality are not the same document.

Once the arrival time is known, the slot is set with a buffer. Fifteen minutes is enough for a child who travels by car with a parent. Thirty is closer to right for a child on a school bus with several stops, or a teenager using the metro from Salah Al Din or Union. The buffer is not politeness. A student who sits down out of breath spends the first ten minutes of a paid hour catching up with themselves.

The table below is for planning, not a published schedule. It shows how the direction of travel changes the first honest slot. Families who want a session earlier than the table suggests are usually better served by a weekend morning, when the road is empty and the child is not already tired.

sections.heading: Choosing between a 45, 60 and 90-minute session
paragraphs: Session length is treated as a billing question and it is really a learning question. A 45-minute session can teach one idea properly and check it. A 60-minute session can teach an idea, practise it and leave with a task. A 90-minute session can work through a full past paper under timed conditions and then mark it, which is a genuinely different activity from teaching. Choosing the wrong length is one of the quieter ways families waste money.

For a Deira household arriving home at four, a 90-minute weekday session is usually a mistake for anyone below Year 11. Attention does not survive it after a bridge crossing, and the second half gets spent re-explaining the first. The same 90 minutes on a Saturday morning is a different proposition entirely, which is why we move paper practice to weekends for most students and keep weekdays for teaching and checking.

Younger students, and students carrying the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education load on top of a full international curriculum, do better with two 45-minute sessions than one 90. The reason is not stamina. It is that progress between sessions is where learning actually happens, and two gaps produce more independent practice than one.

The exception is coursework. An internally assessed investigation needs the student working alone and the tutor reviewing afterwards, so the session length is less important than the interval between sessions. Short and frequent beats long and rare in every coursework month.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs around Deira in dirhams
paragraphs: Most tutoring pages in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in. The figures below are market rates in dirhams, taken from what providers in this market publish themselves, and they are presented as the market rather than as an IB Gram price list. Rates move with level, format and how specialised the subject is, and the specialist end of the range is driven by scarcity rather than by anything a parent can see.

The pattern across the market is consistent. University-student and generalist online tutoring starts low, around AED 45 to AED 65 an hour at the budget end, with one platform advertising from roughly AED 33 to AED 52. Qualified subject tutors working online sit in a wide middle band of roughly AED 150 to AED 300, with one agency publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits carry the travel inside the rate and run higher, commonly AED 180 to AED 350 and up to AED 500 for a specialist. Named or examiner-level tutors are quoted as high as AED 650 by one provider.

Monthly packages circulate too: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Set against private school fees in Dubai, where KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase for the 2026-27 academic year, a single weekly tutoring hour is a smaller line item than most families expect, and a four-subject plan is a larger one.

What we will not do is quote a number before knowing the subject, the level and whether the student needs teaching or technique. A Higher Level Chemistry specialist in a coursework month and a Year 10 mathematics confidence rebuild are different pieces of work at different rates. The trial session exists so that both sides can see the problem before anyone commits to a term.

sections.heading: A home tutor in a Deira apartment against one-to-one online
paragraphs: The phrase parents type is "home tutor", and it deserves a straight answer rather than a redirect. An in-home tutor in Deira is a real option in this market. Someone drives to the apartment, teaches at the dining table and leaves. It works well for younger children, for families who want a visible adult in the room, and for households where screens are already a battleground. It is also the most expensive format per hour of actual teaching, because the travel is inside the price and the traffic is inside the travel.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, and the reason is not cost. It is tutor pool. A Deira family looking for a Chemistry Higher Level specialist who understands criterion-level feedback on an internally assessed investigation is looking for a small number of people. Requiring that person to also live within a twenty-minute drive of Deira in the late afternoon reduces the candidates to nearly none, and the family ends up with availability instead of expertise.

There are real trade-offs and we would rather write them down. A tutor in the room can see a student's written working upside down on the page, can take a pen and annotate, and does not depend on a connection. Online, the equivalent requires a shared screen, a document camera or a phone propped over the page, and a tutor who insists on seeing the working rather than hearing the answer. Those habits are learnable and we expect them, but they are habits rather than automatic.

What online genuinely wins on, in this neighbourhood specifically, is the clock and the catalogue. No crossing of Al Maktoum Bridge is required, the session starts at the agreed minute, a missed week can be rescheduled to a weekend morning rather than lost, and the specialist is chosen on subject and level rather than postcode.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the shortened day and the post-Iftar slot
paragraphs: The UAE academic year has a shape that tutoring plans built elsewhere ignore. Schools shorten the day during Ramadan, the working rhythm of the household changes, and the hours a teenager is alert move several hours later. For a Deira family that may be observing the fast, a 4:30pm session in the second week of Ramadan is close to useless. A 9:00pm session after Iftar can be one of the most productive hours of the year.

The practical move is to decide in advance rather than improvise. Three or four weeks before Ramadan begins, we ask families to pick one of three patterns: keep the existing slot and accept a shorter, lighter session; move the slot to after Iftar for the month; or pause the subject and bank the hours for the fortnight after Eid, which is often when a mock-exam window lands. All three are reasonable. Deciding in week two of Ramadan is what produces missed sessions.

The same planning applies to the rest of the calendar. Term dates in Dubai schools and in Sharjah schools do not always align, which matters for Al Nahda families whose children cross the boundary. Mid-term breaks, National Day, Eid holidays and the long summer all land differently against the two exam seasons, and a revision plan that assumes a European academic year will put its intensive block in the wrong month.

One more detail specific to this district: many Deira households travel in summer for extended periods, sometimes six or seven weeks. A student who stops in late June and restarts in September has lost the gap between content and recall that August is good for. Online delivery means the schedule can follow the family, which is the single most common reason Deira parents give for choosing it.
bullets: Pick the Ramadan pattern three weeks early, not during
Post-Iftar slots work; late-afternoon slots usually do not
Dubai and Sharjah term dates do not always align
A long summer away needs a plan, not a pause

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the paper: the Cambridge and Pearson series
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes an exam calendar, which is strange, because the calendar is what decides when tutoring should start. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year. Those two facts alone should set the shape of a two-year plan.

The deadlines that actually catch families out sit months before the paper. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series put the examination period from 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. Read that order again: entries close more than two months before the first paper. A student who decides in January to sit a subject has usually missed the door.

Cambridge also allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. That is a real risk for a family revising from a timetable found online rather than the one the school issued.

For the IB May session, which is the one Dubai schools sit, we work backwards from the school's own internal deadlines rather than from any published date. IB session and results dates are not confirmed in this project and we will not print one. The school's IB coordinator holds the internal deadlines for every internally assessed component, and those are the dates a tutoring plan has to respect.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch on internally assessed work
paragraphs: This is the part of the market where the real damage happens. One provider found in this SERP sells completed Internal Assessments outright. That is an academic-integrity breach, it triggers an IB malpractice investigation, and the student carries the consequence, not the seller. A Deira family handing over money for finished coursework is buying a risk to their child's diploma.

The boundary is not vague. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain the assessment criteria, discuss whether a research question is viable, point out that a method will not generate usable data, read a draft and say which criterion is under-served, and ask the questions that make a student notice their own gap. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite paragraphs, generate data, choose the question on the student's behalf, or edit a draft into a finished state. Everything submitted must be the student's own work, and the student signs to that effect.

In practice the honest version is slower and produces better marks. A student who is told that criterion C is weak and then has to work out why learns something that transfers to the next piece of assessed work. A student handed a stronger paragraph learns nothing and has to repeat the exercise under examination conditions with nobody to hand them anything.

We also will not supply syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those belong to the boards. We reference them, we tell you the official source, and we work from what the school has legitimately issued. Any tutoring service offering a library of board material has already told you something about how it operates.

No part of an assessed piece may be supplied, rewritten or edited to completion

sections.heading: Starting, and what happens when the hour you want is gone
paragraphs: The first step is not a payment. It is a document. Send the most recent marked paper or school report, name the board and the syllabus code, and tell us the realistic arrival time on a weekday. With those three things a sensible first session can be designed; without them the first session becomes an interview.

The trial session is a diagnostic. The tutor works with your child for an agreed length of time and then writes you a short note saying what the actual problem looks like, which is often not the problem the school report named. Occasionally that note says the child does not need a tutor and needs a fortnight of structured independent practice instead. We would rather say that than sell a term.

Availability is the thing nobody in this market discloses, so here it is plainly. The late-afternoon weekday slots between 4:00pm and 6:00pm are the ones every family in Dubai wants, and for scarce subjects at Higher Level they do go. When the slot you want is unavailable, there are three honest options: take a different hour with the specialist you want, take the hour you want with a different tutor whose subject fit is good rather than perfect, or take a weekend morning. We will tell you which of the three we think is better for your child, and the answer is usually the weekend morning.

For very narrow requirements, a Higher Level subject with a coursework deadline inside six weeks, matching can take longer than the forty-eight hours families expect. We say so at the enquiry rather than accepting the booking and finding someone approximate. A Deira parent who has already been through one bad arrangement is rarely looking for speed.
bullets: Send a marked script, the syllabus code and the real arrival time
The trial produces a written diagnosis, not a sales call
4:00pm to 6:00pm is the contested window across the whole city

process.title: Tell us the journey, not just the school
process.description: We ask which school, how your child travels and what time they actually arrived home last week. In Deira that single answer decides the slot, because the difference between an Al Mamzar arrival and an Al Qusais arrival is most of an hour.

process.title: Send one marked script
process.description: A recent marked paper or report tells a specialist more than a phone call does. It shows where marks were lost, whether the loss is content or technique, and whether the board is Cambridge or Pearson. Without it the first session is spent on discovery.

process.title: Meet the tutor in a diagnostic session
process.description: The first session is scheduled at your chosen slot and is used to test the hypothesis from the script. You receive a written note afterwards naming the actual gap, the order to address it in, and a realistic view of how long that takes.

process.title: Fix a weekly slot and a review date
process.description: Once the format is settled we fix the hour, the subject and a six-week review point tied to the school's next assessment. The review uses school data rather than a feeling, and it is where we decide to continue, change format, or stop.

process.title: Re-shape around the calendar
process.description: Coursework months, Ramadan, mock windows and the examination series each need a different session shape. We change the plan ahead of those months rather than during them, which is the difference between a plan that survives to March and one that quietly stops in January.

whyPoints.title: The slot is built around the school run
whyPoints.description: Nothing else on this page matters if the lesson starts before your child is home. We set the time from the real arrival, add a buffer for the bus or the metro, and move paper practice to weekends where a weekday hour cannot hold it.

whyPoints.title: The syllabus code comes first
whyPoints.description: Two Deira schools can teach the same subject under different board specifications. We confirm the code before matching, because past-paper work on the wrong board is close to wasted time and the Core or Extended decision caps the grade.

whyPoints.title: One tutor, one student, every session
whyPoints.description: No group classes and no rotating tutors. The person who ran the diagnostic is the person teaching in week nine, which is what makes a six-week review meaningful rather than a guess by someone new to the student.

whyPoints.title: Rates in dirhams, sourced to the market
whyPoints.description: Every figure on this page is attributed to the provider that published it, in the currency Dubai families actually use. We do not quote a price before seeing the problem, and we do not present somebody else's rate card as our own.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line is written down
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, explains criteria and gives feedback on work the student has done. No part of an assessed piece is supplied or edited to completion, and no board material is redistributed. That boundary is stated here so you can hold us to it.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits are disclosed up front
whyPoints.description: When a Higher Level specialist is not free in the hour you want, we say so and offer the three real alternatives. Nobody in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is why so many families discover one after paying.

faqs.question: What time can a tutoring session realistically start for a family in Deira?
faqs.answer: It depends on the direction of the school run rather than the school bell. Families whose children attend school in Al Mamzar or Hor Al Anz are often home by 3:20pm and a 3:45pm start holds. Families travelling back from Al Qusais, Muhaisnah or across Al Garhoud Bridge are more realistically looking at 4:15pm or 4:30pm. We ask what time your child actually walked in last week, add a buffer of fifteen to thirty minutes, and set the slot from that. A session that begins before the child is settled loses its first ten minutes every week.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to our apartment in Deira?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video at a fixed weekly time. The reason is tutor pool rather than cost: a Higher Level Chemistry or Analysis and Approaches specialist who can give criterion-level coursework feedback is a small group of people, and requiring them to also live within an afternoon drive of Deira would mean choosing on availability instead of expertise.

faqs.question: How much do private tutors charge per hour in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Dubai span a wide band. Budget online tutoring from university students is advertised from roughly AED 45 to AED 65 an hour, with one platform quoting from about AED 33. Qualified subject tutors working online sit around AED 150 to AED 300, with one agency publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home visits run AED 180 to AED 500 because travel is inside the rate, and one provider quotes AED 650 for named premium tutors. Those are other providers' published figures, not ours.

faqs.question: My child's school is in Oud Metha but we live in Deira. Does that change anything?
faqs.answer: It changes the clock and it changes the board you need to check. The journey crosses Al Shindagha Tunnel or Al Maktoum Bridge at the worst hour of the day, so a 4:00pm start is usually more honest than 3:30pm. The Oud Metha school belt also contains British-curriculum and Indian-curriculum schools with different age-16 examinations, so the first question we ask is which specification your child sits. Past-paper practice on the wrong board teaches the wrong habits and is hard to undo late.

faqs.question: Should we book 45, 60 or 90 minutes a week?
faqs.answer: Sixty minutes is the standard weekly subject slot and suits most students. Forty-five works better on weekdays for younger children or for anyone arriving home after a long school run, because attention after a bridge crossing does not survive ninety minutes. Ninety minutes is the right length for a full timed past paper plus marking, and that belongs on a weekend morning. In a coursework term, two forty-five-minute sessions in the same week beat one long session, because the student needs time to act on feedback between them.

faqs.question: How do Ramadan and the UAE school calendar affect a tutoring plan in Deira?
faqs.answer: Schools shorten the day during Ramadan and the hours a teenager is alert move later, so a mid-afternoon slot that works in January often collapses in Ramadan. We ask families to choose a pattern three or four weeks ahead: keep the slot but run a shorter, lighter session; move it to after Iftar for the month; or pause and bank the hours for the fortnight after Eid, which frequently lands near a mock window. Deciding during the month is what produces missed sessions.

faqs.question: Which exam boards do Deira students actually sit?
faqs.answer: Four appear regularly inside the same apartment block. Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE at age sixteen, CBSE in the Indian-curriculum schools, and the IB continuum at the schools running the Middle Years and Diploma programmes. Cambridge runs June and November series; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in May/June and November. Because the papers, grade scales and command-term habits differ, we confirm the board and syllabus code before matching a tutor rather than after the first session.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach two children in our household at different levels?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends on the codes rather than on goodwill. A tutor covering Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 for one child and Analysis and Approaches Standard Level for another is a realistic match. A tutor covering Cambridge IGCSE Physics and CBSE Grade 10 Science is a worse one, because the papers reward different things. Where the fit does not work, two separate slots in the same evening on the same device is usually cheaper and more effective than compromising on one tutor for both.

faqs.question: What happens if the 4:30pm slot we want is already taken?
faqs.answer: The window between 4:00pm and 6:00pm on weekdays is contested across the whole of Dubai, and for scarce Higher Level subjects it does fill. There are three honest options and we will tell you which we prefer. Take a different hour with the specialist you actually want, take your preferred hour with a tutor whose subject fit is good rather than ideal, or take a weekend morning. For most students the weekend morning produces better work than a weekday slot squeezed against the school run.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an Internal Assessment without crossing the academic-honesty line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary is specific. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain each criterion and its marks, discuss whether a research question is viable, warn that a method will not produce usable data, and read a draft to say which criterion is under-served. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite paragraphs, generate data or edit a draft into a finished state. Everything submitted is the student's own work and the student declares it as such. One provider in this market sells completed coursework; that is a malpractice risk carried by your child.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit, and how would we check?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Parents can ask to see the permit and can check the application route on the MoHRE service page for private tutor licensing.

faqs.question: Does KHDA require Arabic and Islamic Education even in an IB or British school?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. For a Deira student that is several lessons a week sitting on top of a full IGCSE or Diploma load.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start tutoring if the exam series is two months away?
faqs.answer: It depends on which problem you have. If your child understands the material and cannot finish a paper, two months is plenty, because timing and command-term discipline move quickly under timed conditions. If there is a two-year gap in algebraic fluency, two months will improve things without closing it, and we will say so rather than imply otherwise. The other hard constraint is entry deadlines: Cambridge's March 2027 series closed final entries on 27 November 2026, months before the first paper, so a late decision to sit a subject may simply have missed the door.

faqs.question: How quickly can you match a tutor for a Deira family, and what if the subject is unusual?
faqs.answer: For mainstream subjects at IGCSE and Standard Level, a first session is usually arranged within a few days once we have the marked script, the syllabus code and your preferred slot. Narrow requirements take longer: a Higher Level subject with a coursework deadline inside six weeks, or a language pairing that few tutors cover, can take over a week to match properly. We say so at the enquiry stage rather than accepting the booking and finding someone approximate. Nobody in this market publishes a coverage limit, so we publish ours.

dubai/deira.closingHeading: Set the hour first, then the tutor
dubai/deira.closingBody: The arrangements that fail in Deira are almost never the ones where the tutor was wrong. They are the ones where the lesson was booked at an hour that assumed no bridge, no bus route and no mandatory Arabic lesson on a Tuesday. Start from the arrival time, add a buffer, decide whether the week needs teaching or technique, and then pick the specialist on subject and level rather than on who lives nearby. Send a recent marked script, tell us the board and the syllabus code, and we will design a first session around the afternoon your family actually has. Every lesson is one-to-one over live video, and the slot is yours for the term.

Schools teach the course well. What they do not do is choose between Higher and Standard Level for your child, or between Mathematics Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, or decide which admissions tests matter. This page covers those, then explains how one-to-one online lessons fit around them.

dubai/difc.tutorsIntro: Tutors here are matched for two different jobs: teaching a named subject at a named level, and testing whether that level is the right one. The second is a short piece of work with a student's own papers, and it is often the more valuable of the two.

intro.heading: The taught course is the easy part; the decisions are not
paragraphs: DIFC is a dense residential and commercial district built around the Gate, with apartment towers including Index, Central Park, Burj Daman, Sky Gardens, Limestone House and Liberty House, and no school campus of any kind. Its residents are disproportionately in finance, law and professional services, work long and unpredictable hours, and have children who are, on the whole, being pushed and pulled towards competitive university destinations across three continents.

That produces a very particular kind of tutoring enquiry. It is rarely that a child cannot do the work. It is that the family can see a sequence of decisions ahead of them, each one taken at an age when the student has no information, and each one capable of closing a door. Whether to take a subject at Higher Level. Which mathematics course. Whether to drop a science. Whether an admissions test matters. When a predicted grade is set and on what evidence.

Schools in Dubai teach the courses competently and, in the better cases, very well. What schools do not do, and cannot reasonably be expected to do, is make an individual judgement about one family's intended destination with the student's specific attainment pattern in front of them. A head of year advising two hundred students gives sound general advice. A family aiming at a quantitative economics department needs something narrower than general advice.

The gap matters because the decisions are asymmetric. Choosing Standard Level where Higher was achievable costs a student options and is hard to reverse after the first term. Choosing Higher Level where the foundation is not there costs them two years of grinding and often a lower point total than they would have had at Standard Level. The same asymmetry applies to the mathematics route, which is the single most consequential subject choice in the Diploma for a student heading into engineering, medicine or quantitative economics.

The second feature of DIFC households is time. These are families where both parents routinely work past 18:30, where travel is frequent, and where the evening is genuinely compressed. A 20:00 session with a Diploma student is easy to hold here, and a 16:30 session is not. Online delivery is what makes the late slot possible at all, because no tutor is driving anywhere afterwards.

Everything on this page is one-to-one tuition over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For a tower household with a late schedule and a specific academic question, that model matches on the question rather than on the postcode. It also means the people doing the matching are looking at a national pool of subject specialists rather than at whoever happens to serve the central districts on a Tuesday evening, which matters a great deal when the requirement is a single Higher Level subject at an unusual hour.

dubai/difc.programmesIntro: Each programme concentrates its decisions at a different point, and knowing when the decision falls is how a family avoids making it by default. These are the four that matter from DIFC addresses.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across three Higher and three Standard Levels, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The level split is chosen at the start of Year 12 and is difficult to change after the first term, because the Higher Level content diverges early and the internal assessment work begins.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. This page publishes no specific IB session or results date, because the IB is the only authoritative source for its own calendar and second-hand dates circulate incorrectly. Ask your child's Diploma coordinator for the registration deadlines, the internal coursework calendar and the predicted-grade timetable in writing.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Nine or ten subjects with tiering decisions in mathematics and the sciences that cap or open what follows. The IGCSE grade in a subject is the main evidence a school uses when deciding whether to approve a student for Higher Level in it two years later, which makes Year 11 more consequential than it feels.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative timetable zones and states that the correct version for the zone must be used. For a DIFC family with frequent travel, confirming your centre's own exam window early is worth doing before any holiday is booked around the exam season.

programmes.name: International A Level and AS Level
programmes.description: Three or four subjects in depth with no Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay or CAS requirement. The narrowing is both the attraction and the risk: a student who knows their direction gains depth, and a student who does not has closed several routes at sixteen.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE equivalency on the British track, one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, is required alongside five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count. Verify the current rule with the authority rather than from a tutoring page.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight. MYP grades are the evidence a school uses to advise on Diploma level choices, and the criterion that most often holds a strong student back is communication rather than knowledge, which matters because it is correctable.
programmes.countryNote: An MYP 5 student whose mathematics criterion marks are strong in knowledge and weak in investigation is not necessarily a poor candidate for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, but a school reading the overall grade may advise otherwise. This is exactly the kind of case where looking at the component detail changes the decision.

dubai/difc.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects where level and route decisions concentrate. Each note says what the Higher Level step actually adds, because that is the information the choice requires.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At Higher Level this adds proof, deeper calculus and the extended Paper 3 investigation. The entry condition in practice is automatic algebraic fluency: a student who rearranges equations with conscious effort will spend working memory on the algebra rather than on the calculus.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology throughout, with marks for interpreting results in context. Higher Level is genuinely demanding and is accepted by many quantitative departments, but some specify Analysis and Approaches, which is why the requirement has to be checked rather than assumed.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Higher Level adds content depth across organic and physical chemistry and a heavier mathematical load. It is commonly a stated requirement for medicine and related degrees, and the internal assessment demands a research question narrow enough to control with school equipment.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Higher Level physics is mathematically demanding and pairs badly with Standard Level mathematics for an engineering applicant. Fields, rotational work and the mathematics underneath them are where Standard Level students find the step up hardest.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy at Higher Level, with marks turning on command terms and data interpretation rather than volume of recall. For a medicine applicant the usual question is whether it sits alongside Chemistry at Higher Level or below it.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Higher Level adds quantitative work that catches students who chose the subject expecting essays. Diagram accuracy plus an explicit judgement sentence is what reaches the top band at either level, and the internal assessment is a portfolio of tightly limited commentaries.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the named organisation rather than general theory earns the marks. The Higher Level internal assessment is a research project requiring real organisational material, which needs planning time rather than extra teaching.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.description: Higher Level adds the essay component and more demanding analysis. For applicants to competitive humanities or law programmes, this is the subject where writing quality is visible to an admissions reader, which raises the value of sustained correction.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: The Extended or Higher tier is in practice a prerequisite for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level later, and the tier is chosen in Year 9 or 10 on evidence that is often a year stale by the time it binds.

subjects.name: IGCSE Sciences
subjects.description: Separate or triple science keeps all three sciences credible at Higher Level. Combined or double award leaves a content gap that is difficult to close while carrying five other Diploma subjects, which is the most common regret reported by Diploma families.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Immediately south-east and effectively the same district for school purposes. Both share the Financial Centre Road and Sheikh Zayed Road interchanges at the same moment each morning, which is the binding constraint on the run.

regions.name: Business Bay
regions.note: South along the canal, with a newer and more transient tower population. Families in both districts use the same inland and westward campuses and face the same afternoon return congestion.

regions.name: Zabeel and Al Jafiliya
regions.note: Immediately inland, older and lower-rise, with the Trade Centre corridor between. Journeys through here are shorter than they look but cross the busiest surface roads in the central district.

regions.name: Al Quoz and Al Quoz 4

regions.name: Sobha Hartland and Mohammed Bin Rashid City
regions.note: Hartland International School and North London Collegiate School Dubai sit here, reachable inland without joining Sheikh Zayed Road. The most reliable morning direction from a DIFC tower.

sections.heading: What the school does, and what is left to the family
paragraphs: This is the division of labour nobody writes down, and misunderstanding it is how capable students end up with a narrower set of options than they needed. Schools deliver the taught course, set internal deadlines, submit entries and predicted grades, and provide general guidance. Everything that requires a judgement about one student's particular destination sits with the family, whether or not the family realises it.

The point is not that schools are failing. A head of year advising a cohort of two hundred cannot run an individual analysis of whether a specific student's algebraic fluency supports Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level against the published requirement of a specific department three thousand miles away. That is a narrow piece of work and it takes an hour with the right papers in front of you.

The practical consequence is that the decisions get made by default. A student takes the Higher Levels their friends take, or the ones the timetable blocks allow, or the ones a teacher encouraged in passing. Two years later a department's published requirement turns out to specify something slightly different, and the position is irreversible. This is not a rare failure mode; it is the most common one in this district.

The table below sets out the tasks across the final years with who normally handles each. The right-hand column is the family's list. It is shorter than people fear and more specific than people expect, and almost all of it is information-gathering rather than expertise.

sections.heading: Higher Level versus Standard Level, component by component
paragraphs: The Higher and Standard Level distinction is described in most school handbooks as a difference of depth, which is true and not sufficient to decide anything. What a family needs is a component-level comparison: what changes in the papers, what changes in the internal assessment, what changes in the number of hours the student will spend, and what signal from prior attainment indicates a good fit.

The most under-appreciated difference is the hour cost. A Higher Level subject is taught for substantially more timetabled hours than a Standard Level one and requires proportionally more independent work, which means three Higher Levels is not three subjects plus a bit. It is the core of the week. A student taking three Higher Levels with weak independent study habits will produce worse results than the same student taking two, because the capacity constraint binds before the ability constraint does.

The second is the grade ceiling consideration, which runs the opposite way to intuition. A student who would get a six at Higher Level and a seven at Standard Level has a decision to make, and the right answer depends entirely on whether a department specifies Higher Level in that subject. If it does, the six is worth more than the seven. If it does not, the seven is worth more and the student has recovered time for everything else.

The table sets out the comparison. Use the final row as the practical test: the right-fit signal from prior attainment is the single most reliable predictor available, and it is sitting in the student's IGCSE grades and MYP criterion marks already.

sections.heading: Mathematics Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation
paragraphs: This is the most consequential subject choice in the Diploma and the one most often made on the wrong basis. The two courses are not a harder and an easier version of the same thing. Analysis and Approaches is built on algebraic technique, proof and calculus. Applications and Interpretation is built on statistics, modelling and the use of technology, with marks for interpreting results in a described context. Both exist at Higher and Standard Level, giving four distinct courses.

The common error is choosing by perceived difficulty. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is a demanding course, and Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level is not a soft option. The correct basis for the decision is a combination of two things: what the student is actually good at, evidenced by their IGCSE paper performance rather than their overall grade, and what their intended degree specifies.

On that second half, the instruction is to verify rather than infer. Engineering, physics, mathematics and quantitative economics departments frequently specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level. Many other quantitative programmes accept either. In the UAE, institutions such as Khalifa University, United Arab Emirates University, the American University of Sharjah and the Dubai campuses of overseas universities each publish their own requirements by programme, and those published pages are the only reliable source. A general rule from a tutoring website is not one.

sections.heading: Admissions tests and the requirements that are actually sourced
paragraphs: Admissions tests generate more anxiety in this district than almost any other topic, and a large share of that anxiety is misdirected. The first question is not how to prepare for a test but whether the test is required at all for the specific programmes a student is applying to, and the only reliable answer comes from the admissions page of each institution.

What can be stated with a source is the UAE equivalency position, which is a separate matter from any individual university's entry requirements. On the American track, the sourced guidance requires English proficiency demonstrated by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL internet-based test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics demonstrated by at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. On the British track, the requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3 with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded, plus one A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade.

What cannot be stated is an IB points threshold for equivalency. The sourced guidance covers the British and American tracks in detail and names no IB figure, so this page publishes none and nor should any other. Ask the Ministry of Education or your emirate's attestation authority directly. A number quoted in a tutoring advertisement is not a source, and one ranking competitor already publishes an incorrect subject count on the British track.

On preparation, the honest position is that subject-content tests reward subject work and reasoning tests reward practice at the reasoning. What neither rewards is a tutor who has not seen the actual test format. If a test is genuinely required, ask specifically whether the tutor has worked on that test, and if not, prepare from the official published materials rather than from an approximation.

sections.heading: Predicted grades, and why a January mock matters more than a report
paragraphs: Predicted grades are set by the school and they carry real weight in applications. Families frequently treat them as an administrative output and then discover that a prediction has constrained an application. The useful thing to understand is what evidence a school uses, because that evidence is often older and narrower than parents assume.

In most schools the prediction draws heavily on the most recent formal internal assessment, which in a Diploma Year 13 is typically the January or autumn mock, together with the teacher's judgement. That means a mock sat in a bad week, or in a subject where the student had not yet revised a late topic, can anchor a prediction that then shapes which universities are realistic. The mock is not a rehearsal; it is evidence.

The practical implication is that preparation for a mock deserves more attention than it usually gets, and that it should happen weeks earlier rather than in the preceding fortnight. A student who treats a January mock as the real examination will produce a representative result, and a representative result is what you want whether it is high or low: an inflated prediction creates an application that falls over at results time, and a depressed one closes doors that should have stayed open.

Where a prediction does look unrepresentative, the conversation with the school should be evidence-based rather than aggrieved. Bring the specific scripts, the specific components, and the specific improvement since the mock. Schools will revisit a prediction where the evidence supports it, and they reasonably will not where the argument is that the student will work harder from now on.

sections.heading: The DIFC school run and the evening it leaves
paragraphs: There is no school in DIFC, so every student travels, and the journey begins at one of the city's busiest nodes. The Financial Centre Road and Sheikh Zayed Road interchanges absorb DIFC, Downtown and Business Bay traffic simultaneously each morning, which is why a nominally twelve-minute journey takes thirty at 07:30 and why direction matters more than distance here.

The inland routes towards Sobha Hartland, Al Jaddaf and Nad Al Sheba avoid Sheikh Zayed Road almost entirely and are the most reliable from these towers. The westward routes towards Al Quoz and the Al Safa and Jumeirah cluster are slower in the morning, with the Al Quoz industrial corridor adding unpredictability rather than simply distance. Most DIFC shortlists end up weighted towards the inland campuses for exactly this reason.

In the afternoon the return overlaps with the commercial evening peak in the same corridor, so a student leaving campus at 15:10 is back in a DIFC tower nearer 16:15 to 16:45. For most households here that does not matter, because the constraint is not the student's availability but the parents'. Both parents routinely work past 18:30, and travel is frequent.

What that produces is a district where the late evening slot is the norm rather than the exception. Diploma students work well at 20:00 and often better than at 17:00, and online delivery means a 20:30 start is as straightforward to hold as a 17:00 one, because no tutor is driving home afterwards. For younger students in these towers the earlier slot still works, provided someone is present to settle them at the start.

sections.heading: Online delivery, the home-tutor search, and the honest comparison
paragraphs: Parents here search for home tutors because that is the established phrase, and the comparison deserves real figures. In-home tutoring in Dubai runs at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour at market rates, with travel inside the rate, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist. Premium named tutors are advertised from AED 500 to 650. Those are published market figures; IB Gram quotes its own rate after a consultation because it depends on subject, level and tutor.

IB Gram does not provide home visits in the UAE. Home visits are part of our India service only, and every country page on this site says so. The argument for the online model in this district is not cost but availability on two dimensions at once. A DIFC family often needs a specialist in a specific Higher Level subject, and needs them at 20:30. The set of people who satisfy both conditions and can also drive to the Gate District is very small.

The format also fits the work. Testing whether a student's algebraic fluency supports Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level means working through their own papers on a shared screen. Reviewing a mock script against the mark scheme means both documents visible at once. Checking a department's published requirement means opening the page together. None of that is improved by physical presence, and all of it leaves a written record.

The requirements are the usual ones and worth setting up properly: a quiet room with a door, headphones, a second screen or tablet so paper work and the tutor are both visible, and for any mathematical subject at Higher Level a graphics tablet so tutor and student can write on the same page. Families who skip these report a worse experience and usually attribute it to the format rather than the setup.

sections.heading: Getting started from DIFC, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Start with the destination rather than the subject. Which countries and which kinds of programme are genuinely in view, and what do two or three target departments actually publish as their requirements. That takes an evening and it changes every subsequent decision. Then gather the academic evidence: IGCSE grades at paper level if available, MYP criterion marks, the most recent mock script with its mark scheme, and the school's current predicted grades.

With those, a decision block of two or three sessions can test whether a level or route choice holds up. That block is deliberately short and carries no expectation of continuation, because the useful output is a reasoned shortlist to take to the school rather than an ongoing booking. Where ongoing subject support is genuinely needed, it runs weekly at component level with a named target and a review date.

Three things we will not claim. We will not promise a grade, a point total or a university outcome, and a provider that offers one should be treated with scepticism rather than relief. We are not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no tutoring provider in this market holds a regulator's endorsement of its teaching. And we do not perform, expedite or guarantee equivalency, attestation or admission, all of which belong to an authority or an institution.

One boundary stated plainly. Tutors explain assessment criteria and give feedback on the student's own drafts, including on application writing. They do not write or restructure a personal statement, a supplemental essay, an internal assessment, an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay, and they do not reproduce or distribute awarding-body syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Those are referenced and linked. Admissions readers and examiners both notice work that is not the applicant's, and the consequence falls on the student.

process.title: Establish the destination, not just the subject
process.description: Which countries and which kinds of programme are genuinely in view, and what two or three target departments publish as requirements. This takes one evening of reading admissions pages and it determines every level, route and subject decision that follows.

process.title: Gather attainment at component level
process.description: IGCSE results at paper level where available, MYP criterion marks, the most recent mock script with its mark scheme, and the school's current predicted grades. Overall grades hide the information the decision needs; component detail reveals it.

process.title: Run a short decision block
process.description: Two or three sessions testing whether a Higher Level subject or a mathematics route is the right choice, using the student's own papers against the published requirements. The output is a reasoned shortlist for the school, not a recommendation to continue tutoring.

process.title: Then teach, at component level
process.description: Where ongoing support is genuinely needed, the weekly slot targets specific components rather than the subject at large, with timed practice at the real paper duration. Diploma sessions in this district are usually held at 20:00 or later.

process.title: Review against the target on a date
process.description: Each booking carries a named target and a fixed review. When the student can do the thing unaided we say so and step the booking down or close it. Open-ended weekly arrangements nobody reviews are the biggest waste in this market.

whyPoints.title: Decisions tested, not guessed
whyPoints.description: Whether a student should take a subject at Higher Level, or which mathematics route suits them, is answerable from their own component-level attainment in two sessions. It is the highest-value hour available to a Diploma family and almost nobody sells it as a discrete piece of work.

whyPoints.title: Requirements verified, never inferred
whyPoints.description: Engineering, mathematics and quantitative economics departments often specify Analysis and Approaches; many other programmes accept either route. UAE institutions and overseas campuses each publish requirements per programme. We point you to those pages rather than offering a general rule.

whyPoints.title: Sourced figures only, and gaps acknowledged
whyPoints.description: The IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61, SAT 450 and five-subject GCSE requirements are quoted from the sourced equivalency guidance. No IB points threshold appears there, so none appears here. A ranking competitor publishes an incorrect subject count on the British track.

whyPoints.title: Mocks treated as evidence
whyPoints.description: Predicted grades draw heavily on the most recent formal internal assessment, so a January mock shapes which universities are realistic. We prepare for mocks weeks ahead rather than in the preceding fortnight, and we aim for a representative result rather than a flattering one.

whyPoints.title: Late slots that actually hold
whyPoints.description: In a district where both parents routinely work past 18:30, the workable Diploma slot is 20:00 or later. Online delivery makes that as easy to hold as an afternoon one, because no tutor is driving home afterwards and no one has to be let into the building.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on application writing
whyPoints.description: Tutors give feedback on the student's own drafts, including personal statements and supplemental essays. They do not write or restructure them, and they do not produce coursework. Admissions readers and examiners both notice work that is not the applicant's, and the student carries the consequence.

faqs.question: How do we decide whether a subject should be taken at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: From component-level evidence rather than an overall grade. The reliable signals are a strong IGCSE result in that subject and automatic fluency in its fundamentals, meaning the student performs the basic operations without conscious effort. Then check whether the target departments specify Higher Level in that subject, because the answer changes the calculation entirely: a six at Higher Level is worth more than a seven at Standard Level if a department requires Higher Level, and worth less if it does not. Two sessions with the student's own papers settles it.

faqs.question: What is the real difference between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: They are different subjects rather than a harder and easier version of one. Analysis and Approaches is built on algebraic technique, proof and calculus. Applications and Interpretation is built on statistics, modelling and the use of technology, with marks for interpreting results in a described context. Both exist at Higher and Standard Level, giving four distinct courses. Applications at Higher Level is genuinely demanding and Analysis at Standard Level is not a soft option, so choosing by perceived difficulty is the commonest and most expensive error.

faqs.question: Which mathematics course do engineering degrees expect?
faqs.answer: Engineering, mathematics and physics departments frequently specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, and quantitative economics departments commonly do as well. Many other quantitative programmes accept either route. The instruction is to verify rather than infer: institutions such as Khalifa University, United Arab Emirates University, the American University of Sharjah and the Dubai campuses of overseas universities each publish requirements by programme, and those pages are the only reliable source. Requirements also change between admissions cycles, so check the current year.

faqs.question: Is three Higher Levels always better than two plus a strong Standard Level?
faqs.answer: No, and the reason is capacity rather than ability. A Higher Level subject carries substantially more taught hours and proportionally more independent work, so three of them consume the core of the week. A student with weak independent study habits will produce lower results across three Higher Levels than across two, because the time constraint binds before the ability constraint does. The right question is whether any target department specifies Higher Level in the third subject. If none does, the student has recovered a great deal of capacity.

faqs.question: What exactly is a predicted grade based on?
faqs.answer: Usually the most recent formal internal assessment, together with the teacher's professional judgement. In a Diploma Year 13 that typically means the autumn or January mock. The practical implication is that a mock sat in a bad week, or before a late topic was revised, can anchor a prediction that then shapes which universities are realistic. A mock is evidence rather than a rehearsal. Preparing for it properly, weeks ahead rather than in the final fortnight, is one of the better uses of tutoring in an application year.

faqs.question: Can we ask the school to raise a predicted grade?
faqs.answer: You can, and the conversation should be evidence-based. Bring the specific scripts, the specific components where performance has changed, and the measurable improvement since the assessment the prediction was built on. Schools will revisit a prediction where the evidence supports it. They reasonably will not where the argument is that the student intends to work harder from now on, because a prediction they cannot defend damages the school's credibility with admissions offices and ultimately damages other students' applications too.

faqs.question: What are the sourced UAE equivalency requirements for an American-track student?
faqs.answer: On the American track, the sourced guidance requires English proficiency demonstrated by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL internet-based test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics demonstrated by at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. These are equivalency requirements set by the authority and are separate from any individual university's entry requirements, which are usually higher. Verify the current rule on the authority's own page before planning around it.

faqs.question: How many IB points does UAE equivalency require?
faqs.answer: No IB points figure appears in the sourced equivalency guidance, which covers the British and American tracks in detail. This page therefore publishes none, and you should treat any tutoring website that quotes a number as unreliable until you have seen it on the Ministry of Education's own pages or your emirate's attestation authority. Ask the authority directly; it operates the process and publishes the current requirement. One ranking competitor already publishes an incorrect GCSE subject count on the British track, which is a reasonable reason for scepticism generally.

faqs.question: Does my child need to sit an admissions test?
faqs.answer: That depends entirely on the programmes applied to, and the only reliable answer is on each institution's admissions page. The first question is therefore whether a test is required at all, not how to prepare for one. Where a test genuinely is required, ask specifically whether a prospective tutor has worked on that exact test, because subject content and reasoning formats differ and an approximation wastes preparation time. Prepare from the official published materials rather than from third-party imitations of the format.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a personal statement or a supplemental essay?
faqs.answer: With feedback on the student's own draft, yes. A tutor can say where a claim is unsupported, where the writing is vague, where the structure buries the point, and where a paragraph says nothing an admissions reader has not read a thousand times. What a tutor must not do is write it, restructure it into finished prose, or supply content and phrasing. Admissions readers notice work that is not the applicant's, and so do examiners on coursework. The consequence falls on the student, not on the provider.

faqs.question: Can a tutor visit our apartment in the Gate District?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE tutoring online, one-to-one, over live video, and does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. In this district the relevant point is availability on two dimensions simultaneously. A household here often needs a specialist in a specific Higher Level subject at 20:30, and the set of people who meet both conditions and can also drive to DIFC is very small.

faqs.question: What time do Diploma sessions usually run from a DIFC address?
faqs.answer: Later than most published advice suggests, and that is appropriate. In a district where both parents routinely work past 18:30 and travel frequently, the workable slot is 20:00 or later, and Diploma students generally work better late than at 17:00 anyway. Online delivery makes a 20:30 start as easy to hold as an afternoon one, because no tutor is travelling home afterwards. For younger students in these towers, an earlier slot still works provided an adult is present to settle them at the beginning.

faqs.question: Is it too late to change a Higher Level subject after the first term?
faqs.answer: It is difficult rather than impossible, and the difficulty is content rather than administration. Higher Level content diverges from Standard Level early, and the internal assessment work begins in the first year, so a student moving down mid-course has usually done work that does not count and a student moving up has content to recover while carrying five other subjects. Schools will sometimes accommodate a change where the case is strong. The honest conclusion is that the decision should be tested properly before it is made, not afterwards.

faqs.question: If our child took combined science at IGCSE, is a Higher Level science still realistic?
faqs.answer: Not formally, and in practice it creates a gap that is hard to close. Separate or triple IGCSE science keeps all three sciences genuinely credible at Higher Level. Combined or double award covers three subjects at reduced depth, which works for Standard Level and leaves a student entering a Higher Level science starting a term behind on content while also carrying five other Diploma subjects. This is the most commonly reported regret among Diploma families, and it originates in a Year 9 option choice.

faqs.question: What does tutoring cost at this level in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates for an IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist run roughly AED 200 to 450 or more an hour, with TutorChase quoting around AED 270 and Bestimate's specialist band at AED 200 to 450 and above. A qualified subject tutor online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, in-home visits at AED 180 to 500 with travel included, and premium named tutors are advertised from AED 500 to 650. Those are published market figures rather than an IB Gram price list; our rate follows a consultation because it depends on subject, level and tutor.

dubai/difc.closingBody: From a DIFC address the single most useful evening you can spend is reading the published requirements of two or three target departments, because every subject and level decision follows from them. After that, the work is narrow: test whether your child's component-level attainment supports a Higher Level subject or a particular mathematics route, and take a reasoned shortlist to the school. We will do that in two or three sessions and tell you honestly if nothing further is needed. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video, at whatever hour your household actually has.

dubai/discovery-gardens.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover the combinations Discovery Gardens households ask for most: IGCSE Maths and Science for a Year 10, DP Economics or Chemistry for an older sibling, and MYP or Key Stage 3 consolidation for a younger one. Each tutor teaches one named syllabus, and each sibling gets their own slot.

intro.heading: Who actually lives in Discovery Gardens, and what that does to a tutoring brief
paragraphs: Discovery Gardens is one of Dubai's largest apartment communities, built as low-rise clusters around themed gardens between Jebel Ali and Jumeirah Village, with a metro station on the Route 2020 line and a long-established resident population. The households here are mostly working professional families on single or dual salaries, often with two or three school-age children, and often with a long tenancy rather than a two-year posting. That profile changes what a tutoring enquiry looks like compared with a villa community further east.

The first difference is scale. A Discovery Gardens enquiry frequently covers more than one child. A Year 11 sitting Cambridge IGCSEs in June, a Year 8 who has slipped in maths, and a Year 4 whose reading is behind are a single family problem with a single budget, and a plan that only addresses the exam year leaves the other two where they were. Working out which child needs weekly contact and which needs a short diagnostic block is more useful than booking three identical weekly hours.

The second difference is physical. These are apartments, not villas with a study. Two children taught at once in one living room do not both concentrate, and the second one usually ends up listening to the first. This is a solvable problem, but it has to be solved deliberately: separate slots, headphones, one child at the dining table and the other in a bedroom, and a tutor who knows to check at the start of the session whether the student can actually hear and be heard.

The third difference is the board mix. Discovery Gardens children are spread across British, Indian and IB provision, often within one family where an older child started at a CBSE school and a younger one was placed in a British-curriculum school. Dubai licenses 17 different curricula across 227 private schools, with the UK curriculum at 37% of enrolment, Indian curricula at 26%, American at 14% and the IB at 7%. A family straddling two of those is managing two unrelated assessment calendars, and the tutoring has to respect both.

IB Gram delivers all of this online, one-to-one, over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. For an apartment community that is a practical advantage rather than a limitation. A single visiting tutor cannot teach two children different subjects at the same hour, cannot be in the building three evenings a week without the travel showing up in the price, and cannot be a DP Economics specialist and a Key Stage 3 maths teacher at once. Three separate specialists on three separate screens can, and the thirty or forty minutes a visiting tutor would spend getting here stays inside the teaching time instead of being paid for twice.
