dubai/discovery-gardens.programmesIntro: A Discovery Gardens household often spans three stages at once. These are the programmes we support, written for a parent deciding where the limited tutoring budget should actually go first.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 and IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The years with no external examination and therefore the least parental visibility. MYP marks against four criteria out of eight each; British-curriculum schools report against their own internal scales. A student can drift for two years here without a report ever saying so clearly, and the drift shows up in Year 10 as a gap in fundamentals rather than as a difficulty with new content.
programmes.countryNote: For a Discovery Gardens family this is usually the child whose tutoring gets deferred in favour of the exam-year sibling. A short diagnostic block of four to six sessions is a better use of the budget than nothing: it identifies whether the problem is arithmetic fluency, reading comprehension or simply unfinished homework, and that answer determines whether weekly tutoring is needed at all.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years ending in terminal papers, with several subjects tiered. Cambridge splits Core and Extended; Pearson Edexcel splits Foundation and Higher. The tier a student is entered for sets a ceiling on the grade available, which makes the entry decision as consequential as the teaching. Cambridge runs June and November series; Pearson Edexcel runs May/June and November.
programmes.countryNote: The largest group we support in this community. We ask for the syllabus code and the tier from the exam entry before matching, because a parent is often unaware their child has been entered for Core when the target university expects an Extended grade. That one check has changed more outcomes here than any amount of weekly revision.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment worth roughly a fifth to a quarter of the grade, due months before the written papers. The hardest term is not the last one; it is the middle of Year 12, when internal deadlines stack up while content is still being delivered.
programmes.countryNote: Discovery Gardens students taking the Diploma travel out to it, most often towards Dubai Investments Park, The Sustainable City or Jumeirah. That commute is why older siblings here take later slots than younger ones, and why a 90-minute evening block is usually more productive than two short afternoon sessions.

programmes.name: Indian curriculum bridging into IGCSE or the DP
programmes.description: Indian curricula account for roughly a quarter of Dubai private-school enrolment, and this community has a large share of them. A student moving from CBSE Class 9 into IGCSE Year 10, or from Class 10 into DP Year 12, meets a different style of assessment rather than harder content: less recall, more application, extended written answers and marks for method.
programmes.countryNote: We treat this as a bridging problem with a defined scope. The gap is usually in extended writing, in data-handling questions and in the practical or investigative components, not in core mathematics. Six to ten sessions before the new course starts does more for a Discovery Gardens student than a year of weekly tutoring begun after the first bad report.

dubai/discovery-gardens.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects most often requested from this community, with the actual failure point in each rather than a course summary. Matching is by board and code, so an enquiry for science becomes an enquiry for Cambridge 0653 or Pearson 4SD0.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended, Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The tier decision dominates. Beyond that, the recurring weak points are algebraic fractions, transformations of graphs and multi-step problems where the first line is not obvious. Students who can do each skill in isolation and fail a mixed paper need practice at selecting a method, which is a different exercise from revising topics.

subjects.name: IGCSE Combined and Coordinated Science
subjects.description: Three subjects compressed into fewer papers, so what can be safely omitted is genuinely different from the separate sciences. Marks are lost on the alternative-to-practical paper and on six-mark extended answers, where students write what they know instead of what the question asked.

subjects.name: IGCSE English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A large part of this community's demand. The reading and writing paper rewards accurate summary and controlled register, and the speaking component is marked on fluency and development rather than accent. Marks come back quickly here with structured practice, which makes it an efficient subject to tutor.

subjects.name: IGCSE Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Application marks are the gap. A definition scores one mark; applying it to the named business in the case study scores the rest. Students who revise content and never practise case-study application plateau at a middling grade regardless of how much they know.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which exposes any weakness in algebraic manipulation immediately. Proof and calculus in unfamiliar contexts carry the heaviest HL mark loss. The exploration adds a written component many strong mathematicians underestimate.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with a calculator throughout. Marks are lost on interpretation rather than calculation: a correct chi-squared value with no conclusion sentence earns a fraction of the available credit. The AA or AI choice should be checked against the intended degree before Year 12 begins.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation separate grades here. HL adds quantitative content and a third paper. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries built on real news articles, and the common failure is choosing an article that cannot carry the required analysis.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry and energetics are the pivot points; organic mechanisms account for most HL mark loss. The internal assessment is worth about a fifth of the grade and is marked heavily on methodology and uncertainty treatment rather than on the result obtained.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of content defeats more students than conceptual difficulty does. The marks that go missing are on experimental design questions and on applying a known process to an unfamiliar example. Mark schemes here demand precise terminology, which rewards systematic vocabulary work.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the Paper 1 guided analysis cause the most difficulty. Students lose marks for describing a text rather than analysing how it produces an effect. Structured close-reading practice is the single highest-return intervention in this subject.

dubai/discovery-gardens.regionsTitle: Communities we serve alongside Discovery Gardens
dubai/discovery-gardens.regionsIntro: The western apartment and villa belt shares schools, buses and tenancy patterns. These notes describe the kind of household each community tends to contain, because that is what shapes the tutoring brief more than the distance between them.

regions.name: Al Furjan
regions.note: The villa and townhouse neighbour immediately south, with a slightly older household profile and more single-child or two-child families. Shares the Route 2020 metro link and several school bus routes, so study partners cross between the two communities regularly.

regions.name: Dubai Investments Park
regions.note: Where much of this belt's schooling actually sits rather than where its families live. Delhi Private School Dubai, Nibras International School and Greenfield International School all draw heavily from Discovery Gardens households.

regions.name: Dubai South
regions.note: Newer stock around Expo City with a younger household profile and primary-weighted demand. Families here are often in their first UAE posting, which shows up as questions about how the British and IB systems differ rather than about exam technique.

regions.name: Emaar South
regions.note: Townhouses and villas with young families. Tutoring demand skews towards Years 3 to 8, and parents are usually making a first decision about whether a child will take IGCSEs or continue into an IB school.

regions.name: Jebel Ali
regions.note: An older established district with long-tenured residents, many working on industrial or logistics schedules. Weekend morning sessions are requested here more often than anywhere else in the belt because weekday evenings are unreliable.

regions.name: Green Community
regions.note: Low-rise and quiet inside Dubai Investments Park, with short school runs and a high proportion of families whose children attend school within a few minutes of home. Early evening sessions are genuinely workable here.

regions.name: Dubai Production City
regions.note: Mixed apartment and villa stock with a media and services workforce. Household profiles here resemble Discovery Gardens closely, including the two-and-three-child pattern and the mixed-board families.

schoolClusters.city: Discovery Gardens, Al Furjan and The Gardens
schoolClusters.note: The schools within a short bus ride, covering British curriculum with IGCSE at 16 and a mixture of A Level and IB continuation. Option blocks and tier policies differ between them, which is why two children in the same cluster can end up with different grade ceilings.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai Investments Park and The Sustainable City
schoolClusters.note: Where the belt's IB Diploma places and its largest Indian-curriculum schools are concentrated. Most Discovery Gardens Diploma students commute into this cluster, and most of its CBSE enrolment comes from apartment communities to the north.

dubai/discovery-gardens.modesIntro: Three patterns cover almost every household here, and the choice is usually driven by how many children are being taught and how much quiet space the apartment has. All sessions are one-to-one over live video.

modes.title: Staggered sibling slots on the same evening
modes.description: Two or three children taught back to back, each with their own specialist and their own hour, in whichever room is free. One child works at the dining table while another is in a bedroom with headphones. This is the pattern most Discovery Gardens households settle into, and it needs no second tutor in the building.

modes.title: A short diagnostic block instead of an open-ended booking
modes.description: Four to six sessions with a defined question: is this child behind, and in what exactly. Used most often for the middle sibling whose school reports are vague. At the end you get a written read on what is secure and what is not, and a recommendation that may well be that weekly tutoring is unnecessary.

sections.heading: Scheduling two or three children in one apartment
paragraphs: The practical obstacle in this community is not finding a tutor. It is finding two hours of quiet in a three-bedroom apartment between 17:00 and 21:00 while dinner is being made and a younger child wants the television. Families who try to solve this by having two children tutored simultaneously in the same room discover quickly that neither session works, because a one-to-one lesson is a conversation and two conversations in one room cancel each other out.

The arrangement that does work is staggering. One child takes 17:00 to 18:00 at the dining table; the second takes 18:15 to 19:15 in a bedroom; the exam-year student takes 19:30 to 21:00 once the house has settled. Headphones are not optional, and a cheap wired pair outperforms the laptop speakers for both hearing and being heard. A second device matters less than people assume - a tablet propped at eye level with a notebook beside it is fine for most subjects.

The table below is the pattern we propose most often to a three-child household here, and it is worth planning against before the first booking rather than after the first collision. We hold sibling slots consecutively in the same tutor's calendar where the subject allows it, so the schedule is one arrangement to remember rather than three.

One detail parents are surprised by: the youngest child should go first, not last. A seven-year-old at 19:30 has nothing left, while a Year 12 student at 16:30 has not arrived home yet. Ordering the evening by age rather than by convenience is the single change that stops a sibling schedule collapsing in the third week, and it costs nothing to get right at the start.

sections.heading: The board mix inside one Discovery Gardens family
paragraphs: It is common here for siblings to be on different curricula. An older child may have started in an Indian-curriculum school and a younger one been placed in a British-curriculum school when a place opened, or a family may have moved a child into an IB school after a change of plan about university. The result is one household running two assessment calendars, two sets of terminology and two different ideas of what a good report looks like.

This matters for tutoring because the systems reward different things. Indian curricula at Class 9 and 10 place heavy weight on recall and on working through a prescribed set of problems. IGCSE rewards application to unfamiliar contexts and marks method explicitly. The IB adds internally assessed components and a written research piece, so a student is being judged on process over months rather than on performance in a week. A tutor who treats all three as the same job will be ineffective in at least two of them.

The table sets out the curricula licensed across Dubai's private sector with their share of enrolment, what each one examines at 16, and where tutoring usually has to concentrate. The enrolment figures are from Dubai's published 2024-25 private-school data: 387,441 students across 227 schools offering 17 curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37%, Indian at 26%, American at 14% and the IB at 7% of private-school enrolment.

A parent reading that table should take one practical thing from it: ask the school which board and which code, then ask what the first externally marked piece of work will be and when. Those two answers place a child on the right row of the table, and they are the only two facts a tutor genuinely needs before the first session.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that sets the grade ceiling
paragraphs: This is the highest-value conversation available to an IGCSE parent in this community and almost nobody has it in time. Cambridge tiers several subjects into Core and Extended; Pearson Edexcel tiers into Foundation and Higher. The tier is not a difficulty setting applied to the same paper. It is a different syllabus content list, a different paper, and a different range of grades available at the end of it.

A student entered for Cambridge Core Mathematics cannot be awarded the top grades, however well they are taught, because those grades are not available on that paper. Schools make the entry decision on the evidence in front of them, usually at the end of Year 10 or early in Year 11, and they are often right. They are not always right, and a parent who discovers the tier in the spring of Year 11 has very little room left to argue it.

What tutoring can do depends entirely on when the question is asked. In the autumn of Year 10, demonstrating Extended-level work to the school is realistic. In March of Year 11, after entries have closed, the honest answer is that the ceiling is set and the sensible target is the top of the available range. The table below sets out what actually differs so a parent can ask the school a precise question rather than a general one.

There is a reasonable version of the capped tier too. A student who is secure on the core content and would be overwhelmed by the extended specification is better served by a strong grade at the lower tier than by a poor one at the higher. The decision only becomes a problem when nobody told the family it was being made. Asking in Year 10 keeps it a decision; asking in March of Year 11 makes it a discovery.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context for a Discovery Gardens budget
paragraphs: Most tutoring pages either hide the price or quote one number. Neither helps a household deciding how much of a finite education budget should go to tutoring across three children. What follows is a set of market figures with the items a family actually has to weigh against each other, including the school fee position, so the tutoring number sits in context.

The anchor is that Dubai school fees were held flat for 2026-27. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for that academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Fees being static means the discretionary part of the education budget is the part a family can still move, which is exactly why setting the tutoring figure deliberately is worth half an hour of thought.

Every AED figure below is a published market rate attributed to the provider that published it, or a cost set by an examination board or school. None of them is an IB Gram price. Our own starting point is a free trial lesson and a conversation about the household's limit before any session length or frequency is proposed, because the honest answer to how much tutoring a child needs depends on what else that money is doing.

One line in the table is worth reading twice. The in-home monthly package costs roughly twice the online one for half the number of sessions, and the difference is travel. That is not a criticism of in-home tutoring, which some children genuinely need. It is a statement about what a household in this community is buying when it chooses the format, and it deserves to be a choice rather than a default.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: This question is asked less often than it should be, and the answer is clear enough to check. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories are specified: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

Two details are worth a parent's attention. The permit is free, so any tutor explaining a higher rate by reference to licensing costs is describing something that does not exist. And the permit carries a code of conduct: in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit school staff from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. A parent being quietly offered their child's own class teacher is being offered an arrangement with a real problem in it.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor: that needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram does not hold that permit and never describes itself as approved by KHDA, because it operates no premises in the UAE. Any page telling you its tutors are approved by KHDA is making a claim worth checking against KHDA's own register.

One more practical note for this community. Because the permit is issued to an individual rather than to a platform, the question to ask is about the person who will actually teach your child, not about the brand that introduced them. A tutor who answers that question directly and without hesitation is telling you something useful about how the rest of the arrangement will run.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency when your child leaves school
paragraphs: Equivalency is the step that converts a school-leaving qualification into something a UAE university or employer will recognise, and it catches families by surprise because schools do not always explain it until Year 13. It is worth understanding in Year 10, because the subject count and the grades required are decided by choices made then. Four of the ten query clusters we researched contain no competitor page that mentions equivalency at all, and one ranking page publishes the wrong subject count.

On the British track the Ministry requires proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, together with passes in five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five required subjects. That last point is the one most often reported incorrectly, and it changes how a Year 9 options form should be filled in.

On the American track English proficiency is demonstrated by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB there is no points threshold we can publish, because we have not read one on the Ministry's own site, and an unsourced number here would be worse than no number. Verify your child's position through the Ministry's own channel. Equivalency is not a process a tutoring service performs or can guarantee.

sections.heading: Changing school or board mid-year from Discovery Gardens
paragraphs: School moves happen often in this community, usually because a place opens at a preferred school or because a change in circumstances makes a different fee band necessary. A mid-year move is manageable academically if the gap is identified before the first week at the new school rather than after the first assessment. The mistake is assuming the subject names transfer: Physics at CBSE Class 10 and Cambridge IGCSE 0625 overlap substantially and diverge in exactly the places that get examined.

The transition most often needed here is Indian curriculum into IGCSE, and the gap is rarely mathematical. It is in extended written responses, in experimental method questions, in the expectation that a student explains why rather than states what, and in the practical or alternative-to-practical component. A student arriving in Year 10 from Class 9 is usually ahead on content and behind on how answers are expected to be constructed.

The second common move is IGCSE into the Diploma, which is a change in kind rather than degree. The Diploma assesses over two years with internally assessed components, a 4,000-word research piece and a course about knowledge itself. A strong IGCSE student who has never written at length or managed a long deadline finds the first term of Year 12 harder than the content warrants. The table gives a realistic scope for each transition we are asked about most.

Every row in that table has an end date, which is the point of writing it down. Transition support is a defined piece of work with a finish line, not a reason to keep a weekly slot running for two years. When the gap is closed we say so and the sessions stop, and a family that has been told that at the start tends to engage with the work differently.

sections.heading: What a KHDA inspection band actually tells a parent
paragraphs: Parents in this community compare schools by their inspection rating constantly, and the rating is genuinely useful information, but it answers a narrower question than it appears to. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, and it inspects on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. The band describes the school as a whole, across all phases and all curricula it offers.

That whole-school framing is where the misreading happens. A school rated in a high band may have an excellent primary phase and a thinner sixth form, or strong teaching across most departments and a weak one in the subject your child needs. The published inspection report breaks performance down by phase and by subject, and that detail is more useful to a parent choosing tutoring than the headline band is. Reading the report rather than the rating is twenty minutes well spent.

The band also says nothing about fit. A school performing strongly for most of its students can still be the wrong environment for a particular child, and a school in a middle band can be the right one. For tutoring purposes the inspection report is a diagnostic tool: it tells you where the school is likely to be stretched, which is often where a student needs outside support. We ask which school a child attends for exactly this reason, and we do not treat any school's rating as a judgement on the student.

process.title: Give us the household, not just the child
process.description: Tell us how many children need support, what year each is in, and what the realistic budget is across the term. A plan built for three children with one budget looks different from three plans made separately, and it usually spends less for a better result.

process.title: Confirm board, code and tier for each child
process.description: Cambridge 0580 Core and Pearson 4MA1 Higher are different courses with different ceilings. The exam entry confirmation or a recent paper gives us all three facts. This single check has changed outcomes in this community more than any amount of extra weekly revision.

process.title: Map the evening before booking anything
process.description: We work out which room each child will use, where the headphones are, and which slots can be held for a whole term. Staggered sessions are the arrangement that survives in an apartment; simultaneous ones are the arrangement that quietly stops after three weeks.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson for each child
process.description: One full session per child with the proposed tutor, at no cost. Siblings often need different teaching styles, and a tutor who works well with an articulate Year 12 may not be the right person for a reluctant Year 8. If a match is wrong we propose someone else.

process.title: Review the household plan at week four
process.description: We look at what the schools' assessments show, what the session notes record, and whether the budget is going to the child who needs it most. Sometimes the answer is to stop one child's sessions and double another's. We will say so.

whyPoints.title: Built for households, not single bookings
whyPoints.description: Siblings get separate specialists on staggered slots within one schedule, so a Year 12 taking Economics and a Year 8 needing maths are not competing for the same hour or the same tutor. One arrangement to manage rather than three.

whyPoints.title: The tier and the board are checked first
whyPoints.description: We confirm the syllabus code and the tier before matching a tutor, because teaching Extended content to a student entered for Core wastes a term and teaching Core content to an Extended candidate costs grades. Schools can confirm both in a sentence.

whyPoints.title: Costs are published with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is a market rate attributed to whoever published it, or a cost set by a board or a school. We do not quote in dollars, and we do not present other providers' rates as our own prices.

whyPoints.title: A diagnostic option that may end in no booking
whyPoints.description: A short block of four to six sessions with a defined question is often the right answer for a middle child whose reports are vague. Sometimes the finding is that weekly tutoring is not needed, and that is a legitimate outcome of the block.

whyPoints.title: Regulation explained, not implied
whyPoints.description: We set out what the MoHRE private tuition permit is, who needs one and how to check, and we state plainly that IB Gram holds no KHDA training-institute permit and operates no UAE premises. Claims of regulator approval are the most common misrepresentation in this market.

faqs.question: Can you tutor two or three children in the same Discovery Gardens apartment?
faqs.answer: Yes, on staggered slots rather than at the same time. Each child gets their own one-to-one session with a tutor matched to their subject and level, and we schedule those sessions back to back so only one is running per room. Two lessons in the same living room do not work, because a one-to-one session is a spoken conversation and two conversations cancel each other out. Headphones make a larger difference than a second device. We build the household schedule as one arrangement rather than three separate bookings.

faqs.question: Which schools do most Discovery Gardens children attend?
faqs.answer: Families here are spread across the western belt. The most commonly named schools are The Arbor School in Al Furjan, Arcadia Global School and Sunmarke School in Jumeirah Village Triangle, The Winchester School in Jebel Ali, JSS International School, and in Dubai Investments Park Delhi Private School Dubai, Nibras International School, Dove Green Private School and Greenfield International School. Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City draws Diploma students too. Because these schools run different boards, siblings in one family are frequently on different assessment calendars.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child is entered for Core or Extended?
faqs.answer: Ask the school for the exam entry confirmation, which states the syllabus code and the tier for each subject. Cambridge splits Core and Extended; Pearson Edexcel splits Foundation and Higher. The tier is not a difficulty setting on the same paper - it is a different content list, a different paper and a different range of grades available. A capped tier cannot produce a top grade however well a student is taught. Ask during Year 10 or very early in Year 11, because after entries close the ceiling is fixed for that series.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to book one tutor for several subjects in our household?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and it is worth testing rather than assuming. A single tutor can genuinely cover two related subjects for one student, such as Maths and Physics at IGCSE, and that saves scheduling effort. Across siblings at different stages it rarely works: the person who teaches a reluctant Year 8 well is not usually the right person for a Year 12 Economics student aiming at a top grade. We would rather match each child properly than sell a bundle that produces one good outcome and two mediocre ones.

faqs.question: What does tutoring cost per month for a family with two children in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run roughly AED 180-600 a month for budget tutoring, AED 600-1,200 for a mid-band qualified tutor, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, per child. Monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are other providers' published figures, attributed in the cost table on this page. We start with a free trial lesson and a conversation about the household's limit before proposing anything.

faqs.question: My middle child's reports are vague. Do we need weekly tutoring?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and a short diagnostic block is a better first step. Four to six sessions with a defined question - is this child behind, and in exactly what - produces a written read on which specification points are secure and which are not. Sometimes the finding is that the child understands the material and is not completing homework, which is a different problem that weekly tutoring will not fix. We would rather return that answer and release the budget to the sibling who needs it than start an open-ended booking.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working in Dubai need a government permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Because the permit costs nothing, a tutor citing licensing costs to justify a higher rate is describing something that does not exist. Ask directly; it is a fair question.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to apartments in Discovery Gardens?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not place a tutor at any UAE address; visits to a student's home are something we run only in India. Every lesson here is one-to-one over live video. In an apartment community that turns out to be the more workable format: three children can be taught by three different specialists on the same evening without anyone arriving at the building, the travel cost that sits inside in-home rates disappears, and a family is no longer limited to tutors willing to drive to this part of Dubai at 18:00.

faqs.question: My children are on different curricula. Can one plan cover both?
faqs.answer: One plan can cover the household; one tutor usually cannot cover both curricula. Indian curricula at Class 9 and 10 reward recall and prescribed problem sets. IGCSE rewards application to unfamiliar material and awards method marks explicitly. The IB adds internally assessed components and a long research piece. A tutor treating all three the same way will be weak in at least two. We match a specialist per child per curriculum and hold them inside one schedule and one budget conversation.

faqs.question: What is the gap when a child moves from CBSE Class 9 into IGCSE Year 10?
faqs.answer: Usually not the mathematics. Students arriving from an Indian curriculum are frequently ahead on content and behind on how answers are expected to be constructed: extended written responses, explaining why rather than stating what, method marks shown in full, and the experimental or alternative-to-practical component. Six to ten sessions before or during the first term closes most of it. Starting that work after the first disappointing assessment costs a term that did not need to be lost, which is why we ask about recent school moves at the first conversation.

faqs.question: Does a school's KHDA rating tell me whether my child needs a tutor?
faqs.answer: Not on its own. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and the band describes the whole school across all phases and curricula. A school in a high band can have a thinner sixth form or one weak department, and the published report breaks performance down by phase and subject. That detail is the useful part for a parent. Read the report rather than the headline band, and treat it as a map of where the school is stretched rather than a verdict on your child.

faqs.question: What does my child need for UAE equivalency if they sit IGCSEs and A Levels?
faqs.answer: The Ministry requires passes in five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus either one accredited A Level subject at no less than grade E or two AS Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking tutoring site states six subjects are required, which is incorrect. Check your child's own position through the Ministry's official channel. Equivalency is a regulatory process, not something a tutoring service carries out or can guarantee on your behalf.

faqs.question: Can sessions run during school holidays and the long summer?
faqs.answer: Yes, and holidays are often the most productive weeks of the year for a transition or a retake. Because lessons run over live video, a family travelling to India, the UK or elsewhere keeps the same arrangement by time zone rather than pausing for six weeks and losing ground. Intensive blocks of four to ten sessions compressed into two or three weeks work well for bridging into a new curriculum or preparing a November series entry. We set the block, the scope and the end date before it starts.

faqs.question: How long does it take to match a tutor for a Discovery Gardens family?
faqs.answer: Common combinations - IGCSE Maths, Combined Science, English as a Second Language, DP Economics - are usually matched within a few working days, followed by a free trial lesson. Narrow requests take longer: a specific Group 2 language, HL Further Mathematics, or a fixed slot that only works at one hour on one day. When the pool is thin we tell you and offer a different time with the right specialist, a different tutor at your time with an honest account of their coverage, or a short wait with a date on it.

faqs.question: Will a tutor give feedback on my child's Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear limit. A tutor explains each assessment criterion and the marks attached to it, helps the student frame a workable question, teaches referencing and data handling, and gives feedback on work the student has already produced alone. A tutor does not contribute content, reshape the piece into its final form, or correct it line by line until the expression is no longer the student's. The school supervisor signs an authenticity declaration, and we keep session notes so that declaration can be made accurately.

dubai/discovery-gardens.closingHeading: Start with the household, then the tier
dubai/discovery-gardens.closingBody: If you are looking for IB or IGCSE tutoring in Discovery Gardens, the two things worth establishing before anything else are which child most needs the budget and which tier each of them is actually entered for. Those two answers usually reshape the plan a family arrives with. Tell us the year groups, the schools and the realistic limit across the term, and we will come back with a staggered schedule, a specialist per child and a free trial lesson for each. If a short diagnostic block is the better use of the money, we will recommend that instead of weekly sessions.

dubai/downtown-dubai.tutorsIntro: The tutors here are matched for students whose situation is administrative as well as academic: a mid-year arrival on a different syllabus, a private candidate with no school department behind them, or a Year 11 deciding whether to retake. Each works to a named board and a dated calendar.

intro.heading: Downtown Dubai's academic problem is a calendar problem
paragraphs: Downtown Dubai is apartments and nothing else: Burj Khalifa and the Boulevard, Old Town and South Ridge, the Opera District, Burj Views and the Address towers. It has no school campus and almost no long-tenured family housing. What it has is the highest turnover of any central district in the city, and that single characteristic explains most of the academic questions that come from these addresses.

A transient district produces a specific set of problems. Families arrive in November and have to place a child mid-year, often in a different curriculum from the one they left. Students change examination board halfway through a two-year course. Some cannot find a secondary place at all for a term and end up studying at home and sitting papers as private candidates. Others leave Dubai in the middle of Year 11 and need to know whether their entries travel with them.

None of those is a teaching problem in the first instance. They are administrative problems with academic consequences, and the thing that makes them expensive is that the deadlines sit a long way ahead of the events they govern. Cambridge's final entry deadline for the March 2027 series fell on 27 November 2026, more than two months before the exam period opened on 3 February 2027. A family arriving in Dubai in December cannot enter that series, however ready the student is.

This is the gap nobody in this market fills. Across sixty-odd competitor pages, the word November returned no hits at all: no session named, no entry deadline, no results date. Three of six leading pages publish no price either. A family in Downtown Dubai trying to work out what their child can actually sit, and when, is on their own with a search engine.

The second Downtown-specific factor is the school run. Because there is no campus here, every child travels, and they travel out of one of the most congested road nodes in the city. The Al Quoz schools, the Sobha Hartland campuses, Swiss International Scientific School in Al Jaddaf, Kent College in Nad Al Sheba and the Jumeirah cluster are all reachable, and all of them involve joining Sheikh Zayed Road or Al Khail at exactly the wrong time. A workable weekday lesson slot here starts at 17:30 and more often 19:00.

Everything described on this page is one-to-one tuition over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For a household that may be in a different country in eight months, that has an obvious practical value: the tutor, the plan and the session notes travel with the family rather than staying in Dubai.

dubai/downtown-dubai.programmesIntro: Each qualification has its own administrative calendar, and those calendars are the thing a transient household most needs explained. These are the four that matter from Downtown addresses.

programmes.name: Cambridge International IGCSE and O Level
programmes.description: Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. A March series operates in some regions. Entries are made by the centre, which means by the school, and a student without a school needs an approved centre to enter them.
programmes.countryNote: Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For a family comparing two Dubai schools, the exam dates may genuinely differ between them.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including for International GCSE November 2027, and revises them, so the live official PDF is the only version to plan from.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson's results dates are published and useful for planning: June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A Downtown family deciding whether a November retake is worth it can work from those real intervals.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, with internally assessed components in every subject that are moderated by the IB. Registration is handled by the school as an IB World School, which makes mid-course movement between countries more complicated than for a Cambridge or Pearson candidate.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. This page publishes no specific IB session or results date, because ibo.org is the only authoritative source for the IB's own calendar and second-hand dates circulate widely and incorrectly. Ask your child's Diploma coordinator for the registration deadlines and the internal coursework calendar in writing.

programmes.name: International A Level and AS Level
programmes.description: Taken in depth across three or four subjects, with Cambridge and Pearson both offering international routes and modular or linear structures depending on the board. For a family that may relocate, the modular option has a practical advantage because credit banks as it is earned.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE equivalency on the British track, one accredited subject at Advanced Level at a grade of no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, is required alongside five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count. dubai/downtown-dubai.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects most requested from Downtown addresses. The notes concentrate on what transfers cleanly between boards and what does not, because board changes are common here.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Content overlaps heavily but tier naming, paper structure and question style do not. A student moving between the two mid-course needs a few sessions on question framing rather than on content, which is the cheapest board-change fix available.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics
subjects.description: Cambridge offers Core and Extended tiers; Pearson runs a single tier. Practical assessment arrangements differ, which matters for a private candidate, since not every centre offers every component in the same way.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations and organic chemistry carry the grade on both boards, but the way questions are cued differs enough to cost marks. A board change six months before an exam is a technique problem rather than a knowledge problem.

subjects.name: IGCSE Biology
subjects.description: Command terms and data-response conventions differ between the boards in ways that are invisible until a student sits a paper. Practising the correct board's mark-scheme language is the single highest-return intervention here.

subjects.description: A student arriving mid-Diploma from an A Level or AP route will find proof and the extended Paper 3 investigation unfamiliar. The gap is identifiable in one diagnostic session and usually closes in a focused block rather than a year.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics and modelling with technology throughout. Students transferring from a British GCSE background often have strong manipulation and weak interpretation, which is the opposite of what this course rewards.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · Cambridge First Language English · Pearson English Language A
subjects.description: Writing tasks are not transferable between boards: text types, directed-writing conventions and assessment emphasis all differ. For a mid-year arrival this is the subject most likely to look fine and score badly.

subjects.name: Economics and Business
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE Business Studies
subjects.description: Essay and case-study technique is board-specific and responds quickly to correction. A short block before a mock often does more than a term of content revision.

subjects.name: Physics and Chemistry at Diploma level
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a problem for mid-year arrivals specifically, because it needs a research question, data collection time and a school's equipment, and a student who changes school in February has lost part of that window.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: Mandatory in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes required for Arabs and non-Arabs. A newly arrived non-Arab student entering at Year 9 or above starts this subject from a standing position and needs a realistic plan for it.

sections.heading: What the school run out of Downtown actually costs
paragraphs: There is no school in Downtown Dubai, so every child here commutes, and the commute starts at one of the busiest road nodes in the city. The Financial Centre Road and Sheikh Zayed Road interchanges, plus the Al Khail approaches, absorb Downtown, Business Bay and DIFC traffic simultaneously each morning, which is why a journey that the map calls twelve minutes takes thirty at 07:30.

The practical consequence is a two-stage loss. The morning run is long, and the afternoon return is longer, because school dismissal and the start of the commercial evening peak overlap in the same corridor. A child leaving a campus in Al Quoz at 15:10 can arrive back in a Downtown tower closer to 16:30. Add food and decompression and the first realistic weekday study hour sits around 17:30, with 19:00 being the dependable one.

The direction matters more here than the distance. The inland routes towards Sobha Hartland, Al Jaddaf and Nad Al Sheba avoid Sheikh Zayed Road almost entirely, which is why campuses that look further away on a map appear on more Downtown shortlists than the nearer Al Quoz schools. Westward journeys along Al Wasl Road to the Jumeirah and Al Safa cluster are the slowest of the four during the morning window.

The table sets out the four directions with their realistic timings. For a family choosing a school from a Downtown address, the right question to ask the admissions office is not the distance but the bus departure and arrival times for your specific tower, because a route collecting across several buildings behaves very differently from a direct drive.

sections.heading: The session calendar, with the dates that are actually published
paragraphs: This is the section that does not exist anywhere else in this market. Across the competitor pages fetched for this project, the word November returned no hits: no page named a session, an entry deadline or a results date. For a transient district where families need to know what their child can sit and when, that absence is the whole problem.

The dates below come from the awarding bodies' own published pages, with the series named. They are included as worked examples of the intervals involved rather than as a timetable to rely on, because Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, and Cambridge zone timetables differ by centre. The live official PDF is always the version to plan from.

What the table shows is that the administrative decisions sit a long way ahead of the academic ones. Cambridge's final entry deadline for the March 2027 series fell on 27 November 2026, with the exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results released to centres on Cambridge International Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. A family that arrives in Dubai in December has already missed the entry window for that series, regardless of readiness.

Pearson's published intervals are equally usable. The November 2026 International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. That November-to-January gap is the one a family weighing a retake needs, because it tells you when the decision becomes actionable. For IB candidates, no date appears here; ask the Diploma coordinator.

sections.heading: Why the entry deadline matters more than the exam date
paragraphs: Parents plan backwards from the examination because that is the event that feels real. The deadline that actually binds is the entry, and it falls months earlier. Entries are made by the centre, which in practice means the school's exams officer, and they fix the subject, the tier and the components a student will sit. After the deadline, changing any of those is either impossible or expensive.

Three things are decided at entry and are frequently decided badly. The tier, where Core or Foundation caps the attainable grade and is often chosen on performance a year before the exam. The subject set, where a student dropping a subject at entry closes a route they may still want. And the series, where entering a November session rather than waiting for June changes a student's entire revision calendar.

For a mid-year arrival the entry deadline is the first question to ask an admissions office, before anything about curriculum fit. A school may be an excellent match and still be unable to enter a child for the series the family had in mind, because the deadline has passed or because the centre's zone timetable conflicts with a planned relocation. Admissions offices will answer this accurately if asked directly; they rarely volunteer it.

The honest position on tutoring here is that it cannot fix a missed entry. What it can do is make the entry decision better informed: a diagnostic from real work in October tells you whether Higher tier is realistic, which is precisely the information the November entry decision requires and precisely the information most families do not have when they make it.

sections.heading: Sitting as a private candidate from a Downtown address
paragraphs: Private candidacy comes up more often in this district than anywhere else in Dubai, for an unglamorous reason: families arrive mid-year, secondary places in the schools they want are full, and a term or two of studying at home becomes the practical option. It is a legitimate route, and it is administratively demanding in ways that catch people out.

The sequence matters. A private candidate needs an approved examination centre willing to accept external entries for the specific qualification and components, and that willingness is not universal: some centres take certain boards only, and some will not offer components with practical or coursework requirements. The centre, not the family, makes the entry, so the centre's own deadline is the real one and it sits ahead of the awarding body's.

Components are the second trap. Science subjects with practical assessment and subjects with coursework are arranged differently for external candidates depending on board and centre, and a family that assumes a subject is available in the usual form can find in January that it is not. The question to ask a centre, early and in writing, is which syllabus codes and which components they will accept for external candidates in which series.

The third issue is that a private candidate has nobody tracking their calendar. In a school, an exams officer chases entry forms, a head of year chases coursework, and a teacher notices when a student stops working. A private candidate has none of that, which is why private-candidate tutoring is as much about maintaining a schedule as about teaching content. That is a legitimate thing to buy, and it should be set out explicitly rather than assumed.

sections.heading: After results: enquiries, remarks and retakes
paragraphs: Results day is treated as an endpoint and it is actually a decision point with its own short deadlines. A grade that sits one mark below a boundary, a paper that went badly for an identifiable reason, or a subject needed for a specific route all generate options, and every one of those options has a window that closes quickly.

The first option is a review of marking, requested through the centre rather than by the family directly. Awarding bodies operate defined services for this with their own deadlines and fees, published each series, and the request has to go through the school or centre that made the entry. Private candidates request it through their examination centre. What a review does and does not do is worth understanding before paying for it: it checks whether marking was applied correctly, not whether the student deserved more.

The second option is a retake in the next available series. Here the published intervals are what make the decision real. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and the next International GCSE series runs in May or June, which gives a concrete amount of preparation time. Cambridge's June and November series give a similar structure. Counting the weeks before deciding is more useful than deciding emotionally on the day.

The third option, which families under-use, is to accept the result and redirect. A grade that closes one route often leaves several others open, and the cost of a retake is a term of a student's attention that could go into the next qualification instead. sections.heading: Relocating mid-year, in either direction
paragraphs: A district with this much turnover generates two symmetrical problems: children arriving part-way through a course, and children leaving part-way through one. Both are manageable and both are handled badly when the family discovers the issues in sequence rather than mapping them at the start.

For an arrival, the checklist is short and should be worked through before the first day. Which board and syllabus code does the new school enter, and does it match the previous one. Has the entry deadline for the intended series passed. What has the new scheme of work already covered that the student has not met. Are there coursework or internal assessment components already under way that the student has missed part of. And for a Dubai school, what is the position on the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies provision for a student entering at this stage.

For a departure, the questions are about what transfers. Entries made by a Dubai centre stay with that centre unless transferred, coursework marks are held by the school, and internally assessed IB components depend on the receiving school's status. A student mid-Diploma moving between IB World Schools is a different proposition from a student mid-IGCSE, and the Diploma coordinator is the person who knows.

What online tutoring contributes here is continuity. A tutor matched to a student in a Downtown tower in September can still be teaching them in October from a different country, with the same session notes and the same plan, adjusted for whichever syllabus the new school uses. For a household that may move twice in three years, not having to restart the search each time is worth more than it sounds.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs in this market, and the honest bands
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages for Dubai tutoring searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. The bands below are market rates with their publishers named, which is the standard this market does not meet. IB Gram quotes its own rate after a consultation, because it depends on the subject, the level and the individual tutor rather than on a published list.

Market pricing runs roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tutoring, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online sits around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home visits including travel run roughly AED 180 to 500, drawn from Bestimate's 180 to 350 band and home-tutor rates of 200 to 500. An IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist runs AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase quoting around AED 270, and premium named tutors are advertised from AED 500 to 650.

For a transient household the relevant cost is not only the rate but the restart. A family that hires locally in each city pays a search, a trial period and a ramp-up every time, and in practice loses a month of momentum per move. That cost never appears in an hourly comparison and is frequently larger than the rate difference between providers.

One piece of context worth having. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Each school publishes its own fee on its KHDA listing. Against an annual fee, one weekly tutoring session is typically a small single-digit percentage, which is the right frame for deciding whether to buy it rather than comparing hourly rates in isolation.

sections.heading: Getting started from Downtown Dubai, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Start with the administrative facts, because in this district they are usually the binding constraint. The board and syllabus code for each subject, the centre's entry deadline for the intended series, the school's internal coursework deadlines, and whether a relocation is likely inside the next year. Then the academic evidence: the last mock script with its mark scheme, and the teacher's written feedback on any coursework already under way.

The sequence is a consultation, a trial with the named tutor who would hold the slot, and either a finite block or a weekly booking. For board transitions and private-candidate work the block is the right shape, because it has an endpoint. For ongoing subject support the weekly slot carries a review date and a named target rather than running indefinitely.

Three things we will not claim. We publish no IB session or results date, because the IB is the only authoritative source for its own calendar and second-hand dates are wrong often enough to matter. We are not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no tutoring provider in this market holds a regulator's endorsement of its teaching. And we do not perform, expedite or guarantee equivalency, attestation or examination entry, all of which are the authority's or the centre's processes.

One boundary stated as a boundary. Tutors explain assessment criteria and give feedback on the student's own drafts. They do not produce content for an internal assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or coursework component, and they do not reproduce or distribute awarding-body syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Those are referenced and linked to the official source, because reproducing them is both a copyright and an integrity problem.

For the Cambridge March 2027 series, final entries were due on 27 November 2026 while the exam period ran from 3 February to 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results released to centres through Cambridge International Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. Entries are made by the centre, not the family, so the school's exams officer is the person to ask. A household arriving in December has already missed that entry window regardless of how ready the student is.

faqs.question: Which Pearson International GCSE series exist, and when do results arrive?
faqs.answer: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May or June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. On results, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, and revises them, so plan from the live official PDF rather than a restated date.

faqs.question: Do exam dates differ between two schools in Dubai sitting the same subject?
faqs.answer: With Cambridge, they can. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong timetable. So the dates your child sits are centre-specific rather than universal. When comparing two schools from a Downtown address, ask each exams officer for their centre's own timetable, particularly if you are planning travel around the exam window.

faqs.question: Why does nobody publish IB exam dates on this page?
faqs.answer: Because the IB is the only authoritative source for its own calendar, and this project could not verify any IB date from ibo.org directly. Secondary sources circulate dates that converge but are not confirmed, and sending a family to the wrong week is a serious error. UAE schools sit the May session, which is the fixed point you can plan around. For anything more specific, ask your child's Diploma coordinator for the registration deadlines, the internal coursework calendar and the examination window in writing.

faqs.question: Can my child sit IGCSEs as a private candidate in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, through an approved examination centre that accepts external entries for that board and those components. The practical constraints are real: not every centre takes every awarding body, and some will not offer subjects with practical or coursework requirements to external candidates. The centre makes the entry, so its own internal deadline sits ahead of the awarding body's published one. Ask any prospective centre in writing which syllabus codes and which components they will accept for external candidates in which series, well before the deadline.

faqs.question: We are arriving in Dubai mid-year. What should we ask a school first?
faqs.answer: Ask about examinations before curriculum fit. Which awarding body and syllabus code does the school enter for each subject, has the entry deadline for your intended series already passed, and what has the current scheme of work already covered that your child has not met. Then ask which coursework or internal assessment components are already under way, because a student arriving in February may have missed part of a window that cannot be reopened. Finally ask how the school places a new arrival into the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies provision.

faqs.question: How hard is it to change exam board halfway through a course?
faqs.answer: Easier than families fear, and different from what they expect. Content overlaps substantially between Cambridge and Pearson for the same subject, so the student usually knows most of the material. What differs is paper structure, tiering, practical arrangements and the way questions are cued, and those cost marks invisibly until a paper is sat. The fix is a focused block on question framing and the correct board's mark-scheme language, typically six to ten sessions, rather than reteaching a year of content.

faqs.question: What are the options if a grade comes in just below a boundary?
faqs.answer: Three. A review of marking, requested through the centre that made the entry rather than by the family directly, with the awarding body's published deadline and fee for that series. A retake in the next available series, where the published intervals make the decision concrete: Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026 and the next series runs in May or June. Or accepting the result and redirecting, which families under-use and which is frequently the right answer, because a retake costs a term of attention.

faqs.question: Can a tutor visit our apartment in Downtown Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE tutoring online, one-to-one, over live video, and does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. In the most transient district in the city this is a structural advantage rather than a limitation. If the household relocates, the same tutor, the same plan and the same session notes continue in the new time zone, with the syllabus plan adjusted if the receiving school uses a different awarding body.

faqs.question: What time can lessons start given the Downtown school run?
faqs.answer: Plan on 17:30 at the earliest and 19:00 for dependability. There is no campus in Downtown Dubai, so every child travels out through one of the busiest road nodes in the city, and the afternoon return overlaps with the start of the commercial evening peak in the same corridor. A child leaving an Al Quoz campus at 15:10 can be back in a Downtown tower nearer 16:30. The direction matters more than the distance: the inland routes towards Sobha Hartland and Al Jaddaf are the least disrupted.

faqs.question: Does the tier chosen at entry limit my child's grade?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the single most consequential decision made at entry. Cambridge Core and Pearson Foundation tiers cap the attainable grade, while Extended and Higher expose a student to content the lower tier never assesses. The decision is made by the centre at the entry deadline, often on performance from a year earlier, and after the deadline it is difficult or impossible to change. A diagnostic from real work before the deadline is worth considerably more than one afterwards, because it is the information the decision actually requires.

faqs.question: What does a private candidate lose by not being in a school?
faqs.answer: Mostly administration and monitoring rather than teaching. In a school, an exams officer chases entry forms, a head of year chases coursework deadlines and a subject teacher notices when a student stops working. A private candidate has none of that, so the schedule has to be maintained externally. That is a legitimate thing to buy support for and should be set out explicitly in any arrangement, alongside syllabus teaching. The other loss is advice at results time, when remark and retake deadlines are short and nobody is prompting you.

faqs.question: If we leave Dubai mid-course, what happens to the entries and coursework?
faqs.answer: Entries made by a Dubai centre stay with that centre unless they are transferred, and coursework marks are held by the school that supervised them. For Cambridge and Pearson candidates this is usually workable with notice. For an IB Diploma student it is more involved, because internally assessed components and registration depend on the receiving school's status as an IB World School. The Diploma coordinator at both schools is the person who can answer it, and the conversation should start before notice is given rather than after.

faqs.question: What do tutors charge around Downtown and Business Bay?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Dubai run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour at the budget online end, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit with travel included, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist, with premium named tutors advertised from AED 500 to 650. Those are published market figures rather than an IB Gram price list; our own rate follows a consultation because it depends on subject, level and tutor. For a relocating household, the hidden cost is the restart with every local hire.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting tutoring if we may move in six months?
faqs.answer: It depends on what you are buying. A finite block aimed at a specific target, such as a board transition, a coursework component or a tier decision before an entry deadline, delivers inside six months and is worth doing. An open-ended weekly arrangement with no named target is a poor purchase on any timeline. The advantage of online delivery is that the arrangement is not tied to the address: if the family moves, the same tutor and the same plan continue in a different time zone rather than being replaced.

dubai/downtown-dubai.closingBody: From a Downtown Dubai address the most useful thing you can establish before buying any tutoring is which deadline binds: the centre's entry cut-off, the school's internal coursework date, or the series your child is actually registered for. Those decide what is possible. Ask the exams officer for the board, the syllabus code and the centre's own timetable, in writing. Then send us the last marked script and we will plan backwards from the date that matters. All lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video, and continue if your address changes.

dubai/dubai-academic-city.tutorsIntro: The profiles below cover what Academic City households ask for most: Diploma mathematics and sciences at Higher Level, IGCSE option-block subjects in Years 10 and 11, and Extended Essay supervision. Each tutor teaches a named specification and the match is shown before any booking.

intro.heading: A district built around what happens after school
paragraphs: Dubai International Academic City is not a residential community in the ordinary sense. It is a higher-education free zone - university branch campuses, student accommodation, academic offices - with a thin layer of family housing around and inside it, and the adjoining apartment and villa districts supplying most of the rest. The school-age children associated with an Academic City address belong largely to staff households, to postgraduate families, and to households in Silicon Oasis, Academic City's immediate neighbours and Nad Al Sheba.

That demography changes the conversation. In most Dubai communities a parent books a tutor because a mark dropped. Here, a meaningful share of enquiries arrive from parents who work in higher education and who are thinking two or three years ahead: which mathematics route keeps an engineering option open, which five IGCSE subjects have to be protected because the Ministry counts five, whether a strong internally assessed grade will carry weight with an admissions office. They are asking about the destination before the journey has gone wrong.

The second thing that follows from the demography is transfer. Academic City households move internationally more often than average, and they move mid-course, which is the hardest version. A student arriving in Year 11 from an American high school, or in Diploma year one from a British sixth form, is not simply behind. They are on a different assessment model, with coursework already part-completed under rules they have not been taught. That is a specific problem with a specific fix, and it is nothing like ordinary catch-up tutoring.

Both of those make this page different from a standard area page. The useful material for an Academic City family is not a longer list of subjects. It is the route information: what the Ministry of Education actually requires for equivalency and where that is published, what the American track demands by way of test scores, how Analysis and Approaches differs from Applications and Interpretation in admissions terms, and when the paperwork has to start. That is where this page spends most of its words.

On delivery, the position is simple and stated up front. Lessons run one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. For a household in or beside Academic City this is rarely a compromise - the people living here are already comfortable with live-video teaching, and the specialist pool for a Higher Level subject matters far more than whether someone can drive over.

Nothing here promises an admission or a grade, and the equivalency material is descriptive rather than a service. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee any part of equivalency or attestation. What follows is the information in one place, with sources, so that the decisions taken in Year 9 and Year 11 are taken with the destination in view.
