dubai/dubai-academic-city.programmesIntro: Four programmes matter to households around Academic City, and the reason each note below focuses on the exit rather than the content is that these are the families most likely to be asking what the qualification will be worth in two years' time.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internally assessed components in each subject are marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB. The qualification is accepted widely for admission, but the subject and level combination is what a programme prerequisite actually tests - an offer asking for Higher Level Mathematics is not satisfied by a strong Standard Level grade.
programmes.countryNote: Academic City parents working inside the sector tend to ask about Higher Level combinations rather than about predicted totals, which is the right instinct. For UAE equivalency purposes, note that no IB points threshold is published in the Ministry clarification this page cites, so any figure quoted elsewhere should be checked on moe.gov.ae before it is relied on.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years of specification-led courses examined at the end of Year 11, each syllabus carrying a code that determines the papers and any tiering. The grades matter twice: once for sixth-form entry, and again for the Ministry's equivalency count, which requires five accredited subjects at no less than E or grade 3. The option block taken in Year 9 therefore has a consequence most families do not see until Year 13.
programmes.countryNote: Because Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the Ministry's five-subject count, an Academic City family needs five other accredited subjects to clear the floor comfortably. That is an argument for breadth in the option block rather than early specialisation, and it is the single most useful thing to know before choosing options.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject group, each marked out of eight and converted into a 1-7 grade, with no external papers until optional eAssessment at the end of Year 11. For families thinking about the exit, the significant feature is that the MYP produces no externally examined qualification on the standard route, so the first externally recognised result arrives with the Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: A household planning an international move partway through secondary should know that an MYP record is harder to convert than an IGCSE transcript, because there are no subject certificates to present. Where a move is likely, the eAssessment route is worth discussing with the school well before Year 11.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units and outcome-based reporting rather than marks. The things that decide how secondary school goes are reading fluency, number-fact recall and written stamina, and a prose report can conceal all three. The PYP Exhibition in Year 6 is the first extended independent project, and the first honest signal about whether a child can plan work without being told how.
programmes.countryNote: Academic City primary families moving in from another system often arrive without a comparable baseline, because their previous school reported in grades and this one reports in outcomes. A short diagnostic on reading rate and arithmetic recall gives the comparison the two reports cannot.

dubai/dubai-academic-city.subjectsIntro: Subject requests here lean towards the ones that appear in programme prerequisites, which is a different pattern from most Dubai communities. Each note says what the component assesses and, where it matters, what the subject opens or closes further on.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency. Engineering, mathematics, physics and many computer science programmes commonly ask for this route, often at Higher Level, so the Year 11 choice is a route decision rather than a preference. Check the specific programme's own published requirement rather than a general rule.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and substantial graphical-calculator work, with interpretation carrying marks that students expect to be given for the calculation. Suits business, social science and life science destinations; less often accepted where a programme names a calculus-heavy prerequisite.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: A standard prerequisite for engineering admission, which makes Higher Level Physics a route subject as well as a difficult one. Marks are lost in algebra rather than in physics: a correct argument abandoned when the rearrangement becomes untidy. The data-analysis paper is the least-practised component.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Required for most medical, pharmacy and chemical engineering routes. Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the Higher Level papers, while the internally assessed investigation loses marks on uncertainty handling and conclusions that go further than the data allows.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume invites rereading, which does very little. Grades turn on terminology precision and on answering the command term that was actually used. For medical routes it is usually paired with Chemistry, and the pairing is what the prerequisite names.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry the marks and unlabelled diagrams lose them. The internally assessed commentaries are built on published articles, so article choice sets the ceiling before any analysis is written. A common choice for business and finance destinations in the region.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen analysis under timing and rewards a repeatable procedure rather than wider reading. For students whose English proficiency will also be tested separately on an equivalency track, the subject grade and the test score are two different things and both have to be planned for.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: A smaller cohort, so tutor availability is tighter than for the core sciences. The internally assessed solution is where most marks move, and it is usually the first time a student has had to document design decisions rather than simply make them work.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: The tier decision caps the grade, which matters doubly here because the grade counts towards the Ministry's five-subject floor and towards sixth-form entry. Extended candidates lose most marks on multi-step problems that mix two topics and prompt no method.

subjects.name: IGCSE separate sciences
subjects.description: Three separate sciences keep more sixth-form doors open than the co-ordinated route, which is the reason the Year 9 option conversation matters. Practical skills are examined on paper, so the required skill is reading someone else's method and finding its flaw.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first and additional language
subjects.description: Compulsory in Dubai schools under KHDA rules and excluded from the Ministry's five-subject equivalency count, which means it has to be taken seriously for its own sake rather than for the count. First-language and additional-language routes need different tutors.

dubai/dubai-academic-city.regionsIntro: Academic City sits at the southern end of the Al Ain road corridor, with Silicon Oasis above it and the Nad Al Sheba villa districts to the west. The notes below describe where the families associated with this district actually live and what that does to a school run.

sections.heading: Who actually lives here, and what each household asks for
paragraphs: Answering the literal question first: very few families live inside Academic City itself, because the zone is built for institutions rather than households. The school-age population associated with this address is made up of university staff families, postgraduate households with children, and families in the adjoining communities who treat Academic City as their district because they work or study in it. That is a small, highly educated, highly mobile population, and it asks for different things.

The pattern is consistent enough to be worth setting out. Staff households ask route questions early and want evidence rather than reassurance. Postgraduate families often have a child on a curriculum the parents did not themselves sit, so the request is partly translation: what does a 5 mean, what is an internal assessment, why is there no exam until Year 13. Families in the surrounding apartment communities ask the ordinary questions about marks and slots. Transfer families ask the hardest question of all, which is how to land mid-course.

What this means in practice is that the first conversation matters more here than the first lesson. A family planning towards a named engineering programme at a Dubai campus needs to know about Higher Level Mathematics and Physics now, not in Year 13 when an offer condition makes it obvious. A family that has just arrived in Diploma year one from an American high school needs the assessment model explained before anyone teaches them any content.

The table maps the household types against what usually helps most. It is deliberately blunt about the cases where the answer is not tutoring: a route question is often answered in one conversation, and a family that leaves with a clear plan and no weekly slot has had the useful outcome. Selling a term of lessons against a question that needed twenty minutes is how this market loses trust.

sections.heading: The qualification has to be recognised here, not just earned
paragraphs: This is the gap no competitor page in this market fills, and it is the one that matters most to a household living beside the universities. A school certificate earned in Dubai still has to be recognised by the UAE Ministry of Education for a student to progress into higher education here, and the requirements are specific, published and widely unknown among parents until far too late in the process.

On the British track, the Ministry's clarification requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and states that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. On top of that, a student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One tutoring site currently ranking in this market publishes a six-subject requirement, which does not match the clarification.

On the American track, the requirements are test-based. English proficiency is satisfied by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. Mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Mathematics test, and both have to be in place before applying. The article this page relies on does not mention any alternative national test, so do not assume one is accepted.

For the IB, the honest position is that no points threshold appears in the source read for this page. That silence matters: a figure quoted confidently on a tutoring site without a Ministry source behind it is a guess, and it is a guess that could change a family's decision. Verify any IB equivalency requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority, and treat the table below as a map rather than as the authority.

sections.heading: Attestation and paperwork, and why it starts earlier than you think
paragraphs: Equivalency is a recognition decision about a qualification. Attestation is the process of getting documents certified so they can be used officially in the UAE. They are related, often confused, and both are administered by authorities rather than by schools or tutoring platforms. The failure mode is almost always timing: a family discovers in the summer of Year 13 that a certificate issued in another country needs certification from that country first, and the admission cycle does not wait.

There are a few practical habits that make this less painful, and none of them cost anything. Keep original certificates rather than only school-issued statements of results, because an awarding body certificate is the document an authority expects. Keep every transcript from every school a child has attended, including the ones abroad, since a gap in the record is harder to fix years later. And note Cambridge's own timing: for the March 2027 series, results reach schools in mid-May and certificates are issued in late June, so the certificate a family needs does not exist for weeks after the result does.

The second habit is to ask the destination institution directly what it requires, in writing, and to do it at the start of Year 12 rather than at the end of Year 13. Programme-level requirements differ between institutions and between programmes within an institution. Nothing a tutoring page says about admission is a substitute for the published requirement of the specific programme your child intends to apply to.

One boundary deserves stating plainly, because other sites in this market blur it. IB Gram does not perform equivalency or attestation, does not submit documents on a family's behalf, and does not guarantee any outcome of either process. What a tutor can do is make sure the grades the process needs are actually achieved, and make sure a family is not surprised by a requirement in the final term. The official channels are the Ministry of Education and the relevant emirate authority, and those are where the current rules live.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation
paragraphs: Of all the choices a Diploma student makes, the mathematics route is the one that most often closes a door quietly. Both courses are respectable, both are examined rigorously, and they are not interchangeable in admissions. A programme prerequisite naming calculus-heavy mathematics is usually satisfied by Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, and a strong grade in the other route does not substitute for it however good the student is.

The content difference is real rather than presentational. Analysis and Approaches emphasises algebraic manipulation, proof and calculus, with less technology dependence. Applications and Interpretation emphasises statistics, modelling and the use of a graphical calculator, and requires a great deal of interpretation that students expect to be awarded for the calculation alone. Students who move routes to reduce difficulty frequently discover that the second course is not easier, only different.

The exploration is the other half of this decision and it is rarely discussed. It is marked against five lettered criteria for twenty marks in both routes, and in both routes students treat it as a write-up rather than as mathematics. The difference is that an Applications exploration can drift into description if the student is not pushed, while an Analysis exploration can collapse if the chosen topic outruns the student's algebra. Either way the criteria have to be read before the topic is chosen.

What to do with this, practically: look up the published entry requirement for the specific programme at the specific institution, not the general statement on a university's international page. Then choose the route that satisfies it with a grade the student can realistically reach, and plan the tutoring around the exploration term as well as the papers. Where the destination is genuinely undecided, Analysis and Approaches keeps more doors open, which is why it is the safer default rather than the better course.

sections.heading: Choosing IGCSE options with the five-subject rule in view
paragraphs: Year 9 option choices are made by fourteen-year-olds with help from parents who are thinking about the next two years. The Ministry's equivalency rule is thinking about Year 13. Those two timeframes rarely meet, and the result is a family discovering in sixth form that the subject spread they chose is narrower than the recognition process expects.

The arithmetic is not complicated. Five accredited subjects at no lower than E or grade 3 are required, and Arabic and Islamic education do not count towards the five. A student who takes a thin option block and relies on Arabic to make up the number has miscounted. In practice this argues for a conservative structure: English, Mathematics, at least one and preferably two sciences, and two further accredited subjects, with any additional options on top of that rather than instead of it.

The tier decision sits underneath this and is easy to miss. Cambridge runs Core and Extended routes on several subjects with different grade ceilings, so a student entered on the Core route may be capped below the grade a sixth form wants even if the equivalency floor is met. Pearson generally runs a single tier. Ask the examinations officer for the code and the tier on the entry form, in writing, because the report will show neither.

The sciences deserve a specific mention because the choice between three separate sciences and the co-ordinated route has consequences past sixteen. The separate route keeps more sixth-form and Diploma combinations available; the co-ordinated route is lighter and perfectly sound for students not heading towards a science destination. Make that choice against where the student might go, not against which looks easier in Year 10, and revisit it if the destination changes.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs in this market, and what the hour should buy
paragraphs: Three of the most prominent providers in this market publish no price, and two of the ones that do quote in US dollars. So the first thing worth putting on the screen is the AED band, attributed. The figures below were read from provider listings and a published Dubai rate survey in October 2026. They describe the market, not IB Gram's price list; ask for our figure before booking and hold it against the band.

The more useful column is the last one. At every stage the question is not what the hour costs but what it is spent on, and the answer changes sharply with the student's position in the course. An hour in Year 10 spent building a retrieval routine is worth more than the same hour spent re-teaching content the school is still covering. An hour in Diploma year two spent on timed papers is worth more than one spent on notes. Paying a specialist rate for homework supervision is the commonest waste in this market.

For an Academic City household there is a specific version of this. Route conversations - which maths course, which five subjects, what the destination requires - are worth paying for once and are not worth a weekly slot. Coursework supervision is worth paying for in blocks around the school's draft dates rather than continuously. The weekly slot earns its cost on a prerequisite subject where marked work shows a specific, diagnosable failure, and much less elsewhere.

One more honest note on comparison. A provider quoting a low hourly rate and a provider quoting a high one may be selling genuinely different things, and the rate card will not tell you which. Ask each one which specification they will teach, what the first session will consist of, what you receive in writing afterwards, and when the review point is. Those four answers separate providers faster than any price comparison does.

sections.heading: Sources, referencing and the authorship line on an Extended Essay
paragraphs: Living beside a university library does not make the Extended Essay easier; it makes the temptation more sophisticated. The students most at risk in this district are not the ones who cannot write. They are the capable ones with access to academic literature, a good command of other people's arguments, and a growing habit of assembling rather than reasoning. That is where honesty problems start, and they start without any intention to cheat.

The rules a student has to work inside are the school's academic honesty policy and the IB's own requirements, and both centre on one idea: the work must be the student's, and every contribution from anywhere else must be acknowledged. That covers quoted text, paraphrased arguments, data taken from a published study, diagrams, code and help from any tool. A tutor's job is to teach this properly rather than to police it, because a student who understands why attribution exists does not need policing.

On generative tools specifically, the position to take with a student is that the school's policy governs and the IB's guidance governs, and that anything produced by a tool and used in submitted work must be acknowledged in the way the school requires. What a tutor should never do is treat a tool's output as a shortcut through the thinking the assessment exists to measure. If the student cannot explain the reasoning in their own words, the work is not theirs regardless of how it was produced.

The tutor's own line is the same one that applies everywhere on this site, and it does not move. A tutor teaches the criteria by letter and the marks attached to each. A tutor interrogates a research question until it is answerable within the word limit. A tutor questions sources, method and argument, and responds to a draft with questions. A tutor does not supply text, restructure an argument on the student's behalf, or return a rewritten version to be retyped. The test is whether the student can defend every choice unaided.

sections.heading: From school to a Dubai campus: the step nobody rehearses
paragraphs: The students in this district will, more often than average, go to university within a few kilometres of where they went to school. That makes the transition look easy and it is not. The assessment model changes from criteria and command terms to seminars, reading lists and unsupervised deadlines, and the habits that carried a student through a well-run Diploma are not the habits a first undergraduate year rewards.

The practical preparation is narrow enough to be worth naming. Reading at length without being set questions. Writing to a word limit without a criteria grid. Managing a deadline that nobody reminds you about. Working from a reading list rather than a textbook. Those are learnable in Year 13 and almost nobody teaches them, because school assessment does not test them and university assumes them.

Then there are the hard requirements, which on the American equivalency track are test scores rather than skills. English proficiency is met by IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section; mathematics by at least 450 in SAT Mathematics, with both in place before applying. These are floors for recognition rather than competitive scores for admission, and a student aiming at a selective programme should be looking at what that programme itself publishes.

The table sets out those thresholds with their source. Treat it as a starting point for a conversation with the institution rather than as a complete admissions picture, and check the current position on moe.gov.ae and on the programme's own page before relying on it. A requirement quoted on a tutoring page in October is not a requirement guaranteed in the following July.

sections.heading: Coverage, scarcity and the legal position on tutoring
paragraphs: Specialist supply in this market is uneven and predictable. Higher Level Mathematics and Higher Level Physics tighten from February onwards. Computer Science, Psychology and the smaller Diploma options draw on a much smaller pool than a headline subject list implies. Arabic as a first language is thin all year. A platform that implies full coverage at all times is simply not disclosing its gaps, and you find out in session three.

Our position is to disclose it before booking. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the fallback is a specialist based outside the UAE, most often in India, teaching the same specification online, with the base and the time difference stated before anything is confirmed. That is a different thing from routing a Dubai parent to a foreign telephone number and letting them assume local delivery, which two providers in this market do.

On legality, which parents working in education ask about more often than most: private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure appears here.

Two conditions are worth knowing in a university district in particular. The permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules prohibit school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Separately, a tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE centre and claims no approval from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson; lessons are delivered online.

process.description: Tell us where the student might be heading - a named programme, a field, or genuinely undecided. That determines whether the mathematics route, the science option block or neither is the live question. For many Academic City families this conversation produces a plan and no weekly slot, which is a legitimate outcome.

process.title: Send the syllabus code, the level and the deadlines
process.description: Give the IB subject and level or the IGCSE code and tier from the entry form, plus the school's own coursework deadline dates. The code determines the papers and therefore the right tutor. Subject name and year group is not enough, and reports show neither the code nor the tier.

process.title: One diagnostic hour on marked work
process.description: The first session works on returned scripts and a short set of unprompted questions rather than teaching. For a transfer student it works on the gap between the previous specification and the current one. You receive the finding in writing, including whether a weekly slot is actually needed.

process.title: Agree the slot, the tutor's base and the review date
process.description: We set a protected weekly time, name the tutor's location and time zone before you confirm, and fix a review point six to eight weeks out. If no UAE-based specialist is free for a scarce Higher Level subject, you are told at this stage rather than after booking.

process.title: Put the route paperwork on the calendar
process.description: Equivalency and attestation are handled by the authorities, not by us, but the dates belong in the plan. Certificate issue dates, test sittings and the institution's own published requirements go on the same calendar as the exam entries, so nothing is discovered in the final term.

process.title: Review on marks, then continue or finish
process.description: At the review point we compare the plan against marked work and decide to continue, change tutor or stop. Stopping is a normal result. A provider with no review point is selling a standing order, and this is a market where an hour runs from AED 150 to 450.

whyPoints.title: The route is treated as a real question
whyPoints.description: Mathematics route, science options and the five-subject floor are decisions with consequences years later. We set them out against published requirements and sources rather than giving a general reassurance that the IB is well regarded.

whyPoints.description: The Ministry's requirements are quoted with their source and date, and the gaps - including the absence of a published IB threshold - are stated as gaps. IB Gram does not submit, perform or guarantee any part of equivalency or attestation.

faqs.question: Do families with school-age children actually live in Academic City?
faqs.answer: Some do, but the district is built for institutions rather than households, so the numbers are small. Most of the school-age children associated with an Academic City address belong to university staff families, postgraduate households, or families in the adjoining communities - Silicon Oasis, Nad Al Sheba, the Al Ain road corridor - who treat Academic City as their district because they work or study there. Those children are bussed outward to schools in the surrounding areas rather than to a school inside the zone, which is why session timing here behaves like Silicon Oasis timing rather than like a village community's.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to a staff apartment near the campuses?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide in-home tutoring anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service offered only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video with screen sharing, which is how a tutor and a student work through a marked script together. In this district that is rarely felt as a limitation, since most households are already comfortable with live-video teaching. The gain is the tutor pool: for a Higher Level subject the match becomes anyone who teaches that specification rather than anyone who can drive to Academic City at 17:00.

faqs.question: What does the Ministry of Education require to recognise a British-curriculum file?
faqs.answer: Reporting on the Ministry's clarification states that a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. In addition, the file must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at a grade no lower than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One tutoring site ranking in this market publishes a six-subject requirement, which does not match that clarification. Confirm the current position on moe.gov.ae before relying on any summary, including this one.

faqs.question: Is there a published IB points figure for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Not in the source this page relies on, and that is why no figure appears here. The Ministry clarification reported in July 2026 sets out the British and American track requirements in detail and states no IB points threshold. Several tutoring sites publish a number anyway. A figure with no Ministry source behind it is a guess, and it is the kind of guess that changes a family's subject decisions. If you need the IB position, get it from moe.gov.ae or from the emirate attestation authority directly, and get it in writing with the date.

faqs.question: What test scores does the American equivalency track require?
faqs.answer: English proficiency is satisfied by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. Mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Mathematics test. Both have to be in place before applying rather than afterwards. These are recognition floors, not competitive admission scores, so a student targeting a selective programme should work from what that programme publishes. The source read for this page does not name any alternative national test, so do not assume one is accepted without checking.

faqs.question: Should my child take Maths AA or Maths AI for an engineering route?
faqs.answer: Engineering, mathematics, physics and many computer science programmes commonly name Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level, because the course carries the algebra, proof and calculus those degrees assume. A strong grade in Applications and Interpretation does not substitute for a named prerequisite however good the student is. The decision should be tested against the published entry requirement of the specific programme at the specific institution rather than against a general statement about the IB. Where the destination is genuinely undecided, Analysis and Approaches keeps more doors open, which makes it the safer default rather than the better course.

faqs.question: Which five IGCSE subjects should my child protect?
faqs.answer: Work backwards from the equivalency floor and add a margin. English, Mathematics, at least one and preferably two sciences, and two further accredited subjects gives five with room for one to go wrong. Arabic and Islamic education cannot be counted towards the five, so a thin option block that relies on them has miscounted. Check the tier as well as the subject: Cambridge runs Core and Extended routes with different grade ceilings on several subjects, and a Core entry can cap a grade below what a sixth form wants even where the equivalency floor is met.

faqs.question: When should attestation paperwork actually start?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families start it, because the constraint is document issue rather than effort. Keep awarding body certificates rather than only school statements of results, and keep transcripts from every school a child has attended including those abroad. Note the issue lag: for the Cambridge March 2027 series, results reach schools in mid-May and certificates are issued in late June, so the document an authority wants does not exist for weeks after the result. Ask the destination institution in writing at the start of Year 12 what it needs, and route the process through the official channels.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram handle equivalency or attestation on our behalf?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not perform equivalency or attestation, does not submit documents for a family, and does not guarantee any outcome of either process. Both are administered by the Ministry of Education and the relevant emirate authority, and those are the only sources whose current rules count. What tutoring can legitimately do is make sure the grades the process requires are actually achieved, and make sure a family knows the requirements in Year 11 rather than in the final term. Any provider offering to secure equivalency for you is describing something it is not in a position to deliver.

faqs.question: Do universities in the UAE prefer the IB Diploma or A-Levels?
faqs.answer: Neither, as a general rule, because admission requirements are set per institution and per programme rather than per qualification. Both routes are widely used by students progressing into UAE higher education, and both pass through the Ministry's recognition process in their own way. What differs is the prerequisite: a programme may name a specific subject at a specific level, and that condition is satisfied by subject and level rather than by qualification type. Ask the programme directly, in writing, at the start of Year 12, and plan the subject choices from the answer.

faqs.question: How much does IB and IGCSE tutoring cost around Academic City?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Dubai run roughly AED 45-150 an hour at the budget online end, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180-500 for in-home with travel included, and AED 200-450 or above for an IB or IGCSE specialist, with premium providers advertising up to AED 650. Those figures come from provider listings and a published Dubai rate survey read in October 2026, not from an IB Gram price list. Ask us for our figure before booking. The more useful question is what the hour is spent on, which varies far more than the rate does.

faqs.question: Which schools do children from this district attend?
faqs.answer: Mostly schools in the surrounding corridor: Academic City's own small cluster, the Silicon Oasis schools a few minutes north, and the larger British and IB schools in Nad Al Sheba and the Al Khail Road communities. A smaller number travel further west. The practical consequence is board spread rather than the list of names - two children from the same apartment block can sit entirely different Physics papers depending on whether their schools entered them with Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel. Get the syllabus code from the examinations officer before booking a subject tutor.

faqs.question: Can a tutor check the referencing on my child's Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the more valuable things a tutor can teach, because attribution is a skill rather than a rule to obey. A tutor can explain what has to be acknowledged - quoted text, paraphrased arguments, data from a published study, diagrams, code, help from any tool - and can question whether a source is being used or merely assembled. What a tutor cannot do is rewrite the essay, restructure the argument, or supply text. The school's academic honesty policy and the IB's requirements govern, and the student must be able to defend every choice unaided.

faqs.question: Is using an AI tool on Diploma coursework allowed?
faqs.answer: The school's academic honesty policy and the IB's own guidance govern, and both are built on one principle: the work must be the student's and any contribution from elsewhere must be acknowledged in the form the school requires. That covers output from a generative tool exactly as it covers a quotation from a book. The deeper problem is not disclosure but substitution - using a tool to bypass the thinking the assessment exists to measure. A tutor should be teaching that distinction explicitly. If the student cannot explain the reasoning in their own words, the work is not theirs.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for a scarce Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: You are told before booking rather than matched approximately. Higher Level Physics and Higher Level Mathematics tighten from February, and the smaller Diploma options - Computer Science, Psychology, Global Politics - draw on a much smaller pool than the subject lists suggest. The options are a specialist based outside the UAE, most often in India, teaching the same specification online with the base and time difference stated up front, or a waiting-list place with a date attached. What we will not do is fill a Higher Level request with a general subject tutor and let you find out in session three.

dubai/dubai-academic-city.closingHeading: Decide the route, then buy the hours
dubai/dubai-academic-city.closingBody: Households in and around Dubai International Academic City usually have one of two live questions. Either the route is unsettled - which mathematics course, which five IGCSE subjects, what the Ministry will recognise - or the route is clear and a specific subject is not performing. Those need different responses, and only the second needs a weekly slot. Tell us which one you are, send the syllabus code or the IB subject and level, the school's coursework deadlines and the last marked paper. You will get a written diagnostic, the route information with its sources, a named tutor who teaches that specification where one is needed, the rate in AED and a review date. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video.

dubai/dubai-creek-harbour.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed here are matched for bridging work as much as for subject depth. A student arriving into Year 11 IGCSE from an American middle school needs someone who knows what the previous system did not cover, which is a different brief from weekly subject support.

intro.heading: A community of recent arrivals, and what that does to schooling
paragraphs: Dubai Creek Harbour is one of the newest large residential districts in the emirate, and that single fact shapes almost every tutoring conversation that starts here. The towers along Creek Island, Harbour Views, Creek Beach, Creek Rise and The Cove have been handed over in waves over the last few years, which means the overwhelming majority of families living here moved in recently, many of them from outside the UAE. A community of recent arrivals has a different academic profile from an established one, and the difference is not subtle.

There is also no secondary school inside the development. Children here travel out: across Ras Al Khor to Al Jaddaf, east to Dubai Festival City, or further into the eastern suburbs toward Mirdif and Al Warqa. School choice was therefore made under pressure, often against seat availability rather than fit, and sometimes mid-year. A family that arrived in January took the Year 11 or DP1 place that existed, not the one they would have chosen in September with a full list in front of them.

The result is that the most common academic problem in Dubai Creek Harbour is not a weak subject. It is a transition. A student who was doing well in a CBSE school in India, an American school in Texas or a British school in Singapore lands in a new curriculum partway through a two-year course, and the gap is a list of specific topics the previous system did not cover rather than a general weakness. Treated as a general weakness, it costs a term of lessons. Treated as a list, it costs four to six weeks.

The second most common problem is the examination administration that comes with arriving late. Entry deadlines for Cambridge and Pearson sit months before the papers, tiers are chosen before a new school knows the student well, and a child who joined in February may be entered at a tier chosen on incomplete evidence. None of that is anybody's fault, and all of it is worth knowing about before the entry closes rather than after the results arrive.

Lessons for Dubai Creek Harbour families are one-to-one and delivered live over video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a bridging brief that matters more than usual, because the tutor needs to know the syllabus the student is joining and ideally the one they left. That is a specific pairing, and it is not available from whoever happens to be driving past Ras Al Khor at five in the afternoon. The rest of this page is built for that brief: who lives here, what each school across the creek commits a child to, how long each transition takes, what it costs in AED at published market rates, and the entry administration that catches a family who arrived in January.

dubai/dubai-creek-harbour.programmesIntro: Families here choose a programme at the same time as they choose a school, usually in a hurry. These are the four routes available across the creek, with what each one asks of a student who joins it partway through.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internal Assessments carry a substantial share of each subject grade and are set against published criteria, marked internally and moderated by the IB. The programme assumes two continuous years, which is what makes joining it in DP1 term two difficult rather than merely inconvenient.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Creek Harbour families joining the Diploma mid-course usually arrive from an American high school or a British Year 12. The two gaps are different: American arrivals meet Internal Assessment expectations they have never seen, and British arrivals meet breadth, with three extra subjects and Theory of Knowledge appearing where free periods used to be.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked out of eight. Command terms decide the shape of a correct answer, and criterion totals convert to a 1 to 7 subject grade. Year 11 may sit MYP eAssessment on screen, which has its own question style and timing.
programmes.countryNote: Students arriving into MYP from a content-and-test system find the assessment style the hard part. A child used to being graded on right answers is now graded on how an answer is constructed, and the first report card after arrival is often a shock that has nothing to do with ability. Two or three sessions on criteria and command terms resolve most of it.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses examined at the end of Year 11, with Cambridge syllabuses such as 0580 Mathematics and 0625 Physics and Pearson equivalents including 4MA1 and 4PH1. Cambridge tiers several subjects Core or Extended. Entry deadlines fall months before the papers, which is the administrative fact that catches late arrivals.
programmes.countryNote: This is where most Creek Harbour bridging work happens. A student arriving into Year 11 from CBSE has usually met more algebra and less statistics than the IGCSE expects, and has never seen an alternative-to-practical paper. Those are nameable gaps and they close in weeks, provided somebody writes the list.

programmes.name: A Level, after IGCSE
programmes.description: Three or four linear subjects examined at the end of Year 13, with no breadth requirement and considerable depth. University offers are quoted in A Level grades. The absence of coursework in most subjects makes it the simplest route to join late, which is a practical consideration for a family arriving in Year 12.
programmes.countryNote: For a family that arrived in Dubai mid-Year-12, A Level is often the least disrupted option precisely because it is linear and examination-weighted. The honest counterweight is that three subjects narrow the degree options, and the decision deserves one session mapping subject content against intended university courses before it is made.

dubai/dubai-creek-harbour.subjectsIntro: The subject list below is weighted toward what arriving students actually need, with the transition gap named for each. The gap is the useful unit here, because it is what a bridging block is built from.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Arrivals from an American background typically meet the proof and algebraic rigour for the first time. Arrivals from CBSE are often ahead on algebra and behind on the Exploration, which has no equivalent in their previous system.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Graphical calculator technique is the usual gap. Students arriving from systems where calculators are restricted lose time and accuracy marks because the paper assumes routes they have never used.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics (0580 and 4MA1)
subjects.description: The transition gap is statistics, probability and the specific question formats. CBSE arrivals usually have strong algebra and have not met the data-handling content weighting that IGCSE applies.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic nomenclature conventions differ between systems, and the practical assessment component is frequently new to arrivals. Both are closeable in a defined number of sessions once identified.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The gap is rarely the physics. It is units, significant figures and the explanation question, where a student used to marking schemes that reward the right idea meets one that requires the right wording.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume plus terminology. Arrivals often know the biology under different names, and a session mapping their vocabulary onto the new syllabus saves weeks of apparent confusion.

subjects.name: English A and IGCSE English Language
subjects.description: Students arriving from a system that assessed comprehension meet one that assesses analysis and directed writing. The assessment objective split between content and language is the thing to show them explicitly.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Management
subjects.description: Popular with arriving Year 12 students because the content is new to almost everyone. The gap is the evaluation paragraph and diagram accuracy, both of which are technique rather than knowledge.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: A genuine surprise for families arriving from outside the UAE. Arabic is required in Dubai private schools regardless of curriculum, and a student joining in Year 9 with no Arabic needs a plan rather than an apology.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Has no analogue in most systems arrivals come from. Students treat it as unexaminable until February and then discover there is an essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition commentary to produce.

dubai/dubai-creek-harbour.regionsTitle: Dubai Creek Harbour and the schools across the water
dubai/dubai-creek-harbour.regionsIntro: Creek Harbour sits on the Ras Al Khor creek between the wildlife sanctuary and the Festival City side. These are the areas families here actually drive to, and the drive is what sets the earliest lesson slot.

regions.name: Creek Island and Harbour Views
regions.note: The first clusters handed over, closest to the creek edge. Households here are predominantly apartment families with one or two children, and the typical request is a single subject rather than a package.

regions.name: Creek Beach and The Cove
regions.note: Newer waterfront towers with a higher proportion of very recent arrivals. Bridging work and board-switch questions come disproportionately from these clusters, simply because the families are the newest.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf
regions.note: Across Ras Al Khor Road, roughly ten to fifteen minutes outside peak. Swiss International Scientific School Dubai sits here, which makes it the closest IB continuum option for a Creek Harbour family.

regions.name: Dubai Festival City and Al Badia
regions.note: East along the creek, with Deira International School and Universal American School. The most common school choice for Creek Harbour families wanting a British or American route with an IB sixth form.

regions.name: Nad Al Hamar and Ras Al Khor
regions.note: The interchange that governs the afternoon. Between half past three and five o'clock this crossing decides whether a lesson can start before five, which is the single most practical fact on this page.

regions.name: Business Bay and Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Where a large share of Creek Harbour parents work, fifteen minutes out of peak and considerably more inside it. Relevant mainly to whether a parent can be present for a diagnostic session.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: The eastern suburbs, a longer drive but with a wider school choice including Uptown International School's IB continuum. Families who arrived late and took whatever seat existed are often out here.

regions.name: Dubai International Academic City
regions.note: Further east, home to Dubai English Speaking College among others. A long school run from Creek Harbour, which pushes the workable lesson slot to half past six or later.

schoolClusters.city: Across Ras Al Khor: Al Jaddaf and Festival City
schoolClusters.note: The nearest cluster to Dubai Creek Harbour and the one most families here use. Between them these schools cover the IB continuum, the English National Curriculum with an IB sixth form and the American diploma with an IB option, which is why Creek Harbour cohorts are so mixed.

schoolClusters.city: The eastern suburbs, for families who arrived late
schoolClusters.note: Where seat availability often sends a mid-year arrival. The drive is longer, which changes the lesson slot rather than the tutoring, and the curriculum mix here is broader still.
schools: GEMS Wellington Academy Dubai Silicon Oasis

sections.heading: A new community with no school of its own
paragraphs: Most Dubai neighbourhoods grew around a school or acquired one quickly. Dubai Creek Harbour has not yet, and for a family living in Harbour Views or Creek Beach that single absence drives several downstream decisions. School choice is made across a water crossing rather than within walking distance, the drive becomes a permanent feature of the weekday, and the practical earliest lesson slot sits later than it would in a community with a school inside it.

The crossing is the specific constraint. Ras Al Khor Road and the Nad Al Hamar interchange between half past three and five o'clock are the reason a Creek Harbour parent collecting from Festival City or Al Jaddaf arrives home later than the distance suggests. For a family whose child attends a school in the eastern suburbs, the gap is wider still. Nothing about that is unmanageable, but it does mean the realistic weekday window here starts at five and more comfortably at half past six.

The second consequence is cohort mix. Because families chose across three different clusters, a single tower can contain an IB continuum student from Al Jaddaf, a British-curriculum IGCSE student from Festival City and an American-diploma student from the same campus. Those three are on different assessment calendars with different internal deadlines, which means the neighbourly advice a parent receives in the lift is frequently irrelevant to their own child.

The third is that the school-choice decision itself is still live for many households here. Families often take a seat and then reassess after a year. That makes the mapping work on this page genuinely useful: knowing what each route commits a student to, and what a move between routes costs academically, is worth more in this community than in one where the choice was made a decade ago.

sections.heading: The mid-year arrival, and what the first six weeks should actually do
paragraphs: A student who joins a Dubai school in January or February is not behind in the ordinary sense. They are missing specific things, and the difference between those two descriptions is worth several thousand dirhams. A student treated as generally weak gets a term of weekly subject review, most of which covers material they already know. A student treated as having a list gets two sessions a week for a month and then stops.

Writing the list is the entire job of the first session. That means a diagnostic against the new syllabus document rather than a general ability assessment: going through the syllabus content list and establishing, topic by topic, what the previous school covered. It is unglamorous work and it is the highest-value hour in the whole arrangement, because everything after it is either targeted or wasted.

There is a second list, less obvious and often more expensive to ignore: the assessment formats the student has never met. A CBSE arrival has not sat an alternative-to-practical paper. An American arrival has not written an Internal Assessment or met command-term marking. A British arrival joining the Diploma has never done Theory of Knowledge. None of those are content gaps and all of them cost marks until somebody shows the student how the component works.

The table sets out the common arrival routes into Creek Harbour's school options with the gap each one typically brings. Treat the week counts as a planning figure rather than a promise: a student's own starting point moves them, and the honest version is that the block ends when the list is closed rather than on a date fixed in advance.

sections.heading: A curriculum transition map, subject by subject
paragraphs: One competitor in this market has a single subheading about the IGCSE to IB gap. Nobody has a structured version, which is odd given how many Dubai families make a transition of some kind. For a community of recent arrivals the map is the most useful thing a tutoring page can publish, because it converts a vague anxiety into a set of decisions.

The pattern across almost every transition is the same shape: the content overlap is larger than families fear and the assessment difference is larger than they expect. A student moving from CBSE to IGCSE has met most of the mathematics and almost none of the question formats. A student moving from MYP to the Diploma has the inquiry habits and not the factual precision. In both cases the lost term comes from treating the assessment difference as a knowledge problem.

The map also exposes the transitions that are genuinely hard rather than merely unfamiliar. Joining the Diploma in the second term of DP1 is difficult because Internal Assessment timelines have already started and the components are sequenced. Joining A Level in Year 13 is harder still, since the first year's content is assumed and not revisited. A family weighing a move should know which category they are in, and a school is usually honest about it if asked directly.

What a tutor contributes here is narrow and valuable: knowing both syllabuses well enough to write the list. That is why the match matters for a bridging brief. Somebody who teaches IGCSE Mathematics well but has never seen a CBSE syllabus will find the gaps by trial and error over several weeks, which is exactly the cost the bridge was supposed to avoid.

sections.heading: What a bridge and a term of support cost in this market
paragraphs: Pricing in this market is unhelpfully opaque. Three of the six best-ranking Dubai tutoring pages publish no figure at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. The bands below are AED market rates from providers' own published pages and a 2026 Dubai cost survey, with the source named on each row, alongside the indicative monthly figure that band produces for a weekly session. None of it is an IB Gram price list.

For a Creek Harbour family the relevant comparison is usually between a short intensive bridge and a long standing arrangement. Two sessions a week for five weeks at the qualified-tutor band is ten hours. A weekly slot from October to May is roughly thirty. If the problem is genuinely a transition, the first of those is the right purchase and the second is a term of material the student already knows, delivered politely.

Monthly packaging is where the comparison gets muddied, so it is worth reading carefully. Published examples in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. A 2026 Dubai cost survey puts weekly one-hour tutoring at roughly AED 240-600 monthly at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-tier and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Ask three questions of any quote. Is the figure all-in, or does it precede assessment fees, materials and a minimum booking. Is value added tax included in what is shown. And what happens if the first tutor is not the right match, which for a bridging brief is a real risk because the pairing is more specific than usual.

sections.heading: Crossing the creek: in-home tutoring compared with one-to-one online
paragraphs: In-home tutoring is a real service, widely used in Dubai, and for younger children who will not stay on task without an adult present it has a genuine advantage. Market rates run roughly AED 180-500 an hour with travel priced in, according to a 2026 cost survey and tutors' own published pages. The question for a Creek Harbour family is what that costs in tutor choice, given both the water crossing and the specificity of a bridging brief.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. What we arrange here is one-to-one tuition delivered live over video, which means the pairing can be made on a genuinely narrow requirement: a tutor who knows both the CBSE syllabus the student left and the Cambridge syllabus they joined, or who has taught the Internal Assessment component an American arrival has never seen.

The geography sharpens the point. A travelling tutor's earliest Creek Harbour availability depends on where their previous appointment was, and the Ras Al Khor crossing in the late afternoon is the constraint. Families here are already absorbing one crossing a day for the school run; adding a second for a tutor, with the slot set by someone else's route, is a scheduling cost on top of the hourly one.

The honest limitation runs the other way for younger children. A Year 7 or Year 8 student who needs an adult in the room does better with shorter, more frequent online sessions and a parent within earshot for the first fortnight than with a long block on a school night, and better still with a home visit if that is available to them. We say that rather than arguing around it.

sections.heading: Arriving after the entry deadline closed
paragraphs: This is the administrative problem specific to late arrivals, and almost nobody writes about it. Examination entries close months before the papers. For the Cambridge March 2027 series, final entries are due 27 November 2026, with the exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades due 27 February 2027 and results reaching centres on Direct on 13 May 2027. A student who joined a school in January is being entered on evidence their new teachers have barely had time to gather.

Two things follow. The first is tier risk: a Cambridge subject entered at Core rather than Extended caps the grade, and a school with six weeks of evidence may reasonably choose the safer tier. If you believe the tier is wrong, the conversation has to happen before the entry closes, with evidence from the previous school in hand. After the deadline it becomes an administrative matter with its own rules.

The second is the November and March series as options. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, with a March series as well, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in May/June and November. The November 2026 Pearson final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states plainly that the correct zone version of the timetable must be used, since it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who missed a paper after using the wrong one.

For the IB, this page publishes no session or results date. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, and an unverified date on a page a family might plan around is worse than no date at all. Confirm the May session window and the results date with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org, and remember that the internal deadlines for coursework components are set by the school and fall considerably earlier.

sections.heading: Arabic and the UAE mandatory subjects, which arrivals rarely expect
paragraphs: Families moving to Dubai from outside the UAE are frequently surprised by this, and it is better learned on a page than in a Year 9 report. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements schools were to implement from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. The grades are reported separately from the IGCSE or Diploma result.

KHDA is specific about organisation. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies is taught in Arabic for Arab students and in the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs.

Two further points shape what tutoring in these subjects can legitimately be. Teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education in Dubai schools must hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a credential a parent can ask about. And for the mandatory UAE subjects, use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, which means support has to work from the school's own material rather than a parallel syllabus.

In practice a student arriving in Year 8 or Year 9 with no Arabic needs frequency rather than length. Two short sessions a week on script fluency and vocabulary retention achieve more than one long block, because the difficulty is recall between school lessons rather than comprehension. Families who start this in the first term after arriving find it manageable; those who leave it until Year 10 find the catch-up expensive in hours.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with coursework
paragraphs: Arrivals from systems without coursework are the group most exposed to the essay market that operates around Dubai, because they have never been taught where the line sits. At least one site ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments for a four-figure AED sum. A student who submits one has committed malpractice under IB rules, and the investigation and the consequence fall on them rather than on the vendor.

The legitimate side of the line is wide. A tutor can teach the assessment criteria and their mark allocations, explain what a command term requires, help narrow a research question until it will produce usable data, teach the method, statistics or laboratory technique an investigation needs, read a draft the student has written and ask harder questions about it than the student asked themselves, and point out where a claim is unsupported. For an arrival meeting the format for the first time, that teaching is genuinely necessary.

What a tutor must not do is supply text, rewrite a passage into its final form, or take over in any way that makes the submitted piece not the student's own. IB Gram does not supply assessed work, does not edit a draft into a finished submission, and declines requests framed that way. For a family new to the system, knowing that a reputable provider will say no to that request is itself useful information about the market.

There is a practical argument alongside the rules one, and for an arrival it is the stronger of the two. The skill an Internal Assessment tests is the skill the written papers test again, under time pressure, a few months later. A student who did not design their own investigation has not learned to design one, and the deficit resurfaces in a room where nobody can help. For a child already absorbing a new curriculum, a new school and a new country, the component is also the cheapest place to learn how this system actually judges work.
