process.title: Tell us where your child came from and where they have landed
process.description: The previous curriculum matters as much as the new one. A CBSE arrival into Year 11 IGCSE and an American arrival into the same class have different lists, and the tutor match depends on knowing both syllabuses rather than only the one being taught.

process.title: Diagnostic against the new syllabus document
process.description: The first session goes through the syllabus content list and establishes, topic by topic, what the previous school covered. It also identifies the assessment formats the student has never met. The output is a written list, and you get it whether or not you continue.

process.title: Agree the block, with an end date in sight
process.description: Usually two sessions a week for four to six weeks. The block closes when the list closes rather than on a fixed date, and we will say when it is finished rather than letting it roll into a standing commitment nobody reviewed.

process.title: Settle the slot against the real drive
process.description: The school your child attends sets the earliest workable time, and the Ras Al Khor crossing between half past three and five is the reason that time is later than the distance suggests. We agree a slot that holds through the year rather than one that works in October.

process.title: Deal with the entry administration separately
process.description: If the tier or the series is in question, that is a conversation with the school exams officer before the deadline, not a tutoring matter. We will tell you what evidence is worth putting in front of them and when the deadline for that series falls.

process.title: Decide what happens after the bridge
process.description: Some students stop. Others move to a weekly slot in one subject. Either is a legitimate outcome, and the handover note from the bridging tutor means a new weekly tutor does not start the diagnostic again from scratch.

whyPoints.title: The bridge is treated as a list, not a weakness
whyPoints.description: A mid-year arrival is missing specific topics and specific formats. Writing that list in the first session is what turns a term of general review into four to six weeks of targeted work, and it is the single biggest saving available to a family in this community.

whyPoints.title: Tutors are matched on two syllabuses, not one
whyPoints.description: Knowing what a CBSE or American school did not cover is as important as knowing the Cambridge or IB syllabus being joined. Because lessons run online, that pairing can be made from the full roster rather than from whoever crosses Ras Al Khor at five.

whyPoints.title: The commute is priced into the plan
whyPoints.description: Dubai Creek Harbour has no school inside it, so every family here has a crossing built into the weekday. Lesson slots are agreed against the actual school and the actual interchange rather than against a generic afternoon.

whyPoints.title: Market rates appear with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page names the provider or survey that published it, with the monthly figure a weekly session produces. A block of ten hours is priced as a block, not disguised as a monthly subscription.

whyPoints.title: The entry administration is explained rather than ignored
whyPoints.description: Tier decisions and series choices for a late arrival are made by the school before deadlines that fall months ahead of the papers. Knowing which deadline applies, and what evidence moves a tier decision, is worth more than an extra lesson.

whyPoints.title: No regulator or board approval is claimed
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Those bodies appear here to explain a rule or source a date, never to imply an endorsement that does not exist.

faqs.question: Is there a school inside Dubai Creek Harbour?
faqs.answer: Not a secondary school at present, which is why every family here has a commute decision built into the weekday. The nearest cluster is across Ras Al Khor in Al Jaddaf and Dubai Festival City, roughly ten to fifteen minutes outside peak, covering the IB continuum, the English National Curriculum with an IB sixth form and the American diploma. Families who arrived late and took whatever seat existed are often further east in Mirdif, Al Warqa or Academic City, which pushes the earliest workable lesson slot to around half past six. Confirm current provision against the KHDA school listing.

faqs.question: My daughter joined a Dubai school in January from CBSE. Is she behind?
faqs.answer: Probably not in the way it feels. A CBSE student arriving into IGCSE is usually ahead on algebra and arithmetic fluency, and missing specific things: the statistics and data-handling weighting, the applied question contexts, the extended-response marking conventions and the alternative-to-practical paper. That is a list rather than a general weakness, and a list closes in four to six weeks of two sessions a week. The expensive mistake is buying a term of general subject review, most of which covers material she already knows. Ask for a diagnostic against the new syllabus document first.

faqs.question: What assessment formats do American-curriculum arrivals usually find new?
faqs.answer: Three in particular. Structured papers with method marks, where working earns credit even when the final answer is wrong, which changes how a question should be written out. Command-term marking, where outline, explain, discuss and evaluate each require a different answer shape. And coursework, specifically the Internal Assessment, which has no real analogue in most American high school programmes and carries a substantial share of each Diploma subject grade. None of those are content gaps, and all of them cost marks until the student is shown how the component works.

faqs.question: How late is too late to join the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: The designed entry point is the start of DP1, and joining in the first term is straightforward. Joining in DP1 term two is difficult but done: Internal Assessment timelines have started, the components are sequenced and the Diploma core is already running. Joining in DP2 is very hard, because two years of content and four to six internal assessments are assumed. A school will usually be honest about this if you ask directly. For a family arriving mid-Year-12, A Level is often the less disrupted route precisely because it is linear and examination-weighted.

faqs.question: Did we miss the exam entry deadline by arriving in January?
faqs.answer: Possibly, depending on the series. For the Cambridge March 2027 series, final entries are due 27 November 2026, so a January arrival is after it. Cambridge runs June, November and March series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. The school exams officer holds the answer for your child specifically. If a tier was chosen on limited evidence, raise it with the head of subject before the next entry closes rather than after results arrive.

faqs.question: Can the tier my child was entered at be changed?
faqs.answer: It is an administrative process with its own deadlines rather than something a tutor can influence, and the window matters. A Cambridge subject entered at Core caps the grade available for that series, and a school with only a few weeks of evidence may reasonably have chosen the safer option. If you have evidence from the previous school showing stronger attainment, put it in front of the head of subject and the exams officer before the entry closes. After the deadline, the school is working within the board's rules on amendments.

faqs.question: Does my child have to study Arabic even though we just moved here?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, under KHDA requirements schools were to implement from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, and the grades are reported separately. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for the first-language and Arab Islamic Education groups. A student arriving with no Arabic needs frequency: two short sessions a week beat one long one, because retention is the difficulty.

faqs.question: What should the very first tutoring session for an arrival actually produce?
faqs.answer: A written list. Specifically, a topic-by-topic comparison against the new syllabus document establishing what the previous school covered, plus a second list of the assessment formats the student has never met. Everything after that is either targeted or wasted, which is why this hour is the most valuable one in the arrangement. A session that consists of general conversation and a textbook exercise has not done the job. Ask for the list in writing, and keep it, because it is also what tells you when the bridge is finished.

faqs.question: How long does the Ras Al Khor crossing add to our afternoon?
faqs.answer: Enough to change the lesson slot. Outside peak the drive from Creek Harbour to Al Jaddaf or Festival City is ten to fifteen minutes; between half past three and five the Nad Al Hamar interchange makes it considerably longer. For a child at a school in Academic City or Dubai Silicon Oasis, allow twenty-five to thirty minutes outside peak and more during it. The practical consequence is that five o'clock is the realistic floor for most Creek Harbour families and half past six is more comfortable, which is worth settling before booking a weekly slot.

faqs.question: Is a short intensive block better value than a weekly slot?
faqs.answer: For a transition, yes, and it is the main saving available in this community. Two sessions a week for five weeks is ten hours. A weekly slot from October to May is roughly thirty. If the problem is genuinely a list of missing topics and unfamiliar formats, the ten-hour block closes it and the thirty-hour arrangement spends twenty hours on material the student already knows. If the problem is a subject the student has never understood, the reverse is true. The diagnostic tells you which case you are in.

faqs.question: Do tutors come to apartments in Dubai Creek Harbour?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Independent in-home tutors work across Dubai at market rates of roughly AED 180-500 an hour with travel built in, per a 2026 Dubai cost survey and tutors' own published pages. For a bridging brief the trade-off is particularly sharp, because the useful tutor is one who knows both the syllabus your child left and the one they joined. That pairing is narrow, and narrowing it further by driving distance tends to eliminate it.

faqs.question: My son has never written an Internal Assessment. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: With the criteria and the research question, in that order, and early. The criteria are published and they are effectively the instructions; most students have never read them properly. The research question is chosen in roughly the first week of the component, and a question too broad to answer is the most expensive early mistake available. A tutor can explain the criteria and their mark allocations, help narrow the question until the data collection is realistic, and respond to a draft your son has written. A tutor does not supply text or take the work over.

faqs.question: Which schools near Dubai Creek Harbour run the IB continuum?
faqs.answer: The closest is Swiss International Scientific School Dubai in Al Jaddaf, roughly ten to fifteen minutes outside peak, which runs a bilingual IB continuum through to the Diploma. Further east, Uptown International School in Mirdif runs an IB continuum, around twenty-five minutes away. Deira International School in Festival City runs the English National Curriculum with an IB sixth form, which is a different proposition: IGCSE at sixteen and then a choice. Confirm current programme offerings with each school and against the KHDA school listing, because they change by year group and intake.

faqs.question: What does a four to six week bridge cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Two sessions a week for five weeks is ten hours. At the market band for a qualified online subject tutor, which published figures put at roughly AED 150-300 an hour with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, that is the range to budget against. For specialist Diploma work, published rates run AED 200-450 and upwards, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Those are market figures rather than IB Gram prices. Ask whether the quote is all-in, whether value added tax is included, and what happens if the pairing turns out to be wrong.

faqs.question: How do we know when the bridge is finished?
faqs.answer: By the list, which is why it has to be written down. Each item is either closed or still open, and when the content items are closed and the student has sat at least one timed attempt at each unfamiliar paper format, the block is done. At that point some families stop and others move to a weekly slot in a single subject. Both are legitimate, and a provider that cannot tell you the block has finished is selling a subscription rather than a solution. Ask for a handover note either way.

dubai/dubai-creek-harbour.closingHeading: Start with where your child came from
dubai/dubai-creek-harbour.closingBody: Almost every family in Dubai Creek Harbour arrived recently, and almost every academic problem here is a transition rather than a weakness. The cheapest useful step is a diagnostic against the new syllabus that produces a written list of missing topics and unfamiliar assessment formats, because that list is what turns a term of general review into a four to six week block with an end in sight. Tell us the previous curriculum and the new school, and we will match a tutor who knows both. Lessons are one-to-one and delivered live over video, so no second crossing of the creek is needed.

dubai/dubai-festival-city.tutorsIntro: These are the tutor profiles that come up most often against Dubai Festival City requests: Diploma sciences and maths, IGCSE separate sciences, and the internally assessed work that sits between them. Each teaches a named specification, and you see the match and the plan before a single lesson is booked.

intro.heading: The half of the course nobody timetables
paragraphs: A Dubai Festival City family rarely arrives at tutoring because a teacher said something alarming. The usual trigger is a mock paper that came back twelve marks below the term grades with no obvious explanation. The classroom work was done. Homework was submitted. Something still did not transfer. The explanation is almost always the same: the taught course and the examined course are not the same object, and the difference between them is carried by the student, alone, in hours that appear on no timetable.

Both the Diploma and IGCSE are designed on that assumption. A teacher with a class of twenty-two can present content, model one worked example and set practice. The teacher cannot sit beside your child while they discover that they can follow a titration calculation on the board and lose the thread entirely when the same calculation arrives wrapped in six lines of unfamiliar context. That discovery happens at a desk at home, usually at ten at night, usually alone, and usually it does not happen at all.

This is also why a Festival City parent can be handed two accurate and contradictory accounts of the same child. The school says the work is going well. The mock mark says otherwise. Neither is lying. Class performance measures whether a student can follow instruction. Examination performance measures whether they can do the same thing cold, under timing, from a question written by someone who has never met them. Tutoring is only worth paying for if it works on the second thing.

So the question that matters is not which subject to book. It is which part of the independent half has broken. The student may not know the command terms. They may be unable to begin a question without a prompt. They may never have written to a criterion descriptor. They may have sixty pages of neat notes and no retrieval practice whatsoever. Those are four separate problems with four separate fixes, and a tutor who diagnoses the wrong one will be pleasant, expensive and ineffective.

IB Gram starts from that diagnosis. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, scheduled around the Festival City school run rather than around a tutor's driving radius. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. What a Festival City family gets instead is a specialist in the specific paper their child sits, which is a better trade than proximity. The sections below set out what the market charges in AED, which deadlines sit months ahead of the exam, and precisely where a tutor has to stop.

Nothing here promises a grade. No tutor can promise one, and a page that does is telling you more about itself than about your child. What follows is the material a Festival City parent needs in order to decide properly: the rates, the calendar, the regulator, the criteria by letter, and what honest coursework support looks like in practice.

dubai/dubai-festival-city.programmesIntro: Festival City children sit three main routes, and often more than one inside a single family. The notes below describe each programme as it actually runs in Dubai. Read the local note under each: that is the part which changes what tutoring has to do, and it is the part a generic programme summary leaves out.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries internally assessed work marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB, worth roughly a fifth of the grade. The external papers are sat in one session, so two years of work converges on about three weeks. The independent load is heaviest here: reading, past papers, an Extended Essay and an internal assessment per subject all run at the same time.
programmes.countryNote: Deira International School runs the Diploma on the Festival City site itself, so a short drive replaces the commute most Dubai families accept. One consequence is that the school's own internal deadlines, not the IB's, decide when drafts are due. Festival City Diploma requests cluster around Chemistry HL, Mathematics AA HL and Economics, in that order.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years assessed against four criteria per subject group, each marked out of eight and converted into a 1-7 grade by a published boundary table. There are no public examinations until the optional eAssessment at the end of Year 11. Marks accumulate from interim tasks, so a student can be assessed on criterion C in October and not meet criterion D until February, which makes a single reported grade quite hard to interpret.
programmes.countryNote: Because Deira International School carries the full continuum, a Festival City child can move from the Primary Years Programme into the Diploma without ever sitting an external paper before Year 12. That is comfortable right up to Diploma year one, when the first properly timed paper arrives with no history of timed practice behind it.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years of specification-led courses examined at the end of Year 11. Every syllabus carries a code - 0580, 0620, 4MA1 - and the code decides the papers, the tiering and the formula sheet a candidate is given. Cambridge offers Core and Extended routes with different grade ceilings on several subjects; Pearson runs a single tier on most. A tutor who never asks which code your child is entered for is guessing at the paper.
programmes.countryNote: Festival City and the Al Garhoud schools next door sit largely with Cambridge, but Pearson appears often enough in Mathematics and the sciences that it must be checked rather than assumed. Ask the school for the code printed on the entry form, not the subject name written in the report.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The Primary Years Programme replaces subject examinations with transdisciplinary units and a report written against learning outcomes rather than marks. Reading fluency, number-fact recall and written stamina still decide how Year 7 goes, and they are exactly the things a prose report can obscure. The PYP Exhibition at the end of Year 6 is the first extended independent project most children attempt, and the first honest test of whether they can plan their own work.
programmes.countryNote: Festival City primary parents usually arrive holding a report full of positive sentences and no number anywhere in it. A thirty-minute diagnostic on reading rate and arithmetic recall tells you more than the report can, and at that age it is the cheapest useful thing available.

dubai/dubai-festival-city.subjectsIntro: Subject requests from Dubai Festival City cluster around the components with the heaviest independent load. Each note below says what the component actually assesses and which part of it students routinely under-practise. Levels are listed because the same subject name hides two courses with different ceilings and different papers.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the Higher Level papers. The scientific investigation is internally assessed. Most lost marks are not chemistry at all: they are uncertainty handling, conclusions that outrun the data, and graphs with a line of best fit nobody could defend under questioning.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields reward students who can read a situation before reaching for an equation. The recurring failure is algebraic: a correct physical argument abandoned halfway because the rearrangement got messy. Paper 3 rewards data skills that are almost never practised outside the two lessons spent setting up the investigation.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The content volume makes Biology look like a memory subject, which is why students revise it by rereading. Marks are lost on precision of terminology and on command terms: an answer that describes when the question asked for an explanation gets no credit, however accurate the description was.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The Higher Level course is the one most Festival City students name when they ask for help. Calculus and proof are the usual pressure points, but the exploration is where whole grades move, because it is marked against five criteria and treated by students as a write-up rather than a piece of mathematics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and heavy graphical-calculator work. Students who chose this route to avoid proof are often surprised by the volume of interpretation required: a correct regression line with no comment on its validity scores less than a weaker model discussed honestly.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry the marks, and diagrams drawn from memory without axes labelled lose them. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries on real published articles, which means the choice of article determines the ceiling before any analysis is written.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen analysis under timing, which rewards a repeatable reading procedure rather than wider reading. The Individual Oral asks students to connect a global issue to two texts, and it is usually the first assessment where a Festival City student has to build an argument with no prompt sheet.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The tools are straightforward; applying them to an unfamiliar case study under timing is not. Students lose marks by describing a business rather than evaluating a decision, and by ignoring the quantitative sections because they came to the subject expecting prose.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: The Core and Extended routes have different grade ceilings, so the tier decision taken in Year 10 can cap a grade before any revision starts. Extended candidates lose most marks on multi-step problems where no method is prompted and on questions that mix two topics in one stem.

subjects.name: IGCSE separate and co-ordinated sciences
subjects.description: Three separate sciences and the co-ordinated route cover different content at different depths, and the entry decision affects sixth-form options. Practical skills are examined on paper, so students who have done the experiments still need deliberate practice at reading someone else's method and spotting its flaw.

dubai/dubai-festival-city.regionsIntro: Festival City sits on the creek with Al Garhoud on one side and the eastern suburbs behind it, which gives families an unusually short school run by Dubai standards. The notes below cover the communities whose children share the same schools and the same evening timetable.

regions.name: Dubai Festival City
regions.note: Al Badia villas, the marina apartments and the Festival Tower blocks, with Deira International School on the same side of the main road. For most families here the school run is measured in minutes, which makes an early-evening session genuinely workable.

regions.name: Al Garhoud
regions.note: Older low-rise villas with several long-established schools inside the community. Garhoud families often have children at two different schools on two different boards, so sibling sessions have to be matched to specification, not just to age.

regions.name: Al Rashidiya
regions.note: Between the airport road and the creek, with a mix of villa compounds and apartment blocks. Traffic here is shaped by airport shift patterns rather than by school times, which pushes many families towards a later slot.

regions.name: Nad Al Hamar
regions.note: Villa community behind Festival City, feeding a spread of Dubai schools rather than one local anchor. Longer bus journeys are common, so an 18:00 start is more realistic than 16:30 for secondary students.

regions.name: Al Warqa
regions.note: Large established villa district with several Indian-curriculum and British-curriculum schools. Requests from Al Warqa skew towards IGCSE Mathematics and the separate sciences in Years 10 and 11.

regions.name: Mirdif
regions.note: Dense villa suburb immediately east, with a cluster of schools inside its own boundary. Mirdif families frequently ask for MYP criterion work, because several of the local schools run the full IB continuum.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis
regions.note: Apartment-heavy free-zone community a short drive down the Nad Al Hamar road. Many households here have both parents working on site, which makes a fixed weekday slot easier to protect than a weekend one.

regions.name: Al Mizhar and Al Khawaneej
regions.note: Lower-density villa areas further east, where the drive to a Dubai Marina tuition centre would cost more time than the lesson. These are the communities where online delivery stops being a compromise and starts being the obvious choice.

schoolClusters.city: Festival City, Al Badia and Al Garhoud
schoolClusters.note: The schools within a short drive of a Festival City address, covering the IB continuum, the American diploma and the British route to IGCSE. Students we support attend schools across this cluster; the point of listing them is that their boards and syllabus codes differ, and the entry code is what a tutor needs.

schoolClusters.city: The eastern suburbs behind Festival City
schoolClusters.note: Mirdif, Al Warqa, Al Mizhar and Silicon Oasis supply most of the IGCSE and MYP requests that reach us from this side of the city. Several run the continuum, several run Cambridge, and a few run Pearson in Mathematics only, which is exactly why the code matters more than the school name.

dubai/dubai-festival-city.modesIntro: Three shapes of tutoring account for almost every Festival City request. The difference between them is not price per hour but what the hour is spent on, and choosing the wrong shape is the commonest way a tutoring budget gets wasted over a term.

modes.description: A fixed slot, the same tutor each week, working through the specification your child is actually entered for. The session is built around their own marked work, so the tutor is teaching the gaps rather than the syllabus in order. This is the shape that suits a student whose problem is content coverage or technique rather than organisation.

sections.heading: What a Festival City search for a tutor usually means
paragraphs: The literal answer is short. Parents in Dubai Festival City searching for IB and IGCSE tutors want someone to take responsibility for the part of the course their child is supposed to do alone. That part is substantial. It is unsupervised, it is unmeasured until a mock paper measures it, and it is where the gap between a 5 and a 7 almost entirely lives. Class time is not the problem these families are trying to solve.

It helps to separate the course into what a teacher can reliably deliver to a group and what only the student can do. A teacher can explain electrolysis to twenty-two people at once. A teacher cannot make twenty-two people each attempt forty unprompted questions on electrolysis and then diagnose, individually, which of the forty went wrong and why. That second task is the entire content of good tutoring, and it is the reason a one-to-one hour is not just a smaller version of a classroom hour.

The table below splits the main components that way. The right-hand column is the early warning: the observable sign that the independent half has stopped happening, usually weeks before a mark confirms it. Festival City parents who recognise something in that column generally do not need a full programme of tutoring. They need six weeks of properly targeted work on one habit, and then a review.

That is also the honest reason online delivery suits this. The constraint on a Festival City family is not distance to a tutor; Deira International School is minutes away and the Garhoud schools barely further. The constraint is finding someone who knows the specific paper well enough to diagnose at this level of detail. Online one-to-one widens that pool from whoever drives locally to whoever teaches the course.

sections.heading: Command terms: the vocabulary that decides the mark
paragraphs: Both the IB and the two IGCSE boards publish a list of command terms, and both mark to them strictly. The verb at the start of a question is an instruction about structure, not a stylistic preference. A student who answers every question with everything they know about the topic will score well on the ones that happened to ask for everything they know, and will be puzzled by the rest. Festival City students arriving from a strong continuum school are particularly prone to this, because continuum assessment rewards thoughtful discussion and the external papers reward obedience.

The fix is mechanical and fast, which makes it one of the highest-return things a tutor can do in the first month. The student learns what each verb obliges them to produce, practises producing it, and then marks their own attempt against the published scheme until the gap closes. This is not a study skill in the vague sense. It is a specific, checkable behaviour: see the verb, choose the structure, write to that structure.

The table lists the terms that cost the most marks in practice. The pattern across all of them is the same - the student under-delivers on structure while over-delivering on content. A six-mark explain question answered with four accurate descriptive sentences scores badly, and the student walks away believing the subject is unfair rather than believing they answered a different question.

A word of caution about where the terms come from. Each board publishes its own glossary, and the definitions differ slightly between the IB subject guides and the Cambridge and Pearson specifications. Use the glossary for the board your child actually sits, available on the board's own site, rather than a generic list. The distinctions are small but they are the sort of small that decides two marks on every long question.

sections.heading: Internal assessment criteria, named by letter
paragraphs: Internally assessed work is the part of the Diploma most parents understand least and most students treat most casually. It is marked by the teacher against criteria the IB publishes, moderated centrally, and worth a meaningful share of the subject grade. Unlike an examination it is not a test of recall under pressure. It is a test of whether the student can design, execute and discuss a piece of work to a published descriptor, with time to get it right.

Which means the marks are largely available in advance. A student who reads the criteria, knows what each letter rewards and writes to it is competing on comprehension rather than luck. A student who writes a good piece of work and hopes it maps onto the criteria is leaving marks on the table in the one component where leaving marks is avoidable. The difference is almost never ability. It is whether anyone sat down with the descriptor and translated it into a checklist.

The table names the criteria by letter for the components Festival City families ask about most. Treat it as a map rather than as the authority: the IB revises subject guides on a rolling cycle, and your child's teacher works to the current guide for their cohort. Confirm the letters and the mark totals against that guide, which the school can supply, before planning any work around them.

There is a boundary around this support, and it is worth stating before the detail. A tutor teaches the criteria, questions the method and asks the student to defend their decisions. A tutor does not become the author of any part of the work. That line is covered in full further down this page, because it is the single place where well-meaning help can put a student in front of a school's academic honesty process.

sections.heading: Where Festival City students study, and what that changes
paragraphs: Festival City is unusual in Dubai for having a large international school inside the development rather than a drive away. Deira International School sits on the same side of the main road as most of the residential clusters, running the IB continuum, which means a Festival City child can plausibly go from Foundation Stage to Diploma without changing site. Around it, Al Garhoud holds several long-established schools on other boards, and behind it the eastern suburbs add Cambridge and Pearson options in volume.

The practical consequence for tutoring is specification spread. A single Festival City street can contain a Diploma student, an IGCSE student on Cambridge, an IGCSE student on Pearson and an American-diploma student taking Advanced Placement. These are four different courses with four different assessment models, and a tutor matched on year group alone will teach the wrong one competently. This is why the matching question is always the syllabus code rather than the school.

The short school run has a second effect, which is more useful than it sounds. Secondary students in Festival City are typically home earlier than peers commuting from the newer Dubailand communities, so a 16:30 or 17:00 session is realistic rather than aspirational. That matters because the best slot for cognitively demanding work is not the one left over at the end of the evening, and families who can protect an earlier hour should.

Keep the schools and the regulator separate in your thinking. KHDA licenses and inspects Dubai private schools and publishes inspection outcomes on a six-band scale; it does not license private tutors, and no tutoring platform is inspected in that framework. A school's published rating tells you about the school. It tells you nothing about whether your particular child is on top of the independent half of their course.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges to cover the solo hours
paragraphs: Three of the most visible tutoring sites in this market publish no price at all, and two of the remaining ones quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family budgets in. So the first useful thing a page like this can do is put the AED bands on the screen with the names of the providers who published them, and let you judge where a quote sits.

The figures in the table were read from provider sites and from a published Dubai rate survey in October 2026. They are market rates, not IB Gram's price list. The pattern they show is consistent: the same hour costs roughly double at the specialist end of the market compared with the budget end, and an in-home visit carries a premium that is largely travel time being billed to you. Festival City's short school run reduces that travel penalty compared with outlying communities, but it does not remove it.

What the bands do not show is the thing that actually decides value, which is what the hour is spent on. An AED 150 hour spent supervising homework and an AED 280 hour spent rebuilding a student's approach to Paper 3 are not comparable units. Before comparing any two quotes, ask each provider which specification they will teach, what they will do in the first session, and what they will send you afterwards. The answers separate providers faster than the rate does.

For IB Gram's own arrangement, the honest position is that there is no fixed public rate card on this page, because the rate depends on level, subject scarcity and session length. sections.heading: Counting backwards from the paper, not forwards from today
paragraphs: Most tutoring plans are built forwards: we start now, we do an hour a week, we see how it goes. Examination boards do not work forwards. They work from fixed dates, and several of the dates that constrain your options fall months before the paper itself. A family that discovers an entry deadline after it has passed has lost a whole series, and no amount of tutoring recovers that.

Cambridge publishes its key dates in advance, and the March 2027 series makes the point cleanly. Final entries are due in late November 2026 for examinations that begin in February 2027, with results on Direct in May and certificates in late June. The entry carries the syllabus code and, where one exists, the tier - so the decision about Core or Extended is taken in November and determines the grade ceiling for a paper sat three months later.

Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May/June and November, with the November 2026 timetable running to mid-November and results reaching students in January. Both boards publish provisional timetables ahead of each series and both revise them, so a plan should link the live official timetable rather than restate dates from a tutoring page. Every centre is also allocated to one of six Cambridge administrative zones, and using the wrong zone's timetable is a documented way to miss an examination.

IB session dates are a different matter and this page will not state them. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no date here has been confirmed from the IB directly. UAE schools sit the May session; for the exact window, the registration deadlines and the results date, ask your child's IB coordinator or check ibo.org, and build the plan from what they give you.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with coursework, and where it stops
paragraphs: This is the part of the market with real exposure, and it is worth being blunt about it. There are providers in this SERP selling finished internal assessments at a fixed price. A student who submits one is exposed to a school's academic honesty process and, under IB rules, to a malpractice finding that can cost the whole diploma. The commercial risk sits with the provider. The academic risk sits entirely with your child.

What legitimate support looks like is narrower and more useful. A tutor teaches the criteria and the mark allocation. A tutor interrogates the research question until it is answerable. A tutor questions the method, the sample, the controls and the maths. A tutor reads a draft and responds with questions - why this comparison, what does this graph show that the table does not, which limitation would an examiner notice first. The student then goes away and makes their own decisions, in their own words.

What a tutor must never do is supply text, restructure an argument on the student's behalf, or hand back a marked-up document the student simply retypes. The test we apply is simple: at the end of the process the student should be able to defend every choice in the work under questioning, without notes, because every choice was theirs. If they cannot, the support went too far, whoever provided it.

The same boundary applies to the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay, the Personal Project and IGCSE coursework. Ask any prospective tutor directly how they handle a draft. A provider who describes handing back an improved version is describing something that puts your child at risk, and the fact that it is offered openly does not make it safe.
bullets: A tutor teaches criteria by letter and the mark allocation behind each

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the IB
paragraphs: Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of the international curriculum it is licensed for. KHDA's published guidance requires it, and its requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. For a Festival City family on the Diploma or IGCSE track, this means there is a second timetable running alongside the one the tutoring budget is usually aimed at, and it is the one most often ignored until a report arrives.

The rules have specific structural consequences. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combining the two groups is prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic must hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

Instructional time is counted in forty-minute lesson units, with schools permitted to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and with a recommendation that no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than twenty-five minutes. Content is also constrained: using different or additional material without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited. That matters for tutoring, because it limits how far a tutor can stray from the school's own material in these subjects.

Practically, treat Arabic as its own stream with its own tutor and its own goal rather than as a subject to be rescued in June. A non-Arab student working towards Arabic as an additional language is on a different path from an Arab student sitting Arabic as a first language, and these are separate matches. Note also, for later, that Arabic and Islamic Education are excluded from the five-subject count the Ministry uses for British-track equivalency.

sections.heading: Coverage, availability and what happens when nobody is free
paragraphs: No tutoring platform covers every subject at every level at every hour, and the ones that imply otherwise are simply not disclosing their gaps. Scarcity in this market is predictable: Higher Level sciences and Higher Level Mathematics tighten sharply in the weeks before a session, Arabic as a first language is thin all year, and specialist Diploma options such as Psychology or Global Politics are a smaller pool than the headline subject lists suggest.

The table sets out the honest position by subject, including what happens when a UAE-based specialist is not available. The fallback is a specialist based outside the UAE, most often in India, teaching the same specification online, with the time difference and the tutor's base stated before anything is booked. That is disclosed rather than concealed, which distinguishes it from routing a Dubai parent to a foreign phone number and letting them assume local delivery.

On the legal position, which parents increasingly ask about: private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no figure appears here.

Two further points worth knowing. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction, so hiring your child's own teacher privately is not a route to pursue. And a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a specific thing issued to training institutes. IB Gram holds no such permit and operates no UAE centre; lessons are delivered online.

process.title: Send the syllabus code, not the subject name
process.description: Tell us the code on the entry form - 0580, 0620, 4MA1 - or the IB subject and level with the school's own deadline dates. That single detail decides which papers your child sits and therefore which tutor is the right match. A request listing only the subject and year group takes longer to fill and fills less accurately.

process.title: One diagnostic hour on the student's own marked work
process.description: The first session is spent on returned scripts and a short set of unprompted questions, not on teaching. The aim is to identify which part of the independent half has broken: content, command terms, unprompted starts, or retrieval. Everything after this is shaped by what that hour finds, and you receive it in writing.

process.title: Fix the slot around the Festival City school run
process.description: Short commutes here make an earlier session realistic, which is worth having for demanding work. We agree a protected weekly slot and a fallback time, with the tutor's base and time zone stated before you confirm. Two reliable slots are worth more than four optimistic ones nobody keeps.

process.title: Work a plan built backwards from the session
process.description: The plan starts at the examination or coursework deadline and works back to this week, with entry deadlines, mock windows and the school's own draft dates marked. For Cambridge and Pearson the official timetable is linked; for IB dates we work from what your child's coordinator confirms rather than from a figure on a web page.

process.title: Review against marks, then stop or continue
process.description: Every six to eight weeks we compare the plan against actual marked work and decide whether to continue, change tutor or finish. Tutoring that has done its job should end. A provider with no review point and no exit is selling a subscription rather than solving a problem.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the paper, not to the postcode
whyPoints.description: Because lessons run online, the match is made on who teaches your child's specification rather than on who lives within a short drive of Festival City. For a Higher Level subject with a small specialist pool, that is the difference between the right tutor and the available one.

whyPoints.title: The independent half is the actual target
whyPoints.description: Sessions are built around unprompted practice, command terms and retrieval rather than re-explaining what was taught in class this week. Re-teaching the taught half feels productive and changes very little, because that half was never the problem.

whyPoints.title: Criteria named by letter, with the marks shown
whyPoints.description: Internal assessment support starts from the published descriptors and their mark allocations, so the student knows where the marks are before they begin. Most coursework marks are lost to a descriptor nobody read, not to a lack of ability.

whyPoints.title: Figures in AED, with sources and dates
whyPoints.description: Every rate on this page is attributed to the provider or survey that published it and dated to when it was read. You can check each one and judge any quote against it, including ours.

whyPoints.title: A coursework boundary we will not move
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback. No part of an assessed task is produced for the student. The test is whether your child can defend every choice in the work unaided, and that test protects them.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed before you book
whyPoints.description: If no UAE-based specialist is free for a Higher Level subject, you are told, and told where the fallback tutor is based and what time the session would run. Nothing about delivery is left for you to discover afterwards.

faqs.question: Why did my child's mock come back twelve marks below their term grade?
faqs.answer: Because the two measure different things. A term grade largely reflects work done with support available - class explanation, homework help, a second attempt. A mock measures what the student can do cold, under timing, from a question written by a stranger. A gap of ten to fifteen marks between the two usually means the independent half of the course is not happening: no unprompted practice, no timed papers, no command-term work. That is diagnosable and fixable, and it is fixable faster than parents expect, because it is a habit problem rather than a knowledge problem. The first thing to do is read the mock script itself rather than the mark.

faqs.question: Can IB Gram send a tutor to a villa in Dubai Festival City?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide in-home tutoring anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Lessons for Dubai Festival City families are delivered one-to-one over live video, with screen sharing for working through scripts and past papers. The trade is deliberate: instead of choosing from tutors who happen to live within driving distance of Al Badia, you choose from specialists in the exact paper your child sits. For a Higher Level science or a specialist Diploma option, that pool difference matters more than physical presence does.

faqs.question: How much do IB and IGCSE tutors charge for a Dubai Festival City family?
faqs.answer: Market rates in Dubai run roughly AED 45-150 an hour at the budget online end, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180-500 for in-home visits with travel included, and AED 200-450 or more for an IB or IGCSE specialist. Premium providers advertise up to AED 650. Those figures come from provider listings and a published Dubai rate survey read in October 2026, not from IB Gram's price list. Ask us for our figure before booking and compare it against those bands. Also ask what the hour is spent on, because that varies more than the rate does.

faqs.question: Which schools do Dubai Festival City children usually attend?
faqs.answer: Deira International School sits inside Festival City itself and runs the IB continuum, so many local children attend without a meaningful commute. Al Garhoud next door holds several long-established schools on other boards, and the eastern suburbs behind - Mirdif, Al Warqa, Silicon Oasis - add Cambridge and Pearson options in volume. The practical consequence is specification spread: one street can hold a Diploma student, a Cambridge IGCSE student, a Pearson IGCSE student and an American-diploma student. That is why a tutor match should start from the syllabus code rather than the school name.

faqs.question: What are command terms, and why do they cost so many marks?
faqs.answer: Command terms are the verbs that begin examination questions - state, describe, explain, deduce, evaluate, justify - and each one obliges a particular structure of answer. Both the IB and the IGCSE boards publish glossaries and mark to them strictly. A student who answers every question with everything they know scores well only on the questions that asked for that. The commonest loss is a six-mark explain question answered with accurate description: the content is right, the structure is wrong, and most of the marks are unreachable. Drilling the verbs is mechanical, quick, and one of the highest-return things a tutor can do early.

faqs.question: How is the Diploma maths exploration marked, criterion by criterion?
faqs.answer: The exploration is assessed against five criteria lettered A to E - presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics - totalling twenty marks. Criterion E carries the largest share and is the one students most often treat as a formality, submitting mathematics that is correct but below the level of their course. The fix is to choose a topic that forces genuine use of course-level mathematics, then write the reflection as analysis rather than as narrative. Confirm the current criteria and marks against your child's own subject guide, which the school can supply, before planning work around them.

faqs.question: Is the science internal assessment the same in every Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: The sciences share a common model for the internally assessed scientific investigation, marked against criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The criteria wording and the mark total are published in the current subject guide, and the guides are revised on a rolling cycle, so check your child's cohort guide rather than an older summary. Evaluation is where most available marks are abandoned: students report what happened and stop short of discussing honestly what weakened the data and what a better design would have done. That discussion is the cheapest set of marks in the component.

faqs.question: My child has notes for everything and remembers nothing. What fixes that?
faqs.answer: Note-making feels like studying and is almost entirely ineffective as revision, because it is a copying task rather than a recall task. The fix is retrieval: closing the notes and attempting questions, then checking. In practice this means a weekly cycle of unprompted questions on older topics, marked against the published scheme, with the gaps logged and retested a fortnight later. Most students resist it initially because it is uncomfortable and because the first attempt reveals how little has stuck. That revelation is the point. Six weeks of this changes mock performance more reliably than any amount of rereading.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE syllabus code my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's examinations officer, not the subject teacher, and ask for the code on the entry form - a four-digit number such as 0580 or 0620 for Cambridge, or a code such as 4MA1 for Pearson Edexcel. Also ask which tier, because Cambridge runs Core and Extended routes with different grade ceilings on several subjects. Reports and school newsletters usually give the subject name only, and the subject name is not enough: two children in the same year at neighbouring Festival City schools can sit entirely different papers in what the report calls Physics.

faqs.question: Why does a Cambridge entry deadline fall months before the exam?
faqs.answer: Because entries drive logistics: paper production, zone allocation and centre arrangements all run from them. For the Cambridge March 2027 series, final entries are due on 27 November 2026 for examinations starting 3 February 2027, with results on Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. The entry carries the syllabus code and the tier, so a decision taken in November sets the grade ceiling for a paper sat in February. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that using the wrong zone's timetable can cause a candidate to miss an examination.

faqs.question: Can a tutor look at a draft of my child's extended essay?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can teach the criteria and their mark allocations, interrogate the research question, question the method and the use of sources, and respond to a draft with questions rather than corrections. What a tutor must not do is supply text, restructure the argument on the student's behalf, or return a rewritten version to be retyped. The test is whether the student can defend every choice in the essay unaided. If they cannot, the support went too far, and the exposure under IB academic honesty rules falls on the student rather than on whoever provided it.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education part of the five subjects the Ministry counts?
faqs.answer: On the British track they are excluded from the count. The Ministry of Education requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One ranking tutoring site publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong. Both subjects remain compulsory in Dubai schools under KHDA rules regardless of equivalency, so they still need attention. Verify current requirements on moe.gov.ae before relying on any of this.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Dubai need a permit from MoHRE?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Applications go through MoHRE's own channels, where the service is listed with no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount is quoted here. Ask any individual tutor whether they hold the permit, because it is a reasonable question and a quick one to answer.

faqs.question: What time can a lesson start after the Festival City school run?
faqs.answer: Earlier than in most of Dubai, which is a genuine advantage. Families inside Festival City or Al Badia whose children attend the school on the same site are often home by mid-afternoon, making a 16:30 or 17:00 start realistic for secondary students. Al Rashidiya and Nad Al Hamar households with longer bus routes are usually looking at 18:00. The reason this matters is that demanding work should not be scheduled into the leftover hour at the end of the evening. Where an earlier slot is available, protect it, and keep a single agreed fallback time rather than a floating one.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for Higher Level Physics?
faqs.answer: You are told, before booking, rather than matched with someone approximately suitable. Higher Level Physics is the scarcest of the sciences in this market and tightens further from February onwards. The options are a specialist based outside the UAE, most often in India, teaching the same specification online with the time difference and the tutor's base stated up front, or a place on a waiting list with a date attached. What we will not do is fill a Higher Level request with a general science tutor and leave you to discover the mismatch in session three.

dubai/dubai-festival-city.closingHeading: Start with the diagnosis, not the booking
dubai/dubai-festival-city.closingBody: If a mock mark has arrived that does not match the term grades, the useful first step is not booking a term of lessons. It is a single diagnostic hour on your child's own marked scripts, which tells you whether the problem is content, command terms, unprompted starts or retrieval - four different problems needing four different fixes. Send the syllabus code or the IB subject and level, the school's own deadline dates, and the last marked paper. You will get a written assessment, a named tutor who teaches that specification, the rate, and a review point six to eight weeks out. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video.

dubai/dubai-harbour.tutorsIntro: Tutors matched to Dubai Harbour households are chosen as much for availability as for subject: a specialist who can hold a 5:15pm or a weekend slot across a whole term is worth more here than one who can only offer the hour the bus is still moving. Each teaches one named board and level.

intro.heading: One road in, one road out, and no school on it
paragraphs: Dubai Harbour occupies the stretch of coast between Dubai Marina and Palm Jumeirah, with the Emaar Beachfront towers along the sea, a marina, the cruise terminal and Skydive Dubai behind them. It is reached from King Salman Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud Street, with Sheikh Zayed Road behind that and the Palm Jumeirah gateway close by. The geography is the point: it is effectively a peninsula with a single practical entrance, and every child living here leaves it twice a day to go to school somewhere else.

That has consequences a property listing will not mention. The nearest schools sit in Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and The Greens, and the two routes to them, the coast road and Sheikh Zayed Road through the Al Sufouh interchanges, are both busy at exactly the hours a school run happens. A journey that takes twelve minutes at ten in the morning takes twenty-five to thirty-five at half past three, and the bus version takes longer again because it collects from several towers and then from several communities. The honest arrival time for most secondary children here is somewhere between a quarter past four and five o'clock.

Then there is the vertical component, which families underestimate until they have lived here. A tower address adds time at both ends: the drop-off point is not the apartment, lifts are shared with a few hundred other households at the same moment, and a child arriving in the building at ten to five is not at a desk at ten to five. Across a school week that is not a rounding error. It is the difference between a four forty-five slot that works on paper and a five fifteen slot that works in practice.

None of this is a complaint about the development, which is a pleasant place to live. It is the operational reality that should decide the shape of a tutoring arrangement, and almost nobody writes it down. The usual approach is to pick a tutor, agree a time that sounds reasonable, and then spend six weeks discovering that the time was wrong. The better approach is to establish the earliest hour the student is genuinely at a desk, fed and capable of thought, and then find a specialist who can hold that hour every week for a term.

What follows does that in order. The real journey times to the schools Dubai Harbour children attend and the earliest viable session for each. Why the bus timetable rather than the school bell is the clock that matters. What an evening slot costs in attention, and which hours are worth using. How to schedule for a household that travels. How the Ramadan period and the holiday calendar change the pattern. What the market charges in this corridor, including what travel adds to an in-home quote. And how to start, with the limits stated in advance.

dubai/dubai-harbour.programmesIntro: Dubai Harbour children are spread across the Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and Marina school clusters, which means several programmes per building. These are the four that matter for scheduling, because each makes different demands on an evening.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led primary schooling reported against learner attributes rather than percentages. The scheduling implication is the one that matters here: a primary child who has spent fifty minutes on a bus each way has no useful attention left after five o'clock, so any support at this stage belongs in a weekend morning slot or in a short, early, protected window rather than in the evening.
programmes.countryNote: Several primary and all-through campuses within reach of Dubai Harbour run the PYP. For a household on this peninsula the practical question at primary age is whether the bus route is survivable five days a week, because a long daily commute does more damage to a seven-year-old's learning than most of the things parents buy tutoring for.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four published criteria marked out of eight, converted to a grade from 1 to 7. Deadlines are internal and spread across the year rather than concentrated in a series, which makes the Middle Years Programme more forgiving of a disrupted week and less forgiving of a term in which nothing was planned. MYP 5 adds the Personal Project.
programmes.countryNote: For a travelling household the Middle Years Programme has an advantage: assessment is continuous, so a fortnight away costs specific tasks rather than an examination. The corresponding risk is that nothing externally fixed forces the catching up, which is where a weekly online slot that survives the travel does its real work.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, usually three Higher and three Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internal assessment carries 20% in the sciences and in both mathematics courses, and Higher Level mathematics adds a third paper worth 20%. The Diploma is the least travel-tolerant of these programmes because its deadlines are fixed, cumulative and set by the school rather than by the family.
programmes.countryNote: A Diploma student in a household that travels for several weeks a year needs the calendar mapped against the school's internal deadline sheet before the travel is booked, not afterwards. Most of the damage we see is not missed teaching; it is an internal assessment deadline that fell during a trip nobody checked.

programmes.name: IGCSE at Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel
programmes.description: Cambridge splits most subjects into Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C; Pearson Edexcel tiers mathematics as Foundation and Higher with a grade 9 ceiling. Cambridge runs June, November and March series, and every centre is allocated to one of six administrative timetable zones. Pearson runs May or June and November series and publishes provisional timetables ahead of each.
programmes.countryNote: The zone detail matters for a travelling family more than for a settled one. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for a centre's zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. Ask the school which zone it sits in and work from its own confirmed timetable.

dubai/dubai-harbour.subjectsIntro: These notes describe each subject in terms of the kind of session it needs, because on this peninsula the available hour is short and the question is what to spend it on.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Rewards frequent short practice far more than occasional long sessions, which suits a household with a tight evening window. Higher Level adds a third paper worth 20% that needs sustained work, so that component belongs in a weekend slot rather than in forty minutes after a long bus journey.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with the calculator assumed throughout, including on the first paper. The exploration is the component that genuinely needs an uninterrupted stretch, because choosing and securing a dataset is not a task that fits between a bus arrival and dinner.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Two written papers plus one investigation worth 20% at both levels. Problem-solving practice works well in short slots; uncertainty handling, error propagation and the investigation write-up do not, and families here consistently get better value by putting those in a weekend morning.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms separate the levels. Mechanism practice is ideal for a short weekday session because it is drillable. The investigation, marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, needs a long block and a quiet house.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-dense and decided by command terms, which makes it the subject that benefits most from a short, frequent, marked-question routine. Twenty minutes of exam-standard answers marked against a published scheme beats an hour of re-reading, which matters when the available hour is genuinely one hour.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a portfolio of three commentaries on published news articles, worth 30% at Standard Level and 20% at Higher. Each commentary is a discrete piece of work with its own word allowance, which makes it unusually well suited to a household that travels: one commentary per quiet fortnight.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is a timed guided analysis of an unseen text, which can be practised in a single compressed session: one text, one timed attempt, one honest marking. The Higher Level essay needs a longer stretch and should be planned against the school's internal deadline rather than improvised.

subjects.name: English B and English as a second language
subjects.description: Productive skills respond well to frequent short sessions, because speaking and writing improve with repetition rather than with duration. Listening components benefit from a quiet room and headphones, which on a busy tower floor is worth arranging deliberately rather than assuming.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study command and calculation accuracy decide the grade. The Higher Level research project rests on a real organisation within an 1,800 word limit, so the organisation has to be chosen early and the data confirmed available before any writing starts. That is a planning session, not a teaching one.

subjects.name: Geography and Environmental Systems
subjects.description: Both depend on named case studies with specific figures rather than general description, which makes them highly drillable in short slots. Fieldwork-based internal assessment requires a long block and a firm date, and should be scheduled around travel rather than in spite of it.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects with a 950 word commentary, plus a 1,600 word essay on a prescribed title. Thinly timetabled in most schools and almost always deprioritised in a busy week, which makes it the component most likely to be rescued by a protected weekend hour.

dubai/dubai-harbour.regionsIntro: What matters about Dubai Harbour's neighbours is travel time at the two hours that decide a study timetable. These notes are about journeys rather than about amenities.

regions.name: Dubai Marina
regions.note: The immediate neighbour inland, reached in minutes outside peak and considerably longer when the Marina itself is moving. Several Dubai Harbour households use Marina services and clinics, and the two communities share the same school routes towards Al Sufouh and Al Barsha.

regions.name: Jumeirah Beach Residence
regions.note: Adjacent along the coast, with a similar tower profile and the same single-corridor access problem. Families in both communities report the same pattern: the morning run is predictable and the afternoon return is not, which is why evening slots here start later than parents expect.

sections.heading: The Dubai Harbour school run, timed honestly
paragraphs: Everything about tutoring here follows from one number: the hour at which the student is genuinely at a desk. Parents reliably over-estimate it, because they measure from the school's finishing time rather than from the bus arriving at the tower, and because the drop-off point is not the apartment. A child whose school day ends at half past two is not available at three. On a bus route that collects from several towers before heading inland, and then returns in reverse, the realistic figure for a secondary student on this peninsula is somewhere between a quarter past four and five.

The table below sets out the schools Dubai Harbour families most commonly use, the route each one involves, a realistic home-arrival window and the earliest session start we would actually agree to. The arrival windows assume a normal school day and ordinary traffic rather than a bad afternoon, and they assume the bus rather than a parent collecting by car, which is faster but not available to most households five days a week. Treat them as planning figures and check them against your own fortnight.

Two patterns are worth noticing. The Al Sufouh cluster, which is the shortest run available, still lands most secondary students home after a quarter past four, so even the best case does not support a four o'clock lesson. And the inland campuses across Sheikh Zayed Road produce arrival times late enough that a weekday session becomes a compromise rather than a choice, which is the single strongest argument for moving the substantive work to a weekend morning and keeping the weekday hour for short, drillable practice.

sections.heading: The bus timetable is the clock, not the school bell
paragraphs: School bus provision is the part of the system that sets the shape of a family's week, and it is also the part that nobody plans around because it feels fixed and unimportant. It is neither. A bus route from a tower cluster on this stretch of coast collects from several buildings in sequence, which means the first child on is on for the longest, and the last child home is home last in both directions. Two children at the same school living in different towers here can have school days that differ by forty minutes at each end.

The practical consequences are specific. First, the morning pickup can be early enough that a secondary student is leaving before seven, which caps how late a session can run the previous evening without costing sleep. Second, the afternoon arrival is variable rather than fixed: a route that returns at twenty past four in September can return at twenty to five in November because a stop was added. Third, after-school activities and the bus are often mutually exclusive, so a child doing a school club loses the bus and gains a parent collection, which changes the arrival pattern again.

The useful discipline is to measure rather than assume. For two weeks, write down the actual time the child is at a desk, not the time the bus arrived and not the time school ended. The average of that fortnight is the number to build a timetable on, and it is usually twenty to thirty minutes later than the figure a parent would have guessed. Then set the session at that time plus fifteen minutes for food, and hold it. A slot that is reliably achievable is worth more over a term than a slot that is theoretically better and attended two weeks in three.
bullets: Measure for a fortnight: time at the desk, not time off the bus
The first tower on a route is the last one home
A school club usually means losing the bus and changing the pattern
Set the slot at measured arrival plus fifteen minutes, then defend it

sections.heading: What an evening slot costs in attention
paragraphs: Once the arrival time is established, the next question is which of the remaining hours is worth using, and the honest answer is that they are not equal. A student who left the building before seven, spent a day in school and sat on a bus for fifty minutes is not the same student at half past seven as at half past five, and treating the two as interchangeable because both appear free in a calendar is the most common scheduling error in commuter communities like this one.

The table below sets out what each slot is realistically good for. The pattern is consistent across the households we work with on this peninsula: the hour immediately after arrival and food is the best weekday hour available, the hour after that is adequate for review and drills, and anything after eight is better spent sleeping than studying. Where a household has no viable weekday hour at all, which happens often enough with the inland campuses, the correct answer is a weekend morning rather than a bad evening.

This also changes what should happen in each slot. A tired hour is good for practice of things already understood: marked short questions, vocabulary, mechanism drills, past paper questions in a familiar format. It is poor for new content, for anything requiring sustained planning, and for coursework. Families who split their tutoring this way, short drills midweek and the substantive work at the weekend, get noticeably more out of the same number of paid hours than families who spread four identical evening sessions across the week.
