sections.heading: Tower logistics, and the twenty minutes nobody counts
paragraphs: A villa community's school run ends at a front door. A tower community's school run ends at a drop-off point, which is not the same thing. On this stretch of coast the bus or car stops at a designated area, the child walks in, waits for a lift that several hundred other households are also calling at that moment, and arrives upstairs some minutes later. In the morning the sequence runs in reverse and has to be started earlier than the same journey from a villa would require.

Added up across a week, that is a real amount of time and it explains a persistent mismatch between what parents expect and what actually happens. A session agreed for four forty-five because the bus arrives at four thirty will routinely start at five, and after three weeks of starting fifteen minutes late everybody becomes irritated with an arrangement that was simply booked at the wrong time. Booking it for five fifteen in the first place removes the problem entirely and costs nothing.

There is a second, quieter issue specific to apartment living that is worth solving once rather than weekly. Online lessons in a tower need a defined place: a desk rather than a sofa, a wired connection or the 5 GHz band rather than whatever the laptop joins by default, over-ear headphones with a boom microphone so the student can be heard without competing with a shared living space, and a second phone or tablet propped as a document camera so the tutor sees the working rather than the face. That last item changes mathematics and physics lessons more than any other single piece of equipment, and it costs nothing if the household already owns an old phone.

sections.heading: Scheduling for a household that travels
paragraphs: Dubai Harbour households travel more than the average, and the damage that causes to a school year is rarely the missed teaching. It is the deadline nobody checked. An internal assessment date, a mock week, a Theory of Knowledge submission or a coursework checkpoint falls during a trip that was booked in March for July, and the student returns to find a component already late. Schools set those dates themselves, months in advance, and they publish them. Almost nobody reads the sheet before booking flights.

The fix is a fifteen-minute exercise done once a term. Put the school's internal deadline sheet next to the family's travel plans and look for collisions. Where one exists, there are usually three options: move the travel, agree an earlier submission with the school, or plan a defined block of work before departure. All three are easy in advance and none is easy afterwards. For a Diploma student this is the single highest-value piece of administration a parent can do, because the Diploma's deadlines are cumulative and the consequences of a late component are structural rather than cosmetic.

Tutoring itself is the easy part, because lessons are delivered online over live video. The same tutor and usually the same slot continue from another country with the time difference built in, which is the practical advantage of this delivery model for a mobile household and not a marketing line. What needs deciding in advance is whether the weeks away are a pause or a continuation, and either answer is fine as long as it is a decision. sections.heading: Ramadan and the UAE school calendar, for a commuter household
paragraphs: The UAE academic year has a shape that affects when revision realistically happens, and it is another thing no competing page in this market sets out. During Ramadan the school day shortens, which changes the commute and the arrival time in a direction that helps, and concentration moves later into the day, which changes what time a session should be. For most families here the sensible move is to shift to a post-Iftar slot for those weeks and agree it in advance rather than rearranging week by week.

The rest of the calendar matters in less obvious ways. The winter break sits in the middle of the Diploma's first-year content and is the natural place for a short consolidation block. The spring break often falls close to internal deadline season, which makes it the most valuable fortnight of the year for component work and the most commonly wasted. Study leave before an examination series is the period that moves grades most and is entirely unsupervised. And the long summer is the only time in the year when a student can close a content gap without six other subjects competing for the same hours.

For examination timing itself, work from the board's own documents rather than from a tutoring page. Cambridge runs June, November and March series with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, stating that it is essential to use the correct zone timetable and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. Pearson Edexcel runs May or June and November series and publishes provisional timetables ahead of each. For the IB Diploma this page publishes no dates, because none could be verified against ibo.org during research; confirm with the school's IB coordinator.

sections.heading: What travel adds to a quote in this corridor
paragraphs: The search phrase that brings families to this page often contains the words home tutor, and from a peninsula with one entrance that is a reasonable thing to want: somebody who comes to you removes a journey from a week already full of them. The honest answer involves looking at what the market charges and at who is actually available to make that drive at five in the afternoon.

Published Dubai market rates, surveyed in October 2026 from platform and agency rate pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, put an in-home visit at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 200 to 450 for an online subject specialist. The difference is travel time inside the fee rather than better teaching. On this stretch of coast the travel component is worse than average, because a tutor coming here from Al Barsha or Jumeirah at the wrong hour spends forty minutes each way, and they price accordingly or decline. The people who do accept are, predictably, generalists with gaps in their diary rather than Higher Level specialists with full ones.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and nobody will be sent to a Dubai Harbour address. Tuition here is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, with screen sharing for marked work and a document camera for written working. On a peninsula with one road in, that is not a compromise: it removes the travel that was the problem in the first place, and it means the choice of tutor is made on subject, board and level rather than on who is prepared to sit in the Al Sufouh queue twice.

sections.heading: Starting from Dubai Harbour, with the rules and limits stated
paragraphs: The first message should contain the school, the board and syllabus code, the level or tier, and one measured figure: the time the student is actually at a desk on a normal weekday. If you have not measured it, say so and we will start from the table above and correct it after a fortnight. We then name the tutor who would teach, where they are based and what they have taught at that exact level, before any payment, and the trial session is booked at the measured time plus fifteen minutes rather than at whatever hour we would prefer.

On assessed work the position does not move. An internal assessment, an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay must be the student's own work, authenticated by a school supervisor and declared by the school, and a malpractice finding falls on the student. A tutor reads the published criteria with the student, reads a draft the student produced and returns written comments and questions, checks notation and statistical treatment, and plans dated checkpoints back from the school's internal deadline. Nobody here authors any part of a submission, and we do not hand over board syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes.

The limits are these. Coverage is uneven in narrow Higher Level subjects, in less common languages and in uncommon Pearson Edexcel options, and the honest answer is a different hour with the right specialist, an adjacent level or board where the overlap is genuine, or a plain statement that we cannot cover it. The other limit is the clock, and it applies here more than anywhere: if the only hour available in your week is one at which the student cannot think, we will say that a weekend slot is the arrangement that will work rather than take the booking you offered. Data collected through this site is handled under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021, and the privacy link explains how to have it removed.

faqs.question: What time can a tutoring session realistically start in Dubai Harbour?
faqs.answer: For most secondary students, five o'clock or later. The development has no school of its own and one practical entrance, so every child travels out and back on a bus route that collects from several towers before heading inland. The Al Sufouh cluster, which is the shortest run available, still lands most secondary students home between a quarter past four and a quarter to five, and the inland Al Barsha campuses can be half an hour later. Add fifteen minutes for the lift and food, and five or half past five is the honest first slot.

faqs.question: How long is the school run from Emaar Beachfront?
faqs.answer: Twelve minutes to Al Sufouh at ten in the morning and twenty-five to thirty-five at half past three, with the bus version longer again because it serves several towers and then several communities. Inland campuses across Sheikh Zayed Road in Al Barsha and Al Barsha South produce the longest returns from this peninsula. The number worth having is not the distance but the measured time your child is at a desk on a normal weekday, averaged over a fortnight, which is usually twenty to thirty minutes later than a parent expects.

faqs.question: Does the bus route change how we should plan study time?
faqs.answer: Substantially. A route from a tower cluster collects in sequence, so the first child on is on longest and home last, and two children at the same school in different towers can have school days differing by forty minutes at each end. Routes also change during the year when stops are added. A school club usually means losing the bus and switching to a parent collection, which changes the pattern again. Measure the actual desk time for two weeks, set the session at that plus fifteen minutes, and defend the slot.

faqs.question: Is a seven-thirty evening session a bad idea?
faqs.answer: For most students under sixteen in a long-commute household, yes. A child who left the building before seven, spent a day at school and sat on a bus for fifty minutes is not the same student at half past seven as at half past five. The late slot looks free precisely because nothing else wants it. If it is the only hour available, use it for short drills of material already understood rather than for new content or coursework, and consider a weekend morning for the substantive work instead.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our apartment in Dubai Harbour?
faqs.answer: Not through us. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India, and nobody will be sent to a Dubai Harbour address. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, with screen sharing and a document camera for written working. Published in-home rates in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the fee, and on this corridor a visiting tutor loses forty minutes each way at peak, which is why those who accept tend to be generalists with gaps rather than specialists.

faqs.question: What is the best setup for online lessons in a tower apartment?
faqs.answer: Three things, decided once. A wired connection or the 5 GHz band rather than whatever the laptop joins by default, because a dropped connection costs more than a slower processor ever will. Over-ear headphones with a boom microphone so the student can be heard without competing with a shared living space. And a second phone or tablet propped as a document camera, so the tutor sees the working rather than the face, which changes mathematics and physics sessions more than any other single item and usually costs nothing if an old phone is lying around.

faqs.question: We travel for six weeks each summer. Will that hurt my child's grades?
faqs.answer: Not in itself, if the trip is used rather than endured. A long summer contains no competing subject deadlines, which makes it the best window of the year for bridging into the next programme or closing a content gap that term time never allows. Because lessons are delivered online, the same tutor and usually the same slot continue from wherever you are with the time difference built in. The damage from travel almost always comes from mid-term trips colliding with an internal deadline nobody checked, not from the summer.

faqs.question: How do we avoid a trip clashing with a coursework deadline?
faqs.answer: Put the school's internal deadline sheet next to the travel plans once a term and look for collisions, which takes fifteen minutes and prevents the most expensive mistake a mobile household makes. Schools set these dates themselves, months ahead, and publish them. Where a clash exists there are three options: move the travel, agree an earlier submission with the school, or book a defined block of work before departure. For a Diploma student this is the highest-value administration a parent can do, because the deadlines are cumulative.

faqs.question: How should lessons change during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Shift them later and shorten them, and agree it in advance rather than rearranging week by week. The school day shortens during Ramadan, which improves the commute and the arrival time, while concentration moves later into the day. For most households here that means a post-Iftar slot of about forty-five minutes used for review and light practice rather than new content. Families who plan the whole Ramadan period in one conversation before it starts lose far fewer sessions than those who negotiate each week as it arrives.

faqs.question: Which weekend slot works best for Diploma coursework?
faqs.answer: A morning, and a long one. Component work, an exploration, a scientific investigation, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay, or a full timed paper sat under real conditions and then marked, needs ninety minutes to two hours of unhurried attention that no weekday evening in this community can provide. Households on this peninsula consistently get more from one long weekend session plus one short weekday slot than from three or four identical evening hours spread across the week.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge exam timetable applies to my child?
faqs.answer: The one for the centre's administrative zone, and it matters. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones, each with its own timetable version, and states that it is essential to use the correct version and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. Ask the school which zone it sits in and work only from the timetable it confirms. Cambridge runs June, November and March series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October.

faqs.question: When are Pearson Edexcel International GCSE results released?
faqs.answer: Pearson publishes dates per series rather than a fixed annual pattern. For the recent cycle, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable on the Pearson qualifications site is always the document to plan from rather than a date restated on a tutoring page.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in the UAE need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring operates under a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and applications are made through MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, via the smart app, website or e-services system. Tutoring without one brings fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so distrust specific amounts.

faqs.question: What happens if the right specialist cannot hold our slot?
faqs.answer: You get told, and availability is treated as a genuine criterion rather than an afterthought. A Higher Level specialist who can only offer the hour your child is still on the bus is not a match, whatever their credentials. The three honest answers are a different hour of the week, usually a weekend morning, where that specialist is free; an adjacent level or board where the overlap is real and the gap can be named; or a plain statement that we cannot cover it with a suggestion of where to look next.

dubai/dubai-harbour.closingBody: For a household on this peninsula the first useful piece of information is not a subject, it is a time. Record for two weeks when your child is genuinely at a desk, then send that figure along with the school, the board, the syllabus code and the level. You will get back the name of someone who teaches that exact specification and can hold that hour every week for a term, plus a view on whether the substantive work belongs in a weekend morning instead. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video, and they continue from wherever you happen to be.

dubai/dubai-hills-estate.tutorsIntro: Tutors here are chosen for the particular decisions Dubai Hills Estate families face: an IGCSE option block that needs thinking through, a Higher Level science that is harder than the IGCSE was, or a mid-year school change inside the Al Khail cluster. Each tutor teaches one named board and level.

intro.heading: There are two Dubai Hills Estates, and they ask for different help
paragraphs: Dubai Hills Estate runs along Al Khail Road between Umm Suqeim Street and the Al Barsha South edge, and it is really two communities sharing one name. On one side are the villa and townhouse clusters: Sidra, Maple, Club Villas, Golf Place, Fairways, Parkway Vistas. On the other is a dense apartment belt around Dubai Hills Mall and Dubai Hills Park: Park Heights, Collective, Acacia, Mulberry, Park Ridge. The two have different ages, different tenures and different academic worries, which is why a single description of the neighbourhood is useless to a parent.

The villa clusters took their first residents from around 2018 and have aged into families with secondary children. These are the households already inside an examination system: a Year 10 doing IGCSEs, a Diploma student in the middle of internal assessments, a Year 9 about to pick options. They have usually settled on a school and the question they bring is subject-specific rather than school-specific.

The apartment belt turned over later and keeps turning over. Many of these households arrived within the last two or three years, often from another country rather than another part of Dubai, and their children are younger. Their questions are different: which school, which curriculum, what does an inspection rating actually mean, and is my child behind because of the move or because of the subject. The honest answer is usually that six weeks of diagnostic work tells you, and guessing does not.

Both profiles share one school cluster. Dubai Hills Estate families overwhelmingly use the Al Khail campuses and the Al Barsha South ring: GEMS International School Al Khail on the IB continuum, GEMS Wellington Academy Al Khail running the British curriculum with an IB Diploma option, GEMS New Millennium School Al Khail on an Indian curriculum, and then outwards to Kings' School Al Barsha, Nord Anglia International School Dubai, Repton Al Barsha and Dubai Heights Academy. Several families also look east to Hartland International School and North London Collegiate School Dubai in Sobha Hartland.

That cluster offers something unusual: a genuine choice between a British route ending in A Level and an IB route ending in the Diploma, inside a ten-minute drive. The cost of the choice is that it has to be made twice. Once at Year 9, when option blocks quietly decide what is possible at sixteen, and again at Year 11, when a student picks between three Higher Levels and three A Levels. Families who treat the first decision as administrative discover at the second that a door closed two years earlier.

So this page concentrates on the decisions rather than on the neighbourhood. How to read a KHDA inspection report and what it cannot tell you. What a Year 9 option block does to a Diploma application. Why Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel are not interchangeable even in the same subject. What tutoring costs in context against a school fee. And how lessons are actually delivered, which is online, one-to-one, over live video.

dubai/dubai-hills-estate.programmesIntro: The Al Khail cluster offers the full IB continuum and a British route in parallel, so Dubai Hills Estate parents are choosing between programmes rather than inheriting one. These are the four that matter here and what each demands.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Each subject is marked against four criteria out of eight, converted to a 1-7 grade through published boundaries. The later criteria reward investigation, communication and reflection rather than recall, so a student who knows the content can still sit in the middle band. MYP 5 ends with the Personal Project, which is the first substantially self-managed piece of work most students meet.
programmes.countryNote: GEMS International School Al Khail runs the MYP within the community, which makes it the default comparison point for Dubai Hills Estate parents weighing it against a British Key Stage 3. The practical difference parents notice is that MYP reports explain how a child works; Key Stage 3 reports say where they are against year-group expectations.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Nine or ten subjects over two years, with tiering decisions in mathematics and the sciences that cap or open the attainable grade. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel run different syllabus codes, different paper structures and different practical arrangements for the same named subject, and the question styles are not transferable.
programmes.countryNote: The British campuses around Al Khail and Al Barsha South do not all use the same board, and some mix boards across departments. Ask each subject department rather than the school generally, because a family that assumes one board across the timetable will buy the wrong past papers for half the subjects.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at three Higher and three Standard Levels, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Points come from examined papers and from internally assessed work moderated by the IB. The Diploma rewards students who can run their own calendar; it punishes those who cannot, regardless of subject ability.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Hills Estate families often choose the Diploma specifically to keep options open across continents, which is the right reason. The planning point is Higher Level choice: a student aiming at engineering or medicine needs particular Higher Levels, and the Year 9 option block has to have left the prerequisite subjects available.

programmes.name: A Level and AS Level
programmes.description: Three or four subjects studied in depth, with no Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay or CAS requirement. For a student who already knows the direction they want, the depth is an advantage; for a student who does not, narrowing to three subjects at sixteen is the risk.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, plus five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic Education are not counted among those five. Verify the current rule on the authority's own page.

dubai/dubai-hills-estate.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Dubai Hills Estate families ask for most, with the specific thing the assessment rewards. We match one tutor per subject and level rather than a generalist.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency and proof carry the papers. Higher Level Paper 3 is an extended investigation with unfamiliar structure, and it is the component that most often surprises a student who found IGCSE mathematics straightforward.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: The tier decision drives everything. Extended and Higher tier add algebraic fractions, circle theorems, transformations of functions and more demanding problem-solving; Core and Foundation cap the grade a student can reach.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: The mole concept and organic chemistry decide the grade. At Diploma level the internal assessment needs a research question narrow enough to control, which is a design problem rather than a content problem.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: Explanation questions asking for a mechanism, not a formula, are where marks disappear. Electricity is the reliable weak point at IGCSE; at Higher Level it is fields, and the mathematics underneath them.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: Command terms are the hidden curriculum: outline, describe, explain, evaluate and discuss each want a different shape of answer. Data-based questions reward reading the axes and the units before writing anything.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy plus an explicit judgement sentence is what separates a mid-band answer from a top-band one. Higher Level adds quantitative work that catches students who chose the subject expecting essays only.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL · IGCSE First Language English
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis and the individual oral both reward a sustained argument about how a text produces its effect. For IGCSE directed writing, register and audience awareness are worth more than vocabulary.

subjects.name: Business Management and Business Studies
subjects.description: Application to the named case, not general theory, earns the marks. Students who write textbook definitions without tying them to the stimulus material routinely score below what they know.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: A popular Year 9 option whose consequences are poorly understood. The Diploma internal assessment is a developed solution with documentation, which demands sustained independent project work rather than coding talent alone.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first and additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, with Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for Arabic as a first language, so the two streams are genuinely different courses.

sections.heading: What a Dubai Hills Estate parent is actually buying when they book a tutor
paragraphs: A tutor buys you two things and cannot buy you a third. The first is diagnosis: a specialist who looks at a mock script and names the three things costing marks, which is a different exercise from judging how good a student is at the subject. The second is practice under correction, which is the only reliable way exam technique improves. The third thing, a grade, is not for sale and nobody should offer it.

In Dubai Hills Estate the diagnosis part carries more weight than usual, because so many families here are in the middle of a decision rather than in the middle of a problem. A Year 9 parent wants to know whether their child can realistically carry triple science and two languages. A Year 11 parent wants to know whether Higher Level mathematics is a sensible risk. Those questions are answerable from the student's own work, and guessing at them is expensive in a way that shows up two years later.

Delivery is straightforward and worth stating early. Tuition for Dubai Hills Estate households runs online, one-to-one, over live video with a named tutor. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are part of our India service only. For a community that sits beside a school cluster offering two different routes, the advantage is that the tutor can be a specialist in the specific board and level your child sits rather than whoever covers Al Khail on a Tuesday evening.

The practical test of whether tutoring is working is not the next report. It is whether the student can do, unaided, the thing they could not do six weeks ago. If the answer is yes, the block has done its job and should end or step down. If after a term the answer is still no, the diagnosis was wrong and the arrangement should change rather than continue.

sections.heading: Reading a KHDA inspection report properly, and what it will never tell you
paragraphs: KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, and it inspects every private school and publishes the report. For an apartment-belt family new to the city, those reports are the most reliable public information available about a school. They are also routinely over-read, because a six-band judgement about a whole school gets treated as a prediction about one child.

The useful parts of a report are the subject-level and phase-level judgements, not the headline. A school rated the same overall as another can be stronger in secondary science and weaker in primary English, and that distinction matters enormously to a specific family. The report also records what inspectors told the school to improve, which tells you what the school has been working on, and whether it moved since the last visit, which tells you about direction rather than position.

What a report cannot tell you is whether your child is in the right set, whether the option block put them in a mathematics course below their ceiling, whether they are losing marks on command terms rather than content, or whether the teacher of their particular Higher Level subject is a good fit. Those are individual questions and no inspection framework addresses them. For those, the last mock script with the mark scheme beside it is worth more than any rating.

One further piece of context for fee planning. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Dubai's sector is also expanding: six new schools opened during 2025-26 with enrolment up six per cent, and seven more arrive for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 places.

sections.heading: The Year 9 option block is a decision nobody calls a decision
paragraphs: Every British-curriculum school in the Al Khail and Al Barsha cluster runs option blocks at the end of Year 9. A student picks a handful of subjects from columns, the school builds a timetable, and it feels administrative. It is not. Those choices decide what is available at sixteen, and what is available at sixteen decides what is credible at eighteen. The decision is made by fourteen-year-olds, often on the basis of which teacher they liked.

The most consequential choice is in science. Separate or triple science at IGCSE keeps all three Higher Level sciences genuinely open. Combined or double award narrows it, not because universities refuse it, but because a student entering Chemistry Higher Level from combined science starts a term behind on content and usually does not recover the gap while also carrying five other subjects. The second most consequential is mathematics tier, where Core or Foundation caps the grade and therefore the Higher Level route.

Language choices are quieter but matter for the Diploma specifically, since the Diploma requires a language acquisition subject in Group 2. A student who dropped every language at Year 9 has to restart one at sixteen, which is possible but expensive in effort. Conversely, keeping two languages purely to keep doors open can crowd out the science or the mathematics the student actually needs.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: the same subject, two different papers
paragraphs: Parents in this cluster frequently assume that an IGCSE is an IGCSE. It is not. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel both award International GCSEs, and for the same named subject they use different syllabus codes, different paper structures, different practical arrangements and different question styles. A tutor working from the wrong board's past papers can be teaching the subject accurately and still leaving a student unprepared.

The differences are concrete. Cambridge offers tiering in several subjects, so Core and Extended papers exist with different content ceilings. Pearson runs single-tier papers in some of the same subjects. Pearson's International GCSE sits in May or June and November series each year; Cambridge runs June and November series with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative timetable zones, warning that the correct zone version of the timetable must be used.

Schools in the Al Khail cluster do not always use one board across the whole timetable. It is entirely normal for mathematics and the sciences to sit with one awarding body and English or humanities with another, and schools change boards between cohorts. The only reliable source is the subject department or the exams officer, and the question to ask is specific: which syllabus code is my child entered for, in this subject, in this series.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context for a Dubai Hills Estate household
paragraphs: Most pages ranking for Dubai tutoring searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in dollars. That is not useful to a family budgeting in dirhams against a school fee, so the figures below are published with their sources named. They are market rates drawn from published provider pricing and from Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost tables. IB Gram's own rate is quoted after a consultation, because it varies by subject, level and tutor.

The context that makes these numbers legible is the school fee. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Each school's current fee is published on its KHDA listing, which is the figure to check rather than any aggregate. Tutoring, at one weekly session, typically represents a small single-digit percentage of an annual fee in this cluster.

Where the money goes matters more than the headline rate. A weekly hour spread across four subjects produces no change in any of them, because tutoring without independent practice between sessions builds understanding without fluency. One or two subjects, chosen because that is where marks are actually being lost, with homework set and checked, is the structure that moves a grade. A diagnostic from a real mock script is what identifies those subjects.

For a two-year Diploma, the pattern that works is light in Year 12 and heavier in the second half of Year 13: a single subject supported through the first year, a coursework block when internal assessments and the Extended Essay converge, and an intensive run of past-paper work in the final term. Front-loading two Higher Levels from the first week of Diploma Year 1 is a common and expensive mistake.

sections.heading: Why a Dubai Hills Estate family still searches for a home tutor, and what we do instead
paragraphs: The search phrase is honest and worth answering honestly. Parents type it because the in-home model is what this market has historically sold, and because for a younger child the advantages are real: easier to keep on task, a parent nearby, no dependence on a connection. Market in-home rates in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside them, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online.

IB Gram does not provide home visits in the UAE. That is a service we offer only in India, and every country page on the site says the same. What we provide to Dubai Hills Estate households is one-to-one tuition over live video. The reason is not a shortage of tutors in Dubai but the shape of the matching problem: once you require physical presence in Al Khail at 17:30 on a Wednesday, the pool of people who also specialise in Pearson 4CH1 or Analysis and Approaches Higher Level becomes very small.

Online delivery has specific requirements to work properly, and families who skip them report a worse experience. The student needs a quiet room with a door, not a kitchen table beside a television. A second screen or a tablet for working on paper while seeing the tutor helps enormously in mathematics and science. A graphics tablet is worth the cost for any student doing a mathematical subject at Higher Level. And the session needs the same protected hour every week, because a floating appointment is the first thing a busy household drops.

What families notice after a term is that the online format changes what a session contains. There is no social warm-up while a tutor takes off their shoes, screens can be shared so a mark scheme and a script sit side by side, and notes exist afterwards. The format suits diagnosis and corrected practice, which is what secondary tutoring mostly is.

sections.heading: Moving between campuses inside one community: what actually breaks
paragraphs: Because Dubai Hills Estate sits beside a cluster offering several curricula, families here change schools without changing homes more often than in most Dubai communities. A child can move from the IB continuum to a British campus, or from an Indian curriculum to either, with the same journey to school. That makes transfers easy logistically and harder academically than parents expect.

Two things break reliably. The first is unstated prior content: every scheme of work orders topics differently, so a student arriving in February has missed whatever the new school taught in September and covered things the new class has not reached. This is not a knowledge deficit, it is a sequencing mismatch, and it resolves in weeks if it is diagnosed specifically rather than treated as being behind.

The second is assessment language. A student who has spent three years being marked against MYP criteria has learned to write investigations and reflections. Dropped into IGCSE preparation, the same student writes thoughtful answers that do not collect the available marks, because IGCSE mark schemes reward specific content points in a specific form. The reverse is equally true: a student moving from IGCSE into the Diploma writes tight exam answers and underperforms on criterion-marked internal assessment.

The practical approach is a six-week diagnostic block from the new school's own scheme of work and the student's last report, with the aim of naming three or four specific gaps. One of those is usually sequencing, one is usually assessment language, and one is usually a genuine content gap that needs teaching. After six weeks the block is reviewed and, more often than not, stopped.

sections.heading: Coursework support, academic honesty and where the line sits
paragraphs: At least one provider ranking for Dubai tutoring queries sells completed internal assessments. That is academic malpractice under IB rules and the consequence lands on the student: a Diploma candidate found to have submitted work that is not their own faces an investigation that can cost the whole Diploma. This has to be said plainly on a page like this, because the market a Dubai Hills Estate parent is shopping in contains it.

Legitimate coursework support is specific and it is teaching. A tutor explains what each assessment criterion rewards and in what language. They discuss whether a research question can actually be investigated with the equipment and time available. They read a draft the student wrote and say where the evidence does not support the claim. They point out that a paragraph asserts something it has not demonstrated. The student then rewrites it themselves.

The boundary is easier to apply than to describe: if the tutor's words would appear in the submission, it has been crossed. That rules out supplying content, restructuring a draft into finished prose, dictating a conclusion and handing over a model for adaptation. It also rules out reproducing or distributing syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, which are the awarding bodies' copyright. A tutor references and links to the official source instead.

Parents can enforce this with one question at the start of any coursework block: what will you do, and what will my child do. A specific answer to both halves is a good sign. It is also worth asking your school's coordinator what external support must be declared, because schools differ in how they record acknowledged help, and declaring it is always the safer course.

sections.heading: Starting from Dubai Hills Estate, and the limits we will tell you about
paragraphs: The sequence is short. A consultation establishing the board, the syllabus code, the component where marks are going and the hours your household can hold. Then a diagnostic from real work where it exists, a trial session with the named tutor who would teach the slot, and a weekly booking if the fit works. The trial exists to test the working relationship, which is the one thing a credential cannot tell you.

Three limits are worth stating in advance. Specialist cover is not uniform: mainstream requests are matched quickly, while a less commonly taught Diploma option or a narrow internal assessment specialism takes longer, and sometimes the right person is in a different time zone, which affects which slots exist. We say so rather than placing a generalist. Second, we do not quote a public price list, because the rate depends on the subject, level and tutor. Third, nobody here will offer you a grade.

There is one piece of regulatory homework worth doing whoever you hire, including if you hire independently. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents and university students. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published.

One related rule applies to Abu Dhabi and is worth knowing even in Dubai, because families move between emirates. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also addresses serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Asking your child's own teacher to tutor them privately is not the shortcut it appears to be.

process.title: Confirm the board and the code
process.description: Before anything else we establish the examination board and syllabus code for each subject, and for IB students the programme year and the internal deadline calendar. In the Al Khail cluster schools do not always use one board across the timetable, so this is asked department by department rather than once.

process.title: Diagnose from the student's own work
process.description: Where a mock script, internal assessment feedback or school report exists, the diagnostic starts there rather than with a placement test. The output is three or four named things costing marks, which is a different and more useful answer than a judgement of overall ability.

process.title: Trial with the tutor who would teach
process.description: One session with the specific person, not a sales call and not a different tutor. Parents of younger students may sit in. If the working relationship is wrong we rematch; a technically strong tutor who cannot hold a fifteen-year-old's attention is the wrong tutor whatever the credentials.

process.title: Weekly slot with a written record
process.description: A protected hour at the same time each week, with notes against the school's own scheme of work so sessions build rather than restart. Homework is set between sessions, because corrected independent practice is what converts understanding into fluency.

process.title: Review, then stop or step down
process.description: Each block has a target: a component, a tier decision, a set of criteria. We review against it on a fixed date rather than continuing by default, and when the student can do the thing unaided we say so and close or reduce the booking.

whyPoints.title: The board is confirmed before the first session
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 are different papers with different question styles. We establish the syllabus code department by department before booking, because schools in the Al Khail cluster mix boards across the timetable and a tutor on the wrong past papers wastes a term.

whyPoints.title: Decision support, not just subject support
whyPoints.description: Many Dubai Hills Estate questions are choices rather than problems: a Year 9 option block, a mathematics tier, a Higher Level combination. We offer short decision blocks that work from the student's real attainment data and end in a shortlist you can take to the school.

whyPoints.title: AED figures with their publishers named
whyPoints.description: Every rate on this page is attributed to the provider or dataset that published it, and the school fee line points to the KHDA listing rather than an invented average. Our own rate is quoted after a consultation because it depends on subject, level and tutor.

whyPoints.title: A stated coursework boundary
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach the criteria and give feedback on the student's own drafts. They do not supply content for an internal assessment, Extended Essay or Personal Project, and they do not distribute awarding-body material. The reason is that the risk of crossing that line falls on the student.

whyPoints.title: Transfers handled as sequencing, not deficit
whyPoints.description: Families here change campuses without changing homes. A mid-year arrival is usually a sequencing mismatch plus an assessment-language gap, both of which close in weeks when they are diagnosed specifically rather than treated as being generally behind.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated up front
whyPoints.description: Where a niche Diploma option or a narrow internal assessment specialism is thin, we give a realistic match time and explain what time zone the specialist sits in. That is more useful than a fast placement with a generalist who cannot diagnose the component.

faqs.question: Which schools do most Dubai Hills Estate children attend?
faqs.answer: The Al Khail cluster dominates: GEMS International School Al Khail on the IB continuum, GEMS Wellington Academy Al Khail running the British curriculum with an IB Diploma option, and GEMS New Millennium School Al Khail on an Indian curriculum. Beyond those, families use the Al Barsha South ring, including Kings' School Al Barsha, Nord Anglia International School Dubai, Repton Al Barsha and Dubai Heights Academy, and some look east to Hartland International School and North London Collegiate School Dubai in Sobha Hartland. The unusual feature of this community is that a genuine choice between British and IB routes exists within a short drive.

faqs.question: Does a KHDA Outstanding rating mean my child will do well there?
faqs.answer: No, and conflating the two is the most common mistake new arrivals make. A KHDA band describes provision across a whole school. It does not tell you whether your child is in the right set, whether the option block put them in a capped mathematics course, or whether the specific department teaching their Higher Level subject suits them. Read the subject-level and phase-level judgements rather than the headline, and read what inspectors asked the school to improve. For an individual diagnosis, the last mock script with its mark scheme is worth more than any rating.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 9 and choosing options. What decides the most?
faqs.answer: Two choices carry disproportionate weight. The first is science: separate or triple IGCSE science keeps all three sciences credible at Higher Level or A Level, while combined or double award leaves a content gap that is difficult to close while carrying five other Diploma subjects. The second is mathematics tier, because Core or Foundation caps the attainable grade and effectively rules out Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. Language choice matters too, since the Diploma requires a Group 2 language acquisition subject that a student who dropped all languages must restart at sixteen.

faqs.question: Are Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSEs interchangeable?
faqs.answer: They are not. The same named subject carries different syllabus codes, paper structures and question styles. Cambridge Chemistry is 0620 with Core and Extended tiers; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry is 4CH1 as a single tier. Practical arrangements differ, and so does mark-scheme language. Schools in the Al Khail cluster also mix boards across departments and change boards between cohorts, so the only reliable answer comes from the subject department or the exams officer. Ask which syllabus code your child is entered for, in that subject, in that series, before buying any past papers.

faqs.question: Can a tutor visit our apartment in Park Heights or our villa in Sidra?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE tutoring online, one-to-one, over live video, and does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we offer only in India. The practical trade is worth understanding: once physical presence is required at a specific hour in Al Khail, the pool of available people who also specialise in your child's exact board and level becomes very small. Online matching means a Pearson 4PH1 student gets a Pearson 4PH1 specialist, and two children can have separate slots on one evening with no travel.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE tutor cost per hour in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates for a qualified subject tutor online run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. In-home rates sit higher at roughly AED 180 to 500 because travel is inside them. Premium named tutors are advertised from AED 500 to 650. Monthly packages in this market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those figures are the market, not an IB Gram price list; our own rate follows a consultation because it depends on subject, level and tutor.

faqs.question: We are moving our child from the IB continuum to a British campus nearby. What should we expect?
faqs.answer: Expect a sequencing mismatch and an assessment-language gap rather than a drop in ability. Every scheme of work orders topics differently, so an arrival in February has missed autumn content and already covered things the new class has not reached. Separately, a student marked for years against MYP criteria writes thoughtful investigations that do not collect IGCSE marks, because IGCSE mark schemes reward specific content points in a specific form. A six-week diagnostic block from the new school's scheme of work normally names three or four gaps, and that is usually enough.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level Mathematics Analysis and Approaches a sensible risk for my child?
faqs.answer: It depends on two things that can be checked rather than guessed. The first is algebraic fluency: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level assumes manipulation is automatic, and a student who can rearrange equations only with effort will spend their working memory on the algebra instead of the calculus. The second is the IGCSE tier and grade, because Extended or Higher tier at a strong grade is close to a prerequisite in practice. A short decision block using the student's own papers answers this better than a general discussion.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we tutor at once?
faqs.answer: One or two, chosen because that is where marks are demonstrably being lost. A weekly hour spread across four subjects reliably produces no change in any of them, because the student has no time left for the independent practice that converts understanding into fluency. The diagnostic question is not which subjects are hardest but which components are costing marks, and that comes from mock scripts with mark schemes beside them. Narrow is better: one subject, two sessions a week, for a term, moves more than four subjects at one session each.

faqs.question: What should the home setup be for online lessons to work properly?
faqs.answer: A quiet room with a door, not a kitchen table beside a television. A second screen or a tablet so the student can work on paper while still seeing the tutor, which matters enormously in mathematics and science. For any Higher Level mathematical subject, a graphics tablet is worth the cost because it lets the tutor and student write on the same page. And a protected hour at the same time every week, because a floating appointment is the first thing a busy household drops when a week gets full.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a licence, and can I check?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through its app, website and e-services. Those tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule of amounts.

faqs.question: Can we ask my child's own class teacher to tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: It is not the shortcut it looks like. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also addresses serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Beyond the rules, there is a practical problem: the person who teaches a class and the person who marks the work is not well placed to give independent feedback on it. A separate tutor can be blunt about a draft in a way a class teacher cannot.

faqs.question: How much of the Diploma does a student have to manage without a teacher?
faqs.answer: More than most families expect, and this is where points are usually lost. The examined papers are taught in lessons. The Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition, each subject's internal assessment and the CAS portfolio are substantially self-managed across two years, with internal school deadlines that stack up in the window before mock examinations. Students rarely fail these on ability; they run out of calendar. Planning a coursework block backwards from the school's internal deadline, rather than from the exam session, is the single most useful intervention.

faqs.question: Can lessons continue over the summer or during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes to both, with a change of shape. Over the long summer break, a short intensive block works better than a weekly rhythm, especially for closing a diagnosed gap before a new school year or bridging IGCSE into the Diploma. During Ramadan, school hours shorten and afternoons are low-energy, so a post-Iftar slot usually produces better work in less time than a 16:00 session. Because tutors are matched across time zones rather than from one city, holding an unusual slot for several weeks is straightforward to arrange.

faqs.question: What are the UAE equivalency requirements for a British-curriculum student here?
faqs.answer: On the British track, students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among those five required subjects. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject figure, which is wrong. No IB points threshold should be taken second-hand; verify any IB figure on the Ministry's own pages. IB Gram describes this process and does not perform it.

dubai/dubai-hills-estate.closingHeading: Two decisions first, then a tutor
dubai/dubai-hills-estate.closingBody: If you live in Dubai Hills Estate, the two things worth settling before you book anyone are the examination board and syllabus code for each subject, and whether the option block or tier your child is sitting in still leaves the route you want open. Both are answerable from the school and from your child's own work. Once they are settled, matching is quick: one-to-one lessons over live video with a tutor who teaches that exact board and level, a trial session with the person who would take the slot, and a written review date rather than an open-ended booking.

dubai/dubai-internet-city.tutorsIntro: Requests from these towers skew towards mathematics, the sciences, computer science and economics, and towards slots after six. The tutors below are matched on two things at once: the syllabus your child sits, and a working day that makes a 7pm Dubai session a reasonable hour at their end rather than a favour.

intro.heading: Nobody is home at four, and the student can get themselves back
paragraphs: Dubai Internet City occupies a stretch of the Al Sufouh corridor along Sheikh Zayed Road, with its own metro station, a tram line running through the district and the Media City and Knowledge Park free zones either side of it. The households attached to it have a distinctive shape: a high proportion of two-income families in technology, media and professional services, often with both parents in offices within a few kilometres of home and neither of them free at the end of the school day.

That produces a tutoring problem unlike the one in a villa community. In Arabian Ranches or Emirates Hills the constraint is the drive. Here the drive is short or unnecessary, and the constraint is supervision. A Year 10 student is home by half past three, alone, with a phone, and the two hours before a parent returns are either the most productive of the day or entirely lost. Which of those it is depends almost completely on whether something is scheduled in them.

The second feature of this district is genuinely useful and almost never written about. Internet City is one of the few parts of Dubai where a secondary student can move independently. The tram runs along Al Sufouh Road and connects to the metro, several of the schools the corridor uses are a short ride away, and a fifteen-year-old can be home without a parent leaving a desk. That removes the single biggest scheduling constraint most Dubai families face, and it opens up a wider set of workable slots.

The third feature is that parents here are comfortable with video. A household where both adults spend their working day on calls does not need persuading that teaching can happen over a screen, and the practical questions they ask are better ones: how is the session recorded, what does the written note contain, who sees it, and how is a 7pm slot kept consistent across a term. Those are the right questions, and this page answers them.

What follows is built around the evening rather than the afternoon. There is a transport grid for getting home from the corridor's schools; an honest look at what a 7pm session can and cannot achieve; why a tutor's time zone matters more than their postcode once nobody is driving; a term-by-term rhythm across the Dubai school year; what the market charges and what is actually available after six; and the deadlines a working parent should put in a calendar rather than discover. Lessons are delivered online over live video, and IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai, which is a service offered only in India. Every AED figure below is a market rate attributed to the provider that published it in October 2026, and every board date comes from Cambridge or Pearson directly rather than from a secondary summary.

dubai/dubai-internet-city.programmesIntro: Each programme makes a different demand on the evening, which is the only thing that matters in a household where both parents work. The notes below describe each one by the kind of weekly commitment it imposes rather than by its philosophy.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. The weekly commitment is large but, more importantly, it is lumpy: internal assessment and essay deadlines cluster, and a student with no external structure tends to meet them all in the same fortnight. A Diploma student in an unsupervised afternoon needs a schedule more than a tutor.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in the Al Sufouh corridor sit the May session. The dates that actually bind are the school's internal deadlines for each internal assessment and the Extended Essay, held by your IB coordinator. No IB session or results date is published here, because the IB's own site could not be confirmed directly for this project.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessment against four criteria per subject, each out of 8, converted to a 1-7 grade. The weekly load is moderate and steady, with criterion task deadlines spread across the year and the Personal Project in MYP 5. For an unsupervised afternoon this is the easier programme to drift in, because nothing is due tomorrow and something is always due in a fortnight.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP's lack of terminal examinations means an unstructured MYP 4 or 5 does not show up as a crisis until Diploma Year 1. In this corridor, where most students stay at the same school for the Diploma, establishing a working evening routine during MYP 5 is the cheapest intervention available.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Eight or nine subjects with terminal papers and coursework in several. The weekly demand is dominated by past-paper practice, which is the single most effective independent activity available and also the easiest to fake. A student who has been in a room with past papers for two hours has not necessarily done two hours of past papers.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge and Pearson are separate qualifications with different codes and paper structures, and both are used in this corridor. Cambridge sets final entries months before the papers and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, so a working parent's single most useful act is getting the school's own timetable and entry deadline into a calendar early.

dubai/dubai-internet-city.subjectsIntro: Subject requests from this district lean towards mathematics, the sciences and the technology-adjacent options, which reflects both the schools nearby and the households' own working lives. Each note below names the specific demand rather than describing the syllabus.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency, with Higher Level Paper 3 asking for sustained reasoning through one extended problem. The evening work that moves this is unseen problems attempted without a model, which is also the work students avoid most reliably when nobody is in the room.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with the graphic display calculator assumed throughout. Marks leak where an answer is given without its modelling assumption, or a correlation reported without comment. Check university prerequisites before treating it as the easier route; several technical degrees specify Analysis.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Theory carries more weight than students expect, and the internal solution requires a real client and a documented development process. Students who can code well often lose marks on the documentation and the testing evidence rather than on the program itself.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields and mechanics carry the Higher Level load, with the scientific investigation marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Uncertainty handling is the common leak, and it is a technique that can be taught in a handful of evening sessions.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides a large share of the marks and improves quickly. The commentary portfolio is slower, because each commentary has to be anchored to a genuine published article inside a word limit, and poor article choice caps the analysis before any writing begins.

subjects.name: Digital Society
subjects.description: Concept-led rather than content-led, which suits students from technology-minded households and still catches them out. The inquiry project needs a defensible claim and real evidence, and the marking rewards sustained argument rather than familiarity with the technology involved.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: The tier decision sets a grade ceiling in Cambridge subjects, and Extended candidates lose marks on method and on multi-topic questions. Evening past-paper work only helps if it is done against the mark scheme rather than an answer key.

subjects.name: IGCSE Computer Science
subjects.description: Two distinct halves: the theory paper, where marks are lost on precise terminology, and the problem-solving paper, where pseudocode conventions matter as much as the logic. Students who program in their own time often score below their ability on the written conventions.

subjects.name: IGCSE Business Studies
subjects.description: Application to the case material rather than definition of terms. Transferring and able students routinely write accurate content that scores in the bottom band because the answer never engages with the organisation described in the stimulus.

sections.heading: Getting home without a car: the tram, the metro and the independent teenager
paragraphs: This is the one genuine logistical advantage of the Internet City corridor and it goes almost unmentioned on tutoring pages, which tend to assume every Dubai family drives. A tram runs along Al Sufouh Road through the free zones, the metro stops in the district, and several of the schools the corridor uses sit within a short ride. A Year 9 or Year 10 student can therefore be home at a predictable time without an adult leaving work, which is not true in most of the emirate.

The practical consequence is that the session start time is set by the student rather than by a parent's traffic. That makes the slot both earlier and more reliable: a 4:30pm start is genuinely achievable from several of the nearby schools, where in a villa community the same start would depend on a drive nobody can guarantee. It also means the slot does not have to move when a parent's meeting overruns, which is the usual reason a weekly arrangement quietly collapses in November.

The table below sets out indicative journeys. Treat the times as a starting point and check them against your own week, because finishing times differ by year group and by day, and the tram and metro frequencies vary across the afternoon. What matters is that each journey is a known quantity in a way a car journey on Sheikh Zayed Road at four o'clock is not.

Two cautions. First, independent travel suits some fourteen-year-olds and not others, and that judgement belongs to the parent rather than to a tutoring page. Second, a student who gets home alone at 3:45pm and has a session at 4:30pm needs the gap defined, or the gap becomes a phone. The households that make this work treat the arrival and the session as a single routine rather than two separate events.

sections.heading: Two working parents and the 7pm session
paragraphs: A household where both adults work until six has three options for an academically struggling teenager, and only one of them is reliable. The first is supervision after work, which means homework starting at seven when everybody is tired and ending in an argument. The second is leaving the afternoon unsupervised and hoping, which works for a self-directed student and for nobody else. The third is scheduling something into the afternoon that does not require a parent to be present.

The third option is the reason online delivery suits this district specifically. A session at half past four needs nothing from the parents except that the arrangement exists. It converts the least productive two hours of a teenager's day into the most productive, and it does so at the point in the day when concentration is still available. By eight in the evening, after a full school day, most fifteen-year-olds are not learning mathematics regardless of who is teaching them.

The late slot still has a real place. Diploma students in DP1 and DP2 often work better at seven than at four, particularly those with sport or activity commitments after school. The test is empirical rather than theoretical: trial a late session and look at what the student produces in it. A parent should be sceptical of a 7:30pm slot chosen for parental convenience and comfortable with one chosen because the student is demonstrably sharper then.

The written note matters more here than in a household with an adult at home. A parent who was not in the building at five needs to know what was covered, what was set, and whether the session went well, without interrogating a teenager at dinner. That is a small piece of administration and it is the difference between a term of sessions that a parent can steer and a term of sessions they are merely paying for.

sections.heading: Why a tutor's time zone matters more than their postcode
paragraphs: Once nobody is driving, the geography that matters stops being distance and becomes the clock. A tutor's usefulness to a household in this corridor depends on whether a 7pm Dubai slot is a sustainable working hour at their end or a late-night favour. A favour is not a plan: it gets cancelled in week six, and the student loses the continuity that was the whole point of a weekly arrangement.

The table below sets out how the common tutor locations line up against a Dubai evening. It is worth reading because it also explains availability. A family asking for 4:30pm Dubai time is asking for early afternoon in the United Kingdom and mid-morning in the Americas, which is easy to staff. A family asking for 8pm Dubai is asking for late afternoon in the United Kingdom and mid-afternoon on the United States east coast, which is also easy. The difficult slots are the ones that land at three in the morning somewhere.

This is not an argument for a tutor in any particular country. It is an argument for asking the question, because a tutor who takes your slot at an unsustainable hour is a short-term arrangement whatever their subject knowledge. The right question is simple: what time is this session where you are, and is that a normal working hour for you?

IB Gram does not maintain a UAE office or send tutors to UAE addresses, and that is relevant here rather than evasive. The practical consequence of online-only delivery is that your child's tutor is chosen from everyone who teaches that syllabus at a sustainable hour, rather than from the smaller set who could reach the Al Sufouh corridor by car on a weekday evening. For a Higher Level subject with a thin specialist pool, that difference decides whether a suitable tutor exists at all.

sections.heading: The Dubai school year, term by term, and what tutoring should be doing in each
paragraphs: A working parent does not need a philosophy of tutoring; they need to know what the next ten weeks should look like. The Dubai academic year has a predictable shape, and the mistake most households make is treating it as uniform. Support that is identical in October and in April is wasting one of those two months, because the student's problem in each is different.

October and November are for building the system. Content is being delivered, nothing is urgent, and this is when retrieval routines, command-term work and timed practice can be established without competing against a deadline. Families who start here get the most out of a year, and it is also when specialist tutors are most available, before the January rush.

December and January are mock season and the first real diagnosis. A marked mock paper is the most informative document a student produces all year, and the right response to it is analysis rather than panic. February and March are the execution window: the topic list from the mock gets worked through, internal assessment deadlines land, and the Ramadan period usually falls somewhere in here with shortened school days and a shifted household rhythm. April and early May are for timed papers and nothing else.

The table below sets this out in a form that can be put on a calendar. The one period worth flagging to a household in this corridor specifically is the Ramadan window, because two working parents plus shortened school days plus after-Iftar scheduling is a genuine logistical puzzle, and it is much easier solved in advance than in the first week of it.

sections.heading: What an evening slot costs, and what is actually available after six
paragraphs: Availability and price move together in this market and almost nobody says so. The most-requested slots across Dubai are between four and six on weekdays, so those are the ones that fill first and the ones where a family has least choice of tutor in February. Earlier slots and later slots are both easier to book, and for a household in this corridor that is useful information rather than a consolation.

The market bands first, so the comparison is grounded. A budget online tutor, usually a university student, runs AED 45-150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150-300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An IB or IGCSE specialist runs AED 200-450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Premium named tutors reach AED 500-650, with BartyED publishing AED 650. Those are market figures from those providers, gathered in October 2026, and none is an IB Gram price.

The in-home comparison is where this district differs from the Dubai average. In-home rates run roughly AED 180-500 an hour with travel priced in, per Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table at 180-350 and home tutors quoted at 200-500. In a district where the student can get themselves home on the tram, paying a travel premium for a tutor to make the opposite journey through the Sheikh Zayed Road evening peak is a hard case to argue on any grounds except preference.

The honest point about timing is that a family starting in October has a materially better choice of tutor than the same family starting in March, at the same rate. Specialist evening slots fill from January as Year 11 and Diploma Year 2 demand peaks across the emirate. If a problem is already visible in October, acting then buys a better tutor rather than a cheaper one.
