sections.heading: The UAE weekend, and where revision actually fits
paragraphs: The UAE working week shapes revision in ways that catch out families who have moved from elsewhere. The weekend sits on Saturday and Sunday for most private schools, with Friday a short or half day in many of them, and that produces a specific pattern: a long free block at the end of the week and a compressed Friday that is neither a school day nor a weekend day. Most households waste it.

For coursework, that block is the only realistic home for serious work. An internal assessment, an Extended Essay chapter or a piece of data analysis does not fit into a weekday hour between a school day and dinner. Ninety minutes to two hours on a weekend morning, at the stage of the drafting cycle the student is actually at, achieves more than three weekday sessions spent getting restarted each time.

For revision, the weekend's value is the opposite: it is where cumulative work belongs. Weekday evenings suit current topics and the immediate homework; the weekend suits returning to material from two months ago, which is the thing nobody does voluntarily and the thing that decides a terminal paper. A simple rule that works for Year 11 and Diploma students alike is that weekdays handle what is current and one weekend session handles what is old.

The Friday half day deserves its own mention. In a two-income household it is often the one afternoon when a parent is around and the student is free, and it is the best available slot for the conversations that are not tutoring: looking at a mark scheme together, checking what the internal deadlines are, putting the term's dates on a calendar. Those conversations are worth more than an extra hour of content and they cost nothing.

sections.heading: Dates a working parent should diarise rather than discover
paragraphs: The single highest-value hour a working parent can spend on this is putting five or six dates into a calendar in September. Almost every avoidable crisis in a Dubai school year comes from a deadline discovered rather than planned for, and the deadlines are published or obtainable from the school. The table below lists what to diarise, where it comes from and why it matters.

The board deadlines are the hardest edges. Cambridge set final entries for the March 2027 series at 27 November 2026, with the exam period from 3 February to 4 March 2027 and results on Cambridge Direct on 13 May 2027. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise. Ask your school's exams officer which zone it is in.

Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so the live official PDF is the only version to plan against. The November 2026 International GCSE final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which is the figure that matters if a sixth-form place depends on a resit.

The school's own internal deadlines are the ones that bite first for a Diploma family, and they are not published anywhere a parent can find. Ask the IB coordinator in September for the internal assessment and Extended Essay dates for the whole year, in writing. No IB session or results date appears on this page, because the IB's own site could not be confirmed directly for this project; confirm any IB date with your coordinator rather than with a tutoring site.

sections.heading: Checking in five minutes whether a tutor may legally teach here
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit and most parents have never been told. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so any page quoting an amount is not working from a source.

The eligible categories are wider than people expect. The u.ae guidance names teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee, gives a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

For a working parent, the five-minute version is three questions. Does this individual tutor hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. Is my child enrolled at the tutor's own school, because the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's school, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit Abu Dhabi school staff from paid private tutoring of their own students. And if a tuition centre is involved, does it hold a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a licence for premises rather than a badge for an individual.

Those questions also happen to filter for professionalism. A tutor who answers them directly is running something organised. A tutor who is vague, or who tells you the requirement does not exist, has given you the answer. It is worth noting that no online platform holds a KHDA approval for its tutors, because no such approval exists in that form; the permit that exists for institutes applies to premises in Dubai.

sections.heading: Coursework deadlines when both parents work late
paragraphs: Internal assessment and Extended Essay work is where unsupervised afternoons do the most damage, and it is slow damage. Nothing visible goes wrong for weeks. A research question is not chosen, then not narrowed, then not tested, and the student arrives at the school's internal deadline with six weeks of work to do in nine days. No parent saw it happen because there was nothing to see.

The structural fix is to put the stages on a calendar rather than the deadline. A research question chosen by one date, a method agreed by another, data collected by a third, a first draft written by a fourth. Each of those is checkable in two minutes by a parent who was not in the room, and each one that slips is a signal while there is still time to act. The deadline alone gives no warning at all.

This is also where the academic honesty risk concentrates, and it should be named plainly. A student alone at eleven at night with a deadline in two days is who the market's worst pages are built for. The research for this project found a provider selling finished internal assessments at AED 3,750. Buying one is academic malpractice under IB rules, the investigation falls on the candidate, and the consequence reaches the whole Diploma rather than a single grade.

The legitimate version is more useful in exactly that situation. A tutor may teach what each criterion rewards, scale a research question to the weeks that remain, explain how data and uncertainty should be handled, and give written feedback on a draft the student has produced. A tutor may not supply text for submission or hand over a model answer. A parent test that needs no subject knowledge: ask who will have written every word by the end, and treat vagueness as the answer.

process.title: Tell us when the student is actually home and alone
process.description: The useful facts are the arrival time, whether the journey is independent, and what time an adult appears. Those three decide the slot, and the slot decides whether the arrangement survives to February. The subject matters, but it is the second question rather than the first in a two-income household.

process.title: Send the last marked assessment
process.description: A marked mock, a returned test or a criterion-marked task shows where the marks are actually going. In a household where no adult sees the daily work, this is also the only reliable evidence available, which makes it more important here than in a home with a parent at the table each afternoon.

process.title: Trial at the real slot, with the real travel
process.description: The trial runs on a normal weekday at the time you intend to keep, after the actual journey home. That tests two things at once: whether the tutor suits your child, and whether your child can concentrate at that hour having travelled back on their own.

process.title: Agree the note format before the term starts
process.description: A parent who was not present at five needs to know what was covered, what was set and how it went. We agree what the written note after each session contains, so steering the term does not depend on interrogating a teenager over dinner.

process.title: Review against the next marked evidence
process.description: Progress is judged on the next marked assessment rather than on a feeling after a month. If the question types we targeted have not moved, the approach changes or the tutor does, and that judgement is only possible because the targets were written down at the start.

whyPoints.title: The slot fits the household, not the bell
whyPoints.description: Online delivery makes 4:15pm and 7:30pm equally possible, which matters in a district where neither parent is home at four. The unsupervised two hours after school are either the most productive of the day or entirely lost, and the difference is whether something is scheduled in them.

whyPoints.title: Tutors matched by time zone as well as subject
whyPoints.description: A 7pm Dubai slot has to be a sustainable working hour at the tutor's end or it gets cancelled in week six. We ask that question before booking, because continuity is the whole value of a weekly arrangement.

whyPoints.title: Written notes for a parent who was not there
whyPoints.description: After every session you get what was covered, what was set and an honest read on how it went. That is what makes a term steerable by a parent who got home at seven, rather than something they are merely paying for.

whyPoints.title: Coursework tracked by stage, not by deadline
whyPoints.description: Research question, method, data, first draft, each with its own date. Every stage is checkable in two minutes, so a slip becomes visible while there is time to act instead of nine days before the school's internal deadline.

whyPoints.title: No travel premium for a journey nobody needs
whyPoints.description: In-home rates in Dubai run roughly AED 180-500 an hour with the drive priced in. In a corridor where the student can get home on the tram, paying for a tutor to make the opposite journey through the evening peak is hard to justify on any ground but preference.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary survives deadline pressure
whyPoints.description: We teach criteria, scale research questions and give written feedback on the student's own draft. We do not supply submittable text. The pages that do are built for exactly the student sitting alone at eleven at night two days out.

faqs.question: Can my child start a session alone before we get home from the office?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in this corridor that is the normal arrangement. Sessions run online over live video, so no adult needs to be in the building. A student who travels back on the tram or the metro can be at a desk by about a quarter past four, which converts the least productive two hours of the day into the most productive. You receive a written note after each session naming what was covered and what was set, so the term stays steerable without interrogating a teenager at dinner.

faqs.question: Can a tutor visit our apartment in Dubai Internet City instead?
faqs.answer: No. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered online, one to one, over live video, and IB Gram does not make home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service offered only in India. In this district the case for in-home support is weaker than elsewhere anyway: in-home market rates run roughly AED 180-500 an hour with travel priced in, against AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and the student can usually get themselves home on the tram without anyone making the journey.

faqs.question: Is a 7:30pm session too late to be useful?
faqs.answer: It depends on the student rather than the hour. Diploma students in DP1 and DP2 often work better at seven than at four, particularly those with sport or activities until six. Younger students, after a full school day, frequently do not. The test is empirical: trial a late session and look at what the student actually produces in it. Be sceptical of a late slot chosen for parental convenience and comfortable with one chosen because the student is demonstrably sharper at that hour.

faqs.question: Does it matter where my child's tutor is based if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: Their time zone matters; their postcode does not. A 7pm Dubai slot needs to be a sustainable working hour at the tutor's end, or the arrangement becomes a favour and favours get cancelled around week six. A 4:30pm Dubai session is early afternoon in the United Kingdom and early evening in India, so it is easy to staff consistently. Ask directly what time the session is where the tutor is, and whether that is a normal working hour for them.

faqs.question: Which schools can a student in this corridor reach without a parent driving?
faqs.answer: Several, which is unusual for Dubai. The tram along Al Sufouh Road and the metro put the Al Sufouh campuses within fifteen to twenty-five minutes, including Dubai College, GEMS Wellington International School and Regent International School, and the Al Barsha cluster within twenty-five to forty minutes for campuses near a station, including American School of Dubai, Dubai American Academy and Kings' School Al Barsha. Check your own route and finishing time, since these vary by year group and day. Those schools are named as context only.

faqs.question: When in the Dubai school year should we start tutoring?
faqs.answer: October or November if a problem is already visible. That window is for building the system, when content is being delivered and nothing is urgent, so retrieval routines, command-term work and timed practice can be established without competing against a deadline. It is also when specialist tutors are most available, before the January rush. A family starting in March pays the same rate for a materially narrower choice of tutor, because Year 11 and Diploma Year 2 demand peaks across the emirate from January.

faqs.question: How should a working parent handle the Ramadan period?
faqs.answer: By planning it before it starts rather than in its first week. School days shorten, the household rhythm changes, and a 5:30pm slot that worked in November is often wrong. Many families in this corridor move the session to after Iftar and keep the continuity, which online delivery makes practical because nothing depends on a tutor travelling. Ask the school for its Ramadan arrangements as soon as they are published, and decide the replacement slot then, when there is still choice available.

faqs.question: What dates should I put in the calendar in September?
faqs.answer: Six: the school's exam entry deadline, the Cambridge administrative zone and timetable version it uses, the internal assessment and Extended Essay deadlines from the IB coordinator, the mock examination window, the Ramadan term arrangements once published, and the results dates for the relevant series. Almost every avoidable crisis in a Dubai school year comes from a deadline discovered rather than planned. Cambridge set final entries for the March 2027 series at 27 November 2026, months before the February papers.

faqs.question: Why does the Cambridge zone timetable matter for my child?
faqs.answer: Because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states plainly that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. A revision plan built from a timetable found online can therefore be wrong by days. Ask your school's exams officer which zone the centre sits in, and use the school's own version. Pearson revises provisional timetables, so use the live official PDF there.

faqs.question: My child has coursework due and I never see it being done. What should I check?
faqs.answer: Stages rather than the deadline. Put four dates on a calendar: research question chosen, method agreed, data collected, first draft written. Each is checkable in two minutes by a parent who was not in the room, and each slip is a signal while there is time to act. A deadline on its own gives no warning, which is why unsupervised afternoons produce internal assessments with six weeks of work left and nine days to do it in.

faqs.question: Someone offered to produce my child's internal assessment. Is that normal in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It exists in this market and it should be refused. Research for this project found a provider selling finished internal assessments at AED 3,750. Buying one is academic malpractice under IB rules; the investigation falls on the candidate, and the consequence reaches the whole Diploma rather than one grade. Legitimate support teaches what each criterion rewards, scales a research question to the time left, and gives written feedback on a draft the student wrote. Ask who will have written every word, and treat vagueness as the answer.

faqs.question: How do we check a private tutor is permitted to work in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions. Does the individual hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Is your child enrolled at the tutor's own school, which the permit's code of conduct bars. And if a tuition centre is involved, does it hold a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which licenses premises rather than individuals. A tutor who answers directly is running something organised; vagueness, or a claim that no requirement exists, is itself the answer.

faqs.question: Does my child need two sessions a week or one?
faqs.answer: One for maintenance, two while something specific is being closed. A student working through a named list of question types from a marked mock usually needs two a week for six to ten weeks, then one. Two a week indefinitely, with no list attached, is how a family spends a year without ever establishing whether it worked. Agree what the second session is for and when it stops before booking it, and review at the next marked assessment rather than on a feeling.

faqs.question: Where does the UAE weekend fit into revision?
faqs.answer: Weekdays handle what is current; the weekend handles what is old. Cumulative review of material from two months ago is the thing nobody does voluntarily and the thing that decides a terminal paper, and it needs a longer block than a weekday evening between school and dinner. The weekend is also the only realistic home for coursework drafting, where ninety minutes to two hours achieves more than three weekday sessions spent restarting. The Friday half day is the best slot for calendar and mark-scheme conversations with a parent present.

faqs.question: What if no tutor is free in the slot we need?
faqs.answer: The slot between half past five and half past six is the most requested across Dubai, so it fills first and is hardest to book from January onwards. Earlier and later slots are both easier, which is useful rather than consoling in a district where students travel home independently and later sessions are workable. If the specific subject and level combination has a thin specialist pool, you will be told that before booking rather than handed a generalist for a Higher Level subject.

dubai/dubai-internet-city.closingBody: In a household where nobody is home at four, the decisive choice is which evening hour the work happens in. Tell us the arrival time, whether the journey is independent, what time an adult appears, and send the last marked assessment. You will get a named tutor trialled at the real slot after the real journey, written notes after every session, and a plan with a stated end rather than an open subscription. Lessons run online over live video.

dubai/dubai-investment-park.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB and IGCSE subjects to students across Dubai Investments Park, Green Community and the Jebel Ali corridor. Where a family's budget allows one hour a week rather than three, the first job is deciding which hour buys the most, which is a different conversation from which subject feels worst.

intro.heading: Three kinds of household, one question asked first: what does it cost?
paragraphs: Dubai Investments Park is not one place. It runs from Green Community's shaded low-rise villas through residential blocks and labour accommodation to warehousing and light industry, with Expo Road on one side and Jebel Ali on the other. The households that ask us for tutoring here are correspondingly varied, and they are unusually direct about money. In a market where three of the six best-ranking pages for these searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in dollars, that directness deserves a straight answer.

So the structure of this page is unusual. It leads with rates in dirhams, broken down by programme and level, with every band traced back to whoever published it. It then sets tutoring against school fees, because tutoring is a marginal cost on top of a large fixed one and the decision is always made against that backdrop. Then it sets out what you give up at each price point, because the honest answer to whether a group class is good value is that it depends entirely on what you were hoping the hour would do.

The second half of the page is about the households themselves. A Green Community family with a child at the IB school inside the community has a different problem from an apartment family in DIP 2 whose child is bussed to Jebel Ali and gets home at five. The first is usually choosing between Higher Level subjects and worrying about an Internal Assessment. The second is often fitting one hour a week into a crowded evening and wanting it to count. Both are legitimate, and neither is served by a page that says contact us for pricing.

What is not here is a price list for IB Gram. We quote after a consultation and a trial lesson, with the terms written down, because a six-week push before IGCSE papers and a two-year Diploma plan across two Higher Level subjects are different products with different costs. What is here is the market band each of those sits inside, so that you can recognise a quote that is out of line in either direction. A quote well under the budget band usually means a tutor without the subject depth; one well over usually means a brand premium.

A last thing worth saying on a page about money. There is no price at which a grade becomes purchasable. This page makes no promise about any outcome, publishes no satisfaction percentage, carries no star rating, and names no school as a client or partner. Several pages competing for these searches do all four, and one sells finished Internal Assessments outright, which is malpractice with the consequence falling on the student. Spending more does not change any of that.

dubai/dubai-investment-park.programmesIntro: Cost scales with level rather than with subject, which is the single most useful thing to understand before budgeting. The notes below set out what each programme actually demands of a tutoring hour, and therefore why the bands move.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with reporting written against approaches to learning rather than percentages. The useful work at this stage is reading fluency, number sense and the habit of explaining reasoning aloud. Sessions are short, because attention rather than content is the limiting factor, and that keeps the hourly cost at the lower end of every band.
programmes.countryNote: Green Community households with children at the IB school inside the community generally need very little here, and when they do it is reading or early number. Families in the DIP residential blocks whose children travel further often ask for primary support in English, where the gap is written expression rather than conversation.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years, eight or nine subjects, with Cambridge subjects tiered Core or Extended and Pearson structured by paper. Codes differ and are not interchangeable: Cambridge 0580, 0620, 0625 and 0610 against Pearson 4MA1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and 4BI1. Extended-tier work sits in a higher rate band than Core because the teaching demands more subject depth.
programmes.countryNote: This is where most of the enquiries from this part of Dubai land, and where budget decisions bite hardest, because the exam year coincides with the point at which a family is often also paying for a sibling's school place. Two sessions a week across two subjects for a full Year 11 is a real number and worth modelling before committing.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internal Assessments are marked against named criteria and carry a substantial share of most grades. Higher Level teaching requires genuine specialism, which is why the specialist band sits well above the general qualified-tutor band in every published rate card.
programmes.countryNote: A two-year Diploma plan is the largest tutoring commitment most families here will consider, and it is the one where modelling the whole cost in advance changes decisions. Some families conclude that one Higher Level subject supported properly across two years beats three subjects supported thinly for one.

programmes.name: Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge support
programmes.description: Bought as blocks rather than weekly hours, usually four to six sessions attached to a deadline. The work is process coaching: criterion reading, topic feasibility, questioning a draft, referencing. It sits in the specialist band because it requires somebody who knows the criteria, and it is never group work.
programmes.countryNote: Blocks are the most cost-efficient tutoring most Diploma families buy, because they are finite, attached to a real deadline and aimed at a component with a published mark allocation. They are also the area where the market contains outright malpractice, so what the block does and does not include should be in writing.

dubai/dubai-investment-park.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones families in this part of Dubai most often choose to spend their hour on, with a note on what that hour realistically achieves in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE)
subjects.description: The best single-hour investment in most Year 10 and 11 households, because fluency gains compound and transfer into the sciences. Weekly short timed drills marked for working rather than answers move marks faster than long explanatory sessions.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: Narrow and diagnosable. At IGCSE the losses cluster in electricity and the practical-skills paper rather than across the subject, which means a short block aimed at two topics can be better value than an open-ended weekly arrangement.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: Moles and electrolysis at IGCSE; energetics and organic mechanisms at Diploma. A great deal of the lost mark comes from calculations written without working, so partial credit is unavailable. That is cheap to fix and expensive to leave.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: Content-heavy and therefore tempting to tutor at length, which is usually poor value. The gains sit in structuring six-mark explain answers to the mark scheme shape, which is a technique block rather than a term of teaching.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level sits firmly in the specialist band and justifies it. Paper 3 is an unstructured investigative paper, and the skill it tests, sustaining an argument in writing, is not something a general maths tutor reliably teaches.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and calculator work throughout. Students who chose it to avoid algebra find inference harder than expected, and the exploration needs genuine statistical judgement rather than more calculations.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language and English First Language
subjects.description: The hour with the widest spillover, because every other subject is assessed through written English. For a household buying one hour a week, this is frequently the correct answer even when another subject has the lower grade.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Management
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0455 and 0450
subjects.description: Evaluation and diagram accuracy decide the marks. A knowledgeable answer with no judgement in it is the standard failure, and correcting it is a technique job that works well in a short block before a mock.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode discipline and trace tables at IGCSE; data structures and the solution-development project at Diploma. Marks go missing in documentation rather than in code, which students consistently underestimate.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.description: Required in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs. Support must follow the school's own scheme, because the Ministry restricts different or additional content without prior permission.

dubai/dubai-investment-park.regionsIntro: Within a few kilometres this district contains villa communities, apartment blocks, a sustainable development and the edge of Dubai South. Household type, not distance, is what changes the tutoring question.

regions.name: Green Community
regions.note: Low-rise villas and apartments around a lake, with an IB school inside the community. An IB tutor in Green Community is usually working on Higher Level subject choice or Internal Assessment process rather than on basic content gaps.

regions.name: Dubai Investments Park 1
regions.note: Mixed residential and commercial, with families spread across schools in DIP, Jebel Ali and Al Furjan. An IGCSE tutor in Dubai Investments Park is most often booked for Mathematics and English on a single weekly hour.

regions.name: Dubai Investments Park 2
regions.note: More apartment stock and longer school runs westward. Evening slots after five are the norm here, and because lessons are delivered over live video the later slot costs nothing extra in logistics.

regions.name: The Sustainable City
regions.note: A small, settled community with its own IB school. Requests here lean towards Diploma sciences and the Extended Essay, where the cohort is small and Higher Level subject availability can be narrow.

regions.name: Al Furjan
regions.note: Dense villa and townhouse development with several British-curriculum schools close by. IGCSE tuition in Al Furjan is commonly booked around the Year 10 tier decision rather than in the final term.

regions.name: Discovery Gardens
regions.note: Apartment living with the longest school runs in the corridor and the tightest budgets. This is where the one-hour-a-week question is asked most often, and where getting the choice of subject right matters most.

regions.name: Jebel Ali and Dubai South edge
regions.note: Shift patterns in the free zone and the airport district push family evenings later than the Dubai average. An IB DP tutor in Jebel Ali often works a slot after seven, which a travelling tutor could not sustain.

schoolClusters.city: Inside Dubai Investments Park and Green Community
schoolClusters.note: Provision inside the district itself, spanning an IB continuum school and several Indian and British-curriculum schools. The IB school in Green Community is the reason this district has a higher Diploma share of enquiries than its neighbours, and the Indian-curriculum schools here generate most of the transfer questions.

schoolClusters.city: Jebel Ali, Al Furjan and The Sustainable City
schoolClusters.note: Where most secondary students from the DIP apartment blocks actually sit, plus the IB provision in The Sustainable City. These cohorts are large on the British side and small on the IB side, which shows up as narrower Higher Level choice and more requests for subjects the school could not timetable.

dubai/dubai-investment-park.modesIntro: The three arrangements below differ mainly in cost per week rather than in method. Picking between them is a budget decision with an academic consequence, and it is worth making deliberately.

modes.title: One hour a week, one subject
modes.description: The arrangement most households in this district actually buy. It works when the hour is spent on marked work rather than on fresh teaching, and when thirty minutes of independent practice happens between sessions. Without that practice the hour becomes the only work being done and the return collapses, which is a method problem rather than a budget one.

Blocks are finite, aimed at a component with a published mark allocation, and therefore easy to budget. They are also the most cost-efficient tutoring most Diploma families buy, because the marks are concentrated.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs in Dubai, in dirhams, by programme and level
paragraphs: The bands below come from published rate cards read in October 2026. The tier bands themselves are sourced: budget online tutors from around AED 45 to 150, qualified subject tutors online at AED 150 to 300, in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 500 including travel, IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more, and premium named tutors above that, with one provider publishing AED 650. Monthly packages advertised in the market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

What the table does is map those sourced tier bands onto programme levels, which is an interpretation rather than a separate measurement, and it is labelled as such. The logic is straightforward: the level determines how much subject depth the hour requires, and subject depth is what moves a tutor from the qualified band into the specialist band. A Year 7 MYP hour and a Diploma Higher Level hour are not the same job, and no published rate card acknowledges that, which is why parents comparing quotes end up confused.

Read the table as a sanity check rather than a price list. If a quote for Higher Level Chemistry comes in at AED 90 an hour, the question is what subject depth is being supplied at that price. If it comes in at AED 700, the question is what the premium buys beyond the teaching. Both questions are reasonable to ask out loud. IB Gram quotes after a consultation and a trial lesson, with the terms in writing, because the right arrangement for a six-week push is not the right arrangement for a two-year plan.

sections.heading: Tutoring set against school fees, which is the real comparison
paragraphs: No family decides on tutoring in isolation. It is decided against a school fee already paid, and in Dubai that fee is a very large number. The emirate's private sector carried 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, and in May 2026 the regulator confirmed there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. For a household in this district, many of whom moved here on exactly that arithmetic, the freeze is the single most useful piece of budgeting news of the year.

The table sets tutoring into that context using published monthly estimates rather than our own figures. The pattern it reveals is worth noticing: a weekly budget-tier arrangement is a small fraction of a school fee, while a specialist exam-year arrangement across two subjects is not. The decision point is usually not whether to tutor but at what tier, and families frequently discover that one subject supported properly costs less than three supported thinly and does considerably more.

Two further costs deserve a line in any model. Private candidate examination entry fees are a real item for any student entering a paper outside their school's entry, and they are set by the board rather than by a tutor. And the two-year Diploma is a compound commitment: two subjects at two sessions a week across twenty-four months is a number most families have never actually added up. Adding it up before DP1 changes the plan; adding it up in DP2 changes nothing except the mood.

sections.heading: What you give up at each price point
paragraphs: A cheaper hour is not a worse hour in every respect; it is a different trade. A group class at AED 110 per student buys breadth, peers and a timetable, and it costs you the share of attention that your child specifically needs. A university-student tutor at AED 90 buys enthusiasm, recent experience of the exam and genuine patience, and it costs you depth at Higher Level, where the gap between having passed a subject and being able to teach it is widest. Neither is a scandal. Both become one if nobody names the trade.

The column worth reading is the third. A one-to-one hour gives your child the whole hour, which sounds obvious and is in fact the entire product. In a group of four, each student gets a quarter of the questioning and all of the content, which is excellent value for revision breadth and poor value for a specific recurring error. In a centre class of twelve, the content is delivered well and the individual diagnosis does not happen at all, which is also true of the school classroom the child has just left.

The fourth column is what nobody tells you. Group classes cannot work on your child's own marked script. Budget tutors frequently cannot teach the Higher Level extension topics. Premium brand tutors can, and you are also paying for the brand. In-home visits put somebody in the room, and in this corridor they also put between forty and ninety minutes of driving into the arrangement, which is either in the fee or in the narrowness of who is available. Choose the trade deliberately rather than by price alone.

sections.heading: The charges to confirm in writing before the first lesson
paragraphs: A published hourly rate answers less than it appears to. Four questions decide what you actually pay, and none of them is usually on the page you booked from. Is marking between sessions inside the hour or extra? What happens to a lesson cancelled inside twenty-four hours, and does the answer differ depending on who cancels? Are materials included, and if so whose materials are they? And does the rate change in the term before the exam session, which several providers quietly do.

Two more are specific to this market. Ask whether the quoted figure includes VAT, and get the answer in writing. The tax treatment of tuition fees is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority rather than for anybody selling tutoring, so the only honest statement a provider can make is whether their own quoted price is inclusive. And ask what happens to unused sessions in a monthly package at month end, because a package advertised at AED 799 for eight sessions is a different proposition if the eighth expires.

The last question is about people rather than money. Who exactly is teaching, and will it be the same person every week? Several platforms in this market match to a pool rather than to a person, which means the tutor who knows your child's recurring error in week two is not the one in week five. Ask for the individual's name, what they have taught and at what level, and whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free, valid for two years and therefore reasonable to require.
bullets: Is marking between sessions inside the rate or billed separately?
What is the cancellation position inside twenty-four hours, both ways?
Does the rate rise in the term before the exam session?
Does the quoted figure include VAT, confirmed in writing?
Do unused package sessions carry over or expire at month end?
Who is teaching, every week, and do they hold the MoHRE permit?

sections.heading: If the budget is one hour a week, which subject gets it?
paragraphs: This is the most common real question in this district and the one most pages avoid, because answering it honestly means telling some families that the subject they are worried about is not the subject to buy. The rule that works is spillover. Spend the hour where the gain transfers to other subjects, which in most households means written English or Mathematics, even when a third subject has the lower grade on the report.

Written English spills into everything, because every other subject is assessed through it. A student who writes compressed procedural answers loses marks in Biology, Economics, Geography and History simultaneously, and fixing the writing moves all four. Mathematics spills into Physics and Chemistry and into the quantitative parts of Economics and Business. Those two are the high-leverage choices, and a single weekly hour on either will usually show up in more than one subject by the second term.

The exception is a hard deadline. If an Internal Assessment is due in six weeks and the draft is weak, that block outranks the spillover argument, because the marks are concentrated, published and about to be locked in. After the deadline, go back to the spillover rule. The other exception is a genuine content hole, as opposed to a weak grade: a student who has never been taught two units cannot technique their way through them, and that gap needs closing before anything else is worth buying.

One more test is worth applying before you commit the hour. Ask your child which subject they avoid doing homework for. That answer is frequently different from the lowest grade on the report, and it is usually more diagnostic, because avoidance tracks the subject where the student has no idea what a good answer looks like. An hour spent making that visible, with a marked script on screen and the mark scheme beside it, tends to change behaviour in a way that an hour of extra content does not.
bullets: Default to the subject with the widest spillover, usually English or Mathematics
A live coursework deadline outranks spillover, until it has passed
A genuine untaught unit outranks both; technique cannot operate on absent knowledge
Lowest grade on the report is the worst single guide to where the hour goes
Re-decide after the next real assessment rather than every few weeks

sections.heading: Who lives in Dubai Investments Park, and what each household asks for
paragraphs: Green Community households are the most settled in the district, often long-term residents with children who have been at the same school for years, and frequently with an IB continuum school inside the community. Their enquiries are about choice and process rather than remediation: whether Higher Level Chemistry is the right call for a medicine application, whether the Extended Essay topic will sustain four thousand words, whether Maths Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation is the better route for a given degree.

The DIP residential blocks and Discovery Gardens are a different population: shorter tenancies, tighter budgets, longer school runs and a higher share of mid-course arrivals from India, Pakistan, the Philippines and Egypt. Their enquiries concentrate on one or two subjects, a single weekly hour, and value for money, and they often come with a specific, useful piece of evidence attached, because these are families who have already read the report carefully.

The third group is the Jebel Ali and Dubai South working households, where the free zone and airport shift patterns push the family evening later than the Dubai average. The constraint there is simply time of day. An arrangement that requires a lesson before six in the evening does not survive contact with a shift rota, and a tutor who has to drive cannot absorb a slot after seven. Online delivery solves a scheduling problem here rather than a preference.

None of these three groups is better served by a generic page. What they share is a preference for being told the trade-off rather than being sold the premium option, which is why this page leads with sourced bands and with what each price point gives up. The enquiry that works best from any of them is short and concrete: the school, the year, the board, the slot that exists, the budget, and one marked piece of work.

sections.heading: What no amount of tutoring money can buy
paragraphs: There is no price at which a grade becomes a purchasable item, and a page that leads with rates owes you that sentence explicitly. This site publishes no promise about any outcome, no satisfaction percentage, no improvement figure and no star rating. Competing pages in this market publish several of each, including two separate aggregate ratings on the same page with different numbers, and one that shows a rating from twenty reviews next to a claim of several thousand enrolled students. Self-asserted review markup is against Google's own structured-data policy and, as a commercial representation in the UAE, a consumer-protection exposure.

Nor can money buy assessed work legitimately. At least one page ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments. Under IB rules submitting work that is not your own is malpractice, the school is obliged to report it, and the consequence falls on the candidate, who can lose the subject or the whole Diploma. The seller keeps the fee. A tutor may teach research skills, read criteria aloud, challenge a topic, question a draft and point out an unsupported conclusion. A tutor may not supply the text.

And money cannot buy accreditation we do not hold. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. It holds no approval from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, operates no premises in the UAE, and does not send tutors to UAE homes. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific thing issued to specific entities, and claiming it without holding it is the single most dangerous sentence available to a page like this one.
bullets: No outcome promise, no improvement figure, no satisfaction percentage on this site

sections.heading: Starting from Dubai Investments Park
paragraphs: Send four things and the first conversation becomes useful immediately: the school, the year group, the board and syllabus code, and one marked piece of work. If the question is budget rather than diagnosis, say so and say what the budget is; it is a more productive opening than a general enquiry, because the honest advice at one hour a week is different from the advice at three, and nobody is served by pretending otherwise.

From there we identify a specialist at the right level who is free in your slot, and arrange a consultation and a trial lesson before any block is booked, with the terms written down at that point. If the match is wrong after a lesson or two, say so and we change it. If nobody suitable is free in your slot, we say that instead of offering a quiet near-match, which happens most often for narrow Higher Level combinations close to the May session and for the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education streams.

One practical note on the evening. Because lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, a slot at half past seven is as workable as one at half past four, and two subjects or two children can take consecutive slots in a single evening without a second journey for anybody. In a district where shift patterns and long school runs are the norm, that flexibility is usually worth more than a small difference in the hourly figure, and it is the reason we do not run an in-home service here.

faqs.question: How much does a private tutor cost per hour for a family in Dubai Investments Park?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rate cards read in October 2026 put budget online tutors at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, qualified subject tutors online at AED 150 to 300, in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 500 including travel, and IB or IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more, with one provider publishing AED 650 at the premium end. Mapped onto levels, expect the qualified band for most IGCSE work and the specialist band for Diploma Higher Level and coursework process support. Those are other providers' figures, quoted as market context. IB Gram quotes after a consultation and trial lesson, in writing.

faqs.question: Is one-to-one tutoring worth the extra cost over a group class here?
faqs.answer: It depends on what the hour is meant to do. A group of two to four at roughly AED 90 to 180 per student is good value for revision breadth and for a student who works better alongside peers. It cannot work on your child's own marked script, and it cannot diagnose a recurring error, because the questioning is shared. If the problem is a specific repeated loss, such as calculations written without working or answers that describe when the question said explain, one-to-one is the only format that reaches it. If the problem is that a whole syllabus needs a second pass, a group class is defensible.

faqs.question: Which schools are actually inside Dubai Investments Park?
faqs.answer: The district and Green Community contain an IB continuum school alongside several Indian and British-curriculum schools: Greenfield International School, Dove Green Private School, Nibras International School, The Ambassador School and Bright Riders School come up most in our enquiries. Students from the DIP apartment blocks also travel to The Winchester School Jebel Ali, Sunmarke School and Safa Community School, and there is IB provision in The Sustainable City and at South View School nearby. These names are local context only. Verify any school against the regulator's own listing, and note that IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: Which charges should I confirm in writing before the first lesson?
faqs.answer: Six. Whether marking between sessions is inside the hourly rate or billed separately. What happens to a lesson cancelled inside twenty-four hours, and whether the answer differs depending on who cancels. Whether materials are included and whose they are. Whether the rate rises in the term before the exam session. Whether the quoted figure includes VAT, which only the provider can state for their own price. And whether unused sessions in a monthly package carry over or expire. Those six decide what you actually pay far more than a ten-dirham difference in the headline figure does.

faqs.question: If we can only afford one hour a week, which subject should get it?
faqs.answer: Usually the one with the widest spillover, which in most households is written English or Mathematics, even when a third subject carries the lower grade. Written English is how every other subject is assessed, so fixing compressed procedural writing moves Biology, Economics, Geography and History at once. Mathematics feeds Physics, Chemistry and the quantitative parts of Economics. Two exceptions override that: a coursework deadline inside six weeks, because those marks are about to be locked in, and a genuine untaught unit, because technique cannot operate on knowledge that is simply absent.

faqs.question: Are Dubai private school fees going up for 2026-27?
faqs.answer: No. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. That is the backdrop against which most tutoring budgets in this district get approved, and it is worth knowing before you plan. For context, the emirate's private sector carried 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools and 16,846 places.

faqs.question: Does a monthly tutoring package work out cheaper than hourly billing in DIP?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the deciding question is what happens to sessions you do not use. Packages advertised in the Dubai market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Eight sessions a month is two a week, which is a real commitment, and a package only saves money if your household actually uses all eight in a month containing a half-term, a school trip and an exam week. Ask whether unused sessions carry over, and ask what notice is required to stop. If both answers are favourable, packages are usually cheaper per hour.

faqs.question: Does a quoted tutoring rate include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask, and get the answer in writing. The tax treatment of tuition fees in the UAE is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority rather than for anybody selling tutoring, so the only honest statement a provider can make is whether their own quoted figure is inclusive or exclusive of VAT, and whether they hold a tax registration number. Any page that asserts a general VAT position for tuition without citing the authority is telling you something it cannot support. For your own budgeting, treat an exclusive quote as five per cent higher than the number you were given.

faqs.question: Can two children in the same household share a session?
faqs.answer: If they are at the same level in the same subject, yes, and the small-group band applies at roughly AED 90 to 180 per student. If they are at different levels, sharing one hour means neither gets the hour, and the usual arrangement is two consecutive slots in the same evening instead. Because lessons are delivered over live video there is no second journey for anybody, so back-to-back slots cost nothing extra in logistics, come as one booking and produce one written summary. Several households in the DIP apartment blocks use exactly this pattern because only one evening is genuinely free.

faqs.question: Why does this page make no promise about my child's final grade?
faqs.answer: Because no honest one can be made. A grade depends on the student's own work over months, on the school's teaching, on the paper that happens to be set and on grade boundaries that vary by session. Any provider promising a specific score, a specific improvement or a hundred per cent of anything is selling certainty that does not exist, and in the UAE a commercial representation of that kind is also a consumer-protection exposure. What can be promised is a named tutor at a named level, work marked against the official wording, and a plan measured against a real assessment.

faqs.question: Should I trust a tutoring company's star rating?
faqs.answer: Only if the reviews are real, countable and attributable, and only if the number in the page markup matches the number you can see. In this market that is frequently not the case: competing pages show two different aggregate ratings on the same page, and one shows five out of five from twenty reviews next to a claim of several thousand enrolled students. Self-asserted review markup is against Google's own structured-data policy and carries a manual-action risk, which is why this site publishes no rating at all. Ask instead for the tutor's name, what they have taught, at what level, and for how long.

faqs.question: How many sessions should we book to begin with?
faqs.answer: One, then decide. A trial lesson plus a consultation tells you more than a committed block does, and it costs less to walk away from. After that, four sessions is a sensible first commitment for a weekly arrangement, because it is long enough to see whether independent work is actually happening between lessons and short enough to stop without argument. For coursework, buy the block that matches the deadline, usually four to six sessions, with the scope written down beforehand. Avoid open-ended arrangements with no review point; they drift, and drifting is expensive.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates rise closer to the exam session?
faqs.answer: Some providers do increase rates in the term before papers, and availability tightens regardless of price, which is the more important effect. In the weeks before the May session the specialists who teach narrow Higher Level combinations are the first to fill, and no amount of budget creates a free slot that does not exist. The practical response is to book earlier rather than to pay more later. Ask directly whether the quoted rate is fixed for the duration of the arrangement, and get the answer in writing, because this is one of the charges least often stated upfront.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest honest way to support an IGCSE student in this district?
faqs.answer: One weekly hour on the subject with the widest spillover, run as a marked-work cycle, with thirty protected minutes of independent practice between sessions. At the budget-to-qualified band that is roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month on published monthly estimates. The parts that cost nothing do most of the work: closing the notes and answering from memory instead of rereading, sitting twenty minutes of every revision hour under time, marking honestly against the mark scheme wording, and keeping the phone out of the room. A household doing those four things needs less tutoring, not more.

faqs.question: Is a university-student tutor good enough for IB Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and the permit position is separate from the competence question. University students are an eligible category for the MoHRE private tuition work permit, so they can tutor legally. What the budget band does not reliably supply is depth in the Higher Level extension topics and familiarity with how Internal Assessment criteria are actually marked, which are precisely the places Higher Level marks are won and lost. For primary and lower-secondary support, homework supervision or a confidence rebuild, a strong university student can be excellent value. For Higher Level sciences, pay for the specialist band.

dubai/dubai-investment-park.closingHeading: Tell us the budget, and we will tell you which hour buys the most
dubai/dubai-investment-park.closingBody: Most families in this district are not choosing between tutoring and no tutoring. They are choosing how many hours, at which tier, in which subject, against a school fee already paid. That is a decision worth making with published numbers in front of you rather than after three enquiries that all ended in contact us for pricing. Send the school, the year, the board and one marked piece of work, say what the budget is, and we will tell you plainly which hour does the most and whether a short block would serve you better than a weekly arrangement. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, and nothing is promised about the result.

dubai/dubai-marina.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma and MYP subjects and Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE to students at schools around the Marina, Al Sufouh, the Greens and Jumeirah Park. Each works from the student's own assessment calendar.

intro.heading: The lessons are fine. It is the unsupervised half that slips
paragraphs: Schools around Dubai Marina are, on the whole, well staffed and well inspected. A Diploma student at a school in Al Sufouh or Jumeirah Park is being taught the syllabus by subject specialists on a timetable that covers it. So when a Marina parent starts looking for a tutor, the trigger is usually not a teaching failure. It is the discovery that a large and heavily weighted part of the Diploma, and a smaller but decisive part of IGCSE, is produced by the student on their own time, to deadlines the school sets and the family never saw.

The arithmetic is worth seeing plainly. A Diploma student runs an internal assessment in each of six subjects, each one an independent piece of work over weeks or months. On top of that sits an Extended Essay with a 4,000-word limit, a Theory of Knowledge essay with a 1,600-word limit and a Theory of Knowledge exhibition, plus the Creativity, Activity, Service requirement. None of those is delivered in a taught period in the way a syllabus topic is. Each has a school-set internal deadline, and those deadlines are earlier than almost every family expects.

At IGCSE the equivalent gap is narrower but sharper. Class time covers the syllabus once. What it does not cover is the volume of past-paper practice that converts knowledge into marks, the recurring question types that appear every series, and the specific presentational conventions a mark scheme rewards. A Year 10 student who understood a topic in October and has not touched it since will meet it again in a Year 11 mock and perform as if they never learned it. That is a spacing problem, not a comprehension problem.

Which is why the useful first question for a Marina family is not which tutor is best but what exactly is unsupervised. Six internal assessments, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay and two years of retention are four different jobs with four different fixes, and only one of them looks like weekly tutoring. Confusing them produces a lot of hours and very little movement, which is the commonest pattern in this market.

Dubai Marina adds its own practical constraints. Households are mostly apartments, often with one quiet room shared between siblings and a parent on a call. The school run runs on a bus or a car along Sheikh Zayed Road or Al Sufouh Road, so a child is frequently not home and settled until well after four. And the area's population turns over quickly, so a tutor recommendation from a neighbour may be about a child at a different school on a different syllabus.

Lessons here are delivered online, one to one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. In a tower household that is usually an advantage rather than a compromise: no travel sitting inside the hourly rate, no coordination of a visitor past a concierge, and a specialist chosen for the subject and the syllabus code rather than for living within a twenty-minute drive.

dubai/dubai-marina.programmesIntro: Schools in and around the Marina run the full IB continuum and the British route to IGCSE, and the unsupervised component differs at each stage. These notes are about that, not about the programme in general.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external examinations and no coursework deadlines, so the independent half barely exists yet. What does exist is reading volume, and it is the one thing a primary programme assumes and does not supervise. A child who reads at home becomes a student who can handle the Diploma's reading load; a child who does not arrives at Year 7 short of it.
programmes.countryNote: Around the Marina the practical obstacle is the length of the day: a bus from a tower to Al Barsha or Jumeirah Park and back absorbs a large part of the afternoon, and the reading that the programme relies on competes with swimming, football and the pool downstairs. Primary tutoring is rarely the answer here; a protected reading slot usually is.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP introduces the independent habit through criterion-assessed tasks and the Personal Project in the final year. Criteria reward process, planning and reflection, which are exactly the parts a student completes alone, and which parents cannot see going wrong until a grade arrives.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools near the Marina run MYP to Year 9 and switch to IGCSE for Years 10 and 11, while others run MYP 5 straight into the Diploma. That matters because the two routes produce different unsupervised loads: one leads to external papers with past papers to practise, the other to internal tasks with criteria to decode.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with an internal assessment in each, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. The taught syllabus is the part the school controls. The internal components are produced by the student across two years, and the school's own deadlines govern them.
programmes.countryNote: Confirm every Diploma date with your school's coordinator rather than with a third-party page: UAE schools sit the May session, but no IB session or results date in this project has been verified from the IB itself. The binding dates for a Marina family are the school's internal deadlines anyway, and those are published in the school's own assessment calendar.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years, external papers, and syllabus codes that decide everything: 0580 and 0625 for Cambridge Mathematics and Physics, 4MA1 and 4PH1 for the Pearson equivalents. Many Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended, with the tier capping the grade available, which is a decision taken at entry rather than at results.
programmes.countryNote: The unsupervised part here is retention and practice volume. Class time covers the syllabus once across two years; nothing in the timetable returns a Year 10 topic to a student in Year 11 before the mock. Spaced retrieval and marked past papers against the exact code are what close that, and they are straightforward to run weekly.

dubai/dubai-marina.subjectsIntro: For each subject the question is the same: which part of it is taught in lessons and which part is left to the student. These notes name the second part.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Lessons cover the syllabus; the exploration does not teach itself. The internal assessment rewards a narrow, genuinely personal mathematical question explored properly, and the commonest failure is an ambitious topic abandoned halfway. Higher Level adds a paper three investigation that no amount of content revision prepares a student for.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling and statistics route, where the exploration usually involves the student's own data and therefore their own collection problems. Technology fluency is assumed throughout and is rarely taught explicitly, so a student who uses the graphing tool only in class loses time in the examination.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Class practicals demonstrate; the internal assessment demands an investigation the student designed, with uncertainty handled honestly and limitations identified. A verification of a known relationship scores poorly by design. The other unsupervised part is the extended explanation question, which needs practice rather than revision.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics are taught well in most schools around the Marina. What is left to the student is an independent investigation with a question narrow enough to produce usable data, and the discipline to start it before the term it is due. Both are schedulable.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The content is covered thoroughly; command-term discipline is the gap. Explain, outline, suggest, distinguish and evaluate each demand a different structure, and a complete answer that ignores the term scores in the middle bands. The internal assessment adds a design problem the syllabus does not address.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Set texts are taught; the individual oral is largely assembled by the student, who has to choose a global issue, select two extracts that genuinely support it and sustain an argument under time. The Higher Level essay is the other unsupervised component, and a question too broad is the usual cause of a middling mark.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Theory and diagrams come from lessons. The commentary work asks the student to find a published article, select the relevant theory and write to a tight structure, which is a research and selection skill rather than an economics one. Article choice decides more of the mark than most students believe.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study technique is taught; the internal assessment requires a real organisation, a narrow question and primary or secondary research the student organises alone. Broad questions produce broad answers, and narrowing the question early is the single highest-value intervention available.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Taught in a thin timetable slot in most schools and assessed through an essay with a 1,600-word limit on a prescribed title, plus an exhibition. Students who treat it as a general discussion subject underperform; the essay rewards a tightly argued position with counter-claims, which is a structure that can be taught in a couple of sessions.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A supervisor is assigned and meets the student a handful of times across a year. Everything between those meetings is unsupervised. The failure pattern is consistent: a question too large, reading started too late, and a first full version produced in the fortnight before the school's deadline rather than months earlier.

dubai/dubai-marina.igcseSubjectsIntro: At IGCSE the unsupervised work is practice rather than coursework, and it is specific to the syllabus code. These are the subjects Marina families most often ask about.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics
igcseSubjects.description: The tier decision caps the grade, and it is made at entry. Beyond that the whole game is marked past papers: recurring question types, method marks, and the habit of showing a line of working that earns credit even when the final answer is wrong.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics
igcseSubjects.description: Electricity and fields are where marks disappear, because both reward algebraic confidence under time pressure. Practical questions ask about apparatus, error and results from experiments the student has done once, which is why practical papers need their own practice rather than general revision.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry
igcseSubjects.description: Moles and the quantitative topics separate grades more than any other content area. The other recurring loss is the practical and data paper, where questions about method and sources of error are marked on precision rather than on recall.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology
igcseSubjects.description: Content heavy and the most forgiving of the three sciences to revise, and the most punishing of imprecise language. Marks go to the specific term rather than to a description of it, which is a habit built through marked answers instead of reading.

igcseSubjects.name: First Language English
igcseSubjects.description: Directed writing is the component where students who read well still lose marks, because it is assessed on register and audience rather than on quality of prose. Marked drafts against the published criteria move this faster than anything else.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
igcseSubjects.description: Both reward applying a named concept to the specific case in the question. Students who define well and apply loosely sit in the middle bands. Data-response technique and diagram accuracy are trainable from past papers with a mark scheme in hand.

igcseSubjects.name: Computer Science
igcseSubjects.description: Confident coders frequently underperform on the theory paper, particularly on data representation and on the precise pseudocode conventions the mark scheme expects. The fix is paper practice rather than more programming.

igcseSubjects.name: Additional Mathematics
igcseSubjects.description: Taken by stronger cohorts around the Marina as a bridge into Higher Level Diploma mathematics or A Level. It is unforgiving of gaps in algebraic fluency, and it is the subject where a weekly hour of supervised practice pays back most visibly.

regions.note: Across Sheikh Zayed Road, with a cluster layout that puts households on different sides of the Metro and therefore on different bus timings. The same schools serve both, but a JLT pickup can leave a child home half an hour later than a Marina one.

regions.note: Immediately inland, and home to several of the schools Marina children attend. For a family in a tower, the commute is short in distance and unpredictable in time, which is the usual reason a four o'clock session start fails twice and then gets moved.

regions.note: Low-rise apartment communities a few minutes along Sheikh Zayed Road, sharing the same school cluster. Households are often longer-established than in the Marina, which shows up as more settled subject choices and fewer mid-course school changes.

schoolClusters.note: Students at these schools are supported by IB Gram tutors. They are named as context about the cluster a Marina family chooses within, not as any relationship. The schedule is the product as much as the teaching is.

sections.heading: What a Marina parent is usually actually asking
paragraphs: Three requests arrive from Dubai Marina households in roughly equal numbers, and they look identical in a first message. The first is a subject that is genuinely behind, where a topic was not understood and the student has fallen further each term. The second is a coursework component with a school deadline approaching and nothing on paper. The third is a strong student whose grades are good and whose parents suspect, correctly, that nobody is supervising the independent half of the course.

These three need different purchases. The first needs weekly teaching in that subject. The second needs a term of structured supervision built around the school's own deadline. The third needs a planning session and a schedule, and frequently no ongoing tutoring at all. A provider that sells weekly hours to all three is serving its own revenue, and the third case is where that does most damage: a capable student loses an evening a week to a lesson they do not need while the Extended Essay goes on sitting untouched.

The way to tell them apart in one conversation is to ask what has actually been assessed and when the next fixed date is. A student with falling internal grades across a term in one subject is case one. A student with a supervisor meeting next month and no research question is case two. A student with solid grades, an unclear idea of their internal assessment deadlines and an Extended Essay topic chosen but not started is case three, and the first useful thing anybody can hand them is a calendar.

Marina families are also unusually likely to arrive with a recommendation from a neighbour. It is worth asking two questions about it: which school and which syllabus. The Marina draws on at least two distinct school clusters running different programmes and different boards, and a tutor who was excellent for a Pearson 4MA1 candidate in Year 11 may be the wrong match for a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches student at a different school.

sections.heading: The half of the Diploma that nobody teaches in a lesson
paragraphs: A Diploma student carries a set of components that are examined but not taught in the way a syllabus topic is taught. Each subject has an internal assessment produced by the student over weeks. The Extended Essay is an independent research piece with a 4,000-word limit and a supervisor who meets the student a handful of times. The Theory of Knowledge essay has a 1,600-word limit and is written on a prescribed title, alongside an exhibition. Creativity, Activity, Service runs across both years and has to be evidenced.

The weighting is not marginal. Internal assessments contribute a substantial share of each subject grade, and the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge combine to contribute up to three further points on top of the subject total. A student who produces six rushed internal assessments and a late Extended Essay has given away more points than they would lose from a weak paper in a single subject. The components also compete with each other, because they land in overlapping windows set by the school.

The school's internal deadlines are the dates that matter, and they are published in the school's assessment calendar rather than announced. Confirm every Diploma date with your school's coordinator rather than from a third-party page: UAE schools sit the May session, but no IB session or results date in this project has been verified from the IB itself. What is verifiable from the school is when each internal assessment draft is due, and that is the information a plan is built on.

The useful intervention is unglamorous. Put every internal deadline on one page in date order. Work backwards from each to a date for the question, a date for data or reading, and a date for a full version. Then look at where three components collide and move the one with the most flexible deadline. That exercise takes an hour, and it prevents the specific failure that costs Marina students points: three deadlines in the same fortnight, all addressed at once, all rushed.
