sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks go missing between Year 10 and the final paper
paragraphs: At IGCSE the unsupervised gap is not coursework. It is the twenty-month interval between learning a topic and being examined on it, during which nothing in the timetable brings it back. A student who understood electricity in Year 10 and meets it in a Year 11 mock has forgotten the parts that were never retrieved, and the mock reads as a collapse in ability. It is nothing of the kind, and treating it as one leads to a term of re-teaching content the student already met.

The second loss is practice volume. A school covers the syllabus and sets past papers in the final months. A student aiming at the top grades needs considerably more marked practice than that, spread across both years, because the recurring question types in a syllabus are learnable and the mark-scheme conventions are not obvious. Showing a line of working that earns method marks when the final answer is wrong is a trained habit, not an instinct.

The third is the tier decision, which is made at entry and caps what is achievable. In the Cambridge model many subjects split into Core and Extended, and Pearson into Foundation and Higher. A student entered for a capped tier cannot reach a grade above the ceiling however well they perform, and the decision sits on the entry form months before the papers. Marina parents should ask the school which tier each subject has been entered at and what grade it caps at, in writing.

What fixes the first two is cheap and dull: spaced retrieval of old topics in a deliberate order, and marked full-length papers under time against the exact syllabus code. What fixes the third is a conversation with the school before entries close. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series put final entries on 27 November 2026, more than two months before an exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027, which is a useful illustration of how early those decisions harden.

sections.heading: What tutoring costs around Dubai Marina, with the rates attributed
paragraphs: Three of the six competitor pages researched for this project publish no price at all, and the two that do quote United States dollars rather than dirhams. The figures below are market rates in dirhams with the publisher named, so a Marina household has a reference point before the first call. They are other providers' numbers, not a price list for this site.

Budget online tutoring, generally delivered by university students, is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits between AED 150 and 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits, which carry the tutor's travel inside the rate, run AED 180 to 350 on Bestimate's Dubai table and AED 200 to 500 from independent home tutors. IB and IGCSE specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named tutors reach AED 650 as published by BartyED.

For a Marina household the variable that moves the number most is specificity rather than ambition. A Standard Level subject for a Year 12 student is widely supplied. Higher Level Chemistry in the final term, Theory of Knowledge essay supervision, or a Pearson code a school uses and few tutors have taught, are thinly supplied and price accordingly. Rates also rise as a session approaches, which argues for buying coursework supervision in the autumn rather than intensive hours in the spring.

Put next to school fees the figures read differently. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year in Dubai, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Monthly tutoring packages visible in the market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, with Bestimate estimating AED 240 to 600 a month for budget weekly sessions and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support.

sections.heading: In-home tutoring in Dubai Marina compared with one-to-one online
paragraphs: Parents search for a home tutor in Dubai Marina because it is the phrase that describes what they want: someone whose whole attention is on their child. That is a reasonable thing to want and it is what one-to-one teaching delivers. The question worth examining is whether the person needs to be in the room, and in a Marina tower the answer is usually no, for reasons that have nothing to do with pedagogy.

The practical arithmetic is the travel. An in-home visit prices the tutor's journey into the hour, and a journey into the Marina at five o'clock is not a short one. The rate reflects it: Bestimate's Dubai table puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online tutor, and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500. The same money buys a more specialised tutor online, or more hours of the same one.

The larger constraint is the pool. An in-home arrangement limits the choice to tutors willing to travel to the Marina at the time your child is free, which for a Higher Level Chemistry specialist in March is close to nobody. Online, the constraint disappears and the match is made on the subject, the level and the syllabus code. For a household whose child needs Theory of Knowledge essay supervision or a specific Pearson code, that difference is the whole decision.

To be explicit about what is on offer here: IB Gram does not provide in-home visits anywhere in the UAE, and home visits are a service offered only in India. Lessons for Marina families run online, one to one, over live video, scheduled around the school run. The honest version of the comparison is in the table below, including the cases where an in-home tutor genuinely is the better answer.

sections.heading: Where the hour comes from in a Marina week
paragraphs: The most common reason a tutoring arrangement fails in this area is not the tutor. It is that nobody worked out, before agreeing a weekly slot, which hour was actually free. A Marina week is dense: a school run that lands between four and five depending on the route and the bus, swimming or football on two or three evenings, siblings on different schedules, and a flat where the quiet room is also where a parent takes calls.

Working out the real availability takes ten minutes and prevents months of friction. Write down, for each weekday, the time the child is actually at a desk with the door shut. For most Marina households that is later than parents assume, often after half past five, and on two evenings it does not exist at all. Then choose one or two of the remaining slots, and protect them. A session at an hour that only works when everything goes right will be cancelled twice and then abandoned.

The second logistical variable is the space itself. Online lessons need a corner the student can occupy for an hour without negotiation, headphones, and a connection that holds. In a two or three bedroom apartment with two children in school, that frequently means a rota rather than a room, and a rota works if it is agreed in advance and fails if it is improvised. Families with two children in the Diploma often stagger sessions on different evenings for exactly this reason.

The third is the calendar beyond the week. Half terms, travel over the long breaks, Ramadan with its shortened school hours and post-iftar study pattern, and school trips all interrupt a weekly arrangement. A plan that assumes thirty-six uninterrupted weeks is a plan that will miss its own deadlines. Building in the interruptions, and treating the week before Ramadan as a deadline for anything that would otherwise sit unfinished, is more useful than adding hours.
bullets: Write down the hour the child is genuinely at a desk, not the hour they are home
In most Marina households the realistic start is later than four o'clock
Agree the study space as a rota in advance when siblings share a quiet room

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the dates that actually bind
paragraphs: Of the competitor pages researched for this project, the word November returned no hits at all: no session named, no registration deadline, no results date. For a Marina family that absence is the reason a coursework plan slips, because the dates that bind a Diploma or IGCSE student are mostly not the ones published in a school newsletter.

For IGCSE the board dates are published and precise. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. The zone belongs to the school, so ask which one it is in.

The published key dates for the Cambridge March 2027 series show how early the real deadlines sit: final entries 27 November 2026, exam period 3 February to 4 March 2027, forecast grades 27 February 2027, results on Direct 13 May and certificates in late June. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes and revises provisional timetables, so work from the live official version.

For the Diploma the binding dates are the school's own. UAE schools sit the May session, but no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, so every Diploma date should come from your school's coordinator or ibo.org. What the school can give you is the internal deadline for each internal assessment, the Extended Essay milestones and the Theory of Knowledge submission dates, which is what a plan is actually built from.

sections.heading: When a weekly session is the wrong purchase
paragraphs: There are several situations in which buying a weekly hour is a worse decision than doing nothing, and a Marina family is more likely than most to be sold one, because the area is well supplied with providers and households here are used to buying services. Naming the cases is more useful than listing benefits.

The first is the capable student with no plan. Grades are fine, the problem is three internal deadlines in one fortnight and an Extended Essay that exists as a topic. What they need is an hour with a calendar, a narrowed research question and a schedule, which is a one-off piece of work. A weekly subject lesson takes the evening in which they could have been doing the thing that is actually behind.

The second is the student with too many sessions already. A Diploma student with four weekly tutors has no discretionary time left, and the independent components are precisely what gets squeezed. Cutting tutoring in the two subjects that are performing well usually raises the total, because it returns the hours to the coursework. That is an uncomfortable recommendation for a provider to make, which is why it is rarely made.

The third is the student whose difficulty is not academic. Sleep, screens, a friendship problem, the aftermath of a family move, or genuine anxiety about the Diploma's workload all present as falling grades, and no amount of subject teaching addresses any of them. A tutor who notices this should say so, and the right next conversation is with the school rather than a purchase. A fourth case is the student whose subject level is wrong, where the answer is a conversation with the coordinator about moving from Higher to Standard Level rather than two years of support propping up the wrong choice.
bullets: A capable student with no schedule needs a plan, not a weekly lesson
Four weekly tutors leaves no time for the components that carry the points
Falling grades sometimes signal sleep, anxiety or upheaval rather than teaching

sections.heading: The line between teaching a coursework component and doing it
paragraphs: Because so much of what a Marina family buys is supervision of independent work, the honesty boundary is not an abstract principle here. It is the day-to-day content of the service, and it is worth writing out so a parent can hold any provider to it.

A tutor can teach the subject content the component rests on. Explain how each published criterion is applied, and show what each band looks like in practice. Test whether a research question is answerable with the data or reading available, before the student commits months to it. Read a draft the student has produced and say where it does not yet meet the criteria. Rehearse an individual oral under time and review the recording. Build a schedule backwards from the school's deadline and hold the student to it.

A tutor cannot supply text for submission, turn a draft into a finished piece, or hand over material presented as the student's own. The work has to be the student's own under IB academic-honesty rules, and a breach puts the student's diploma at risk rather than the provider's reputation. One operator in this market sells completed internal assessments outright at a published price; for a family under deadline pressure in March, that is the most expensive thing available in this market and the risk sits entirely with the child.

Two related rules. Published syllabuses, subject guides, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson, so the correct practice is to reference and link the official source rather than redistribute copies. And on the tutor's own standing: private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tutor work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with those tutoring without one subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted at a family.
bullets: A tutor teaches content, explains criteria and reviews the student's own draft
Nothing is written for submission, at any price or any deadline
Official subject guides and mark schemes are linked to, never redistributed

process.title: Say what is unsupervised, not what is weak
process.description: The most useful first message names the next fixed date: a supervisor meeting, an internal assessment deadline, a mock window. Add the school, the syllabus codes and the last report. That tells us whether this is a teaching job, a supervision job or a scheduling job, and the three cost very different amounts.

process.title: A free trial lesson with a specialist in that subject
process.description: One lesson at no cost with a tutor who teaches that subject at that level, run as a working session rather than a sales call. The tutor teaches something and then reports what they found. If the match is wrong, say so and a different tutor is proposed before any payment.

process.title: Every internal deadline on one page
process.description: Before any weekly rhythm starts, the school's own dates go onto a single sheet in order, with the collisions marked. That one exercise prevents the specific failure this page is about: three components addressed in the same fortnight, all of them rushed, each costing marks that were available.

process.title: Protect one realistic hour, not an optimistic one
process.description: Sessions are set at a time the student is genuinely at a desk after the Marina school run and after sport, with the study space agreed in advance where siblings share a room. A slot that only works on a perfect week is cancelled twice and then quietly dropped.

process.title: Review at the end of the term and cut what is not needed
process.description: At term's end the tutor says plainly what has changed and what has not. Where a subject no longer needs weekly support, it stops, because the hour is worth more to the coursework. Where a different specialist is needed, that is said rather than absorbed into the existing arrangement.

whyPoints.title: The plan is built from your school's dates
whyPoints.description: Internal assessment and Extended Essay deadlines come from your child's school assessment calendar, not from a generic timeline. For a Diploma student those are the dates that bind, and they are earlier than most families expect. The first piece of work is usually getting them onto one page.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery means the specialist is not local
whyPoints.description: A Higher Level Chemistry teacher or a Theory of Knowledge essay supervisor does not have to be willing to drive into the Marina at five o'clock. Lessons run live online over video, so the match is made on subject, level and syllabus code. Home visits are offered only in India, and that is stated plainly rather than implied.

whyPoints.title: Recommendations to buy less, when that is right
whyPoints.description: A capable student with three colliding deadlines needs a schedule, not a weekly hour, and a student with four tutors usually needs fewer. Those recommendations are made here because the alternative is selling hours that crowd out the components carrying the points.

whyPoints.title: Figures carry their source and their currency
whyPoints.description: Every market rate on this page is in dirhams and attributed to the provider that published it. Nothing here is presented as a price list for this site. Where a number could not be verified it is left out: no IB exam date, no inspection rating invented for a school, and no fine amount.

whyPoints.title: The coursework boundary is written down
whyPoints.description: Teaching the content, explaining the criteria, testing a research question and reviewing the student's own draft are what is on offer. Text for submission is not, at any deadline. In a market where completed internal assessments are openly sold, that is a real distinction rather than a disclaimer.

faqs.question: My son's school in Al Sufouh teaches well. Why would he need a tutor at all?
faqs.answer: Frequently he would not, for teaching. The gap in a well-taught Diploma is the independent half: an internal assessment in each of six subjects, an Extended Essay with a 4,000-word limit, a Theory of Knowledge essay limited to 1,600 words and an exhibition, none of which is delivered in a taught period. If his grades are solid and his deadlines are unclear, the useful purchase is a planning session and a schedule rather than weekly lessons. If a specific subject has been slipping across a term, that is a different problem with a different answer.

faqs.question: How early should an Extended Essay actually be started?
faqs.answer: Earlier than the school's first hard deadline suggests, because the real constraint is reading rather than writing. A workable sequence is a subject and a rough area in the first term of DP1, a narrowed research question before the long summer, the bulk of the reading over that summer, and a full version well before the school's deadline rather than in the fortnight preceding it. The 4,000-word limit is not the difficulty; a question too broad to answer in 4,000 words is. Narrowing it early is the cheapest improvement available and costs nothing.

faqs.question: Do you send a home tutor to our apartment in Dubai Marina?
faqs.answer: No. Lessons for Marina families run online, one to one, over live video, and IB Gram does not provide in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. In a tower household this usually works better: no travel priced into the hour, no building access to coordinate, a late slot available when the school run overruns, and a tutor matched on the exact syllabus code rather than on willingness to drive into the Marina at five o'clock on a weekday.

faqs.question: My daughter is in Year 10 and her mock result in a topic she understood last year was poor. What happened?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly forgetting rather than misunderstanding. A topic learned once and never retrieved decays, and nothing in an IGCSE timetable returns Year 10 material to a student before the Year 11 mock. The mock then reads as a collapse in ability when it is a spacing problem. The fix is spaced retrieval in a deliberate order rather than re-teaching the topic from the start, plus marked past papers for the exact syllabus code. Re-teaching content she already met is the expensive version of this, and it is the usual response.

faqs.question: Which tier has her school entered her for, and does it matter?
faqs.answer: It matters a great deal and the school is the only place to find out. In the Cambridge model many subjects split into Core and Extended, and Pearson into Foundation and Higher, with the lower tier capping the grade available regardless of performance. The decision sits on the entry form, which closes months before the papers: Cambridge's final entries for the March 2027 series were due 27 November 2026 against an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027. Ask the school in writing which tier each subject has been entered at and what grade it caps at.

faqs.question: How much do IB and IGCSE tutors in Dubai Marina charge?
faqs.answer: Market rates in dirhams run from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tutors, with EdFlik listing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52; AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; AED 180 to 500 for in-home visits including travel; and AED 200 to 450 and above for IB and IGCSE specialists, with TutorChase at AED 270 and premium named tutors at AED 650 as published by BartyED. Those are other providers' published figures, quoted so you have a reference before the first call.

faqs.question: Can one tutor supervise two internal assessments in different subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends on how close the subjects are. The criteria differ by subject and so does the subject knowledge required to test whether a research question is viable, so a single tutor covering a science and a humanity is unlikely to be strong at both. Closely related pairs, such as two sciences at Standard Level or mathematics and physics, are more realistic. The scheduling part, getting every deadline onto one page and working backwards from each, can be done once for all six components by whoever does it first.

faqs.question: Our flat is small and both children study at the kitchen table. Does online tutoring work in that?
faqs.answer: It works if the space is agreed as a rota rather than improvised. The requirement is a corner the student can occupy for an hour without negotiation, headphones and a connection that holds. Households with two children in school commonly stagger sessions onto different evenings for this reason, which has the side benefit of spreading the cost across the week. What does not work is a session booked at an hour when the room is contested, because it gets cancelled twice and then dropped.

faqs.question: What is the Theory of Knowledge exhibition and does it need support?
faqs.answer: It asks the student to link three objects to a prescribed prompt and explain how each one shows knowledge in practice, and it is assessed alongside the 1,600-word essay. Most of the available mark is decided by object selection, which students rush because the component feels minor. One or two sessions on choosing objects that genuinely illustrate the prompt, and on writing commentary that analyses rather than describes, usually covers it. Beyond that, time is better spent on the subjects carrying the bulk of the points.

faqs.question: A neighbour recommended a tutor who was excellent for her son. Why might that not transfer?
faqs.answer: Because the Marina draws on more than one school cluster, running different programmes and different boards. A tutor who was excellent for a Pearson 4MA1 candidate in Year 11 may be a poor match for a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches student at a different school, and a strong IGCSE science tutor is not automatically a Diploma internal assessment supervisor. The two questions worth asking about any recommendation are which school and which syllabus code, since those determine whether the experience is relevant.

faqs.question: Can sessions move later during Ramadan and through the long summer?
faqs.answer: Yes, and both are worth planning rather than improvising. During Ramadan school hours shorten and the productive study window for most teenagers moves after iftar, so sessions shift later and are often better shorter and more frequent. The week before Ramadan is worth treating as a deadline for anything that would otherwise sit unfinished through it. The long summer between the Diploma years is the single most valuable block available, and it is when the Extended Essay reading and the Higher Level set texts should be done.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a Diploma student actually need?
faqs.answer: For most Marina students, one or two in the single subject genuinely behind, plus bounded supervision on whichever coursework component is closest to its deadline. Four weekly tutors is almost always too many, because it removes the discretionary time the independent components require and those are where the points leak. The honest test is whether the hours are displacing the internal assessments or supporting them. Where they are displacing them, cutting two subjects usually raises the total.

faqs.question: What can a tutor legitimately do with my child's internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Teach the content it rests on, explain how each published criterion is applied and what each band looks like, test whether the research question can be answered with the available data, read a draft the student has written and say where it falls short, and build a schedule backwards from the school's deadline. What a tutor cannot do is supply text for submission or rework a draft into a finished piece. The work has to be the student's own, and a breach of IB academic-honesty rules puts the diploma at risk rather than the provider.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor start for a subject in the final term?
faqs.answer: Usually within a few days for mainstream subjects at Standard Level or IGCSE. Higher Level specialists in the term before a session are thinly supplied across the whole market, because that is when every family wants one, and where no suitable specialist is free that is said rather than filled with whoever is available. The sequence is a short conversation about dates and syllabus codes, a free trial lesson with a subject specialist, then a protected weekly slot. Nothing is charged before the trial has happened.

faqs.question: Do you cover both Cambridge and Pearson for the same subject?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the distinction matters more than families expect. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 are different examinations with different paper structures, different tiering and different mark-scheme conventions, and the same is true across the sciences with 0625 against 4PH1. Past-paper work has to use the exact code the school enters, because practising the wrong one trains the wrong habits. The first question we ask is which code appears on your child's entry, not which subject they take.

faqs.question: My son is strong but says he has no time. Is that a scheduling problem or an excuse?
faqs.answer: Usually a scheduling problem, and it is testable. Write down for each weekday the hour he is genuinely at a desk with the door shut, rather than the hour he is home. In most Marina households that is later than parents assume and on two evenings it does not exist. If the honest total is six or seven hours a week against six internal assessments and an Extended Essay, the constraint is real and the answer is to cut something rather than add a tutor. That conversation is more useful than a lesson.

dubai/dubai-marina.closingHeading: Start with the deadlines, then decide what to buy
dubai/dubai-marina.closingBody: Around Dubai Marina the teaching is rarely the problem. The problem is the half of the course nobody supervises: six internal assessments, an Extended Essay with a 4,000-word limit, a Theory of Knowledge essay limited to 1,600 words, and two years of IGCSE content that no timetable returns to a student before the mock. Send the school, the syllabus codes and the next fixed date, take a free trial lesson with a specialist in whichever subject worries you most, and ask for every deadline on one page. Lessons run online, one to one, timed to your school run. If the answer is a schedule rather than a tutor, that is what you will be told.

dubai/dubai-media-city.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are asked for by Media City and Al Sufouh families for one reason: a student who understands the lesson and still loses marks. That is a technique and independent-study problem, and it responds to past-paper work with the mark scheme visible rather than to the content being explained again.

intro.heading: The lesson is not the problem. The twenty hours after it are
paragraphs: Dubai Media City sits in the Al Sufouh corridor between Internet City, Knowledge Park and Al Barsha, and the households attached to it send children to some of the longest-established schools in the emirate. Parents here very rarely open a conversation by criticising the school, and they are usually right not to. The complaint is more precise and more interesting: my child follows the lesson, does the homework, and still comes out of the paper two grades below where the classwork suggested.

That gap has a structural cause rather than a teaching one. A secondary class delivers the syllabus once, at the pace of the group. Everything that converts delivery into marks happens afterwards and alone: consolidating a topic into something retrievable six months later, practising unseen questions under timing, learning what each command term actually demands, reading a mark scheme to see where the marks sit, and building an internal assessment from a blank page. None of that is class time, and almost none of it is explicitly taught.

A Diploma student carries six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. An IGCSE student in Year 11 carries eight or nine subjects with coursework in several. The independent work attached to that is not a modest supplement to school; for a Higher Level science or mathematics subject it is the larger part of the grade. Most students arrive at Year 11 or Diploma Year 1 with no system for any of it, because no previous stage required one.

The results of that show up in a recognisable pattern. Classwork is fine. Homework is submitted. The mock paper comes back with marks lost on questions the student can genuinely answer, because they described where the paper said evaluate, or spent eighteen minutes on a six-mark question, or had never seen the mark scheme for the style of question that opens Paper 2. Those are fixable in weeks, and they are fixable without covering a single new piece of content.

This page sets out what class time covers and what it leaves behind, how internal assessment criteria actually allocate marks, what the command terms demand, where the big subjects leak marks, and what the Dubai market charges for one-to-one against group formats. Lessons are delivered online over live video, one to one, which also means a Media City household does not add a car journey to an evening that is already full of independent work. Every AED figure quoted here is a market rate attributed to the provider that published it in October 2026, and every rule about assessment is stated as the board or the regulator states it. Where something could not be checked against a primary source, it has been left off the page rather than estimated, which is why no IB session or results date appears anywhere below.
bullets: A class delivers the syllabus once; retrieval, timing and technique happen alone
Internal assessment carries roughly a fifth to a quarter of most Diploma subject grades
Most marks lost by capable students are technique losses, not knowledge gaps
Command terms are published instruction lists, and most students have never read theirs
Market rate for a qualified online subject tutor in Dubai: AED 150-300 per hour

dubai/dubai-media-city.programmesIntro: Each programme loads independent work differently, and the shape of that load is what decides whether a student needs support and what kind. The notes below describe each one by what it expects a student to do without supervision.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. The independent load is unusually heavy and unusually varied: an internal assessment in each subject, a 4,000-word research project, a Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition, and cumulative revision across two years of content. Managing it is a scheduling skill the Diploma assumes rather than teaches.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students at the Al Sufouh and Al Barsha schools sit the May session. The dates that bind hardest are the school's own internal deadlines for each internal assessment and the Extended Essay, which your IB coordinator holds. No IB session or results date appears on this page, because the IB's own site could not be confirmed directly for this project.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8, converted to a 1-7 grade. The independent demand here is mostly project management across several concurrent criterion tasks, culminating in the Personal Project in MYP 5. What the MYP does not require is cumulative revision for a terminal examination, which is precisely why the move to Diploma Year 1 catches so many students out.
programmes.countryNote: In this part of Dubai a large share of MYP students stay in the same school for the Diploma, so the habits formed in MYP 4 and 5 travel directly into Diploma Year 1. Building a retrieval routine during MYP 5 is far cheaper than repairing its absence in the first Diploma report.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Eight or nine subjects sat as terminal examinations, with coursework in several and tiering in some Cambridge subjects. The independent load is dominated by past papers, and the quality of that practice varies enormously. A student working through papers and checking final answers is doing something quite different from a student working through papers with the mark scheme open beside them.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel are separate qualifications with different codes and paper structures, and Dubai schools use both. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct zone timetable, so revision schedules should be built from the school's own version rather than a timetable found online.

dubai/dubai-media-city.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects where the independent-study gap costs the most marks, with the specific technique failure that produces the loss rather than a description of the content.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level Paper 3 asks for sustained reasoning through one extended problem, which cannot be prepared by repeating routine exercises. Students who do every question in the textbook and no unseen problems plateau. The independent work that pays is unfamiliar questions attempted without hints, then marked honestly.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Marks leak in uncertainty treatment and in questions requiring a derivation rather than a formula. The scientific investigation is marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, so a well-executed experiment with a weak design is capped before the data is even considered.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Higher Level extensions assume the Standard Level material is automatic. Students who revise topics in isolation cannot answer the questions that join energetics to equilibrium or organic mechanisms to spectroscopy. Interleaved practice, not topic-by-topic revision, is what moves this subject.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The highest-volume Diploma science and the one most damaged by rereading notes. Retrieval practice from blank paper is the method that works, and almost nobody does it unprompted. The second leak is command terms: outline answered as describe, explain answered as a list.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries a large share of the marks and is quick to fix. The commentary portfolio is slower: each commentary must be anchored to a genuine published article within a word limit, and students routinely choose articles that cannot support the analysis required.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen analysis under time pressure. Strong readers lose marks writing about content instead of construction, and the individual oral needs a global issue traced through two texts with a rehearsed structure. Both respond to timed practice against the published criteria.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: Extended candidates lose marks on method and on questions spanning two topics at once. The common independent-study error is practising the topics that feel comfortable. Working from a list of the specific question types most recently got wrong is a different and much faster activity.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics and Chemistry
subjects.description: Electricity and moles produce most of the enquiries. Both are concentrated in a small number of recurring question types, which makes them ideal targets for independent work provided the student is practising against mark schemes rather than answer keys.

subjects.name: IGCSE English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and the analysis question carry the risk. The independent work that helps is writing to time against the published criteria and then being shown where the marks were not awarded, which is not the same as being told the writing was good.

dubai/dubai-media-city.regionsTitle: Media City and the Al Sufouh corridor
dubai/dubai-media-city.regionsIntro: The households tied to Media City are spread across the free-zone corridor and the communities either side of it. These are the areas that matter, and what each one contributes to the school and study week.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: The district Media City sits inside, and home to several long-established secondary schools. Students here often walk or take a short ride to school, which means the evening is genuinely available for independent work rather than consumed by a commute.

regions.name: Dubai Internet City
regions.note: Immediately adjacent along Sheikh Zayed Road, sharing the same metro stations and the same working-parent profile. Households in both free zones ask for the same kind of support, which is technique rather than content.

regions.name: Dubai Knowledge Park
regions.note: The education free zone next door, holding university branch campuses. Older Diploma students here sometimes have a clearer sight of university entry requirements than their school's careers timetable provides.

regions.name: Barsha Heights
regions.note: Inland across Sheikh Zayed Road, with a dense apartment population and a short drive to the Al Barsha schools. Evening slots from here work reliably because the school run is short in both directions.

regions.name: The Greens and The Views
regions.note: Low-rise apartment communities a few minutes inland, feeding the same school cluster. These households tend to have older children in Years 10 to 13, which is exactly where the independent-study load bites.

regions.name: Al Barsha
regions.note: Where a large share of the corridor's children are actually enrolled, across British, American and IB schools within minutes of each other. A ten-minute school run leaves more study time than most Dubai districts manage.

regions.name: Jumeirah Beach Residence and Dubai Marina
regions.note: West along the coast, sharing the school cluster and the free-zone employers. The commute is longer, which compresses the available weekday study window by about half an hour each way.

regions.name: Palm Jumeirah
regions.note: Across the trunk road, with its own access constraints. Families here use the same Al Sufouh and Al Barsha schools and face the same independent-study problem with less margin in the evening.

schoolClusters.city: Al Sufouh and Media City corridor
schoolClusters.note: The schools closest to the free zones, including selective British secondaries and IB continuum campuses. The short school run is the practical advantage of this corridor, and it is why the independent-study question dominates here rather than the logistics question.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South
schoolClusters.note: The main cluster for the corridor, spanning British, American and IB curricula within a few minutes of each other. Siblings at different schools on different systems is common, and so is a household running two revision regimes at once.

dubai/dubai-media-city.schoolDisclaimer: These schools are named to describe the Media City corridor's school options; IB Gram has no affiliation with, endorsement from or commercial relationship with any of them.
dubai/dubai-media-city.modesIntro: Three formats address the independent-study gap, and all three run over live video. The format matters less than the activity: what distinguishes useful sessions here is working against mark schemes rather than re-explaining content the student already followed in class.

modes.title: Weekly technique session
modes.description: A fixed slot built around unseen questions rather than topic coverage. The student attempts questions cold, the tutor marks them against the published mark scheme in front of them, and the session is spent on the gap between the answer given and the marks available. Over a term this changes how a student reads a question, which is the thing that moves the grade.
bullets: Questions attempted cold, then marked against the published scheme
Command terms taught as instructions, with the student's own errors as examples
Timing practised deliberately, with a mark-per-minute budget
Written list after each session of the specific question types still failing

modes.title: Independent-study coaching block
modes.description: A short run of sessions whose subject is the student's study system rather than a syllabus. Retrieval practice from blank paper, interleaving across topics, spacing across weeks, and a realistic weekly schedule across six Diploma subjects. It suits a capable student whose classwork is fine and whose results are not.
bullets: Builds a retrieval routine the student can run without supervision
Replaces rereading notes with practice that produces the content from memory
Interleaves topics so cross-topic questions stop being a surprise
Sets a weekly schedule across all subjects, not just the weak one

modes.title: Internal assessment and Extended Essay supervision
modes.description: Structured sessions on the student's own coursework, built around the published criteria. The tutor teaches what each criterion rewards, interrogates the research question until it can produce usable data, and gives feedback on drafts the student has written. The text remains the student's own from first word to last, as IB academic honesty requires.
bullets: Criteria explained letter by letter against the current subject guide
Research question narrowed until the data collection is actually feasible
Feedback on the student's own draft, in writing, against each criterion
No supply of submittable text, model answers or ghost material

sections.heading: What class time covers, and what it leaves to the student
paragraphs: It is worth laying this out explicitly, because the assumption that school covers the syllabus and tutoring covers the rest is too vague to act on. A secondary class delivers content, models worked examples, sets and marks homework, and runs internal assessments. That is a substantial amount of work and the schools in this corridor generally do it well. What a class of twenty-four cannot do is give each student individual feedback on timed unseen questions every week, which is where the marks are won.

The table below separates the two columns. The pattern that emerges is consistent: anything that requires one-to-one diagnosis of a specific student's error, or repeated practice with individual feedback, sits in the independent column. That is not a criticism of the school. It is arithmetic. Twenty-four students producing one piece of timed work a week generates more marking than any teacher's timetable contains.

The consequence column is the one parents recognise. A student can be fully engaged in lessons and still be losing a quarter of the available marks on things nobody has diagnosed for them: a command term consistently misread, a question type never practised, a mark scheme never seen. Those losses are stable across papers, which is why they show up as a persistent gap between classwork and results rather than as an erratic one.

What this means for choosing a tutor in Al Sufouh or Al Barsha is specific. A tutor who re-explains the lesson is working in the school's column and duplicating something that already happened. A tutor who puts an unseen paper in front of the student, marks it against the scheme while they watch, and names the three recurring errors is working in the column the school cannot reach. Ask which of those a prospective tutor intends to do.

sections.heading: The independent-study load nobody budgets for
paragraphs: Add it up honestly for a Diploma student. Six subjects each needing weekly consolidation. Three of them at Higher Level with roughly double the content. An internal assessment in each, several of them requiring data collection. A 4,000-word Extended Essay. A Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition. Creativity, Activity, Service commitments with their own reflections and deadlines. None of that is optional and almost none of it is timetabled.

Students handle this in one of three ways. A minority arrive with a working system, usually built during MYP 5 or Year 11, and they cope. A larger group works hard without a system, which produces long hours with poor returns: rereading notes, highlighting, redoing questions they can already do. A third group simply defers, and the deferral compounds, because the Diploma's internal deadlines are spread deliberately to prevent a final-term rescue.

The second group is the one worth intervening with, because the input is already there. A student spending two hours an evening on ineffective methods does not need more hours; they need the hours redirected. Retrieval from blank paper instead of rereading. Interleaved topics instead of blocks. Unseen questions instead of familiar ones. Spacing across weeks instead of cramming before a test. These are unglamorous changes and they produce visible movement within a term.

For an IGCSE student in Year 11 the arithmetic is different but the principle is the same. Eight or nine subjects, terminal papers, coursework in several. The temptation is to revise by subject in sequence, finishing one before starting the next, which guarantees that the first subject revised is the weakest by June. A schedule that touches every subject every fortnight feels less satisfying and works considerably better.

sections.heading: Internal assessment criteria: the part that is never taught twice
paragraphs: Internal assessment carries roughly a fifth to a quarter of the grade in most Diploma subjects. It is introduced once, usually in a lesson or two, and then the student is expected to produce it largely alone over several months. Among capable students it is the single most common place to lose marks that were fully available, and the reason is almost always the same: the student wrote the piece and then read the criteria, rather than the other way round.

The criteria are published, specific and marked letter by letter. The mathematical exploration is assessed on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. The science investigation is assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. A technically competent piece of mathematics with no genuine reflection has forfeited a defined share of the marks, and more mathematics does not recover them. Confirm the exact criteria and allocations against the current subject guide through your school's coordinator, because guides are revised.

The table below sets out where students tend to stop and what a tutor can legitimately do about it. The column that matters is the last one, because it is also the honesty boundary. Teaching what a criterion rewards and giving feedback on a student's own draft is support. Producing the text is malpractice, and the research for this project found a provider in this market selling finished internal assessments at AED 3,750.

The practical sequence that works is short. Read the criteria before choosing the topic. Choose a research question narrow enough that the data can actually be collected in the time available. Write a first draft early and badly. Get it diagnosed against each criterion. Redraft. Students who follow that sequence rarely need rescuing in the final fortnight, which is when most of the enquiries from this corridor actually arrive.

sections.heading: Command terms: the published instruction list most students never read
paragraphs: Every examination board publishes a list of command terms with defined demands. These are instructions, not stylistic preferences, and the mark scheme is built on them. A student who writes a thorough description when the paper says evaluate has usually demonstrated the knowledge and scored in the lowest band available. This is the cheapest mark recovery in the whole of secondary education, and it is routinely left undone because it looks too simple to be the problem.

The reason it persists is that nobody owns it. The subject teacher assumes it was covered elsewhere, the student assumes the words mean what they mean in ordinary English, and the parent cannot see the error because the answer reads perfectly well. It only becomes visible when somebody sits with the paper, the mark scheme and the student and shows that two marks were available for a judgement the student never made.

The table below covers the terms that cause the most damage. The useful exercise is not memorising it but applying it to the student's own marked work: find three answers where the command term was not honoured, and the pattern becomes obvious to the student within one session. After that, the correction is largely self-sustaining, which is why this work has such a good return per hour.

There is a related habit worth building at the same time. Before writing, a student should note the command term and the mark allocation, then decide how many distinct points the answer needs. A six-mark question in most schemes wants six creditable statements, not one long paragraph. Students in strong schools often write too much and too generally; the paper rewards specificity against the instruction given.

sections.heading: Where the big subjects actually leak marks
paragraphs: In mathematics at Higher Level the leak is unfamiliarity rather than inability. A student who works through every textbook exercise becomes fluent in question types they have already seen, which is not what Paper 3 tests. The independent work that pays is unseen problems attempted cold, with no hint and no worked example, followed by honest marking. Most students avoid this because it feels like failure, and avoiding it is precisely what keeps them at a 5.

In the sciences the leak splits in two. The first is cross-topic questions: energetics joined to equilibrium, fields joined to circuits, respiration joined to enzymes. Revision done topic by topic produces students who can answer within a topic and stall across two. Interleaving fixes it and nothing else does. The second is uncertainty and data handling, which carries real marks in both the papers and the investigation and is almost never practised deliberately.

In the essay subjects the leak is structure under time. A student with good ideas and no plan writes a first paragraph of three hundred words and runs out of time, and the mark scheme rewards the argument they never reached. Planning to a template for two minutes before writing recovers more marks than another month of reading. In English the parallel problem is writing about content rather than construction, which timed practice against the criteria exposes quickly.

Across all of them, the diagnosis has to come from the student's own marked work rather than from a general description of common errors. Two students at the same school with the same grade in the same subject usually lose their marks in different places. The first session of useful tutoring is therefore spent reading a marked paper, not delivering a topic, and any tutor who does not ask for one before starting is guessing.

sections.heading: What one-to-one costs against a group class in this corridor
paragraphs: Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and Barsha Heights have a reasonable supply of tuition centres as well as individual tutors, so families here genuinely have a format choice rather than a single option. The table below compares the formats on what each can and cannot fix. The AED figures are Dubai market rates gathered in October 2026 and attributed to the provider that published them; none is an IB Gram price.

The bands themselves: a budget online tutor, generally a university student, runs AED 45-150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150-300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An IB or IGCSE specialist runs AED 200-450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Premium named tutors reach AED 500-650, with BartyED publishing AED 650. A published monthly online package of AED 799 for eight sessions works out at roughly AED 100 an hour.

The distinction that matters for an independent-study problem is whether the format can diagnose one student's specific errors. A group class can deliver content efficiently and cheaply, and for a student who genuinely missed a topic that is good value. It cannot look at this student's marked paper and name the three recurring technique failures, because the other seven students in the room have different ones. For a technique problem, a group class is the wrong instrument at any price.

The reverse is also true and worth saying. A student who simply has not covered a topic does not need a specialist at AED 300 an hour to be taught it. Matching the format to the actual problem is how a family in this corridor spends sensibly: group or budget support for content gaps, specialist one-to-one for technique and internal assessment work, and nothing at all for the parts the student can genuinely self-manage.

sections.heading: Exam technique treated as a subject of its own
paragraphs: Most schools teach exam technique incidentally, inside subject lessons, which is reasonable and insufficient. Treated deliberately, it is a small and teachable body of skills: reading a question for its command term and mark allocation, budgeting time per mark, deciding question order, knowing when to abandon a question and return, and writing in the form the mark scheme rewards. A student can be taught all of it in a handful of sessions.

The time budget is the part students find most surprising. In a paper of a hundred marks over two hours, a mark is worth just over a minute, and a six-mark question that takes eighteen minutes has cost twelve minutes of marks elsewhere. Students almost never time individual questions in practice, so they discover this in the mock, where it costs them. Practising with a watch on the desk feels artificial and is the fastest available improvement.

Question order is the second quick win. Nothing requires a paper to be answered front to back, and for many students starting with the question type they are strongest at builds enough momentum to attempt the harder ones properly. The counterpart is the discipline to leave a stuck question after a set time, which has to be rehearsed, because in the room every student's instinct is to keep pushing at the thing that is not working.

The last piece is the post-mortem. A mock paper is the single most valuable document a student produces each year and most of them never look at it again. Working through a marked mock question by question, categorising each lost mark as knowledge, technique or timing, gives a precise list for the term ahead. Families in this corridor who do that one exercise in January are consistently in a better position by April than those who respond to the mock result by booking more hours.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and what help with my IA should mean
paragraphs: The independent nature of internal assessment work is exactly what makes this market risky. A student alone with a 4,000-word Extended Essay and a deadline in three weeks is the customer those pages are built for, and the research for this project found one selling finished internal assessments at AED 3,750. Buying one is academic malpractice under IB rules. The investigation lands on the candidate, the consequence reaches the whole Diploma, and the seller carries none of it.

The legitimate boundary is specific enough to check against. A tutor may teach what each criterion rewards and the marks it carries, question a research question until it can generate usable data, explain how data and uncertainty should be handled, teach the structure of a reflection, and read a draft the student has produced to say where it falls short. A tutor may not supply text for submission, rewrite a passage into its final form, or hand over a model answer intended to be submitted.

There is a test a parent can apply without knowing the subject. Ask what the student will have written by the end of the engagement, and who will have written it. A provider whose answer is that your child will produce every word, with feedback, is describing teaching. A provider who is vague about authorship, or who offers a finished document, is describing something that puts your child at risk while charging them for it.

The same boundary covers Theory of Knowledge, the MYP Personal Project and IGCSE coursework. It is worth stating to the student as well as the parent, because the pressure to cross it usually arrives at eleven at night two days before a deadline, when nobody is asking a tutor's advice. A student who understands that the criteria are the route to the marks has somewhere to go at that hour that is not a purchase.

process.title: Send a marked paper, not a description
process.description: The first thing we ask for is the most recent marked mock or unit test. Two students with the same grade in the same subject at the same school usually lose their marks in different places, and only the paper shows where. A description of the problem from a parent or a student is a starting point, not a diagnosis.

process.title: Get the losses categorised
process.description: Every lost mark on that paper is classified as knowledge, technique or timing. The proportions decide the plan. A student losing most marks to technique does not need content re-taught, and a student losing most marks to timing needs a watch on the desk more than another explanation.

process.title: Trial the tutor on an unseen question
process.description: The trial session is spent on a question the student has not seen, marked against the published scheme while they watch. That shows you what the tutor actually does in a session, which is more informative than a conversation about experience and subject knowledge.

process.title: Fix the slot and the question-type list
process.description: Before weekly sessions start we agree the named question types being targeted and the assessment date they are aimed at. The list is short on purpose. Three recurring errors closed properly is worth more than nine topics revisited lightly.

process.title: Review at the next marked assessment
process.description: Progress is judged against the next marked mock or test, not against a feeling after four weeks. If the targeted question types have not moved, the plan changes or the tutor does. A list that was written down at the start is what makes that judgement possible.

whyPoints.title: We work in the column the school cannot reach
whyPoints.description: A class of twenty-four cannot give every student individual feedback on timed unseen work each week. That is arithmetic, not criticism. One-to-one sessions spent marking a student's own attempts against the published scheme are doing the thing class time structurally cannot.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis comes from your child's own paper
whyPoints.description: The first session reads a marked mock and categorises every lost mark as knowledge, technique or timing. General lists of common errors are useless for an individual student, because two students with the same grade lose marks in different places.

whyPoints.title: Command terms and mark schemes get taught explicitly
whyPoints.description: The published instruction lists are where capable students in strong schools lose the most recoverable marks. Teaching them against the student's own wrong answers makes the correction self-sustaining within a few sessions.

whyPoints.title: Study method is treated as teachable
whyPoints.description: Retrieval from blank paper, interleaving and spacing are specific techniques, not advice. A student already working two hours an evening does not need more hours; they need those hours redirected, and that is a short piece of coaching.

whyPoints.title: The coursework boundary is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: We teach criteria, question research designs and give written feedback on the student's own draft. We do not supply submittable text. One provider in this market sells finished internal assessments; the risk from that transaction falls entirely on your child.

whyPoints.title: We will tell you when tutoring is the wrong purchase
whyPoints.description: A student who has simply missed a topic may be better served by a group class at a fraction of the cost, and a student who can self-manage may need nothing. Matching the format to the real problem is the part most providers have no incentive to do.

faqs.question: My child understands the lessons in Media City but underperforms in exams. Why?
faqs.answer: Because understanding a lesson and earning marks are different skills, and the second one is mostly built outside class. A class delivers content once at the pace of the group; converting it into marks requires retrieval from memory, unseen questions under timing, reading mark schemes and honouring command terms. None of that is class time. The losses are usually stable across papers, which is why the gap between classwork and results persists rather than fluctuating. Start by categorising every lost mark on the last marked paper as knowledge, technique or timing.

faqs.question: Is a tutor in Al Sufouh supposed to re-teach the lesson?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and a tutor who does is duplicating work the school already did well. The useful activity is different: put an unseen question in front of the student, let them attempt it cold, then mark it against the published scheme while they watch and name the recurring error. That is one-to-one diagnosis, which a class of twenty-four structurally cannot provide. Ask any prospective tutor which of the two they intend to do, because the answer predicts whether the sessions will move a grade.

faqs.question: What are command terms and why do they cost my child marks?
faqs.answer: They are the published instruction words in every exam question, and the mark scheme is built on them. State, outline, describe, explain, discuss, evaluate, justify and deduce all demand different things. A student who writes a thorough description where the paper said evaluate has shown the knowledge and scored in the lowest band. Nobody owns teaching this: the teacher assumes it was covered elsewhere and the student assumes the words mean what they mean in ordinary English. Applying the list to three of your child's own wrong answers fixes it quickly.

faqs.question: How much independent work does an IB Diploma student in Dubai actually have?
faqs.answer: More than the timetable suggests. Six subjects needing weekly consolidation, three of them at Higher Level with roughly double the content, an internal assessment in each, a 4,000-word Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition, and Creativity, Activity, Service commitments with their own reflections. Almost none of it is timetabled, and the internal deadlines are spread deliberately so a final-term rescue is not possible. Managing that load is a scheduling skill the Diploma assumes rather than teaches.

faqs.question: My child revises for hours with no result. What should change?
faqs.answer: The method rather than the hours. Rereading notes, highlighting and redoing questions already mastered feel productive and produce little. The replacements are specific: retrieval practice from blank paper, interleaving topics so cross-topic questions stop being a surprise, spacing across weeks rather than cramming before a test, and unseen questions attempted without a worked example. A student already spending two hours an evening does not need more hours, and redirecting those hours usually shows movement within a term.

faqs.question: Which schools do Dubai Media City families mostly use?
faqs.answer: The corridor's children are spread across Al Sufouh and Al Barsha. Nearby options include Dubai College, GEMS Wellington International School, Regent International School and Dubai British School Jumeirah Park, with the larger Al Barsha cluster covering American School of Dubai, Dubai American Academy, Kings' School Al Barsha, Nord Anglia International School Dubai and Horizon International School. The school run here is short by Dubai standards, which is why the independent-study question dominates. Those schools are context only; IB Gram holds no relationship with any of them.

faqs.question: What exactly is marked in an IB internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Published criteria, letter by letter, and they vary by subject. The mathematical exploration is assessed on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. The science investigation is assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. A technically strong piece with no genuine reflection has forfeited a defined share of the marks, and adding more subject content does not recover them. Confirm the current criteria and allocations with your school's IB coordinator, because subject guides are revised periodically.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's Extended Essay without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary is checkable. A tutor may narrow a research question until it is answerable within the word limit, teach the method and the reflection process, explain what each criterion rewards, and give written feedback on a draft the student has produced. A tutor may not supply text for submission or hand over a model answer. A simple parent test: ask who will have written every word by the end of the engagement. Vagueness about authorship is the warning sign.

faqs.question: Is a group class in Al Barsha better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: For a content gap, often yes. A published monthly package of AED 799 for eight sessions works out at roughly AED 100 an hour, and if your child genuinely missed a topic, having it delivered again in a group is efficient. For a technique problem it is the wrong instrument at any price, because a group cannot diagnose this student's recurring errors while seven others in the room have different ones. Match the format to the actual problem rather than to the headline rate.

faqs.question: How should my child use a marked mock paper?
faqs.answer: As the most valuable document they produce all year, which most students never open again. Work through it question by question and classify every lost mark as knowledge, technique or timing. The proportions dictate the term's plan: a technique-heavy loss pattern means mark schemes and command terms, a timing-heavy one means a watch on the desk. Families who do this exercise in January are consistently better placed by April than those who respond to a mock result by simply booking more hours.

faqs.question: How do I budget exam time per question?
faqs.answer: Start from marks per minute. In a hundred-mark paper over two hours, a mark is worth a little over a minute, so a six-mark question that takes eighteen minutes has cost twelve minutes of marks elsewhere. Students almost never time individual questions in practice and therefore discover this in the mock. Practising with a watch on the desk, deciding question order deliberately, and rehearsing the discipline of leaving a stuck question after a set time are the fastest available improvements.

faqs.question: Does Cambridge or Pearson set the timetable my child should revise against?
faqs.answer: The board does, and the school's own version is the one to use. Cambridge International runs June and November series with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, stating it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so the live official PDF rather than a copy is what to plan against.

faqs.question: Do tutors supporting Media City students need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Individuals giving private lessons in the UAE do. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years, with a two-working-day completion time stated on MoHRE's service page. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Can lessons run over live video for a subject with practical work?
faqs.answer: Yes, with one honest limitation. The practical skills assessed in IGCSE and Diploma sciences are mostly assessed through written questions and through the investigation report rather than through observed laboratory performance, and both are taught well over video with shared data sets and screen annotation. What video cannot replicate is handling the apparatus itself, which is the school's job and happens in school. Design, data analysis, uncertainty treatment and evaluation are where the marks sit, and those transfer completely.

faqs.question: When is it right to stop tutoring?
faqs.answer: When the targeted question types have stopped failing and the student has a study system they run without supervision. That is a real end point and it should be named at the start. Open-ended weekly support with no list attached can continue for years while nobody establishes whether it is working, because nothing was defined as the thing it should fix. If the list is closed and the marks have moved, fewer sessions is the honest recommendation.

dubai/dubai-media-city.closingHeading: Start with the marked paper, not the timetable
dubai/dubai-media-city.closingBody: If your child is following lessons in Al Sufouh or Al Barsha and still coming out of papers below the classwork, the next useful step is not more hours. It is reading the last marked mock and sorting every lost mark into knowledge, technique or timing. Send us that paper with the school, the year group and the board, and you will get the categorised list and a short set of named question types to target. Sessions run online over live video, one to one, so the evening stays available for the independent work that actually earns the marks.

intro.heading: An apartment community in a free zone, with four curricula in one building
paragraphs: Dubai Production City sits off Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road between Motor City and Dubai Studio City, built as a free zone for printing, publishing, packaging and media production and now dominated by mid-rise apartment towers with a mall and a lake at the centre. The residential population is almost entirely apartment-based, which rules out the villa-household assumptions most tutoring pages are written on.

The working profile is distinctive too. A large share of residents are employed by or run businesses inside the free zone, and a meaningful number hold freelance or small-business permits rather than conventional salaried contracts. That matters for tutoring in a practical way nobody writes about: income is lumpy. A household invoicing project by project cannot comfortably commit to an open-ended monthly arrangement, and the standard tutoring model, which is an indefinite weekly retainer, is a poor fit.

The third feature is curriculum spread. There is no school inside the community, so children travel to Motor City, Sports City, Jumeirah Village or Al Barsha South, and the neighbours are not on the same system. One stairwell will hold a child on an Indian board, a child on Cambridge IGCSE, a child on Pearson Edexcel International GCSE and a child in the IB Middle Years Programme, each with different papers, different series and different internal deadlines. Advice passed between families is therefore often confidently wrong.

One more feature of the community shapes the enquiries. A free zone built for printing, publishing and media production attracts people whose own work is project-based and deadline-driven, and who are used to scoping a piece of work before agreeing to it. They ask the questions a producer asks: what exactly am I buying, how long is it, what does it cost in total, and what happens if it does not work. Those are reasonable questions about a tutoring arrangement and almost nothing in this market is set up to answer them, which is why so many households here end up buying nothing at all.

Put those three together and you get the specific requests we see from this community: what does this actually cost in total, can we buy a defined block rather than an open commitment, and how do I know the person on the other end of the call is who they say they are. Those are good questions and most providers answer none of them directly. Three of the six agency pages ranking for these searches publish no price at all.

This page answers them. It covers who lives here and what each household wants, how to buy tutoring in blocks with the scope written down, who is legally permitted to tutor in the UAE and how a parent verifies it, what a quoted rate includes and which extras appear later, when a tuition centre is the better purchase, what a free-zone resident should know before tutoring themselves, and what Dubai's school expansion means for a family choosing now. Lessons are one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not visit homes in the UAE; home visiting is an India-only service.
