dubai/dubai-production-city.programmesIntro: Three programme families run across the schools this community uses, and the mix inside one building is the complication. The notes below cover what distinguishes each for a parent trying to compare two children.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two boards with different papers for the same subject. Cambridge uses four-digit codes such as 0580 for Mathematics, with a Core and Extended split that fixes the grade ceiling at entry. Pearson Edexcel uses codes such as 4MA1 and offers modular entry on some subjects. Past papers from the wrong board teach the wrong mark scheme.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs June and November series, with a March series in some regions, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with a separate timetable for each. Pearson runs May or June and November, with the November 2026 International GCSE timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. Two children in this community can therefore sit the same subject in different months.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, totalling thirty-two and converted to a 1 to 7 grade. There is no public examination at most schools, which confuses parents comparing an MYP child with a sibling sitting IGCSE: one has terminal papers and the other has a continuous assessment record.
programmes.countryNote: MYP provision used by this community sits mainly in Al Barsha South and the Jumeirah Village schools. Because the programme is assessed continuously, a dip is visible earlier here than in an IGCSE course, which is an advantage if a parent knows how to read the criteria rather than the grade.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects graded 1 to 7, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an internal assessment weighted by its subject guide, so coursework and papers both matter and neither can rescue the other entirely.
programmes.countryNote: Confirm all IB dates and deadlines with your school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org. This page publishes none, because they could not be verified from the IB directly for this project, and in practice the school's internal deadlines bind a student weeks earlier.

dubai/dubai-production-city.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects most often requested from this community, described by where the marks are actually decided rather than by syllabus heading.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The Core and Extended decision caps the grade before any paper is sat, and it is taken by the school. Within the paper, unshown method and misread question demands account for most recoverable marks, both of which respond to timed practice against a mark scheme.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: Circuit reasoning when conditions change is the IGCSE sticking point. At Diploma level the problem is the move from recall to derivation, along with uncertainty handling in practical work that is examinable and rarely practised deliberately.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: Mole calculations presented without units or working lose marks that the chemistry would otherwise have earned. Higher Level depth in energetics and kinetics cannot be absorbed late, and the internal assessment needs a question narrow enough to measure.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: Content volume pushes students into rereading rather than answering. Marks follow command terms precisely, so a description offered where an explanation was demanded scores nothing, and that habit is cheap to correct.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Reasoning marks dominate, so an unjustified correct answer collects a fraction of the available credit. Higher Level adds a long problem-solving paper, and the exploration must contain genuine mathematics rather than an applied formula.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Marks follow application to the stimulus rather than recall of frameworks. The internal assessment needs an organisation willing to share real figures, which households working inside a free zone are often unusually well placed to arrange.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram precision decides grades, and an unlabelled axis costs marks the written analysis cannot recover. Higher Level adds quantitative questions, and commentaries need published articles chosen to support the required analysis.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and comprehension under time pressure. The frequent loss is register rather than language: a strong piece written in the wrong form for the stated audience loses marks before the quality of the English is considered.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions differ between boards, and a student who learned Python at school can write answers an examiner cannot credit. The IB solution needs a real client and documented success criteria, arranged early in the first Diploma year.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Taught in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab pupils. Children who join Dubai schooling later need script and vocabulary work the timetable cannot pace individually.

sections.heading: Who lives in Dubai Production City, and what each household wants
paragraphs: Four household types produce nearly all the enquiries from this community, and they want visibly different things. The first is a family working inside the free zone on a salaried contract, with school-age children at Motor City or Sports City schools, asking the ordinary question about a slipping grade. These are straightforward and usually resolved with a weekly slot against the right syllabus code.

The second is a freelance or small-business household, where income arrives project by project. They ask about total cost and about commitment length before they ask about subjects, and they are right to. An open-ended monthly retainer is a genuinely poor product for this household, and providers who only sell that are excluding a large part of this community's demand without noticing.

The third is a multi-board household, often with children at two different schools on two different systems, where the parent is trying to compare two reports that are not comparable. The useful first step there is not tutoring at all; it is establishing what each child is actually entered for, which takes one email to each school and resolves half the confusion.

The fourth is an apartment household with a space problem rather than an academic one. Two children, one quiet room, and a lesson that needs a desk and a headset. That is a real constraint and it has practical answers: shorter sessions at staggered times, a headset rather than speakers, and a lesson scheduled when the flat is quietest rather than when a template says it should be.

sections.heading: Why a project-income household should buy blocks rather than retainers
paragraphs: The default tutoring product is an indefinite weekly arrangement billed monthly, with a notice period. It exists because it suits providers: revenue is predictable and attrition is slow. For a household whose income arrives in lumps, it is the wrong shape, and the usual outcome is a family that avoids tutoring entirely until a crisis, then buys expensively under deadline pressure.

A block fixes that. Agree a number of sessions, an objective, and a total figure before the first lesson. Six or eight sessions is usually enough to establish whether an arrangement is working and to move something measurable. At the end there is a review against marked school work and a decision: renew, stop, or change something. No notice period, no rollover, no awkward conversation about cancelling.

The discipline this imposes is good for the teaching as well as the budget. An open arrangement has no natural moment to ask whether it is working, which is precisely why so many drift on for months without anyone checking. A block has an end date built in, and the end date forces the question. Providers dislike that for obvious reasons, and it is the main reason to insist on it.

What to get in writing is short: the number of sessions, their length, the objective, the total cost, what happens if a session is missed by either side, and whether anything else is charged. If a provider will not write that down, that is the answer to the question you were asking. We will, and the figure does not change afterwards.

sections.heading: Is the person teaching your child legally permitted to do it?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and the position is clearer than most parents assume. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 on the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, and it is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days.

The eligibility list is broad rather than narrow. It includes teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. That last category surprises parents and is genuinely in the published guidance. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any figure circulating online should be treated as unverified, and this page does not quote one.

There is a separate and important restriction on school staff. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. This is press-reported and should be verified against the current policy document before anyone relies on it, but the direction is unambiguous: your child's own classroom teacher, privately, is not an arrangement to seek out.

For a free-zone community where a number of residents hold individual permits of their own, there is a final point. A permit authorises an individual to provide private lessons. It does not authorise premises, staff or a centre, and it is not an accreditation from any education regulator. Nobody holding one has been approved by KHDA, and any provider describing themselves that way is making a claim the permit does not support.

sections.heading: How a parent verifies a tutor in five questions
paragraphs: Verification is easier than it sounds and almost nobody does it. The questions below take five minutes and eliminate most of what goes wrong in this market, which is not fraud so much as mismatch: a competent tutor teaching the wrong board, or a generalist taking a Higher Level subject they have never taught.

First, ask which syllabus code and level they have taught, and how recently. The answer should be specific, naming 0580 or 4MA1, Higher or Standard Level, rather than mathematics in general. Second, ask what they would do in the first session. A tutor who says they would read the student's most recent marked script is describing a diagnosis; one who says they would assess the student's level with their own test is often describing a sales process.

Third, ask whether they hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit. The permit is free and valid for two years, so there is no good reason not to hold one, and the question itself tells you how seriously the arrangement is being treated. Fourth, ask what they will and will not do with coursework. The right answer includes explicit refusals, and a tutor who is vague here is a risk to your child rather than to you.

Fifth, ask what you will receive after each session and what happens if progress does not come. A written note and a review date against marked school work is the correct answer. No written record and no review point is how arrangements drift for months. None of these five questions requires you to know anything about the subject, which is precisely why they work.

sections.heading: What a quoted rate includes, and the extras that appear later
paragraphs: Published rates in this market are both scarce and incomplete. Three of the six agency pages ranking for these searches quote no figure at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars rather than dirhams. The table below collects Dubai market rates published in October 2026 with the publisher named for each band. These are market figures, not an IB Gram price list, and their value is as a benchmark for a quote you have in hand.

The question that matters more than the headline rate is what sits inside it. Ask whether the figure is per sixty-minute hour or per session, because a ninety-minute lesson quoted at an hourly rate is a different number. Ask whether marked homework, a written session note and messaging between lessons are included. Ask about registration fees, materials charges, minimum session blocks, and what happens financially when a session is cancelled by either side.

Monthly packaging is common and worth reading carefully. Packages seen in this market in October 2026 include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year work. A package is good value when it matches what your child needs and poor value when it bundles sessions you will not use.

One contextual figure. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package worth AED 1.5 billion. For this community that means tutoring is the part of the education budget still in play, which is an argument for spending it in defined, reviewed blocks rather than as an indefinite standing cost.

sections.heading: When a tuition centre is the better purchase
paragraphs: One-to-one tuition is not always the right answer, and a page selling it should say so. A small group class at a tuition centre can be better value where a student needs structured revision coverage of a syllabus rather than diagnosis of a specific weakness, where the subject is examined by predictable paper types, and where the student works better with peers than alone. For a budget-constrained household it also buys more contact hours per dirham.

The limits are equally clear. A group cannot diagnose. If two students in a class of six have different gaps, the teaching addresses neither precisely, and a student who is quietly lost in school will usually be quietly lost in a group as well. Group classes cannot supervise an individual component, because an investigation or an essay is by definition the student's own. And the timetable is the centre's rather than yours, with two car journeys attached.

The comparison below sets out the models honestly rather than against an invented competitor. Each has a job it does well. Where a household's problem is coverage, a centre is often the sensible purchase. Where the problem is a specific recurring error, a missed foundation or an unfinished coursework component, one-to-one is what moves it, and a group is an expensive way of not addressing it.

Two practical cautions about centres. Any tuition operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute rather than an individual tutor permit, so asking about it is reasonable. And a centre advertising itself as approved by an examination board for teaching, as opposed to being an approved examination centre for sitting papers, is making two different claims that are easy to conflate.

sections.heading: If you are thinking of tutoring yourself from a free-zone licence
paragraphs: This community contains a lot of people who teach something, and the question comes up often enough to answer directly on a parent-facing page. An individual providing private lessons needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit described above, which is free and valid for two years. A free-zone trade licence for a media or consultancy activity does not substitute for it, and the two regulate different things.

The line that matters is between an individual and an operation. Once there are premises, employed teachers or a centre offering timetabled classes in Dubai, the relevant instrument is a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. That process begins with an initial approval, allows a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and requires annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. It is a substantial undertaking rather than a formality.

The reason this belongs on a page for parents is the claim it generates. Holding either instrument does not make anyone accredited by the IB, Cambridge, Pearson or the Ministry of Education, and the phrase a parent should be most sceptical about in this market is the claim that a platform's tutors have been approved by KHDA. An individual permit is not an approval of teaching quality, and a training-institute permit is a licence to operate premises rather than an endorsement of a curriculum.

IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, no board accreditation and no UAE premises, and does not present itself as holding any of them. We are an online tutor-matching platform, and the honest description of what we offer is one-to-one teaching over live video by tutors matched on subject and level. Anything beyond that would be a claim we cannot evidence, which is exactly what several pages in this search cluster do.

sections.heading: What Dubai's school expansion means for a family choosing now
paragraphs: Supply conditions shape what a family can do, and Dubai's private school market is unusually well documented. In the 2024-25 academic year it held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen different curricula. By enrolment share the UK curriculum accounted for 37 per cent, the Indian curriculum 26 per cent, the US curriculum 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate 7 per cent. That last figure explains something families in this community notice: IB places are a smaller share of a very large market, so they cluster in particular districts rather than being available everywhere.

The market is also growing quickly. Six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. For 2026-27 Dubai adds seven new private schools, four following the UK curriculum and three offering the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. For a parent in an apartment community with no school inside it, that is directly relevant: new capacity in nearby districts changes the commute, and new schools typically open with small upper year groups and thin option blocks.

The fee position matters alongside it. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. A household budgeting for the year can treat school fees as fixed and tutoring as the variable, which is the opposite of the usual assumption.

The practical conclusion for a family choosing a school now is to ask about year-group size rather than about the overall inspection band. A new school with three IB classes in the primary phase and eleven students in Year 12 is a different proposition from an established one, and the difference shows up precisely in the subjects a small option block cannot run. KHDA inspection reports break performance down by phase and subject, which is where that question gets answered.

sections.heading: Getting started from Dubai Production City
paragraphs: Start with the entry details, because this community runs several boards at once and half the confusion resolves there. Send each child's school, the exact syllabus code and tier from the examination entry, the most recent marked work, and the date of the next assessment. If two children are on different systems, say so, because the advice is genuinely different and should not be averaged.

Then buy a diagnostic rather than a plan. One or two sessions, no commitment, spent reading marked work with the student to establish whether the problem is content not known, technique not trained, timing lost under pressure, or confidence gone. You get a written summary naming which. A meaningful number of those summaries conclude that no paid work is needed yet, and we would rather write that than sell a block.

If work is warranted, we will propose a defined block with the session count, objective and total cost written down, ending in a review against marked school work. No rollover, no notice period, no automatic renewal. For a household with project-based income that structure is the difference between tutoring being usable and being avoided until a crisis.

Three limits stated before payment. We make no promises about grades, we place no tutors in UAE homes because every lesson is one-to-one online, and we hold no permit, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson and will not imply one. Where a specialist is scarce, we will tell you how long the match will take before you commit rather than after.

process.title: Send the entry details for each child
process.description: School, exact syllabus code and tier from the examination entry, most recent marked work, and the next assessment date. Where two children are on different boards, send both sets, because the past papers, mark schemes and series differ.

process.title: Buy a diagnostic, not a plan
process.description: One or two sessions with nothing attached, spent reading marked work with the student. The written summary says whether the problem is content, technique, timing or confidence, and sometimes says that no paid work is needed yet.

process.title: Agree a block in writing
process.description: Session count, length, objective, total cost, what happens when either side misses a session, and confirmation that nothing else is charged. The figure does not change afterwards, and there is no notice period because there is no rolling commitment.

process.title: Verify before the first lesson
process.description: Ask which syllabus code and level the tutor has taught and how recently, whether they hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit, and what they will refuse to do with coursework. Five minutes of questions removes most of what goes wrong.

process.title: Review at the end of the block
process.description: Progress measured on work a teacher marked, not on how sessions felt, with three honest options: renew, stop, or change the tutor or diagnosis. A block has an end date built in, which is what forces the question to be asked at all.

whyPoints.title: Blocks, not open-ended retainers
whyPoints.description: A defined number of sessions with a written objective, a total cost and a review at the end. For households whose income arrives project by project, that is the difference between tutoring being affordable and being postponed until there is a crisis.

whyPoints.title: Verification you can do yourself
whyPoints.description: We publish the five questions to ask any tutor, including ours, and the regulatory position behind them. A parent who can check a syllabus code, a permit and a coursework boundary does not need to take anyone's marketing on trust.

whyPoints.title: The right board, not the better-known one
whyPoints.description: In a community running Cambridge, Pearson Edexcel, the MYP and Indian boards in one building, matching the tutor to the exact code and series matters more than anywhere. Practising the wrong board's papers is the most common wasted term here.

whyPoints.title: Honest about when we are the wrong purchase
whyPoints.description: Where a household needs structured syllabus coverage rather than diagnosis, a small group at a centre may be better value, and this page says so. A provider that never recommends an alternative is not giving advice.

whyPoints.title: No claims we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: No grade promises, no invented statistics, no KHDA or examination-board approval, and no UAE premises. Every rate names its publisher, every regulatory statement names its source, and where something could not be verified the page says so.

faqs.question: Can we buy a fixed number of sessions instead of a monthly commitment?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a project-income household it is the better structure. A block of six or eight sessions with a stated objective, a total cost agreed in writing and a review against marked school work at the end gives you a knowable figure and a natural decision point. There is no rollover and no notice period to negotiate. The discipline also helps the teaching, because an open arrangement has no moment at which anyone has to ask whether it is working.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor is legally allowed to teach privately here?
faqs.answer: Ask directly whether they hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system under the service name Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a two-working-day completion time. Because it costs nothing, there is no good reason for a serious tutor not to hold one, and asking tells you how the arrangement is being treated.

faqs.question: Is it true that a school student can hold a tutoring permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The published eligibility list for the private tuition work permit includes teachers registered at government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. That last category surprises most parents. It is not a reason to dismiss a young tutor for straightforward homework support, but it is a reason to ask about subject depth before putting a Higher Level Diploma subject in their hands.

faqs.question: Can my child be tutored by their own class teacher?
faqs.answer: It is not an arrangement to seek out. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. This is press-reported and worth verifying against the current policy document, but the direction is clear. A different teacher who knows the same syllabus is the straightforward alternative.

faqs.question: What does it mean when a provider says its tutors are approved by KHDA?
faqs.answer: In practice, nothing you can rely on. KHDA issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises and staff, which is a licence to operate rather than an endorsement of teaching quality. An individual tutor holds a MoHRE permit, which is also not an approval of quality and not issued by an education regulator at all. Neither makes anyone accredited by the IB, Cambridge, Pearson or the Ministry of Education. Treat the phrase as a marketing claim and ask what specifically is held.

faqs.question: Two of my children are on different boards. Does advice transfer between them?
faqs.answer: Less than you would hope. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel set different papers for the same subject, with different command terms and mark schemes, and their series fall in different months. An MYP child is assessed continuously against four criteria while an IGCSE sibling sits terminal papers. A tutor who suits one is not automatically right for the other, and past papers from the wrong board actively teach the wrong technique. Start by confirming each child's board, code and series in writing with the school.

faqs.question: Where should a child take an online lesson in a two-bedroom apartment?
faqs.answer: Anywhere with a desk, a chair and a headset, which matters more than the room. A headset removes most of the household noise problem in both directions and is the single cheapest improvement available. Where two children need lessons, stagger them rather than running both at once, and prefer shorter sessions, which are easier to fit into a quiet window. We schedule around when the flat is actually quiet rather than around a standard slot.

faqs.question: Is a group class at a centre ever better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Yes, for a specific job. Where a student needs structured coverage of a syllabus and timed practice rather than diagnosis of a particular weakness, a small group buys more contact hours per dirham and the peer setting helps some students work. What a group cannot do is diagnose an individual gap, adapt pace to one child, or supervise an investigation or essay, which is by definition the student's own work. If the problem is a recurring specific error, one-to-one is what moves it.

faqs.question: What should be written down before the first lesson?
faqs.answer: Six things: the number of sessions, their length, the objective, the total cost, what happens financially if a session is missed by either side, and confirmation that nothing else is charged. Ask specifically about registration fees, materials charges and minimum blocks, because those are where a headline rate becomes a different number. A provider unwilling to put that in writing has answered the question you were really asking.

faqs.question: Do tutors come to apartments in Dubai Production City?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service IB Gram operates only in India, and every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video. For an apartment community that is usually the better arrangement: no visitor in a small flat, no travel cost folded into the rate, and a tutor chosen for your child's exact syllabus rather than for living close enough to drive over. Market figures also put in-home rates above online rates at every level, with the difference being travel time.

faqs.question: What do monthly tutoring packages in Dubai actually cost?
faqs.answer: Packages observed in this market in October 2026 include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year work. A package is good value only when the session count matches what your child needs rather than what is convenient to bill.

faqs.question: Are school fees going up this year?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a household budgeting the year, that means fees can be treated as fixed and tutoring is the movable part, which is an argument for buying it in reviewed blocks rather than as an indefinite monthly standing cost.

faqs.question: How many IB schools are there actually in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The International Baccalaureate accounted for 7 per cent of private school enrolment in Dubai in 2024-25, in a market of 387,441 students across 227 schools offering seventeen curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent and the Indian curriculum at 26 per cent. For 2026-27 Dubai adds seven new private schools, three of them offering the IB, creating 16,846 new places in total. The practical consequence is that IB provision clusters in particular districts rather than being available in every neighbourhood.

faqs.question: What should I ask a new school about its sixth form?
faqs.answer: Year-group size and option blocks, not the inspection band. Ask how many students are in the current Year 12, how many option columns the timetable runs, how many students took each Higher Level subject last year, and whether each subject is taught by a specialist. A school opening with strong primary provision and eleven students in Year 12 cannot offer the choice an established one can, and KHDA reports break performance down by phase and subject where the band does not.

faqs.question: What will IB Gram not do or claim?
faqs.answer: We will not promise a grade or publish a success statistic we cannot support with a sample size, date and method. We will not send a tutor to a UAE address, because delivery here is online only. We will not write, rewrite, translate or complete any part of an assessed component. We hold no permit, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and we operate no office, centre or branch in the UAE.

dubai/dubai-production-city.closingHeading: Agree the scope before you agree the subject
dubai/dubai-production-city.closingBody: For a household in this community the useful order is unusual: establish what each child is actually entered for, buy one diagnostic session with nothing attached, then agree a defined block with the session count, objective and total cost written down. That gives you a knowable figure, a real decision point at the end, and a tutor matched to the exact syllabus rather than to the better-known board. Send the entry details and the last marked piece of work and we will tell you what the diagnosis is, what a block would cost, and whether a small group at a centre would serve you better than we would.

dubai/dubai-silicon-oasis.tutorsIntro: The profiles below are the ones Silicon Oasis families book most: IGCSE Mathematics and the separate sciences in Years 10 and 11, Diploma maths and chemistry, and MYP criterion work. Each tutor teaches a named specification, and the agreed slot is confirmed in writing before lesson one.

intro.heading: The hour between the bus and bedtime is the whole constraint
paragraphs: Ask a Silicon Oasis parent what makes tutoring hard and almost nobody says the subject. They say the week. The school bus turns into the community somewhere between half past three and half past four depending on the route. One or both parents are still in the free zone or on the Dubai-Sharjah road until six. Dinner, younger siblings, Arabic homework and whatever the school set that day all land in the same two hours. Somewhere inside that, a tutoring session is supposed to happen.

This is not a trivial logistics complaint. It is the reason tutoring plans fail here more often than they fail for lack of a good tutor. A family books three sessions a week in September because three sounds serious. By late October one of the three has been cancelled twice, a second has drifted to nine at night where nothing useful happens, and the third is carrying all the weight. The plan did not fail academically. It failed because it was never a timetable a real household could keep.

Silicon Oasis has its own version of this. The community is apartment-dense and free-zone adjacent, so a high proportion of households have both parents working on site or close by, with fixed office hours rather than flexible ones. Children attend schools inside the community and schools a long drive away, often within the same building. And the UAE working week is Monday to Friday with a short Friday, which creates one genuinely underused slot that almost nobody asks for.

So the honest starting question is not how many hours of tutoring your child needs. It is how many hours this household can protect for a whole term without resentment. For most Silicon Oasis families the answer is two. Two sessions that always happen beat four that mostly do not, and once you accept two, the next question becomes interesting: which two subjects deserve them, and what gets left alone.

IB Gram is built around that answer. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, so no part of the schedule depends on a tutor's drive time. IB Gram does not operate home visits in Dubai; in-home tutoring is offered only in India. For a Silicon Oasis household the practical effect is that a session can start fifteen minutes after the bus arrives, and that a cancelled slot can be rescheduled the same week rather than negotiated around someone's route across the city.

The rest of this page is the scheduling and cost detail competitors leave out: what time a session can realistically begin from each route, what the formats actually cost in AED, how the UAE calendar moves a plan, who is legally permitted to teach your child privately, and where a tutor has to stop on assessed work.

dubai/dubai-silicon-oasis.programmesIntro: Silicon Oasis households run across all four programmes at once, partly because the community's schools sit on different boards and partly because families move between them. The note under each programme describes what it does to an evening, which is the part that decides whether a plan survives October.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years of specification-led teaching examined at the end of Year 11. The syllabus code - 0580, 0625, 4MA1 and so on - decides the papers, the tiering and what appears on the formula sheet. Cambridge runs Core and Extended routes with different grade ceilings on several subjects; Pearson generally runs a single tier. Eight or nine subjects at once makes this the year group with the worst mismatch between work to be done and hours available.
programmes.countryNote: Silicon Oasis Year 11 families almost always arrive asking for three or four subjects and leave with two. Mathematics and one science is the usual honest answer, because those are the subjects where a weekly hour changes the paper, while English and the humanities respond better to self-marked practice the student can do without a slot.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internally assessed work in each subject is marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB. The external papers all fall in one session, so two years converge on about three weeks. The scheduling problem here is different from IGCSE: fewer subjects, but coursework deadlines that cluster and cannot be moved.
programmes.countryNote: A Diploma student living in Silicon Oasis is usually travelling further than a Year 10 sibling, because the local schools that run the full Diploma are fewer than those running IGCSE. That means a later start on weekdays, and it is the main reason Diploma families here end up with one weekday slot and one weekend block.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria per subject group, each marked out of eight and converted to a 1-7 grade. There are no external papers until optional eAssessment at the end of Year 11, so all marks come from interim tasks spread across the year. A student can be assessed on one criterion in October and not meet another until February, which makes the reported grade hard to read in isolation.
programmes.countryNote: MYP requests from Silicon Oasis are usually criterion-shaped rather than subject-shaped: a strong student with a weak criterion C in sciences, or a mathematician whose criterion D reflections are thin. Those are short, specific pieces of work that suit a six-week block rather than a year-long slot.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units with a report written against learning outcomes rather than marks. Reading fluency, number-fact recall and written stamina remain the things that decide how Year 7 goes, and they are exactly what a prose report can hide. At this age session length matters more than session count: thirty focused minutes is worth more than a tired hour.
programmes.countryNote: Primary families in Silicon Oasis have the easiest scheduling problem on paper - the children are home earliest - and the hardest in practice, because the youngest child's slot competes with an older sibling's. A short early session for the younger child before the secondary slot opens is usually the arrangement that holds.

dubai/dubai-silicon-oasis.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Silicon Oasis families most often ask for, with a note on whether a weekly slot is the right tool for each. Some subjects move with an hour a week. Others move with marked practice the student does alone, and paying for a slot on those is poor value.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: The subject that responds most reliably to a weekly hour, because the failures are specific and diagnosable. Extended candidates lose most marks on multi-step problems that mix two topics and signpost no method. The tier decision taken in Year 10 caps the grade, so check it before booking anything.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and the practical paper account for most of the lost marks. Students who have done the experiments still need deliberate practice at reading someone else's method and finding its weakness, which is the skill the written practical paper actually tests.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles calculations and organic chemistry are where grades are decided, and both reward drill rather than explanation. A weekly slot works well in Year 11 and is often wasted in Year 10, where the content is still being taught and self-marked practice does the same job.

subjects.name: IGCSE Biology
subjects.description: Looks like a memory subject, which is why students revise it by rereading. Marks turn on terminology precision and command terms: a described answer to an explain question earns nothing extra, however accurate. Responds better to a retrieval routine than to a weekly lesson.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Calculus and proof are the pressure points at Higher Level. The exploration moves whole grades because it is marked against five lettered criteria and students treat it as a write-up. A slot here earns its cost, particularly in the term the exploration is drafted.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and heavy calculator work. Students who chose this route to avoid proof are surprised by how much interpretation is required: an unexamined regression line scores less than a weaker model discussed honestly.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the Higher Level papers. Most lost marks are not chemistry: they are uncertainty handling and conclusions that outrun the data in the internally assessed investigation.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Rewards students who read a situation before reaching for an equation. The recurring loss is algebraic - a sound physical argument abandoned when the rearrangement gets untidy. The data-analysis paper is rarely practised outside the lessons spent setting up the investigation.

subjects.name: Business Management and Economics
subjects.description: Both reward application to unfamiliar material under timing. Economics marks sit in correctly labelled diagrams; Business Management marks sit in evaluating a decision rather than describing a company. Short blocks before mocks work better than a year-long slot.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: A compulsory part of every Dubai school timetable and the stream most tutoring budgets forget until a report arrives. It needs its own tutor and its own goal rather than being folded into an academic slot, and the match is different again for Arabic as a first language.

dubai/dubai-silicon-oasis.modesIntro: Three session shapes fit a Silicon Oasis week. The choice is not really about teaching style; it is about which shape survives a term in a household where both parents work fixed hours and the bus decides the start time.

modes.description: A single fixed hour, same tutor, same day, starting fifteen to thirty minutes after your child's usual arrival. It is deliberately early in the evening, because demanding work does not belong in the leftover hour before bed. Everything else in the week is built around keeping this one slot untouched.

sections.heading: What time a session can realistically start from each route
paragraphs: A direct answer first. For a Silicon Oasis family whose child attends a school inside the community, a session can begin at 16:15 or 16:30. For a child bussed from Nad Al Sheba or Mirdif, 17:15 is the honest floor. For a Diploma student travelling from the Al Barsha or Umm Suqeim corridor, 18:00. Those three numbers decide more about whether tutoring works than the choice of tutor does.

The reason is simple and under-discussed. A session that starts at the edge of a child's capacity produces the appearance of tutoring rather than the effect. The student is physically present, the tutor works, the hour is billed, and nothing transfers because attention was gone before the first question. Parents notice this as a vague sense that the lessons are not landing, and they usually blame the tutor.

The table below maps the main routes into Silicon Oasis against a realistic arrival window and the earliest start we would recommend. These are operational figures from scheduling Dubai families rather than a published survey, and they will be wrong for your household by fifteen minutes in one direction or the other. Tell us which school and which route, and we set the slot from that rather than from an average.

One consequence of online delivery is worth naming here, because it is the whole reason the timing conversation is even possible. A tutor who drives has to fit your household between two other households and a journey across Dubai, so the slot you are offered is the one that suits the route. A tutor teaching over live video can start at 16:20 on a Tuesday because nothing has to physically arrive anywhere.

sections.heading: Two slots, and the discipline of choosing which two
paragraphs: Once the honest number of weekly sessions is two, the planning question changes shape entirely. It is no longer how much tutoring to buy. It is which two subjects will convert an hour into marks, and which subjects should be handled by the student alone with a marking scheme and a timer. Getting that allocation right is worth more than adding a third session, and it costs nothing.

The sorting rule is reasonably reliable. Subjects where failure is specific and diagnosable - Mathematics, Chemistry, Physics - convert a slot into marks efficiently, because a tutor can watch the student work and see exactly which step breaks. Subjects where failure is diffuse - essay subjects, content-heavy Biology, the humanities - respond better to repeated marked practice, which a disciplined student can run themselves with a past paper and a published scheme.

Year group changes the answer too. A Year 10 student at the start of IGCSE usually needs nothing beyond a study routine, and paying for two slots in October of Year 10 is often money spent eleven months early. A Year 11 student in January needs the slots badly, pointed at the two weakest papers. A Diploma student in the exploration term needs one slot on maths coursework and the other kept free for whichever subject's internal assessment is next.

The table gives the allocations we recommend most often by situation. Treat it as a starting position to argue with rather than a prescription - your child's weakest subject is not necessarily the one where an hour buys the most. The subject to fund is the one where a specific, fixable failure is visible in the marked work.

sections.heading: Online, in-home and group tuition with Silicon Oasis travel priced in
paragraphs: The format comparison usually gets made on price per hour, which hides the part that matters in a community like this. An in-home tutor charges for travel whether or not the invoice says so, and Silicon Oasis sits far enough from the villa districts where many freelance tutors live that the premium is real. A group class is cheaper per head and slower per head, which is a reasonable trade for some students and a waste for others.

The figures below are market rates read from provider sites and a published Dubai rate survey in October 2026. They are not IB Gram's price list; ask us for our figure before booking and compare it against the band. What the table adds to a generic comparison is the Silicon Oasis column: what each format actually involves from an apartment in this community, rather than in the abstract.

Note the honest entry on in-home tutoring. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai, because in-home tuition is a service offered only in India. The row exists because it is a genuine option in this market and you should be able to compare it properly, including the part where you are paying someone to sit in traffic on Al Ain Road. If physical presence matters more to your family than specialist match, an in-home tutor is the right choice and we will say so.

The one format worth more attention than it gets is the sibling-shared session, where two children at a similar stage in the same subject take one hour together. It only works when the stages genuinely match, and it fails badly when a parent forces it on children two years apart. Where it does work, it halves the cost per child and halves the number of slots an evening has to absorb, which in a Silicon Oasis week is the bigger saving.

sections.heading: Ramadan, term breaks and the calendar a plan has to respect
paragraphs: A term plan written in September that ignores the UAE calendar will be rewritten twice before February. Ramadan shortens school days and shifts the whole household rhythm, with the useful study window moving to after Iftar for many families. Term breaks in the Dubai school year are long enough that a four-week gap can undo a term of progress if nothing is set to carry over it. Exam windows then compress everything into a few weeks.

The practical approach is to decide in advance what happens at each of those points rather than improvising. During Ramadan, families who want to keep continuity usually move to shorter sessions at a later hour, or pause the academic slot and keep only a coursework checkpoint. Both are reasonable. What does not work is leaving the slot nominally in place and cancelling it weekly, because that produces the cost of tutoring with none of the effect.

Term breaks need the opposite treatment. A short holiday block - three or four sessions across a two-week break - holds position far better than a full programme, and it is also the only time of year when a student has the capacity to fix something structural rather than keeping up. The summer break is long enough to need a deliberate decision: either a genuine block with a target, or a clean stop with a restart date in the diary.

Then there are the board deadlines, which move independently of the school calendar. Cambridge's March 2027 series takes final entries on 27 November 2026 for examinations beginning 3 February 2027, with results on Direct on 13 May. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May/June and November, with November 2026 papers finishing on 19 November and results reaching students in January. IB session dates are not stated on this page: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so ask your child's coordinator for the confirmed window and build the plan from that.

sections.heading: Which schools Silicon Oasis children attend, and why the code matters more than the bus
paragraphs: Silicon Oasis is unusual in having schools inside the community while also sitting within reach of Academic City, Nad Al Sheba, Mirdif and Al Warqa. The result is a community where neighbouring apartments can hold a Cambridge IGCSE student, a Pearson IGCSE student, a Diploma student and a child on an Indian curriculum, all leaving on different buses at different times.

For tutoring this creates one recurring error. Parents describe their child's course by subject and year group, a tutor is matched on that, and three sessions in it becomes clear the tutor has been teaching the wrong specification. Cambridge and Pearson differ in paper structure, in tiering and in what appears on the formula sheet, and the difference is not cosmetic. The fix takes one question: ask the school's examinations officer for the syllabus code on the entry form.

Dubai's private school market gives some sense of the spread. KHDA counted 227 private schools with 387,441 pupils in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with the British route the largest by enrolment and the IB accounting for around 7% of enrolment. Dubai is adding seven new private schools for 2026-27, four British and three IB, creating 16,846 places - so the mix in a community like this keeps shifting rather than settling.

Keep the regulator's role clear in your own mind. KHDA licenses and inspects Dubai private schools and publishes inspection outcomes on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. It does not license private tutors, and no tutoring platform is inspected under that framework. A school's inspection band tells you about the school; it tells you nothing about whether your child's slot is being used well.

sections.heading: Is the person teaching your child legally permitted to do it?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and the rules are more specific than most parents realise. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen.

MoHRE's own service page lists the permit as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount appears on this page; a figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source.

Two conditions matter for a Silicon Oasis family in particular. First, the permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Hiring your child's own teacher privately is therefore not the shortcut it appears to be. Second, a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute.

IB Gram holds no such permit and operates no centre, office or branch in the UAE; lessons are delivered online. Equally, no claim of approval, accreditation or licensing by KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson appears anywhere on this site, because none is held. The table sets out the categories so that you can ask an individual tutor a precise question rather than a vague one.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with assessed work, said plainly
paragraphs: There are providers ranking for these searches that sell finished internal assessments at a fixed price. It needs saying directly: a student who submits purchased work is exposed to their school's academic honesty process and, under IB rules, to a malpractice finding that can cost an entire diploma. The provider takes the fee. The student takes the consequence, and it is not a proportionate one.

Legitimate support is narrower and genuinely more useful. A tutor teaches the criteria by letter and the marks attached to each. A tutor interrogates a research question until it is answerable within the word limit. A tutor questions the method, the sample, the controls and the mathematics. A tutor reads a draft and replies with questions - why this comparison, what does the graph show that the table does not, which limitation would an examiner notice first. The student then makes their own decisions, in their own words.

What a tutor must never do is supply text, restructure an argument on the student's behalf, or hand back a rewritten version to be retyped. The test is straightforward: at the end, the student should be able to defend every decision in the work under questioning, without notes, because every decision was theirs. If they cannot, the help went too far regardless of who gave it or how it was described.

The same boundary covers the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay, the MYP Personal Project and IGCSE coursework. Ask any prospective tutor how they handle a draft, and listen for whether the answer involves giving the student a better version. Note also that past papers, mark schemes and subject guides belong to the boards: a tutor should reference and link official material rather than distribute copies of it.

sections.heading: How to tell whether the slot is working, not just filling the evening
paragraphs: Tutoring is unusually easy to continue paying for without evidence. The session happens, the student seems more confident, everyone feels better, and nobody checks whether marks moved. In a household already stretched for time, that is the worst possible outcome: the evening is being spent and the problem is still there. So the review mechanism matters as much as the teaching.

What counts as evidence is narrow. School report grades are too slow and too soft. Confidence is not evidence. The things that count are marks on the student's own returned papers, scores on timed past papers marked against the published scheme, and whether the specific failure identified in the diagnostic has stopped appearing. If the diagnostic said the student cannot start an unprompted question, the test is whether they now start unprompted questions.

Set the review point before the first session, not when doubt arrives. Six to eight weeks is right for a weekly slot: long enough for a habit to change, short enough that a wrong match is not carried for a term. At that point there are three legitimate outcomes - continue, change tutor, or stop - and stopping should be a normal result rather than a failure. Tutoring that has done its job should end.

Ask for the written record too. Each session should produce a short note naming what was worked on and what the next target is, which is also how you spot drift: four consecutive notes on the same topic mean something is not landing. A provider who cannot produce that record is asking you to take the benefit on trust over a whole term, in a market where the hour costs AED 150 to 450.

process.title: Tell us the school, the route and the arrival time
process.description: Give us the school name, the bus route and roughly when your child walks through the door. That is what sets the slot. A request without it gets a generic evening offer, which is the single commonest reason a tutoring plan collapses by half term in a community with Silicon Oasis commutes.

process.title: Send the syllabus code with the subject
process.description: Ask the examinations officer for the code on the entry form - 0580, 0625, 4MA1 - or give the IB subject and level with the school's own deadline dates. The code decides the papers and therefore the correct tutor. Subject name plus year group is not enough to match on accurately.

process.title: One diagnostic hour on returned work
process.description: The first session works on marked scripts and a short set of unprompted questions rather than teaching. It identifies which specific failure is costing marks, and you receive that in writing. Everything after it is shaped by the finding, including whether two slots are needed or one will do.

process.title: Fix two protected slots and one fallback
process.description: We agree a weekday slot timed off the bus, a weekend block for the heavier work, and a single named fallback time for the weeks something collapses. The tutor's base and time zone are stated before you confirm. Two slots that always happen beat four that mostly do not.

process.title: Build the term backwards from the deadlines
process.description: The plan starts at the examination or coursework deadline and works back to this week, with entry deadlines, mock windows, Ramadan and term breaks marked. Cambridge and Pearson dates come from the official timetables; IB dates come from your child's coordinator rather than from a tutoring page.

process.title: Review on marks at six to eight weeks
process.description: We compare the plan against actual marked work and decide to continue, change tutor or stop. Stopping is a normal outcome. A provider with no review point and no exit is selling a standing order, and in a week this tight that is an evening you cannot get back.

whyPoints.title: The slot is set from your bus, not our diary
whyPoints.description: Because nobody has to drive anywhere, a session can start fifteen minutes after your child gets home rather than whenever a tutor's route allows. In a community where arrivals range across two hours, that is the difference between a session that works and one that is merely attended.

whyPoints.title: Two slots planned honestly
whyPoints.description: We plan for the number of sessions a working household can actually protect, then argue carefully about which two subjects earn them. Over-booking in September is the commonest way a Silicon Oasis tutoring budget gets wasted by November.

whyPoints.title: Matched on specification, not on uniform
whyPoints.description: Silicon Oasis children attend schools on several boards, so the match starts from the syllabus code. Cambridge and Pearson differ in papers, tiering and formula sheets, and a tutor teaching the wrong one can do it competently for a whole term.

whyPoints.title: Rates in AED with their sources named
whyPoints.description: Every figure on this page is attributed to the provider or survey that published it, and dated to October 2026. You can check each one and hold any quote, including ours, against it.

whyPoints.title: The calendar is in the plan, not a surprise
whyPoints.description: Ramadan, term breaks, mock windows and board entry deadlines are marked before the first session. The Cambridge entry deadline that falls in November decides a grade ceiling in February, and finding that out late costs a whole series.

whyPoints.title: A coursework line that does not move
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question and give feedback; no part of an assessed task is produced for the student. The test is whether your child can defend every choice unaided, and that test exists to protect them rather than us.

faqs.question: What time can a tutoring session start for a Dubai Silicon Oasis family?
faqs.answer: It depends on the route rather than the community. A child at a school inside Silicon Oasis is usually home by about 16:00, so a 16:15 start is realistic and worth protecting. A child bussed from Mirdif, Al Warqa or Nad Al Sheba typically arrives between 16:45 and 17:30, which puts the floor at about 17:30. A Diploma student travelling from the Al Barsha or Jumeirah corridor is often not back until 18:00. Tell us the school and the route and we set the slot from that, because a session timed at the edge of a child's capacity produces attendance rather than progress.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send tutors into Dubai Silicon Oasis apartments?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide in-home tutoring anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service offered only in India. Lessons for Silicon Oasis families run one-to-one over live video with screen sharing, which is how a tutor and a student work through a marked script together. The practical advantage in this community is timing: a session can begin minutes after the bus arrives, because nothing has to travel. The second advantage is the tutor pool, which becomes everyone who teaches your child's specification rather than everyone who can reach Silicon Oasis by car.

faqs.question: Is the Friday short day any good as a tutoring slot in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It is the most underused slot in the week. UAE schools and offices run Monday to Friday with a shortened Friday, so most students are free from early afternoon and are not yet tired. A session at 14:00 on a Friday lands on a student with capacity left, competes with almost nothing else in the family timetable, and survives exam season better than an evening slot. It suits primary and Middle Years students particularly well, since they fade earliest. Very few families ask for it, which also means availability is better than in the weekday evening peak.

faqs.question: We both work in the free zone. Does an online lesson need supervising?
faqs.answer: Not supervising, but it needs a setup. The student should be in a room with a door, on a laptop rather than a phone, with the subject material and a notebook already open before the session starts. For primary and lower Middle Years children, an adult or older sibling in the house helps for the first few sessions until the routine holds. You get a short written note after each session naming what was covered and what the next target is, so you can see what happened without having been in the room. That written record is also how drift gets spotted early.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week can a Silicon Oasis evening actually hold?
faqs.answer: For most working households, two. One weekday slot timed off the bus and one longer weekend block is the arrangement that survives a full term. Families who book three or four in September typically lose one to cancellations and let another drift to nine at night, where very little transfers. Two sessions that always happen outperform four that mostly do not, and the planning energy is better spent choosing which two subjects earn the slots. Subjects with specific diagnosable failures, such as Mathematics and the sciences, convert an hour into marks faster than essay subjects do.

faqs.question: Which schools do most Dubai Silicon Oasis children attend?
faqs.answer: Some attend schools inside the community or in neighbouring Academic City; many are bussed to Nad Al Sheba, Mirdif, Al Warqa or Al Qusais, and a smaller number travel across to the Al Barsha corridor. The important point for tutoring is the spread of boards rather than the list of names. Two children in neighbouring apartments can sit entirely different Physics papers depending on whether their school entered them with Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel. Ask the school's examinations officer for the syllabus code on the entry form before booking any subject tutor.

faqs.question: Is a small group cheaper than one-to-one for a Silicon Oasis child?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per hour and slower per hour. A group of two to four works reasonably for general revision where everyone needs the same content covered again. It works poorly for a specific diagnosed failure, because the tutor cannot stop and watch one student attempt forty unprompted questions while three others wait. A sibling-shared session is the better version of this idea when two children are genuinely at the same stage in the same subject: it halves the cost per child and, more valuably in a tight week, halves the number of slots the evening has to hold.

faqs.question: What does in-home tutoring cost once Silicon Oasis travel is counted?
faqs.answer: Market rates for in-home one-to-one in Dubai run roughly AED 180-500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online and AED 200-450 or more for an IB or IGCSE specialist. Those figures come from a published Dubai rate survey and provider listings read in October 2026. The travel component is real in this community, because Silicon Oasis is a drive from the villa districts where many independent tutors live. IB Gram does not offer in-home visits in the UAE, so the row is here for comparison rather than as something we sell.

faqs.question: Should we keep the Silicon Oasis slot running through Ramadan or pause it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for many families that is the better arrangement. School days shorten, the household rhythm changes, and the genuinely productive window often sits after Iftar. Two approaches work: move to shorter sessions at a later hour, or pause the academic slot and keep only a coursework checkpoint so deadlines do not slip. Both are reasonable and both should be decided in advance. What does not work is leaving the slot nominally in place and cancelling week by week, which produces the full cost of tutoring and almost none of the effect.

faqs.question: What should happen to the plan over the long summer break?
faqs.answer: Decide deliberately rather than drifting. A long break is the only point in the year when a student has capacity to fix something structural instead of keeping up, so a genuine block with a stated target - rebuilding algebra before Year 11, or drafting an exploration properly - is good value. A clean stop with a restart date in the diary is equally valid. The arrangement to avoid is a nominal weekly slot through July and August that is cancelled half the time, because it costs money, achieves nothing and makes the restart in September harder.

faqs.question: Do private tutors working in Dubai Silicon Oasis need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE lists the service with no fee and a two-working-day completion time through its app, website and e-services. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so no figure is quoted here. Asking an individual tutor whether they hold it is a fair and quick question.

faqs.question: Can we hire a teacher from my child's own school for private lessons?
faqs.answer: That route is closed, and deliberately so. The MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct barring a tutor from serving students affiliated with their own school, and Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school. The conflict of interest is obvious once stated: the person teaching the class, setting the assessments and reporting the grade should not also be paid privately by the family. A specialist who teaches the same specification elsewhere gives you the subject knowledge without the conflict.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help my child meet a school coursework deadline?
faqs.answer: A tutor can help the student meet it; a tutor cannot meet it for them. Support means teaching the criteria and their mark allocations, questioning the research question until it is answerable, interrogating method and data, and responding to a draft with questions rather than corrections. It does not mean supplying text, restructuring the argument or handing back a version to retype. The test is whether your child can defend every choice in the work unaided. Purchased or ghostwritten coursework exposes the student to a school academic honesty process and, under IB rules, to a malpractice finding.

faqs.question: How will we know the slot is working rather than just filling the evening?
faqs.answer: By looking at marks on your child's own returned work and on timed past papers scored against the published scheme, and by checking whether the specific failure named in the diagnostic has stopped appearing. Confidence is not evidence and school report grades are too slow. Set a review point before the first session - six to eight weeks is right for a weekly slot - with three legitimate outcomes: continue, change tutor, or stop. Stopping should be a normal result. Ask also for the short written note after each session, because four consecutive notes on the same topic mean something is not landing.

faqs.question: What should we send before the first Silicon Oasis session?
faqs.answer: Four things, and none of them take long. The syllabus code or the IB subject and level, taken from the entry form rather than the report. The school's own coursework deadline dates for this term. The last two pieces of marked work, including the one that went badly. And the bus arrival time, which sets the slot. With those, the diagnostic hour can be spent on diagnosis rather than on collecting information, and you get a written assessment, a named tutor who teaches that specification, the rate and a review date.

dubai/dubai-silicon-oasis.closingHeading: Set the slot first, then choose the subject
dubai/dubai-silicon-oasis.closingBody: The order most families use is to pick a subject, book a tutor and then try to find an hour. In a Silicon Oasis week that order fails. Start from the hour: tell us when your child actually gets home, how many sessions this household can protect for a whole term, and which two subjects show a specific, fixable failure in the marked work. Send the syllabus code, the school's deadline dates and the last marked paper. You will get a written diagnostic, a named tutor teaching that specification, the rate in AED, the tutor's base and time zone, and a review date six to eight weeks out. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video.

dubai/dubai-south.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB and IGCSE subjects to students across Dubai South, Expo City and the Jebel Ali corridor. Each arrangement is planned around the published dates for the series your child is actually entered for, because an entry deadline four months before a paper is the thing that decides what is still possible.

intro.heading: A young community, a thin school map, and a calendar nobody counts backwards
paragraphs: Dubai South is a district built around an airport and an Expo site, and its residential population has arrived faster than its schools. The Residential District, the Golf District, MAG 5 Boulevard, The Pulse and Expo City now house a substantial number of families, and the nearest established school provision sits outside the district, in Dubai Investments Park, Jebel Ali, Al Furjan, The Sustainable City and on the Remraam edge. Dubai's private sector is expanding to meet exactly this kind of demand, with the 2026-27 intake adding seven new private schools and 16,846 places, but the arithmetic has not caught up yet.

That has two practical consequences, and neither is about traffic. The first is subject availability. Where a nearby school runs a small Diploma cohort, Higher Level choice narrows, and a student who wants Higher Level Physics and Higher Level Economics in the same timetable may not be able to have both. The second is the shift pattern. The free zone, the logistics district and the airport run around the clock, and family evenings here start later and less predictably than the Dubai average.

Those two constraints are why this page is organised around the exam calendar rather than around the neighbourhood. If a family may change school, change emirate or sit a subject as a private candidate, the governing facts are entry deadlines and session windows, not geography. Cambridge final entries for a March series fall months before the papers. Forecast grades fall weeks before them. Pearson publishes provisional timetables that can be revised. A plan built forwards from today misses all of that; a plan built backwards from the published dates does not.

One thing this page deliberately does not contain is an IB exam date. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Secondary sources converge on a window, and we are not publishing it, because a date on a page like this one becomes something families plan around. Confirm every IB date with your school's Diploma coordinator or with the IB directly. We will write about the May session as the one UAE schools sit, and leave the dates to the source that owns them.

What follows is the calendar counted backwards, the two examination boards' published session structures side by side, what private candidate entry actually involves, the school map around Dubai South with its curriculum and regulator for each, how a two-year Diploma gets planned from a community with one nearby IB school, and the limits on what we can honestly offer. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE.
