dubai/dubai-south.programmesIntro: The four routes below are read here through the calendar: what each one locks in, and when. That is the information a family in a fast-changing catchment needs most, because it tells you when a decision stops being reversible.

programmes.name: Cambridge International IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Subjects are tiered Core or Extended in many cases, and the tier is fixed at entry. Final entries fall months before the papers, which is the single most under-appreciated fact in the whole process.
programmes.countryNote: Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and the board states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. For a family that has just moved into Dubai South from another country, that is the detail most likely to go wrong.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson International GCSE examinations are available in May and June and in November each year. The structure of papers, the formula provision and the assessment of practical skills differ from Cambridge, and a student sitting both boards across their subject set needs two distinct sets of exam habits rather than one.
programmes.countryNote: The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which can be revised, so always work from the live official document.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internal Assessment deadlines are set internally by each school, not by the IB, which is why two students in neighbouring communities can be working to deadlines weeks apart. The May session is the one UAE schools sit, with a November session also available.
programmes.countryNote: No IB session or results date appears on this page. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so nothing could be verified at source, and publishing an unconfirmed date on a page families plan around would be irresponsible. Ask your school's Diploma coordinator for the current dates and treat their answer as authoritative over anything on the open web.

programmes.name: Private candidate entry
programmes.ageRange: Any age, outside a school's own entry
programmes.description: A route for a student whose school does not offer a subject, who is repeating a paper, or who is between schools. Entry is made through an approved examination centre rather than through a tutor, fees are set by the board and the centre, and the student is responsible for meeting the entry deadline and sitting the correct zone timetable.
programmes.countryNote: This matters more in Dubai South than in older districts, because thin local provision means more students want a subject their school cannot timetable. A tutor can teach the syllabus; a tutor cannot enter a candidate, and any provider implying otherwise has misunderstood the process. Find the centre first, confirm the deadline, then build the teaching plan.

dubai/dubai-south.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones most often requested by families in this catchment, and the notes concentrate on how each behaves against a session deadline, since that is the organising question on this page.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE)
subjects.description: The tier decision is fixed at entry, which makes it a calendar decision as much as an academic one. Extended-tier fluency is built over months rather than weeks, so a student aiming to move tier needs the diagnostic done well before the entry deadline, not after mocks.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: Practical-skills assessment differs between boards, and a student changing school mid-course can find the format changed under them. The topics where marks go missing, electricity above all, are narrow enough to target inside a six-week block before a session.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: Multi-step calculation discipline is the highest-return work close to a session, because method marks are available and routinely unclaimed. Diploma students working to an internal Internal Assessment deadline need that date before anything else is planned.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: The volume of content makes it a poor subject to leave late, and a good one for a long run of short weekly sessions. Six-mark explain answers built to the mark scheme shape are the technique that matters in the final term.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level Paper 3 is an unstructured investigative paper, and the skill it tests, sustaining written reasoning, needs months rather than a revision block. Students in small Diploma cohorts often have fewer classmates to compare working with, which is where one-to-one helps.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries make up the Internal Assessment and need real published articles, so the planning deadline is set by the school and not by the student. Diagram accuracy and evaluation are the marks; description is where students spend their time.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language and English First Language
subjects.description: Worth starting earliest of any subject, because every other paper is marked through written English and the gains take longest to accumulate. Also the subject where a student arriving mid-course from another system gains most quickly.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The pre-released case material rewards structured work months ahead of the papers, which makes it unusually calendar-sensitive. Students who start the case late write knowledgeable answers with no evaluation in them.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The Diploma solution-development project has an internal school deadline and carries documentation marks that students treat as paperwork. Pseudocode and trace-table discipline at IGCSE is quick to teach and quick to lose.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.description: Required in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs. Support follows the school's own scheme, because the Ministry prohibits different or additional content without prior permission.

dubai/dubai-south.regionsIntro: Dubai South is a set of districts rather than a neighbourhood, and the differences between them are about working patterns and distance to the nearest school rather than about housing style.

regions.name: Residential District
regions.note: The largest concentration of families, with most children travelling to Jebel Ali, Dubai Investments Park or Al Furjan. An IGCSE tutor in Dubai South usually starts here at six in the evening or later, after the longest school runs in the corridor.

regions.name: Expo City
regions.note: A newer population with a high share of international postings and short tenancies. Enquiries here are often about moving mid-course, and the first question is always the receiving school's internal assessment calendar rather than the subject.

regions.name: The Pulse and MAG 5 Boulevard
regions.note: Apartment living with tight budgets and long commutes. This is where the one-hour-a-week decision is made most often, and where an evening slot after seven is routine rather than exceptional.

regions.name: Golf District and Emaar South
regions.note: Townhouse and villa stock, still filling. An IB tutor in Emaar South is frequently working with a student in a small Diploma cohort where the school could not timetable a preferred Higher Level combination.

regions.name: Aviation and Logistics Districts
regions.note: Shift work around the clock, which is the single biggest scheduling constraint in this catchment. Because lessons are over live video, a slot at half past eight in the evening costs nothing extra and is often the only one that works.

regions.name: Jebel Ali and Dubai Investments Park
regions.note: Where most Dubai South secondary students actually sit. An IB DP tutor in Jebel Ali often picks up subjects a nearby school could not offer, taught alongside the student's school timetable rather than instead of it.

regions.name: The Sustainable City and Remraam edge
regions.note: The nearest IB continuum provision and the nearest British secondary school respectively. IGCSE tuition in Remraam tends to be booked around the Cambridge entry deadline, once the tier decision becomes real.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai Investments Park, Green Community and The Sustainable City
schoolClusters.note: The nearest established provision to Dubai South and the location of the two closest IB continuum schools. Diploma cohorts here are smaller than in central Dubai, which shows up as narrower Higher Level subject choice rather than as weaker teaching, and it is the single most common reason a Dubai South family asks for a subject tutor.

schoolClusters.city: Jebel Ali, Al Furjan and the Remraam edge
schoolClusters.note: Where most of the district's British-curriculum students travel. These are larger cohorts with broader IGCSE offers, and the requests that come from them are more often about a specific weak topic than about availability. The school run from the Residential District to this cluster is the longest in the corridor.

modes.description: A block planned from the published exam window and entry deadline rather than from today. The first session establishes what is already locked, what is still reversible and how many weeks remain, and the block closes on a date fixed at the start. This is the default for any student within six months of a series.

sections.heading: The exam calendar counted backwards, using Cambridge's own published dates
paragraphs: Almost every family plans forwards. They look at today, estimate how many weeks remain, and distribute revision across them. Examination boards work in the opposite direction, and their deadlines sit much earlier than parents expect. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series put the examination period at 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due on 27 November 2026 and forecast grades due on 27 February 2027. Results appear on the board's direct service on 13 May and certificates in late June.

Read that sequence and a plan writes itself. The subject and tier decisions are effectively locked at the final entry deadline in November, which is before most schools have finished their first mock cycle. That means a student hoping to move from Core to Extended tier needs the diagnostic conversation in September or October, not after January mocks. By the forecast-grade deadline in February the school needs enough marked evidence to forecast fairly, which makes the autumn's marked work matter for something beyond practice.

The table sets the sequence out with the owner of each date named, because that is the part families get wrong. Some of these dates belong to the board and cannot move. Others belong to the school and vary between schools in the same emirate. Mock windows, coursework deadlines and internal submission dates are school decisions, which is why the first useful document in any plan is the receiving school's own internal assessment calendar rather than anything published by a board.

sections.heading: Cambridge and Pearson sessions side by side, and the IB dates we will not publish
paragraphs: A student in this catchment may sit papers with both boards in the same year, and the two behave differently. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for IGCSE, O Level and International A Level, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May and June and in November each year. The structures are similar enough to blur and different enough to matter.

Two published details are worth memorising. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, and those can be revised, which is why any date on a page like this one should be treated as a worked example rather than as the live document.

For the International Baccalaureate this page publishes no date at all. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, so nothing could be confirmed at source. Secondary sources agree on a window and we are not repeating it, because a date published here becomes a date a family plans around. The May session is the one UAE schools sit, a November session also exists, and your school's Diploma coordinator holds the current dates. That is a less satisfying answer than a table of dates and it is the only honest one available.

sections.heading: Private candidate entry, and what it means when the school cannot offer a subject
paragraphs: In an older district this section would be a footnote. In Dubai South it is not, because thin local provision means a meaningful number of students want a subject their nearest school cannot timetable. A small Diploma cohort cannot run eight Higher Level options, and a British school with one set per subject cannot always build a timetable that allows a particular pair. The student's choices are then to drop the subject, change school, or sit it outside the school's own entry.

The third route works and it has rules. Entry is made through an approved examination centre, not through a tutor and not through a platform. Fees are set by the board and the centre. The candidate is responsible for meeting the entry deadline and for sitting the paper on the correct zone timetable, which is exactly the point at which Cambridge's own warning about zone versions becomes relevant. The order of operations matters: find the centre and confirm the deadline first, then build the teaching plan backwards from the session.

What a tutor does in this arrangement is teach the syllabus across the available months, alongside the student's school timetable rather than instead of it. That is a long commitment, usually a year or more, and it needs an honest conversation at the start about workload, because a student adding a subject to a full timetable is adding real hours. What a tutor cannot do is enter the candidate, obtain their results, or influence a centre's decisions. Any provider suggesting otherwise has misdescribed a process it does not control.

sections.heading: The school map around Dubai South, with curriculum and regulator
paragraphs: Dubai South's own school provision is young, so the practical map is the ring of schools around it. The table below lists the ones that come up most often in enquiries from this catchment, with the area, the curriculum and board, the programmes offered and the regulator. There is deliberately no inspection-rating column. Ratings should only be published where they have been read on the regulator's own site, and none were read for this page; a competitor's school table ships that column empty on every row, which is worse than omitting it.

Read the programmes column carefully if you have a Diploma student. Two of the nearest schools run an IB continuum, which means a child can move from the Primary Years Programme through the Middle Years Programme to the Diploma without changing systems. The rest run British routes to IGCSE and then A Level, which is a different two-year decision at sixteen. Choosing between those two paths is a bigger decision than choosing between two schools on the same path, and it is worth making before Year 9 rather than during Year 11.

The regulator column is uniform here because every school listed sits in Dubai and is therefore regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. That changes the moment a family moves emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are governed by the Department of Education and Knowledge, Sharjah by its own Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the federal Ministry of Education.

sections.heading: Who lives here, and when the evening actually starts
paragraphs: The Aviation and Logistics Districts and the free zone operate around the clock, and a significant share of households in the Residential District, The Pulse and MAG 5 Boulevard are built around a rota rather than around a nine-to-five. That changes the tutoring question in a way that no amount of pedagogy addresses. An arrangement requiring a lesson at five in the afternoon, with a parent present, does not survive a rota change. An arrangement at half past eight, with a written summary a parent reads at eleven, does.

The Expo City and Golf District populations are different again: more international postings, shorter tenancies, more mid-course arrivals. For them the organising fact is the receiving school's internal assessment calendar, because a child who arrives in January is landing inside somebody else's timetable of mock windows and coursework deadlines. Asking for that document in the first week saves a term of guessing, and schools generally supply it when asked directly by a subject teacher rather than through the office.

The third pattern is the long school run. From the Residential District to the Jebel Ali cluster is the longest regular journey in this corridor, and a child who leaves before seven in the morning and gets back after four thirty has already had a longer day than a child in central Dubai. That is an argument for shorter, more frequent sessions rather than one long weekly hour, and for not scheduling anything demanding on a Thursday.

sections.heading: Planning a two-year Diploma when the nearest cohort is small
paragraphs: A small Diploma cohort is not a weak one. What it is, reliably, is narrow. A school with twenty Diploma students cannot run every Higher Level option, cannot always build a timetable that allows a particular pair of Higher Levels, and will have one teacher per subject rather than three. That last point is the one families underestimate: in a large cohort a student who does not get on with one teaching style has alternatives, and in a small one they do not.

The planning response is to decide the subject combination against the university destination before the school's option blocks are published, rather than after. If a medicine application is likely, Higher Level Chemistry is usually required and Higher Level Biology often expected, and those two have to be available together. If an engineering route is likely, the Mathematics choice between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation matters more than most students realise, because a number of universities state a preference. Check the specific universities rather than the general reputation of each course.

Where the timetable genuinely cannot deliver the combination, the options are to change school, to accept a substitution, or to sit a subject outside the school's entry as a private candidate. All three are real and all three have costs. What makes the decision tractable is doing it in Year 11, with the option blocks and the university requirements side by side, rather than in the second term of the first Diploma year when a change means repeating work. A tutor can help teach a subject the school cannot offer; nobody can retrospectively widen an option block.
bullets: Small cohorts mean narrow Higher Level choice and one teacher per subject
Decide the combination against named university requirements, not general reputation

sections.heading: Honest limits: coverage, permits and assessed work
paragraphs: Three disclosures belong on a page like this one. The first is coverage. There are slots and subject combinations for which no suitable specialist is free, most often narrow Higher Level pairings in the weeks before the May session, and the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education streams, where schools follow a prescribed scheme and must ensure their own teachers of those subjects hold the appropriate KHDA approval. When that happens we say so and offer an alternative with its limits stated, rather than quietly supplying a near match.

The second is the permit position. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the Ministry's app, website and e-services system with a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so this page quotes no figure. Where a tutor teaches from outside the UAE over live video, that permit does not apply to them, and the right question becomes what they have taught and at what level.

The third is assessed work. A tutor may teach research skills, read assessment criteria aloud, challenge a research question, question a draft and show that a conclusion is not supported by the evidence. A tutor may not supply text for an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or Personal Project. The candidate carries the consequence of malpractice, which can reach the loss of the subject or the whole Diploma, and the school is obliged to report it. At least one page competing for these searches sells completed assessed work, and the fee is the only thing that provider has at risk.

sections.heading: Starting from Dubai South
paragraphs: Send three things and the first conversation is immediately useful: the school with the year group, the board and syllabus code for each subject in question, and the school's internal assessment calendar. If your child has already sat a mock, a marked script is worth more than all three, because it shows whether marks are going on content, on command terms, on timing or on working a marker cannot follow.

We then establish the session your child is entered for and count backwards from the published dates. That single step changes most plans, because it usually reveals that the subject and tier decisions are closer to being locked than the family assumed, and that the autumn's marked work matters for the forecast grade rather than only for practice. Teaching is planned inside whatever weeks remain, with a trial lesson and a consultation first and the terms written down before any block starts.

If the arrangement needs to sit late in the evening, it can. Because lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, a slot at half past eight is as available as one at half past four, consecutive slots can cover two children or two subjects in one evening, and a written summary after each session means a parent on shift can read what happened without having been in the room. In this district that flexibility is usually the deciding factor, and it is the reason we do not run an in-home service anywhere in the UAE.

process.title: Identify the series, not just the year
process.description: Which board, which session, and whether the entry has already been made. The answer determines what is still reversible. A tier decision after a final entry deadline is not a decision, and knowing that early changes the plan completely.

process.title: Get the school's internal calendar
process.description: Mock windows, coursework deadlines and internal submission dates are set by the school, not the board, and they differ between schools in the same emirate. That document governs what is achievable this term more than any published exam date.

process.title: Count the weeks backwards
process.description: From the published exam window to the forecast-grade deadline to the entry deadline to today. The number of usable weeks is almost always smaller than a family expects, and seeing it written down ends most arguments about intensity.

process.title: Confirm the centre if it is a private entry
process.description: Where a subject sits outside the school's own entry, the examination centre and its deadline come first and the teaching plan second. We teach the syllabus; the centre enters the candidate and sets the fee.

process.title: Place the slot where the rota allows
process.description: Late evening, weekend morning, or consecutive slots in a single evening. Because nobody is travelling, the slot can follow the household rather than the other way round, and it can move when a rota changes.

whyPoints.title: Planned from published dates
whyPoints.description: Cambridge's March 2027 key dates and Pearson's published session structure are on this page with their sources named. Of the pages competing for these searches, none names a session, an entry deadline or a results date at all.

whyPoints.title: No unverified IB dates
whyPoints.description: The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so nothing could be confirmed at source and nothing is published here. A date on a page families plan around has to be verified, and saying so is more useful than a confident guess.

whyPoints.title: Built for a thin school map
whyPoints.description: Where a nearby cohort is small, the problem is narrow Higher Level choice rather than weak teaching. We can teach a subject a school cannot timetable, alongside the school timetable, with the examination centre identified first.

whyPoints.title: Slots that survive a rota
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video, so a half past eight start is ordinary, consecutive slots cover two children in one evening, and a written summary lets a parent on shift read what happened afterwards.

whyPoints.title: No invented inspection ratings
whyPoints.description: The school table on this page carries curriculum, programmes and regulator, and no rating column, because none was read from the regulator's own site. A competitor's version ships that column empty on every row.

whyPoints.title: Limits stated before you book
whyPoints.description: No home visits in the UAE, no UAE premises, no regulator or board accreditation, no supplied text for assessed work, and a plain statement when no specialist is free in the slot you need.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE exams actually held, and when do entries close?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Its published key dates for the March 2027 series put the examination period at 3 February to 4 March 2027, with final entries due 27 November 2026 and forecast grades due 27 February 2027. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations run in May and June and in November, and the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Always work from the live official timetable, since provisional versions can be revised.

faqs.question: Why might my child's exam timetable differ from a cousin's in another country?
faqs.answer: Because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and each zone has its own version of the timetable. The board states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. For a family that has recently moved into Dubai South from elsewhere, this is the single most likely administrative error, because the natural instinct is to use the timetable a relative or a previous school sent. Ask your centre which zone it is in and work only from that document.

faqs.question: Can my child sit an IGCSE subject their school near Dubai South does not offer?
faqs.answer: Yes, as a private candidate through an approved examination centre. That is more common in this catchment than in older districts, because smaller nearby cohorts cannot timetable every option. The order of operations matters: identify the centre and confirm its entry deadline and administrative zone first, then build the teaching plan backwards from the session. A tutor can teach the syllabus alongside the school timetable, usually across a year or more. A tutor cannot enter a candidate, obtain results or influence a centre, and fees are set by the board and the centre rather than by anyone teaching.

faqs.question: Which schools are nearest to Dubai South for an IB Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Greenfield International School in Dubai Investments Park and Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City are the two nearest IB continuum routes, both regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. Sunmarke School in Al Furjan offers a British route with post-sixteen Diploma provision. The practical consideration is cohort size rather than quality: a smaller Diploma group means narrower Higher Level choice and one teacher per subject rather than several. Check the published option blocks against the universities your child is likely to apply to before Year 11 ends. IB Gram has no affiliation with any school named here.

faqs.question: When should we start preparing for a February or March examination series?
faqs.answer: Earlier than feels necessary, because the decisions close before the papers. For the Cambridge March 2027 series, final entries are due 27 November 2026, which means the subject and tier decisions are effectively locked more than two months before the first paper. A student hoping to move from Core to Extended tier needs that diagnostic in September or October. Once entries are in, the useful work is timed papers marked against the official wording rather than another pass through content, and the forecast-grade deadline of 27 February 2027 makes the autumn's marked work count for something real.

faqs.question: Why will you not tell me the IB exam dates for next May?
faqs.answer: Because we could not verify them from the IB. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, so no session or results date in this project was confirmed at source. Secondary sources converge on a window, and repeating it here would turn an unverified figure into something families plan around, which is exactly how wrong dates spread. What we can say is that the May session is the one UAE schools sit and that a November session also exists. Your school's Diploma coordinator holds the current dates and should be treated as authoritative over anything on the open web.

faqs.question: What does a forecast grade deadline mean for us?
faqs.answer: It means the school has to submit a predicted outcome to the board by a fixed date, and for the Cambridge March 2027 series that date is 27 February 2027. The school can only forecast from evidence it holds, which is marked classwork, coursework and mock papers. The practical consequence is that the autumn's marked work is not just practice; it is the evidence base for a figure that goes to the board and, in many cases, informs university conversations. A student who improves after the deadline has improved for the examination, which is what matters most, but the forecast will not reflect it.

faqs.question: How late can a tutoring session start for a family working airport shifts?
faqs.answer: Later than most people assume. Because lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, a slot at half past eight in the evening is as available as one at half past four, and it can move within the week when a rota changes. A written summary goes to the parent after each session, so somebody on shift can read what happened at eleven at night rather than needing to be in the room at six. For the Aviation and Logistics Districts this is usually the deciding factor, and it is one of the reasons IB Gram does not run an in-home service anywhere in the UAE.

faqs.question: Does Dubai South have enough school places for a community growing this fast?
faqs.answer: The supply is increasing but the nearest established provision still sits outside the district, in Dubai Investments Park, Jebel Ali, Al Furjan, The Sustainable City and on the Remraam edge. Dubai's private sector is expanding: the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent. For a family here the practical effect today is a long school run and narrower Higher Level choice, both of which are planning constraints rather than quality judgements.

faqs.question: Is a November resit series worth taking?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and the decision should be made with the published dates in front of you. Both Cambridge and Pearson run a November series, and Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which gives a sense of the turnaround. The arguments for are a fresh grade on the certificate and a short, focused preparation window. The arguments against are the overlap with the next year's coursework and the risk of splitting attention. Decide on the basis of whether the marked script from the first attempt shows a recoverable, specific loss rather than a general shortfall.

faqs.question: What happens to our plan if we move emirate midway through Year 11?
faqs.answer: Two things change. The regulator changes: Dubai is governed by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain by the Department of Education and Knowledge, Sharjah by its Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the federal Ministry of Education. The examination position may also change, because entries are made by the centre and the new school may use a different board or a different administrative zone. Ask the receiving school immediately whether your child's entries transfer or need remaking, and check the deadline.

faqs.question: How do we plan a Diploma when the nearest school has a small cohort?
faqs.answer: Decide the subject combination against named university requirements before the option blocks are published, not after. A small cohort usually cannot run every Higher Level option or allow every pairing, and it will have one teacher per subject rather than several. If a medicine route is likely, check that Higher Level Chemistry and Biology are available together. If engineering is likely, check each target university's stated preference between Mathematics Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation. Where the timetable cannot deliver, the realistic options are changing school, accepting a substitution, or private candidate entry alongside school.

faqs.question: When do Pearson Edexcel results reach students?
faqs.answer: On the board's published examples, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, and those can be revised, so the live official document is the one to work from rather than any date restated on a third-party page. If results matter for a university deadline, check the published release date against that deadline early, because a gap of a single week can decide an application.

faqs.question: Are there entry fees we should budget for as a private candidate?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they are set by the examination board and the centre rather than by any tutor. Budget them separately from tuition and confirm them with the centre in writing before committing to the route, along with the entry deadline and the centre's administrative zone. The common error is to budget the teaching and discover the entry cost late, which turns a planned decision into a rushed one. No tutoring provider should be collecting entry fees on a centre's behalf, and if one offers to, that is a reason to ask more questions rather than fewer.

faqs.question: How far ahead should we book a specialist before the May session?
faqs.answer: Earlier than price alone suggests, because the constraint close to a session is availability rather than cost. The specialists who teach narrow Higher Level combinations fill first, and no budget creates a slot that does not exist. For a May session, a conversation in the autumn is comfortable, in January workable, and in March limited to whoever happens to be free. If you are reading this inside six weeks of the papers, the useful plan is a short block of timed-paper technique on two named topics rather than a search for the ideal specialist.

dubai/dubai-south.closingHeading: Count the weeks backwards before you book anything
dubai/dubai-south.closingBody: The most useful thing a family in this catchment can do is write down four dates: the entry deadline, the school's mock window, the forecast-grade deadline and the examination window itself. For the Cambridge March 2027 series three of those are published and one belongs to your school. Once they are on paper, how much tutoring is worth buying and what it should be spent on become straightforward questions rather than anxious ones. Send us the school, the board and the codes, and the school's internal calendar, and we will count the weeks with you. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, at a time your rota allows.

dubai/dubai-sports-city.tutorsIntro: The profiles below reflect what Sports City households book: IGCSE Mathematics and the sciences, Diploma Higher Level subjects, Sports, Exercise and Health Science, and short recovery blocks after a competition absence. Each tutor teaches a named specification.

intro.heading: A community where the timetable belongs to somebody else
paragraphs: Dubai Sports City is one of the few residential communities in the emirate organised around facilities rather than around housing. Cricket, football and golf academies sit inside it, the stadium and training grounds define its geography, and a meaningful proportion of the children living here train seriously - several evenings a week, with weekend fixtures and a competition calendar set by somebody who has never heard of the Cambridge entry deadline.

That produces a tutoring problem with a different shape from anywhere else in Dubai. In most communities the obstacle is a school run and a tired evening. Here the obstacle is a fixed external schedule that does not negotiate: training is at six, the squad session is on Saturday, the tournament is the second week of March. A tutoring plan that assumes a free weekday evening has already failed, and so has one that assumes twenty uninterrupted weeks.

The household mix is also wider than the name suggests. Sports City contains apartment towers with families who have nothing to do with sport, the Victory Heights villas next door, staff households attached to the academies, and families who relocated specifically for a training programme. Those four groups ask for different things, and the third and fourth are the ones most poorly served by a standard area page, because the standard advice assumes a schedule they do not have.

There is a second problem specific to the serious athlete, which is absence. A student who misses a fortnight for a tournament has not missed a fortnight of content; they have missed a fortnight of content plus the practice that would have consolidated it, plus whatever coursework checkpoint fell in that window. Recovering it by doubling up on return rarely works, because the returning student is also tired. It needs a plan made before the absence, not after.

On delivery: lessons run one-to-one over live video with screen sharing. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. For a family in this community that is not a limitation but the single feature that makes continuity possible - a session can run from a hotel room in another country, at a time that works for a tutor in a third, which no visiting tutor can offer.

No figure on this page is an IB Gram price; the rates quoted are market rates with the provider that published each named. Nothing here promises a grade, and nothing here suggests that sport and academic work are in opposition. The point of the sections below is that both can be planned properly at the same time, provided the plan is built around the schedule that already exists.

dubai/dubai-sports-city.programmesIntro: Four programmes run through this community, and the note under each describes how it behaves for a student whose week is already committed - which is the information a training household actually needs.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years of specification-led courses examined at the end of Year 11, with the syllabus code deciding the papers, the tiering and the formula sheet. Eight or nine subjects run simultaneously, so the course is unusually unforgiving of absence: a fortnight away touches every subject at once rather than one.
programmes.countryNote: For a Sports City student with a competition calendar, the decision that matters is the option block. A set of eight subjects with three coursework components is far harder to recover after an absence than a set with one, and that is a Year 9 decision rather than something to manage in Year 11.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internally assessed work in every subject is marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB. The coursework clustering is the problem for an athlete: several immovable school deadlines falling in the same weeks as a competition block.
programmes.countryNote: CAS is the one part of the Diploma a serious athlete finds straightforward, since sustained sporting commitment maps onto it naturally. The Extended Essay is the hard part, because it needs sustained independent writing time in exactly the terms when training volume is highest, and it cannot be done in fragments.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject group, each marked out of eight and converted to a 1-7 grade, with no external papers until optional eAssessment at the end of Year 11. Because marks come from interim tasks spread across the year, a missed window can mean a missing criterion score rather than a missed lesson.
programmes.countryNote: This is the stage where an absence does most hidden damage for a training household, because a student away during the week a criterion is assessed may simply have no mark for it. Ask the school in advance which criteria are being assessed when, and plan the absence around the assessment calendar.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units with outcome-based reporting rather than marks, and no public examinations. Reading fluency, number-fact recall and written stamina are what matter, and they are built by habit rather than by catch-up. Short, frequent work suits a child who already trains several times a week.
programmes.countryNote: Primary-age athletes in this community are often the most tired children in Dubai by seven in the evening. Twenty-five minutes before training, or on a non-training afternoon, achieves more than an hour after it, and parents consistently underestimate how much the training load costs a nine-year-old's attention.

dubai/dubai-sports-city.subjectsIntro: Below are the subjects Sports City families ask for most, including the two sporting subjects that are frequently treated as soft options and are not. Each note says what is assessed and where marks are lost.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: A full Diploma science subject with external papers and an internally assessed investigation, covering anatomy, exercise physiology, biomechanics and skill acquisition. Students arrive expecting their sporting knowledge to carry them and find the physiology and data-handling demands are those of any other science.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physical Education
subjects.description: A written theory paper on anatomy, physiology, training principles and psychology, plus assessed practical performance and analysis. The theory paper is where grades are decided and where sporting students are most complacent, because being good at a sport is not the same as explaining it in the examiner's terms.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The usual pairing for students heading towards physiotherapy, sports science or medicine. Content volume invites rereading, which achieves little; grades turn on terminology precision and on answering the command term that was actually used.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Required for most medical, pharmacy and physiotherapy-adjacent routes. Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the Higher Level papers, and the internally assessed investigation loses marks on uncertainty handling rather than on chemistry.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: The subject that suffers most visibly from absence, because the content is cumulative: two missed weeks in Year 10 can still be causing losses in Year 11. The tier decision caps the grade, so check it before planning any recovery work.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof and calculus are the Higher Level pressure points. The exploration needs sustained uninterrupted time, which makes it the single hardest Diploma component to fit around a competition season and the one to schedule into an off-season block.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and graphical-calculator work, and the route many sporting students find more natural because the data is real. Interpretation carries marks students expect for the calculation alone, which is the recurring loss.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Biomechanics makes this attractive to athletes, and the mechanics content genuinely rewards an intuitive feel for forces. The loss is algebraic rather than conceptual, and the data-analysis component is barely practised outside the lessons spent setting up the investigation.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A common choice for students interested in sports administration and management. The tools are quick to learn; applying them to an unfamiliar case study under timing is not, and students describe organisations when the question asked them to evaluate a decision.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Popular with students who have encountered sports psychology in their own training. The subject is methodologically demanding in a way the applied version is not, and tutor supply is thinner than for the core sciences, so book earlier.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen analysis under timing, which rewards a repeatable procedure rather than wider reading - useful for a student whose reading time is limited. The Individual Oral needs preparation that cannot be compressed into the week before.

sections.heading: Who lives in Sports City, and what each household actually asks for
paragraphs: The direct answer is that this community holds four quite different groups, and only one of them is the family everybody assumes. There are apartment households with no connection to sport, who ask the ordinary questions about marks and slots. There are the Victory Heights villa families, larger and more often running several children through one evening. There are academy staff households. And there are families who moved to Dubai specifically for a training programme, who are often the most academically anxious of the four.

That last group deserves separate treatment because their position is genuinely difficult. A family that relocated for a sporting pathway has made a decision with an uncertain outcome, and the academic record is the part of the plan that has to work regardless. They are frequently managing a child who trains more than their peers, sleeps less, travels more, and is sitting the same examinations on the same days as everyone else. Reassurance is not useful to them. A workable schedule is.

The apartment and villa split matters too, in a less dramatic way. Apartment households here are often two working parents with one or two children and a tight evening; villa households more often have three or four children and an arrival spread of two hours. The first needs a well-placed single slot; the second needs a stagger. Treating them the same is the commonest planning error in this community.

The table maps the four groups against what helps most. One pattern runs through all of them: the first thing to collect is the schedule that cannot move - training times, fixture days, travel dates, school assessment windows - and only then decide what tutoring goes where. Most plans are built in the opposite order and then fail when the immovable thing moves everything else.

sections.heading: Training load and study load in the same week
paragraphs: Twelve hours of training a week is not twelve hours taken out of a study timetable. It is twelve hours plus travel to and from the facility plus the recovery cost, and the recovery cost is the part families underestimate. A fourteen-year-old who finishes a hard session at eight has perhaps forty minutes of low-quality attention left. Scheduling demanding academic work into that window produces attendance rather than learning, and it slowly convinces the student they are bad at the subject.

The practical response is to stop treating the evening as uniform. Each student has one or two genuinely productive windows in a day, and for an athlete those windows are usually before training or on a clear afternoon rather than after a session. Finding them and defending them is worth more than adding hours. A thirty-minute session in a good window beats ninety minutes in a bad one, consistently and measurably.

The second response is to change the shape of the work rather than the amount. Drill-shaped material - number facts, moles calculations, vocabulary, command terms, calculator technique - survives a short tired session reasonably well. Sustained material - an exploration, an Extended Essay, a full timed paper - does not, and should be placed in the off-season, on a clear weekend, or in a school holiday. Mismatching the work to the window is why many athlete study plans produce so little.

The table sets out the common training patterns with a study pattern that fits each. These are operational recommendations from scheduling students with heavy commitments rather than published research, and they will need adjusting for your child. Send the training schedule along with the school arrival time and the plan can be built from both instead of from one.

sections.heading: A fortnight away for a tournament: the recovery that works
paragraphs: A student who misses two weeks has missed three things, not one. The content taught in those weeks. The practice that would have consolidated it. And whatever assessment or coursework checkpoint fell inside the window, which in the Middle Years Programme can mean a criterion with no mark against it at all. Treating the absence as a content gap and catching up on notes addresses the smallest of the three.

The recovery plan that works is made before the absence. Two or three weeks ahead, ask the school for three things in writing: what will be taught in each subject during the window, what will be assessed, and what the deadlines are for anything due in that period. With those, the student can pre-learn the cumulative subjects - Mathematics first, because it is the one where a two-week hole keeps causing losses a year later - and submit or pre-agree anything with a deadline.

During the absence, the realistic aim is maintenance in one or two subjects, not coverage in eight. Thirty minutes every second day on Mathematics, plus reading for an essay subject, keeps the cumulative damage small. Trying to keep eight subjects running from a hotel room fails and leaves the student feeling they have failed, which is the worst outcome of the three available.

On return, the mistake is doubling up. A student coming back from a competition block is physically and mentally tired, and a fortnight of double sessions produces a second dip. A better sequence is one diagnostic session to establish what is actually missing, then a focused block on the cumulative subject only, with the non-cumulative subjects picked up through normal class teaching. Written out in advance, that recovery takes three to four weeks rather than a term.
bullets: Ask the school in writing what will be taught, assessed and due in the window

sections.heading: Sports subjects as academic subjects
paragraphs: Two courses in this space get consistently misjudged in both directions. Students pick them expecting their sporting knowledge to carry them, and some parents worry they will be seen as soft. Both views are wrong. IGCSE Physical Education and the Diploma's Sports, Exercise and Health Science are examined academic courses with anatomy, physiology, biomechanics and data handling in them, and the written papers are where grades are decided.

The specific trap for an athlete is that the subject is familiar in the wrong register. A competitive swimmer knows a great deal about training principles in practice, and almost none of it is phrased the way an examiner requires. The gap between knowing how a periodised training block feels and being able to explain adaptation in the terms the mark scheme wants is exactly the gap a tutor closes, and it is wider than students expect.

The second trap is the practical or coursework component, which looks like free marks. Assessed practical performance is marked against criteria, and analysis of performance is a written task with its own requirements. Being excellent at the sport contributes but does not complete it. Students who leave the analysis to the last week routinely lose marks they had already earned on the field.

The table sets out what each course assesses and where marks go missing. Confirm the exact components and weightings against the current syllabus or subject guide for your child's cohort, which the school can supply, since both the Cambridge syllabus and the IB subject guides are revised on a cycle. On the broader question: a sports subject taken seriously and well sits perfectly alongside sciences and mathematics, and what a university programme cares about is its own published prerequisite rather than a general impression.

sections.heading: Apartment families and villa families: two different requests
paragraphs: It is worth separating these explicitly, because the same page serves both and the right answer differs. An apartment household in Sports City is typically two working parents with one or two children, a short local school run, and one usable evening slot that has to carry everything. A Victory Heights villa household is more often three or four children, several schools, and an arrival spread approaching two hours.

For the apartment household the task is placement. There is one good window, it needs identifying precisely, and it needs defending against everything else that wants it. The practical answer is usually a single weekly slot timed from the child's actual arrival with one named fallback time for the weeks it collapses - and a clear decision about which subject gets it, since there is only one.

For the villa household the task is sequencing. Several children cannot share a window, and the best hour of the evening should go deliberately to whoever has the nearest public examination rather than by default to the loudest. The pattern that holds is youngest first and earliest, protected hour to the nearest deadline, latest arrival moved to a weekend block. One household fallback slot works better than one per child.

Both households benefit from the same underlying feature, which is that online delivery decouples the number of sessions from the number of tutors who can physically attend. A single visiting tutor can serve one slot and one stage. Three children at three stages can each have a specialist at a different hour only when nothing has to travel, which is the practical reason this community's schedules work better online than they look on paper.

sections.heading: What the market charges, and what flexibility is worth asking about
paragraphs: Rates in this market span roughly an order of magnitude and the spread reflects what is being sold. At the lower end, homework supervision and content recap. In the middle, a qualified subject tutor teaching a named specification. At the upper end, specialists in a particular paper, and above them providers selling scarcity. The figures below were read from provider listings and a published Dubai rate survey in October 2026, and they describe the market rather than IB Gram's price list.

For a training household there is a second dimension that matters as much as the rate, which is what happens when a session cannot go ahead. A fixture is rescheduled, a tournament is extended, a squad session is added. Any provider's cancellation and rescheduling terms therefore have a direct cost to this kind of family, and those terms are rarely on a website. Ask for them in writing before booking, alongside the rate.

The questions worth asking are specific. How much notice is required to move a session without charge? Can an unused session be carried to the following week or does it lapse? Is the same tutor available at a different hour while the student is travelling, and if not, who is? What happens to a block if a competition absence runs longer than planned? A provider with clear answers to those four is a better fit here than one with a slightly lower rate and vague terms.

The last column of the table is deliberately about what to ask rather than what to pay, because flexibility is priced inconsistently across this market and we are not in a position to publish anyone else's terms. For our own arrangement, ask for the rate, the notice period and the carry-over position together, and compare the whole package rather than the hourly figure.

sections.heading: Which schools Sports City children attend, and what the board spread means
paragraphs: This area is comparatively well served, with schools inside Sports City and Victory Heights and more immediately west in Motor City. A child at one of the local schools can be home by mid-afternoon, which is exactly what a training household needs, because it opens the window before training rather than only the one after it.

Older students travel more, often north across Al Khail Road or south towards the Arabian Ranches cluster, and that is where the scheduling gets genuinely tight: a secondary athlete home at half past five with training at seven has no usable academic window on a training day at all. For those students the plan has to be built on non-training afternoons and weekend blocks, and pretending otherwise produces a schedule that is abandoned by October.

The board question applies here as everywhere. Schools in this cluster choose examination boards subject by subject, so a single student can sit Cambridge in the sciences and Pearson in Mathematics, and two children in the same building can be on different boards in the same subject. Ask the examinations officer for the board, the syllabus code and, on Cambridge subjects, the tier, in writing, before buying practice material or booking a tutor.

For market context: KHDA counted 227 private schools and 387,441 pupils in Dubai in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, and confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year. Dubai is adding seven new private schools for 2026-27, four British and three IB, creating 16,846 places. KHDA licenses and inspects those schools; it does not license private tutors, and IB Gram claims no approval from it or from any examination board.

sections.heading: Coursework and honesty when a student is away
paragraphs: Absence puts pressure on exactly the components where the honesty line matters, and the pressure arrives with a reasonable-sounding justification: the student was at a tournament representing their country, the deadline did not move, surely some latitude applies. The school's academic honesty policy does not contain a travel exception, and neither does the IB's. So this is worth settling in advance rather than at eleven at night three days before a deadline.

What a tutor can legitimately do is considerable. Teach the criteria by letter and the marks attached to each. Identify which criterion is currently scoring nothing. Question the research question until it is answerable in the word limit. Interrogate method, data, sources and reasoning. Respond to a draft with questions rather than corrections. Help the student decide which two hours of work recover the most marks in the time that remains.

What a tutor must not do does not change because a student was away: no supplied text, no restructured argument, no rewritten section handed back to be retyped. The test is whether the student can defend every decision in the work under questioning, without notes, because every decision was theirs. Providers in this market sell completed internal assessments at a fixed price; the provider keeps the fee and the student faces a malpractice finding that can cost the whole diploma.

The practical protection for a travelling student is scheduling rather than rescue. Where the sporting calendar is known a year ahead - and it usually is - coursework should be placed in the off-season deliberately, with drafts finished before the competition block rather than during it. That is the whole argument for an off-season block, and it is the one piece of planning that most reliably keeps an athlete out of a deadline crisis.

sections.heading: Coverage, time zones and the permit position
paragraphs: Specialist supply tightens in predictable places. Higher Level Mathematics and Higher Level Physics are the first to fill, from February onwards. Psychology and the smaller Diploma options draw on a shorter list than the subject grids imply. Sports, Exercise and Health Science has a genuinely narrow pool, because it is a smaller cohort subject, and it should be booked earlier than a core science rather than at the same time.

Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the fallback is a specialist based outside the UAE, most often in India, teaching the same specification online, with the base and the time difference stated before anything is confirmed. For a travelling household that detail is operational rather than ethical housekeeping: a tutor two and a half hours ahead of Dubai is a different proposition again when the student is at a tournament three time zones the other way, and the arithmetic has to be done before the block starts.

The honest version of travelling continuity is that it works well for maintenance and poorly for recovery. A thirty-minute consolidation session from a hotel room is genuinely useful. A full ninety-minute teaching session after a day of matches is not, however willing everyone is. Setting expectations at that level before a trip is what stops a travelling arrangement being judged a failure for not doing something it was never going to do.

On the regulatory position: private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so none is quoted. IB Gram operates no UAE centre, holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, and delivers lessons online.

process.title: Send the training schedule with the school details
process.description: Training days and times, fixture pattern, and the travel dates you already know, alongside the school and the usual arrival home. The immovable schedule is collected first and the tutoring is placed around it, which is the opposite of how most plans are built.

process.title: Send the syllabus code and the marked work
process.description: The code and tier from the entry form, or the IB subject and level, plus the last two pieces of marked work including one that went badly. For a student who has already missed time, that is also what shows whether the absence left a cumulative gap or a surface one.

process.title: Identify the genuinely productive window
process.description: One diagnostic conversation to work out when this student is actually able to work: usually before training or on a clear afternoon rather than after a session. Thirty minutes in a good window beats ninety in a bad one, and defending that window matters more than adding hours.

process.title: Place sustained work in the off-season
process.description: Explorations, Extended Essays, internally assessed investigations and cumulative content gaps go into the quietest part of the sporting calendar, scheduled a term ahead. Fixture lists are published in advance, which makes this the one piece of planning that reliably prevents a deadline crisis.

process.title: Agree the travelling arrangement before the trip
process.description: Session times set against the itinerary, the tutor's own time zone stated, and a written list of what to keep up and what to let go. The aim while away is maintenance in one or two subjects, not coverage in eight, and saying so in advance keeps everyone honest.

process.title: Diagnose on return, then review on marks
process.description: One session to establish what is actually missing before adding any hours, because doubling up on a tired returning student produces a second dip. Then a review against marked work at six to eight weeks, with continue, change tutor or stop as the three legitimate outcomes.

whyPoints.title: The immovable schedule is collected first
whyPoints.description: Training times, fixtures and travel dates are gathered before anything is booked, and the session is placed relative to them. A plan built from a school timetable alone is a plan that assumes an evening this household does not have.

whyPoints.title: Lessons travel with the student
whyPoints.description: Because delivery is online, a session can run from a hotel room at a time agreed against two clocks. A fortnight of maintenance in one subject is what stops a competition block becoming a term of damage.

whyPoints.title: Absence is planned for, not patched
whyPoints.description: Before a trip we ask the school what will be taught, assessed and due in the window, pre-learn the cumulative subjects, and write down what to let go. Recovering an unplanned fortnight takes three times as long.

whyPoints.title: Sports subjects treated as real subjects
whyPoints.description: IGCSE Physical Education and Sports, Exercise and Health Science have written papers, physiology content and assessed analysis. The work is translating what an athlete already knows into the register the mark scheme requires.

whyPoints.title: Rates in AED with sources, and flexibility questioned
whyPoints.description: Every figure here is attributed to the provider or survey that published it and dated to October 2026. For a training household the notice period and carry-over terms matter as much as the rate, so ask for all three together.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line has no travel exception
whyPoints.description: Criteria taught, method questioned, drafts answered with questions - and no supplied text, whatever the fixture list did to the deadline. The protection for a travelling student is scheduling coursework early, not rescuing it late.

faqs.question: Who actually lives in Dubai Sports City?
faqs.answer: Four fairly distinct groups. Apartment households with no connection to sport, who ask the ordinary questions about marks and timing. The Victory Heights villa families next door, often with three or four children and a wide arrival spread. Academy staff households, whose working hours match training hours rather than office hours. And families who relocated to Dubai specifically for a training programme, who are usually the most academically anxious because the academic record has to work whatever happens with the sport. Those four need different plans, and the fourth is the one standard area advice serves worst.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to an apartment in Dubai Sports City?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide in-home tutoring anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service offered only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video with screen sharing. For a training household this is the feature that makes the whole thing work rather than a compromise: a session can run from a hotel room at a tournament, at a time agreed against two clocks, and three children at three stages can each have a specialist at a different hour. No visiting tutor can offer either.

faqs.question: My child trains five evenings a week. When does studying happen?
faqs.answer: Before training, or on a clear afternoon - almost never after a session. A fourteen-year-old finishing a hard session at eight has perhaps forty minutes of low-quality attention left, and demanding work placed there produces attendance rather than learning. The practical plan is thirty to forty-five minutes of drill-shaped work immediately after school on training days, with sustained work moved to non-training afternoons, weekends or the off-season. Send the training schedule with the school arrival time and the session gets placed from both rather than from a guess.

faqs.question: My child will miss three weeks for a tournament. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Plan it two or three weeks ahead rather than afterwards. Ask the school in writing for three things: what will be taught in each subject during the window, what will be assessed, and what is due. Then pre-learn the cumulative subjects before leaving, Mathematics first, because a two-week hole there is still costing marks a year later. While away, maintain one or two subjects at thirty minutes every second day rather than attempting all eight. On return, diagnose before adding hours - doubling up on a tired student produces a second dip.

faqs.question: Can lessons continue while we travel for competitions?
faqs.answer: Yes, with expectations set properly. A thirty-minute consolidation session from a hotel room is genuinely useful and keeps the cumulative damage small. A ninety-minute teaching session after a day of matches is not, however willing everyone is. The arrangement is agreed before the trip: session times set against the itinerary, the tutor's own time zone stated so the slot is actually workable, and a written list of what to keep up and what to let go. Travelling sessions are for maintenance, not for recovery.

faqs.question: Is IGCSE Physical Education a serious academic subject?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is misjudged in both directions. The written theory paper covers anatomy, physiology, training principles and psychology, and that paper is where the grade is decided. The trap for an athlete is that the material is familiar in the wrong register: knowing how a training block feels is not the same as explaining adaptation in the terms the mark scheme requires. The assessed practical and the written analysis of performance are also marked against criteria, and students who leave the analysis to the final week lose marks already earned on the field.

faqs.question: What is Sports, Exercise and Health Science and who should take it?
faqs.answer: A full Diploma science subject covering anatomy, exercise physiology, biomechanics and skill acquisition, with external papers and an internally assessed investigation. It suits students with a genuine interest in the science of performance, not students looking for an easier science - the data handling and physiology demands are those of any group four subject. Tutor supply is narrower because the cohort is smaller, so book earlier than for Biology or Chemistry. Confirm the exact components and weightings in the current subject guide for your child's cohort.

faqs.question: Does taking a sports subject weaken a university application?
faqs.answer: What matters is the published prerequisite of the specific programme, not a general impression about subject prestige. A programme that requires Chemistry and Mathematics at a particular level requires those subjects; a sports science course will usually name Biology or a science. A sporting subject taken seriously and graded well alongside sciences and mathematics is not a liability. Look up the requirement for the specific programme at the specific institution, in writing, at the start of Year 12, and choose the subject set from that rather than from assumptions.

faqs.question: Which schools do Dubai Sports City children attend?
faqs.answer: Many stay local: there are schools inside Sports City and in Victory Heights alongside, with more immediately west in Motor City. Older students more often travel, north across Al Khail Road or south towards the Arabian Ranches cluster. That matters for a training household because a secondary student home at half past five with training at seven has no usable academic window that day. Those schools also choose examination boards subject by subject, so ask the examinations officer for the board, the code and the tier in writing.

faqs.question: How do villa and apartment households here differ in what they need?
faqs.answer: Apartment households are usually two working parents with one or two children and a single usable evening window, so the task is placement: find the one good window, decide which subject gets it, and defend it with one named fallback time. Villa households in Victory Heights more often have three or four children and an arrival spread approaching two hours, so the task is sequencing: youngest first and earliest, the protected hour to whoever has the nearest public examination, latest arrival moved to a weekend block, and one household fallback slot.

faqs.question: What should we ask about moving sessions when fixtures change?
faqs.answer: Four specific questions, before booking and in writing. How much notice is needed to move a session without charge. Whether an unused session carries to the following week or lapses. Whether the same tutor is available at a different hour while the student is travelling, and who covers if not. And what happens to a block if a competition absence runs longer than planned. For a training household those terms have a real cost, and they are rarely published on any provider's site, so compare the whole package rather than the hourly rate.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a Physical Education coursework component?
faqs.answer: Within the same boundary that applies to every assessed component. A tutor can teach the criteria and what each is worth, explain the structure a performance analysis needs, question whether the evidence supports the claims being made, and respond to a draft with questions. What a tutor must not do is write any part of it, restructure the argument, or hand back a rewritten version to be retyped. The test is whether your child can defend every choice unaided. A tournament schedule does not create an exception to that.

faqs.question: My child is pursuing a US college sports route. What academic work matters?
faqs.answer: Two things that are easy to under-plan. The subject record itself, which has to satisfy whatever the institution publishes, and the standardised testing, which usually has to be sat on a fixed date that may collide with a fixture. Requirements differ by institution and by programme and they change, so get them in writing from the institutions in question rather than from general advice. For the UAE side, note that on the American equivalency track English is evidenced by IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in SAT reading and writing, with at least 450 in SAT Mathematics.

faqs.question: How late can a session start after evening training?
faqs.answer: Later than 20:30 is rarely worth paying for, and for a student under about fifteen the limit is earlier than that. The issue is not willingness but recovery: after a hard session the available attention is both short and poor quality, and demanding work placed there teaches the student that they cannot do the subject. If the only free slot is after late training, the better answer is a shorter session on a non-training day plus consolidation work the student does alone, rather than a full lesson nobody gets value from.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is in a different time zone while we travel?
faqs.answer: It is stated before you book, because it decides whether a travelling arrangement is viable at all. A tutor two and a half hours ahead of Dubai is one proposition when the student is at home and another when they are at a tournament several time zones the other way. We do that arithmetic against your itinerary before the block starts rather than discovering it in week two. Where the overlap does not work, the honest answer is a different tutor for the travelling period or a maintenance plan the student runs alone.

dubai/dubai-sports-city.closingHeading: Send the fixture list with the syllabus code
dubai/dubai-sports-city.closingBody: The plan that works for a Dubai Sports City family starts from the schedule that cannot move. Send the training days and times, the fixture pattern, any travel dates you already know, the school and usual arrival home, and the syllabus code or IB subject and level with the last marked work. You will get a session placed in a window your child can actually use, sustained work scheduled into the off-season, a written arrangement for any competition block including the tutor's time zone, the rate in AED with the notice and carry-over terms, and a review date six to eight weeks out. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video.
