dubai/dubailand.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma, MYP and IGCSE subjects to students across the Dubailand belt. Each one works to the syllabus version your child's school entered, at the level printed on the report, and in a slot chosen around the bus timetable rather than around a drive.

intro.heading: Dubailand's real problem is not finding a tutor, it is finding an hour
paragraphs: Dubailand is not a neighbourhood so much as a belt: Arabian Ranches and its two newer phases, Mudon, Town Square, DAMAC Hills, Motor City, Dubai Sports City, Liwan, The Villa and the Dubai Hills edge. Nearly every family here drives or buses out of the community for school and back into it again, which means the academic day does not end at the final bell. It ends somewhere between half past three and a quarter to five, depending on which gate the bus leaves from and whether Emirates Road is behaving. That single fact shapes every tutoring decision a Dubailand parent makes.

Parents searching for IB and IGCSE tutors in Dubailand are rarely short of options. Community groups carry dozens of offers a week. What they are short of is a usable hour that is not already spoken for by the return journey, football at the Ranches, swimming at Motor City, or the twenty minutes a Year 11 student needs simply to stop being in a car. A tutor who adds a further forty minutes of someone else's travel to each side of that hour is competing against the only quiet part of the evening.

That is why delivery matters more here than in most of Dubai. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard, the student's own past-paper script on screen and written feedback sent afterwards. Nobody drives anywhere. A session booked for a quarter past four starts at a quarter past four. The lesson can also be split: twenty-five minutes of Maths while the mind is fresh, a break, then thirty-five minutes of Chemistry, which no visiting tutor charging door-to-door would ever agree to.

The second thing online delivery changes is who is available. A Dubailand villa in a twenty-minute radius of a tutor's home might reach four or five people who teach Physics. Opened up to live video, the same family can work with a Physics specialist who has taught the current IB Diploma syllabus for a decade, or an IGCSE Extended examiner-trained teacher who knows exactly how Pearson 4PH1 Paper 2 differs from Cambridge 0625 Paper 4. The pool stops being a function of geography and becomes a function of subject.

This page is written for the parent who has already decided tutoring is worth trying and now wants the operational detail: what time a session can start from each community, what the Dubai market charges and who publishes those figures, what KHDA inspection bands actually mean when you read a school report, what a tutor may and may not do with an Internal Assessment, and what the first fortnight looks like. Every figure on the page carries its source. Nothing here is a promise about a grade.

dubai/dubailand.programmesIntro: Dubailand schools run three broad routes: a British primary and IGCSE path, an IB continuum, and a mixed path where children transfer at Year 7 or Year 10. The programme notes below are written for this belt specifically, because the transfer points are where most families first ask for help.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP assesses how a child inquires, not how much they have memorised. Learning is organised into transdisciplinary units, and the written reports a parent receives describe approaches to learning rather than percentages. Support at this stage is about reading fluency, number sense and the habit of explaining reasoning out loud, because those three things decide how smoothly MYP goes.
programmes.countryNote: In the Dubailand belt the PYP schools sit mainly on the Al Khail and Al Barsha South side, which means a long bus run for a seven-year-old. Early-evening sessions rarely work for this age group here; a twenty-five minute morning slot at the weekend tends to be far more productive than a tired half-hour at five o'clock on a Tuesday.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP marks run on four criteria per subject, each scored out of eight, and the conversion from criterion marks to a one-to-seven grade is where most families lose track. The Personal Project in the final year is a supervised independent piece. Support focuses on reading the criterion descriptors properly and on the written communication that MYP sciences and individuals-and-societies subjects demand.
programmes.countryNote: Dubailand MYP students frequently arrive from a British Year 7 or an Indian curriculum, and the shift from right-answer marking to criterion marking unsettles them for a term or two. The commonest request we see from Arabian Ranches and Town Square families is help reading a criterion grid, not help with the content itself.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internal Assessments in most subjects carry twenty to twenty-five per cent of the final grade and are marked against named criteria by letter. The two years are front-loaded with coursework deadlines that bunch in the second half of DP1 and the first half of DP2.
programmes.countryNote: For a Dubailand DP student the binding constraint is the evening. A DP1 with HL Chemistry, HL Maths AA and an Extended Essay cannot absorb three separate tutoring journeys a week. Two online slots, one of them split across subjects, is the pattern that survives the belt's commute without eating the only hours left for independent practice.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years, usually eight or nine subjects, sat as Core or Extended tiers in Cambridge subjects and as single or tiered papers with Pearson. Syllabus codes matter: Cambridge Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 against Pearson 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1. Papers, formula provision and practical assessment differ between the two boards.
programmes.countryNote: Dubailand's British schools do not all use the same board, and some split boards by department, so an IGCSE tutor in Dubailand has to confirm the code before the first lesson. A student doing Cambridge 0580 Extended and Pearson 4CH1 in the same year is common here and needs two different exam-technique habits.

dubai/dubailand.subjectsIntro: Requests from the Dubailand belt cluster heavily in the sciences and maths, partly because the DP cohorts at the nearby IB schools are science-weighted and partly because those are the subjects where an evening hour converts most directly into marks.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebra-heavy IB route. HL adds proof, complex numbers and a harder calculus load, and Paper 3 is a long investigative paper sat without the structure of Papers 1 and 2. Marks go missing in unjustified steps rather than wrong answers, so written method is the main teaching target.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The statistics and modelling route, with the graphic display calculator available in every paper. Students who chose it to avoid algebra often find the statistical inference and the modelling write-ups harder than expected. Teaching concentrates on choosing the right test and interpreting output in context.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: The gap between quoting a law and applying it under exam conditions is wider in Physics than anywhere else. At IGCSE, electricity and the practical-skills paper account for most lost marks; at DP, the HL extension topics and uncertainty treatment in the Internal Assessment do.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics at DP level, moles and electrolysis at IGCSE. HL students lose marks by describing rather than explaining, which is a command-term problem rather than a content problem. Data-based questions reward a habit of annotating the stem before answering.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: The volume of named detail makes Biology feel like memorisation until a student meets a six-mark explain question. Teaching here is about structuring extended answers against the mark scheme and about the statistical treatment that the DP Internal Assessment expects.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides more marks than prose quality. HL adds the quantitative paper and a heavier policy-evaluation load. The three commentaries that make up the Internal Assessment need real published articles and a tight word limit, and students routinely overshoot on description and undershoot on evaluation.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis against a guiding question, Paper 2 a comparative essay, and the Individual Oral a ten-minute spoken analysis of a global issue through two works. Most of the gain comes from learning to build an argument rather than from reading more texts.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE)
subjects.description: Extended tier carries the grades most Dubailand parents are aiming at, and the step from Core to Extended is largely algebraic fluency plus trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles. Non-calculator confidence and clean working are what separate a 6 from an 8.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A case-heavy subject where the pre-released material rewards early, structured preparation. HL students sit an additional paper and need the tools used accurately rather than listed. Teaching focuses on applying one framework well instead of naming four.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode discipline and trace tables at IGCSE; data structures, object-oriented design and the HL extension at DP. The DP solution-development Internal Assessment is a software artefact plus documentation, and the documentation is where marks are usually lost.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Arabic is compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs. Support here is about the school's own scheme of work and assessment, since the Ministry restricts the use of different or additional content.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed by an exhibition of three objects with commentaries and an essay on a prescribed title. Students who treat it as an opinion piece lose marks that a clear knowledge question and a worked counter-position would have secured. Sessions here are structural rather than content-led.

dubai/dubailand.regionsIntro: The belt is not uniform. Bus routes, gate positions and distance from Emirates Road change the earliest workable session time by an hour between one community and the next, so the notes below are operational rather than descriptive.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches
regions.note: Short runs to JESS Arabian Ranches and Ranches Primary School, so children are often home before four. An IB tutor in Arabian Ranches can realistically take a half past four slot through the week, which is the best of the belt.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches 2
regions.note: A longer internal loop and a later gate time push the return to around four. Families here tend to settle on a twin-slot pattern, one weekday evening and one weekend morning, rather than two tired weekday hours.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches 3
regions.note: The newest phase, with most children bussed out towards Al Khail or Barsha South. Returns after a quarter past four are normal, and a five o'clock start works better than fighting it.

regions.name: Mudon
regions.note: An online tutor in Mudon is usually booked for five o'clock or later, because the school run reaches well beyond the community. Shorter, more frequent sessions hold attention better here than a single long one.

regions.name: Town Square
regions.note: High density, young families, and long bus routes to the Barsha South and Motor City schools. IGCSE tuition in Town Square is most often booked in the Year 10 spring, once the first set of mock papers has come back.

regions.name: Motor City
regions.note: GEMS Metropole sits inside the community, so some children walk home. An IGCSE tutor in Motor City can often start at a quarter past four, and the split-subject hour works well at that time.

regions.name: Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Victory Heights Primary and GEMS United are both on the doorstep, which keeps the commute short. An IB DP tutor in Dubai Sports City frequently takes two sixty-minute slots midweek during the DP2 coursework crunch.

regions.name: DAMAC Hills
regions.note: Jebel Ali School relocated into this side of Dubailand, but many secondary students travel further. An IB tutor in DAMAC Hills usually works a later evening slot, with the weekend carrying the heavier session.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Closest of the belt to the Al Khail IB schools. An IB tutor in Dubai Hills Estate can take an early slot, which matters for HL sciences where tiredness costs accuracy.

regions.name: Liwan and The Villa
regions.note: GEMS FirstPoint School and The Aquila School draw from here. A Maths AA tutor in Dubailand is most often requested by families on this side at the start of DP1, when the HL decision is still reversible.

schoolClusters.city: Arabian Ranches, Liwan and The Villa
schoolClusters.note: The older, more settled end of the belt, with British primary provision inside the communities and secondary schooling split between the Ranches campuses and schools further along Al Ain Road. Students here typically sit IGCSE at sixteen before choosing between A Level and the IB Diploma.

dubai/dubailand.modesIntro: Three patterns cover almost every Dubailand family. The choice is driven less by subject than by how late the bus gets in and how many siblings are competing for the same evening.

modes.description: The pattern that survives the belt's commute. A midweek session carries the current topic while it is still live in class, and a longer weekend morning session carries past papers, marking feedback and the slower thinking that a tired Tuesday cannot support. Most Year 10 and MYP families start here.

sections.heading: What a Dubailand parent is actually asking when they search for a tutor
paragraphs: The search phrase is about subject and place. The question underneath it is almost always about time. Parents in this belt have usually worked out that their child needs help in one or two subjects; what they have not worked out is where an hour is going to come from, and whether adding a stranger's drive to each side of that hour makes the problem worse. Answering the time question first is the only honest way to answer the tutoring question.

The second buried question is competence at a specific level. A parent whose daughter is sitting Cambridge 0580 Extended does not need a maths tutor in general, she needs someone who knows that the non-calculator paper rewards clean algebraic working and that the Extended tier's trigonometry goes well beyond the right-angled triangle work her daughter met in Year 9. The same applies at Diploma level, where HL Chemistry and SL Chemistry are different teaching jobs rather than the same job at two speeds.

The third is trust, and it is the one most pages skip. A parent wants to know who is teaching, whether that person holds the private tuition work permit the UAE requires, what happens if the match is wrong, and where the line sits on coursework. Those are answerable questions with specific answers, and the rest of this page gives them. What nobody can honestly answer is what grade your child will end up with, and any page that offers you that number has told you something about itself.
bullets: Time first: which slot is genuinely free after the bus gets in
Level second: the syllabus code and tier, not just the subject name

sections.heading: The Dubailand school run, timed, and what it leaves behind
paragraphs: The belt's communities sit between ten and thirty-five minutes from the schools that most of their secondary students attend, and the bus adds collection stops on top of that. The practical effect is a return window stretching from about half past three in Motor City to nearly five o'clock in parts of Mudon and DAMAC Hills on a slow day. The table below sets out indicative windows that families in each community describe, together with the earliest session time that tends to hold up week after week rather than collapsing after a fortnight.

Treat the figures as planning ranges, not measurements. Gate times differ by school, bus routes change between terms, and a Sunday in January behaves differently from a Thursday in May. What does not change is the ordering: the communities with schools inside them get the early slots, and the communities on the Emirates Road side do not. A family who books a half past four session from Town Square because a neighbour in Motor City manages one will spend six weeks arriving late and then conclude that tutoring does not work.

The useful consequence is that the slot should be chosen before the tutor. Decide which thirty, forty-five or sixty minutes genuinely exists in your week, then ask whether a specialist is available in it. Because delivery is over live video, that question has a much better answer than it would if the pool were limited to people who could drive to your villa by five o'clock. It also means a slot that only exists at half past seven on a Tuesday is still workable.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor on Al Ain Road against a specialist on live video
paragraphs: In-home tutoring is a real and reasonable choice, and plenty of Dubailand families use it, particularly for primary-age children where a screen is a poor medium. It is worth saying plainly what it costs and what it does to an evening. A tutor driving from Al Barsha or Al Qusais to Arabian Ranches 3 at five o'clock is committing between twenty and forty-five minutes each way, and that time is either priced into the hour or recovered by the tutor working only within a narrow radius. Both outcomes limit who your child can be taught by.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home tutoring at the door is a service we run only in India. That is a deliberate position rather than a gap. The entire value of removing the journey is that subject specialism stops being rationed by distance. A family in Mudon can work with an HL Physics teacher who would never have been reachable by car, and a student who needs Economics commentary feedback on Tuesday and Maths AA proof work on Saturday can have two different specialists rather than one generalist.

sections.heading: What the Dubai tutoring market charges, and who published the number
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages for these searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in dollars. That is not accidental: a published rate invites comparison. The rates below are other providers' own published figures, read in October 2026, grouped by provider model rather than by brand. They are offered so that a Dubailand parent can recognise an unreasonable quote, not as a league table of competitors.

The useful context is school fees, because tutoring is a marginal cost on top of a large fixed one. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. For a belt where many families moved specifically for the fee-to-villa ratio, that freeze is the backdrop against which a tutoring budget gets approved or refused. Two sessions a week for a full Diploma year is a significant number and deserves to be stated rather than discovered.

A note on what the figures do not include. Published hourly rates rarely say whether marking between sessions is counted, whether a cancellation inside twenty-four hours is charged, whether materials are extra, or whether the rate rises in the term before exams. Those four questions are worth more than a ten-dirham difference in the headline rate. Ask them in writing before the first lesson, and ask whether the quoted figure includes VAT, since the treatment of tuition fees is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority rather than for a tutoring page.

sections.heading: Building a week that survives DP1 and Year 11 in this belt
paragraphs: A tutoring hour is only worth what the six days around it do with it. The failure pattern we see most often from Dubailand families is two sessions a week with no independent practice between them, which turns the tutor into the only person doing the work. The fix is uncomfortable but simple: the session sets a specific, finishable task, the task gets done before the next session, and the next session starts by marking it. Thirty minutes of independent work between lessons changes the return on the hour more than a third lesson would.

Where the belt's geography bites is Thursday. A student who gets home at half past four, has a club at six and a family commitment on Friday has no usable study block until Saturday morning. Planning around that honestly is better than pretending Thursday evening is available. For most Dubailand DP students the workable shape is a midweek session on Monday or Tuesday, independent work on Wednesday, and the longer session on Saturday or Sunday morning, with Friday left alone.

Year 11 is different again, because the mock cycle lands in November and January and the real papers in the spring. The week needs to flip from topic coverage to timed-paper work earlier than most students expect, usually by the start of the second term. The practical marker is this: once a student has seen every topic once, the session should mostly consist of questions done under time and then marked out loud, not of further explanation. Explanation feels more productive and converts into fewer marks.
bullets: One finishable task set at the end of every session, marked at the start of the next
Thirty minutes of independent work between lessons, protected in the calendar
Friday left clear in most Dubailand households rather than optimistically booked
Switch from explanation to timed questions once every topic has been seen once
Mock results used to re-plan the block, not simply filed

sections.heading: Ramadan, the long summer and how a Dubailand timetable bends
paragraphs: Two features of the UAE calendar reshape tutoring in ways a generic revision plan ignores. The first is Ramadan, when school days shorten and the whole household's rhythm shifts later. For a fasting student, an afternoon session is close to useless and a post-Iftar session is often the most alert hour of the day. Families in the belt who move their slot to around half past eight in the evening for the month tend to keep momentum; families who pause for four weeks come back to a visibly colder start, particularly in maths.

The second is the summer. The Dubai academic year ends in early July and resumes in late August or the first days of September, and a very large share of Dubailand families travel for most of that gap. A DP1 student going into DP2 across a long break with Internal Assessment drafts unfinished returns to a September that is already behind. The realistic answer is not a full summer timetable. It is two or three sessions placed deliberately: one to set the IA plan before travel, one mid-break to review what was written, one in the final week to restart habits.

Short breaks matter in a different way. The autumn and spring half-terms sit close enough to mock cycles to be genuinely useful, and a block of four or five sessions across a week converts better than the same five spread over five weeks, because the student is holding the whole subject in mind at once. That intensive pattern is also the one most compatible with a belt where term-time evenings are already crowded.
bullets: Post-Iftar slots during Ramadan rather than a four-week pause
Two or three deliberately placed summer sessions, not a full holiday timetable
Half-term blocks of four or five sessions in a single week before mock cycles

sections.heading: Reading a KHDA inspection report without being misled by the band
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects schools on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. Dubai's private sector carried 387,441 students across 227 schools offering seventeen curricula in 2024-25, with UK provision at thirty-seven per cent of enrolment, Indian at twenty-six, American at fourteen and the IB at seven. The sector is also still growing: the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools and 16,846 places.

What a band does not tell you is how your child's particular subject and set is doing. An Outstanding judgement is an aggregate across phases, subjects and groups of students, and a school can hold it while a single Diploma subject is being taught by its third teacher in two years. The detail that matters sits further inside the report, in the subject-level attainment and progress judgements and in the recommendations. Reading those before deciding which subject needs tutoring is a more reliable guide than the headline.

The other thing worth knowing is what the regulator governs and what it does not. KHDA licenses schools, approves curricula and inspects. It does not vet individual private tutors, and no tutoring platform can describe itself as approved by it. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute; IB Gram does not operate premises in the UAE and holds no such permit, so any page claiming regulator approval for a tutor is telling you something inaccurate.
bullets: Six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak, judged across the whole school

sections.heading: Internal Assessments, practicals and the work that has to stay the student's own
paragraphs: This is the part of the market with the real risk in it. One page ranking for these searches sells finished Internal Assessments outright. Under IB rules that is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student, not the seller. A Diploma candidate found to have submitted work that is not their own can lose the subject or the whole Diploma, and the school is obliged to report it. No tutoring arrangement is worth that exposure, and any provider offering it has told you what they think of your child's position.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial. They can teach the research skills the task requires, discuss the choice of topic and push back on one that cannot generate enough analysis, explain the assessment criteria letter by letter and what each band descriptor actually asks for, question a draft, point out that a conclusion is not supported by the data, show how a similar argument is structured in a different context, and teach referencing. All of that is teaching, and all of it is permitted. What is not permitted is text that originated with anyone other than the candidate.

Practical science is the related question for IGCSE families. Cambridge and Pearson both assess practical skills, either through a laboratory examination or an alternative written paper, and the skills examined are planning, observation, recording, analysis and evaluation. Those are teachable without a bench: a student can plan an investigation, interpret somebody else's results table, identify the variable that was not controlled and rewrite a conclusion. The laboratory work itself belongs to the school, and a tutor's job is to make sure the student can describe and criticise it.
bullets: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback; the text must originate with the candidate
Criteria explained letter by letter, with band descriptors read as written
Topic feasibility challenged early, which is where most IA marks are won or lost
Practical skills taught through planning, analysis and evaluation of results
Official syllabus documents cited and linked, never reproduced or supplied as downloads

sections.heading: Getting started from Dubailand, including what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: The first conversation is about facts rather than aspiration: which school, which year, which board, which syllabus code if you have it, which papers your child has already sat, and what the last report or mock actually said. If you have a marked script, that is worth more than any description of the problem, because a marked script shows whether marks are being lost on content, on command terms, on time, or on presentation. Those four problems need four different responses.

From there we identify the slot before the tutor, for the reasons set out earlier on this page, and then look for a specialist who teaches that subject at that level and is free in it. A trial lesson and a consultation come before any block is booked, and the terms are confirmed in writing at that point. If the match is wrong after one or two lessons, say so and we change it; a tutor who suits a quiet, methodical Year 10 is often the wrong person for a fast, impatient DP2.

Sometimes the honest answer is that nobody suitable is free in the slot you need. That happens most often for niche Higher Level combinations in the weeks before May papers, and for the mandatory Arabic streams where KHDA requires teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education to hold its approval and schools follow a prescribed scheme. When it happens we say so, offer a different slot or a different tutor with a clear statement of what they do and do not cover, and leave the decision with you. Disclosing a coverage gap is cheaper than hiding one behind a waiting list.
bullets: Bring the school, year, board, syllabus code and a marked script if you have one
Slot chosen first, specialist second

whyPoints.description: A twenty-minute radius around a Dubailand villa might reach a handful of people who teach Physics. Online, the constraint becomes who teaches HL Physics on the current syllabus and is free at your time, which is a far better question to be limited by.

faqs.question: What time can a tutoring session realistically start for a child in Dubailand?
faqs.answer: It depends on which community you are in. Children at schools inside Motor City, Dubai Sports City or Dubai Hills Estate are often home between half past three and four, so a quarter past four start holds up through the term. From Mudon, DAMAC Hills, Town Square or Arabian Ranches 3 the bus commonly arrives after four, and a five o'clock or quarter past five start is more sustainable. Because lessons are delivered over live video there is no travel to add at either end, so the slot can also sit later in the evening without anyone driving across the belt in the dark.

faqs.question: Can we book a tutor to visit our villa in Arabian Ranches or Mudon?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; tutoring here is delivered one-to-one over live video, and home tutoring at the door is a service we run only in India. That is a deliberate choice rather than a limitation. Removing the drive means a family in Mudon can be taught by a Higher Level Physics specialist who would never have been within reach by car, and it means a session can be split across two subjects without anyone paying for a second journey. If you specifically want someone in the room, an in-home provider is the right choice and the market rate is roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel.

faqs.question: How much does an IB tutor cost per hour for a Dubailand family?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates read in October 2026 put a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, and an IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more. TutorChase published AED 270, Unitors published IB from AED 200, and BartyED published AED 650 at the premium end. In-home visits run around AED 180 to 500 including travel. Those are other providers' own figures, quoted here as market context. IB Gram quotes after a consultation and a trial lesson, with the terms set out in writing, because a six-week push before mocks is not the same product as a two-year Diploma plan.

faqs.question: Which schools do most children in the Dubailand belt actually attend?
faqs.answer: Primary provision sits largely inside the communities: JESS Arabian Ranches, Ranches Primary School, GEMS Metropole in Motor City, Victory Heights Primary in Sports City and The Aquila School on the Liwan side. Secondary and Diploma students more often travel outwards to GEMS International School Al Khail, Dubai Heights Academy, Nord Anglia International School Dubai, GEMS Founders School in Al Barsha South, GEMS FirstPoint School and Fairgreen International School. That outward travel is exactly why the belt's tutoring evening starts later than the rest of Dubai. These schools are named as local context only; IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring as effective as having someone at the kitchen table in Dubailand?
faqs.answer: For secondary students the honest answer is that the format matters less than the match. What a screen gives you is the student's own script visible to both people at once, a shared whiteboard that keeps a record, and the ability to pause and send the marked work afterwards. What it costs you is the physical presence that helps some younger children settle. For primary-age children an in-home tutor is often the better choice. For a Year 11 sitting Cambridge 0580 Extended or a Diploma student on Higher Level Chemistry, having the right specialist in the slot that actually exists beats having a nearer generalist in a slot that does not.

faqs.question: Does my child's tutor need a MoHRE private tuition permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, if they are providing private tutoring in the UAE. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years through MoHRE's smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific amount you read with caution. Ask any tutor to confirm their permit before the first lesson.

faqs.question: Can a Dubailand session move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a fasting student it usually should. School days shorten during Ramadan and the household rhythm moves later, which makes a mid-afternoon lesson close to unproductive. A slot around half past eight in the evening tends to be the most alert hour of the day. Families in this belt who move the time keep their momentum; families who pause for the whole month generally come back to a noticeably colder restart, most visibly in maths, where fluency fades faster than knowledge. Because nobody is travelling to the lesson, moving the slot by four hours for a month costs nothing operationally.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week do Dubailand Diploma students usually start with?
faqs.answer: Two is the common starting point, and the shape matters more than the count. In this belt the pattern that survives the commute is one midweek session that carries the topic while it is still live in class, and one longer weekend morning session for past papers and marking feedback. Thirty minutes of independent work between the two does more for the result than a third lesson would, because without it the tutor becomes the only person doing the work. Families with a single problem subject often start with one session and add a second only when a mock or an Internal Assessment deadline makes the case.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Maths AA and Physics for a student in Dubailand?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, because a single tutor across both subjects can use the mechanics and calculus overlap deliberately rather than by accident. The limit is Higher Level. At Higher Level the two subjects diverge enough that most strong teachers are genuinely specialist in one, and a student taking HL Maths AA and HL Physics is usually better served by two people. Where a split-subject hour is used, we tell you before you book whether it is one tutor or a handover between two, and what each of them has actually taught at that level.

faqs.question: What does a KHDA inspection rating tell me about my child's Dubailand school?
faqs.answer: Less than parents expect about a specific subject. KHDA inspects on six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak, and the band is an aggregate across phases, subjects and groups of students. A school can hold a strong overall judgement while one Diploma subject is on its third teacher in two years. The useful part of the report is further in: the subject-level attainment and progress judgements, and the recommendations. Read those before deciding which subject needs support. KHDA regulates and inspects schools and approves curricula; it does not vet individual private tutors, so no tutoring platform can describe itself as approved by it.

faqs.question: How can a tutor help with an Internal Assessment without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: By teaching rather than supplying. A tutor can discuss topic choice and say plainly when a topic cannot generate enough analysis, explain each assessment criterion letter by letter and read the band descriptors as written, teach the research and referencing skills the task needs, question a draft, point out where a conclusion is not supported by the data, and show how a comparable argument is structured elsewhere. What they must never do is provide text. The candidate carries the consequence of malpractice, which can cost the subject or the whole Diploma, so any provider offering a finished piece is offering you your child's risk.

faqs.question: My child sits IGCSE papers in six weeks. Is it worth starting now in Dubailand?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the six weeks are used for paper technique rather than another pass through content. At that range the gains come from timed questions marked against the official mark scheme wording, from learning which question types your child reliably loses marks on, and from fixing the mechanical things, which are usually working that cannot be followed, command terms read too quickly, and the last fifteen minutes of a paper spent on the wrong question. Four to five sessions in a single week during a half-term converts better than the same five spread thinly, because the whole subject stays in mind at once.

faqs.question: How do science practicals work if the lessons are online?
faqs.answer: The laboratory work belongs to the school, and that does not change. What the examination actually tests is planning, observation, recording, analysis and evaluation, and all five are teachable over video. A student can plan an investigation and have the plan picked apart, interpret somebody else's results table, identify the variable that was not controlled, redraw a graph with sensible scales and rewrite a conclusion that overreaches the data. Cambridge and Pearson both assess these skills, either through a practical examination or an alternative written paper, and the alternative paper in particular rewards exactly this kind of work.

faqs.question: What do I need to send to get matched with a tutor in the Dubailand belt?
faqs.answer: Five things: the school, the year group, the board and syllabus code if you know it, the slot that genuinely exists in your week, and a marked script or report page. The script is the most valuable item, because it shows whether marks are being lost on content, on command terms, on timing or on presentation, and those four problems need four different first lessons. If you do not have one, the last report will do. We only collect what is needed to make the match, and you can ask for it to be deleted at any point.

faqs.question: Does the Ministry of Education equivalency file affect an IGCSE student in the Dubailand belt?
faqs.answer: It can, if your child will apply to a UAE university or need a UAE certificate equivalency. For the British track the Ministry requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject figure, which is wrong. Verify your own case on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority; IB Gram describes the process but does not perform it.

intro.heading: You cannot judge teaching you never see, so this page is about what you get to see
paragraphs: A parent who hires an in-home tutor at least gets to watch. You hear the explanation from the next room, you see the exercise book afterwards, and you form a view. Move the same lesson onto video and that casual oversight disappears, which is the real objection behind most searches for a home tutor rather than an online one. It is a fair objection and it deserves a mechanical answer rather than reassurance, so this page sets out exactly what evidence a 4AC1 arrangement produces and when you receive it.

The evidence starts before the teaching does. Nobody at IB Gram plans a first Accounting lesson from a phone conversation. The teacher reads the candidate's most recent marked script, a class test or returned homework, and writes down the error types they can see in it. That written note is the baseline, and it exists before you have paid anything. A tutor who cannot tell you from a marked paper what is going wrong has not yet earned the hour, and you should be able to test that claim at no cost.

Accounting makes this unusually easy to verify, because the subject leaves a trail. Every answer is a ledger account, a journal entry, a statement or a set of workings. There is no essay to interpret and no verbal performance to judge. A posting is either on the right side or it is not. So the weekly note on a 4AC1 arrangement can be concrete in a way that a report on an English session struggles to be: it names the adjustment, the direction of the error and whether the same fault recurred from the previous fortnight.

Pearson helps here too. Its mark schemes for accounting components credit method as well as answer, and carry own-figure rules that let a correct process applied to an earlier wrong number still earn marks. Teaching to that structure produces visible, trackable gains, because a candidate can move several marks without the final figure ever becoming correct. Parents watching only the total miss that movement entirely, which is why the notes you receive report component marks and method credit rather than a single percentage.

None of this promises a grade, and nothing on this page will. Examination outcomes depend on the candidate, the paper and the day, and no tutor controls any of the three. What an evidence-led arrangement can commit to is that you will know, every single week, what was taught, what was marked, which faults repeated from earlier weeks and what the next session is going to target. If that record stops being worth the money it costs, you will be able to see as much from the record itself rather than from a vague feeling at the end of the term.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-accounting-4ac1-home.programmesIntro: An Accounting candidate in Dubai passes through three points where the evidence you need changes shape. Early on it is about whether the recording system has been built; later it is about marks per paper; at the end it is about whether a retake is worth paying for.

programmes.name: Building the recording system
programmes.description: The first year of 4AC1 builds double entry, day books, the cash book and the ledger, finishing at the trial balance. Faults introduced here survive into every later statement, so the useful evidence in Year 10 is not a grade. It is whether the candidate can post an unfamiliar transaction correctly without prompting, which a teacher can test in four minutes and report on honestly.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools vary in when they start 4AC1 content, because some run a three-year Key Stage 4 from Year 9 and others compress it into two years. Ask the department which model your child's campus uses. A candidate on a compressed timetable will meet the year-end adjustments far earlier than a parent expects, and the evidence worth asking for shifts correspondingly sooner.

programmes.name: Marks per paper, not topics covered
programmes.description: By the second year the question stops being what has been taught and becomes how many marks each component is returning. Mocks give the first real data. Reading them properly means separating marks lost to content, marks lost to format and marks lost to running out of time, because those three need different fixes and a grade on the front page hides all of them.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai mock seasons cluster in November and again in February, which gives families two usable data points before the summer series. Many schools in the emirate issue a mock grade without a component breakdown. Asking the subject teacher for the marks per component, rather than the overall grade, is the single most useful request a Dubai parent can make, and it costs nothing.

programmes.name: Deciding what the evidence says about a retake
programmes.description: Pearson results arrive with component marks. A candidate three marks below a grade boundary on one component and thirty below on another is in a completely different position from one evenly short across both, and only the breakdown tells you which. A retake costs an entry fee and a term of effort, so the decision should rest on that breakdown rather than on disappointment.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, where results land during the August holiday for the summer series and in January for November entries, the practical difficulty is that the school is often closed or mid-term when the decision has to be made. Having the component figures in hand, and a teacher who has read them, is what makes a calm decision possible in that window.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-accounting-4ac1-home.subjectsIntro: Each area below carries a specific, observable failure mode. These are the things a weekly note can report on honestly, because they are either happening or they are not.

subjects.name: Posting an unfamiliar transaction
subjects.description: The four-minute diagnostic that tells you whether double entry is a model or a memorised slogan. A candidate who hesitates on direction, rather than on which accounts are involved, has a structural gap worth reporting immediately.

subjects.name: Journal entries that reverse an error
subjects.description: Correcting an error means reversing the original entry, not patching the destination account. Candidates who patch produce answers that look plausible and score nothing. This is visible in a script at a glance, which makes it easy evidence.

subjects.name: Control account differences explained in words
subjects.description: The mark scheme wants the difference accounted for, not eliminated. A candidate who forces a total to agree has learned the wrong objective, and the fault shows up identically on every reconciliation question they attempt.

subjects.name: Depreciation posted to the correct side
subjects.description: Calculation marks are usually secured and posting marks are usually not. Tracking these separately in a weekly note shows movement that a single grade would hide completely, because the arithmetic was never the problem.

subjects.name: Paired adjustments completed in both statements
subjects.description: Accruals, prepayments and the allowance for irrecoverable debts each have two consequences. Half-completed adjustments are the most common recurring fault in the subject, and they are countable, so they belong in the report.

subjects.name: Statement format reproduced from memory
subjects.description: Headings, subtotals and the order of current assets carry marks before any figure is checked. A candidate who can draw the blank pro-forma under time has banked those marks; one who cannot loses them silently every time.

subjects.name: Incomplete records worked backwards
subjects.description: Reconstructing figures from mark-up, margin and control totals separates confident candidates from procedural ones. Progress here is slow and visible, which makes it a good indicator of whether understanding is genuinely deepening.

subjects.name: Three-part interpretation answers
subjects.description: Comparison, cause, consequence. Candidates reliably write the first and stop. Counting how many interpretation answers reach three parts is the clearest single measure of whether exam technique is improving week to week.

subjects.name: Own-figure marks claimed correctly
subjects.description: Where a mark scheme allows own-figure credit, carrying an earlier wrong number forward consistently still earns method marks. Candidates who restart the question instead lose them. Teaching this changes scores without changing understanding.

sections.heading: The own-figure rule, and how a Pearson accounting mark scheme really awards marks
paragraphs: Most families assume an accounting answer is right or wrong. Pearson mark schemes for accounting components do not work that way. They credit method as well as outcome, and they carry own-figure provisions: where a candidate has made an earlier error and then applies the correct process to their own incorrect number, the later marks are still available. A candidate who understands this scores several marks on a question whose final figure never becomes correct, and a candidate who does not scores zero on the same work.

That has two practical consequences. The first is behavioural. Candidates who spot an earlier mistake mid-question often restart, run out of time and abandon the final parts, where most of the marks sit. The correct instruction is to carry the figure forward, label it, and complete the question. Teaching that takes one session and is worth more than a term of content revision for some candidates. It is also observable: either the script shows a completed question or it shows an abandoned one.

The second consequence is about reporting. If method and own-figure marks are available, then progress is measurable below the level of the grade. A weekly note can say that interpretation answers reaching three parts rose from one in four to three in four, or that paired adjustments were completed in both statements on every attempt this fortnight. Those are the sentences you should expect. A report that says your child is improving nicely has told you nothing a mark scheme could verify.

sections.heading: Twelve weeks of 4AC1, and the evidence each block produces
paragraphs: A twelve-week arrangement is long enough to change something and short enough to judge. What follows is the shape most 4AC1 blocks take for a candidate who has the recording topics and is losing marks in the year-end adjustments and the interpretation questions, which describes the majority of requests from Dubai. A candidate with gaps in double entry itself needs the first four weeks spent differently, and the teacher will say so after reading the script rather than after week three.

The sequence matters. Adjustments come before statements, because a statement built on a wrong adjustment cannot be marked usefully. Interpretation comes late, because it needs completed statements to interpret. Timed full papers come last, because they are a measurement instrument rather than a teaching method, and spending week two on a full paper produces a score and no learning. Families who ask for mock papers from the first session are usually asking for reassurance rather than progress.

Each block below names what you should actually receive at the end of it. If a block passes and the evidence described in the table has not arrived, that is a reason to ask a direct question rather than wait for the next report. The whole arrangement is designed so that you can tell it is working without having to take anyone's word for it, which is the only sustainable answer to the oversight problem that sends Dubai parents looking for a home tutor in the first place.

sections.heading: Four diagnostics that tell you whether 4AC1 teaching is working
paragraphs: The first diagnostic is recurrence. Any fault can be explained once and appear to be fixed. The question is whether it returns six weeks later under exam pressure, which is why a recurrence log is kept rather than a topic checklist. A tutor who cannot tell you whether the depreciation posting error has reappeared since October is not tracking the thing that determines the grade. Explanation is cheap; unlearning a procedural habit is the work.

The second is completion. Count abandoned questions. A candidate who restarts after spotting an earlier error and then runs out of time loses marks that were available under own-figure rules. The proportion of questions finished, regardless of accuracy, is a clean measure of whether exam discipline is improving. It needs no judgement to report and it moves quickly once a candidate trusts the rule.

The third is format independence: can the candidate draw the statement layout from memory, under time, with no prompt and no textbook open beside them? Those marks are awarded before any figure is checked and they are lost silently when the layout is only half remembered. The fourth is interpretation depth, counted as the share of written answers that reach a comparison, a cause and a consequence rather than stopping at the first of the three. All four measures are countable, all four appear in the weekly note by name, and none of them requires anyone to make a promise about a grade.

sections.heading: Dubai terms, Ramadan and the weeks revision actually has
paragraphs: The usable revision weeks in a Dubai academic year are fewer than the calendar suggests, and planning from the calendar rather than from the real weeks is how families run out of time. The school year in the emirate runs from late August or early September to early July across three terms, with a winter break in late December and a spring break in the second half of the academic year. The working and school week runs Monday to Friday, so weekend sessions mean Saturday and Sunday.

Ramadan shifts roughly eleven days earlier each year, which places it inside the spring term for the coming cycle and therefore directly across the run-up to the summer series. School days shorten during the month, concentration patterns change, and families who fast reasonably want sessions moved later in the evening. Confirm the announced dates each year rather than working from an estimate, then plan around them deliberately. Sessions after Iftar work well for many households and badly for others, and the only way to know is to try one and ask.

Pearson's two series give the year its real structure. The November window runs late in the first term, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026, and results arriving the following January, as the November 2025 series results reached students on 22 January 2026. The summer series sits after the spring break. The table counts the available weeks honestly, which usually surprises families who assumed the spring term was long.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies running alongside 4AC1
paragraphs: A Dubai timetable is not only the international curriculum. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum the school teaches, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. That means a 4AC1 candidate is carrying mandatory subjects alongside their option blocks, and the hours have to come from somewhere. Families who plan Accounting revision as though the week contained only examined subjects discover the shortfall in February.

The rules are specific enough to be worth knowing. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Two further details affect planning. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Schools must also ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, so support in those subjects follows the school's material rather than an alternative scheme.

sections.heading: What a progress report may say, and what it must never promise
paragraphs: A useful report is boring. It names the topic taught, the questions attempted, the marks awarded against the published criteria, the error types that appeared, and whether any of them had appeared before. It ends with what the next session will target. Nothing in it is an adjective. A parent reading six of those in a row can see a trend without being told there is one, and can see the absence of a trend just as clearly, which is the point of writing them down.

What a report must never contain is a predicted outcome dressed as a commitment. No tutor can promise a grade, a specific improvement or a place at a university, and any provider offering that is selling something they cannot deliver. Examination performance depends on the candidate, the paper and the day. A teacher can report that interpretation answers improved from one in four to three in four; a teacher cannot promise what that converts to in August, and should not imply it.

Two other lines hold firm. Pearson syllabus documents, mark schemes and past papers are referenced and linked from their official source rather than reproduced or supplied as downloads, because reproducing them is a copyright matter. And no statistic appears in a report or on this page without a count, a date and a method behind it, which is why you will find no satisfaction percentage and no star rating here. The record is the evidence, and the record is yours to keep.

faqs.answer: Accounting mark schemes credit method as well as final answer, and own-figure provisions mean that where a candidate makes an earlier error and then applies the correct process to their own incorrect number, later marks remain available. The practical lesson is to carry the wrong figure forward, label it, and finish the question rather than restarting. Candidates who restart run out of time and abandon the parts carrying most of the marks. Confirm how it is applied on the specific component against the published mark schemes at qualifications.pearson.com, which is where the authoritative wording lives.

faqs.question: Why do you count abandoned questions instead of only marking them?
faqs.answer: Because completion is a separate skill from accuracy and it moves faster. A candidate who spots an earlier mistake, restarts and then runs out of time loses marks that own-figure rules had already made available to them. Counting the proportion of questions finished, regardless of whether the final figure is correct, measures exam discipline directly and needs no judgement to report. It is one of the quickest changes to produce visible movement on a 4AC1 script, and it tends to improve within three sessions once a candidate trusts the rule.

faqs.question: My child understands Accounting in class but loses marks in exams. Why?
faqs.answer: Three causes account for most of it, and a marked script usually shows which. Format marks are lost when a statement layout is half remembered under time, before any figure is checked. Paired adjustments are half completed, so the income statement is corrected and the position statement is not. And interpretation answers stop after the comparison without reaching a cause or a consequence. None of those is a knowledge gap, which is why more content revision does not fix them. Each one is countable, so the weekly note can show whether it is actually changing.

faqs.question: How many weeks before we can see whether the arrangement is working?
faqs.answer: Two sessions produce the first comparable data and six weeks produce a trend. A twelve-week block is the usual unit, because it is long enough to change a procedural habit and short enough to judge without committing to a year. Movement in completion and format marks tends to appear early; interpretation depth and incomplete-records confidence move more slowly. The honest answer at week two is whether the right faults were identified, which the script and the first marked questions will show. Grade movement is not visible that fast and anyone claiming otherwise is guessing.

faqs.question: Can a tutor guarantee my child a particular Accounting grade?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider offering that should be treated with real scepticism. Examination performance depends on the candidate, the paper and the day, and no tutor controls any of the three. What can be committed to is a weekly record naming what was taught, what was marked, which faults recurred and what the next session targets. That record lets you judge the teaching on its own terms. A guarantee is a sales device, and in this market it is often attached to conditions that are never published on the same page.

faqs.question: Will the teacher follow my child's school scheme of work for 4AC1?
faqs.answer: Yes, by default. Running a parallel course means the candidate meets each topic twice at different times and consolidates neither, so sessions follow the school's topic order and reinforce what was taught that week. The exception is where the baseline note shows a structural gap in the recording system, because statements built on faulty double entry cannot be marked usefully. In that case the first weeks go backwards deliberately and the note will say so plainly, rather than quietly running a different syllabus and reporting as though nothing changed.

faqs.question: Can we get Pearson past papers and mark schemes from the tutor?
faqs.answer: They are referenced and linked from their official source rather than reproduced or supplied as downloads. Pearson specifications, past papers and mark schemes are published at qualifications.pearson.com, and copying them into handouts is a copyright matter rather than a service. There is a practical benefit as well: working from the live source means your child practises against the current document rather than a cached copy from three specification revisions ago. The teacher will tell you which papers to work from and in what order, which is the part that actually needs expertise.

faqs.question: How do mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons affect revision time?
faqs.answer: They take real timetable hours. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA calculates instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Plan the Accounting week around the real timetable rather than the examined subjects alone. Families who count only option blocks consistently find themselves short of revision weeks by the second term.

faqs.question: What should I ask my child's school for before a tutoring arrangement starts?
faqs.answer: Three things, all free. The component marks from the most recent mock rather than the overall grade, because the breakdown is what identifies the fix. The specification code and the series your child is entered for, confirmed in writing by the exams officer. And the most recent marked script itself, which the school will usually release on request. With those three a teacher can produce a real baseline note. Without them, any plan offered to you is an assumption about an average candidate rather than a statement about yours.

faqs.question: Does the evidence record change in the weeks before a Pearson series?
faqs.answer: Yes, deliberately. Up to that point the useful measures are error types and recurrence, because the work is unlearning procedural faults. In the last six to ten weeks the record shifts to marks per component on full timed papers, plus time spent per question, because the task becomes converting existing knowledge into marks under the clock. Priority is set by marks lost per hour of revision rather than by topic order. The block also has a defined stop point, since revision running into the exam day costs more in fatigue than it returns.

faqs.question: What happens if the notes show the teaching is not working?
faqs.answer: You stop, or the match changes, and the record is what makes that conversation straightforward. Every six to eight weeks the notes get read together and a decision gets made: continue, change frequency, change teacher, or end it. Some families take the written plan and work it themselves, which is a legitimate outcome and sometimes the right one. A record designed to show movement also shows its absence, and a provider unwilling to act on that is relying on inertia rather than on results.

faqs.question: Can sessions move later in the evening during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and many Dubai families ask for exactly that. School days shorten during the month and concentration patterns change, so a 17:00 slot that worked in January often does not work then. Post-Iftar sessions suit some households well and others not at all, and the only way to find out is to try one and review it honestly. Confirm the announced dates for the year rather than working from an estimate, then rebuild the weekly rhythm around them. Because delivery is over video, moving a slot costs nothing and no travel has to be rearranged.

intro.heading: The price of 4AC1 help in Dubai, and what you are actually buying
paragraphs: Three of the six pages currently ranking for Accounting tuition in Dubai publish no price at all. Two quote in US dollars, a currency no Dubai family pays a tutor in. This page starts in dirhams because that is the first question every parent asks and the last one the market answers. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Accounting carries the code 4AC1, it is examined by written paper with no coursework component, and the going rate for one-to-one teaching on it in Dubai sits in a band wide enough that two families can pay AED 120 and AED 480 for the same hour and both believe they got a fair deal.

The band is wide because an Accounting hour is not one commodity. A university student who sat the subject themselves three years ago, teaching from a textbook, is selling supervision. A teacher who has marked stacks of scripts on this specification is selling diagnosis: the ability to look at a candidate's trial balance and name which standard error type produced the difference, then build the next forty minutes around that single fault. Both appear in the same search results. Neither advertises which one they are, and the hourly figure alone will not tell you.

What moves the number in Dubai is specific to Dubai. The emirate has 227 private schools serving 387,441 pupils across 17 curricula, with 37 per cent of those pupils on a UK curriculum. The Accounting cohort is therefore large in total but thin on each campus. Few schools time-table more than one Accounting teacher, so when a Year 11 group loses its specialist mid-year the demand for private help spikes inside one community, and in-home rates in that cluster follow the shortage. Online delivery flattens that curve, because the pool is no longer limited to whoever can reach Al Barsha by half past four.

KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai will not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. For a household already paying those fees, the freeze is the backdrop against which a tutoring decision gets made: the school line is fixed, so the discretionary education spend is where the arithmetic happens. Knowing the market band, and knowing what makes one hour worth more than another, is the difference between buying teaching and buying attendance.

Everything below is costed, dated and attributed. Where a figure comes from a published provider rate it is described by provider model and the month it was checked, not by brand name. Where a figure would be ours, it is not published at all: IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson rather than from a price list, and a number invented for a landing page would be worse than silence. What follows instead is the specification, the error patterns, the Pearson calendar and the permit position, which together decide whether the hour you pay for comes back as marks.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-accounting-4ac1-tuto.programmesIntro: Accounting sits at one point in a longer route: an option chosen in Year 9, examined at 16, then either dropped or carried into a post-16 course that assumes it. The stages below are where a 4AC1 decision actually gets made, and each one changes what an hour of teaching should be spent on.

programmes.name: The option block that leads to Accounting
programmes.description: Accounting is almost never compulsory. It appears in a Year 9 option column alongside Business, Economics and a second language, and the choice is usually made on a twenty-minute conversation at an options evening. Families pick it because it sounds practical, then discover in Year 10 that it rewards procedural accuracy far more than commercial instinct. An hour of teaching at this stage is worth spending on whether the subject suits the candidate at all.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the option conversation is complicated by the fact that many British-curriculum schools offer Business Studies and Accounting in the same block, forcing a choice between them. Schools inspected by KHDA publish their option booklets in the spring term, and the Accounting group in a single Dubai campus is often small enough that the subject runs only if enough pupils choose it. Asking the head of department how many sat it last series is a fair question.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Accounting
programmes.description: The qualification itself: double entry, the books of original entry, control accounts, year-end adjustments, the financial statements of sole traders, partnerships and limited companies, manufacturing accounts, incomplete records, and ratio analysis. Assessment is by written paper, split across two components, with no coursework and no internally assessed element. That matters for tutoring, because every mark is won in exam conditions rather than in a portfolio built over months.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools entering 4AC1 do so through their own Pearson centre number, and the entry is made by the school's exams officer, not by the family. Ask which series your child is entered for and get the code confirmed in writing: a candidate preparing from Cambridge 0452 material for a Pearson 4AC1 entry will meet question styles they have never practised. The two specifications cover similar ground but ask for it differently.

programmes.name: Where 4AC1 leads after Year 11
programmes.description: A good 4AC1 grade opens A Level Accounting where a school offers it, A Level Business or Economics where it does not, BTEC Business, or IB Diploma Business Management and Economics. None of those courses formally require Accounting at 16. What they assume is comfort with structured numerical reasoning and the discipline of showing workings, both of which 4AC1 trains hard.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's post-16 market splits sharply: most British-curriculum schools run A Levels, a growing group runs the IB Diploma, and 2026-27 adds seven new private schools to the emirate, four on a UK curriculum and three offering the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. A candidate who may move between those routes benefits from understanding why the same ratio is read differently in A Level Accounting and in IB Business Management.

programmes.name: Sitting 4AC1 as a private candidate
programmes.ageRange: Any age · outside a school entry
programmes.description: Some families in Dubai sit Accounting outside their child's school entry, usually because the school does not offer the subject or the timetable will not carry it. A private candidate finds an examination centre that accepts external entries, pays that centre's entry and administration fee directly, and meets the same deadlines a school candidate does without a school chasing them.
programmes.countryNote: The practical constraint in Dubai is centre availability rather than the specification. Entry fees for private candidates are set by the centre and vary, so collect two or three written quotes before committing, and confirm that the centre is approved to run the Pearson International GCSE series you want. The family carries the admin burden here: registration dates, identity documents and the timetable are all yours to track.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-accounting-4ac1-tuto.subjectsIntro: A 4AC1 grade is decided in a small number of places. The areas below are where candidates in the Dubai cohort most often lose marks, each with what the paper is actually testing and what an hour of teaching should fix first.

subjects.name: Double entry and the books of original entry
subjects.description: Day books, the cash book, the petty cash imprest system and the three-column ledger. Candidates who learned the rule as a slogan rather than as a model of two accounts moving together make consistent, predictable errors here, and those errors propagate into every later statement.

subjects.name: The trial balance and correction of errors
subjects.description: A difference on the trial balance has a short list of possible causes. Knowing which error types a trial balance can detect, and which it cannot, converts a guessing question into a procedure. Marks are lost by correcting the symptom in the wrong account rather than reversing the original entry.

subjects.name: Control accounts and bank reconciliation
subjects.description: Sales and purchases ledger control accounts, and the reconciliation between the cash book and the bank statement. These questions reward candidates who can hold two records side by side and explain a difference rather than force it to zero. Timing differences and unpresented cheques are the usual sticking point.

subjects.name: Depreciation and asset disposal
subjects.description: Straight line and reducing balance methods, the provision for depreciation account, and the profit or loss on disposal. Candidates routinely calculate the charge correctly and then post it to the wrong side, or forget that the disposal removes both the cost and the accumulated depreciation.

subjects.name: Accruals, prepayments and irrecoverable debts
subjects.description: The adjustments that turn a cash record into a profit figure. Each one touches both the income statement and the statement of financial position, and the mark scheme follows both. Most lost marks come from adjusting one and not the other, or from the sign going the wrong way.

subjects.name: Financial statements of sole traders
subjects.description: Income statement and statement of financial position, prepared from a trial balance plus a list of adjustments. The format itself carries marks: headings, subtotals, the order of current assets, and the treatment of drawings. Presentation is not decoration in this paper, it is assessed.

subjects.name: Partnership accounts
subjects.description: Appropriation accounts, interest on capital, partners' salaries, and current versus capital accounts. The arithmetic is modest; the difficulty is keeping the partnership agreement's terms straight and applying them in the order the question gives them rather than the order the candidate remembers.

subjects.name: Limited company accounts
subjects.description: Share capital, reserves, and the statement of changes in equity in the form the specification expects at this level. Candidates who have met company accounts only through newspaper coverage bring assumptions that do not match the required layout, and lose marks on structure before they lose any on calculation.

subjects.name: Manufacturing accounts and incomplete records
subjects.description: Prime cost, factory overheads and the transfer to the income statement; then the reverse problem, reconstructing figures from fragments using mark-up, margin and control totals. Incomplete records questions are where strong candidates separate themselves, because they require working backwards confidently.

subjects.name: Ratio analysis and interpretation
subjects.description: Profitability, liquidity and efficiency ratios, then the written interpretation. Calculation marks are usually secured; the interpretation marks are usually not. The paper wants a comparison, a cause and a consequence for the business, in that order, and candidates stop after the comparison.
