sections.heading: What Business tuition costs in the Dubai market, in dirhams
paragraphs: Pricing in this market is unusually opaque. Of the providers ranking for these searches, three publish no hourly figure at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars rather than dirhams. The bands below come from providers' own published pricing and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. They describe the market rather than an IB Gram price list, and they are here so a parent can place a quote before accepting it.

Budget online provision runs from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject teacher online sits between about AED 150 and AED 300, with Unitors advertising IGCSE from AED 150. In-home one-to-one, travel included, is commonly AED 180 to AED 500, with Bestimate's band at AED 180 to 350 and independently advertised home tutors reaching AED 500. Subject specialists at IGCSE and A Level run AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named tutors reach AED 650 at BartyED. Monthly packages appear at AED 799 online for eight sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 in-home for four two-hour sessions.

For Business there is a specific thing to ask about, and it is not the rate. Ask whether extended answers are marked in writing between lessons, because a tutor who talks through an answer verbally is not doing the work that moves the marks. Marking one extended answer properly takes twenty to thirty minutes outside the lesson. A provider charging specialist money without it is selling the cheap half of the service, and the rate card will not tell you which you are being offered.

Context for the budget: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for 2026-27. For most families the live question is how few tuition hours can do the job rather than how many are affordable. The honest answer for 4BS1 is that one weekly hour with marking from the autumn of Year 11 outperforms three hours a week bought in April, because the limiting factor is how much marked correction a student can act on.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the Pearson series for a Business candidate
paragraphs: No competitor page in this cluster names an exam session, a deadline or a results date, which leaves parents to guess whether tuition bought in February can still work. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year, Dubai centres use both, and entry deadlines sit months before the papers. Entries are handled by the school's exams officer, never by a tutor.

The published milestones worth diarising are these. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, and provisional documents can be revised — so the live timetable at qualifications.pearson.com is the authority rather than any figure restated on a tutoring page.

Counting backwards reorders the plan in a way that matters for this subject specifically. Stimulus reading belongs first and early, because every other skill is applied to it. Calculation drilling runs in short bursts throughout, because accuracy decays and because a calculation met in February will be forgotten by May without revisiting. Extended answers need to start early enough to accumulate twenty or more marked responses before the series, which means autumn rather than spring. Whole papers belong in the final six weeks and teach little before then, because a student without the reading routine will repeat the same omission across every paper.

For resit candidates the window is tighter than it looks: results in August, an entry decision within days, and a paper in late October or November. That plan should be built deliberately around error analysis of the actual script rather than by compressing a May plan, because the fastest gains come from the specific marks that were lost.

sections.heading: Model answers, mocks and the honesty line
paragraphs: 4BS1 has no coursework, which removes the sharpest version of the academic-honesty problem. Nothing a tutor touches is submitted for assessment. What remains are two softer questions that parents ask and that deserve straight answers.

The first is about model answers. Showing a student a strong response and taking it apart is legitimate teaching and good practice; handing over a bank of answers to memorise is not teaching at all, and it fails in the exam, because the stimulus will be different and a memorised answer cannot engage with it. We use exemplars the way a cookery teacher uses a finished dish — to show what the target looks like — and then make the student build their own from the stimulus in front of them.

The second is about school mocks and assessments. A mock is the school's assessment and a tutor should not be inside it. Preparing for a mock is proper work; discussing a mock after it has been sat and marked is the single most useful hour in a term. Writing any part of an answer that will be submitted as a student's own is not something to go looking for, and a tutor who offers it is telling you something about the rest of their service.

On materials, Pearson's specification, past papers, mark schemes and sample assessment materials are published documents. We cite them and link them; we do not reproduce or redistribute them, and we do not hold or offer unreleased material. A tutor claiming access to papers or grade boundaries before publication is a reason to walk away rather than a competitive advantage. For students who continue to the IB Diploma later, the internal assessment rules are stricter again, and the habit of doing one's own work is worth establishing at 16.

sections.heading: Why the search says tutor in Dubai and the lesson happens on video
paragraphs: Parents search for a tutor in Dubai, so the delivery answer belongs in plain words rather than in a footnote. IB Gram delivers 4BS1 tuition to Dubai families one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. We do not make home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. Nobody will be arriving at a Dubai address, and a page that leaves that ambiguous is worth a second read.

For Business the format suits the work. Case-study material can be shown on screen and annotated by both people at once, which is better than two heads over one printed sheet. Calculations are worked on a shared whiteboard, with every version saved so the student ends a block with a formula sheet in their own hand. Marked extended answers arrive as files the parent can open, which is a firmer record than a verbal summary at the door. And the comparison that matters most is the pool: an online family chooses a teacher of this specification, while an in-home family chooses from those willing to drive to their community at a particular hour.

Removing travel also removes the main cause of hours paid for and not delivered. A visit lost to traffic, a flat tyre or half-term travel is usually an hour gone. An online session moves to another slot, runs during school exam leave, and continues from a hotel room. Over a year that difference is several sessions, which is a real number at Dubai rates.

On the legal framework, private tutoring in the UAE operates under the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible categories include teachers in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure quoted at you as unverified; MoHRE's private tutor licensing page is the official route. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai is a separate legal animal requiring a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which IB Gram neither holds nor claims.

sections.heading: KHDA inspection reports, option blocks and what the grade is for
paragraphs: Three questions close the page out, and all three have concrete answers that the pages currently ranking for this search do not give.

On schools, Dubai private schools are regulated by KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, and which inspects annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. The published report is more useful to a parent than the headline band: it comments on teaching and assessment and on student outcomes by phase, and a department's standing can differ markedly from the school's overall rating. For other emirates the map is ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

On equivalency, the Ministry of Education's British-track requirements were clarified publicly in 2026: five subjects recognised at GCSE or IGCSE at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary Levels at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five, and Business can sit inside them. One page ranking in this market states that six IGCSE subjects are required; the sourced figure is five. Equivalency is a Ministry process we describe and never perform or guarantee, and moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation channel is where to verify it. Nothing about tutoring is required for it.

On what the grade is for, Business at 16 is not a prerequisite for a business degree and no page should suggest that any subject or any tutoring is required for a university place. What it does provide is early practice at reading a situation and making a defensible decision about it, which is the skill the first year of a management or finance degree assumes. Meanwhile Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the licensed curriculum in every Dubai private school, with separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs and instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, which is real timetable arithmetic when deciding how many tuition hours a week can carry.

process.title: Send the code, a mock paper and the slot
process.description: Pearson 4BS1 confirmed rather than assumed, the most recent mock or marked assessment, and the evening slot that survives a bad week. The mock is the valuable one: it shows within minutes whether the losses are stimulus reading, calculations, chains or timing.

process.title: A trial lesson at no charge
process.description: Thirty minutes with the tutor who would actually teach, no card details taken, nothing owed afterwards. The student reads one case study aloud and attempts two calculations. That is usually enough to identify which of the three skills is costing the grade.

process.title: Stimulus reading first, almost always
process.description: Three or four sessions on annotation before any extended answers are attempted, because every other skill is applied to the case study. Families find this odd for a fortnight and persuasive by the fourth session, when answers get shorter and start scoring better.

process.title: Calculations drilled in short bursts, not blocks
process.description: Timed sets of five from a blank page, with the formula written before the numbers and the unit treated as part of the answer. Spread across the year rather than taught once, because accuracy decays and a formula met in February is gone by May.

process.title: Weekly extended answer, then review at six weeks
process.description: One answer written midweek, marked before the session, with the hour spent pushing chains to a second consequence. At six weeks we compare the baseline against a current script and decide whether to continue, change tutor or reduce hours.

whyPoints.title: The stimulus is treated as the exam
whyPoints.description: A forty-second annotation routine drilled until it survives exam pressure: classify the firm, mark the two load-bearing figures, find the constraint. Students who learn it write shorter answers that score higher, which is the clearest single improvement available in this subject.

whyPoints.title: Calculations drilled with units, not just method
whyPoints.description: Break-even, contribution, margin of safety, profit margins, market share, cash-flow closing balances. The marks are lost to a missing percentage sign or a per-unit confusion rather than to the arithmetic, so the drill is presentation discipline from a blank page against a clock.

whyPoints.title: Chains pushed to the second consequence
whyPoints.description: The tutor asks 'and therefore' until the chain runs out, usually three iterations. Each link is tied back to something in the stimulus, which is why the reading routine comes first. Students who stop at one consequence are not weaker; they think stopping is finishing.

whyPoints.title: Local examples that name a mechanism
whyPoints.description: A hub airline for economies of scale, free zones for location incentives, Dubai's capped 2026-27 school fees for a price ceiling with rising demand. One or two sentences, mechanism stated, then straight back to the firm in the stimulus where the marks are.

faqs.question: What does Edexcel IGCSE Business 4BS1 examine in each paper?
faqs.answer: The specification covers business activity and enterprise, people in business, business finance, marketing and business operations, assessed by written examination using stimulus material supplied in the paper. There is no coursework, so every mark is earned on the day. The exact component structure, durations and weightings are published on the current specification at qualifications.pearson.com, which is the document to check rather than any tutor's recollection. What matters more for planning is that nothing is banked and nothing is lost: a weak mock leaves every mark still available.

faqs.question: Which calculations must my child know for 4BS1 Business?
faqs.answer: Revenue, total costs, contribution per unit, break-even output, margin of safety, gross and net profit margin, market share and cash-flow closing balances. None is mathematically hard and all of them leak marks to presentation: a per-unit figure used as a total, a margin left as a decimal, a closing balance that ignores the opening one. The habit worth most is writing the formula before the numbers, which protects against the commonest error in the subject — dividing fixed costs by price instead of by contribution.

faqs.question: Why does my child's Business answer stop at one reason?
faqs.answer: Because stopping feels like finishing. Asked what happens when a firm raises prices, most students write that revenue per unit rises and end the paragraph. The marks sit further along: revenue per unit rises, so total revenue rises only if demand holds, which for a firm with a few large business customers it may not, and if they switch the lost share is slow to rebuild. We teach it by asking 'and therefore' until the chain runs out, usually three iterations, and tying each link to the stimulus.

faqs.question: Can my child write about Emirates or Careem in a Business exam?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the example names a mechanism. A sentence about a famous local company that does not explain a cost, pricing or risk consequence reads as padding. A hub airline illustrates economies of scale and concentration risk; a locally founded ride-hailing business illustrates external finance, growth and exit for its owners. Keep it to one or two sentences, state the mechanism, and return immediately to the firm in the stimulus, which is where the marks are actually attached.

faqs.question: Is Edexcel IGCSE Business a written-exam-only subject?
faqs.answer: Yes. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Business is assessed entirely by written examination, with no coursework or controlled assessment component. That has two consequences worth explaining to a student. Timed practice is the whole of the preparation, because there is no portfolio mark to protect a weak paper. And nothing is lost in advance: a student with a disappointing January mock still has every mark available, which is a more useful thing to hear at sixteen than encouragement.

faqs.question: How much of 4BS1 is numbers rather than writing?
faqs.answer: Less than parents fear and more than students prepare for. The quantitative element is arithmetic with units — percentages, ratios, simple multiplication and division — plus reading figures accurately from a table or a cash-flow forecast. It is a minority of the paper by marks but a reliable source of lost ones, because students revise the writing and assume the sums. A short calculation drill repeated in bursts across the year is one of the cheapest grade improvements available in the subject.

faqs.question: What does a Business IGCSE tutor charge an hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates run roughly AED 45 to 150 for budget online provision, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject teacher online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit with travel included, and AED 200 to 450 or above for a subject specialist. Those bands come from providers' own published pricing and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table. The question that matters more than the rate is whether extended answers are marked in writing between lessons, because that is the work that moves the marks.

faqs.question: How do break-even questions work in Edexcel Business?
faqs.answer: Break-even output is fixed costs divided by contribution per unit, where contribution is selling price minus variable cost per unit. The answer is in units, never in currency. The commonest error is dividing by price instead of contribution, which is why we insist the formula is written before the numbers. Margin of safety then follows as actual or budgeted output minus break-even output, again in units unless a percentage is requested. Showing the intermediate figure matters, because method marks exist and a bare wrong answer earns nothing.

faqs.question: My child confuses cash flow with profit in Business. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: Extremely, and it is a definition problem rather than a reasoning one, which makes it quick to fix. Profit is revenue minus costs over a period; cash flow is money actually moving in and out, which can be negative in a profitable month if customers pay late. The clearest demonstration is a cash-flow forecast where a profitable firm runs out of money, built once with the student rather than explained. Most students stop confusing the two after building that example themselves.

faqs.question: Should my child take Business 4BS1 or Economics 4EC1 in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The honest difference is the unit of analysis. Business reasons about one named firm from a case study; Economics reasons about markets and economies using diagrams. Students who like concrete decisions and have a head for figures often prefer Business; those comfortable with abstraction and graphs tend to prefer Economics. Taking both is common in Dubai and works, provided the registers stay separate — a Business answer that drifts into government policy scores as poorly as an Economics answer that becomes a management memo.

faqs.question: Do Dubai schools enter Business for the November series?
faqs.answer: Some do, chiefly for resit candidates and for students who joined late. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year, and the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers and are handled by the school's exams officer, not by a tutor. If a November entry is a possibility, raise it before summer results arrive, because the deadline will not wait for a change of mind once the grade is known.

faqs.question: How many 4BS1 topics are there and which are hardest?
faqs.answer: The specification groups content into enterprise and business activity, people in business, finance, marketing and operations. Across marked scripts the hardest in practice are cash flow and sources of finance, not because the ideas are difficult but because they combine a calculation with a judgement and students meet them late. Break-even is the third, and almost all of its lost marks are the same single error. Ask your child's teacher for the scheme of work order, because what is 'hard' is usually what was taught last.

faqs.question: Are Business lessons for Dubai students run over video?
faqs.answer: Yes. Sessions are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE — home visiting is a service we run only in India. The format suits the subject: case studies are annotated by both people on screen, calculations are worked on a shared whiteboard with every version saved, and marked extended answers arrive as files. It also means the tutor is chosen on 4BS1 experience rather than on willingness to drive to your community.

faqs.question: Does KHDA publish anything useful about a school's Business results?
faqs.answer: KHDA is responsible for overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai and inspects schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. The published report is more useful than the headline band: it comments on teaching, assessment and student outcomes by phase, and a single department can sit well above or below the school's overall rating. It will not give you subject-level grade distributions, so for that the honest route is to ask the head of department directly how the Business cohort performed.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a Business mock answer without writing it?
faqs.answer: Preparing for a mock is proper work, and discussing a mock after it has been sat and marked is probably the most useful hour in a term — the script shows exactly which marks were lost and why. What a tutor should not do is contribute to any answer that will be submitted as the student's own. Model answers are useful as exemplars to take apart, not as banks to memorise, because the stimulus in the real paper will differ and a remembered answer cannot engage with it.

faqs.question: How early in Year 10 should Business tutoring start?
faqs.answer: Earlier is cheaper, which surprises families. A short Year 10 block that installs the stimulus-reading routine and the calculation discipline leaves a student able to use their school teaching properly for the whole of Year 11, rather than paying someone later to supply what the school already provides. The risk is decay: calculation accuracy fades without practice. A refresher in the autumn of Year 11 protects the earlier work at a fraction of the cost of a full year of weekly hours.

intro.heading: What the paper asks, and what your child's script says about it
paragraphs: A marked chemistry script is a document most parents cannot read, and schools rarely have time to translate it. The grade is at the front, a few comments appear in the margin, and somewhere inside it there is a precise account of what went wrong. That account is usually not about understanding chemistry. It is about a missing state symbol, an equation balanced on one side only, an observation described as a colour change rather than as a white precipitate, or a two-step calculation abandoned after the first step.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry is examined through Paper 1C, two hours for 110 marks, and Paper 2C, one hour fifteen minutes for 70 marks. That is 180 marks in total, with Paper 1C carrying 61.1% of the subject total and Paper 2C 38.9%. The entry is untiered, so there is no Foundation or Higher decision to make, and the result is reported on the 9 to 1 scale. There is no coursework and no separate practical examination, though practical chemistry is examined throughout both written papers.

The specification is organised into four sections: Principles of chemistry, Inorganic chemistry, Physical chemistry and Organic chemistry. A student does not experience it that way. They experience a sequence of question stems, each with a particular shape of answer that earns credit, and most of the gap between a grade 6 and a grade 8 script lives in whether the student recognises the shape. Describe a test for a sulfate wants a reagent, a condition and an observation in that order. Explain in terms of structure wants the structure and then the consequence, as two separate statements.

That is why this page is organised around script detail rather than around topics. It sets out the equation types a 4CH1 candidate must write, the precise observation wording for the qualitative tests, the question stems and what each one awards, and the presentation conventions that lose marks silently: state symbols, significant figures, units on concentration answers, charges written on ions. None of this is advanced chemistry. All of it is examined, and almost all of it is teachable inside a handful of sessions once somebody has read the script and named the pattern.

On delivery, the honest position first. Parents search for a home tutor because the child is at home in Dubai and the problem is urgent, and the phrase deserves an answer rather than a deflection. The in-home chemistry market in the emirate is real, and published rates sit at AED 180 to 350 an hour in Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table, with home tutors advertising to AED 500, largely because travel sits inside the figure. IB Gram does not operate in it. Lessons are delivered one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service offered only in India. For a script-level problem, working on a shared screen with the marked paper open is in several respects better than sitting beside it.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-chemistry-4ch1-home-.programmesIntro: Three things change what a 4CH1 student needs, and none of them is the specification. They are how long the school's Key Stage 4 runs, what the student was studying before they arrived in Dubai, and what else is on the timetable alongside chemistry.

programmes.name: The year before 4CH1 starts
programmes.description: The cheapest place to intervene in chemistry and the most commonly skipped. The skills that decide a 4CH1 grade are mostly mathematical and notational: ratio, rearranging, standard form, writing formulae from charges, balancing. A Year 9 student who can do those arrives at the specification able to learn chemistry rather than fighting arithmetic. One term of weekly work here removes a problem that costs several times as much to remove in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools differ on whether Year 9 is a general science year or already the first year of a three-year Key Stage 4. Ask the head of science which model applies and request the scheme of work. A three-year course means the first 4CH1 content lands in Year 9 and the student is being assessed on it a full two years before the paper.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry
programmes.description: Two written papers, 180 marks, untiered, no coursework, four specification sections. The qualification rewards precision more than breadth: a student who writes equations correctly, gives observations in the scheme's words and completes multi-step calculations will out-score a student who knows more chemistry and presents it loosely. That is an encouraging fact, because precision is teachable in weeks and breadth is not.
programmes.countryNote: Check the exam entry statement for the code. Dubai schools frequently enter Pearson for one science and Cambridge for another, and Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry is assessed differently, including its practical arrangements. A family tutoring to the wrong specification usually discovers it in the first session, which is a wasted hour that a two-minute check prevents.

programmes.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside chemistry
programmes.ageRange: All year groups in Dubai private schools
programmes.description: These subjects are required in every Dubai private school regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed for, and they occupy real timetable space that a chemistry revision plan has to respect. Families budgeting tutoring hours routinely forget them, then find there is no free evening left. Knowing the weekly load before planning a chemistry block avoids a commitment nobody can keep.
programmes.countryNote: KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with the advice that no mandatory lesson run shorter than 25 minutes, and the requirements applied from the start of the 2025-26 academic year.

programmes.name: Arriving mid-course from another curriculum
programmes.description: Dubai's school population turns over constantly, and a student joining a 4CH1 class from an American, Indian or national-curriculum background has a specific and diagnosable gap rather than a general weakness. Usually it is notation and equation convention rather than content: the chemistry is familiar, the way Pearson expects it written is not. Three or four sessions on convention closes most of it.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's private sector offered 17 different curricula across 227 schools in 2024-25, with 387,441 students enrolled, so mid-course transfers between curricula are ordinary here rather than exceptional. Seven new private schools join the 2026-27 intake, adding 16,846 places, which means more cohorts assembled from mixed backgrounds in the same chemistry classroom.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-chemistry-4ch1-home-.subjectsIntro: The ten items below are not topics. They are the discrete skills a 4CH1 script is marked on, which is the level at which lost marks are actually diagnosable. Each lists where it is examined and the error that recurs.

subjects.name: Writing formulae from charges
subjects.description: Deriving the formula of a compound from the charges on its ions, including polyatomic ions such as sulfate, nitrate, carbonate and ammonium. A student who cannot do this cannot write a correct equation, so the error propagates through the whole paper. The recurring mistake is a missing bracket in a formula with two polyatomic ions.

subjects.name: Balancing symbol equations
subjects.description: Balancing by inspection without altering a formula. The error that costs marks is changing a subscript to balance an equation, which produces a different substance. Students also stop after balancing the atoms they noticed first, leaving hydrogen or oxygen unbalanced because those were counted last.

subjects.name: Ionic equations and spectator ions
subjects.description: Writing the net ionic equation by removing the ions present unchanged on both sides, with charges and state symbols intact. A compact, teachable skill most students have never been taught explicitly, and securing it recovers marks in salt preparation, precipitation tests and electrolysis in the same two or three sessions.

subjects.name: Half equations at electrodes
subjects.description: Writing the oxidation and reduction half equations at the anode and cathode, with electrons balanced. The usual loss is an unbalanced electron count or an equation written with the electrons on the wrong side. Once secure, electrolysis becomes one of the most predictable mark sources on the paper.

subjects.name: Two-step mole calculations
subjects.description: Mass to moles, moles through the equation ratio, moles back to mass or volume. Single-step questions are usually answered; two-step questions are where scripts stop halfway and earn one mark of three. Writing the equation ratio explicitly before substituting is the habit that fixes it.

subjects.name: Titration and concentration arithmetic
subjects.description: Moles per cubic decimetre, grams per cubic decimetre, converting burette readings in cubic centimetres, and using the mole ratio from the equation. The characteristic error is an answer out by a factor of a thousand with otherwise correct working, which is a unit problem rather than a chemistry one.

subjects.name: Qualitative analysis observations
subjects.description: Flame colours, precipitate colours with sodium hydroxide, tests for carbonate, sulfate, halide and ammonium ions, and the gas tests. Marked on exact wording: a white precipitate scores where a colour change does not. Pure recall with a predictable question style and among the cheapest marks available.

subjects.name: Bond energy and sign conventions
subjects.description: Calculating overall energy change from bond energies broken and formed, and assigning the correct sign. Most of the loss here is a sign error rather than an arithmetic one, usually because the student added the two totals instead of subtracting, or dropped the negative on an exothermic answer.

subjects.name: Equilibrium explanation answers
subjects.description: Stating the direction of shift and the reason, in two separate statements. Answers that say the equilibrium moves without saying which way, or that name a condition without saying what it does to yield, score half. The Haber process is the context most often used in these questions.

subjects.name: Organic naming, isomers and purification
subjects.description: Naming within the homologous series, drawing and identifying structural isomers, and describing filtration, crystallisation and distillation in the right order. Organic questions are pattern-based and the recall load is smaller than students assume once the general formulae are secure.

sections.heading: What a home tutor would do, and what happens over video instead
paragraphs: The phrase home tutor describes a delivery method, and the honest answer is that IB Gram does not use it anywhere in the UAE. Chemistry lessons run one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service offered only in India. The in-home market in Dubai is real and families use it: published rates run AED 180 to 350 an hour in Bestimate's 2026 table, with individual home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online and AED 200 to 450 and above for a specialist.

For a script-level chemistry problem, the comparison is not obvious in the direction most parents assume. The work in a 4CH1 session is reading a marked paper, writing equations, correcting notation and redrafting an observation answer. All of that happens on a surface both people can write on. Over video that surface is a shared screen that captures everything: the annotated question, the corrected equation, the redrafted answer. In a living room it is the student's own exercise book, and whatever the tutor wrote in it leaves with the handwriting.

What an in-home session genuinely gives is presence. A person in the room, a phone put away, and a parent who can see the hour happening. Those matter, particularly for a younger student or one who will not start work unsupervised. The counterweight is selection: a visiting tutor must be someone who could reach that community at that hour, which in the newer interior communities of Dubai is a small group and has nothing to do with whether they have taught Pearson 4CH1. The table sets the two side by side on the things that matter for this specification.

sections.heading: The equations a 4CH1 candidate has to be able to write
paragraphs: Equation writing is the load-bearing notation skill of this specification, and it is examined in four distinct forms that students routinely treat as one. A word equation, a balanced symbol equation, a net ionic equation and an electrode half equation each have different rules, and a candidate who has only practised the second form will lose marks on the other three without understanding why. Separating them explicitly, and drilling them separately, is a couple of sessions of work with a disproportionate return.

The commonest single error in the whole subject sits here: balancing an equation by changing a subscript inside a formula. It is understandable, it produces a balanced line, and it describes a different substance, so it earns nothing. The second commonest is stopping once the atoms the student noticed first are balanced, which usually leaves hydrogen or oxygen out. The third is omitting state symbols in a question that required them, which is a presentation mark rather than a chemistry one and is lost silently.

Charges are the other half of the problem. A student who cannot derive a formula from ionic charges cannot write any of the four equation forms reliably, because every one of them starts with correct formulae. Polyatomic ions are where this breaks: sulfate, nitrate, carbonate, hydroxide and ammonium, and particularly the bracket that is needed when two of them appear. Fifteen minutes of formula writing at the start of each session, cold, closes this inside a month.

sections.heading: Question stems, and what each one actually pays for
paragraphs: Chemistry marks are lost in bulk to answering a different question from the one printed. Pearson stems are consistent across series, and each has a shape of answer the scheme rewards. Describe a test for wants a reagent, a condition if there is one, and an observation. Explain in terms of structure wants the structure and then its consequence, as two statements. Suggest wants a plausible reason applied to an unfamiliar context, not a recited one. State wants one line.

A student who has never seen a mark scheme does not know any of this, and most have not. The single most efficient session in 4CH1 tutoring is often the one spent going through a past paper with the scheme open, question by question, counting how many separate statements the scheme is looking for and matching them to the marks available. Two marks means two things. The realisation that the paper is telling the student how much to write changes behaviour permanently and takes about an hour.

The table below lists the stems that recur and what each pays for. The right-hand column is the diagnostic one for a parent reading a marked script: if the losses cluster on explain stems, the problem is answer structure rather than chemistry, and that is four sessions of work. If they cluster on calculate stems, it is arithmetic. If they cluster on describe a test, it is recall, and that is the cheapest repair in the subject.

sections.heading: Qualitative analysis: the observations marked on exact wording
paragraphs: Tests for ions and gases are the most predictable marks on a 4CH1 paper and among the most frequently dropped, because they are marked on the words rather than on the sense. A candidate who writes that the solution turns cloudy where the scheme wants a white precipitate has described the right event and scored nothing. The remedy is not more chemistry; it is learning a short table of standard observations in standard phrasing, which is one or two hours of work and recovers marks on every paper.

The language conventions are worth stating explicitly because students guess them. Precipitates are described by colour and as a precipitate. Gas evolution is effervescence or bubbles of gas, with the identity established by a named test. Limewater turns milky, not white. A glowing splint relights in oxygen; a lighted splint gives a squeaky pop with hydrogen. Damp red litmus turns blue with ammonia and is bleached by chlorine. Each of these is a fixed form of words.

The second half of the skill is knowing which test identifies what and in what order a question wants it. Add dilute acid first for a carbonate; add dilute hydrochloric acid before barium chloride for a sulfate; add dilute nitric acid before silver nitrate for a halide. Students who learn the reagents without the sequence lose the order mark. The table gives the standard set in the wording a scheme recognises, and it is worth printing and keeping beside the student's revision.

sections.heading: State symbols, units and significant figures: the marks lost in silence
paragraphs: Some 4CH1 marks are lost without the student ever making a chemical error. A correct equation without the state symbols the question required. A correct concentration without the unit. A correct calculation rounded to one significant figure where the data supports three. A correct ionic equation with the charges omitted. None of these is a misunderstanding, and all of them are counted. Across a 180-mark qualification this category commonly accounts for a grade boundary's worth of marks.

They persist because nobody flags them. A classroom teacher marking thirty scripts marks the chemistry and moves on; the student sees a tick with a mark deducted somewhere and reads it as carelessness. Named explicitly and required on every line for a few weeks, the whole category closes. The rule we use in sessions is simple and slightly pedantic: nothing is finished until it carries its units, its charges and its state symbols, and nothing is rounded until the final line.

Significant figures deserve their own mention because students handle them inconsistently. The convention to teach is to carry full precision through the working and round only at the end, to the precision of the least precise datum given. A student who rounds at each step produces an answer that drifts and sometimes falls outside the acceptable range the scheme allows, which converts a correct method into a wrong answer. Both habits are mechanical, teachable and visible in a marked script within three weeks.

sections.heading: Practical chemistry examined without a practical paper
paragraphs: 4CH1 has no coursework and no separate practical examination, yet practical chemistry runs through both written papers. Students are asked to name apparatus, give a method in sequence, identify variables, describe observations precisely, choose a purification technique and justify a safety precaution. Because nothing appears on the examination timetable, this is the least-revised material on the specification and the marks are available on every paper.

The purification questions are the most predictable. Filtration separates an insoluble solid from a liquid; crystallisation recovers a soluble solid from its solution; simple distillation separates a solvent from a dissolved solid; fractional distillation separates liquids with different boiling points. A salt preparation wants add excess, filter off the unreacted solid, evaporate and crystallise, in that order. Students who know the four techniques and the order of a salt preparation answer most practical questions correctly.

Delivery deserves one plain statement. IB Gram does not run laboratory sessions in Dubai and does not send tutors to UAE addresses, because home visits are a service offered only in India. The laboratory work belongs to the school, which has the equipment and the technician. What a tutor adds over live video is conversion: the student's own practical write-up opened on a shared screen and marked the way Pearson words these questions, so that an afternoon already spent in a school laboratory becomes marks on a paper. Safety answers are worth drilling in the same hour, because they are marked on specificity: wear eye protection because the acid is corrosive earns credit where be careful does not, and a reason attached to a precaution is what the scheme looks for.

sections.heading: What one 4CH1 session fixes, and the order it happens in
paragraphs: The first session is not a lesson and should not feel like one. The student brings their most recent marked chemistry: a mock, a topic test, a returned past paper. The tutor locates every lost mark, sorts them by cause into notation, arithmetic, recall, answer structure and genuine content gap, counts each pile and names the largest. That statement is what a family gets at the end of the free thirty minutes, and it is usually more specific than anything the school report said.

The second through fifth sessions work on the largest pile only. This is the part families find counter-intuitive, because covering content feels like progress and fixing notation feels like admin. The arithmetic is against them: a student losing eleven marks to state symbols, missing units and unbalanced equations will gain more from four sessions on notation than from a term of content revision, and the notation work also makes every future topic cheaper to learn.

From roughly the sixth session the pattern becomes maintenance plus timed practice. A section of a past paper each week under real conditions, marked against the real scheme, with the categories tracked so a parent can see whether the original problem has gone or has simply moved. Content teaching enters only where the diagnosis found a genuine gap, which in chemistry is most often rates, energetics or the organic section that the school has not yet reached. The order is deliberate rather than conventional: notation first because it is quick and compounds, then arithmetic because it recovers whole question types, then recall because it is cheap, and content teaching last because it is the slowest thing to buy and the easiest to get from the school.

sections.heading: Honesty, past papers and the permit question
paragraphs: 4CH1 carries no coursework, which removes the commonest academic-honesty risk in international qualifications. What remains is school-set work, mocks and homework, and the line is still worth stating plainly: a tutor teaches, questions, marks and gives feedback on work the student has written. A provider offering to produce assessed work is selling the student a risk, and at least one operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments for other qualifications at AED 3,750, which is an integrity breach the student carries rather than the seller.

Past papers and mark schemes belong to Pearson. A tutor should name the series and the paper, point to the official source and work through material the school has already issued, rather than distributing scans. Reproducing secure or unreleased material is a copyright problem and, for an unreleased paper, a malpractice exposure for the candidate. Any provider advertising a library of mark schemes as a feature is describing something it should not be circulating.

On permits: private tutoring in the UAE is lawful and regulated, under the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so ignore any figure quoted as fact. Dubai's schools are regulated by KHDA; IB Gram holds no approval, licence or endorsement from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Pearson or Cambridge.

process.title: Photograph the marked paper
process.description: Three pages of your child's most recent marked chemistry is the whole of what is needed to start. Not a description of the problem, not a grade history: the actual script, with the marker's annotations visible. Everything a specialist can say about cause, priority and duration comes from reading that rather than from a conversation about it.

process.title: Free thirty-minute script reading
process.description: A 4CH1 specialist goes through the paper with the student, locating lost marks and sorting them by cause. The output is a written statement of the largest category and a realistic view of how long it takes to close. No card details are taken, and families who use that statement themselves have still had the useful part of the hour.

process.title: Fix the notation layer first
process.description: Where the diagnosis points at equations, state symbols, charges, units or significant figures, that work comes before any content revision. It is mechanical, it closes in four to six sessions, and it makes every subsequent topic cheaper to learn. Covering content first feels better and delays the thing that was actually costing marks.

process.title: Re-test with questions never seen
process.description: A repair is only real if it survives a gap. Unseen questions a fortnight after the block ends, marked against the scheme, show whether the habit has formed. Testing at the end of the same session shows only that the student remembers the last hour, which is the most common way tutoring reports overstate progress.

process.title: Track the categories, not the mood
process.description: Written feedback after each session names the specification point and the marks at stake, so the count of notation errors or abandoned two-step calculations can be compared week to week. That is reportable. Progress described as pleasing is not, and a parent who was not in the room has no way to check it.

process.title: Say so if the match is wrong
process.description: Two or three sessions is enough to know. Another 4CH1 specialist picks up the same script reading, the same category counts and the same priority order, so nothing is re-assessed or re-charged. Confirm that in writing with any provider before the first paid hour, because the alternative is paying twice for one diagnosis.

whyPoints.title: The script comes before the syllabus
whyPoints.description: A 4CH1 session that starts at the first page of the specification is working blind. Starting at the student's own marked paper locates the lost marks, counts them and puts the biggest pile first, which usually turns out to be notation rather than chemistry and takes weeks rather than terms.

whyPoints.title: Observation wording taught as wording
whyPoints.description: Qualitative analysis is marked on exact phrases. A white precipitate scores and a cloudy solution does not, and no amount of chemical understanding closes that gap. Teaching the fixed forms of words is one or two hours and makes those marks available on every paper the student sits.

whyPoints.title: Four equation forms, drilled separately
whyPoints.description: Word, symbol, net ionic and half equations have different rules, and students who have practised only balanced symbol equations lose marks across the other three. Separating them and drilling each is a couple of sessions with a return that shows up in electrolysis, salt preparation and precipitation at once.

whyPoints.title: Presentation marks named out loud
whyPoints.description: State symbols, charges, units and significant figures are counted and are lost silently, because classroom marking has no time to flag them individually. Required on every line for a few weeks, the whole category closes, and across 180 marks it is often worth a grade boundary.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what the format does and does not do
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one to one over live video. IB Gram does not arrange home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE. Where an in-home tutor would genuinely serve a student better, for instance a younger child who will not start work unsupervised, this page says so rather than arguing the other way.

whyPoints.description: Every AED band here is attributed to the provider that published it, every regulatory statement traces to u.ae, KHDA, MoHRE or Pearson, and no claim of approval is made because none is held. No tutor can promise a particular grade, and any provider that does should be asked to put the refund terms on the same page.

faqs.question: My child's 4CH1 marks dropped and the report says careless. What does that usually mean?
faqs.answer: In chemistry it usually means one of five specific things, and they are separable. Missing state symbols on equations that required them. Omitted units on concentration or mass answers. Two-step calculations abandoned after the first step. Observations described loosely where the scheme wants fixed wording. Equations balanced by altering a formula. None of these is a misunderstanding of chemistry, all of them are counted, and together they commonly account for a grade boundary's worth of marks on a 180-mark paper. A marked script shows which ones apply within about twenty minutes.

faqs.question: How many marks are in Paper 1C and Paper 2C of 4CH1?
faqs.answer: Paper 1C carries 110 marks over two hours and Paper 2C carries 70 marks over one hour fifteen minutes, giving 180 marks in total, so Paper 1C is 61.1% of the subject total and Paper 2C is 38.9%. The entry is untiered, with no Foundation or Higher decision, and the result is reported on the 9 to 1 scale. The specification also identifies content examined only in Paper 2C. Confirm the current structure and that content split on the live specification at qualifications.pearson.com for your child's series.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks when the observation is basically right?
faqs.answer: Because qualitative analysis is marked on wording rather than on sense. A sulfate test answered as the solution turns cloudy describes the right event and earns nothing, where a white precipitate forms earns the mark. Limewater turns milky, not white. Ammonia turns damp red litmus blue. A glowing splint relights in oxygen. Each of these is a fixed form of words, and most students have never been told they are fixed. Learning the standard table in standard phrasing is one or two hours and recovers marks on every paper.

faqs.question: What is the most common equation mistake in Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry?
faqs.answer: Balancing by changing a subscript inside a formula. It produces a balanced line and describes a different substance, so it scores nothing, and students do it because it works arithmetically. The second commonest is stopping once the atoms noticed first are balanced, which usually leaves hydrogen or oxygen unbalanced. The third is omitting state symbols where the question required them. All three are mechanical. Fifteen minutes of equation writing at the start of each session, cold and with charges shown, closes the set inside a month.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a symbol equation and an ionic equation in 4CH1?
faqs.answer: A balanced symbol equation shows every substance involved with correct formulae and balanced atoms. A net ionic equation shows only the species that actually change, with the spectator ions removed and the charges and state symbols kept. A half equation shows what happens at one electrode, with the electrons balanced. Students who have practised only the symbol form lose marks on the other two without knowing why, because the rules differ. Drilling the forms separately takes two or three sessions and recovers marks in electrolysis, precipitation and salt preparation at once.

faqs.question: Does a 4CH1 student need to know significant figures?
faqs.answer: Yes, and handling them badly turns correct methods into wrong answers. The convention to teach is to carry full precision through the working and round only at the final line, to the precision of the least precise datum in the question. A student who rounds at every step produces an answer that drifts and can fall outside the range a scheme accepts. It is a mechanical habit, visible in a marked script within three weeks of being required on every line, and it costs nothing to fix.

faqs.question: Does an Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry tutor come to our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Not with IB Gram. Chemistry lessons are delivered one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service offered only in India. The in-home market in Dubai is real, with rates published at AED 180 to 350 an hour in Bestimate's 2026 table and home tutors advertising to AED 500, since travel sits inside the figure. For script-level chemistry work the shared screen has a specific advantage: the annotated question, the corrected equation and the redrafted answer all survive the session, where notes in an exercise book do not.

faqs.question: How do online lessons handle writing equations and drawing structures?
faqs.answer: On a shared surface both people can write on. The student writes the equation, the tutor corrects it alongside, and the corrected version is saved and sent afterwards. Organic structures, isomers and apparatus diagrams work the same way, and a structure can be redrawn three times in a minute, which is the practice a student needs when the error is in the drawing convention rather than in the chemistry. Every version stays available, so a parent who was not present can see what changed during the hour.

faqs.question: Which purification technique does my child need to know for 4CH1?
faqs.answer: Four, and the order of a salt preparation. Filtration separates an insoluble solid from a liquid. Crystallisation recovers a soluble solid from its solution. Simple distillation separates a solvent from a dissolved solid. Fractional distillation separates liquids with different boiling points. A salt preparation wants add excess, filter off the unreacted solid, evaporate and crystallise, in that sequence. Students who know the four techniques and that order answer most practical questions on the paper correctly, and the whole set is two to three hours of work.

faqs.question: Is organic chemistry in 4CH1 as hard as it looks?
faqs.answer: It looks harder than it is, because it arrives last and is revised least. The content is pattern-based: alkanes, alkenes, alcohols and carboxylic acids each have a general formula, a naming convention and a short set of reactions, and once the pattern is visible the recall load drops sharply. Addition against substitution, the bromine-water test, oxidation of alcohols, esterification and addition polymerisation form a brief list of named reactions. The real difficulty is calendar rather than conceptual, so pre-teaching the homologous series before the school reaches them pays well.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help if my child joined a Dubai school mid-course?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the gap is usually narrower than it feels. A student arriving into a 4CH1 class from an American, Indian or national-curriculum background generally knows the chemistry and does not know the notation and answer conventions Pearson expects: equation forms, state symbols, observation wording, the shape of an explain answer. Three or four sessions on convention closes most of it. Dubai's private sector ran 17 different curricula across 227 schools in 2024-25, so mid-course transfer is ordinary here rather than exceptional.

faqs.question: How do Arabic and Islamic Education fit around a chemistry revision plan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: They occupy real timetable space and have to be planned around. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with the advice that no mandatory lesson be shorter than 25 minutes. Families who map the whole weekly load before committing to chemistry hours end up with a plan that survives the term.

faqs.question: Can 4CH1 sessions move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the sensible approach is to agree the alternative slot before the month begins rather than renegotiating during it. Dubai school days shorten in Ramadan and household routines change, so a 17:00 chemistry session frequently stops working and a post-Iftar one works better. Since lessons run over live video on Gulf Standard Time there is no travel to rearrange, which makes the shift straightforward. The same applies in reverse for summer and winter travel, when sessions can follow a family abroad if the time difference allows.

faqs.question: Can a chemistry tutor mark my child's practical write-ups from school?
faqs.answer: Marking and giving feedback on work the student has written is exactly what a tutor is for, and school practical write-ups are useful material because the student has already done the laboratory work. The write-up is opened on a shared screen and marked the way Pearson words practical questions, which converts an afternoon already spent into examination marks. What a tutor must never do is produce assessed work on a student's behalf. 4CH1 carries no coursework, which removes the commonest version of that risk entirely.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting 4CH1 tutoring in Year 9?
faqs.answer: It is the cheapest intervention available in this subject, if the school's Key Stage 4 runs over three years. The skills that decide a 4CH1 grade are largely notational and mathematical: writing formulae from charges, balancing, ratio, standard form, rearranging. A Year 9 student who has those arrives at the specification able to learn chemistry rather than fighting arithmetic. Ask the head of science whether Year 9 is a general science year or already the first year of the course, and ask for the scheme of work while you are there.

faqs.question: How soon should we expect to see the chemistry marks move?
faqs.answer: It depends on which category the script showed. Recall repairs such as the ion tests appear in the next topic test, within two or three weeks. Notation work, meaning state symbols, charges and units, shows up over three to four weeks once it is required on every line. Two-step calculation work takes four to six weeks because the habit has to become automatic. A genuine content gap across a whole section is a term. No tutor can promise a particular grade, and any provider offering one deserves real scepticism.

intro.heading: Costing chemistry help by the problem, not by the hour
paragraphs: An hourly rate tells a family almost nothing on its own. Two students in the same Year 11 chemistry class at the same Dubai school can need four hours and forty hours respectively, and both will be quoted the same rate per hour. The number that actually governs the spend is the hour count, and the hour count comes from the diagnosis. So this page costs 4CH1 by the problem: how many hours a mole-calculation weakness typically absorbs, how many an ionic-equation weakness takes, and why a late start on organic chemistry is the most expensive version of all.

The rate bands themselves are published and worth having in front of you. In Dubai, in October 2026, budget online tutoring advertises from AED 33 to 65 an hour and broadly occupies AED 45 to 150. Qualified subject tutors working online are quoted AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing International GCSE tuition from AED 150. Specialists in IGCSE, IB and A Level sit at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at around AED 270 and Bestimate's table reaching AED 450 and beyond. In-home one-to-one carries travel and is published at AED 180 to 350, with individual home tutors advertising to AED 500. A named or examiner-badged tutor is quoted at AED 500 to 650 and above, with BartyED at AED 650.

4CH1 sits naturally in the specialist band rather than the general one, and the reason is structural rather than snobbish. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry is examined through Paper 1C, two hours for 110 marks, and Paper 2C, one hour fifteen minutes for 70 marks, making 180 marks in total with no coursework and no separate practical paper. It is untiered and reported on the 9 to 1 scale. A tutor who has not taught this code will not know which content the specification examines only in Paper 2C, and the first three paid hours become research.

Chemistry also has an unusually clear single point of failure, which makes it easier to cost than most subjects. The mole is the load-bearing idea. Empirical formula, reacting masses, concentration, titration arithmetic, gas volumes and percentage yield all depend on it, and a student who is insecure there will drop marks across the whole of the Principles and Physical sections no matter how much content revision they do. Diagnose that and you can tell a family, honestly, that this is six to eight hours of work rather than a term. Miss it and they pay for a term.

What this page will not do is print an IB Gram price list, because a quote that precedes a look at the marked script is a guess. A specialist reads the student's own marked chemistry in a free thirty-minute session, counts where the marks went, and gives an hour estimate before any money is discussed. No card details are taken for that session. Lessons are delivered one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not arrange home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE, since home visits are a service offered only in India.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-chemistry-4ch1-tutor.programmesIntro: The route a Dubai school has entered your child for changes the cost of chemistry support before any rate is discussed. Three separate sciences, a double award, a November retake and a post-16 continuation imply very different hour counts for the same student.

programmes.name: Chemistry 4CH1 as one of three separate sciences
programmes.description: The most common entry in Dubai's British-curriculum schools and the most expensive to support if all three sciences are tutored at once. Chemistry as a single subject is examined in full depth across the four specification sections, which means content gaps are visible and targetable. Most families who stagger subjects by term rather than running them in parallel keep the monthly figure flat and still finish the two years covered.
programmes.countryNote: Check the exam entry statement rather than asking the student. Dubai schools frequently enter Pearson for one science and Cambridge for another, and a family that buys 4CH1 tutoring for a child sitting Cambridge 0620 has bought the wrong specification. The codes appear on the statement the examinations officer issues, and that document is the only reliable source for them.

programmes.name: Science Double Award 4SD0
programmes.description: Worth two International GCSEs across biology, chemistry and physics rather than three separate ones. Cheaper to tutor in total than three single subjects, and harder to target, because a chemistry weakness sits inside a qualification that also carries the other two sciences. Diagnosis takes longer here and the first session often has to establish which science the lost marks actually came from.
programmes.countryNote: Double Award is common in Dubai schools with wide-ability intakes and in schools where students carry a heavier non-science timetable. It is not a soft option, but it does change the equivalency arithmetic: five accredited subjects at no less than grade 3 is the Ministry of Education threshold, and a double award counts as two of them, which some families discover only when applying.

programmes.name: November series retake
programmes.description: Pearson International GCSE runs in November as well as in May and June, so a summer chemistry grade below what a sixth form requires does not cost a year. A retake block is the most predictable spend in this subject: the previous script already contains the diagnosis, so the hour count can be estimated accurately and the work aimed only at the sections that lost marks.
programmes.countryNote: The November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, which places preparation in the first term of the Dubai academic year. Not every Dubai centre enters candidates for November, so confirm with the school before planning a block; families whose school does not may need to enter through an approved examination venue as a private candidate instead.

programmes.name: International A Level and IB Diploma Chemistry
programmes.description: Where unresolved 4CH1 arithmetic becomes expensive. Both post-16 routes assume fluent mole calculations and both add substantially to the quantitative load, with the IB Diploma also requiring an internal assessment. Families who spend modestly in Year 10 on securing the mole typically spend less at seventeen, because post-16 specialist support sits at the top of the published rate bands.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai had 387,441 private-school students across 227 schools in 2024-25, with 37% on a UK curriculum and 7% in the International Baccalaureate, so most 4CH1 students in the emirate face a genuine choice of route at sixteen. Students aiming at medicine or engineering routes should treat chemistry as a prerequisite subject and plan the Year 10 and Year 11 work accordingly.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-chemistry-4ch1-tutor.subjectsIntro: The ten content areas below are where 4CH1 marks are won and lost, with an honest note on how many tutoring hours each typically absorbs. Confirm current content against the live specification on qualifications.pearson.com, since Pearson revises specifications between series.

subjects.name: The mole and reacting masses
subjects.description: Relative formula mass, moles, empirical formula, reacting mass calculations, percentage yield and percentage composition. The load-bearing skill of the whole qualification and the single most common root cause of a disappointing grade. Typically six to eight hours of drilling to secure, and it pays back across every other section.

subjects.name: Concentration, titration and gas volumes
subjects.description: Moles per cubic decimetre, grams per cubic decimetre, titration arithmetic and the molar volume of a gas. Marks here are lost almost entirely to unit handling: cubic centimetres against cubic decimetres, and dividing where a student should multiply. Three to four hours, provided the mole is already secure.

subjects.name: Atomic structure, bonding and structure
subjects.description: Electronic configuration, ionic and covalent bonding, giant structures, metallic bonding and the link between structure and physical properties. Explanation marks dominate, and they are lost by describing a structure without connecting it to the property the question asked about. Two to four hours.

subjects.name: Ionic and half equations
subjects.description: Writing balanced ionic equations, spectator ions, half equations at electrodes and state symbols. A discrete, teachable skill that students routinely leave as a gap because it is never the main point of a lesson. Two to three hours and it recovers marks in electrolysis, acids and redox simultaneously.

subjects.name: Acids, bases, salts and preparation
subjects.description: Neutralisation, salt preparation methods, solubility rules, pH and the practical sequence for making a pure dry sample. The marks sit in method order and in state symbols rather than in theory. Two to three hours, often combined usefully with the practical-technique work.

subjects.name: Electrolysis
subjects.description: Products at each electrode for molten and aqueous electrolytes, half equations, and the reasoning behind which ion is discharged. One of the highest-yield topics to repair because the question style is predictable and the marks are reliably available once half equations are secure. Two to three hours.

subjects.name: Tests for ions and gases
subjects.description: Flame tests, precipitate colours, tests for carbonates, sulfates, halides and ammonium, and the gas tests. Pure recall with a predictable question style, which makes it the cheapest marks on the paper and the most commonly neglected. One to two hours.

subjects.name: Rates, energetics and equilibrium
subjects.description: Rate experiments and graph interpretation, exothermic and endothermic changes, bond energy calculations, reversible reactions and industrial conditions. Bond energy arithmetic and sign conventions cause most of the loss, and equilibrium explanation questions need a stated direction of shift and a reason. Four to six hours.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry and homologous series
subjects.description: Alkanes, alkenes, alcohols, carboxylic acids, esters, isomerism, addition and substitution, polymerisation and crude-oil fractions. Taught last in most Dubai schools and therefore revised least. Six to ten hours if started late, which is why the late-organic start is the costliest version of a 4CH1 problem.

subjects.name: Practical technique in written questions
subjects.description: Apparatus naming, method sequence, variables, observations, safety, purification by filtration, crystallisation and distillation. There is no separate practical paper in 4CH1, so these marks get the least dedicated revision of anything on the specification. Two to three hours and they are available on every paper.

sections.heading: What a 4CH1 problem costs to fix, by diagnosis
paragraphs: Chemistry is unusually tractable to cost because its failure modes are discrete. A student is not generally bad at chemistry; they are insecure in the mole, or they cannot write an ionic equation, or they met organic chemistry six weeks before the paper. Each of those has a known shape and a known duration, and a provider who has read a marked script can give an hour estimate rather than a vague recommendation. The table below sets out the estimates we work from, in hours rather than in dirhams, so that any rate band on this page can be applied to them.

The estimates assume one to one work and a student who does the practice between sessions. They are honest about the asymmetry in both directions. A tests-for-ions gap is one or two hours and recovers marks on every paper, which makes it the best-value repair available in the subject. A late organic chemistry start is six to ten hours under time pressure, which is the single most expensive position a 4CH1 family can be in, and the reason is simply the calendar: organic is taught last and the series does not move.

Read the right-hand column before the hours column. It gives the signal a parent can look for in their own child's marked paper, which means the diagnosis does not depend on taking a provider's word for it. A script where every calculation question lost marks but the explanation questions scored is a mole problem. A script where electrolysis and acids both lost marks in the same way is an ionic-equation problem. A script that is strong until the last two questions is usually a syllabus-coverage problem rather than an understanding one.

sections.heading: The four sections of 4CH1, and how the 180 marks are reached
paragraphs: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry is organised into four sections: Principles of chemistry, Inorganic chemistry, Physical chemistry and Organic chemistry. It is assessed through Paper 1C, two hours for 110 marks, and Paper 2C, one hour fifteen minutes for 70 marks, which makes 180 marks and puts Paper 1C at 61.1% of the subject total against 38.9% for Paper 2C. There is no coursework, no controlled assessment and no separate practical examination. The entry is untiered and the result is reported on the 9 to 1 scale.

The structure has a cost consequence families should know about. Because the specification identifies a body of content examined only in Paper 2C, a student who revises the four sections evenly without separating out that subset arrives at the shorter paper least prepared, in the paper with the least time to recover. Checking which content that is, on the live specification for the relevant series, is twenty minutes of a parent's evening and can redirect several tutoring hours.

The section weightings are not published as a simple percentage split per section, so this page does not invent one. What the table records instead is what each section demands of a student and what that implies for the hour count, which is the more useful quantity for planning. Verify the current specification content and the paper structure on qualifications.pearson.com for your child's cohort, because the version in use at the time of entry is the one that counts and Pearson does revise between series.

sections.heading: The mole: one skill, most of the grade, and most of the invoice
paragraphs: If a 4CH1 script is going to collapse in one place, it collapses at the mole. Relative formula mass, moles from mass, empirical formula, reacting masses, limiting reagents, percentage yield, concentration and gas volumes are all the same idea wearing different clothes, and a student who has learned each as a separate procedure has learned six fragile things instead of one robust one. The symptom is characteristic: the student can sometimes do these questions and cannot say why the method works, so performance looks like inconsistency rather than a gap.

This is why diagnosis changes the price so much. A family who buys general chemistry tutoring for a mole problem will spend a term covering content the student mostly knows, because content revision feels productive and is comfortable for both sides. A family who identifies the mole will spend six to eight hours drilling conversions until the student can move between mass, moles, concentration and volume without pausing, and then find that the content revision they were about to buy is no longer needed. Same rate, a quarter of the invoice.

The drill itself is unglamorous and should be. Ten minutes at the start of each session, cold, with no formula triangle and no prompt sheet: grams to moles, moles to grams, moles to concentration, concentration to volume, both directions, with units written on every line. Significant figures and state symbols get folded in because the paper penalises their absence. Dubai cohorts arriving from different previous curricula vary sharply in where they start here, which is an argument for the diagnostic session rather than for assuming a level.
