sections.heading: Dubai rate bands, and where a 4CH1 specialist actually sits
paragraphs: The bands below are published figures from named providers, read in October 2026, with no IB Gram row because IB Gram quotes after a free diagnostic rather than from a list. Inventing a figure to sit competitively against the others would be exactly the behaviour that makes this market hard to read. What the table does instead is say what each band buys in terms of 4CH1 specifically, which is the comparison a chemistry parent actually needs.

The honest point about the cheapest band is that it has a legitimate use. A university-student tutor at AED 50 an hour is a reasonable purchase for supervised practice, for drilling mole conversions once someone has established that drilling is the right work, or for keeping a student working through a holiday. What that band is unlikely to supply is knowledge of how Pearson words an electrolysis question, which content sits only in Paper 2C, or what a mark scheme awards for a method answer. If the problem is technique rather than effort, the cheap option does not touch it.

The top band deserves a caution. Rates of AED 500 to 650 and above are frequently attached to an examiner claim, and examiner status should never be used to imply access to marking, boundaries or paper content, nor accepted without evidence. A better test costs nothing: ask the tutor to mark one page of your child's chemistry and explain, mark by mark, where the scheme would and would not award credit. Anyone who knows 4CH1 can do that in ten minutes, at any price point, and the answer tells you more than a badge does.

sections.heading: One to one, a pair or a group of four: the chemistry arithmetic
paragraphs: Group tutoring is cheaper per student and is not simply a worse version of one to one. It works well for recall-heavy material where every student needs the same thing: tests for ions, naming organic compounds, learning salt-preparation methods. It works badly for arithmetic repair, because the whole point of mole drilling is that the student works at their own speed with immediate correction, and a group of four necessarily moves at one speed. Families who understand that distinction buy the right format for each problem rather than one format for everything.

The arithmetic is worth doing properly. A monthly package advertised at around AED 799 for eight online sessions is roughly AED 100 a session, but that comparison only holds if the sessions are one to one and an hour long. A group of four at AED 100 a head is AED 400 an hour of a tutor's time, which is above the specialist one-to-one band, and whether that is good value depends entirely on whether the four students share a weakness. Ask how many are in the group and whether the roster is fixed for the term.

A pair is the underused option. Two students at a similar standard, ideally from the same school and the same teaching set, can be taught chemistry together more effectively than four can, and the per-student rate drops meaningfully. The constraint is honesty about the standard: a pairing where one student is two grades ahead becomes a one-to-one lesson that the other watches. In Dubai this format works best within a single community or school year group, where the parents already know each other and can agree a fixed slot.

sections.heading: Organic chemistry, taught last and revised least
paragraphs: Section 4 of the specification arrives at the end of most Dubai schemes of work, often in the spring of Year 11, and it is the section students revise least because they have seen it least. The consequence is predictable enough to plan around: scripts where the first three sections hold up and the organic questions are attempted thinly or abandoned. Six to ten hours of tutoring will repair it, and those are the most expensive hours in the subject, bought at the point in the year when specialist diaries are full and timing is least negotiable.

The content itself is more learnable than students expect, because it is pattern-based. Homologous series behave consistently: the alkanes, alkenes, alcohols and carboxylic acids each have a general formula, a naming convention and a small set of reactions, and once a student sees the pattern the recall load drops sharply. Addition versus substitution, the bromine-water test, oxidation of alcohols, esterification and addition polymerisation form a short list of named reactions rather than a large one.

The cheap intervention is calendar work rather than teaching. A family that knows organic chemistry lands in the spring can buy a short block in the autumn to pre-teach the homologous series, so that the school's own lessons land on prepared ground. Three hours in November is worth more than eight in April, and it is also easier to book. That is the clearest example on this page of why chemistry tutoring is best costed by timing rather than by hourly rate.

sections.heading: Practical marks in a specification with no practical paper
paragraphs: 4CH1 has no coursework and no separate practical examination, and yet practical chemistry is examined throughout both written papers: naming apparatus, giving a method in the right order, identifying variables, describing observations precisely, purifying by filtration, crystallisation or distillation, and commenting on safety. Because nothing practical appears on the examination timetable, these marks receive the least dedicated revision of anything on the specification, and they are available on every paper.

The questions reward precision of language more than laboratory experience. An observation answer that says the solution changed colour earns less than one that says a white precipitate formed. A method answer that lists apparatus without sequence loses order marks. A salt-preparation question wants add excess, filter, evaporate, crystallise in that order, with state symbols where equations appear. All of this is teachable over video using the school's own practical write-ups, which is the most efficient use of work the student has already done.

On delivery, the honest position: IB Gram does not run laboratory sessions in Dubai and does not send tutors to UAE addresses, because home visits are a service offered only in India. The practical work belongs to the school, which has the fume cupboard and the technician. What a tutor adds over live video is translation: opening the student's own write-up on a shared screen and marking it the way Pearson words these questions, so that a laboratory afternoon already spent converts into marks on the paper.

sections.heading: Two series a year, and what the retake decision costs
paragraphs: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in May and June and again in November, which gives a Dubai family a second decision point that most competitor pages never mention. The practical effect on cost is significant: a chemistry grade below a sixth-form requirement in August does not require a repeated year, it requires a finite block of work in the autumn. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026.

The dates that govern a family's planning are the administrative ones rather than the examination ones. Entries are made by the centre well in advance, and for a comparable series Cambridge's published March 2027 dates show the shape clearly: an examination period of 3 February to 4 March 2027 with final entries due 27 November 2026, more than two months ahead. Pearson released June 2026 results to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

Two instructions follow for anyone costing a retake. Ask the school for the entry deadline rather than the paper date, because the entry is the irreversible step and the one that sits earliest. And treat every published timetable as provisional until the final version appears: Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, so the live PDF on qualifications.pearson.com is the only version worth building a tutoring block around. Cambridge makes the same point more bluntly for its own candidates: every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for that zone, and Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after consulting the wrong one.

sections.heading: Permits, honesty and the things money should not buy
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is lawful and regulated. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published, any specific amount quoted to a parent should be disregarded. MoHRE's own listing is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a two-working-day completion time.

Dubai's private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi has ADEK, Sharjah the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah the federal Ministry of Education. IB Gram holds no permit, licence, accreditation or endorsement from any of them, nor from Pearson or Cambridge, and any provider claiming otherwise should be asked to produce the document. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules additionally bar school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school.

The last thing money should not buy in this subject is assessed work. 4CH1 has no coursework, which removes the commonest route to trouble, but one competitor in this market sells completed Internal Assessments for other qualifications at AED 3,750, and that is an academic-integrity breach that puts the student at risk rather than the seller. A tutor teaches, questions, marks and gives feedback on work the student produced. On equivalency, the sourced British-track rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level at E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level; a 4CH1 grade can be one of the five, and no tutoring provider performs or guarantees the process.

process.title: Send the marked chemistry paper first
process.description: Three photographed pages of the student's own marked work settle in ten minutes what a phone call cannot settle at all. The pattern of lost marks tells a specialist whether this is a mole problem, an equation problem or a coverage problem, and those are six hours, three hours and a term respectively. Everything on the price side follows from that.

process.title: Free thirty-minute diagnostic, then an hour estimate
process.description: A 4CH1 specialist reads the script with the student, sorts the lost marks by cause and names the largest. The output is an hour estimate and a priority, in writing, before any rate is agreed. No card details are taken. Families who stop there with a clearer idea of the problem have still had the useful part.

process.title: Buy the block, not the term
process.description: Agree a finite number of sessions aimed at the named weakness, with an unseen re-test a fortnight after it ends. If the problem has closed, stop. If it has not, the feedback shows why and the next block is chosen on evidence. Open-ended monthly arrangements are how a six-hour problem becomes a two-term commitment.

process.title: Pre-teach the sections that arrive late
process.description: If the school teaches organic chemistry in the spring, three hours in the autumn to lay down the homologous series is worth more than eight hours in April and is far easier to book. The same logic applies to rates and energetics. This is the only genuine saving available in 4CH1 tutoring, and it depends on asking for the scheme of work.

process.title: Re-cost after each school assessment
process.description: Every mock changes the hour estimate. Closed categories drop out, new ones appear, and the remaining weeks get re-allocated by marks available per hour rather than by specification order. A provider who never revises the estimate downwards when a problem closes is not costing the work, they are selling a subscription.

process.title: Change tutor without restarting
process.description: Two or three sessions are enough to know whether a match works. Say so and another 4CH1 specialist picks up the same diagnosis, the same priority list and the same hour estimate. Nothing is re-assessed and nothing is re-charged, which is the specific thing to confirm in writing with any provider before the first paid hour.

whyPoints.title: Hours estimated before rates discussed
whyPoints.description: The quantity that decides a chemistry bill is the hour count, not the hourly figure, and the hour count comes from a marked script. Quoting a rate before anyone has looked at the student's work is the standard practice in this market and the reason families routinely buy four times the tutoring the problem needed.

whyPoints.title: The mole treated as the main event
whyPoints.description: Most 4CH1 grades that disappoint disappoint for one arithmetic reason, and content revision will not touch it. Securing mole conversions in six to eight hours of drilling recovers marks across Principles and Physical chemistry at once, which is both the fastest improvement and the cheapest.

whyPoints.title: Every figure sourced, nothing invented
whyPoints.description: Each AED band on this page names the provider or rate table that published it and the month it was read. No statistic appears without its origin, no rating is asserted, and no regulator is claimed as an endorser. A page a parent can check is worth more than a page that flatters itself.

whyPoints.title: Formats matched to problems
whyPoints.description: A group of four is good value for ion tests and poor value for mole drilling. A pair at the same standard beats both on cost for shared weaknesses. Recommending one format for every diagnosis is simpler to sell and wastes money, so the format follows the problem rather than the price list.

whyPoints.title: Timing advice that reduces the bill
whyPoints.description: Pre-teaching the sections a Dubai school covers late, especially organic chemistry, converts eight expensive April hours into three cheap November ones. Advice that shrinks a family's spend is unusual in this market and is the clearest evidence that the diagnosis is being run for the student rather than for the invoice.

faqs.question: What does an online Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry 4CH1 tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market bands for October 2026: budget online tutoring from AED 33 to 65 an hour and broadly AED 45 to 150; qualified subject tutors online at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing International GCSE tuition from AED 150; IGCSE and IB specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase about AED 270. A 4CH1 entry sits naturally in the specialist band because the paper split and the Paper 2C content are code-specific. IB Gram quotes after a free thirty-minute diagnostic, with no card details taken, because the hour count matters more than the rate.

faqs.question: How many hours does it take to fix a mole-calculation weakness in 4CH1?
faqs.answer: Six to eight hours of one-to-one work for most students, provided they practise between sessions. The work is drilling rather than teaching: cold conversions between mass, moles, concentration and volume in both directions, with units on every line and no formula triangles. Secured in Year 10 it stays at six to eight hours. Left to the spring of Year 11 it competes with organic chemistry revision and takes substantially longer, which is why diagnosing it early is the single largest saving available in this subject.

faqs.question: Which part of 4CH1 gives the best value for a few tutoring hours?
faqs.answer: Tests for ions and gases. Flame tests, precipitate colours, the tests for carbonates, sulfates, halides and ammonium, and the gas tests are pure recall with a predictable question style, and most students have never systematically learnt them. One to two hours makes those marks reliably available on every paper. Electrolysis is close behind, at two to three hours once half equations are secure, because the question style repeats across series. Both are cheaper repairs than any amount of general content revision.

faqs.question: How is Paper 1C weighted against Paper 2C in 4CH1?
faqs.answer: Paper 1C runs two hours for 110 marks and Paper 2C runs one hour fifteen minutes for 70 marks, giving 180 marks in total: 61.1% of the subject total in the first paper and 38.9% in the second. The more useful fact is the content split. The specification identifies material examined only in Paper 2C, and a student who has revised the four sections evenly without separating that subset arrives least prepared at the shorter paper. Check the live specification on qualifications.pearson.com for your child's series.

faqs.question: Is there coursework or a practical exam in Edexcel IGCSE Chemistry 4CH1?
faqs.answer: No. 4CH1 is two written papers with no coursework, no controlled assessment and no separate practical examination. Practical chemistry is still examined inside both papers: apparatus, method order, observations, purification by filtration, crystallisation and distillation, variables and safety. Because nothing practical sits on the examination timetable, these marks get the least revision of anything on the specification and are available on every paper. Two to three hours spent on the language of observation and method answers is among the better-value work in the subject.

faqs.question: Why is organic chemistry the most expensive part of 4CH1 to fix?
faqs.answer: Because of the calendar rather than the content. Section 4 is taught at the end of most Dubai schemes of work, often in the spring of Year 11, so students have seen it least when the series arrives. Repairing it then takes six to ten hours, bought when specialist diaries are full and timing is least negotiable. The content itself is pattern-based and more learnable than students expect. Three hours of pre-teaching the homologous series in the autumn is worth more than eight hours in April.

faqs.question: Is a group chemistry class in Dubai better value than one to one?
faqs.answer: It depends on the problem. Groups work well for recall-heavy material where everyone needs the same thing: ion tests, naming organic compounds, salt-preparation methods. They work badly for arithmetic repair, because mole drilling requires one student working at their own speed with immediate correction. Do the arithmetic before deciding: a group of four at around AED 100 a head is AED 400 of a tutor's hour, which is above the specialist one-to-one band. Ask how many are in the group and whether the roster is fixed for the term.

faqs.question: Can two students from the same Dubai school share a 4CH1 tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a pair is the most underused format in this market. Two students at a similar standard, ideally in the same teaching set, can be taught chemistry together effectively, and the per-student rate drops meaningfully against one to one. The requirement is honesty about the standard: if one is more than a grade ahead, the session becomes a one-to-one lesson the other watches. Pairings work best inside a single community or year group where the families can agree a fixed slot for the term.

faqs.question: My child's marked paper shows the method right and the number wrong. What is that?
faqs.answer: Almost always a unit problem rather than a chemistry problem, and it is one of the cheaper repairs. Concentration and gas-volume questions are where it shows: cubic centimetres treated as cubic decimetres, grams per cubic decimetre confused with moles per cubic decimetre, dividing where the student should multiply. The tell is an answer out by a factor of a thousand with the working otherwise correct. Three to four hours of conversion drilling fixes it, provided the mole itself is already secure; if it is not, start there instead.

faqs.question: Does a cheaper tutor at AED 50 an hour make sense for chemistry practice?
faqs.answer: For some work, genuinely yes. Once a diagnosis exists and the task is supervised practice or conversion drilling, a budget online tutor at the advertised AED 33 to 65 an hour is a reasonable purchase and a sensible way to keep a student working through a holiday. What that band is unlikely to provide is specification knowledge: how Pearson words an electrolysis question, which content sits only in Paper 2C, and what a mark scheme awards for a method answer. If the lost marks are technique rather than effort, the cheap option will not reach them.

faqs.question: How do I know whether my child sits Pearson 4CH1 or Cambridge 0620?
faqs.answer: The exam entry statement issued by the school carries the exact codes, and it is the only document that settles it. Ask the examinations officer for it in writing. The distinction matters because the two specifications are assessed differently, including the practical arrangements, and buying 4CH1 tutoring for a Cambridge candidate wastes the first sessions. Dubai schools quite commonly enter Pearson for one science and Cambridge for another, so check each subject separately rather than assuming a single board across the sciences.

faqs.question: Can we book a short block before a November chemistry retake?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a retake it is the right structure. Pearson runs International GCSE in November as well as in May and June, and the November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, so preparation falls in the first term of the Dubai year. A retake block is finite and easy to cost, usually six to ten weeks of two sessions a week aimed only at the sections the previous script lost marks on. Confirm first that your child's school enters November candidates, since not every Dubai centre does.

faqs.question: Does a chemistry tutor in Dubai have to hold a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so disregard any figure quoted as fact. MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time. Since the permit is free and quick, there is no cost reason for a tutor not to hold one.

faqs.question: What should a 4CH1 tutor never agree to do?
faqs.answer: Produce assessed work on a student's behalf. 4CH1 has no coursework, which removes the commonest route to trouble, but the principle holds across every qualification a Dubai student sits: a tutor teaches, questions, marks and gives feedback on work the student has written. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, which is an academic-integrity breach that endangers the student rather than the seller. A tutor should also reference Pearson past papers and mark schemes rather than distributing copies, because Pearson owns that material.

faqs.question: Does a 4CH1 grade count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: It can be one of the five required subjects. The sourced British-track rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. One ranking competitor states six subjects; the sourced figure is five. No verified IB points threshold exists, so accept none without a moe.gov.ae source. Equivalency is handled by the authority, and no tutoring provider performs or guarantees it.

faqs.question: How quickly should we expect the chemistry marks to move?
faqs.answer: It depends on which diagnosis applies, and honest providers say so rather than promising a timeline. Recall repairs such as ion tests show up in the next topic test, within two or three weeks. Unit and conversion work shows up over four to six weeks, once the drilling has become automatic. A genuine content gap across a whole section takes a term, and organic chemistry started late may only partly close before the series. No tutor can promise a particular grade, and a provider offering one should be treated with real scepticism.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-computer-science-4cp.tutorsIntro: The teachers below work on Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Computer Science. A figure is quoted only after one of them has seen a program your child wrote, because the number of hours a candidate needs is the whole of the cost and it cannot be guessed from a phone call.

intro.heading: The real cost of 4CP0 support is hours, not the hourly rate
paragraphs: Every tutoring comparison in this market argues about the hourly figure, which is the less important half of the sum. A candidate who needs four sessions at AED 300 has spent less than one who needs twenty at AED 150, and the second family will have spent four months discovering it. So this page prices hours as well as rates: how many sessions a given problem usually takes, which problems are quick, and which are genuinely a term of work. That is the arithmetic a quote should be judged against.

The rates themselves are not secret, they are just rarely published. Across the Dubai market in October 2026, budget online platforms advertise from the mid-forties an hour, qualified subject teaching online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, visiting in-home tutors at roughly AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the rate, subject specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, and a premium tier marketed on examiner background reaching AED 650. Monthly packages run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

Computing has one pricing feature that other subjects do not. The software is free. Python costs nothing, the editors most Dubai schools use cost nothing, and the onscreen component is sat in an environment the examination centre provides. There is no equipment to buy beyond a keyboard, a usable screen and a quiet desk. Compare that with a science subject requiring practical access, and the only real cost in a 4CP0 plan is teaching time. That makes the hours question decisive rather than incidental.

What moves the number in Dubai specifically is the shape of computing departments here. The emirate has 227 private schools serving 387,441 pupils across 17 curricula, and growth is fast: six new schools opened in 2025-26, enrolment rose six per cent, and 2026-27 adds seven more schools and 16,846 places. New campuses open with lean departments, so one computing specialist frequently covers several year groups. The pool of people in Dubai who can teach the onscreen component properly is therefore small, and small pools price upward near an examination series.

IB Gram publishes no 4CP0 price list on this page, and the reason is the same arithmetic. The figure depends on how many hours the candidate actually needs, which depends on evidence nobody has until a teacher has read a program the student wrote themselves. So a quote follows a free trial lesson, one per family, bookable without any card details. The published market bands on this page are what you should measure that quote against, and the hours table further down is what you should measure the proposed plan against. Both are printed here precisely so that you can argue with us.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-computer-science-4cp.programmesIntro: The cost of 4CP0 support changes sharply depending on when a family starts. The three entry points below carry different hour counts and therefore different totals, which is worth knowing before anyone compares hourly figures.

programmes.name: Starting in the first year of the course
programmes.description: The cheapest point to start, measured per mark gained. A candidate beginning in Year 10 can build programming capability slowly, in short weekly sessions, which costs less per week and far less in total than compressing the same work into the spring of Year 11. Practical skill in particular needs calendar time rather than concentrated hours, because it is a habit rather than a body of knowledge.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools differ in whether Key Stage 4 runs over two years or three, and a three-year model changes the budget considerably. Ask the department which model applies, then plan the spend across the real number of terms. Families who assume two years and discover three have usually under-bought early support and over-bought late support, which is the most expensive sequence available.

programmes.name: Starting in the examination year
programmes.description: The most common starting point and the most variable in cost. A candidate who needs written technique only can often be served by six to eight sessions. One who cannot yet write a program from a stated problem needs a longer block, because the missing capability is constructive. The difference between those two cases is several thousand dirhams, and only reading the candidate's own code reveals which applies.
programmes.countryNote: Availability in Dubai is the hidden cost here. Computing specialists are booked earliest in the weeks before a Pearson window, so a family starting in March for a summer series is choosing from whoever is left rather than from the whole pool. That is not a price rise exactly, but it has the same effect on what a given budget buys.

programmes.name: Re-entering for the next series
programmes.description: Two Pearson series a year make a retake genuinely viable, and the decision should be made on component marks rather than the overall grade. A candidate three marks short on one component is a short, cheap block of work. One evenly short across both components is a term. A fresh entry fee applies either way, and that fee sits with the school or the centre rather than with any tutor.
programmes.countryNote: Timing is awkward in Dubai because summer results land during the long holiday, with June 2026 results reaching students on 20 August 2026, and November results arrive in January, as the November 2025 series results reached students on 22 January 2026. Having the component breakdown in hand lets a family decide calmly in a window when the school may be closed or mid-term.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-computer-science-4cp.subjectsIntro: Hours are the cost, so here is what the common 4CP0 problems usually take. These are planning figures from typical cases rather than promises, and a teacher who has read the candidate's own work will revise them in either direction.

subjects.name: Starting a program from a stated problem
subjects.description: The single most common presenting problem and one of the quicker ones to shift, because the missing piece is a planning sequence rather than knowledge. Read the problem, name the inputs, choose the structure, write the smallest working version, extend it.

subjects.name: Lists, loops and file handling in Python
subjects.description: Genuine content work rather than technique, so it takes real weeks. Each construct has to be written repeatedly against different problems before it becomes available under exam pressure. This is where a longer block earns its cost.

subjects.name: Debugging from a traceback
subjects.description: Reading an error message, locating the line it names and reasoning about the cause. Cheap to teach and disproportionately valuable, since it is the only diagnostic tool a candidate has in the exam room once something fails.

subjects.name: Test cases and validation habits
subjects.description: Trying a valid input, a boundary and something invalid before declaring a program finished. Two sessions of deliberate practice changes a habit that otherwise costs marks on every practical question for two years.

subjects.name: Trace tables done to the end
subjects.description: A strict column-by-column method, every cell filled, the trace carried through rather than abandoned once the answer looks obvious. Among the cheapest mark recoveries in the specification.

subjects.name: Binary, hexadecimal and overflow
subjects.description: Timed conversion drills in both directions plus binary addition and overflow. Skipped in revision because it looks trivial, then slow and inaccurate under time. One or two sessions usually settles it for good.

subjects.name: Written answers with mechanism and consequence
subjects.description: The slowest technique fix, because it changes how a candidate writes across every topic. Write, mark against the published criteria, find the missing required element, rewrite. Three cycles per topic, several topics.

subjects.name: Network and protocol vocabulary
subjects.description: Rewriting every device as a function rather than a name, which is what the mark scheme credits. Mechanical, repetitive and reliable, and it carries over into the questions about security and performance.

subjects.name: Threat-to-defence pairing in cybersecurity
subjects.description: Candidates name a defence without linking it to the threat in the question. Practising the link on past questions is quick work and recovers marks that were already within reach of what the candidate knew.

subjects.name: Logic gates and truth tables
subjects.description: Procedural and reliable once the method is fixed, which makes it a sensible first session for a candidate who needs an early win before the harder written topics are tackled.

sections.heading: What a 4CP0 home tutor costs in Dubai, by who you would be hiring
paragraphs: The Dubai market has clear tiers and they are visible in the advertised rates, even though most providers avoid printing a figure. At the bottom, budget platforms and recent school leavers advertise from the mid-forties an hour. In the middle, qualified subject teachers working online sit at roughly AED 150 to 300. Visiting in-home tutors are advertised at roughly AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the rate, subject specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, and a premium tier marketed on examiner background reaches AED 650.

For computing the tier matters more than it does in some subjects, because what distinguishes the tiers is whether anyone watches the candidate type. A cheap session is usually a walkthrough of a finished example program, which is pleasant, understandable and almost useless for building the constructive skill the onscreen component tests. A session at the qualified tier sets a problem, lets the candidate write, and intervenes at the point of error. Those are different products at any price.

IB Gram does not publish a rate card here. The total depends on hours, the hours depend on evidence, and the evidence is a program the candidate wrote. sections.heading: Why coding tuition travels badly, and what the in-home premium pays for
paragraphs: A visiting tutor in Dubai is selling an hour plus a journey, and the journey is inside the rate whether the invoice itemises it or not. Forty minutes each way to Arabian Ranches or Dubai Hills at five in the afternoon is more than an hour of a working day gone, and nobody absorbs that for nothing. That is the honest explanation for the gap between AED 180 to 500 in-home and AED 150 to 300 online at a comparable level of teacher, and it has nothing to do with quality.

For computing there is a second cost that is easier to miss. Two people leaning at one laptop is a worse teaching setup than two full-size screens showing the same editor. The teacher cannot comfortably read the traceback, the candidate cannot comfortably type, and the session drifts towards demonstration because demonstrating is physically easier than supervising. The format quietly changes what gets taught, which is a real loss dressed up as a convenience.

The third factor is the pool. A Dubai family hiring in-home is choosing from people who can reach their community on a weekday afternoon. Computing departments in this emirate are small and growing fast, so that local pool is thin to begin with. The same family online is choosing from computing specialists across time zones that overlap with Gulf Standard Time evenings. The table puts both options against the measures that actually differ for a programming lesson.

sections.heading: The technical setup for 4CP0, and why it costs nothing
paragraphs: Computing is unusual among examined subjects in having no equipment bill. Python is free. The editors most Dubai schools use for teaching are free. The onscreen component is sat in an environment the examination centre provides, so nothing has to be licensed, subscribed to or bought for the exam itself. A provider who suggests otherwise, or who bundles software into a package price, is charging for something that is available at no cost.

What does matter is matching. Confirm with the school which Python version and which editor the onscreen paper runs in, then practise in something close to it. An unfamiliar interface costs minutes in a timed practical paper, and minutes are the scarcest resource in that room. This is a free adjustment that families routinely skip, and it is worth more than an extra paid session in the final fortnight.

The hardware requirements are modest but real, and they are worth checking before anyone buys extra tuition hours. A physical keyboard rather than a tablet, because touchscreen typing measurably slows timed work and the onscreen component is typed from start to finish. A screen big enough to hold a problem statement and a code editor at the same time, since switching between windows wastes seconds a candidate will want back. A quiet desk for an uninterrupted hour. That is the whole list, and nothing on it needs replacing annually. Families in apartment communities such as Dubai Marina or JLT routinely find the quiet hour harder to arrange than any piece of the equipment, and it affects the quality of preparation more than a faster machine ever would.

sections.heading: Hours against starting point: budgeting a 4CP0 block honestly
paragraphs: A quote for 4CP0 support is really a claim about how many hours a candidate needs, and that claim should be visible. The table below pairs the common starting points with the weeks and hours they usually take, then prices each one at the two tiers a Dubai family is realistically choosing between: qualified teaching at AED 150 to 300 an hour, and subject specialist at AED 200 to 450. The figures are arithmetic on those published bands rather than our prices.

Read it as a range rather than a prediction. A candidate who can already write programs and is losing marks on written precision sits at the cheap end, because technique fixes faster than capability. A candidate who has not yet built text-based programming at all sits at the expensive end, and compressing that work into the weeks before a series makes it more expensive rather than less, because practical skill needs calendar time to settle.

The point of publishing this is comparison. If a provider proposes thirty sessions for a candidate whose only problem is written vocabulary, the hours are wrong even if the hourly rate is attractive. If a provider proposes six sessions for a candidate who cannot start a program, the total is low and the plan will fail. Asking which row of this table your child is in, and why, is a reasonable question and a good test of whether anyone has actually looked at their work.

Where a school enters a candidate, the fee appears on the school invoice and is set by the school as the Pearson centre. Where a family enters a private candidate, the examination centre bills them directly and the amount varies by centre, so collect two or three written quotes and confirm that the centre is running the series you need.

A retake carries a fresh entry fee each series, which is worth weighing against the component marks before committing. Two Pearson series a year make a retake practical, but a candidate evenly short across both components is buying a term of work plus a fee, while one three marks short on a single component is buying a short block plus a fee. The breakdown is free and arrives with the results.

Then there is VAT, which is the line most often left vague. Ask every provider whether the quoted figure includes it and get the answer in writing, because the difference across a year of weekly sessions is material. sections.heading: Who may legally charge you for a computing lesson in Dubai
paragraphs: Paid private tuition in the UAE runs through a permit system, and a parent can check it in one question. Individuals giving private lessons require a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. The MoHRE service listing for it shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website or e-services system.

Because the permit is free and quick, there is no cost argument for a tutor not holding one, and anyone offering private tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. The permit is not a quality mark, though. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Ask about the permit and the subject record as two separate questions.

Two related points matter for anyone comparing providers on price. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai is regulated differently from an individual tutor and requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, so no provider should describe itself as approved by KHDA without holding one. And in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school. A cheap rate offered by your child's own class teacher is not a bargain, it is a problem.

sections.heading: Group classes for programming, and when the saving is actually real
paragraphs: Tuition centre group classes of two to four pupils are advertised in this market at roughly AED 90 to 160 per pupil per hour, a genuine saving against one-to-one. For some subjects and some candidates that is the sensible purchase. For the practical half of 4CP0 it usually is not, and it is worth understanding why rather than taking anyone's word for it.

Programming errors are individual and they happen in the moment. The value of a session is someone noticing that this particular candidate's loop condition inverts, right now, at the keystroke, and stopping them before the habit sets. In a group of four, three pupils wait while one error is addressed, and the teacher necessarily shifts towards demonstrating on a shared screen because that is the only way to use an hour with four people in it. Demonstration is exactly the mode that fails to build constructive skill, so the saving is real and the thing you were buying has quietly gone.

The written component is a different matter. Theory technique, trace tables, vocabulary precision and marking against published criteria all work reasonably in a small group, because the errors are common rather than individual. A sensible split for a budget-conscious Dubai family is therefore group work for the written component, if a good local class exists, and one-to-one for the practical. That combination costs less than full one-to-one and loses nothing that matters, which is a better answer than defending the expensive option.

sections.heading: How the lesson runs, and what IB Gram does not sell in the UAE
paragraphs: Every 4CP0 session for a Dubai family happens online, one-to-one, over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and home visiting is a service offered only in India. That is stated on every country page on this site and it is stated here, in the body rather than the footer, because a page that targets this search phrase and then redefines it quietly has wasted your time.

In practice the session looks like this. A shared editor is open on both screens. The teacher sets a problem and says nothing while the candidate plans it, then watches the typing. When an error appears it is read aloud and interpreted rather than fixed silently, because a candidate who cannot read a traceback has no diagnostic tool in the exam. The hour ends with a working program the candidate wrote, and a short written note sent the same day.

What the format changes is who is available to teach. A Dubai family hiring locally is choosing from a thin pool of people who can be in their community on a weekday afternoon. Online, the pool is computing specialists in overlapping time zones. Where no specialist is free at the level needed, we say so rather than substituting someone who is not, and we say it before a payment rather than in week three. That disclosure costs us bookings and is worth more than the bookings.

faqs.question: How much should a 4CP0 block cost in total, not per hour?
faqs.answer: Hours decide the total, so start there. A candidate whose only problem is written precision often needs six to eight sessions, which at the published Dubai bands of AED 150 to 300 an hour comes to roughly AED 900 to 2,400. A candidate who cannot yet write a program unaided usually needs eight to twelve sessions, and one weak on both components from Year 10 can need twenty-four to thirty. Those are arithmetic on market rates rather than our prices. Ask any provider which band your child sits in and why, because that answer is the quote.

faqs.question: Why is a visiting tutor in Dubai more expensive than the same teaching online?
faqs.answer: Because the journey is inside the rate whether or not the invoice shows it. Forty minutes each way to a community like Arabian Ranches or Dubai Hills at five in the afternoon costs more than an hour of a working day, and nobody absorbs that for free. The Dubai market advertises visiting tutors at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for qualified teaching online as at October 2026. For a coding lesson the in-home format also gives a worse view of the editor, so you pay more for a weaker setup.

faqs.question: Do we have to buy software or a licence for 4CP0 practice?
faqs.answer: No. Python is free, the editors most Dubai schools use for teaching are free, and the onscreen examination environment is provided by the examination centre. Nothing in a 4CP0 plan requires a licence or a subscription. A provider who bundles software into a package price is charging for something available at no cost. What is worth doing, and costs nothing, is confirming with the school which Python version and which editor the onscreen paper runs in, then practising in something close to it so the interface does not eat exam minutes.

faqs.question: Is a cheap 4CP0 tutor at AED 60 an hour a false economy?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the test is what happens in the hour rather than the figure itself. At the budget tier a session is usually a walkthrough of a finished example program. That is understandable and almost useless for the onscreen component, which tests whether a candidate can produce code from a stated problem under time. If nobody watches your child type, the hour has not built the thing being examined. Twelve cheap sessions that do not change capability cost more than five that do, which is why hours and rate have to be judged together.

faqs.question: Does the quoted 4CP0 tutoring rate include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask, and get the answer in writing before committing, because across a year of weekly sessions the difference is material. Some providers quote inclusive, others exclusive, and the gap is rarely explained. IB Gram states whether VAT applies to a given arrangement at the point of quoting, which is after the free trial lesson. This page deliberately does not state how UAE VAT law treats tuition fees in general: that is a Federal Tax Authority question, the answer depends on the provider's registration and activity, and no tutoring site should be your source for tax advice.

faqs.question: What does a 4CP0 examination entry cost, and is it part of the tutoring fee?
faqs.answer: It is never part of a tutor's rate. Where your child's school enters them, the fee is set by the school as the Pearson centre and appears on the school invoice. Where a family enters a private candidate, the examination centre bills them directly and the amount varies by centre, so collect two or three written quotes and confirm the centre is running the series you need. A retake carries a fresh entry fee each series, which is worth weighing against the component marks before deciding.

faqs.question: How many hours does it take to fix a child who cannot start a program?
faqs.answer: Typically three to four sessions, which surprises families who expect it to be the expensive problem. The missing piece is usually a planning sequence rather than knowledge: read the problem, name the inputs, choose the structure, write the smallest working version, then extend it. Once that sequence is in place a candidate who already understands loops and conditions can start work unaided. The expensive problem is different: a candidate still uncertain about lists and file handling needs real content weeks, usually eight to twelve, because that is capability rather than technique.

faqs.question: Is a group programming class in Dubai worth the lower per-pupil rate?
faqs.answer: For the written component, often yes. For the practical half, usually not. Group classes of two to four pupils are advertised at roughly AED 90 to 160 per pupil per hour, a real saving. But programming errors are individual and happen at the keystroke, and in a group of four the teacher has to shift towards demonstrating on a shared screen because that is the only way to use the hour. Demonstration does not build constructive skill. A sensible budget split is group work for theory technique and one-to-one for the coding.

faqs.question: Does starting 4CP0 support in Year 10 cost less than waiting for Year 11?
faqs.answer: Less per mark gained, yes, and usually less in total for a candidate with real practical gaps. Programming capability is a habit rather than a body of knowledge, so it needs calendar time to settle and cannot be compressed efficiently. Short weekly sessions across Year 10 cost less per week and build something that holds. Compressing the same work into the spring of Year 11 costs more, because availability tightens before a series and because rushed practical practice does not stick. A candidate needing written technique only is the exception and can start late cheaply.

faqs.question: What hardware does my child actually need at home for 4CP0?
faqs.answer: Three things and none of them expensive. A physical keyboard rather than a tablet, because the onscreen component is typed under time and touchscreen input measurably slows a candidate. A screen large enough to hold a problem statement and an editor side by side. And a quiet desk for an uninterrupted hour. In apartment communities such as the Marina or JLT the quiet hour is usually harder to arrange than the equipment, and it affects preparation quality more than any upgrade would.

faqs.question: How do I check that a Dubai tutor is permitted to teach my child for money?
faqs.answer: Ask directly whether they hold a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. The MoHRE service listing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time, so there is no cost reason to be without one. Operating without it exposes the tutor to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Treat it as a legality check rather than a quality check: eligible applicants include university students and school students aged 15 to 18.

faqs.question: Can my child's own school computing teacher tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: Avoid arranging it, even where it is offered cheaply. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to pupils enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct of its own. Beyond the rules, it is a poor arrangement on its own terms: the person marking your child's class work should not also be paid to prepare them for it. A cheap rate from inside the school is not a saving worth the conflict it creates.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a computing tutor to a villa or apartment in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE on this platform, and home visiting is a service offered only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. The market does sell visiting tutors at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour as at October 2026 and that is a legitimate option elsewhere. For programming specifically the online setup is better rather than merely cheaper, because a full-size shared editor beats two people leaning at one laptop every time.

faqs.question: What happens if no 4CP0 specialist is free when we want to start?
faqs.answer: You get told, before a payment rather than in week three. Computing specialists in this market book out earliest in the weeks before a Pearson series, and the honest answer in that window is sometimes that nobody suitable is available at the level needed. Substituting a generalist who can cover the theory but not supervise code is how a family spends eight weeks discovering a mismatch. Where the gap is short, we will say when a slot opens. Where it is not, we will say that too, which costs bookings and keeps the page honest.

faqs.question: Can we buy only a diagnostic and then work on the plan ourselves?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a fair number of families it is the right purchase. Two paid sessions on top of the free trial are enough for a teacher to read a program the candidate wrote, set a fresh problem to confirm where the constructive step breaks, and hand back a written plan naming what to practise and in what order. That plan is yours whether you continue or not. Parents who can supervise practice at home often need nothing more, and a provider who never offers this option is selling hours rather than solving a problem.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-computer-science-4cp.tutorsIntro: The teachers below work on Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Computer Science and the post-16 computing courses that follow it. Each one writes code in front of the candidate rather than describing it, because reading a program is a different skill from producing one under exam conditions.

intro.heading: Two papers, two skills, and the gap most 4CP0 candidates fall into
paragraphs: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Computer Science, code 4CP0, is assessed in two components that reward almost opposite habits. One is written: definitions, explanations, trace tables, truth logic, descriptions of how a network or a processor behaves. The other is practical and onscreen, where a candidate is given programming problems and has to produce working Python under time pressure. A student can be strong at one and weak at the other, and most are. The marks, however, come from both.

The failure pattern in Dubai schools follows from that split. A candidate who enjoys programming treats Paper 1 as something to glance at the week before, then discovers that written computer science has a vocabulary and a precision the paper insists on. Describe what a router does and the mark scheme wants a specific function named, not a general sense of networking. Explain lossy compression and it wants the mechanism and a consequence. Confident programmers lose marks on written questions about the very things they can do with their hands.

The reverse pattern is just as common and more serious. A candidate who revises hard from a textbook can learn the theory well and still freeze in front of an empty editor, because writing a program from a specification is a constructive skill that reading about programs does not build. Lessons spent explaining loops do not fix it. Only writing code does, under the same conditions the exam imposes, with someone watching the keystrokes rather than the finished file.

This is where an online format earns its place rather than apologising for it. Programming teaching is screen work from beginning to end. A shared screen shows the editor, the error message and the candidate's own cursor at full size, and a teacher can stop them at the exact moment the indentation goes wrong rather than afterwards, once the program has failed and the trail has gone cold. Sitting beside someone at a kitchen table gives you a worse view of a code editor than sharing it does, and it narrows your choice of teacher down to whoever happens to live close enough to drive over on a weekday afternoon.

Everything on this page is organised around the two components. The content map says what each one asks for. The marks-lost table says where candidates in this cohort actually drop them, topic by topic. There is a comparison with the Cambridge route and with Edexcel ICT, because Dubai schools run all three and families are frequently told they are interchangeable. They are not. And there is a plain statement of what a tutor may and may not do with a piece of a student's code, which matters more in this subject than in most.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-computer-science-4cp.programmesIntro: Computer Science at 16 sits inside a longer sequence, and the right teaching at each point is different. The three stages below are where the decisions that affect a 4CP0 grade actually get made in a Dubai school.

programmes.name: Choosing Computer Science over ICT
programmes.description: Many Dubai schools offer Computer Science and ICT in the same option column, and the two are regularly described to families as versions of one subject. They are not. Computer Science is about how computation works and requires programming; ICT is about applying software to tasks and requires practical competence in office and media packages. A pupil who likes using computers is not automatically suited to writing programs about them.
programmes.countryNote: Ask the Dubai school two concrete questions before the option form goes back. Which specification code does the department enter, since 4CP0 and Cambridge alternatives are assessed differently? And is there a programming language used across Key Stage 3 that leads into it? A pupil arriving in Year 10 having only used block-based tools will need text-based Python from the first week, and that is a planning matter rather than a problem.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Computer Science
programmes.description: The qualification covers computational thinking, data and data representation, the components and behaviour of computer systems, networks, and the issues computing raises, assessed on a written component. Alongside it sits an onscreen component where candidates solve programming problems in Python. There is no coursework and no internally assessed element, so nothing accumulates over the two years except capability.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools enter 4CP0 through their own Pearson centre number, and the entry is made by the exams officer rather than the family. Confirm the code in writing: a candidate revising from Cambridge material for a Pearson entry will practise a programming paper that is assessed in a different format. Check also which Python version and which editor the school uses, because the onscreen component is sat in a specific environment.

programmes.name: Where 4CP0 leads after Year 11
programmes.description: A sound 4CP0 grade leads into A Level Computer Science, IB Diploma Computer Science at Standard or Higher Level, or a BTEC in computing. A Level raises the theory substantially and adds a substantial programmed project. The IB route adds an internally assessed solution with documented design. Both assume a candidate who can already write and debug their own code without supervision.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's post-16 provision is expanding quickly: the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four on a UK curriculum and three offering the International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. A candidate who may move between an A Level and an IB route should understand that the IB course requires a documented, internally assessed solution, which changes what a tutor is permitted to do with their work.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-computer-science-4cp.subjectsIntro: The topics below are where 4CP0 marks are concentrated and where this cohort most often loses them. Each entry names what the paper actually wants, which is usually narrower than a revision guide suggests.

subjects.name: Decomposition and abstraction
subjects.description: Breaking a problem into subproblems and deciding what detail to discard. The written component asks candidates to justify a decomposition, not merely describe one, so answers that list the parts without explaining why that split helps score low.

subjects.name: Searching and sorting algorithms
subjects.description: Linear and binary search, bubble and merge sort. Marks go to candidates who can state the precondition binary search requires and compare efficiency in terms of the number of comparisons rather than in terms of speed as a feeling.

subjects.name: Pseudocode, flowcharts and trace tables
subjects.description: The single highest-yield written skill in the subject. A trace table done properly is almost unloseable marks; done carelessly it costs every one of them. Candidates skip columns, update variables in the wrong order, or stop tracing once they think they can see the answer.

subjects.name: Binary, hexadecimal and data representation
subjects.description: Conversions in both directions, binary addition and overflow, character sets, and how images and sound are represented. The arithmetic is simple enough that candidates assume it needs no practice, which is exactly why it costs marks under time pressure.

subjects.name: Compression, lossy and lossless
subjects.description: The mark scheme wants a mechanism and a consequence: what is discarded or encoded, and what that means for file size and quality. Answers that say a file becomes smaller without saying how earn nothing, however confidently they are written.

subjects.name: The processor and the fetch-execute cycle
subjects.description: Registers, the role of the control unit and arithmetic logic unit, and the stages of the cycle in order. Candidates who learned the cycle as a diagram without the register names cannot answer questions that specify where a value is held at a given stage.

subjects.name: Logic gates and truth tables
subjects.description: AND, OR, NOT and their combinations, read from a circuit and written into a table. The marks are procedural and reliable, which makes this a good early win for a candidate who needs confidence before harder topics.

subjects.name: Networks, topologies and protocols
subjects.description: Wired and wireless networks, topologies, the purpose of specific protocols, and the role of devices. Precision is everything here: naming a device is not describing its function, and the paper is reliably asking for the function.

subjects.name: Cybersecurity threats and mitigation

sections.heading: What 4CP0 actually assesses, component by component
paragraphs: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Computer Science is assessed across two components and nothing else. One is a written paper covering the principles of the subject. The other is sat onscreen, where candidates are given programming problems and produce Python solutions in a provided environment. There is no coursework, no portfolio and no internally assessed element, which means nothing can be banked over two years and every mark is won on the day. Confirm current timings and mark totals on the specification document at qualifications.pearson.com rather than from any tutoring page, this one included.

The written component rewards precision of language far more than breadth of reading. A candidate who can describe the general idea of a protocol will not score; one who names its specific function will. The same applies across data representation, processor behaviour and network devices. Answers are marked for mechanism and consequence, which is why strong students who revise by reading summaries plateau: summaries contain the ideas without the exact formulations the scheme credits.

The onscreen component rewards something else entirely, and it cannot be revised by reading about it. A candidate has to decompose a stated problem, choose the right constructs, write syntactically correct Python, test it against the cases the question implies, and debug whatever fails, all against a clock that does not pause. The table below maps both components to the capability each one requires and to the preparation that genuinely builds it, which is the distinction most revision plans miss entirely.

sections.heading: The empty editor problem: why reading about Python does not build Python
paragraphs: Ask a Year 11 candidate in Dubai to explain a for loop and most will do it well. Give the same candidate a stated problem, an empty editor and twenty minutes, and a significant proportion will produce nothing usable. That gap is not a knowledge gap and it does not close with more explanation. Writing a program from a specification is a constructive act with its own sequence: read the problem, identify the inputs, decide the structure, write the smallest working version, then extend it. Nobody acquires that sequence by watching it performed.

The practical teaching move is to stop demonstrating. In a session the candidate types and the teacher watches, intervening at the moment the indentation slips or the loop condition inverts rather than after the program has failed and the trail has gone cold. Error messages are read aloud and interpreted rather than fixed silently, because a candidate who cannot read a traceback in the exam has lost the only diagnostic tool available to them.

Testing is the part almost nobody is taught. A question implies its test cases: a valid input, a boundary, something invalid. Candidates who run their program once with the obvious input and submit lose marks that were available for handling the rest. Building a habit of trying three cases before declaring a program finished takes a few sessions and pays back on every practical question. It also makes revision measurable, because the number of cases a candidate tests unprompted is a thing you can count.

sections.heading: Where 4CP0 candidates lose marks, topic by topic
paragraphs: Lost marks in this subject cluster tightly, and they are rarely where families expect. The theory topics that feel hardest, processor architecture and network protocols, are usually taught carefully because teachers know they are difficult. The losses concentrate instead in topics that feel easy: binary conversions skipped in revision because they seem trivial, trace tables rushed because the answer seems obvious, compression answered with a general statement because the idea feels simple.

Written-answer losses have one dominant cause, which is vocabulary rather than knowledge. A mark scheme awards credit for naming a function, a mechanism or a consequence. Candidates who understand the topic but write around it in general terms score a fraction of what they know. Fixing this is unglamorous: write the answer, mark it against the published criteria, see which required element is missing, rewrite it. Three cycles on one topic changes how a candidate writes across all of them.

Practical losses divide between syntax and structure, and the two are not equally serious. Syntax errors cost time but remain recoverable in the exam room provided a candidate can read a traceback and locate the line it names. Structural errors, where the program approaches the stated problem in the wrong way altogether, are not recoverable under time, because fixing them means starting again with minutes left. That is why the two-minute planning step before any typing begins matters far more than typing speed ever will, and why sessions that look unproductive because nobody is writing code are often the ones doing the real work. The table below sorts the most common failures by component, with what a single session can realistically be expected to fix.

sections.heading: Trace tables, pseudocode and the reasoning the written paper rewards
paragraphs: A trace table is the closest thing to free marks in this specification, and it is lost more often than almost anything else. The method is mechanical: one column per variable plus one for output, one row per iteration, every cell filled even when the value has not changed, and the trace continued to the end rather than stopped at the point the candidate believes they can see the answer. Candidates who shortcut any of those steps produce tables that are internally inconsistent and score partially or not at all.

Pseudocode runs into a different problem. The paper is not testing whether a candidate can write in a particular dialect; it is testing whether their algorithm is unambiguous and complete. Answers fail by omitting initialisation, by leaving a loop condition implicit, or by mixing pseudocode with Python syntax in a way that makes the intent unclear. Writing pseudocode deliberately, as a plan the candidate then implements, trains both this and the planning habit the practical component needs.

The connection between the two is the reason to teach them together. Reasoning about a program without running it is one capability, assessed in written form through traces and pseudocode, and used silently in the practical paper every time a candidate predicts what their loop will do before executing it. A candidate who can trace reliably debugs faster, because they can locate a fault by reasoning instead of by trial. Sessions that treat trace tables as a written-paper exercise alone miss that transfer entirely.

sections.heading: 4CP0 against Cambridge Computer Science and Edexcel ICT
paragraphs: Dubai schools run all three of these qualifications, often in the same corridor, and families are routinely told they are broadly the same subject. They are not, and the differences matter for both tutoring and post-16 choices. Pearson 4CP0 assesses programming onscreen in Python. Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science, code 0478, has historically assessed algorithms and programming on a written paper where candidates may answer in pseudocode or a high-level language. Pearson 4IT1 is ICT: applied software competence, assessed with a practical component in office and media packages rather than programming.

The practical consequence is that practice material does not transfer cleanly. A candidate entered for 4CP0 who revises from Cambridge programming questions will prepare for a written format they will never sit, and will arrive at an onscreen paper with no timed practice in an editor. A candidate moving between schools mid-course can find their entry code changed under them, which is worth checking rather than assuming. Always confirm the current syllabus content for any of these codes on the awarding body's own site, because specifications are revised.

For post-16 planning, the three routes lead to different places. Computer Science at 16, on either board, is the normal entry to A Level Computer Science or IB Diploma Computer Science, both of which assume independent programming. ICT at 16 builds applied capability that leads naturally into BTEC and business-facing computing courses. Neither is a weaker option in the abstract. They are different subjects, and the mismatch arises only when a family is told otherwise at an options evening.

sections.heading: Academic honesty with code, and what a tutor may do with a program
paragraphs: Computing is the subject where the line between help and substitution is easiest to cross, because a working program can be handed over in seconds and looks identical whoever typed it. The rule here is simple and it does not bend. A tutor teaches, questions, reviews and gives feedback on code the student has written. No tutor at IB Gram produces a program for a candidate to submit, and no session ends with the teacher's file saved under the student's name. Examination boards treat substituted work as malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student.

4CP0 itself carries no coursework, which removes most of the risk at this level: the onscreen component is sat under examination conditions in a supervised environment, so nothing can be submitted that was not produced there. The exposure arrives afterwards. A Level Computer Science includes a substantial programmed project, and IB Diploma Computer Science includes an internally assessed solution with documented design. Both are the student's own work and both are where providers in this market have been known to offer more than they should.

There is a second line about material. Specifications, past papers and mark schemes are referenced and linked from qualifications.pearson.com rather than reproduced or supplied as downloads, because copying them is a copyright matter. Code examples used in a session are written during the session and belong to the candidate. If any provider offers to supply a finished project, a completed solution or a ready-made program for submission, that is not a service level to negotiate. It is a reason to stop talking to them.

sections.heading: Dubai schools, KHDA and the timetable collisions that create 4CP0 gaps
paragraphs: Dubai's private school sector is large and still growing: 227 private schools served 387,441 pupils across 17 curricula in 2024-25, with 37 per cent of those pupils on a UK curriculum. Six new schools opened during 2025-26, enrolment rose by six per cent, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven more schools and 16,846 places. Growth on that scale means new campuses opening with small departments, and computing is one of the first subjects to be covered by a single specialist across several year groups.

Private schools in Dubai are regulated by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects schools on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak. An inspection report is a genuinely useful document for a parent choosing a school, and it is published by the regulator rather than by the school. It does not, however, tell you how many pupils took Computer Science last series, which is the question that actually predicts departmental depth.

The timetable collision that creates most 4CP0 tutoring requests is structural rather than anyone's fault. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and those hours are not optional. A pupil carrying mandatory subjects, a full option block and a practical computing component has a crowded week, and practical coding practice is the first thing to be squeezed because it has no homework deadline attached. That is exactly the gap a weekly session is for.
