faqs.question: What are the two components of Pearson Edexcel 4CP0 Computer Science?
faqs.answer: One is a written paper on the principles of the subject: computational thinking, data and data representation, computer systems, networks, and the issues computing raises. The other is sat onscreen, where candidates solve programming problems in Python in a provided environment. There is no coursework and no internally assessed element, so nothing accumulates across the two years. Confirm the current timings and mark totals on the specification document at qualifications.pearson.com rather than from any tutoring page, because Pearson revises specification documents and an assessment weighting needs an authoritative source.

faqs.question: Which programming language does my child need for the 4CP0 onscreen paper?
faqs.answer: Python is the language used for the Pearson onscreen component, and the paper is sat in a provided environment rather than in whatever editor the candidate prefers. Two things are worth confirming with the school: the Python version in use and the editor the onscreen paper runs in, because an unfamiliar environment costs minutes a candidate does not have. Practising in something that resembles the exam setup is part of the preparation, not a nicety. A candidate who has only ever used a browser-based tool will lose time to the interface alone.

faqs.question: My child can explain loops but cannot write a program. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: Very, and it is the most common presenting problem in this subject. Explaining a construct is receptive; writing a program from a stated problem is constructive, and the second is not built by doing more of the first. The fix is to stop demonstrating. In a session the candidate types and the teacher intervenes at the moment the error appears rather than after the run fails. Sessions end with a working program the candidate wrote and can explain line by line. Movement here is usually visible within three or four sessions.

faqs.question: Why do strong programmers lose marks on the 4CP0 written paper?
faqs.answer: Because the written component credits precise formulations rather than general understanding. Describe what a network device does and the mark scheme wants a specific function named. Explain compression and it wants a mechanism and a consequence. A candidate who understands the topic but writes around it in general terms scores a fraction of what they know. The remedy is mechanical: write the answer, mark it against the published criteria, identify the missing required element, rewrite it. Three cycles on one topic changes how a candidate writes across all of them.

faqs.question: How should a candidate complete a trace table without losing marks?
faqs.answer: One column per variable plus one for output, one row per iteration, every cell filled even when a value has not changed, and the trace carried to the end rather than stopped once the answer seems obvious. Those four rules account for almost every lost mark on trace questions. The skill transfers directly to the practical paper, because a candidate who can reason about a program without running it debugs by logic rather than by trial. Trace tables are the closest thing to reliable marks in this specification and the most frequently thrown away.

faqs.question: Is Pearson 4CP0 the same subject as Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478?
faqs.answer: The theory overlaps substantially, but the programming assessment does not. Pearson assesses programming onscreen in Python. Cambridge has historically assessed algorithms and programming on a written paper where candidates may answer in pseudocode or a high-level language. A candidate entered for 4CP0 who practises from Cambridge programming questions prepares for a format they will never sit and arrives with no timed editor practice. Confirm the entry code in writing with the school's exams officer, and check the current syllabus content on the awarding body's own site before buying revision material.

faqs.question: Should my child take Computer Science or ICT at IGCSE in Dubai?
faqs.answer: They are different subjects rather than easier and harder versions of one. Computer Science is about how computation works and requires writing programs. ICT is about applying software to tasks and is assessed on practical competence in office, database and media packages. A pupil who enjoys using computers is not automatically suited to programming about them. Computer Science is the normal route into A Level or IB Diploma Computer Science; ICT leads naturally into BTEC and business-facing computing. Choose on what the pupil actually likes doing, not on which name sounds more rigorous.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write a program for my child to submit?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody at IB Gram will. A tutor teaches, questions, reviews and gives feedback on code the student has written. No session ends with a teacher's file saved under a student's name. 4CP0 itself carries no coursework, so the onscreen paper is produced under supervision and the risk is low at this level. The exposure arrives at A Level, which includes a programmed project, and at IB Diploma Computer Science, which includes an internally assessed solution. Any provider offering a finished project is offering malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student.

faqs.question: How many sessions does the practical 4CP0 component usually take to fix?
faqs.answer: Depends where the candidate starts, and any provider quoting a number before seeing code is guessing. As a frame: a candidate who knows the constructs but cannot start a program often shows real movement within three or four sessions, because the missing piece is a planning sequence rather than knowledge. A candidate who is still uncertain about lists, loops and file handling needs a longer block, usually eight to twelve weeks of weekly practice. The honest answer comes after reading one program the candidate wrote themselves, which costs nothing.

faqs.question: What does testing mean in the 4CP0 practical paper?
faqs.answer: Every programming question implies its test cases: a valid input, a boundary value, and something invalid that the program should handle rather than crash on. Candidates who run their program once with the obvious input and move on lose marks that were available for the rest. Building a habit of trying three cases before declaring a program finished takes a few sessions and pays back on every practical question. It is also countable, which makes it a useful progress measure: how many cases did the candidate try without being prompted?

faqs.question: When are the 4CP0 exam series and who makes the entry?
faqs.answer: Pearson examines International GCSE qualifications in a May/June series and a November series each year, and the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. The entry is made by your child's school as the examination centre, not by you, and the deadline sits months before the paper. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, so a family planning travel should work from the live official timetable rather than a date restated on a tutoring page.

faqs.question: Does my child need a particular computer at home for 4CP0 preparation?
faqs.answer: Nothing expensive, but a few things matter. A physical keyboard rather than a tablet, because the practical component is typed under time and touchscreen input slows a candidate measurably. A screen large enough to show code and a problem statement together. And an installation of Python that matches what the school uses closely enough that syntax behaves identically. Python itself is free and the editors commonly used in schools are free, so the setup carries no licence cost. The constraint is a quiet hour at a desk rather than hardware.

faqs.question: Are 4CP0 lessons for Dubai families taught online or at a Dubai address?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram makes no home visits in the UAE, and home visiting is a service offered only in India. For this subject the format is an advantage rather than a compromise: a shared screen shows the editor, the error message and the candidate's cursor better than sitting beside them does, and it means you are choosing from computing specialists across overlapping time zones rather than from whoever can drive to your community by half past four.

faqs.question: How do mandatory UAE subjects affect a computing timetable in Dubai?
faqs.answer: They take real hours. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. A pupil carrying those lessons, a full option block and a practical computing component has a crowded week, and coding practice is usually the first thing squeezed because no homework deadline enforces it. Planning the week from the real timetable rather than from the examined subjects alone is what prevents the squeeze.

faqs.question: What does KHDA tell me about a Dubai school's computing department?
faqs.answer: Less than parents assume, though the reports are still worth reading. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai and inspects schools on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak, publishing the results itself. That gives you a view of the school, not of one department. For computing depth, ask the school directly how many pupils were entered for the subject in the last series and whether the post-16 course is offered. Those two answers predict departmental strength better than any band.

intro.heading: The delivery answer first, then the arithmetic
paragraphs: IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE. Home visiting is a service we operate only in India. Everything we deliver to a family here happens one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. That is stated in the first paragraph because a parent who needs a person in the room should find out now rather than after a phone call, and because the rest of this page is more useful once it is out of the way.

The phrase stays in the heading because it is what parents in this city actually type, and because the underlying question is a real one. 'Home tutor' has stopped meaning 'tutor who travels' for a large share of Dubai families; it means private, one-to-one, outside school, arranged by the parent. The genuine decision underneath is how many hours to buy, in what format, and at what rate — and that decision is badly served by a market where three of the agencies ranking for this search publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars.

So this page does the arithmetic instead. It prices in-home tutoring in Dubai line by line, including the travel that sits inside the fee and is never itemised. It works out what one session a week buys over a year against what two buy, by starting point rather than in general. It compares a group class, a paired session and one-to-one for this specific subject, since the answer differs by subject and nobody says so. It explains how the monthly packages in this market are structured and which clause in the terms matters. And it discloses what happens when no tutor of this specification is free at the hour you want, which no competitor page in this cluster does.

The subject matters to the arithmetic. Economics has no coursework, so every mark is earned in a written paper on the day, and the single most valuable thing an hour of tuition produces is a marked long answer with the judgement paragraph rebuilt. That takes a tutor twenty to thirty minutes outside the lesson. A family buying hours without marking is buying the cheap half of the service, whatever the format and whoever is in the room. This changes what a sensible number of hours looks like: fewer lessons with marking beats more lessons without it, reliably.

What follows uses market rates published by named providers and by Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. None of them is an IB Gram price list. They are here so that a parent can look at a quote and know whether it sits at the budget, qualified or specialist end of the market, which is a question nobody in this SERP currently answers.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-economics-4ec1-home-.programmesIntro: Which qualification a student sits changes what the hours have to achieve, and therefore how many are worth buying. These are the routes behind the Dubai students who reach us through this search.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Economics
programmes.description: Assessed entirely by written examination across the market system, business economics, government and the economy, and the global economy. No coursework means no banked marks, so the hours have to produce exam performance rather than a portfolio. The current specification at qualifications.pearson.com gives the component structure and weightings.
programmes.countryNote: In budget terms the absence of coursework is good news: nothing is lost before the paper is sat, so a family starting in October of Year 11 has a full runway. It also means a last-minute block in April is salvage rather than strategy, because there is no partial credit already secured to build on.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Business
programmes.description: The subject most often bought alongside Economics, working at the level of a named firm through case-study stimulus rather than at the level of markets through diagrams. Also examined by written paper, so the same marking logic applies to the hours.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Dubai family wants both subjects covered, one tutor who teaches both is usually better value than two, provided the student keeps the registers separate. We will say if the combination is not realistic for a particular tutor rather than stretching one across both.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Accounting
programmes.description: Double entry, final accounts and interpretation. The most mechanical of the commerce group, and the one where hours convert into marks most predictably, because errors are traceable to a specific step rather than to a habit of thought.
programmes.countryNote: Families budgeting across two commerce subjects often find Accounting needs fewer hours than Economics for the same grade movement. That is worth knowing when a fixed tuition budget has to be split between subjects in Year 11.

programmes.name: A Level Economics and IB Diploma Economics
programmes.description: The continuation routes after 16 in Dubai. Both assume the diagram fluency and the weighing habit 4EC1 is meant to install, and both expose a student who reached a good IGCSE grade by memorising answers rather than constructing them.
programmes.countryNote: If sixth form is the reason for buying hours now, the brief is different and cheaper: fewer sessions, aimed at method, finished before the series. That plan survives into Year 12, which a crash block in April does not.

subjects.description: Moderately hour-hungry. A diagram block of four to six sessions, then one marked long answer a week. Roughly thirty marked answers across Year 11 is the realistic target, and it is achievable on one hour a week if the writing happens between lessons.

subjects.description: Similar hour profile, with the hours weighted towards case-study reading and the calculation set. Students who read the stimulus closely need fewer hours than those who answer in general terms.

sections.heading: What in-home Economics tutoring in Dubai costs, line by line
paragraphs: An in-home hourly rate is a bundle, and nobody itemises it. Taking it apart is the most useful thing a parent can do before comparing two quotes, because two providers charging AED 250 can be selling quite different things. The components are teaching time, travel, marking, materials and the risk the provider carries on cancellations — and the proportions vary enormously.

The market bands are these, from published sources. In-home one-to-one in Dubai, travel included, runs roughly AED 180 to AED 500: Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table gives AED 180 to 350 and independently advertised home tutors reach AED 500. Monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions appear at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799. Online, qualified subject teachers sit at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors advertising IGCSE from AED 150; specialists run AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270; budget provision starts around AED 45, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Premium named tutors reach AED 650 at BartyED. Online monthly packages appear at AED 799 for eight sessions.

Inside an in-home fee, travel is the line that is never shown and is often the largest after teaching time. A tutor making one visit to Nad Al Sheba or Mirdif in the evening peak gives up more than an hour in a car for a one-hour booking, and that time is paid for either in the rate or by the tutor restricting themselves to three nearby communities. Marking is the line most often missing entirely: a provider quoting AED 300 for a visit with no written marking is charging specialist money for the cheap half of the service.

The table itemises what we would expect to find inside a Dubai in-home quote and what a parent can remove. The practical advice is to ask for the quote broken into teaching, marking and travel. A provider who cannot or will not do that is usually one where marking does not exist.

sections.heading: Travel time is the hidden hour
paragraphs: The number that changes a tuition decision in this city is not the hourly rate. It is the travel, and it acts on both sides of the transaction. For the family, an in-home visit means an arrival window rather than a start time, because the drive from Al Barsha to Mirdif at six in the evening is not a fixed quantity. For the tutor, it means a one-hour booking costs two hours of their evening, which is why in-home tutors cluster their work into a few communities and why a family outside those communities faces either a premium or a short list.

This is the mechanism behind something parents notice and cannot explain: a highly recommended tutor is 'not taking anyone new' in one community while having availability in another. It is not preference. It is arithmetic. Three bookings in the same cluster is a workable evening; three bookings spread across the city is not, at any rate the market will bear.

The consequence for a narrow brief is severe. Pearson 4EC1 is a specific specification, and the pool of tutors who have taught it is much smaller than the pool of people who can teach economics. Filter that pool by willingness to drive to a particular community at a particular hour on a particular weekday, and the list can reach zero. At that point a family either waits, accepts a tutor who has not taught the specification, or changes format. The third option is the only one that does not cost something real.

Removing travel also removes the main cause of lost sessions. A visit cancelled because of traffic, a flat tyre or a family trip is usually an hour gone. An online session moves to another slot, runs from a hotel room during half-term, and continues through school exam leave. Over a year, that difference alone is several hours of teaching a family paid for and did not receive.

sections.heading: One session a week or two? The arithmetic by starting point
paragraphs: Families ask this question in the abstract and it only has concrete answers. The variable that matters is not ability but the specific deficit, because the deficits take different amounts of time. A student whose diagrams are unlabelled needs four to six focused sessions and then one a week. A student who has never written a judgement paragraph needs a year of weekly marked answers. A student who has not met exchange rates at all needs two sessions on content before weekly practice is worth anything.

The second variable is capacity to absorb marking. One marked long answer a week, properly reviewed, generates about as much correction as a sixteen-year-old can act on alongside nine other subjects. Two a week works for a short block, particularly before a series, and stops working as a standing arrangement because the student starts attending lessons rather than changing behaviour. This is the honest reason we usually decline a request for three hours a week in October.

The third is the calendar. Thirty marked long answers is the figure we aim at across a Year 11, and it is achievable on one hour a week starting in September. Starting in February, the same thirty requires three hours a week and will not happen. Which means the single most cost-effective decision in this whole market is to start earlier rather than to buy more, and it is the advice families most often ignore and most often regret.

sections.heading: Group class, paired session, one-to-one: what each buys for Economics
paragraphs: Cheaper formats are not worse formats; they are formats that move different marks. Being specific about which is which saves families money, and it is a conversation the market avoids because the expensive option is more profitable. For Economics the split is unusually clean, because the subject's marks come from three distinguishable performances.

Diagram fluency and definitions respond well to a group or paired setting. They are drillable, benchmarkable and slightly competitive, and a student is often sharper with a peer in the room than with an adult. A tuition-centre group class at the lower end of the market can do real work here, and a family on a budget should not be talked out of it.

Long-answer judgement does not work in a group. The useful minutes are spent on one student's sentence, with their particular habit of listing rather than weighing, and five other students are watching someone else's problem being solved. This is the part that has to be one-to-one and marked, and it is also the part that carries the highest-value marks. A family with a limited budget is usually better served by fewer one-to-one hours on judgement than by many group hours on content.

The table compares the three formats on what they move. The rate ranges are market figures from the sources already cited; the judgement is ours, based on which marks each format can realistically shift. A family can also mix them deliberately: a group class for content coverage through the autumn, then one-to-one hours bought for the judgement work in the spring, which is cheaper than either format run alone for a full year and is the plan we suggest most often to families naming a fixed budget.

sections.heading: Tutor continuity, and why the third change is the expensive one
paragraphs: Every change of tutor costs roughly three sessions. The new tutor has to establish what the student can already do, which means a diagnostic, a first marked answer and a recalibration. One change in a two-year course of study is normal and often correct. Three changes means nine sessions spent on diagnosis, which at specialist rates is a meaningful share of a year's budget spent discovering things that were already known.

The practical defence is to make the first match carefully and to give it six weeks before judging it. Six weeks is roughly the point at which a marked baseline answer can be compared with a current one, and the comparison is more reliable than a student's report of whether they like the tutor. Liking matters — a student who dreads the hour will not write between sessions — but it is not the same signal as progress, and families sometimes change a tutor who was working.

The defence on our side is to hold one named tutor for the year wherever possible, and to say early if that is not possible. A tutor whose availability changes in January is a problem we should raise in December, not a surprise in the week it happens. Where a change is unavoidable, the handover should include the marked scripts and the tracker, so the incoming tutor starts from evidence rather than from a conversation.

One thing worth asking any agency directly: who employs the tutor, and what happens if the match does not work. An agency with a replacement process will tell you how it works; a marketplace will usually tell you to pick someone else. Neither is wrong, but the second means the diagnosis cost falls on you each time, and it should be priced into the comparison.

sections.heading: How families pay in this market, and the clause that matters
paragraphs: Three payment structures are common in Dubai, and they distribute risk differently. Hourly, paid as you go, puts all the flexibility with the family and tends to carry the highest headline rate. A block of hours bought up front gets a discount and transfers the risk of non-use to the family. A monthly package — AED 799 for eight sessions online, AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, on the figures published in this market — is the most common and the least transparent, because the terms do the work rather than the price.

The clause to read is carry-over. A month with a half-term in it has fewer usable weeks, and a package that expires monthly quietly costs more per delivered hour than the headline suggests. Second is the cancellation window: twenty-four hours is normal and reasonable; same-day cancellation being chargeable is also reasonable, provided it is stated. Third is whether marking is included and in what volume, since 'eight sessions' says nothing about whether eight long answers come back marked.

On conditions attached to anything described as free, we state ours: the trial lesson is thirty minutes, requires no card details, and carries no obligation to continue. Where any provider offers a free trial, the useful questions are how long it lasts, whether it is with the tutor you would actually get, and whether declining is straightforward. A trial with a different tutor from the one who would teach is a sales call rather than a lesson.

On data, a tuition enquiry about a minor involves personal information governed by UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection. The information needed to match a tutor is year group, school, board, subject code and a parent contact. A child's photograph, full report history and grade records are not needed for matching, and a provider collecting them should be asked why and for how long. Deletion can be requested at any time.

sections.heading: If no 4EC1 specialist is free: the fallback, disclosed
paragraphs: No competitor page in this cluster admits a coverage limit, and every matching service has one. Pearson 4EC1 at the hour a particular Dubai family needs is a narrow brief, and there are weeks when nobody suitable is available. The useful thing is to publish what happens next rather than to improvise it on a call.

Our order of preference is: the right tutor at a different hour, which families resist and which is usually the best option; the right tutor starting in two or three weeks, with a date given; a tutor who teaches the Cambridge equivalent, which transfers for diagrams, definitions and judgement but not for Pearson's command-word conventions or paper structure, and we say which parts transfer; or an honest statement that we cannot cover this brief this term. We do not put a general economics graduate on a 4EC1 brief and let a family discover it in week four.

This matters more for Economics than for a large subject like Mathematics, because the specification-specific knowledge is a larger share of the value. The difference between a tutor who has taught 4EC1 and one who has not shows up in small, decisive things: whether the original curve stays visible on a shifted diagram, how much is written for a four-mark question, whether the judgement sentence is treated as the target or the afterthought.
The table sets out what we tell families about availability by brief. It is a disclosure rather than a promise about timing, and the honest version of the last column is sometimes 'nothing suitable'.

sections.heading: The two topics worth paying for separately
paragraphs: If a family can only buy a handful of hours, the question becomes which content to spend them on. Across marked scripts two sections stand out, not because they are the hardest but because of where they sit in the school year. Exchange rates and the balance of payments are taught late in most schemes of work, arrive when Year 11 is already busy with mocks, and depend on a diagram students have had the least practice drawing.

Exchange rates are worth an hour on their own, and in Dubai the hour is unusually productive because the example is local. The dirham's peg to the US dollar converts an abstract topic into a policy constraint with visible consequences: a student can reason about what happens to competitiveness and tourism when the dollar strengthens and the central bank cannot let the currency fall. That argument, attached to a correctly labelled diagram, is something most candidates worldwide cannot produce.

The balance of payments is worth a second hour for a different reason: it is where students confuse categories. A current account deficit is not a government deficit, imports are not debts, and a trade surplus is not automatically good. These are definition failures rather than reasoning failures, and they are cheap to fix once named — which is exactly why a targeted hour beats a general revision block.

Elasticity is the third candidate and the most commonly misjudged. It is taught early, assumed understood, and then needed in almost every section of the paper. A student who cannot say confidently whether a revenue claim depends on elastic or inelastic demand will leak marks across the whole specification, and a diagnostic question on it belongs in the first session rather than the tenth.

sections.heading: Private candidates, November entry and the position on home visits
paragraphs: Two practical matters close out the page. The first is private candidacy. A student not entered through their school — because of a resit, a late subject addition or a move between systems — sits as a private candidate at a centre that accepts them, and the entry is arranged with that centre rather than with a tutor. Deadlines sit months before the papers. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November, the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and results timings are published: June 2026 reached students on 20 August 2026 and November 2025 on 22 January 2026. Pearson issues provisional timetables that can be revised, so the live timetable at qualifications.pearson.com is the authority.

The second is the permit question, which parents are entitled to ask any tutor. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include teachers in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so any figure quoted at you is unverified. MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service is the official route. Separately, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school, so 'your child's own teacher, privately' is not an arrangement to seek out.

On delivery, to close where the page opened: IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE, and that is not a limitation we are reluctant about. It is what lets a family in Mirdif or International City choose a tutor on 4EC1 experience instead of on willingness to drive. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity requiring a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which we neither hold nor claim.

What a family gets instead is a named tutor, a protected weekly hour on Gulf Standard Time, a long answer marked between sessions, a written note each week, and a six-week review at which reducing hours is a genuine outcome. That is the whole offer, and it is deliberately easier to compare against a quote than a package description is.

process.title: Send the code, the mock and the budget
process.description: Three things shape the plan: Pearson 4EC1 confirmed rather than assumed, the most recent mock or marked assessment, and the number of hours you are willing to buy. The third is not a rude question — a plan built for one hour a week is a different plan, not a worse one.

process.title: A trial lesson at no charge
process.description: Thirty minutes with the tutor who would actually teach, no card details taken, no obligation afterwards. Two diagrams drawn from blank axes and one extract read aloud is usually enough to identify which deficit is costing the grade and therefore how many hours it needs.

process.title: Agree the hours in writing, with the carry-over rule
process.description: How many sessions, over how many weeks, how many marked answers included, and what happens to an hour cancelled at short notice. Half-terms and school exam leave are named in advance so a month with fewer usable weeks does not quietly cost more per hour.

process.title: Run the plan, with evidence each week
process.description: The protected hour on Gulf Standard Time, one long answer written midweek and marked before the session, a short written note naming what the student is now doing differently, and the marked script sent to you rather than summarised.

process.title: Review at six weeks: continue, change or reduce
process.description: The baseline answer against a current one. Continuing is one outcome; changing tutor is another; reducing hours is the third and we propose it when the evidence supports it, which most families are surprised to be offered by anyone selling hours.

whyPoints.title: The fee is taken apart rather than quoted
whyPoints.description: Teaching, marking, travel, materials, cancellation risk and margin are different things inside one hourly rate. Asking a provider to split a quote into teaching, marking and travel is the fastest way to find out whether marking exists, and a provider who will not split it usually has an answer you want to know.

whyPoints.title: Hours are costed by deficit, not sold as a package
whyPoints.description: Unlabelled diagrams need a five-session block; a missing judgement paragraph needs a year of weekly marked answers; an unmet topic needs two content sessions first. Those are different purchases, and quoting one package for all three is how families end up buying hours they cannot use.

whyPoints.title: Cheaper formats are recommended where they work
whyPoints.description: Diagram drilling and definition testing work in a paired or group setting and cost less. Long-answer judgement does not, because the useful minutes belong to one student's sentence. We say which is which, including when a tuition-centre class is the right call for a budget.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits are published, not improvised
whyPoints.description: When no tutor of this specification is free at your hour, the options are a different hour, a dated wait, a Cambridge-trained substitute with the transferable parts named, or an honest no. Placing a general economics graduate on a 4EC1 brief is the failure that costs a term.

whyPoints.title: Reducing hours is a real outcome
whyPoints.description: At the six-week review we compare a baseline marked answer with a current one, and sometimes the answer is fewer sessions or none. Proposing that is unusual in a market paid by the hour, which is precisely why it belongs in the review rather than in a sales line.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and data stated up front
whyPoints.description: One-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; no home visits in the UAE, a service that exists only in India. For matching we need year group, school, board, subject code and a parent contact, nothing more, under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021, deletable on request.

faqs.question: How much does an Economics home tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: In-home one-to-one in Dubai runs roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel inside the fee: Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table gives AED 180 to 350 and independently advertised home tutors reach AED 500. Monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions appear at AED 1,599 to 1,799. Online, qualified subject teachers sit at AED 150 to 300 and specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. Those are market figures from the providers that publish them, not our price list. Ask for any quote split into teaching, marking and travel.

faqs.question: Does an in-home Economics tutor charge for travel time in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Almost never as a separate line, and always inside the rate. A tutor making one visit to Mirdif or Nad Al Sheba during the evening peak gives up well over an hour of driving for a one-hour booking, and that is paid for either in a higher quoted rate or by the tutor only accepting bookings in two or three nearby communities. That second effect is why a recommended tutor can be unavailable in your community while having slots in another. It is arithmetic rather than preference.

faqs.question: Is one Economics session a week enough, or should we book two?
faqs.answer: One hour a week with a long answer written and marked between lessons is the common and usually sufficient pattern, because the limiting factor is how much marked correction a sixteen-year-old can act on alongside nine other subjects. Two a week works for a short pre-series block or for a student starting late with a named deficit. Three is rarely productive as a standing arrangement. The highest-return decision is starting in September rather than February: thirty marked answers is easy on one hour a week from autumn and impossible from spring.

faqs.question: What is the difference in price between a group Economics class and one-to-one?
faqs.answer: A tuition-centre group class is the cheapest option per student and a specialist one-to-one hour the dearest, with paired sessions between them. The more useful question is what each format moves. Group and paired settings work well for diagram drilling, definitions and timed short answers, which are drillable and slightly competitive. They do not work for long-answer judgement, where the useful minutes are spent rebuilding one student's sentence. A limited budget often does better on fewer one-to-one hours on judgement than many group hours on content.

faqs.question: What happens if no 4EC1 specialist is available when we ask?
faqs.answer: We say so, and name the options in order: the right tutor at a different hour, which families resist and which is usually best; the right tutor starting in two or three weeks with a date given; a Cambridge-trained tutor, where we state that diagrams, definitions and judgement transfer but Pearson command-word conventions and paper structure do not; or an honest statement that we cannot cover the brief this term. What we do not do is place a general economics graduate on a 4EC1 brief and let you find out in week four.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an Economics tutor to our villa in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. All delivery to UAE families is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For this subject that is an advantage rather than a compromise: diagrams are drawn, deliberately broken and redrawn on a shared whiteboard with every version saved, marked answers reach you as files, and the tutor is chosen on 4EC1 experience rather than on willingness to drive to your community at six in the evening.

faqs.question: How long does a course of Economics tutoring usually run?
faqs.answer: It depends on the starting point rather than on a standard length. A Year 10 with no specific problem can run one hour a week across two school years with slack in the plan. A Year 11 starting in September needs a five-session diagram block and then weekly marked answers to the series. A Year 11 starting in March gets eight to ten weeks of two hours, which covers diagrams, the judgement shape and three full papers while dropping definition depth and most content teaching. Naming what gets dropped is part of an honest plan.

faqs.question: Can we start Economics tutoring in Year 10 and stop before Year 11?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for some students it is the better buy. A Year 10 block that installs diagram fluency and the judgement sentence shape leaves a student able to use their own school teaching properly for the whole of Year 11, which is cheaper than paying someone to supply what the school already provides. The risk is decay: definitions and diagram labelling fade without testing. A short refresher in the autumn of Year 11 protects the earlier investment at a fraction of a full year's hours.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper university-student tutor good enough for 4EC1?
faqs.answer: For diagram drilling and definition testing, often yes, and a family on a budget should not be talked out of it. Budget online provision in this market starts around AED 45, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Where it falls short is specification knowledge and marking: whether the original curve must stay visible on a shifted diagram, how much to write for a four-mark question, whether a judgement sentence is the target. Those come from having taught the course, not from having studied economics.

faqs.question: Do we pay per hour or per month for Economics tutoring?
faqs.answer: Both exist in Dubai. Hourly keeps flexibility with the family and carries a higher headline rate. Monthly packages are more common and less transparent: the published examples in this market are AED 799 online for eight sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 in-home for four two-hour sessions. The clause that decides the real cost is carry-over, because a month containing a half-term has fewer usable weeks. Read that, the cancellation window, and whether a stated number of sessions includes the same number of marked answers.

faqs.question: Will the same Economics tutor stay with my child all year?
faqs.answer: That is what we aim for, and we say early if it is not possible rather than announcing a change in the week it happens. Every change costs roughly three sessions, because a new tutor needs a diagnostic, a first marked answer and a recalibration. One change in two years is normal; three means nine sessions spent rediscovering known things. Where a change is unavoidable, the handover should include the marked scripts and the tracker so the incoming tutor starts from evidence rather than from a conversation.

faqs.question: Can Economics sessions move to post-Iftar timing in Dubai during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we plan for it rather than treating it as a disruption. Weekly slots are re-agreed for the month and returned to the original time afterwards. For a student fasting through a school day, two shorter focused sessions often work better than one full hour, and diagram drilling suits that format better than long-answer rebuilding does. School exam leave and family travel are the other predictable interruptions in a Dubai year, and online delivery means a session can run from wherever your child happens to be.

faqs.question: What should an Economics tutor send a parent each month?
faqs.answer: Each week, the marked long answer and a short note saying what was covered and the single thing your child is now doing differently. Each month, a paragraph on whether the plan is working, which should reference the baseline answer rather than general impressions. If none of that arrives, the hour is a conversation rather than tuition, whatever the format or the rate. Ask for it in week one rather than month three, by which point a term of evidence has gone unrecorded.

faqs.question: Which Dubai areas do your Economics tutors cover?
faqs.answer: All of them, because nobody is travelling. Sessions run over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so Mirdif, International City, Nad Al Sheba and Al Furjan are served identically to The Greens or Jumeirah. That is the practical point of the format: the communities where in-home tutors are scarcest and quote highest are exactly the ones where an online specialist costs the same as anywhere else. What varies by area is the realistic start time, which depends on your school run rather than on the tutor's.

faqs.question: Can my child take Economics 4EC1 as a private candidate in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, through a centre that accepts private candidates, and the entry is arranged with that centre rather than with a tutor. Deadlines sit months before the papers. Pearson International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026 and November 2025 results on 22 January 2026. Provisional timetables can be revised, so check the live timetable at qualifications.pearson.com and speak to the centre's exams officer early.

faqs.question: Is exchange-rate theory worth a separate session?
faqs.answer: For a Dubai candidate, yes, and it is one of the best hours a family can buy. The topic sits late in most schemes of work, arrives when Year 11 is busy with mocks, and uses a diagram students have drawn least often. The local example makes it unusually productive: the dirham's peg to the US dollar removes exchange rate adjustment as a policy tool, so a student can reason about competitiveness and tourism when the dollar strengthens. Two sentences of that beside a labelled diagram is an answer most candidates cannot write.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-economics-4ec1-home-.closingHeading: Buy fewer hours, earlier, with marking in them
dubai/edexcel-igcse-economics-4ec1-home-.closingBody: If you have been pricing an Edexcel IGCSE Economics 4EC1 home tutor in Dubai, the decision that saves the most money is not which rate to accept but when to start and what to include. Thirty marked long answers is straightforward on one hour a week from September and impossible from February on any budget. Ask any provider to split a quote into teaching, marking and travel, and ask whether the trial is with the tutor who would actually teach. Ours is thirty minutes, needs no card details and carries no obligation. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-economics-4ec1-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Economics to Years 10 and 11. Sessions are run on a shared whiteboard so diagrams can be drawn and corrected live, with long answers marked between lessons against the published criteria.

intro.heading: Why a student who understands economics still scores a 5 in 4EC1
paragraphs: Economics punishes a particular kind of student: the one who follows the news, argues well at dinner and understands every concept in the course. They explain inflation clearly, they know what a subsidy does, and they come out of the paper at a grade 5. The reason is almost never understanding. It is that the paper awards marks for three specific technical performances — a correctly labelled diagram, an answer anchored in the extract, and a judgement that weighs one effect against another — and a student can be fluent in economics without ever having been drilled in any of them.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Economics carries the specification code 4EC1. The content divides into the market system, business economics, government and the economy, and the global economy, assessed by written examination. The current specification at qualifications.pearson.com sets out the components, their durations and their weightings, and it is the document to check rather than a tutor's memory of an earlier version. What does not change between versions is the three performances above, which is where a course of study should spend its time.

Take the diagram first. A demand and supply diagram is worth marks for the axes, for the curves being labelled, for the shift going the right way, for the new equilibrium being marked, and for the old one still being visible. A student who draws a beautiful curve and forgets to label the vertical axis has thrown away a mark that cost no knowledge at all. Across a paper, labelling errors alone routinely account for a grade. This is the cheapest thing a tutor fixes and the reason the first three sessions are often spent with a pen rather than a textbook.

The second performance is the extract. Data-response questions give a student a passage and a figure or two, and the marks sit in using them. A student who writes a correct, general answer about exchange rates when the extract was about a specific currency movement has answered a different question. The habit to install is mechanical: before writing anything, underline two figures and one phrase from the extract, and make sure each appears in the answer. It takes forty seconds and it is the difference between application marks and no application marks.

The third is judgement, and it is where the highest-value marks sit. The long question's final marks are awarded for weighing: this effect matters more in the short run, that one depends on how responsive demand is, this conclusion holds unless the government also does something else. Students leave those marks unwritten because they run out of time, because nobody told them the sentence was worth more than the paragraph above it, or because they think a judgement needs to be original. It does not. It needs to be a comparison, stated, with a reason.

Extract figures underlined and used before a sentence is written
The judgement sentence treated as the highest-value mark on the page
UAE and Gulf examples rehearsed so they come out under pressure
Lessons one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time

dubai/edexcel-igcse-economics-4ec1-tutor.programmesIntro: 4EC1 sits in the social-science option block at 16, and which programme a Dubai student is on changes how much of the course arrives as new material. These are the routes that matter for Economics tuition in this city.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Economics
programmes.description: Graded 9-1 and assessed by written examination across the market system, business economics, government and the economy, and the global economy. There is no coursework component, which means every mark is earned under time pressure on the day and makes timed practice the whole of the preparation.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai centres can enter either the May/June or the November Pearson series, and both are used here, with November carrying resits and private candidates. Because there is no coursework to bank, a weak mock in January is entirely recoverable — a point worth making to a Year 11 who has decided the grade is already fixed.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Business
programmes.description: The subject 4EC1 is most often confused with and most often taken alongside. Business works at the level of the firm through case-study stimulus; Economics works at the level of the market and the economy. Both reward applied judgement, but the content overlaps less than option-evening conversations suggest.
programmes.countryNote: A good number of Dubai schools timetable both and let students take either or both. Where a family is choosing, the practical question is whether the student prefers reasoning with diagrams or reasoning about a named firm, because that preference predicts the grade better than general ability does.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme, Individuals and Societies
programmes.description: The alternative route at 16 in Dubai's IB schools, assessed against criteria rather than by terminal paper. Students transferring into a 4EC1 class from MYP arrive with strong inquiry habits and no experience of answering a four-mark question in four minutes.
programmes.countryNote: The gap is timing and precision rather than content, and it closes quickly with drilled short-answer practice. Dubai sees enough mid-phase school moves for this to be a recurring brief, usually appearing as a student whose extended writing is good and whose short answers are oddly weak.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-economics-4ec1-tutor.subjectsIntro: Economics is rarely taken alone. Dubai option blocks pair it with business and humanities subjects, and families usually ask about one of the codes below in the same conversation.

subjects.name: Economics (4EC1)
subjects.description: The market system, business economics, government and the economy, the global economy. Marks are lost on diagram labelling, on answers that ignore the extract, and on long questions that explain thoroughly and never judge.

subjects.name: Business (4BS1)
subjects.description: Enterprise, people, finance, marketing and operations, assessed through case-study stimulus. Students who do well here read the stimulus closely and use the named firm rather than writing about business in general.

subjects.name: Accounting (4AC1)
subjects.description: Double entry, final accounts and interpretation. The most mechanical of the three commerce subjects and the one where consistent practice shows up fastest, because errors are traceable to a specific step.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (4MA1)
subjects.description: Tiered, with a grade ceiling on the Foundation tier. Relevant to Economics because percentage change, index numbers and reading graphs carry into 4EC1 data response more than students expect.

subjects.name: Geography (4GE1)
subjects.description: Human geography overlaps directly with development and trade in Economics. Students taking both can reuse case-study material, provided they adapt the examples to what each paper's command words actually ask for.

subjects.name: History (4HI1)
subjects.description: Source handling and extended writing. The weighing habit that earns Economics judgement marks is the same habit History rewards in a 'how far do you agree' question, which is why the two transfer well.

subjects.name: English Language A (4EA1)
subjects.description: Non-fiction reading and transactional writing. Weak extract handling in Economics is sometimes a reading problem rather than an economics problem, and this is where that shows up first.

subjects.name: Mathematics B (4MB1)
subjects.description: The untiered alternative used by some Dubai schools for stronger mathematicians, often alongside Economics for students pointing at an economics or finance degree where quantitative confidence matters.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first language
subjects.description: Required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs and Standard Arabic as the language of instruction. It occupies real timetable space alongside option subjects.

sections.heading: The six diagrams that carry a 4EC1 grade
paragraphs: Economics at this level is unusual in that a small, closed set of diagrams accounts for a disproportionate share of the marks. Learn them properly and a predictable slice of every paper becomes free. Learn them approximately and the same slice leaks marks in ways that look careless on a script and feel unfair to a student who understood the question perfectly.

The errors are consistent across scripts and they are nearly all labelling. An unlabelled vertical axis. A curve shifted without the original left visible, so the examiner cannot see the change. A new equilibrium not marked. Price and quantity axes swapped, which happens more often than anyone admits under time pressure. An arrow showing a movement along a curve when the question described a shift of it. None of these indicate a misunderstanding of economics, and all of them cost marks.

The drill we use is deliberately repetitive and students find it tedious for about two sessions. Draw the diagram from blank axes. Then the tutor redraws it with one element removed or wrong, and the student finds the fault. Then it is drawn again against a ninety-second clock. A shared whiteboard makes this work better than paper, because the tutor can break a diagram instantly and because every version is saved, so the student ends the block with a sheet of diagrams they drew themselves rather than one photographed from a revision guide.

The table lists the set we drill, what each one is normally asked about, and the specific labelling failure that costs the mark. The diagram set your child's school teaches may differ slightly in emphasis, so confirm the list with their teacher — but these six cover the territory most papers draw on.

sections.heading: Data response is a reading test wearing an economics costume
paragraphs: Every data-response question hands the student an extract and some figures, and a large share of the available marks is reserved for using them. Students who have revised hard are the most likely to lose those marks, because they arrive with a prepared answer and deliver it. The examiner sees a competent general answer about inflation and credits only the part that engages with the particular situation described.

The fix is a forty-second routine, done before any writing. Read the extract once. Underline two figures and one phrase. Write those three things at the top of the answer space. Then make sure each one appears in the response, used rather than quoted — a figure that is copied into a sentence without being interpreted earns nothing. Students resist the routine because it feels like wasted time when the clock is running. It is the highest-return forty seconds on the paper.

There is a second-order skill here that separates grade 6 from grade 8: choosing which figure matters. An extract will contain numbers that are decorative and numbers that are load-bearing, and the load-bearing one is usually the one that changed. A student who notices that unemployment fell while output also fell has something to say; a student who repeats the population figure has filled a line. We practise this by giving extracts and asking only one question — which number is the question really about — before any answer is written.

Marking shows the pattern clearly. Across a set of scripts, the students who lose application marks are rarely the ones who understood least. They are the ones who wrote most. Volume feels like effort and reads like avoidance, and the correction is to write less while pointing at more of the extract.
bullets: Forty seconds before writing: two figures and one phrase underlined
Each underlined item used in the answer, not quoted decoratively
Identify the load-bearing number, which is usually the one that changed
Shorter answers that engage the extract beat longer general ones
Practise by asking which number the question is actually about

sections.heading: The judgement sentence, written three ways
paragraphs: The last marks on a long question are the most valuable and the most often unclaimed. They are awarded for judgement: a comparison between two effects, with a stated reason for favouring one. Students leave them unwritten for three reasons — time ran out, nobody told them the final sentences outweighed the paragraph above, or they believe a judgement must be clever. None of those is hard to fix once named.

What a judgement actually requires is modest. It compares: this effect is larger than that one. It conditions: this holds in the short run, or if demand is inelastic, or unless the government also raises the subsidy. It commits: having compared and conditioned, it says which way the answer falls. Three clauses. A student who writes those three clauses reliably will out-score a student who writes two extra paragraphs of explanation, every time.

We teach it as a sentence shape rather than as a thinking style, because a shape can be practised. The student writes the comparison clause first, then the condition, then the commitment, and reads it back. After a few weeks they start writing the judgement sentence before the body paragraphs, which is a strong sign the habit has transferred — it means they now know where the answer is going before they start arguing for it.

The table below is the version we show parents, because it makes the grade bands legible without a mark scheme. It is an illustration of answer shapes, not a reproduction of Pearson's criteria, which are published on the specification and should be read there.

table.caption: THREE WAYS TO END A 4EC1 LONG ANSWER — AN ILLUSTRATION, NOT A MARK SCHEME
columns: How it reads to an examiner
rows: 'A subsidy lowers costs, so supply increases and price falls.'
Any comparison; the highest-value marks are untouched
'A subsidy helps consumers. However, it costs the government money.'
Two points placed side by side with nothing weighed
A reason for preferring one over the other
'The consumer gain is larger here because demand is price-sensitive, though it depends on the subsidy lasting beyond one year.'
A judgement with a stated reason and a condition
Nothing essential; this is where the top marks sit
'On balance the subsidy is justified in the short run, because the cost is fixed while the fall in price is sustained.'
A decision taken, with a basis for it
Nothing, provided the body paragraphs support the decision

sections.heading: Definitions where close is not close enough
paragraphs: A surprising share of marks in 4EC1 are awarded for definitions, and a surprising share of those are lost by students who could explain the concept for ten minutes. The reason is that mark schemes reward a specific element, and a near-miss definition omits it. 'Inflation is when prices go up' is not what the mark scheme wants, because it leaves out the general level and the sustained period. The student knows both. They just did not write them.

This makes definitions one of the few areas in the course where rote work genuinely pays. We build a list, not from a glossary but from the student's own errors as they appear in marked answers, and test it orally at the start of sessions. Thirty definitions, tested cold and repeatedly, is a small investment that recovers marks across every section of the paper. It is also the part of the course a parent can supervise without knowing any economics, which makes it useful homework.

The second half of the problem is precision under pressure. A student who can define opportunity cost calmly will produce 'what you lose' in the exam hall. The drill is therefore timed and verbal: the tutor says a term, the student has eight seconds. It feels like a quiz and it works, because the retrieval under mild pressure is what the exam actually requires.

The table lists definitions where the near-miss is common enough to be predictable. These are drawn from marked scripts rather than from a textbook, which is why some obvious terms are absent — students rarely get those wrong.

sections.heading: Using UAE examples instead of textbook ones
paragraphs: Examiners read thousands of answers about British bus fares and American tariffs. A student writing about something real, specific and local stands out for the right reason, provided the example is used to make an economic point rather than to show local knowledge. Dubai students have better examples available than most candidates in the world and almost never use them, because the textbook was written elsewhere.

Several are directly usable. The dirham is pegged to the US dollar, which turns the exchange-rate section from an abstraction into a policy choice with visible consequences: a student can discuss why a pegged currency removes one policy tool and what that does to competitiveness when the dollar moves. The UAE introduced value added tax in January 2018 and a federal corporate tax in 2023, giving two concrete indirect and direct tax examples with dates. Free zones such as those at Jebel Ali and Dubai Silicon Oasis are a live illustration of incentives attracting foreign investment.

The best example in the whole course, and the one nobody uses, is school fees. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. That is a maximum-price intervention in a market the student is personally inside: a price cap, a market with rising demand, and a predictable set of consequences to reason about. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25 across 17 curricula, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new schools creating 16,846 places, with enrolment up 6% in 2025-26. A student who can discuss supply responding to demand using those figures is writing an answer the examiner has not read before.

The discipline is to use the example economically. A paragraph about Dubai that never names a mechanism is tourism marketing. A sentence that says the fee freeze is a price ceiling, that excess demand is the predictable consequence, and that new school places are the supply response, is economics with a local example attached. We rehearse three or four of these per student so they emerge under pressure, and we keep them short.

sections.heading: What Economics tuition costs in the Dubai market, in dirhams
paragraphs: This market publishes very little pricing. Of the providers competing for these searches, three publish no hourly figure at all and two quote in US dollars. The bands below are market rates taken from providers' own published pricing and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. They are the market, not an IB Gram price list, and they are here so that a parent can judge a quote before accepting it.

Budget online provision runs from about AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject teacher online sits between roughly AED 150 and AED 300, with Unitors advertising IGCSE from AED 150. In-home one-to-one, travel included, is commonly AED 180 to AED 500: Bestimate's band is AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertise to AED 500. Subject specialists at IGCSE and A Level run AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named tutors reach AED 650 at BartyED. Monthly packages appear at AED 799 online for eight sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 in-home for four two-hour sessions.

For Economics specifically there are two questions worth asking that the rate does not answer. The first is whether long answers are marked in writing outside the lesson, which takes a tutor twenty to thirty minutes per question and is where the judgement marks are won. The second is whether the tutor has taught this specification rather than economics in general. A university economics graduate can explain elasticity beautifully and still not know that the diagram needs the original curve left visible, which is the kind of thing only specification experience teaches.

On value, the arithmetic favours starting early and buying few hours. One marked long answer a week from October of Year 11 is roughly thirty marked questions before the series. The same budget spent in April buys eight, at the point where the student has least capacity to absorb feedback. Families who ask us how to spend less are usually told to start sooner rather than to buy a cheaper tutor.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the Pearson series
paragraphs: No competitor page in this cluster names an exam session, a registration deadline or a results date, which is a strange gap given that the calendar decides whether tuition bought in February is useful. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and in November each year, and Dubai centres use both series. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers, and they are handled by the school's exams officer rather than by a tutor.

The published dates worth diarising are these. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also issues provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, and those provisional documents can be revised — so the live timetable at qualifications.pearson.com is the authority, not this page.

Counting backwards changes what a sensible plan looks like. Diagram drilling belongs early, because every later question depends on it and because it is the cheapest grade available. Definition work runs throughout, tested orally, because it decays. Long-answer practice needs to start early enough that thirty marked questions are possible before the series, which means autumn of Year 11 rather than spring. Full timed papers belong in the final six weeks and are largely wasted before then, because a student without the diagrams and the judgement sentence will simply repeat the same errors across five papers.

A note for resit candidates. If a November entry is a possibility, the conversation with the school's exams officer needs to happen before summer results arrive, because the deadline does not wait for a change of mind. November is also a shorter runway than students expect: results in August, decision in days, exam in late October or November. A compressed plan for that series looks different and should be built deliberately rather than by shortening the May one.

sections.heading: Online delivery, honesty, and the permit position
paragraphs: Families search for a tutor in Dubai, so the delivery answer belongs in plain words. IB Gram delivers 4EC1 tuition to Dubai families one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not make home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For Economics the format is a straightforward advantage, because the subject's central teaching tool is a diagram being drawn, broken and redrawn on a shared whiteboard, with every version saved for revision. A single sheet of paper on a kitchen table cannot do that.

The stronger argument is the pool. A Dubai family hiring in-home chooses from teachers willing to drive to their community at a specific hour. For a code like 4EC1, where the difference between a general economics graduate and a teacher of the specification is measured in labelling conventions and command-word habits, that geographic filter is expensive. Online, the filter is specification experience instead, which is the one that correlates with the grade.

On honesty, 4EC1 has no coursework component, which removes the sharpest version of the problem — there is no assessed essay for anyone to over-help with. What remains is materials. Pearson's specifications, past papers and mark schemes are published documents; we cite and link them and do not reproduce or redistribute them. A tutor offering a private archive of unreleased papers is a reason for caution rather than a selling point, and the same goes for anyone claiming access to grade boundaries before they are published.

On permits, private tutoring in the UAE operates under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which introduced the MoHRE private tuition work permit. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible categories include school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so any specific figure quoted at a parent is unverified. MoHRE's own private tutor licensing page is the official route. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai would additionally require a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute; IB Gram holds no such permit and operates no UAE premises.

sections.heading: Option blocks, equivalency and where 4EC1 leads
paragraphs: Two questions follow once the grade problem is in hand. Does Economics count for what comes next, and is it the right choice against Business. Both deserve concrete answers, and neither is handled well by the pages currently ranking for this search.

On equivalency, the UAE Ministry of Education's British-track requirements were clarified publicly in 2026: a student must pass five subjects recognised at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and show either one Advanced Level at grade E or better or two Advanced Subsidiary Levels at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five, and Economics can sit inside them. One page ranking in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced figure is five. Equivalency is a Ministry process that we describe and never perform or guarantee, and moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation channel is where to verify it.

On Economics against Business, the honest distinction is the unit of analysis. Economics reasons about markets and economies using diagrams; Business reasons about a named firm using a case study. Students who enjoy abstraction and are comfortable with graphs tend to prefer Economics; students who like concrete decisions and have a head for figures often do better in Business. Taking both is common in Dubai and works, provided the student keeps the registers separate — a Business answer that drifts into macroeconomics scores as poorly as an Economics answer that becomes a management memo.

Finally, the timetable context. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with any additional or different content requiring prior Ministry permission. For a family deciding how many tuition hours a week can carry, that is real arithmetic rather than a footnote, and it is one reason we argue for fewer, earlier, better-used hours.

process.title: Send the code, the board and the mock paper
process.description: Three things make matching quick: Pearson 4EC1 confirmed rather than assumed, the school's most recent mock paper or marked assessment, and the evening slot that survives a bad week. The mock matters most, because it shows whether the losses are diagrams, extract use or judgement.

process.title: A trial lesson at no charge
process.description: Thirty minutes, no card details taken, nothing owed afterwards. The tutor asks the student to draw two diagrams from blank axes and to read one extract aloud. That is usually enough to identify which of the three failure modes is costing the grade.

process.title: Diagram block first, almost always
process.description: Four to six sessions on the whiteboard before anything else, because every later question depends on it and because it is the fastest grade available. The student finishes with a one-page diagram sheet in their own hand, saved from the session whiteboard.

process.title: Weekly long answer, marked between lessons
process.description: From then on, one long question written midweek and marked before the session, with the hour spent on the judgement paragraph. The parent receives the marked answer and a short note naming the single thing the student is now doing differently.

process.title: Review at week six, then plan the series
process.description: We compare the baseline answer with a current one and decide whether to continue, change tutor or reduce hours. Six weeks before the series the plan moves to full timed papers and a final-fortnight routine the student can run without a tutor.

whyPoints.title: The diagram set is drilled, not described
whyPoints.description: Six diagrams account for a predictable share of every 4EC1 paper, and almost all the lost marks are labelling rather than understanding. Drawing them from blank axes against a clock, with deliberately broken versions to spot, is the fastest available improvement in the subject.

whyPoints.title: Judgement is taught as a sentence shape
whyPoints.description: Compare, condition, commit. Three clauses, practised until they arrive under pressure. Students leave the highest-value marks on the page because nobody told them the final sentences outweigh the paragraph above, which is a fixable problem rather than a ceiling on ability.

whyPoints.title: Local examples the examiner has not read before
whyPoints.description: The pegged dirham, UAE value added tax from 2018, free zones, and the KHDA 2026-27 fee freeze as a maximum-price intervention in a market the student is personally inside. Used to name a mechanism, kept short, and rehearsed so they emerge in the exam.
