whyPoints.description: Every AED band here is published by a named provider or taken from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table. Regulatory and market facts cite u.ae, KHDA, MoHRE or Pearson. There is no statistic on this page about our own students, because we would have to show the data.

whyPoints.title: Specification experience, not economics in general
whyPoints.description: A university economics graduate can explain elasticity well and still not know that the original curve must stay visible. Tutors on this page have taught Pearson 4EC1, which is the experience that shows up in labelling conventions and command-word habits.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and limits stated up front
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram makes no home visits in the UAE, a service that exists only in India. When no specialist in the code is free at the hour you need, we say so and name the alternatives rather than substituting quietly.

faqs.question: Which diagrams does my child have to draw in Edexcel IGCSE Economics 4EC1?
faqs.answer: The working set is small: demand and supply with a shift, price elasticity of demand, external costs and benefits, maximum and minimum price intervention, the circular flow of income, and exchange rate determination. Confirm the emphasis with your child's teacher, since departments vary slightly. Almost all lost diagram marks are labelling rather than understanding — an unlabelled axis, an original curve rubbed out, a new equilibrium left unmarked. We drill each one from blank axes against a ninety-second clock, which is the cheapest grade available in the whole course.

faqs.question: How are the two 4EC1 Economics papers split between micro and macro?
faqs.answer: The specification divides the content into the market system, business economics, government and the economy, and the global economy, assessed by written examination. The exact component structure, durations and weightings are published on the current specification at qualifications.pearson.com, which is the document to check rather than a tutor's recollection of an older version. What matters more for planning is that there is no coursework, so every mark is earned on the day. A weak mock in January is therefore fully recoverable, which is worth telling a Year 11 who has decided the grade is already settled.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks on diagram labelling in Economics?
faqs.answer: Because the mark is for the label, not the shape. Scripts consistently show the same faults: a vertical axis left blank, the original curve erased so no change is visible, price and quantity axes swapped under time pressure, a movement along a curve drawn where the question described a shift. None of these indicates weak economics, which is why students find the lost marks unjust. The fix is repetition with deliberate sabotage: the tutor redraws the diagram with one element wrong, the student finds it, then draws it again against a clock.

faqs.question: Can my child use UAE examples in a 4EC1 answer?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is an advantage if the example names a mechanism rather than showing local knowledge. Strong options include the dirham's peg to the US dollar as an exchange-rate policy constraint, value added tax introduced in the UAE in January 2018 as an indirect tax, the Jebel Ali and Silicon Oasis free zones as investment incentives, and KHDA's confirmation in May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for 2026-27 as a maximum-price intervention. Keep each to a sentence or two and name the economic consequence.

faqs.question: What does an evaluation mark in Economics actually require?
faqs.answer: Three clauses, not originality. A comparison: this effect is larger than that one. A condition: in the short run, or if demand is price-sensitive, or unless the government also acts. A commitment: therefore the answer falls this way. Students lose these marks because time ran out, or because nobody told them the final sentences outweigh the explanation above them. We teach it as a sentence shape and practise it until it arrives under pressure, and students who write it reliably out-score those who add two more paragraphs of explanation.

faqs.question: How much maths is in Edexcel IGCSE Economics 4EC1?
faqs.answer: Less than parents fear and more than students expect. The quantitative demand is percentage change, index numbers, simple calculation from a table, and reading graphs accurately — the kind of arithmetic a confident Foundation-tier mathematician can handle. Where it bites is in data response, when a figure has to be interpreted rather than copied. A student who struggles to say whether a number went up by a fifth or by a fifth of a percentage point will lose application marks, and that specific gap is worth a session or two of drilling early.

faqs.question: What does an Edexcel IGCSE Economics tutor cost per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates run roughly AED 45 to 150 for budget online provision, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject teacher online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit including travel, and AED 200 to 450 or above for a subject specialist. Those bands come from providers' own published pricing and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table. Two questions matter more than the rate: whether long answers are marked in writing between lessons, and whether the tutor has taught this specification rather than economics in general.

faqs.question: Which Economics topics do Dubai students meet last and understand least?
faqs.answer: Consistently, exchange rates and the balance of payments. They sit late in most schemes of work, they arrive when Year 11 is already busy with mocks, and they require a diagram students have had least practice with. The second candidate is elasticity, which is taught early, assumed understood, and then needed constantly. Both are worth pulling forward deliberately: a session on exchange rates in the autumn costs an hour, while meeting it for the first time in March costs a section of the paper.

faqs.question: Does 4EC1 Economics have any coursework or internal assessment?
faqs.answer: No. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Economics is assessed entirely by written examination, which has two consequences. The first is that timed practice is the whole of the preparation, because there is no banked mark to protect a weak paper. The second is more cheerful: nothing is already lost. A student with a poor mock in January has every mark still available, which is a genuinely useful thing to say to a sixteen-year-old who has written the year off.

faqs.question: How do I know whether my child's school uses Edexcel or Cambridge for Economics?
faqs.answer: Ask the department directly, and ask subject by subject rather than school by school. Several Dubai schools enter Pearson for some subjects and Cambridge for others, so a parent who knows the school is 'a Cambridge school' can still have a child sitting Pearson 4EC1. The specification code on a mock paper is the quickest confirmation. It matters because command-word conventions, diagram expectations and paper structure differ, and a term of practice on the wrong board's past papers is a term misspent.

faqs.question: Is Economics a sensible IGCSE option for a student heading to a business degree?
faqs.answer: It is a reasonable choice and not a requirement, and no page should tell you that tutoring or a particular subject is necessary for a university place. What Economics genuinely provides is early practice at reasoning with diagrams and weighing trade-offs, which the first year of most economics and finance degrees assumes. Business provides concrete decision-making about firms instead. Students who take both and keep the registers separate do well; students who blur them lose marks in both papers for answering in the wrong idiom.

faqs.question: How many 4EC1 past papers should my child complete before the exam?
faqs.answer: Fewer than you would guess, done properly. Five or six full papers marked carefully in the final six weeks beats fifteen skimmed, because the value is in the correction rather than the attempt. Before that window, individual long questions are the better unit: roughly thirty marked long answers across Year 11 is a realistic and effective target. Papers attempted before the diagrams and the judgement sentence are secure simply repeat the same errors, which is discouraging and teaches nothing.

faqs.question: Are Economics lessons for Dubai students taught online?
faqs.answer: Yes. Sessions are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE — that service exists only in India. For this subject the format helps rather than compromises: diagrams are drawn, deliberately broken and redrawn on a shared whiteboard, every version is saved for revision, and marked long answers reach the parent as files. The choice of tutor is also made on 4EC1 experience rather than on who will drive to your community at six.

faqs.question: Does my child need to learn exact definitions for Economics, or is close enough fine?
faqs.answer: Precision pays here more than anywhere else in the course. 'Inflation is when prices go up' loses the mark because it omits the general price level and the sustained period, both of which the student knows. We build a list of around thirty terms from the student's own marked errors rather than from a glossary, and test them orally with an eight-second limit, because retrieval under mild pressure is what the exam requires. It is also homework a parent can supervise without knowing any economics.

faqs.question: Can a tutor explain the UAE dirham peg in a way that helps in the exam?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the best examples available to a Dubai candidate. The point to make is not that the dirham is pegged to the dollar but what a peg does: it removes exchange rate adjustment as a policy tool, so when the dollar strengthens, UAE exports and tourism face a competitiveness effect the central bank cannot offset by letting the currency fall. Stated in two sentences and attached to a labelled exchange rate diagram, that is an answer most candidates worldwide cannot write.

faqs.question: How many weekly Economics sessions does a Year 11 in Dubai usually book?
faqs.answer: One hour a week, with a long answer written and marked between sessions, is the common and usually sufficient pattern. Two a week makes sense for a short pre-series block or for a student starting late with a specific deficit, such as never having drawn the externality diagram. More than two is rarely productive, because the limiting factor is the student's capacity to absorb marked feedback rather than the amount of teaching. Starting in October beats doubling up in April on the same budget.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-economics-4ec1-tutor.closingHeading: Start with two diagrams and one marked long answer
dubai/edexcel-igcse-economics-4ec1-tutor.closingBody: If you are weighing up an Edexcel IGCSE Economics 4EC1 tutor in Dubai, the quickest useful diagnostic costs half an hour. Ask your child to draw a demand and supply shift from blank axes, then to write one long answer under timed conditions. Between them, those two tasks show whether the lost marks are labelling, extract handling or the missing judgement sentence — and the three need different terms of work. Send us the specification code, the most recent mock and the evening slot that survives a bad week, and take a trial lesson at no charge with no card details required. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-english-language-a-4.tutorsIntro: Tutors below teach Pearson Edexcel International GCSE English and mark at this level. Ask one question first: what will I be holding in my hand after four weeks? A tutor who answers with documents, a marked script, an error log, a baseline mark and a comparison, is describing a method. A tutor who answers with adjectives is not.

intro.heading: How a Dubai parent can tell whether English tutoring is actually working
paragraphs: English is the subject where parents are least equipped to judge progress, and providers know it. In maths, a parent can look at a page of practice and see whether the answers are right. In English Language A, the work looks the same whether it is improving or not: a page of prose, a tick, a comment reading good effort, more detail needed. Three months can pass pleasantly before a mock result makes it clear that nothing moved.

The remedy is not trust, it is documentation. A 4EA1 plan should generate a small number of specific artefacts on a predictable schedule, and each one should answer a question a parent can check. A baseline mark on a timed task answers where we started. An annotated script answers what specifically is costing marks. An error log answers whether the same fault keeps recurring. A comparison on an unseen paper answers whether anything has changed. None of that requires you to be an English teacher.

This page is built around those artefacts rather than around the syllabus, because the syllabus is published by Pearson and the artefacts are not published by anybody. English Language A is assessed through non-fiction reading and transactional writing in the larger first component and through poetry, prose and imaginative writing in the second, where some schools enter a coursework route instead. Confirm your child's option with the English department; everything after that is about evidence.

The format question deserves answering directly, because the search that brought you here is for a home tutor. In-home tuition exists in Dubai, serves families well in some circumstances, and has one clear advantage for a nervous younger writer: somebody is physically beside them while they write. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India, and UAE delivery is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

For the evidence argument specifically, the online format is an advantage rather than a concession, and the reason is unglamorous. Annotation on a shared document is saved. Four weeks later the student can place the first marked piece beside the fourth and see that the same comma splice has appeared in all four, which is the moment a persistent error becomes visible and therefore fixable. A paper script annotated in a living room and put into a bag does not produce that comparison, and the comparison is the mechanism.

What follows is a reading guide as much as a service page. It explains the week-by-week artefact schedule, how to read a marked reading response and a marked writing response without specialist training, what a genuine draft-to-draft improvement looks like against a cosmetic one, which mark changes are signal and which are noise, and where the annotation boundary sits between helping a student write and writing for them. The last of those is not a technicality; it is the line that protects your child.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-english-language-a-4.programmesIntro: The evidence a parent should expect changes with the stage, because what can be demonstrated in Year 8 is not what can be demonstrated in the February of Year 11. Each stage below names the artefact that matters most at that point.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9: before the qualification
programmes.description: The evidence here is a writing sample every few weeks and an error log that gets shorter. There is no exam mark to track, which makes the log the only honest measure. A student whose log still carries the same three punctuation faults after a term is not improving, however pleasant the sessions are, and that is a finding worth acting on early.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's transfer-heavy cohort means a student may arrive in Year 8 with strong reading and untaught writing conventions, or the reverse. A report that averages the two conceals it. A single timed writing sample, read properly, separates them in one session.

programmes.name: Year 10: building the record
programmes.description: The year where a real evidence trail can be built because there is time for it. A baseline timed piece in September, pieces marked across the year, an error log that visibly shrinks, and a second full timed paper in the summer term to compare against the baseline. That trail is what makes Year 11 decisions evidence-based rather than anxious.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools commonly set the first full component-style assessment in the spring of Year 10. Request the criteria grid along with the mark, because the grid is where the examiner's reasoning sits and the mark on its own tells you nothing diagnostic.

programmes.name: Year 11: evidence under time pressure
programmes.description: The only evidence that counts now is a mark on an unseen timed paper. Session impressions are unreliable this close to a series, and so is improvement on work the student has already seen. The cycle becomes: timed paper, marked, losses ranked, one category attacked, next timed paper. Everything else is decoration.
programmes.countryNote: The Dubai spring term compresses mocks, entry deadlines and often Ramadan into a short run. Build the timed-paper schedule around the school's own mock dates so marked feedback arrives before them rather than after, which is a calendar decision made in October, not February.

programmes.name: Where the school enters the coursework route
programmes.description: The evidence question becomes sharper, because the pieces are the student's own and must remain so. What a parent should see is a record of the student's successive attempts with the tutor's questions and comments on them, which is a different document from a polished final piece appearing after one session. The first demonstrates teaching; the second demonstrates nothing good.
programmes.countryNote: Because the coursework option is a school-level entry decision, confirm it before planning. Then ask the department for its internal deadline schedule, because the evidence cycle has to fit inside those dates rather than around an exam series.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-english-language-a-4.subjectsIntro: Each component below is paired with the evidence that shows whether it is improving, because that pairing is the practical content of this page. Reading and writing improve at different rates, and tracking them together is how a stalling plan stays invisible for a term.

subjects.name: Non-fiction reading: retrieval questions
subjects.description: The most measurable marks in the qualification. Evidence of improvement is a clean score on retrieval items across two consecutive unseen sections. If these are still being lost, the problem is question reading rather than comprehension, and that is visible on the script in seconds.

subjects.name: Non-fiction reading: inference and method
subjects.description: Where a 5 becomes a 7. Evidence of movement is quotation length shrinking and comment on effect appearing. A script where quotations run to two lines and the comment restates them is a paraphrasing habit, and the fix is observable within a block of six sessions.

subjects.name: Transactional writing: form and audience
subjects.description: Letters, articles, reports, speeches and reviews. Evidence here is binary and fast: either the conventions of the named form appear or they do not. A student who produced an article without a headline in week one and with one in week three has demonstrably learned something.

subjects.name: Transactional writing: register and control
subjects.description: The slow component. Evidence of real movement is sentence variety in the first paragraph and a register that holds to the end rather than drifting. This is measured across terms by comparing paragraph openings in pieces written months apart, not within a block.

subjects.name: Poetry and prose close reading
subjects.description: Evidence is whether the response answers the question asked rather than delivering prepared content about the text. A marked script showing accurate material that does not address the question is a specific, correctable finding, and it is the most common high-ability loss in this component.

subjects.name: Imaginative writing
subjects.description: Marked on structure and control, not invention. Evidence of progress is a plan existing before the prose, a word budget respected per section, and an opening that arrives at something inside a hundred words. All three are checkable on the page by a parent.

subjects.name: Accuracy: punctuation, agreement and tense
subjects.description: The component with the cleanest evidence of all. An error log listing the student's own recurring faults either shortens over a term or it does not. Nothing else in English tutoring is this easy to verify, which is why a plan without a log is hard to assess.

subjects.name: Timing and pacing
subjects.description: Evidence is a completed paper. A student who left the final task unfinished in October and finished it with five minutes spare in February has gained marks that no amount of style teaching would have delivered. Track completion before tracking quality.

subjects.name: English Literature alongside 4EA1
subjects.description: Often taken together, with close reading and essay structure transferring between them. The evidence worth watching is whether a technique taught in one subject shows up unprompted in a marked script from the other, which is the sign it has actually been learned.

subjects.name: English Language B (4EB1) as the alternative entry
subjects.description: A different qualification for students working in English as an additional language. The evidence that the question needs raising is a persistent gap between a solid reading mark and a weak writing mark, with criteria comments returning to range and idiom.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-english-language-a-4.regionsIntro: These notes are about when a Dubai student can realistically sit a timed piece with a fresh brain, because the timed piece is the evidence everything else is judged against. Logistics decide whether that happens weekly or never.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Short commutes make a weekday timed paper genuinely feasible, which elsewhere in the city is a weekend-only proposition. Families here can run a full evidence cycle inside the school week, and that cadence is the single biggest advantage available to an English plan.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Arabian Ranches 2
regions.note: Long bus runs mean writing after 16:30 produces evidence of tiredness rather than of ability. The workable pattern here is timed writing on a weekend morning and the session itself midweek, spent reading the annotation that came back.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Strong demand for English support in the exam year, with the better-known tutors committed early. The practical consequence for an evidence trail is that a weekly slot secured in September produces a year of comparable data; one secured in February produces a fortnight of it.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and Jumeirah Beach Residence
regions.note: Quiet writing space is the scarce resource in high-rise households. Timed pieces often work better early on a weekend morning than on a weekday evening, and saved screen annotation matters more here because re-reading happens in short stretches.

regions.name: Mirdif and Uptown Mirdif
regions.note: Large Year 11 cohorts with mock windows clustered in a tight fortnight. The evidence calendar here has to be built backwards from the school's own mock dates so that marked work lands before them and can actually be used.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Circle and Al Furjan
regions.note: Students travelling out to Barsha and Dubai Hills schools and arriving home late. Annotation the student reads alone, at their own pace, replaces the live explanation they are too tired to absorb, and that shifts where the value of a session sits.

regions.name: Business Bay and Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Mixed catchments across the city and busy households. Scheduling consistency rather than tutor proximity is what protects an evidence trail here, and a held recurring slot is worth more than any particular postcode.

regions.name: Town Square, Mudon and outer Dubailand
regions.note: Longer runs in both directions and newer schools with growing cohorts. A fixed Saturday morning for the timed piece, held from the start of Year 10, is what makes a comparable record exist at all by the following spring.

schoolClusters.city: Jumeirah, Dubai Hills and Al Barsha
schoolClusters.note: Secondaries across this belt return marked English work with criteria grids, and the grid is the document worth asking for. Students we support here most often arrive with a mark, no grid, and no idea which criterion the mark was lost against.

schoolClusters.city: Mirdif, Arabian Ranches and eastern Dubai
schoolClusters.note: English departments here teach mixed first-language and additional-language cohorts in the same classes, which is why a persistent reading-writing gap needs to be read as evidence about the entry rather than as a motivation problem.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School, Arabian Ranches

dubai/edexcel-igcse-english-language-a-4.modesIntro: Three session shapes, described by the evidence each one produces. If a shape does not produce a document you can read, it cannot be assessed, and anything that cannot be assessed will drift.

modes.title: The marked-piece cycle
modes.description: One timed piece between sessions, annotated against the published criteria and returned before the next session, with one instruction carried forward. The session itself is spent on the annotation rather than on new material. The evidence is a growing folder of comparable pieces, which is the only way a slow writing gain becomes visible before a mock exposes it.
bullets: One timed piece per cycle, always under exam conditions
Annotation against the criteria, with a stated turnaround in working days
One instruction forward, not a list the student will ignore
A folder you can read end to end at any point

modes.title: Reading-technique block with before and after
modes.description: Six sessions on the non-fiction reading section and the Component 2 close reading, bracketed by a timed section at each end. The second section is unseen and marked the same way as the first. The evidence is two marks on comparable unseen work, which is a stronger claim than any amount of session-by-session improvement.
bullets: A timed, marked section before the first session
Six sessions on question reading, quotation and comment on method
A second unseen timed section at the end, marked identically
A written comparison of the two, including what did not move

modes.title: Error-log clinic
modes.description: Short, repetitive and the easiest thing in English tutoring to verify. The log is built from the student's own marked pieces, drilled for three weeks and then tested under time pressure. The evidence is the log itself: a list that shortens, with dates. If it does not shorten, the plan is wrong and you will know inside a month.
bullets: Log built from the student's own scripts, never from a textbook list
Each entry dated when added and dated when it stops recurring
Tested under time pressure, because accuracy collapses there first
Visible to the parent without interpretation

sections.heading: What you should be holding after four weeks
paragraphs: A month is long enough to know whether a plan has a method, and short enough that changing course costs little. By the end of four weeks a 4EA1 plan should have produced a small set of documents, each answering a question you can check without specialist knowledge. If what you have instead is a verbal report that your child is engaging well, the plan has no method and four more weeks will not produce one.

The table below is the schedule. It is deliberately modest: five artefacts across four weeks, none of them onerous to produce for a tutor who is already marking. The point is not volume. The point is that each document is comparable with a later version of itself, which is what turns a sequence of sessions into a measurable plan.

Ask for this schedule before booking rather than after. A provider who agrees to it is committing to work that takes real time, and the commitment itself is informative. A provider who explains that English does not work that way is describing their own process rather than the subject, because the published criteria are specific and markable and every school English department in Dubai marks against them weekly.

One caution about week one. The baseline piece should be sat cold, under time, before any teaching happens. Parents sometimes want the tutor to prepare the student first, which is understandable and destroys the measurement. A baseline that has been coached is not a baseline, and without it there is nothing for week twelve to be compared against.

sections.heading: The home-tutor question, answered on what you can verify
paragraphs: Searches for a home tutor are usually searches for reliability: someone who turns up, knows the subject, and makes something happen. Those are reasonable requirements and they are not the same as a delivery format. It is worth separating them, because in English the thing that determines whether a plan works is whether the writing gets read properly, and that has nothing to do with where the reading happens.

A visiting tutor has genuine advantages. A younger or anxious writer benefits from someone physically beside them while they draft. A parent can hear the session without arranging anything. There is no screen to manage and no connection to fail. For a Year 7 or 8 student those advantages can be decisive, and families who choose in-home tuition for them are choosing sensibly.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all; home visits are a service we provide only in India, and UAE delivery is one-to-one over live video. The table below therefore compares the two formats on the one axis this page is about, which is what a parent can actually verify, rather than on comfort or cost. On that axis the online format has specific, mechanical advantages that are worth stating plainly.

The core of it is that screen annotation persists. A marked piece lives in a shared folder, so week four can be placed beside week one. An error log is a living document rather than a note in a book. A recorded explanation can be re-watched by a student who was too tired to absorb it at 17:30 after a long run home from Barsha. None of that is impossible on paper; all of it is harder, and in practice harder means it stops happening by November.

sections.heading: Reading a marked non-fiction response without being an English teacher
paragraphs: A marked reading response looks opaque and is not. The reading section of Component 1 asks a small number of question types in a predictable order, and the marks are lost in a small number of recognisable ways. A parent who learns to spot three of them can assess the quality of the tutoring themselves, which is worth more than any assurance.

Look first at quotation length. In a strong response, quotations are short, sometimes a single word, embedded in the student's own sentence. In a weak one they run to a line or two and the comment that follows restates them in different words. That is paraphrasing, it scores low across the whole section, and it is the single most common reason a competent reader sits at a 5. It is also correctable within about six sessions, so if it is still visible in week ten, something is wrong with the plan rather than the child.

Look second at whether the answer addresses the question asked. Underline the verb in the question and check that the response does that operation. A question asking how the writer creates an impression wants method and effect; an accurate summary of content, however well written, is answering a different question. Students with good general ability lose more marks here than weaker students do, because they have more content to offer.

Look third at mark allocation against length. A question worth two marks does not want a paragraph, and a question worth six does not want two lines. A script where every answer is the same length regardless of value is a pacing problem that will cost marks at the end of the paper, and it is visible to anybody who glances down the page. These three checks take five minutes and require no training beyond this paragraph.
bullets: Short embedded quotations with comment on effect: good. Long quotations restated: not
Underline the question's verb and check the response performs it
Compare answer length with the mark in brackets, question by question
If paraphrasing is still visible in week ten, change the plan, not the child

sections.heading: Reading a marked writing piece, and the criteria grid beside it
paragraphs: The criteria grid is the most useful document your child's school produces about English and the one parents least often ask for. It sets out what the examiner is awarding marks against, in bands, and a marked piece with its grid tells you which specific quality was found wanting. A mark without the grid tells you only that the piece was better or worse than some unstated standard.

When you have both, read in this order. Which criterion sits lowest? That is the target, and it should be the thing the tutor's instruction for the next piece addresses. If the grid says the lowest band was for organisation and the tutor's comment is about vocabulary, those two documents disagree, and the disagreement is worth raising. Alignment between the grid and the instruction is the clearest sign that a tutor is marking rather than reacting.

Then look at the opening paragraph by itself. Transactional writing is assessed partly on how quickly form, audience and purpose are established, and an opening that spends four sentences warming up has cost marks before anything else happens. Compare the opening of the current piece with the opening from three weeks earlier. If they are structurally identical, the instruction is not landing, whatever the overall mark did.

Then count sentence types in one paragraph. A paragraph of five simple sentences and a paragraph with varied structure read very differently to an examiner and look similar to a parent. This is the slowest thing to change in English and the most honest measure of whether real development is happening rather than exam polishing. Checking it monthly rather than weekly is realistic, and three months is the shortest interval at which a genuine change should be expected to show.
bullets: Always ask the school for the criteria grid alongside the mark
Check that the tutor's next instruction targets the lowest criterion
Compare opening paragraphs across three weeks, not whole pieces
Count sentence types once a month; expect change over terms, not weeks

sections.heading: Draft one to draft three: what real improvement looks like
paragraphs: Redrafting is where most of the learning in English happens and also where the most dishonest tutoring hides. A piece that improves dramatically between drafts may show a student who has understood an instruction, or a student who has had sentences supplied. Those two look identical in the final version and completely different in the sequence, which is why the sequence should be visible to you.

A genuine improvement is specific and partial. The student was told to vary sentence openings, and in draft two the openings vary while the vocabulary stays flat. That is a student applying one instruction, which is exactly what should happen. A draft two that is better in every dimension at once, with phrasing the student has never used before, is not a student learning. It is a different hand on the page, and the student carries the consequence of that, not the tutor.

The table below sets out what to look for across a three-draft sequence. The column worth attending to is the last one, which names the pattern that indicates the work is no longer the student's. You do not need to be suspicious to use it; you need to know what a healthy sequence looks like so that you recognise an unhealthy one if it appears.

There is a practical point alongside the integrity one. A piece redrafted more than three times stops teaching anything, because the student is polishing a text rather than practising the skill of producing one to time. Two or three drafts, then a fresh timed piece applying the same instruction to unfamiliar material, is a better cycle than five drafts of a single essay, and it produces evidence that transfers to an exam hall.

sections.heading: Which mark changes mean something, and which are noise
paragraphs: English marks move around for reasons that have nothing to do with learning. A different task type, a more familiar topic, a better night's sleep, a kinder marker: any of these can shift a mark by a band in either direction. Parents reading single marks as signals will be reassured and alarmed at random, and both reactions make it harder to run a plan properly.

The reliable signals are narrow. A change in a specific criterion that was targeted, sustained across two consecutive pieces, is signal. A recurring error disappearing from the log and staying gone under time pressure is signal. A paper that now gets finished, where previously it did not, is signal and it is usually worth several marks. An overall mark rising by one on a single piece is noise, and treating it as evidence invites the opposite reading next month.

The table sets out common observations and what each probably means. Note how often the honest answer is wait for the next piece. That is not evasion. One data point in English is genuinely uninformative, and a plan that reacts to every piece will change direction constantly and arrive nowhere, which is itself a common failure mode in heavily supervised tutoring.

A specific case deserves naming because it alarms parents most: a mark that falls after a month of work. This is common and often positive. A student who has been told to attempt more ambitious sentence structures will write worse before they write better, because they are operating outside their automatic range. The same happens when a student stops over-preparing content and starts answering the question. If a fall coincides with the plan deliberately disturbing a habit, it is expected. If it coincides with nothing, ask.

sections.heading: The error log: the most useful page in the folder
paragraphs: Of everything in a 4EA1 plan, the error log is the document that most reliably tells a parent whether the tutoring is working, and it is the cheapest to produce. It is a dated list of the specific faults appearing in the student's own writing: comma splices, subject-verb disagreement, tense drift, apostrophe errors, run-on sentences, the particular wrong word this student always reaches for. Not common errors in general. These errors, with dates.

It works because it is falsifiable. A plan either shortens the list or it does not, and nobody can argue about it. Three entries added in September that are still being added in December is an unambiguous finding. The same three entries last appearing in October, with nothing new added since, is also unambiguous, and it means the accuracy work has held.

The log also solves the problem of feedback volume. A marked piece can generate fifteen observations, and a student will act on none of them. The log lets the tutor choose, honestly and visibly, which one error to attack this cycle, while the rest stay recorded rather than forgotten. One instruction per cycle is not a shortcut; it is the only rate at which instructions are actually followed.

Ask to see the log monthly, and read it yourself. You do not need to understand the grammatical terminology to see whether the list is shortening and whether the dates are recent. If the log is produced on request rather than maintained, the dates will tell you, because a maintained log has entries scattered across weeks and a manufactured one has them all added on the same day.
bullets: Entries are the student's own recurring faults, with the date each was added
An entry is closed only when it stops appearing under timed conditions
One error per cycle is attacked; the rest stay recorded
Read the dates: a maintained log looks different from a manufactured one

sections.heading: Whose writing is it? The annotation boundary, stated plainly
paragraphs: Everything on this page depends on the writing being the student's own, and in English that boundary is easier to cross than in any other subject. A single rephrased sentence from a tutor can lift a paragraph, and nobody would notice. Which is precisely why the rule has to be explicit rather than assumed, and why a parent should say it out loud in the first conversation.

The working rule is about sequence. The student attempts first, always. The tutor reads the attempt, marks it against the criteria, names what was lost and why, and sets one instruction for the next attempt. Questions are legitimate teaching: what is this paragraph for, who are you addressing, where does this sentence end. Supplying the sentence is not, and a model answer handed over before the student has attempted anything, for a piece that will be submitted, is not teaching at all.

This matters most where a school has entered the coursework route in place of the second written paper, because then forty per cent of the qualification sits on work produced under school conditions and submitted under the student's name. The exposure of crossing the line falls on the student. Research into this market found a provider selling finished assessed work for international qualifications at a fixed price; no grade is worth the finding that follows from buying that.

Two related boundaries, for completeness. Pearson specifications, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Pearson: they are referenced and linked, not reproduced or distributed as downloads. And nobody here is described as a Pearson examiner unless current examiner status can be evidenced. IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from Pearson, Edexcel, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE or the Ministry of Education, and nothing on this site should be read as implying otherwise.
bullets: The student attempts first, every time, before any feedback exists
Questions about purpose and audience are teaching; supplied sentences are not
The boundary matters most on the coursework route, where work is submitted
Pearson materials are linked and cited, never reproduced or distributed

sections.heading: Evidence the school already holds, and how to ask for it
paragraphs: Before buying anything, there is a free evidence pack sitting in your child's school. Most of it is handed over on request and most parents never request it, which means plans get built on a reported grade when a far better picture was available for the cost of an email. Three items are worth asking for by name.

The first is the component-level breakdown rather than the overall English grade. Knowing whether the weakness is in the first component or the second changes where every hour goes, because the first carries the larger share of the qualification and contains the fastest-moving marks in the subject. The second is the criteria grid from the most recent marked assessment, which is where the examiner's reasoning sits. The third is which option the school entered for the second component, including whether the coursework route applies.

Two more questions are worth adding. What support does the department already run this term: clinics, revision sessions, past-paper practice? Those sit inside the fees you already pay, and any plan that ignores them is charging you for something you have. And what does the department think the ceiling is and why? Teachers are usually candid when asked directly and privately, and their answer is better information than any external assessment, because they have read a term of the student's writing.

Bring all of it to the first tutoring conversation. A tutor who reads the grid and the component split before proposing anything is working from evidence. A tutor who proposes a package before seeing them is pricing an average student. The distinction shows up in the first ten minutes and it predicts most of what follows.
bullets: Ask for the component-level marks, not the overall English grade
Ask for the criteria grid from the most recent marked assessment
Confirm which option the school entered for the second component
Ask what free departmental support runs this term, and use it first

process.title: A cold baseline before any teaching
process.description: The student sits one timed piece and one reading section with no preparation, and both are marked against the published criteria. It feels counterintuitive and it is the only way to have something comparable later. A coached baseline is not a baseline and leaves the plan unmeasurable.

process.title: A written note ranking the losses
process.description: After the trial you receive a short written document naming the loss categories in order of size, with an honest note on which move in weeks and which move across terms. You keep this document whether or not you continue, and it is the thing every later review is read against.

process.title: One instruction per cycle, visibly carried
process.description: Each session works from the annotated piece returned since the last one and sets a single instruction for the next. Fifteen observations produce no change; one produces change. The instruction is written down so you can see whether it was addressed in the following piece.

process.title: A dated error log, open to you
process.description: Recurring faults from the student's own writing are logged with the date added, attacked one at a time, and closed only when they stop appearing under timed conditions. The log is readable without specialist knowledge, and it is the fastest honest check on whether the plan is working.

process.title: A review on unseen work, then a decision
process.description: After eight to ten sessions the student sits a full timed paper, marked the same way as the baseline, and the two are compared in writing including what did not move. You then decide whether to continue, change component, or stop. Sessions run one-to-one over live video.

whyPoints.title: The plan produces documents, not impressions
whyPoints.description: A baseline, annotated scripts, a dated error log and an unseen comparison. Each one answers a question a parent can check without being an English teacher, which is what makes a stalling plan visible in week four rather than in results week.

whyPoints.title: Marking is the work, and it is scheduled
whyPoints.description: Reading a timed response closely against the criteria takes a marker thirty to fifty minutes, and the turnaround is stated in working days before anything is booked. The session is built on what the marking found, not on fresh general material.

whyPoints.title: Reading and writing tracked separately
whyPoints.description: Reading marks move within weeks and writing craft moves across terms. Tracking them together is how a plan hides a failure for a whole term. Both are measured, reported and reviewed independently.

whyPoints.title: One instruction at a time
whyPoints.description: A marked piece can generate fifteen observations and a student will act on none of them. One instruction per cycle, written down and checked in the next piece, is the only rate at which feedback changes anything.

whyPoints.title: The annotation boundary is explicit
whyPoints.description: The student attempts first, always. Tutors mark, question and instruct; they do not supply sentences for work submitted under a student's name. The rule is stated at the start rather than discovered during a coursework deadline.

whyPoints.title: The school's own evidence comes first
whyPoints.description: Component marks, criteria grids, the option entry and the department's own clinics are free and already available. The first conversation asks for them, because a plan built without them is a plan built on a single reported grade.

faqs.question: Can we book an Edexcel IGCSE English Language A 4EA1 home tutor in Dubai?
faqs.answer: In-home tuition exists in the Dubai market, so families can find one, and for a younger or anxious writer having someone physically beside them has real value. IB Gram is not that provider: home visits are a service offered only in India, and UAE delivery is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For the evidence trail this page is about, the online format helps rather than hinders, because annotated work, drafts and the error log live in a shared folder where week one can be placed beside week four and compared.

faqs.question: How will I know whether 4EA1 tutoring is actually working?
faqs.answer: By holding four documents rather than by asking. A cold baseline mark on a timed piece, so there is something to compare against. Annotated scripts returned within a stated turnaround, showing which criterion lost the mark. A dated error log that either shortens or does not. And a mark on a fresh unseen timed paper after eight to ten sessions, compared with the baseline in writing. None of those requires you to be an English teacher. If after a month you have none of them, the plan has no method.

faqs.question: What should I receive after each English session?
faqs.answer: Two things at minimum: the annotated piece from the previous cycle, marked against the published criteria, and one written instruction for the next piece. Not a list of twelve improvements, which a student will ignore entirely, but one. You should also be able to see the error log and the next timed task that has been set. If what arrives is a verbal summary of how the session went, there is nothing to compare next month against and nothing to hold anyone to.

faqs.question: How do I read a marked transactional writing response myself?
faqs.answer: Ask the school for the criteria grid alongside the mark, then read in three steps. Which criterion sits lowest? That is the target, and the tutor's next instruction should address it; if the grid says organisation and the comment says vocabulary, those documents disagree. Then read only the opening paragraph and compare it with one from three weeks earlier, because openings carry form, audience and purpose marks. Then count sentence types in one paragraph. Three checks, five minutes, no training beyond this answer.

faqs.question: What does the criteria grid on my child's English paper actually mean?
faqs.answer: It is the band description the examiner awards against, broken into the qualities being assessed, and it is the most useful English document a school produces. A mark on its own tells you the piece was better or worse than some unstated standard. The grid tells you which specific quality was found wanting, which is what makes a mark diagnostic rather than decorative. Request it every time marked work comes home. Most departments hand it over without hesitation, and a tutor who reads it before proposing a plan is working from evidence.

faqs.question: How long before a 4EA1 mark moves?
faqs.answer: It depends which marks. Reading-section technique, form conventions and rule-based accuracy errors commonly move inside a block of six sessions, and the movement shows on an unseen timed section. Sentence control, analytical precision and vocabulary range move across terms rather than weeks, because they are habits rather than rules. A provider quoting a timescale before reading a marked piece is guessing. A provider who separates the fast marks from the slow ones in week one is telling you something useful and verifiable.

faqs.question: My child's mark went down after a month of tutoring. What does that mean?
faqs.answer: Often something good, which surprises parents. A student told to attempt more ambitious sentence structures writes worse before writing better, because they are operating outside their automatic range. The same happens when a student stops delivering prepared content and starts answering the question in front of them. If the fall coincides with the plan deliberately disturbing a habit, it is expected and should recover across two more pieces. If it coincides with no change in the plan at all, ask what the annotation says and whether the piece was genuinely sat to time.

faqs.question: What is an error log and why does it matter more than a grade?
faqs.answer: It is a dated list of the specific faults appearing in your child's own writing: their comma splices, their tense drift, the particular wrong word they always reach for. Not common errors in general. It matters because it is falsifiable: the list either shortens or it does not, and nobody can argue about dates. Three entries added in September still being added in December is an unambiguous finding. It also solves feedback volume, letting one error be attacked per cycle while the rest stay recorded rather than forgotten.

faqs.question: How many drafts should one piece of writing go through?
faqs.answer: Two or three, then move to a fresh timed piece on unfamiliar material. Beyond three drafts a student is polishing a text rather than practising the skill of producing one to time, and exam marks come from the second. The useful pattern is: timed draft sat cold, one instruction, draft two addressing that instruction only, then a new timed piece applying the same instruction without prompting. A gain that appears on redrafts and vanishes on unseen work has not been learned.

faqs.question: Can a tutor annotate my child's work without doing it for them?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the distinction is about sequence rather than intensity. The student attempts first, always. The tutor then reads the attempt, marks it against the criteria, names what was lost and why, and sets one instruction for the next attempt. Questions are legitimate teaching: what is this paragraph for, who are you addressing, where should this sentence end. Supplying the sentence is not teaching, and a polished model handed over before any attempt exists, for work that will be submitted, exposes the student rather than the tutor.

faqs.question: What evidence should I ask the school for before starting tutoring?
faqs.answer: Three documents and two questions, all free. The component-level marks rather than the overall English grade, because that split determines where every hour should go. The criteria grid from the most recent marked assessment. Confirmation of which option the school entered for the second component, including whether the coursework route applies. Then ask what departmental support runs this term, since clinics and revision sessions sit inside fees you already pay, and ask the teacher privately what they think the ceiling is and why.

faqs.question: Does annotation on a screen work as well as marking on paper?
faqs.answer: For the purpose of tracking progress it works better, which is a mechanical point rather than a preference. Screen annotation persists in a shared folder, so the week-one piece can be opened beside the week-four piece and the same recurring fault becomes visible across both. A dated error log is a living document rather than a note in a book. A student too tired to absorb an explanation at 17:30 can re-read it later. All of this is possible on paper and in practice it stops happening by November.

faqs.question: Should I sit in on my child's English sessions?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and for a specific reason rather than as supervision. Sitting in once near the start tells you whether the tutor is working from the student's marked writing or delivering general content, which is the most important thing to establish and takes one session to see. After that, the documents tell you more than observation does, and a parent in the room changes how a teenager writes and talks. Read the annotated pieces and the error log instead; they are the honest record and they do not perform for an audience.

faqs.question: How do we measure reading progress separately from writing progress?
faqs.answer: By marking them separately and reporting them separately, which sounds obvious and is routinely not done. Reading is measured on timed unseen sections, where technique gains appear within weeks: shorter quotations, comment on method, answers matched to the question's verb. Writing is measured on timed pieces compared months apart, looking at opening paragraphs and sentence variety rather than at the overall mark. Combining the two into one English grade is precisely how a plan that is improving reading and ignoring writing stays invisible for a term.

faqs.question: What does a stalled 4EA1 grade usually turn out to be?
faqs.answer: In the reading section, paraphrasing: long quotations restated in different words instead of short quotations with comment on effect. In transactional writing, the form conventions of the named task absent, or an opening that spends four sentences warming up. Across both, answers not matched to the question's verb and the same handful of accuracy errors recurring unaddressed. All four are visible on a marked script within minutes and all four are correctable. What a stalled grade rarely turns out to be is a lack of effort.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-english-language-a-4.closingHeading: Ask what you will be holding in four weeks
dubai/edexcel-igcse-english-language-a-4.closingBody: The useful question to put to any provider is not how experienced they are but what documents you will have after a month. A cold baseline mark. Send one marked piece and its criteria grid, take the free trial as a diagnostic, and read the baseline note that comes back: it will rank the losses and say which move in weeks and which move across terms. dubai/edexcel-igcse-english-language-a-4.tutorsIntro: Tutors below teach Pearson Edexcel International GCSE English and mark at this level. The question worth asking first is not how many years they have taught but how many pieces of transactional writing they have marked against the published criteria this term, and how quickly a marked piece comes back to you.

intro.heading: What you are actually paying for when you buy 4EA1 tuition in Dubai
paragraphs: English Language A carries the Pearson code 4EA1 and is assessed in two components. Paper 1 covers non-fiction texts and transactional writing and carries the larger share of the qualification at sixty per cent over two hours and fifteen minutes. Paper 2 covers poetry and prose texts and imaginative writing at forty per cent over an hour and a half, and Pearson offers a coursework route in place of that second paper. Which route your child sits is a decision the school made, not one you can choose late, so confirm it on the Pearson subject page before planning anything.

That structure is why English tuition is priced badly in this market. In maths and science, the lesson is the product: a tutor explains a method, the student practises, the mark moves. In English, the lesson is the smaller half. The product is a piece of writing produced to time, read closely by someone who knows the criteria, annotated line by line, and returned with one specific instruction for the next attempt. That reading and annotating takes thirty to fifty minutes for a single Paper 1 Section B response, and somebody is either paying for it or not getting it.

Published Dubai rates do not distinguish between the two. Unitors lists International GCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour. TutorChase quotes AED 270. BartyED quotes AED 650 at the named tier. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Those are their figures. None of them tells you whether a marked essay is included, and that single omission is the difference between a useful purchase and an expensive conversation.

The second reason English quotes are hard to compare is that the subject contains two different jobs. Reading questions on Paper 1 Section A test retrieval, inference and analysis of a writer's method, and they respond to technique: a student can be taught to quote short, comment on effect and answer the question asked. Writing tasks test something slower. Sentence variety, control of register, structural shape and accuracy improve over months, not weeks, and a plan that prices them as a six-week fix is mispricing them.

There is a third cost most families never see, and it is specific to Dubai. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are mandatory in every Dubai private school whatever the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA calculates their instructional time in forty-minute lesson units with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students. Those hours are already in your child's week. Any English plan has to fit the time that remains, and a plan that assumes an empty weekday evening is a plan that will be abandoned by October.

IB Gram delivers 4EA1 support as one-to-one online tuition over live video in Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are a service offered only in India and are not sold in the UAE. What follows prices the real job: the component structure you are preparing for, the market bands by provider model, what twenty hours typically buys at different starting grades, the coursework question and its honesty boundary, and the four questions that make two English quotes comparable.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-english-language-a-4.programmesIntro: 4EA1 spending behaves differently at four points in a student's school career, and the same hourly rate buys a different thing at each one. Identify the point before agreeing a plan, because the most expensive mistake available here is buying exam-technique hours for a student who needs eighteen months of writing practice.

programmes.name: Lower secondary English before 4EA1
programmes.description: The cheapest hours in the whole sequence, and the ones that actually determine the 4EA1 grade. Sentence control, paragraph shape, punctuation accuracy and reading stamina are built here or not at all. A student who arrives in Year 10 writing in two sentence types will meet that limitation again as a Paper 1 Section B mark, and by then it costs five times as much to address.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's international cohort means a significant share of students meet formal English writing instruction in different sequences across different systems before Year 9. A student who transferred at Year 7 or 8 may have strong reading and untaught writing conventions, which a report rarely separates.

programmes.name: Year 10 of English Language A
programmes.description: The year where tuition money produces the most grade movement per dirham, because writing improvement is slow and Year 10 is the only year with enough runway for it. Work here is volume plus feedback: regular timed pieces, marked properly, with one instruction carried into the next attempt. Nothing about this is dramatic and it is why Year 11 goes better.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools often set the first full 4EA1-style assessment in the spring of Year 10. That marked paper, with its criteria grid, is the single document that makes an English tuition conversation useful rather than speculative.

programmes.name: Year 11 and the exam series
programmes.description: Reading technique, timing and question-reading dominate, because they move inside weeks and writing craft does not. A sensible Year 11 plan takes the available writing level as given, protects it against accuracy slippage under time pressure, and spends most of its hours on the reading section and on the structure of responses, which is where recoverable marks sit.
programmes.countryNote: The Dubai spring term compresses mocks, internal deadlines and the entry window, often with Ramadan inside it. Reading-technique work survives a compressed term far better than a writing-development programme does, which is why the sequencing across the two years matters.

programmes.name: The coursework route in place of Paper 2
programmes.ageRange: Set by the school, usually Year 10-11
programmes.description: Where the school has entered the coursework option instead of the second written paper, the shape of the support changes and so does its honesty boundary. A tutor teaches the skills, questions the thinking and gives feedback on what the student has already produced. A tutor does not supply sentences, structure or content for a folder that will be submitted under the student's name.
programmes.countryNote: Because the option is a school-level entry decision in Dubai as everywhere else, the first thing to establish is which route your child is on. Families sometimes buy a term of Paper 2 preparation for a student whose school entered coursework, which is money spent on the wrong component entirely.

programmes.name: After 4EA1: A Level, IB and university entry
programmes.description: The 4EA1 grade is a gatekeeper rather than a destination. It appears in sixth-form entry requirements, in the five-subject count for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, and in university English-proficiency decisions. Knowing which of those three uses applies to your child changes the target grade and therefore the budget.
programmes.countryNote: The published MoE requirement for the British track is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count. Verify your child's own case on moe.gov.ae; equivalency is not something a tutoring service performs or influences.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-english-language-a-4.subjectsIntro: The list below separates the parts of 4EA1 that respond quickly to paid hours from the parts that do not. That separation is the whole of the cost argument on this page, because buying the slow work in a short window is the commonest way to spend money on English without moving a grade.

subjects.name: Paper 1 Section A: non-fiction reading
subjects.description: The fastest-moving marks in the qualification. Retrieval, inference and analysis of a writer's method are teachable techniques: quote short, comment on effect, answer the question actually asked. A student stuck at a 5 here is usually paraphrasing rather than analysing, which is correctable within a block of six.

subjects.name: Paper 1 Section B: transactional writing
subjects.description: Letters, articles, reports, speeches and reviews assessed on form, audience, register and accuracy. The fastest gains come from form conventions and planning discipline rather than from style. The slow part is sentence variety and control, which improves across terms rather than across sessions.

subjects.name: Paper 2: poetry and prose texts
subjects.description: Anthology-based close reading where marks turn on linking a specific textual choice to a specific effect. Over-prepared students arrive with memorised content and lose marks for not answering the question in front of them. Technique work rather than more reading is usually what is needed.

subjects.name: Paper 2: imaginative writing
subjects.description: Narrative and descriptive writing marked on structure and control, not on inventiveness. Students lose marks to runaway plots and to opening paragraphs that spend three hundred words arriving. A planning routine and a hard word budget per section are the two highest-return interventions.

subjects.name: The coursework alternative to Paper 2
subjects.levels: Where the school has entered it
subjects.description: Two assessed pieces in place of the second written paper, produced under school conditions. Tuition here is skills teaching and feedback on work the student has already produced, never provision of material for submission. Establish which route the school entered before buying any preparation.

subjects.name: Accuracy: punctuation, agreement and tense
subjects.description: The cheapest marks nobody buys. Comma splices, subject-verb agreement and tense drift are rule-based errors that persist because they are never systematically diagnosed. A list drawn from the student's own marked pieces, drilled for three weeks, holds under exam pressure.

subjects.name: Timing and pacing across the papers
subjects.description: Paper 1 runs over two hours with reading and writing to balance, and students routinely over-invest in Section A and arrive at the writing task with twenty minutes. A timing plan tested on full papers is worth more marks than another term of content and costs a fraction of it.

subjects.name: English Language B (4EB1) as an alternative route
subjects.description: A different qualification for students working in English as an additional language. A student placed in 4EA1 who should be on 4EB1 will absorb tuition hours indefinitely without the grade moving, so the entry question is worth settling before the budget is committed.

subjects.name: English Literature alongside 4EA1
subjects.description: Frequently taken together, and the overlap is real: close reading and essay structure transfer in both directions. One tutor across both is usually better value than two bookings, provided the literature texts are named before the plan is agreed.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first or additional language
subjects.description: Runs alongside the Pearson curriculum under KHDA requirements, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and specified languages of instruction. Its weekly hours are part of the time budget an English plan must fit inside, which is a scheduling cost rather than a fee.

sections.heading: Why an English hourly rate tells you less than a maths one
paragraphs: Hourly rates in Dubai are quoted the same way across every subject, which quietly misrepresents English. A maths hour is largely self-contained: the tutor diagnoses, teaches a method, sets practice, and the practice can be checked quickly. An English hour is the visible part of a cycle whose expensive part happens afterwards, when somebody reads a timed response closely enough to say which sentence lost the mark and why.

That reading is not quick. A single Paper 1 Section B response takes a competent marker thirty to fifty minutes to annotate properly against the criteria: identifying where form conventions slipped, where register drifted, which sentence patterns repeat, which errors are systematic rather than careless, and then choosing the one instruction most likely to move the next attempt. Multiply by a weekly cycle across a school year and the marking is comparable in volume to the contact time.

So a quoted rate is answering a question you have not asked. The useful question is what the total package includes, and the table below sets out the three versions of English tuition that hide behind a single hourly number. The middle column is where most of the market sits and where most of the disappointment originates: a lesson that discusses writing in general without ever reading a piece the student produced to time.

This is also why the cheapest tiers behave differently in English than in science. At AED 33 to AED 65 an hour, published by Tutopiya and EdFlik, a student can get genuinely useful homework supervision and content recall in a science subject. In English, the same rate buys conversation about writing, because nobody can afford to spend forty minutes marking an essay at that price. That is arithmetic, not a judgement about the tutors.

sections.heading: The 4EA1 components you are buying preparation for
paragraphs: Before any rate is agreed, establish which components your child is actually sitting. Pearson's specification for English Language A sets out Paper 1, non-fiction texts and transactional writing, at two hours and fifteen minutes and sixty per cent of the qualification, and Paper 2, poetry and prose texts and imaginative writing, at an hour and a half and forty per cent, with a coursework route available in place of that second paper. Read the current subject page on the Pearson site and confirm your child's option with the school.

That sixty-forty split has a direct budget consequence. Paper 1 carries more marks and contains the fastest-moving component in the subject, the non-fiction reading section. If hours are limited, they belong there. A plan that divides time evenly across the two papers is spending the same money for less movement, and a plan that leads with Paper 2 anthology coverage is usually responding to what feels unprepared rather than to where the marks are.

The coursework question matters more than its share of the qualification suggests. Families occasionally buy a term of Paper 2 preparation for a student whose school entered coursework, or the reverse. One email to the English department settles it. It also settles the honesty question, because support for a submitted folder has a boundary that support for a sat paper does not, and that boundary should be stated before the first session rather than discovered mid-term.

paragraphs: The useful comparison is not between named companies but between business models, because the model predicts what you get for the money better than the brand does. The table below compares models and quotes only published figures, each attributable to the provider that published it. IB Gram does not appear with a rate because no rate is published on these pages; our pricing follows a diagnostic and a written plan.

Read the marking column first. It is the one that separates two otherwise identical AED 200 hours, and it is almost never on a provider's website. Ask it directly and listen for whether the answer contains a turnaround time. Within two working days, annotated against the criteria, is an operational commitment. We give detailed feedback is a sentence.

The in-home line deserves a straight explanation rather than a dismissal. Bestimate's Dubai table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350, independent home tutors up to AED 500, and monthly in-home packages at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Part of that premium is the drive, and in English a two-hour in-home block can genuinely suit a student who writes better with someone sitting beside them. IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India.

What an online model changes for English specifically is less about price than about the reading. Annotation on a shared screen is saved, revisited and compared with the previous piece, which is how a student sees that the same comma splice has appeared four weeks running. A paper script annotated in a living room and put in a bag does not produce that comparison, which is the mechanism by which writing actually improves.

sections.heading: What twenty hours of 4EA1 support actually buys
paragraphs: Twenty hours is roughly a term of weekly sessions, and it is the unit most families end up buying whether or not they plan it that way. What it delivers depends almost entirely on the starting point and on which component the hours are spent in. The table below is built from the mechanics of the qualification rather than from any claim about outcomes, and it deliberately contains no promised grades, because nobody can honestly promise one.

The pattern is consistent. Students losing marks to technique, question reading, form conventions and accuracy get a lot from twenty hours, because those are rule-based gains that hold under pressure. Students whose underlying writing level is the ceiling get less, because sentence control and structural range are built over terms. That is not a reason to skip the hours; it is a reason to buy them in Year 10 rather than in the March of Year 11.

The third row is the one worth reading twice. A student on a secure 6 who wants a 7 is usually not short of content or technique; they are short of the specific analytical precision and sentence variety that separate the top bands, and that is the slowest gain in the subject. Families who buy twenty hours expecting that movement in a term are frequently disappointed by a tutor who did nothing wrong.

What should accompany any twenty-hour plan is a mid-point review on evidence. After eight to ten sessions, the student sits a full timed paper, it is marked, and the mark is compared with the baseline from the diagnostic. If the categories that were supposed to move have not moved, the plan changes rather than continuing. Ten hours spent in the wrong component is the single most common waste in English tuition, and a mid-point review is what catches it.

sections.heading: Language A or Language B: the entry question that decides the bill
paragraphs: A share of the money spent on English tuition in Dubai is spent on the wrong qualification. English Language A and English Language B are different Pearson International GCSE qualifications aimed at different students, and a child entered for 4EA1 who would be better served by 4EB1 can absorb tuition hours for a year without the grade responding. This is worth resolving before the budget is committed, and it costs one conversation with the English department.

The signal is not nationality or home language. It is whether the student is operating in English as a first language in an academic register, or working in English as an additional language with a developing vocabulary range. A student in the second category sitting a first-language paper is being assessed against criteria written for the first category, and tuition cannot change that framing. It can only help them cope with it.

Where the school has entered 4EA1 and that is settled, the practical consequence for spending is a different allocation of hours. Vocabulary range and idiomatic control become the long slow project, and the recoverable marks sit in the reading section, in form conventions and in accuracy. A plan that spends twenty hours trying to raise register in a term is spending in the wrong place, however well it is taught.

Where the school is open to a conversation about the entry, the evidence to bring is the marked work rather than an opinion. Comments on a criteria grid referring repeatedly to vocabulary range, expression and idiom tell a story. So does a strong reading mark alongside a weak writing mark. The decision belongs to the school, and the reason to raise it early is that it determines what the tuition is for and therefore what it should cost.
