sections.heading: The coursework route and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Where a school has entered the coursework option in place of Paper 2, forty per cent of the qualification rests on pieces the student produces themselves. That changes what tuition can legitimately be. A tutor teaches the skill, questions the thinking, reads what the student has already written and gives feedback on it. A tutor does not supply sentences, paragraphs, structures or content for a folder submitted under the student's name.

The distinction is about sequence, and it is easy to apply. Feedback on an attempt the student made is teaching. A model handed over before the student attempts anything, for a piece that will be submitted, is not teaching, and the exposure falls on the student rather than on the provider. Any family paying for coursework-route support should state this expectation out loud in the first conversation and notice how it is received.

This matters commercially as well as ethically, because the UAE market contains providers selling completed assessed work. Research into this sector found one operator advertising finished Internal Assessments for international qualifications at a fixed price. Whatever the qualification, buying submitted work exposes the student to a malpractice finding, and no grade is worth that. It is also a reason to be cautious about everything else such a provider says about its prices and its people.

The second boundary is material. Pearson specifications, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Pearson. A tutoring service references and links them; it does not reproduce or distribute them as downloads, and a provider offering a bundle of papers as a selling point is offering something it is not entitled to supply. IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from Pearson, Edexcel, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE or the Ministry of Education.

sections.heading: Where 4EA1 money gets wasted, and the four questions that prevent it
paragraphs: Four waste patterns account for most of the money spent on English tuition in Dubai without a grade moving, and all four are avoidable before the first invoice. None of them involves a bad tutor. They involve buying a reasonable product for the wrong problem, at the wrong time, in the wrong component.

The first is buying lessons without marking, which is paying for the cheap half of the cycle. The second is buying writing development in the spring of Year 11, when there is no runway for a slow gain and the recoverable marks are in reading, timing and accuracy. The third is spending hours on the component that feels unprepared rather than the one carrying the marks, which usually means Paper 2 anthology coverage while Paper 1 Section A sits at a 5. The fourth is never checking at the mid-point whether anything has changed.

Against those four, four questions. What is included beyond the hour, and what is the marking turnaround? Which component will the first six sessions target, and what evidence says so? What will we look at after eight sessions to decide whether to continue? And what happens if the honest answer turns out to be that the school's own English clinic, or an entry-level conversation about 4EA1 against 4EB1, is the better first step?

A provider who can answer the fourth question without flinching is the one to book. The answer involves sending you somewhere else for part of the work, and that is a signal about everything else they will tell you. Departmental clinics, revision sessions and past-paper practice are inside the school fees you already pay, and a plan that ignores them is overcharging you by omission.

sections.heading: Timing the spend: why Year 10 hours cost less per mark
paragraphs: English is the clearest case in the Pearson suite for spending early, and the reason is mechanical rather than motivational. Writing improves through volume plus feedback over months. Reading technique improves through targeted practice over weeks. A two-year course therefore has a natural spending order: the slow work goes in Year 10, where there is runway, and the fast work goes in Year 11, where there is not.

Families overwhelmingly do the opposite, because Year 10 feels early and a Year 11 mock result feels urgent. The consequence is that the same budget buys less. Twenty hours spent in Year 10 on timed writing with proper marking changes what the student can produce. The same twenty hours in March of Year 11 can only organise what they already produce, which is worth real marks but fewer of them.

There is a Dubai-specific layer to this. The spring term compresses mocks, internal deadlines and the exam entry window, and Ramadan frequently sits inside that compression with shortened school days and a different evening rhythm. A writing-development programme does not survive that term intact. A reading-technique block and an accuracy clinic do, because they are short, structured and tolerant of a disrupted week.

The practical scheduling conclusion is to hold one fixed weekly slot from early in Year 10 and keep it, rather than buying an intensive later. Because delivery here is one-to-one over live video, that slot survives family travel, school holidays and a Ramadan timetable shift with a calendar edit rather than a renegotiation, and continuity is the variable that writing improvement is most sensitive to.

faqs.question: How much does Edexcel IGCSE English Language A 4EA1 tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates for International GCSE tuition run from about AED 33 an hour at the budget-platform end to AED 650 at the named tier. Tutopiya lists AED 33 to AED 52, EdFlik AED 45 to AED 65, Unitors from AED 150, TutorChase around AED 270 and BartyED AED 650. Bestimate's rate table puts specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. For English the number alone is incomplete: ask whether criteria-referenced marking of timed writing is included and what the turnaround is, because that is the half of the cycle the rate usually hides.

faqs.question: Why is English tuition quoted differently from maths or science tuition?
faqs.answer: It usually is not quoted differently, and that is the problem. A maths hour is largely self-contained. An English hour is the visible part of a cycle whose expensive part is the marking: reading a timed response closely enough to identify which sentence lost the mark takes a competent marker thirty to fifty minutes. Across a school year that reading is comparable in volume to the contact time. A rate that excludes it is a rate for the cheaper half, which is why two AED 200 hours from different providers can be very different purchases.

faqs.question: Should criteria-referenced marking be included in the hourly rate?
faqs.answer: It should be included in the plan, whether it sits inside the hourly rate or alongside it. What matters is that somebody reads the student's own timed writing against the published criteria and returns annotation the student can use, within a stated number of working days. Ask for the turnaround as a number. An operational commitment sounds like annotated against the criteria within two working days. A sentence about detailed feedback is not a commitment, and in English it is the difference between a plan that moves a grade and one that discusses moving it.

faqs.question: Do English tutors in Dubai charge more than science tutors?
faqs.answer: Not materially, on published rates: the same AED bands appear across subjects, from Tutopiya's AED 33 to AED 52 up to BartyED's AED 650. The real difference is in what the rate covers. In a science subject at the budget tier a student can get useful homework supervision and content recall. In English the same rate cannot cover forty minutes of essay marking, so what is bought is conversation about writing rather than feedback on it. That is arithmetic rather than a comment on the tutors involved.

faqs.question: What does the 4EA1 coursework route change about the cost?
faqs.answer: Less than it changes the shape. Where a school has entered the coursework option in place of the second written paper, forty per cent of the qualification rests on pieces the student produces under school conditions, and support has a firm boundary: skills teaching and feedback on work already written, never material supplied for submission. The cost consequence is that the work is driven by the school's internal deadlines rather than by the exam series. Establish which route your child is on before buying any preparation, because families do buy the wrong one.

faqs.question: My child speaks English as an additional language. Is 4EA1 the right paper?
faqs.answer: It may not be, and this is worth settling before committing a budget. English Language A and English Language B are different Pearson qualifications for different students, and a child entered for the first-language paper who would be better served by 4EB1 can absorb a year of tuition without the grade responding. The entry is the school's decision. Bring evidence rather than opinion: a strong reading mark alongside a weak writing mark, and criteria comments returning repeatedly to vocabulary range, expression and idiom, are the signals to discuss with the department.

faqs.question: How many hours does it take to move a 4EA1 grade 5 to a 7?
faqs.answer: No honest answer exists without seeing a marked piece, and any provider who gives one before that is guessing. What can be said is where the hours go. A student at 5 because they paraphrase rather than analyse in the reading section has recoverable marks within a block of six. A student at 5 because sentence control and range are the ceiling is on a project measured in terms, not weeks. Those two students have the same reported grade and very different budgets, which is why the diagnostic comes before the quote.

faqs.question: Is a group English class worth the saving for 4EA1?
faqs.answer: For some things, yes. Group teaching delivers form conventions, exam structure and the mechanics of each component efficiently, and a student who can ask questions in a room gets real value from it. What a group cannot do is read your child's individual writing against the criteria and name the specific sentence patterns costing marks, because that is individual work by definition. A sensible hybrid is group work on structure and conventions plus a short one-to-one block for marked writing, which keeps most of the saving.

faqs.question: Do we pay extra for having transactional writing tasks marked?
faqs.answer: That depends entirely on the provider and it is the question to ask first. Marking a Paper 1 Section B response properly against the criteria takes a reader thirty to fifty minutes, so it is a real cost that is either inside the rate, charged alongside it, or quietly not happening. None of the published Dubai rate ranges states which. Ask how many pieces a month are marked, what you receive, and within how many working days, and compare two quotes on those three answers rather than on the hourly figure.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest useful thing we can do before paying anyone for 4EA1?
faqs.answer: Three things, all free. Ask the English department which components your child is entered for, including whether the coursework route applies, because families do buy preparation for the wrong one. Ask for the component-level marks rather than the reported grade, so you know whether Paper 1 or Paper 2 is the weakness. And ask what the department already provides: clinics, revision sessions and past-paper practice are inside fees you have paid. Those three answers often change the plan before a single hour is bought.

faqs.question: Does a 4EA1 grade count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: The published requirement for the British track is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. How a specific certificate is counted is a decision for the Ministry and the attestation authority. Verify your child's own case on moe.gov.ae or with the school registrar. IB Gram does not perform or influence equivalency, and tutoring is not required for it.

faqs.question: Should we pay a tutor to cover the Paper 2 set texts?
faqs.answer: Only after checking where the marks are. Paper 1 carries sixty per cent of the qualification and contains the fastest-moving component in the subject, so hours spent on anthology coverage while the non-fiction reading section sits at a 5 are hours spent in the lower-yield place. Where the texts genuinely have not been covered, that is the school's teaching to establish rather than a tutor's to replace, and the right call is a conversation with the department first. Where they have been covered, the gain is in technique, not in more reading.

faqs.question: When in the two years is 4EA1 tuition best value?
faqs.answer: Year 10, clearly, and the reason is mechanical. Writing improves through volume plus feedback over months; reading technique improves over weeks. So the slow work belongs where there is runway and the fast work belongs in the exam year. Twenty hours in Year 10 changes what a student can produce. The same twenty hours in March of Year 11 can only organise what they already produce. The Dubai spring term, with mocks, entry deadlines and often Ramadan compressed together, makes that contrast sharper rather than softer.

faqs.question: What should a 4EA1 quote include before we compare it with another?
faqs.answer: Four things, all answerable in one call. What is included beyond the contact hour, and specifically the marking turnaround in working days. Which component the first six sessions will target, and what evidence supports that choice. What will be reviewed after eight sessions, against what baseline, to decide whether to continue. And what the provider will say if the honest finding is that the school's own support or an entry-level conversation should come first. Two quotes answered on those four points are genuinely comparable; two hourly rates are not.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover 4EA1 and English Literature at the same time?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and it is normally better value than two bookings. Close reading, quotation discipline and essay structure transfer directly between the two qualifications, so work done for one pays part of the bill for the other. The condition is that the literature texts are named before the plan is agreed, because text-specific preparation is not interchangeable. Where a student is weak in both, sequence matters: establish the reading technique once, then apply it in both subjects, rather than running two parallel programmes.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-english-language-a-4.closingHeading: Price the whole cycle, not the hour
dubai/edexcel-igcse-english-language-a-4.closingBody: You now have the published Dubai bands with their sources, the component structure the hours are being spent on, what twenty hours tends to buy at different starting points, and the four questions that make two English quotes comparable. The next step costs nothing: send one marked piece of writing with its criteria grid, take the free trial as a diagnostic, and read the written baseline that comes back. It will name the loss categories in order of size and say which move in weeks and which move across terms. If the honest finding is that the school's own clinic or a conversation about the entry comes first, you will be told that. Sessions run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-english-language-b-4.tutorsIntro: Tutors below teach Pearson Edexcel International GCSE English and correct additional-language writing at this level. When comparing quotes, ask what the rate covers besides the hour: for 4EB1 the correction of timed writing is the component that does the work, and it is the component most often left out of a price.

intro.heading: What you are paying for, and how much of it is the drive
paragraphs: Start with the two published bands, because the gap between them is the whole of the home-tutor cost question. Bestimate's Dubai tutoring rate table puts in-home one-to-one tuition at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500, and monthly in-home packages at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Unitors lists online International GCSE tuition from AED 150. EdFlik publishes AED 45 to AED 65, Tutopiya AED 33 to AED 52, TutorChase around AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 at the named tier. Those are their figures, published by them.

A large share of the in-home premium is not teaching. It is a car in Dubai traffic. A tutor delivering a sixty-minute lesson in Arabian Ranches from an address in Deira is committing well over two hours to that booking, and that time is recovered somewhere: in the rate, in a two-hour minimum, or in a service radius so tight that your choice of tutor shrinks to whoever lives nearby. None of those three is dishonest. They are what distance costs in a city of this size.

For English Language B the arithmetic has a second layer, and it is the one that catches families out. 4EB1 is the Pearson International GCSE for students working in English as an additional language, assessed by written examination with no coursework route, so the whole grade rests on exam performance. Confirm the current paper structure on the Pearson subject page with your school. What that structure means commercially is that the work which moves a grade is correction: somebody reading timed writing closely enough to name which error family is costing marks, repeatedly, over months.

Correction is expensive because it takes real time, and it is the first thing to vanish from a cheap hour. At AED 33 to AED 65 an hour nobody can afford to spend thirty minutes on a written piece, so what gets bought at that rate is conversation about English rather than correction of it. That is arithmetic, not a judgement about the tutors involved, and it is why the cheapest option on a language paper is frequently the most expensive thing a family does.

There is a third cost, invisible on any rate card, which is time. An additional-language learner in a Dubai private school is also carrying mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies, required in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA calculating their instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit. A plan that assumes two free weekday evenings is a plan that will be abandoned by November, and abandoned plans are the purest waste in this market.

IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India, and UAE delivery is one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. What follows prices the real job: the travel arithmetic community by community, what correction costs and who should pay for it, the group-class maths, the permit position and how to check it, what a full year realistically comes to, and what to put in writing before money changes hands.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-english-language-b-4.programmesIntro: The same hourly rate buys a different thing at each stage, and for an additional-language learner the difference between spending early and spending late is larger than in any other subject. These four stages are the budget decisions, in the order they arrive.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9: the cheapest hours you will ever buy
programmes.description: Range grows fastest when there is no exam pressure and no deadline, and the hours are both cheaper in effect and more productive. A student who arrives in Year 10 with a working vocabulary and reliable sentence control needs a fraction of the support of one who does not. Families almost never spend here, and it is the clearest value in the whole sequence.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai receives transfer students at every year point, and a new arrival in Year 8 with strong reading and untaught writing conventions is a very common profile. Spending a term on writing then costs less than spending a year on it in the exam years.

programmes.name: Year 10: where the money does the most work
programmes.description: The year with enough runway for a slow variable to move. A term of weekly correction in Year 10 changes what a student can produce under time. The same spend in Year 11 can only organise what they already produce. If a family has one block of budget for this qualification, it belongs here, and that is a sequencing decision rather than a sales position.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai departments commonly set the first full exam-style assessment in the spring of Year 10. That marked piece, with its band description, is the document that makes a quote specific instead of generic, and it is free.

programmes.name: Year 11: paying for recoverable marks only
programmes.description: Range is largely fixed by now, so money spent trying to raise it buys very little. What remains available is task coverage, question operations, pacing, paper completion and the rule-based accuracy errors. A block aimed squarely at those is good value. A general English course at this point is not, and intensity does not accelerate language acquisition.
programmes.countryNote: The Dubai spring term compresses mocks, entry deadlines and often Ramadan into a short run, and demand for English support concentrates into the same weeks. Effective prices rise through scarcity even where advertised rates do not.

programmes.name: Resit and private-candidate entry
programmes.description: Pearson International GCSE subjects are examined in a May or June series and again in November each year, so a disappointing grade is a months-long problem rather than a lost year. The tuition cost of a resit is usually modest because the work is narrow. The entry is the part to check, and the deadline sits well before the paper.
programmes.countryNote: A student no longer enrolled at a Dubai school sits as a private candidate through a centre accepting external entries, and that centre sets both its own fee and its own registration cut-off. Confirm the cut-off before buying any hours, because the deadline fixes the calendar.

programmes.name: When a proficiency test is the better purchase
programmes.description: Universities frequently want a test score rather than a school qualification, and published MoE guidance for the American track sets English proficiency at a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. Where a target university wants a test, some of the tutoring budget may belong there instead.
programmes.countryNote: Test preparation and 4EB1 preparation overlap only partly, so they compete for the same hours. Establishing which the destination actually requires, in writing, before committing a budget is the single cheapest thing a family can do in this whole process.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-english-language-b-4.subjectsIntro: This list prices the work rather than describing the syllabus: which parts of 4EB1 respond to paid hours quickly, which take terms, and which neighbouring subjects a family usually ends up funding alongside it.

subjects.name: Task coverage and audience
subjects.description: The cheapest marks on the qualification. A checklist applied to every piece, until the student checks it unprompted, recovers marks lost for not doing everything the task asked. Two or three sessions of work, and nothing to do with language level.

subjects.name: Question operations in the reading section
subjects.description: Fast and inexpensive. An additional-language student who understands a passage can still default to retrieval where inference was wanted, which scores at the bottom. A block of six sessions is the normal shape and the gain shows on an unseen timed section.

subjects.name: Pacing and paper completion
subjects.description: Cheap and frequently worth more than anything else available. A student who leaves the final task short is losing more marks than a term of range work would recover. One session plus two timed papers usually fixes it permanently.

subjects.name: Rule-based accuracy errors
subjects.description: Subject-verb agreement, irregular past forms, plurals, capitalisation. These clear in weeks because a rule can be taught and drilled. Correction is the cost here, not explanation, and a short personal list beats any general grammar programme.

subjects.name: Pattern-based accuracy errors
subjects.description: Article use, preposition choice, countability, tense consistency across a paragraph. These take a term or more and improve by falling in frequency rather than disappearing. Budget them as a long correction programme, never as a block with an endpoint.

subjects.name: Vocabulary range and collocation
subjects.description: The slowest and most expensive thing to shift per mark gained. It is why spending in Year 10 beats spending in Year 11. Reading volume does part of the work for free, which is the only genuinely cheap lever available on this element.

subjects.name: English Language A (4EA1) as the alternative entry
subjects.description: The first-language qualification, with a coursework option available in place of one component. A student sitting the wrong one of the two can absorb a year of paid hours without the grade responding, which makes the entry question the first budget decision rather than an academic footnote.

subjects.name: Written subjects across the timetable
subjects.description: An additional-language limitation costs marks in every subject with extended writing. Money spent on English accuracy therefore pays in several places, which is a genuine argument for funding it ahead of a second subject tutor.

subjects.name: English proficiency test preparation
subjects.description: A separate purchase with partly overlapping content. Where a target university asks for a test score, some of the budget belongs here. Establish the requirement in writing before splitting hours between two programmes competing for the same evenings.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first or additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students. Its weekly hours are a scheduling cost on any English plan rather than a fee, and ignoring them is how plans collapse.

regions.note: Villa districts reached from most of the city only through the afternoon peak. A sixty-minute lesson here can commit over two hours of a tutor's day, which is why two-hour minimums are common in this belt and why the quoted rate sits at the upper end of the published band.

regions.note: Newer communities at the edge of the network. Travel in both directions is the single largest input into any in-home quote here, and families often find the available pool of English specialists narrows sharply once travel time is priced honestly.

sections.heading: The travel arithmetic: what an in-home hour actually costs in Dubai
paragraphs: The in-home premium is usually presented as a convenience charge and is mostly a time charge. Work it out from the tutor's side and the published rates stop looking arbitrary. A tutor who leaves at 15:15 to reach a 16:00 lesson in the villa belt and gets home at 18:00 has sold one hour and spent nearly three. Whatever they charge has to cover the three, which is why the Bestimate band for in-home visits sits at AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors are quoted up to AED 500.

This produces two effects a parent feels directly. The first is the two-hour minimum, common in the outer communities, which turns a sixty-minute need into a one-hundred-and-twenty-minute invoice. The second is the service radius: a tutor who prices travel honestly can only serve a narrow band of the city, so your choice collapses from every English specialist in Dubai to the handful who live within a sensible drive. On a qualification where the specialism is narrow, that collapse costs more than the dirhams do.

The table below works through representative journeys. The figures are a straightforward estimate of commitment rather than a traffic claim, and the point of the final column is to show what proportion of the rate is paying for teaching. In the outer communities, less than half of it is.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service is available only in India, and UAE delivery is one-to-one over live video. The reason this page does the arithmetic anyway is that a parent comparing an in-home quote with an online one deserves to know what the difference is buying. Sometimes a visiting tutor is the right answer, particularly for a younger writer who needs someone beside them. For a Year 10 or 11 student on 4EB1, the travel premium almost always buys less than the same money spent on correction would.

sections.heading: Why the cheapest hour is the expensive choice on a language paper
paragraphs: In most subjects a budget tutor delivers real value. Homework gets supervised, content gets recalled, confidence improves, and at AED 33 to AED 65 an hour, the rates published by Tutopiya and EdFlik, that is a reasonable purchase. On an additional-language English paper the same rate behaves differently, and the reason is time rather than talent.

The work that moves a 4EB1 grade is correction. Somebody has to read a timed piece closely enough to see that the article errors are not random but follow a pattern, that the same four verbs are being formed wrongly, that a paragraph drifts tense in the third sentence every time. That reading takes twenty-five to forty minutes for a single piece. At the budget tier nobody can afford to spend it, so what the hour contains is discussion of English instead of correction of it, and discussion does not clear an error family.

This is why families regularly report a year of affordable tutoring with no movement. Nobody behaved badly. The product simply did not contain the active ingredient, and the parent had no way to know, because the rate card does not mention correction and neither does the website. The question has to be asked directly, and the answer to listen for is a number of working days rather than a reassurance.

The honest implication is uncomfortable but useful: for this qualification, fewer corrected pieces beat more uncorrected hours. A family with a limited budget gets more from one properly corrected timed piece a fortnight than from a weekly conversational hour, and the correction-only cycle described above exists precisely for that case. Buying less of the right thing is almost always better than buying more of the wrong one.

sections.heading: Group classes and centres: the per-student arithmetic
paragraphs: Group tuition is the genuine low-cost option in Dubai and deserves a fair hearing rather than a dismissal. A centre class splits a tutor's rate across several students, which makes the per-head cost materially lower, and for parts of this qualification that trade works. Task conventions, exam structure, question operations and pacing can all be taught once to a room.

What a group cannot split is correction. Reading one student's timed writing closely enough to identify their specific error families is individual work by definition, and in a class of six it either happens for one student at a time, slowly, or it happens superficially for everyone. Since correction is the active ingredient on 4EB1, a group-only plan tends to teach the cheap marks well and leave the expensive ones untouched.

There is a second group effect specific to additional-language learners, and it cuts both ways. A room of students at a similar level produces useful speaking practice and normalises the experience of being wrong, which has real value for a student who has gone quiet in a mainstream English class. The same room moves at the pace of its median student, which for a learner at either end of the range means hours spent on the wrong thing.

The arithmetic below compares the models on the thing that matters rather than on headline price. Read the correction column first. The combination most families should price, and rarely do, is group work for the structural content plus a correction-only cycle for the individual writing, which keeps most of the saving and all of the active ingredient.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE, and how do you check?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and a parent is entitled to ask about it plainly. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

Because the permit is free, no component of any quoted rate is a permit fee, and a provider presenting one is describing something else. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. That page, rather than any summary of it, is the thing to check.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount can responsibly be quoted and a figure circulating online should be treated as unverified. One boundary is worth knowing before you ask anybody: a teacher at your child's own school tutoring your child privately runs against professional-ethics rules and the permit's code of conduct, which bar serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's rules for private and charter school staff are explicit about this.

A separate point on premises. A tutoring operation with staff and a location in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE premises, and holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from Pearson, Edexcel, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE or the Ministry of Education.

sections.heading: Budgeting a 4EB1 year, with the session calendar counted backwards
paragraphs: A year of support is the unit most families end up buying, usually without planning it as one. Planning it changes the total, because the Pearson calendar dictates when hours are worth most and when they are worth least. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects are examined in a May or June series and again in November. For the November 2026 series the final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so any plan should work from the live official timetable on the Pearson support site rather than from a date printed on a tutoring page, this one included. Your school's exams officer holds the authoritative version for your centre.

Counted backwards, the spending pattern becomes clear. Hours bought in the autumn of Year 10 are buying range growth at ordinary prices, and range is the slow variable that cannot be bought later. Hours bought in the spring of Year 11 are buying technique at peak demand, which is worth real marks but fewer of them per dirham. A family that spends the same total in the earlier window gets more, and that is the single most actionable cost finding on this page.

The table below is a planning frame, not a price list. No IB Gram rate appears, because none is published on these pages and any figure attached to our name here would be invented. What the table does is convert published bands into the shapes families actually buy, so that a quote can be checked against a pattern. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget tier, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-tier, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support; a quote far outside those deserves an explanation.

sections.heading: Siblings, shared hours and the per-child arithmetic
paragraphs: Families with two or three children in a Dubai school often want one booking to serve more than one of them, and the honest answer depends on how close the two students are in both level and qualification. Where the match is good the saving is real. Where it is not, a shared booking quietly becomes a group class of two moving at the pace of the stronger child.

The cases that work are narrow. Two siblings on the same qualification, within a grade of each other, with overlapping error families, can genuinely share a weekly session and the correction can still be individual. Two siblings on 4EB1 and 4EA1 cannot share a session usefully, because the expectations they are judged against are different and the teaching diverges immediately.

A better structure for mismatched siblings is a shared contact hour on the parts that genuinely overlap, which for English means question operations, task coverage and pacing, plus separate correction priced per piece. That keeps most of the saving and preserves the individual element, which is the part that moves a grade. Ask any provider to price that structure explicitly rather than assuming a sibling discount covers it.

One practical warning. A shared session changes how a teenager behaves, particularly a less confident additional-language learner sitting beside a more fluent sibling. Some students work harder; others stop speaking entirely. That is worth one trial session to find out, because the saving is irrelevant if the quieter child stops participating.

sections.heading: What to send, and what to get in writing, before any money moves
paragraphs: Most families ring three providers, hear three hourly rates and choose on instinct. The rates are not comparable because they describe different products, and five minutes of preparation turns three numbers into three like-for-like offers. Send the same three documents to each provider and ask the same four questions.

Send the most recent marked timed piece with its band description, the section or component marks if the school publishes them, and confirmation of which English qualification your child is entered for. Those three documents let a provider quote on your child rather than on an average, and a provider who quotes without reading them has told you something about how they work.

Then ask four things and write the answers down. What is the correction turnaround, in working days, and what will I receive? Which losses will the first six sessions target, and what in the marked piece says so? What gets reviewed, against what baseline, before I commit to a second block? And what happens if the honest answer is that the entry itself, or the school's own support, should come first?

Get three things in writing before paying: the session count and total cost of the first block, what happens to a missed or rescheduled session, and the exit terms after one month. If a free trial is offered, get the condition attached to it stated on the same page as the word free, because a conditional free trial not described as conditional is the first thing to be careful about. None of this is adversarial. It is the paperwork any competent provider already has and will send in an afternoon.
bullets: Send the marked piece with its band description, the section marks, and the entry
Ask for the correction turnaround as a number of working days
Get the first block's session count, total cost and exit terms in writing

sections.heading: Spending on a slow variable without wasting it
paragraphs: Language range improves over terms, which creates a genuine budgeting problem: a family is being asked to fund something that will not visibly change for months. The temptation is either to give up at week eight or to escalate intensity, and both responses cost money without changing the outcome. There is a third option, which is to split the budget by speed.

Spend the first block on the fast losses. Task coverage, question operations, pacing, paper completion and rule-based accuracy all move inside six sessions and all of them show up on an unseen timed paper. That gives a family early, checkable evidence that the provider works, which is the thing most needed before committing to a long correction programme.

Then fund the slow work at the cheapest sustainable cadence rather than the most impressive one. A correction-only cycle every fortnight across a year costs a fraction of weekly one-to-one and delivers most of the accuracy benefit, because the active ingredient is the correction and not the conversation. Add reading volume, which is free and is one of the few genuine levers on collocation and idiom.

Finally, review on a fixed date agreed in advance rather than when somebody becomes anxious. One unseen timed paper at the midpoint, marked the same way as the first, with the error families counted. If the fast losses recovered and the open families have dropped from six to four, the money is working and slow is simply what slow looks like. If nothing has moved on either measure, change the method. Spending more on an unchanged method is the single most common way families waste money on this qualification.
bullets: Buy the fast losses first; they give early checkable evidence
Fund the slow correction work at a fortnightly cadence, not a weekly one
Reading volume is free and is a real lever on collocation
Fix the review date in advance, and change the method rather than the budget

process.description: The student sits an unseen timed piece with no preparation and it is corrected against the published expectations. The output is a written split of the losses into the fast ones, which move inside six sessions, and the slow ones, which take terms. You keep that document either way.

process.description: You receive the session count, what each session targets, the correction turnaround in working days and the total cost, before anything is booked. Where the honest finding is that the entry should be reviewed with the school first, the plan says that instead of selling a block.

process.title: Correction at the cadence the budget supports
process.description: Weekly where that is sustainable, fortnightly where it is not, and correction-only where a contact hour is not the active ingredient. Slots run in Gulf Standard Time and survive family travel and a Ramadan timetable shift with a calendar edit rather than a lost month.

faqs.question: How much does an Edexcel IGCSE English Language B 4EB1 home tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai figures put in-home one-to-one tuition at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour in Bestimate's rate table, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500 and monthly in-home packages at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Online qualified tuition is published from AED 150 by Unitors. A large part of that gap is recovered travel time rather than teaching. IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India, and UAE delivery is one-to-one over live video.

faqs.question: What does an in-home visit actually add to the hourly rate?
faqs.answer: Mostly a car in Dubai traffic. A tutor leaving at 15:15 for a 16:00 lesson in the villa belt and returning by 18:00 has sold one hour and spent close to three, and the rate has to cover all three. That produces the two effects parents feel: two-hour minimums in the outer communities, and a service radius narrow enough that your choice shrinks to specialists who live nearby. On a qualification where the specialism is narrow, that second effect usually costs more than the dirhams.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper tutor a false economy for an additional-language learner?
faqs.answer: Often, and for a specific mechanical reason. What moves a 4EB1 grade is correction: reading a timed piece closely enough to see that the article errors follow a pattern and that the same four verbs are formed wrongly. That takes twenty-five to forty minutes per piece. At the published budget tier of AED 33 to AED 65 an hour, nobody can afford to spend it, so the hour contains discussion of English rather than correction of it. Families then report a year of affordable tutoring with no movement, and nobody behaved badly.

faqs.question: How much does correction work cost, and who should pay for it?
faqs.answer: It costs real time, which is why it is the component most often missing from a rate. The useful approach is to price the cycle rather than the hour: one timed piece corrected properly plus one session built on that correction. Ask what the turnaround is in working days and what you receive, and compare two providers on those two answers rather than on the hourly figure. A provider who will not quote a turnaround is quoting for the contact hour alone, which on this qualification is the cheaper half of the job.

faqs.question: Does a tuition centre group class work out cheaper for 4EB1?
faqs.answer: Per head, clearly yes, and for some of the work it is genuinely good value. Task conventions, exam structure, question operations and pacing can all be taught once to a room, and a group of similar-level learners gives a quiet student useful speaking practice. What a group cannot split is correction of one student's individual writing, which is the active ingredient here. The structure worth pricing, and rarely offered, is group work for the structural content plus a correction-only cycle for the writing.

faqs.question: Can two siblings share a 4EB1 booking to halve the cost?
faqs.answer: Only when the match is close: the same qualification, within a grade of each other, with overlapping error families. Two siblings on 4EB1 and 4EA1 cannot usefully share a session, because the expectations they are judged against differ and the teaching diverges immediately. A better structure for mismatched siblings is a shared contact hour on the genuinely overlapping parts plus separate per-piece correction. Trial it once before committing, because some students work harder in a shared session and others stop speaking entirely.

faqs.question: What does the UAE private tutor permit cost, and do we pay for it?
faqs.answer: Nothing, and no. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the smart app, website and e-services system. Any component of a quoted rate presented as a permit or licensing fee is describing something else. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published fine schedule.

faqs.question: How do I check a tutor is legally allowed to teach privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the permit and ask which eligibility category they applied under, since the resolution lists registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Pair that with a marking question, because eligibility and competence are different things. One boundary to know in advance: a teacher at your child's own school is barred by professional-ethics rules and the permit's code of conduct from tutoring students affiliated with that school, which in Abu Dhabi ADEK states explicitly.

faqs.question: What should we budget for a 4EB1 resit in the November series?
faqs.answer: The tuition part is usually modest, because a resit is narrow work aimed at named losses rather than a course repeated, so a defined block at the tier rate is the normal shape. The entry is what needs checking. A student still at a Dubai school ordinarily has entries handled by the school; one who has left sits as a private candidate through a centre accepting external entries, and that centre sets its own fee and its own registration cut-off. Confirm the cut-off first, because the deadline rather than the exam date fixes your calendar.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to start 4EB1 support in Year 10 or Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10, decisively, and the reason is what the money can buy in each window. Vocabulary range and the pattern-based accuracy families move over terms, so they can only be bought where there is runway. By the spring of Year 11 the range is largely fixed and the available marks are task coverage, question operations, pacing and rule-based errors. The same total spent earlier buys both sets of marks; spent later it buys one. Dubai demand also concentrates city-wide into the spring, so effective prices rise through scarcity.

faqs.question: Do we pay for sessions missed during Ramadan or family travel?
faqs.answer: That depends entirely on the provider, which is why it belongs in writing before the first payment. Ask specifically what happens to a missed session, a rescheduled session and an unused session inside a monthly package, because package terms are where this usually bites. Because delivery here is online over live video, a Ramadan timetable shift to post-Iftar hours or a trip abroad is a calendar edit rather than a lost month, which removes most of the reason the question arises in the first place.

faqs.question: Should we buy a monthly package or pay per session for 4EB1?
faqs.answer: Judge it on the terms rather than the headline saving. Market packages in Dubai include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. A package is good value when the cadence genuinely matches the plan and the slot is held. It is poor value when it fixes a frequency no diagnostic has justified, or when unused sessions expire. For a slow variable like language range, a sustainable fortnightly correction cycle across a year often beats a weekly package bought for three months.

faqs.question: What should we send when asking three providers for a quote?
faqs.answer: The same three documents to each, so the quotes are comparable: the most recent marked timed piece with its band description, the section or component marks where the school publishes them, and confirmation of which English qualification your child is entered for. Then ask each the same four questions about correction turnaround, which losses the first six sessions target, what gets reviewed before a second block, and what they would say if the entry itself should be reviewed first. A provider who quotes without reading the documents has answered something.

faqs.question: How much should a full year of 4EB1 support realistically cost?
faqs.answer: Use the published monthly bands as the sanity check rather than any single rate. Bestimate's estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget tier, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-tier, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. A year at mid-tier weekly cadence therefore sits in four figures a month for most of the year. A quote far outside those bands in either direction deserves a specific explanation, and a fortnightly correction cycle costs materially less than weekly contact.

faqs.question: Would paying for an English proficiency test be better value than tutoring?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends on what the destination actually requires. Universities frequently ask for a test score rather than a school qualification, and published Ministry of Education guidance for the American track sets English proficiency at a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. Establish the requirement in writing before splitting a budget, because test preparation and 4EB1 preparation overlap only partly and compete for the same evenings. dubai/edexcel-igcse-english-language-b-4.tutorsIntro: Tutors below teach Pearson Edexcel International GCSE English and have marked additional-language writing at this level. The useful opening question is not about years taught but about measurement: ask how they will show you, in numbers, that your child's range has grown between October and February.

intro.heading: Measuring progress when a student is learning the language and sitting the exam at once
paragraphs: English Language B carries the Pearson code 4EB1 and is designed for students working in English as an additional language. It is assessed by written examination, and unlike English Language A it carries no coursework alternative, so everything rests on performance in the exam room. Confirm the current paper structure, duration and weightings on the Pearson subject page and with your child's English department, because those details are Pearson's to set and your school's to administer.

That single fact, no coursework, changes what tutoring has to achieve and how it should be judged. There is no folder of produced work building towards a grade across two years, no internal deadlines absorbing part of the risk. What exists is a student's performance on one unseen paper under time pressure, which means the only evidence that counts is performance on unseen papers under time pressure. Everything else is preparation for the measurement, not the measurement itself.

The deeper problem is specific to this qualification. A 4EB1 student is doing two things simultaneously: acquiring a language and learning to be examined in it. Those develop at different speeds and respond to different work. Exam technique can move in weeks. Vocabulary range, idiomatic control and grammatical accuracy move over months, in small increments that are genuinely invisible week to week. A parent watching for improvement will see nothing for a term and conclude, often wrongly, that nothing is happening.

So the method here is counting rather than sensing. Vocabulary range can be measured by counting distinct word families in a timed piece. Accuracy can be measured by tracking error families rather than individual mistakes. Technique can be measured on a timed reading section marked the same way twice. None of this is sophisticated and all of it is more honest than asking a tutor whether things are going well, because a tutor's impression of a pleasant session is not evidence about a language.

The other question this page answers is whether your child is on the right qualification at all. Some Dubai students sitting English Language A would be better served by 4EB1, and some sitting 4EB1 are capable of the first-language paper and are being under-assessed. Both errors cost a grade and both are decided by the school rather than by a tutor. What a family can do is bring evidence to the conversation, and the second section sets out exactly what evidence that is.

IB Gram delivers 4EB1 support as one-to-one online tuition over live video in Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are a service offered only in India and are not sold in the UAE. What follows is the measurement system: the entry decision and its evidence, what the reading section rewards, how to count vocabulary growth, the error families that persist longest for additional-language writers, three fixed evidence points across a year, and what a stalled 4EB1 grade usually turns out to be.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-english-language-b-4.programmesIntro: An additional-language learner meets English at four different stages, and the measurement that makes sense changes at each one. Using a Year 11 measure on a Year 8 student produces discouragement; using a Year 8 measure on a Year 11 student produces false comfort.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9: building range before the qualification
programmes.description: The only measure that matters here is range, and it is countable: distinct word families in a piece of writing, length of the longest controlled sentence, number of connective types used accurately. No exam mark exists to track, which makes these counts the honest substitute. A student whose counts are flat across two terms needs a different method rather than more hours.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools receive additional-language learners at every year point, from every prior system, and a single English grade averages reading and writing into a number that hides which one is the problem. A timed writing sample read properly separates them in one session.

programmes.name: Year 10 of English Language B
programmes.description: The year with enough runway for range to grow measurably. Work is volume plus correction: regular timed pieces, one error family attacked at a time, vocabulary counted monthly. Exam technique is introduced but not emphasised, because technique applied to a thin range produces a well-organised thin answer, which the mark scheme recognises as exactly that.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai departments commonly set the first full exam-style assessment in the spring of Year 10. Ask for the mark and the band description together, because for an additional-language writer the band description is where the specific limitation is named.

programmes.name: Year 11 and the exam series
programmes.description: Measurement switches to unseen timed papers only. At this point the language range is largely what it is, and the recoverable marks sit in question reading, task completion, timing and the accuracy errors that are rule-based rather than intuitive. A plan that spends this year trying to raise range is spending it in the one place it cannot win.
programmes.countryNote: The Dubai spring term compresses mocks, entry deadlines and often Ramadan into a short run. Technique and accuracy work survives that compression. A range-building programme does not, which is why the sequencing across the two years is the decision that matters most.

programmes.name: The entry question: Language A or Language B
programmes.description: A real decision with real consequences, owned by the school. The evidence is a persistent pattern across marked work rather than a single impression: a solid reading mark beside a weak writing mark, band comments returning repeatedly to range and idiom, or the opposite pattern in a student who has been placed too low. Bring the pattern, not the preference.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai English departments often teach first-language and additional-language students in the same classes, which is precisely why the entry sometimes sits wrong in both directions. Raising it with marked evidence in Year 9 or early Year 10 is manageable; raising it in Year 11 rarely is.

programmes.name: After 4EB1: sixth form, equivalency and university
programmes.description: The grade is used in three different places with three different thresholds: sixth-form entry set by the individual school, the Ministry of Education equivalency count for the British track, and university English-proficiency requirements which often ask for a separate test rather than a school qualification. Establish which of the three applies before setting a target grade.
programmes.countryNote: The published MoE requirement for the British track is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the count. Verify your child's own case on moe.gov.ae or with the school registrar rather than relying on any tutoring page.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-english-language-b-4.subjectsIntro: Each element below is paired with how it is measured, because measurement is the content of this page. For an additional-language writer, several of these move on completely different timescales, and treating them as one subject is why a year of effort can read as no progress.

subjects.name: Reading: locating and selecting information
subjects.description: Measured by a clean score on retrieval items across two consecutive unseen passages. Losses here are almost always question reading rather than comprehension, which is good news because question reading is rule-based and moves fast. Visible on a script within minutes.

subjects.name: Reading: inference and writer's purpose
subjects.description: Measured by whether the response answers the operation the question asked rather than summarising the passage. An additional-language student who understands the text and summarises it will score consistently below their comprehension, and that gap is correctable within a block of sessions.

subjects.name: Writing: task fulfilment and audience
subjects.description: The fastest-moving writing marks. Measured in binary terms: did the response do everything the task asked, in the form it asked for, addressed to the stated reader. Students lose these marks to incomplete task coverage far more often than to language, and incomplete coverage is a checklist problem.

subjects.name: Writing: vocabulary range
subjects.description: Measured by counting distinct word families in a timed piece and tracking the count monthly. This is the slowest element in the qualification and the one most often described rather than measured. A count that rises from the sixties to the eighties across a term is real evidence of growth.

subjects.name: Writing: grammatical accuracy by error family
subjects.description: Measured by family, not by incident. Articles, prepositions, tense consistency, subject-verb agreement, word order and countability each behave differently and clear at different rates. Counting total errors tells you nothing; counting them by family tells you what to teach next.

subjects.name: Writing: sentence control and connectives
subjects.description: Measured by the length of the longest sentence the student controls accurately and by how many connective types they use correctly. Both are countable in one paragraph. Range here grows across terms and collapses first under time pressure, which is why it is tested on timed work.

subjects.name: Exam technique and timing
subjects.description: Measured by paper completion before quality. A student who leaves the final task unfinished is losing more marks than any language limitation is costing them, and finishing is a planning gain available within weeks. Track completion first, then track quality.

subjects.name: English Language A (4EA1) as the alternative entry
subjects.description: The first-language qualification, assessed with a coursework option available in place of one component. A student placed on 4EB1 who is operating comfortably in academic English may be under-assessed, and the evidence for that is a ceiling effect: high marks with band comments that have nothing left to criticise.

subjects.name: Subject English across the curriculum
subjects.description: An additional-language limitation shows up in every written subject, not just in English. Measured by whether extended answers in science or geography are losing marks for expression rather than content. Where they are, English work pays a dividend across the whole timetable.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first or additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and specifying the language of instruction for each. Those weekly hours are part of the time budget any English plan has to fit inside.

sections.heading: Language A or Language B: making the entry decision on evidence
paragraphs: A share of the money spent on English tuition in Dubai is spent fighting the wrong qualification. English Language A and English Language B are different Pearson International GCSE qualifications written for different students, and a child sitting the wrong one will absorb hours indefinitely while the grade sits still. Before any plan is costed, this question deserves settling, and the evidence for it is already in your child's marked work.

Neither nationality nor home language decides it. What decides it is whether the student is operating in academic English as a first language or working in English as an additional language with a developing range. A student in the second category entered for the first-language paper is assessed against criteria written for the first, and tuition can only help them cope with that framing, not change it. The reverse error also happens: a capable student placed on 4EB1 and quietly under-assessed.

The table sets out the evidence for each direction. The pattern that matters is persistence across several pieces, not a single bad result. Band comments are the most useful source, because they name the limitation the marker actually found, and comments returning repeatedly to range, idiom or expression are telling you something different from comments about structure or content.

The decision belongs to the school. What a parent brings is a pattern, politely and in writing: the component or section marks, two or three marked pieces, and the recurring band comments. Raised in Year 9 or early Year 10 this is a manageable conversation. Raised in Year 11, after entries are made, it rarely is, which is the practical reason to look at it now rather than after the next mock.

sections.heading: What the reading section rewards, and how to see it on a script
paragraphs: Reading is the fastest-moving part of 4EB1 and the easiest for a parent to assess. The paper asks a predictable set of operations, and an additional-language student who understands a passage can still lose a substantial number of marks by performing the wrong operation. That is a technique loss sitting on top of a comprehension level, and the two need separating before any teaching is planned.

The clearest marker is whether the answer does what the question's verb asked. A question asking why the writer chose a particular word wants an effect, not a definition. A question asking what the passage suggests wants an inference, not a quotation. Students working in an additional language frequently default to retrieval, because retrieval is the operation they are most confident of performing correctly, and retrieval answers to inference questions score at the bottom.

The second marker is answer length against the mark allocation. A two-mark question answered with a paragraph costs time that the writing section then does not have, and a six-mark question answered in a line leaves marks on the table. Scanning down a marked script for uniform answer length tells a parent in thirty seconds whether pacing is being managed, with no subject knowledge required at all.

The third is whether the student is answering from the passage or from general knowledge. An additional-language learner who finds a passage hard will sometimes substitute what they know about the topic for what the text says, and the mark scheme rewards the text. This is diagnosable, correctable and nothing to do with language level, which is why it should be fixed before anyone concludes that comprehension is the limiting factor.
bullets: Check that the response performs the operation the question's verb named
Scan answer length against the mark in brackets, question by question
Watch for general knowledge substituted for what the passage states
Separate technique loss from comprehension level before planning teaching

sections.heading: Counting vocabulary growth instead of sensing it
paragraphs: Vocabulary range is the slowest thing to change in 4EB1 and the thing most often reported in adjectives. Her vocabulary is improving is not a statement anyone can check, and over a term it is the kind of statement that keeps a plan running that is not working. It can be counted, and counting takes a few minutes a month.

Three counts are enough. First, distinct word families in a timed piece: count once, record the number and the word count of the piece. Second, the longest sentence the student controls accurately, measured in words, taken from the same piece. Third, the number of distinct connective types used correctly, which is a reasonable proxy for how many relationships between ideas the student can express. All three come from a single timed piece and all three are comparable month to month.

What a real gain looks like is modest and unmistakable. Distinct word families rising from the sixties to the eighties in a piece of similar length across a term is genuine growth. A longest controlled sentence moving from twelve words to eighteen is genuine growth. Four connective types becoming seven is genuine growth. None of those would be audible in conversation, and all of them show up in a mark eventually, which is the point of measuring them.

The table sets out each measure, how to take it and what movement to expect. Note the frequency column: monthly, not weekly. Weekly counts on a slow variable produce noise and invite a plan to change direction constantly. Note also the last column, which names what each measure cannot tell you, because a measure used beyond its range is worse than no measure.

sections.heading: Error families: what persists, what clears, and in what order
paragraphs: Counting total errors in a piece of additional-language writing is close to useless. A long piece has more errors than a short one, a difficult task produces more than an easy one, and a student attempting ambitious structures will generate errors that a cautious student avoids by writing nothing interesting. What is informative is families: which kinds of error, how many kinds are still open, and which have stopped appearing.

The families behave differently and clear in a fairly reliable order. Rule-based errors go first, because a rule can be taught, drilled and checked: subject-verb agreement, basic tense formation, plural forms, capitalisation. These should be clearing within weeks, and a plan where they are still open after a term has a method problem rather than a student problem.

Then come the pattern-based errors, which take months: article use, preposition choice, countability, tense consistency across a paragraph. These resist explanation because the underlying system is partly arbitrary, and they clear through exposure and correction rather than through rules. Progress here is measured by frequency within a family dropping, not by the family closing, and expecting closure within a term sets everyone up to feel like a failure.

Last are the collocation and register errors, which are the most persistent and the least visible to the student: words that are individually correct and do not belong together, or a formal word dropped into a casual sentence. These are the final difference between a good mark and a top one, and they are a multi-year project. The table below sets the families out with what each needs and the realistic timescale, so that a plan can attack them in an order that produces visible wins early.

sections.heading: Three evidence points across a year, and why three is the right number
paragraphs: Measure too often and you are reading noise. Measure once and you have no trend. Three fixed points in an academic year, each on an unseen timed paper marked the same way, is enough to show direction and few enough that each one is taken seriously and prepared for properly.

The first point is a cold baseline, sat before any teaching. This is the hardest one to insist on, because parents reasonably want the tutor to help before measuring, and a coached baseline destroys the entire series. Everything later is compared against it, so it has to be genuine: unseen material, exam time limit, no preparation, marked against the published expectations.

The second point sits in the middle of the year, far enough from the baseline for a slow variable to have moved. This is where a plan is confirmed or changed. If the rule-based error families have closed and the counts have risen, the method is working and the pace is appropriate. If the counts are flat, the method changes. It is a decision point, not a progress report, and it should be scheduled before the plan starts rather than arranged when someone gets nervous.

The third sits close to but before the school's own mock window, so that what it reveals can still be acted on. The table below sets out the three with what each one is for. The column worth reading is the last: what each point can legitimately conclude. A baseline cannot tell you about progress. A mid-point cannot tell you about a final grade. Treating any single point as more informative than it is produces exactly the overconfidence and panic that a measurement series exists to prevent.

sections.heading: When a 4EB1 grade stalls: reading the script rather than guessing
paragraphs: A stalled grade on this qualification almost always has one of four causes, and all four are visible on a marked paper. Guessing between them is expensive, because each needs different work and three of the four responses are wasted on the wrong diagnosis. Reading the script costs twenty minutes.

The first cause is incomplete task coverage. The student wrote well and did not do everything the task asked, which costs marks that have nothing to do with language. This is the most common cause and the cheapest to fix: a checklist, applied to every piece, until it becomes automatic. A parent can diagnose it by reading the task and ticking off what the response covered.

The second is the wrong operation in the reading section, discussed earlier: retrieval delivered where inference was wanted. The third is unfinished papers, where the final task is short or missing, and the marks lost there typically exceed anything language work would have recovered in the same period. Both are technique, both move in weeks, and both are frequently misread as evidence that the student's English is not good enough.

The fourth cause is genuine: the range is the ceiling. The student completes the tasks, performs the right operations, finishes the paper, and the writing is accurate within a narrow band of vocabulary and sentence patterns. This is the honest case where progress is slow, and the correct response is to say so, keep the range work going, and bank the technique and accuracy marks that remain available. What it is not is a reason to buy more intensity, because intensity does not accelerate language acquisition and the student's confidence is a resource worth protecting.

Wrong operation in reading: retrieval given where inference was asked

sections.heading: Where the grade is used: sixth form, equivalency and university English
paragraphs: A 4EB1 grade is read in three different places with three different thresholds, and families often aim at the wrong one. Settling which applies changes the target and therefore the plan, and all three answers are obtainable for free before any tutoring is bought.

The first is sixth-form entry, set by the individual school. Dubai sixth forms split between A Level and IB Diploma and publish their own English requirements, which sometimes distinguish between the first-language and additional-language qualifications and sometimes do not. Email the admissions lead naming your child's intended subjects and ask directly. A written answer removes a term of speculation.

The second is Ministry of Education equivalency, which matters for recognition of the certificate in the UAE. The published requirement for the British track is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. How a specific certificate is counted is a decision for the Ministry and the attestation authority. Verify on moe.gov.ae or with the school registrar; IB Gram does not perform, guarantee or influence equivalency, and tutoring is not required for it.

The third is university English proficiency, which frequently asks for a separate test rather than a school qualification. The published MoE guidance for the American track, for instance, sets English proficiency at a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT. A family planning towards a university that wants a test score should know that early, because test preparation and 4EB1 preparation overlap only partly and competing for the same hours is a real risk.

sections.heading: Arabic alongside English: the mandatory-subject load on an additional-language learner
paragraphs: A 4EB1 student in a Dubai private school is not learning one additional language, in most cases. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements on this were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. That is a real weekly load, and any English plan has to fit the time that remains rather than an imaginary empty evening.

The structure is specific. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies.

KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should be at least twenty-five minutes. For the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, which is a genuine constraint on how any Arabic or Islamic Education support can be described. Schools must also ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

The practical consequence for an English plan is scheduling honesty. A student carrying mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education alongside a full international curriculum and an additional-language English qualification has a demanding week, and a tuition plan that assumes two free weekday evenings will be abandoned by October. One held slot that survives the year produces more measurable progress than three that collapse in November, which is the practical argument for a format that travels and a cadence the family can actually sustain.
