sections.heading: Pearson series, entry, and how 4PM1 lessons run for Dubai families
paragraphs: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year, and 4PM1 follows the same pattern. The published reference points are worth knowing for planning: the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also issues provisional timetables that are subject to revision, so the live official timetable is the only one to plan against.

Entry is made by the centre, which matters more for 4PM1 than for mainstream subjects because not every Dubai school will enter a candidate for a syllabus it does not teach. That conversation needs to happen early, in writing, with the maths department and the examinations officer, and it needs to cover both willingness and the deadline. A family who assumes entry is a formality and discovers otherwise in February has lost the year.

Sessions for Dubai families are delivered one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with slots moved to post-Iftar timing through Ramadan. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service it runs only in India. For 4PM1 this costs almost nothing, because the work is a shared workspace: the candidate writes, the tutor watches each line appear, and a correction on an identity proof lands at the step where the argument broke rather than at the end.

What the format buys is availability of the right person. 4PM1 is a minority entry, and a tutor who teaches it regularly is a narrow specialism within a narrow specialism. Selecting by driving distance from Tilal Al Ghaf or Al Khawaneej is an unpromising way to find somebody who marks integration and identity questions every week. The first lesson is free, with no card details, and the best use of it is a real 4PM1 question rather than a conversation about one.

process.title: Establish whether the school teaches and will enter 4PM1
process.description: Two separate questions, both for the maths department in writing: is Further Pure Maths taught as a set, and will the centre enter a candidate who is studying it outside the timetable. Also ask for the entry deadline. A family who assumes entry is automatic can lose a whole year to that assumption.

process.title: Sit a timed Higher 4MA1 paper
process.description: The readiness evidence that matters most. Not a 4PM1 paper first, because a candidate who has not been taught the content cannot show anything useful. What the 4MA1 paper reveals is algebraic stamina: whether the candidate finishes early with marks to spare, which is what 4PM1 consumes.

process.title: Attempt a real 4PM1 question set
process.description: On material the candidate has actually been taught, marked against the published scheme. The point is not the score but how they behave: whether they attempt an identity by demonstration or by substitution, whether the constant of integration appears, whether the calculator mode was checked.

process.title: Take the free first lesson on a real question
process.description: One hour, no card details, spent working through a genuine 4PM1 problem rather than discussing the syllabus. The candidate will discover within twenty minutes whether this feels like interesting difficulty or like drowning, and that reaction is better evidence than any assessment.

process.title: Get a written recommendation, including no
process.description: The output of the readiness work is a recommendation with the marked evidence attached. Sometimes it is that the candidate should secure a grade 9 on 4MA1 and read ahead into A Level content instead. That is a legitimate result of paying for advice, and nobody is pushed towards an entry.

process.title: Agree a coverage plan with a halfway checkpoint
process.description: If the decision is to proceed without a taught set, the plan is written down before the first paid session: which of the ten areas when, two sessions a week, and a date at the midpoint where the family and tutor decide honestly whether to continue to entry or withdraw.

whyPoints.title: Planned against the 4PM1 specification itself
whyPoints.description: Further Pure Maths is not a harder version of 4MA1 and cannot be taught from a general further maths scheme. Sessions work to the ten content areas in the Pearson specification, with the overlap and the genuinely new material separated, so paid hours go where the department runs shortest of time.

whyPoints.title: Integration and radians taught from first principles
whyPoints.description: The two areas a candidate meets cold are also the two most often taught as recipes. Integration is built as the reverse of differentiation so the constant is understood rather than remembered, and radian work includes a rehearsed calculator-mode check, because that single setting can cost every mark in a question.

whyPoints.title: Identity proof treated as its own skill
whyPoints.description: A candidate trained by 4MA1 to find a number will try to solve an identity or verify it by substitution, neither of which earns anything. Working one side towards the other with every step defensible is a technique, and it is taught and drilled rather than assumed.

whyPoints.title: An honest answer on whether to enter
whyPoints.description: 4PM1 is untiered, so there is no lower paper to fall back on and the entry decision carries real consequence. Readiness is assessed from a marked timed 4MA1 paper and a real 4PM1 question set, and the written recommendation is sometimes not to enter. Nobody is sold a second syllabus to fill a timetable.

whyPoints.title: Realistic about self-study
whyPoints.description: Covering ten content areas outside the school timetable needs two sessions a week for most of a year plus genuine independent problem work. That is stated before any money is taken, with a written coverage plan and a halfway checkpoint at which withdrawing is a respectable decision.

whyPoints.title: No guarantees, every date checkable
whyPoints.description: No grade is promised and no statistic appears without a source. Pearson dates come from Pearson's own published pages and must be confirmed against the live official timetable. IB Gram is independent, holds no board or regulator approval, and operates no office or centre in the UAE.

faqs.question: What is Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1?
faqs.answer: An additional maths qualification taken alongside a mainstream IGCSE rather than instead of one, commonly assessed by two equally weighted written papers with a calculator permitted. It is untiered, so every candidate sits the same papers and the full grade range is available. The specification covers logarithmic functions and indices, the quadratic function, identities and inequalities, graphs, series, the binomial series, scalar and vector quantities, coordinate geometry, calculus and trigonometry. Confirm the assessment detail and content list against the 4PM1 specification on qualifications.pearson.com for your centre's version.

faqs.question: Is 4PM1 tiered in the same way as 4MA1?
faqs.answer: No, and that difference matters. 4MA1 splits into Foundation and Higher entries with different papers and different grade ceilings, so a candidate can be entered at a level that suits them. 4PM1 is a single untiered entry: every candidate sits the same papers and there is no lower alternative to fall back on. A candidate who is not ready sits exactly the same assessment as one who is. That is why the entry decision deserves marked evidence rather than encouragement, and why some honest recommendations are not to enter.

faqs.question: Which 4PM1 topics have no equivalent in Higher 4MA1?
faqs.answer: Integration, radian measure with the associated arc length and sector area work, the binomial series, fluent use of the laws of logarithms to solve equations with the unknown in an exponent, and identity proof as a task. Roughly two thirds of the specification extends material a Higher 4MA1 candidate has met, including quadratics, graphs, coordinate geometry, vectors, differentiation and the sine and cosine rules. The remaining third is new ground, and it is where paid hours earn the most because departments also tend to reach it last.

faqs.question: Does 4PM1 include integration as well as differentiation?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the topic most candidates meet completely cold, since Higher 4MA1 covers differentiation of polynomials and no integration at all. 4PM1 requires indefinite and definite integration and areas under curves. The usual difficulties are conceptual rather than technical: understanding that the reversal of differentiation is not unique, which is what the constant of integration represents, and rewriting terms into an integrable form, which stalls candidates who are shaky on index laws rather than on integration itself.

faqs.question: Do 4PM1 candidates have to work in radians?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a habit change rather than a difficult idea. An angle measured as arc length over radius takes ten minutes to understand and months to become instinctive after four years of degrees. The practical risk is the calculator: a question answered with the machine in degree mode produces a sequence of plausible wrong numbers with correct method and no partial credit route out. A rehearsed mode check before every trigonometric question, practised under timing until automatic, is the only reliable fix.

faqs.question: How much harder is 4PM1 than Higher 4MA1?
faqs.answer: It is a different kind of demand rather than simply a steeper one. 4MA1 rewards a correct answer with method shown; 4PM1 rewards a defensible argument, so identity proofs and multi-stage calculus problems penalise a gap in the middle of otherwise correct work. It also assumes algebraic stamina: most questions need several lines of confident manipulation before the examinable idea is reached. Candidates who were scoring top marks on 4MA1 through hard work rather than fluency often find the first 4PM1 paper genuinely alarming.

faqs.question: Which Dubai schools actually teach 4PM1?
faqs.answer: A minority, typically the larger British-curriculum centres with an International A Level sixth form and a maths department big enough to staff an additional set. It is not something a parent can establish from a prospectus, so ask the department directly: whether Further Pure Maths runs as a timetabled set, and whether the centre will enter a candidate studying it outside the timetable. Those are two separate questions with two separate answers, and both need to be settled before any entry deadline rather than after one.

faqs.question: Can my child self-study 4PM1 if the school does not teach it?
faqs.answer: It is possible for a genuinely fluent candidate and a poor idea for a borderline one. Covering all ten content areas outside the timetable realistically needs two sessions a week for most of a year plus substantial independent problem work, alongside nine other subjects in a Year 11 timetable. Before starting, agree a written coverage plan and a midpoint checkpoint at which continuing to entry or withdrawing are both acceptable outcomes. Also confirm in writing that the centre is willing to enter the candidate at all.

faqs.question: Where do 4PM1 candidates most often lose marks?
faqs.answer: Five places, and none of them is a knowledge gap. Treating an identity as something to solve or verify by substitution rather than demonstrate. Omitting the constant of integration, which also breaks any boundary-condition work that follows. Leaving the calculator in degree mode for a radian question. Running out of time because the algebra was correct but slow. And computing correctly without stating the conclusion the question asked for, such as classifying a stationary point rather than just finding the second derivative.

faqs.question: Does 4PM1 genuinely help with International A Level Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is where most of its value sits. Integration, radians, trigonometric identities, series and the binomial expansion all reappear in the first pure units, so a candidate who met them at sixteen meets them again at seventeen having already made the conceptual leap. For International A Level Further Mathematics the effect is larger, because that course assumes a starting fluency a standard IGCSE does not build. Ask which specification your intended Dubai sixth form runs, since the modular route brings the first assessment forward.

faqs.question: Is 4PM1 useful preparation for IB Maths Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Arguably it is the strongest case for taking it. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is proof-heavy and calculus-heavy from early on, and candidates arriving from a standard IGCSE usually meet radians, integration and identity manipulation in the same term as five other Diploma subjects, an extended essay and theory of knowledge. A 4PM1 candidate has met each of those once already. For a candidate at a British-curriculum school intending to move to an IB sixth form at sixteen, the timing works out particularly well.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does 4PM1 realistically need?
faqs.answer: Where the school teaches it, one tutored hour a week on the new third of the specification is usually enough, concentrated on integration, radians, identities and the binomial series, with independent problem work in between. Where the school does not teach it, two sessions a week for most of a year is the realistic minimum and independent practice is not optional. Anyone quoting a smaller number for full self-study delivery has not looked at the ten content areas against a Year 11 timetable.

faqs.question: Does a 4PM1 grade matter to universities?
faqs.answer: As a credential, comparatively little. No admissions process treats it as a requirement, and a candidate presenting a grade 9 on their mainstream maths IGCSE is not disadvantaged against one presenting that plus 4PM1. Its value is preparation for a demanding sixth-form course rather than the certificate itself. The corollary matters too: a weak 4PM1 grade sitting beside a modest mainstream grade tells an admissions reader something unhelpful, which is an argument for only entering a candidate who is ready.

faqs.question: Can 4PM1 be sat in the November Pearson series?
faqs.answer: Pearson makes International GCSE available in May/June and November each year, and the published reference points include a November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. Whether a particular Dubai centre enters 4PM1 in November is a separate question for the examinations officer, since a minority entry is not always offered in both series. Confirm all dates against the live official timetable on qualifications.pearson.com rather than a search result.

faqs.question: Does 4PM1 count towards the five subjects the Ministry of Education requires?
faqs.answer: For the British track the Ministry requires five subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one subject at Advanced Level at E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the count of five. A Further Pure Maths certificate is an IGCSE subject like any other for that purpose. Verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority. IB Gram does not perform equivalency and tutoring is not required for it.

faqs.question: How does an identity proof get taught over live video?
faqs.answer: Through a shared workspace, which suits proof better than most things. The candidate writes each line and the tutor watches it appear, so an intervention lands at the step where the argument broke rather than after the conclusion is already wrong. That is exactly what proof teaching requires: catching the move where a candidate started working on both sides at once, or substituted a value instead of demonstrating. Lessons for Dubai families run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; nobody is sent to a UAE address.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-further-pure-maths-4.closingHeading: Start with whether, not with how
dubai/edexcel-igcse-further-pure-maths-4.closingBody: The right first step with Edexcel IGCSE Further Pure Maths 4PM1 in Dubai is not booking a term of lessons. It is establishing two things: whether the school teaches and will enter the syllabus, and whether the candidate is ready for an untiered paper with no fallback. One timed Higher 4MA1 paper and one real 4PM1 question set, both marked against the published schemes, answers the second question in a fortnight. The free first hour is spent on a genuine 4PM1 problem, because twenty minutes of real work tells a candidate more than any conversation. Lessons run one-to-one over live video.

intro.heading: The honest answer to a home tutor search, before anything is sold
paragraphs: An Edexcel IGCSE Geography 4GE1 home tutor in Dubai is a real thing you can buy. Independent tutors advertise visits across the city, agencies place them, and rates published by UAE providers in 2026 put in-home one-to-one work in a band of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour depending on the tutor's experience and the distance travelled. If the deciding factor for your family is that somebody physically arrives, that market exists and you should use it with your eyes open about what the premium buys.

What the premium mostly buys is travel. A tutor crossing Dubai at six in the evening is pricing the journey into the hour, and the practical consequence is a smaller pool of available people, less flexibility when a fixture or a work trip moves, and a tendency for the slot to drift later in the exam term when traffic is worst. For a subject like geography, where the useful work is reading a marked script and rewriting an answer side by side, none of that travel is doing anything for the teaching.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai. Home visits are a service we run only in India. For UAE families, tuition is delivered one to one, online, over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. That is a deliberate position rather than a limitation, and the reason is specification coverage: 4GE1 schools choose which specification topics they teach, so the tutor who has actually taught your child's entered topics is rarely the tutor who lives twenty minutes away. Over video, proximity stops being a filter.

The rest of this page is written for a parent comparing options on cost and logistics rather than on syllabus detail. It prices the Dubai market model by model with the sources named, shows what the same budget buys online against in-home, explains how to verify that a tutor is legally permitted to tutor in the UAE, sets out what evidence should arrive each month so you can judge whether the money is working, and puts the cost in context against school fees in a year when KHDA has confirmed no fee increase for 2026-27.

One thing this page will not do is quote a price for IB Gram in AED and call it the market rate. Every figure below is attributed to the published source it came from and dated, because a tutoring page that presents its own pricing as market research is not research. Three of the six best-ranking Dubai tutoring pages publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not a currency a Dubai household transacts in, so the bare numbers below are worth more than the prose around them. Our own commercial answer is a first session at no charge, one per student, after which you decide, and the decision should rest on the written diagnosis that session produces rather than on anything written here.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges, model by model, with the sources named
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking tutoring pages for Dubai searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family transacts in. So here is the AED picture assembled from rates that providers and rate-trackers published themselves and that we read in October 2026. Treat every band as the market, not as our price list, and treat the top of each band as the number a tutor quotes in March rather than in September.

The pattern across the sources is consistent. Budget online provision, typically a university student or a generalist, advertises from roughly AED 33 to 150 an hour. Qualified subject tutors working online sit at roughly AED 150 to 300. In-home one-to-one, with travel priced in, runs about AED 180 to 500. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level provision is quoted around AED 200 to 450 and above, and premium named or examiner-branded provision has been published as high as AED 650. Monthly figures published for weekly one-hour sessions run from about AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support.

For 4GE1 specifically, two adjustments apply. Humanities subjects generally sit below maths and sciences within each band, so a geography quote tends to land in the lower half of whichever tier the tutor belongs to. Against that, specification-specific experience is scarcer in humanities than families expect, because the entered-topic variation between schools is wider, so a genuinely matched 4GE1 tutor prices like a specialist rather than like a general humanities tutor. The useful question is not which tier is cheapest. It is which tier can mark a long evaluative answer against the levels descriptors.

sections.heading: What travel does to the hour you are paying for
paragraphs: The in-home premium is not a quality premium. It is a travel premium, and it is worth seeing it broken down, because the parts a family never sees on the invoice are the parts that decide whether the arrangement survives to half term. A tutor driving from Al Barsha to Town Square at six in the evening is committing well over an hour to a sixty-minute lesson. That commitment has to be priced, and it is priced inside the hourly rate rather than as a line item.

The second cost is optionality. A tutor who will travel to your community at your hour is a much smaller set than a tutor who has taught your child's entered 4GE1 topics. Families usually discover this at the point where the first match is not working: replacing an in-home tutor mid-term means restarting the search within the same narrow radius, while replacing an online tutor means choosing from everyone available at that hour. For a subject where entered-topic experience is the thing that matters, that is the whole argument.

The third is drift. Visits start late when traffic is heavy, and the heaviest traffic coincides with the exam term. Access procedures in gated communities absorb minutes at the start, and a tutor with a second student across town absorbs minutes at the end. None of those minutes teach anything. A screen share that opens at the agreed minute and spends the full hour on a marked script is not a compromise against a visit; for this subject it is a straightforwardly better use of the same money.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to tutor in the UAE, and how do you check?
paragraphs: This is the question the in-home market makes most urgent and the one almost nobody in the Dubai tutoring SERP answers. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and MoHRE's own service page for it is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system with a two-working-day completion time. The permit is granted free of charge for two years.

Eligibility is broader than families assume. It covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so if you see a specific amount quoted on a tutoring site, that amount is not sourced from the ministry.

Two further rules matter for an in-home arrangement. A school teacher tutoring their own enrolled students is a problem rather than a shortcut: Abu Dhabi's ADEK ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the permit carries a code of conduct that also addresses serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Separately, a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram holds none of these as endorsements and claims none; the permit question is about the individual you are inviting to teach your child.

sections.heading: The tutor pool problem nobody mentions in a home tutor quote
paragraphs: 4GE1 schools choose which specification topics they teach. That single fact is what breaks a proximity-based tutor search for this subject. A tutor can be an excellent geographer, have taught IGCSE for a decade, and still not have taught the combination of physical and human environments your child's school entered. In sciences this matters less, because the content is largely fixed. In geography it decides whether the first month is teaching or orientation.

Run the numbers in your head. The set of geography tutors in Dubai is already modest. Narrow it to those with Edexcel rather than Cambridge experience, then to those who have taught the entered topics, then to those free at seven on a Tuesday. Now narrow it again to those willing to drive to your community. The last filter is the one with no educational value at all, and it is usually the one that removes the specialist. Families who insist on it generally end up with a competent generalist and describe the result as fine rather than useful.

Online delivery drops that last filter. It also makes a mid-term change survivable, which matters more than parents expect: a wrong match discovered in week three costs three weeks if the tutor can be replaced from the same hour's availability, and costs a term if the replacement has to live nearby. We will say plainly when no entered-topic specialist is free at your hour, and offer either a different hour or a tutor who states clearly which topics they have and have not taught. What we will not do is present a general humanities tutor as a 4GE1 specialist.

sections.heading: Evidence: how a Dubai parent judges whether the money is working
paragraphs: The weakness of in-home tutoring as a product is not the teaching. It is the reporting. A tutor leaves, your child says it went well, and four months later the report arrives. Nothing in that loop lets a parent decide in week six whether to continue. So the test to apply to any provider, including this one, is simple: what arrives in writing, how often, and does it contain a number you can compare to last month's number.

For a written subject like geography, the comparable numbers are available and specific. The mark and the band of the long answer attempted each week. The timing log from a full paper, question by question. The count of case studies rebuilt to template and dated. The ranked list of question types by marks lost, revisited at half term. Four quantities, all of them produced as a by-product of the teaching rather than as extra administration, and all of them visible to a parent who does not teach geography.

What we do not report is a satisfaction score, a percentile or a predicted grade, because none of those can be evidenced on a single student's work and all of them appear on competitor pages without a sample size, a date or a method. If a provider shows you a figure like that, ask how many students it covers and when it was measured. The absence of an answer is the answer, and it tells you something about everything else on the page too.

sections.heading: Putting the cost in context against Dubai school fees
paragraphs: Tutoring is a second education bill in a city where the first one is already substantial. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with UK curriculum schools accounting for 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian 26 per cent, US 14 per cent and International Baccalaureate 7 per cent. Against that, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package.

That fee freeze is the right anchor for a tutoring decision this year, because it means the household education budget is not moving underneath you. A family deciding whether to add a weekly geography slot is making a marginal decision against a fixed base rather than a rising one. Published monthly figures for weekly one-hour sessions run from roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end up to AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support, so the honest range for a year of 4GE1 support is wide and depends almost entirely on which tier you buy and when you start.

The sequencing advice follows from the numbers rather than from sales logic. Start earlier in the academic year, when rates and slots are both softer. Buy one subject properly rather than three approximately. Front-load the diagnosis, because the first session is what tells you whether this is a technique problem solvable in a term or a content problem that needs longer. And treat the exam-term intensive as a top-up on work already done, not as the plan, because the published premium for late starts is real and the available improvement is smaller.

sections.heading: Scheduling around the Dubai school run, activities and Ramadan
paragraphs: Most Dubai private schools run Monday to Friday with a lighter Friday, so the realistic slots for a Year 10 or Year 11 are weekday evenings between five and eight, and Saturday mornings. Those are also the hours the in-home market is most constrained, because a visiting tutor can serve at most two or three households in an evening and is competing with traffic to do it. The scheduling advantage of online delivery is unglamorous and decisive: the slot you agree is the slot that happens, including in the weeks when the roads do not cooperate.

Build the plan around the school's assessment calendar rather than around the exam date alone. Mock weeks and internal assessment weeks are not revision weeks, and a schedule that assumes they are slips by a fortnight before half term. School trips, sports fixtures and music commitments move more often in Dubai than families admit when the plan is drawn up in September, which is the argument for a fixed weekly slot plus one written task between sessions rather than occasional long blocks.

Ramadan shifts the working day across the UAE, and families routinely move tuition to post-Iftar slots for the month. That works well for a written subject if it is planned in week one of the term rather than improvised in the week itself, because the whole family's evening rhythm changes at once. If the exam term and Ramadan overlap in a given year, decide in advance which weeks are for timed practice and which are for lighter consolidation, and accept that the timed papers should sit outside the heaviest weeks.

Treat mock weeks as assessment weeks, not revision weeks
Plan post-Iftar timing for Ramadan in advance, not in the week
One short written task between sessions is what makes the hour compound

sections.heading: What a first session has to produce before you spend anything
paragraphs: A free first session is only worth having if it produces a document. Ours is one session per student at no charge, and the deliverable is a written diagnosis: the question types ranked by marks lost, one long answer annotated against the levels descriptors, and a statement of which two specification topics should get the deep work. If a provider offers a trial that produces nothing in writing, you have had a sales call with a teacher present.

Before that session, send two things: the last marked geography paper or long answer, and the most recent school report comment on geography. Two documents are enough to separate four different problems that look identical from the outside, namely missing content, misread command words, poor time budgeting and an unusable case-study bank. The remedies for those four are completely different, and buying tuition before you know which one you have is how families end up paying for general revision.

After the session, the decision should be concrete. A weekly slot, a fortnightly rhythm with longer written tasks, or no tuition at all, which is sometimes the right answer and is a thing we say. If the match between tutor and student is wrong, we propose a different tutor rather than defending the first one, and the slot is not tied to a package you have to exit. The point of attaching the diagnosis to the first hour is that you can judge the rest of the arrangement on evidence you already hold.

process.description: The last marked geography answer plus the school's latest report line. Those two documents separate a content problem from a command word problem from a timing problem, which is the distinction that decides whether you need a term of teaching or four sessions of technique.

process.description: Which 4GE1 specification topics were entered and which exam series the student is sitting. One email to the humanities lead. Without it, any tutor is partly guessing, and in a subject with school-chosen topics that guess is expensive.

process.description: One session per student at no charge, ending in a written ranking of question types by marks lost and one annotated long answer. Judge the provider on that document rather than on the conversation, and compare it to what any other quote offers before it is paid.

process.description: Long-answer band, timing log, dated case studies, and the ranked question-type list. If the top item from the first session has not moved, the plan changes or the tutoring stops. Those are the only two honest options.

faqs.question: Can we book a home tutor for Edexcel IGCSE Geography 4GE1 in Dubai?
faqs.answer: You can buy in-home geography tuition in Dubai from independent tutors and from agencies that place them, at published rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour. IB Gram is not one of those providers: we do not offer home visits in Dubai or elsewhere in the UAE, and home visits are a service we run only in India. What we deliver to Dubai families is one-to-one online tuition over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. For 4GE1 specifically that trade is favourable, because the tutor can be chosen for entered-topic experience rather than for driving distance.

faqs.question: What does an in-home geography tutor charge per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published UAE rates read in October 2026 put in-home one-to-one tuition at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions advertised between AED 1,599 and 1,799. Humanities subjects usually sit in the lower half of whichever band a tutor belongs to, so a general geography visit tends to be quoted nearer the bottom of that range and a specification specialist nearer the top. Those are market figures from providers and rate trackers, not an IB Gram price, and the top of each band is what gets quoted once the spring term starts.

faqs.question: Is the travel time included in a Dubai home tutor's hourly rate?
faqs.answer: Almost always, and that is the point parents miss. A tutor driving from one side of Dubai to another at six in the evening commits well over an hour to a sixty-minute lesson, and that commitment is priced inside the hourly figure rather than itemised. You also pay in minutes: gated access, tower parking and a second student across town absorb time at both ends of the visit. Ask any in-home quote two questions, namely where the tutor is travelling from and what happens to the lesson when traffic is bad.

faqs.question: Does an online geography session really work as well as a tutor at the kitchen table?
faqs.answer: For this subject the honest answer is that it works better, because the work that moves a 4GE1 grade is reading a marked script against a mark scheme and rewriting an answer. On a screen share both people see the same annotation at the same time, which is awkward with one paper copy between two heads. The in-home format wins on two genuine things: a young or easily distracted student, and a household that wants a visible adult presence. Neither of those is about geography, and both are legitimate reasons to choose differently.

faqs.question: What should a Dubai family budget each month for 4GE1 geography support?
faqs.answer: Published monthly figures for weekly one-hour sessions run from roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 for mid-tier provision, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. For geography, a realistic plan is one weekly session through the year at mid-tier rates, with a denser block in the final eight to twelve weeks. Starting in September costs less per hour than starting in March and gives a better choice of slot, because Year 11 demand across Dubai arrives all at once after the winter break.

faqs.question: Are tutoring fees in Dubai quoted with VAT included or added?
faqs.answer: Ask, and get the answer in writing before the first invoice. We will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition as a general rule here, because that is a Federal Tax Authority question and tutoring pages that assert it are guessing. What a parent can reasonably require is that any quoted AED figure states whether it is inclusive or exclusive, and that a provider charging VAT shows a tax registration number. The market bands cited on this page are the figures providers published; whether each is inclusive is not consistently stated by those sources.

faqs.question: How do I check that a geography tutor is permitted to work in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask directly about the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service through its smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time. Eligibility covers school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine amounts are published, so ignore any figure quoted online.

faqs.question: Can my child's own geography teacher tutor them privately in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a boundary to avoid rather than a shortcut to arrange. The private tuition permit carries a code of conduct addressing tutors serving students affiliated with their own school, and in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school. Beyond the rules, the arrangement is bad for the student: the person marking the school assessment should not also be the person paid to prepare them for it. Ask for a tutor with no connection to your child's school.

faqs.question: Why is it hard to find a 4GE1 geography specialist near our community?
faqs.answer: Because 4GE1 schools choose which specification topics they teach, so the useful tutor is not the nearest geographer but the one who has taught your child's entered combination. Filtering an already modest pool by Edexcel rather than Cambridge experience, then by entered topics, then by your available hour, leaves a small set. Adding a willingness to drive to your community removes most of what is left, and that last filter does nothing for the teaching. This is the main reason we deliver 4GE1 online rather than by visit.

faqs.question: What written evidence should arrive after each paid session?
faqs.answer: Four things, cumulatively: the annotated long answer with its mark and band, a per-question timing log whenever a full paper is sat, the count of case studies rebuilt to template and dated, and a ranked list of question types by marks lost that gets revisited at half term. All four are by-products of the teaching, so no provider needs extra administration to produce them. If what arrives instead is a satisfaction rating or a predicted grade, ask how many students it covers and when it was measured.

faqs.question: Does it cost more to start geography tutoring in the exam term?
faqs.answer: Yes, in two currencies. Rates harden from January as Year 11 demand across Dubai arrives at once, and the specialists with entered-topic experience fill their evening slots first, so the money buys a narrower choice. The second cost is the available improvement: technique work on command words and time budgeting still pays in eight weeks, but rebuilding a case-study bank and closing content gaps does not compress well. Starting in the autumn is cheaper per hour and materially more useful per hour.

faqs.question: Is a small group class a reasonable way to save money on geography?
faqs.answer: For content coverage, yes, and the per-hour cost is the lowest of the three formats, with online monthly packages of eight sessions advertised from around AED 799. For the long evaluative questions, no. Those marks come from individual marking against levels descriptors and from rewriting one answer properly, which a group format cannot give every student in the time available. A workable compromise is group teaching for content with occasional one-to-one sessions bought specifically for long-answer marking.

faqs.question: Do Dubai school fees and tutoring costs both rise every year?
faqs.answer: Not this year on the school side. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. Tutoring is a separate, unregulated market and moves with demand rather than with policy, which is why the same tutor quotes differently in September and in March. For a household planning a year of geography support, the useful consequence is that the base education bill is fixed, so the tutoring decision is a marginal one against a stable number.

faqs.question: What happens if the first tutor is not the right match for our child?
faqs.answer: Say so early and we propose a different tutor from the same hour's availability, without restarting the search. That is the structural advantage of online delivery over an in-home arrangement: replacing a visiting tutor means finding another person willing to drive to your community at your hour, which can cost a term. We would rather be told in week two than discover it in a half-term review. There is no package to exit, and the written diagnosis from the first session transfers to whoever takes over.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-geography-4ge1-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work on Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Geography and the humanities subjects that sit beside it. Each one marks to the published mark scheme first and teaches second, because a 4GE1 script tells you more in ten minutes than a term of lesson observation.

intro.heading: Geography is a writing subject with a mark scheme, and that is where the marks go
paragraphs: Parents searching for an Edexcel IGCSE Geography 4GE1 tutor in Dubai almost always describe the same pattern. The child enjoys the subject, can talk fluently about flooding or urban growth, revises the topic booklets the school hands out, and then comes home with a score in the middle of the paper. Nothing in that description is a knowledge problem. The 4GE1 papers are marked by tariff and by command word, and a student who answers a nine-mark question in the style of a four-mark question will lose five marks while writing something entirely correct.

That is the uncomfortable part of this subject and the reason it responds quickly to the right kind of help. A physics misconception takes weeks to unpick. A geography student who has never been shown what the word assess requires, or who has never seen a levels-marked answer annotated line by line, can move a grade in a term because the content is already in their head. The work is in the shape of the answer: a named example with a date, a figure quoted from the resource booklet, a consequence traced two steps rather than one, and a judgement that actually appears in the final sentence.

IB Gram delivers this as one-to-one online tuition over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Dubai address, and home visits are a service we run only in India. For a subject like geography that is not a compromise. A Dubai family gets a tutor who has marked hundreds of 4GE1 scripts rather than whichever humanities graduate happens to live near Arabian Ranches, and the screen share means the child's own script, the mark scheme and the resource booklet sit side by side where both of you can see them.

Dubai also shapes the practical side of this. KHDA inspects private schools in the emirate annually on a six-band scale, and British-curriculum schools dominate the market by enrolment, which means most Dubai students meet 4GE1 in Year 10 after an MYP or Key Stage 3 programme that did not ask for extended evaluative writing. Alongside that, KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in every private school regardless of the licensed curriculum, so a Year 11 timetable in Dubai carries more compulsory subjects than the equivalent timetable in the UK. Geography is frequently the subject whose independent study time disappears.

What this page does is set out what 4GE1 actually assesses, where the marks are lost question type by question type, what a Dubai student can realistically use as a case study, what the Geographical Investigation permits a tutor to do, and how to count a revision plan backwards from the written papers. If you read nothing else, read the mark tariff table and the command word section. Those two blocks explain most mid-paper geography grades in this city.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-geography-4ge1-tutor.programmesIntro: Most Dubai students arrive at 4GE1 from one of three routes, and the route changes what the first month of tuition has to cover. The gap is rarely the same gap twice.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Geography (4GE1)
programmes.description: A two-year course examined by two written papers, one on physical environments and one on human environments, each sat with a resource booklet of figures, maps, graphs and photographs. Question tariffs run from one mark up to the long evaluative questions, which are marked in levels rather than by points. The Geographical Investigation element rewards a student who can describe a method, defend a sampling choice and admit a limitation.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, 4GE1 is normally taught across Years 10 and 11 in British-curriculum schools licensed by KHDA, with the written papers sat in the June series and a smaller number of students entered in November. Schools choose which specification topics they teach, so two Dubai students in the same community can sit genuinely different combinations. Ask the humanities lead which topics were entered before buying any tuition.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Geography (0460/0976)
programmes.description: The other IGCSE geography route taught in the UAE. It shares much of the physical and human content with 4GE1 but differs in paper structure, in how fieldwork is assessed and in the house style of its command words. A student who revises from Cambridge resources for an Edexcel paper usually writes competent geography in the wrong format.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools switched board at some point in the past decade, which leaves older sibling notes and second-hand revision guides circulating in the wrong format. If your child's folder says 0460 anywhere on it and the entry is 4GE1, the first session is spent separating what transfers from what misleads. Both boards publish their specifications openly; check the code on the exam entry slip, not the textbook cover.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme, Individuals and Societies
programmes.description: The route many Dubai students take before an IGCSE or Diploma humanities course. MYP assesses against criteria A to D and rewards inquiry, conceptual framing and reflection. It does not train a student to answer a tightly tariffed exam question against the clock, which is the single biggest adjustment when a student transfers into a 4GE1 class mid-course.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai has a large MYP population because the emirate's IB sector is substantial, and movement between IB and British schools inside the city is common at the end of Year 9. A student arriving into Year 10 geography from MYP typically writes too much, structures by inquiry question rather than by command word, and has never been shown a levels mark scheme. That is a six-week adjustment, not a crisis.

programmes.name: Where 4GE1 geography leads next
programmes.description: A strong IGCSE geography grade feeds A Level Geography, IB Diploma Geography and IB Environmental Systems and Societies. Each of those raises the evaluative demand sharply: the Diploma expects synthesis across units, and A Level expects independent investigation. The habits built for the long 4GE1 questions are the habits those courses assume you already have.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Year 11 students usually choose between A Level and the IB Diploma in the spring term, and geography is one of the subjects where the two routes feel most different. Students who found the long evaluative questions in 4GE1 the most satisfying part of the course tend to settle better into Diploma Geography; those who preferred the map and data work often prefer A Level. Neither route needs tutoring to be chosen well.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-geography-4ge1-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the specification areas a 4GE1 candidate may meet, with what each one actually assesses. Your child's school will have entered a subset. The skills rows at the end apply to every entry.

subjects.name: River Environments
subjects.description: Drainage basin processes, channel landforms, hydrographs and flood management. Marks are lost on hydrograph interpretation, where students describe the shape of the curve instead of explaining the catchment characteristic that produced it, and on flood schemes answered without a named river and a date.

subjects.name: Coastal Environments
subjects.description: Wave processes, erosional and depositional landforms, coastal management and conflict between users. The recurring error is sequencing: a landform explanation that names three processes without ordering them in time scores in the lower band however accurate the vocabulary.

subjects.name: Hazardous Environments
subjects.description: Tectonic and tropical storm hazards, vulnerability, prediction and response. The strongest answers separate hazard from disaster and tie impact to the level of development of the place named. Weak answers list impacts for a generic earthquake with no country, no year and no magnitude.

subjects.name: Economic Activity and Energy
subjects.description: Employment structure, sectoral shift, energy supply and demand, and the environmental cost of extraction. Students in the Gulf often know the energy content well and still lose marks by writing about the region generally instead of answering with the figures in front of them in the resource booklet.

subjects.name: Rural Environments
subjects.description: Rural change, agricultural systems, depopulation and rural-urban migration drivers. Marks go missing where a student explains migration only from the push side. The mark scheme usually wants both pull and push, and a specific place where each applies.

subjects.name: Urban Environments
subjects.description: Urban growth, land use patterns, informal settlements and sustainable city management. This is the topic where Dubai students have the most usable local material and the least practice at using it precisely, which is a fixable problem rather than a knowledge gap.

subjects.name: Fragile Environments
subjects.description: Desertification, deforestation, climate change and management of fragile ecosystems. Answers need a mechanism, not a label: explaining how overgrazing reduces infiltration and raises surface runoff scores where naming overgrazing as a cause does not.

subjects.name: Globalisation and Migration
subjects.description: Transnational corporations, trade, aid, interdependence and migration flows. The command words here are often evaluate or assess, which means the final paragraph must contain a judgement supported by something earlier in the answer rather than a summary of both sides.

subjects.name: The Geographical Investigation
subjects.description: Hypothesis framing, sampling, data collection, presentation technique, analysis and evaluation of method. Examiners reward a student who can justify why a sampling strategy suited the question and name one specific weakness in their own data, which is the opposite of the confident write-up students are tempted to produce.

subjects.name: Resource booklet and map skills
subjects.description: Grid references, cross sections, proportional symbols, choropleth reading, scattergraph interpretation and quoting data accurately. These are low-tariff, high-frequency marks. A student who practises them for twenty minutes a week usually gains more than one who rereads a topic booklet for two hours.

subjects.name: Command words and levels marking
subjects.description: Define, describe, explain, suggest, assess and evaluate each demand a different structure, and the long questions are marked holistically against level descriptors. Teaching a student to read the command word and the tariff before writing anything is the highest-value habit in the whole course.

subjects.name: Timing and question order
subjects.description: Students lose marks at the end of papers far more often than at the start. Rationing time by tariff, deciding question order in advance and accepting an imperfect final answer are examinable habits in practice, and they are trainable in a handful of sessions with a clock running.

sections.heading: What the two 4GE1 papers actually put in front of your child
paragraphs: A 4GE1 candidate sits two written papers, one on physical environments and one on human environments, and each arrives with a resource booklet. That booklet is the part parents most often underestimate. It contains figures, maps, graphs, photographs and short text extracts, and a large share of the lower-tariff marks are available to any student who can read them accurately and quote from them precisely. Students who revise only from topic notes walk into the exam having practised the half of the paper that rewards memory and skipped the half that rewards technique.

The specification also leaves schools a choice of topics. Pearson sets out a bank of physical and human environments, and a Dubai school teaches a subset of them. This matters more than families expect, because two children in the same compound, both sitting 4GE1 in the same series, can be examined on different topics. Buying tuition before confirming which topics the school entered is the fastest way to waste the first three sessions. The entry information sits with the exams officer or the humanities lead, and it takes one email to obtain.

The exact duration and weighting of each paper is set by the live specification, and Pearson revises documents between series, so the honest instruction is to check the current version on qualifications.pearson.com rather than trust a figure on a tutoring page. What does not change is the shape of the demand: short questions testing recall and skills, mid-tariff questions testing explanation, and long questions testing evaluation with a judgement. A tutor who starts by mapping your child's last paper onto those three bands will tell you within one session where the grade is actually going.

sections.heading: The mark tariff ladder, from a one-mark definition to a nine-mark judgement
paragraphs: Almost every mid-paper geography grade in Dubai traces back to a student answering every question in the same register. They write a paragraph for a two-mark question and a paragraph for a nine-mark question. The first wastes four minutes, the second caps the answer two bands below what the child knows. Geography examiners publish levels descriptors for the long questions, and those descriptors reward structure and judgement as much as content. A student who has never seen one cannot write to one.

The ladder below is what we teach in the first fortnight, and it is deliberately mechanical. Mechanical is what a tired sixteen-year-old can execute in the last ten minutes of a paper. Once a student can look at a tariff and know roughly how many developed points, how many named examples and how much judgement the answer needs, the quality of their geography stops being the limiting factor. Before that point, teaching more content is pouring water into a bucket with a hole in it.

Time budgeting falls out of the same table. The practical rule we use is slightly more than one minute per mark, with a fixed ninety seconds of planning reserved for the long question and nothing reserved for the one and two-mark questions. Students resist planning because it feels like lost writing time. Showing them two of their own answers, one planned and one not, marked against the same descriptors, settles that argument faster than any amount of advice.

One developed point per two marks is a safe working ratio
Named example means place, date and a figure, not a country
The judgement belongs in the final sentences, not the first

sections.heading: The command words, and what each one changes about the answer
paragraphs: Describe and explain are the two command words Dubai students confuse most, and the confusion costs marks in both directions. Describe asks what is happening: the pattern, the trend, the distribution, with data quoted. Explain asks why, and an explanation that stops at the first step scores as a description. If a student writes that deforestation increases flood risk, that is a statement. If they write that removing tree cover reduces interception and infiltration, so a greater share of rainfall reaches the channel as surface runoff and the lag time shortens, that is an explanation, and it is worth roughly double.

Suggest is the command word that frightens students and should not. It appears where the examiner knows the candidate has not seen the specific place in the figure, and it licenses a reasoned inference from the stimulus. The correct response is to use the figure explicitly: because the photograph shows terraced slopes above the settlement, the likely reason is X. Students who treat suggest as a memory test write about somewhere else entirely and score nothing, despite knowing more geography than the mark scheme requires.

Assess, evaluate and to what extent are the three that carry the long-question marks, and they all demand the same missing ingredient: a judgement that a marker can find. Weighing two sides and stopping is a level two answer in most levels schemes. Weighing two sides and then stating which carries more weight, and why, in a sentence that refers back to the evidence already given, is what moves an answer into the top band. We practise this by giving students a complete two-sided answer with the judgement deleted and asking them to write only the last forty words.
bullets: Describe: pattern, trend, distribution, with figures quoted from the booklet
Explain: a mechanism in at least two linked steps, every time
Suggest: reason from the stimulus, say so explicitly, do not recall
Assess and evaluate: two sides plus a stated judgement, in that order
Compare: use comparative connectives, never two separate descriptions

sections.heading: Where 4GE1 marks disappear in Dubai classrooms, in order of cost
paragraphs: The most expensive single habit is the undated, unnamed case study. Students arrive with notes that say a developing country or a tropical storm, and examiners cannot award example marks for a category. The second most expensive is the unfinished paper. In marked scripts we see across Dubai cohorts, the last long question is frequently half the length of the first, which is a timing problem dressed up as a knowledge problem. Both of these are habits, and habits respond to practice under a clock faster than they respond to explanation.

Third is misreading the figure. A student who quotes a value from the wrong axis, or who reads a choropleth key one band out, loses marks on questions they understood completely. This is why we spend twenty minutes a week on booklet skills even with strong candidates. Fourth is the missing mechanism, the explanation that names a cause and never shows how it operates. Fifth is the judgement that never appears, which caps the long questions. Fixing those five accounts for most of the realistic grade movement available in a term.

There is a sixth pattern specific to transfers, and Dubai has a lot of transfers. A student who studied geography under a different board or in a different country frequently has excellent content knowledge in the wrong shape: Cambridge-style structures for an Edexcel paper, or MYP criterion-led paragraphs where the paper wants a tariffed answer. That student does not need teaching. They need translating, and the first marked paper tells you exactly which of their habits transfer and which have to be retired.

sections.heading: Case studies a Dubai student can actually defend in an answer
paragraphs: A case study earns marks when it carries a place name, a date and at least one figure, and when the student can connect it to the question rather than recite it. Most students in Dubai carry too many case studies in too little detail. Two well-built examples per topic, each on a single page, outperform six half-remembered ones, because under exam pressure a student reaches for what is retrievable. We rebuild them to a fixed template: place, date, scale of event or process, two causes, two consequences, one management response, one figure.

Dubai and the wider UAE supply genuinely usable material for several specification areas, and examiners do not require British examples. Urban growth, water supply in an arid environment, desalination and its energy cost, coastal modification, migration and labour mobility, and the shift of an economy away from hydrocarbon extraction are all topics where a student living here can speak with specificity. The important discipline is sourcing: a figure quoted from a government statistics page is defensible, and a figure half-remembered from a classroom slide is not.

The trap is recency. Geography case studies age, and a student using a 2011 figure for a process that has changed substantially since will be marked on what they wrote, not on what they meant. We date every example on the page and replace anything older than roughly a decade unless the event itself is the point, as with a specific earthquake or storm. Students find this reassuring rather than tedious, because a dated page is a page they can trust in the exam hall.

sections.heading: The Geographical Investigation: what a tutor may and may not do
paragraphs: Enquiry work is where families most often misunderstand what tutoring is for, so this section states the boundary plainly. A tutor may teach enquiry design, explain sampling strategies, question a student's reasoning, demonstrate a presentation technique on different data, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not supply sentences, restructure a write-up on the student's behalf, or hand over material for submission. The work a student submits must be the student's own, and the ethical line here is also a practical one: an investigation a student did not build cannot be defended in an exam answer about method.

That boundary is not a limitation on usefulness. The marks in enquiry work sit in justification and evaluation, and both are teachable through questioning. Why this sampling interval and not that one. What would have changed if the data had been collected at a different time of day. Which of your presentation choices actually shows the relationship, and which one just looks tidy. A student who has been asked those questions ten times writes a different evaluation from one who has been handed a model answer.

On data, a Dubai student has more options than they assume. Primary collection can be local and small-scale: a land use transect along a single street, a pedestrian count at two times of day, an environmental quality survey across two communities, a microclimate comparison between a shaded and an unshaded site. Secondary data is available from government statistics portals and from published reports. What examiners penalise is a method described so vaguely that nobody could repeat it, and that is a writing problem a tutor is allowed to fix by teaching.

sections.heading: KHDA, mandatory subjects and the Year 11 timetable squeeze
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects schools annually on a six-band scale. For a parent planning geography support, the inspection report is useful for one narrow purpose: it tells you how the school's humanities provision was judged, which is a better guide than a prospectus. It says nothing about any individual tutor, and no tutoring provider can claim a KHDA endorsement.

The requirement that changes a Year 11 timetable is the mandatory subject rule. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes organised for Arab and non-Arab students and combined classes prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. The practical consequence is a fuller week than the equivalent British timetable, and the subject that loses independent study time is often an optional humanity.

This is worth knowing before you buy tuition, because it changes what good tutoring looks like. A Dubai Year 11 does not have four spare evenings. A single fixed online slot with a short written task between sessions respects that reality, where a schedule built on long weekend blocks tends to collapse by half term. Where Arabic first-language work is also under pressure, the honest advice is sometimes to sequence support rather than run two subjects at once, and we will say so.

sections.heading: A twelve-week 4GE1 plan counted backwards from the written papers
paragraphs: Pearson runs International GCSE series in May/June and in November each year, and the entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so every plan should be built against the live timetable on qualifications.pearson.com rather than a date copied from a tutoring site. For the published series we can point to: the June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and the November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those dates tell you how long a retake decision actually takes.

The structure below is what twelve weeks looks like when it is counted backwards rather than forwards. Counting forwards produces a plan that covers content and runs out of time before the practice that converts content into marks. Counting backwards forces the awkward decision early: which two topics get the deep work and which ones get consolidation only. Parents sometimes find that decision uncomfortable, and it is still better made in week twelve than discovered in week two.

Two practical notes. First, mock weeks and school assessment weeks are not revision weeks, and planning as if they were is the commonest reason a schedule slips. Second, Ramadan shifts the working day across the UAE, and families routinely move sessions to post-Iftar slots. If the exam term and Ramadan overlap in a given year, build that into the plan in week twelve rather than improvising in week four.

sections.heading: Permits, equivalency and the questions worth asking before you pay
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any page quoting an amount is guessing.

The second thing worth understanding is equivalency, because it decides which IGCSE results actually count later. For the British track, the Ministry of Education requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among the five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Geography counts as one of the accredited subjects. Verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae before relying on it, because this is the authority's process and not something a tutoring provider performs.

Which leaves the questions we would ask a prospective tutor. Which specification code have you taught, and in which series. Can you mark a long question against the levels descriptors in front of me. What comes back in writing after each session. What happens when no specialist is free at our hour. And, in this market specifically, do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. A tutor who answers those five clearly is a different proposition from one who answers with testimonials.

process.description: A marked 4GE1 question or mock paper, plus the school's most recent report comment on geography. Two documents are enough to see whether the problem is content, command words, timing or the case-study bank, and that distinction decides what the first month contains.

process.description: Which specification topics were entered, which series the student is sitting, and whether any internal enquiry work is still outstanding. One email to the humanities lead or exams officer. Tuition built without this information usually spends its first three sessions on topics that are not examined.

process.title: Fix a weekly slot and a written task
process.description: One recurring online slot in Gulf Standard Time, agreed around the school run, activities and prayer times, plus one tariffed question to complete between sessions. The written task is what makes the weekly hour compound instead of resetting.

process.description: At half term, compare the ranked list of question types from the first session with current marked work. If the weakest question type has not moved, the plan changes. That review is the point at which tutoring either earns its continuation or does not.

whyPoints.description: A geography teacher is not automatically a 4GE1 teacher. Tutors working on this page have taught the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE specification and marked to its mark schemes, which is what allows a session to start from a levels descriptor rather than from a textbook chapter.

whyPoints.title: Marked evidence after every session
whyPoints.description: You receive the annotated question, the mark awarded, the band it sits in and the one change that would move it. Progress in a writing subject is visible in scripts long before it appears in a report, and a parent who can see the scripts can judge the tuition.

whyPoints.description: Online delivery widens the pool from the humanities teachers within driving distance of your community to those who have actually taught the entered topics. For a subject with school-chosen options, that is the difference between useful and approximate.

whyPoints.description: Enquiry and coursework support is teaching, questioning and feedback on the student's own material. No part of a submission is supplied by a tutor. That boundary protects the student, who is the person an examination board would penalise.
