sections.heading: Evidence discipline, and the proof a candidate forgets to keep
paragraphs: Evidence is the part of 4IT1 that feels like paperwork and behaves like marks. A practical task is credited on what can be seen, so a step completed perfectly and not captured is a step that did not happen as far as the marking is concerned. Candidates understand this in the abstract and forget it under time, because capturing evidence interrupts the flow of doing the task and the task feels like the real work.

The routine that solves it is small and it is the same every time. Finish a discrete step, capture the screen immediately, name the capture so that it identifies the step it belongs to, and only then move on to the next instruction. Captures should show enough of the surrounding context to prove what was actually done rather than being cropped tightly to a single dialogue box. File names should identify the task and the step in words, rather than being sequential numbers that mean nothing at all to a marker working through an unfamiliar folder under time pressure.

Building the habit takes about two sessions and it is best done early, in Year 10, when there is no pressure attached. A candidate who installs it then spends the practical paper thinking about the task rather than remembering to be organised, which is worth more than any single technique. It also carries forward: the applied and vocational computing courses that follow ICT at 16 include assessed units produced over weeks, and in those courses unevidenced work is a far more expensive mistake than it is here.

sections.heading: Spreadsheet tasks: the formulae that score and the ones that look right
paragraphs: Spreadsheet work carries a large share of the practical marks and it is the most teachable part of the subject, because the faults are procedural. The first rule a candidate needs is that any cell the brief describes as calculated must contain a formula referring to other cells, not a number. This sounds obvious and is violated constantly, usually by strong candidates who can do the arithmetic in their heads and see no reason to make the spreadsheet do it.

The second rule concerns cell references. A model that works for one row and breaks when copied down has not been built correctly, and briefs often require exactly that copying. Candidates who have never had the difference between a reference that moves and one that is fixed explained properly will produce something that looks right in the first row and is wrong in the rest, which is a single mark in understanding and several in output.

The third area is conditional logic and the presentation that goes with it. Briefs commonly ask for a value that depends on a condition, and then for the result to be formatted in a stated way and charted with stated labels. Candidates get the logic and lose the formatting, or get both and mislabel the chart axes. Working through a brief's formatting requirements as a deliberate final pass, rather than as something done while building, recovers those marks reliably and takes a few minutes.

sections.heading: Database tasks: structure first, then queries that match the wording
paragraphs: Database tasks punish loose thinking earlier than any other part of the paper, because everything downstream depends on the structure. If a field meant to hold a date is set as text, sorting breaks and date-range queries cannot work. If a field meant to hold a number is set as text, numeric criteria fail. Candidates who set everything loosely and expect to sort it out later find they cannot, because the query simply cannot return what the structure does not support.

Queries are the second gate and the fault there is approximation. A brief states criteria precisely, including ranges, exclusions and whether conditions combine. Candidates read the criteria, form a general sense of which records are wanted, and build a query that returns roughly those. Roughly is not a mark. The practice that fixes it is translation: write the stated criteria out as explicit conditions on paper first, then build the query from the written conditions rather than from the impression.

Reports are the third, and the losses there are almost entirely skipped instructions. A brief will specify which fields appear, how records are sorted, and sometimes how they are grouped. A default report containing the right data but in the wrong order misses those marks completely. For Dubai families there is also a practical constraint worth naming: the database package schools most often teach runs on Windows and has no macOS version, so a Mac-only household cannot practise this task area at home. Where that applies, the session plan should weight database work more heavily, and we will say so rather than pretend otherwise.

sections.heading: The written paper's scenario trap
paragraphs: The written component of 4IT1 is where knowledgeable candidates underperform most visibly. Questions are set inside a scenario about a specific organisation, and the mark scheme credits answers that address that organisation. A candidate who writes an accurate textbook description of the technology has demonstrated knowledge and not answered the question, which feels unfair until you read the question stem again and notice it asked why the technology suits this particular situation.

There are a handful of recurring stems and each has a required answer shape. Why does this device suit this task wants a property of the device linked to the task. Describe a risk to the organisation's data wants a named threat with its mechanism. Explain how this measure reduces that risk wants the link between the safeguard and the threat already named. State an environmental impact wants a consequence attributed to a cause. Give an advantage and a disadvantage for the business wants both tied to the business in the question.

Learning those shapes is quick and it transfers across every topic in the written paper, which makes it the highest-return work available anywhere in the theory half of the course. The method is mechanical rather than clever: write an answer, mark it against the published criteria, identify the required element that is absent from it, and rewrite the answer, then repeat the cycle on a different topic until the shape becomes automatic under time. ICT specialists are fewer in number than maths or science teachers, and within ICT the database task area is the narrowest capability of all. That is the real constraint on matching, and it tightens sharply before a Pearson series.

What that means practically: outside the weeks immediately before a series, a match for written technique is usually quick and a match for practical work takes a little longer. In the eight weeks before a window, specialists book out first and the wait can exceed a fortnight. The honest options at that point are a waiting slot, a diagnostic only, or being told to look elsewhere. Substituting someone who can cover the theory but cannot supervise practical work is not one of them.

There is also a category of question that is not ours to answer. Where a private candidate needs a centre able to run the practical component, that is a matter for the centres themselves, and we will point you at them rather than acting as an intermediary. faqs.question: What exactly does the 4IT1 practical paper mark?
faqs.answer: Whether the instructions in the brief were carried out, item by item. Not whether the output looks professional, and not whether the candidate understands the software. If the brief specifies a currency format to two decimal places, that formatting is a mark. If it specifies a file format or a set of dimensions for an image, those are marks. The brief is effectively the mark scheme. That one fact explains most of the losses in this component, and it is why a session begins with reading the brief rather than opening the software.

faqs.question: Why did my child lose marks on a spreadsheet that gave the right answers?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly because values were typed where formulae were required. A cell the brief describes as calculated must contain a formula referring to other cells, not a number, because the task tests building a model rather than doing arithmetic. Strong candidates do this most often, since they can calculate in their heads and see no reason to make the spreadsheet work. The second likely cause is formatting left at defaults: currency symbols, decimal places and axis labels are specified in the brief and therefore marked.

faqs.question: How important are screenshots and file names in 4IT1?
faqs.answer: They decide whether work counts. A practical task is credited on what can be seen, so a step completed perfectly and not captured did not happen as far as marking is concerned. Captures taken at the end from memory miss steps; captures cropped to a single dialogue box omit the context that proves what was done; files named generically cannot be matched to the task they answer. The routine is small: finish a step, capture immediately, name it so it identifies the step, then move on. Two sessions installs it.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an ICT tutor to our home in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE on this platform, and home visiting is a service offered only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. For practical ICT this is an advantage rather than a concession: the candidate works in their own installation with their own folders, the teacher sees the full screen at full size, and nobody can quietly take the mouse. A visiting tutor at a tilted laptop sees less and usually ends up doing the task.

faqs.question: Why do database tasks cost so many marks in 4IT1?
faqs.answer: Because everything downstream depends on the structure. A field meant to hold a date set as text breaks sorting and makes date-range queries impossible. A numeric field set as text makes numeric criteria fail. Candidates who set field types loosely and intend to sort it out later find they cannot, since a query cannot return what the structure does not support. The second cause is approximation in queries: briefs state criteria precisely, including ranges and how conditions combine, and roughly the right records earns nothing.

faqs.question: Can my child practise 4IT1 database work on a MacBook?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and it is worth knowing before anyone sells you hours that assume otherwise. The database package Dubai schools most commonly teach runs on Windows and has no macOS version. A Mac-only household therefore has no straightforward route to practise that task area between lessons. The honest options are access to a Windows machine, use of a school computer room, or accepting that database work happens in session time and weighting the plan accordingly. Confirm with the department which package they teach before arranging anything.

faqs.question: My child knows the ICT theory but the written paper marks are low. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the written component credits answers tied to the organisation in the scenario, and knowledge written generally scores a fraction of what the candidate knows. A correct textbook description of cloud storage does not answer a question about why it suits this particular business. There are only a handful of recurring question stems and each has a required shape: a device property linked to the task, a threat with its mechanism, a safeguard linked to the named threat, a consequence attributed to a cause. Learning those shapes transfers across every topic.

faqs.question: What is the quickest 4IT1 improvement available before a series?
faqs.answer: Two things, both procedural. First, a formula check: going through a completed spreadsheet task and confirming every cell the brief described as calculated actually contains a formula. Second, a formatting pass done deliberately at the end of each task rather than while building, since currency, decimals, headings and labels are specified and therefore marked. Neither requires new knowledge and both can be installed in a session or two. On the written side, practising the recurring answer shapes is the equivalent quick gain.

faqs.question: Should a 4IT1 candidate work on practical or written technique first?
faqs.answer: Whichever the component breakdown says, which is why that breakdown is the first thing to ask the school for. Practical marks respond faster, because the faults are procedural habits that change in a few sessions. Written answer shape changes more slowly but transfers across every topic once it does. A candidate weak on both usually starts with the practical routines, since they are quick wins that build confidence, then moves to written technique with enough weeks left for the repetition it needs.

faqs.question: How long does it take to fix an evidence habit for 4IT1?
faqs.answer: About two sessions to install and then a few weeks of applying it before it becomes automatic. The routine itself is simple: complete a discrete step, capture the screen immediately with enough context to show what was done, name the capture so it identifies the step, then continue. Best done in Year 10 while there is no pressure attached. It also pays forward, because the applied and vocational computing courses after 16 include assessed units produced over weeks, where unevidenced work is a far more expensive mistake.

faqs.question: What should I ask my child's school before booking 4IT1 sessions?
faqs.answer: Four things, all free and all more useful than a grade. The specification code and the series your child is entered for, confirmed in writing by the exams officer. The marks per component from the last mock rather than the overall grade. Which software packages and versions the practical component is taught and examined in. And, if possible, the practical attempt itself along with the brief it answered, because an attempt without its brief tells a teacher very little about which instructions were missed.

faqs.question: How quickly can a 4IT1 specialist be matched for a Dubai family?
faqs.answer: Outside the weeks before a series, usually within a few days for written technique and within about a week for practical work. In the eight weeks before a Pearson window it can exceed a fortnight, because ICT specialists are fewer than maths or science teachers and book out first. Where nobody suitable is free, the options offered are a waiting slot, a diagnostic block only, or being told to look elsewhere. Substituting a generalist who can cover theory but not supervise practical tasks is not among them.

faqs.question: Can a tutor complete a practical task for my child to hand in?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody here will. A tutor sets briefs, watches the candidate work, and gives feedback on what the candidate produced. The teacher does not take the mouse, which is a teaching decision as much as an integrity one. 4IT1 carries no coursework and the practical paper is sat under examination conditions, so exposure at this level is low. It rises on the vocational courses that follow, where assessed units must be the student's own. Any provider offering finished output for submission is offering malpractice.

faqs.question: Does a private 4IT1 candidate in Dubai need a special examination centre?
faqs.answer: One able to run the practical component, which is a narrower requirement than for a written-only subject. Confirm that capability before paying any entry fee, since a centre accepting external candidates for written papers may not be equipped for the practical one. Entry fees are set by the centre and vary, so collect two or three written quotes. IB Gram does not arrange, perform or guarantee any examination entry: we can tell you what to ask, and the centre answers it.

faqs.question: When are the 4IT1 papers sat, and who makes the entry?
faqs.answer: Pearson examines International GCSE qualifications in a May/June series and a November series each year, and the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Your child's school makes the entry as the examination centre and holds a deadline that sits months before the paper. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including International GCSE November 2027, so work from the live official timetable rather than from a date restated on any tutoring page, including this one.

intro.heading: The money questions in 4IT1 are not really about the hourly rate
paragraphs: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE ICT, code 4IT1, is one of the few subjects at this level where a family can spend money on the wrong thing entirely. The hourly rate for teaching is the visible cost and it is the one every comparison argues about. The costs that actually catch Dubai families out sit elsewhere: the database software a candidate cannot run on the laptop at home, the entry fee for a private candidate, and the hours spent teaching theory to a child whose problem is that they have never built a working spreadsheet model.

Start with the rates, since they are rarely published. Across the Dubai market in October 2026, budget platforms advertise from the mid-forties an hour, qualified subject teaching online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, visiting in-home tutors at roughly AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the rate, and subject specialists for international qualifications at AED 200 to 450 and above. Monthly offers run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Small group classes are advertised at roughly AED 90 to 160 per pupil per hour.

Now the part nobody prices. The 4IT1 practical component requires a candidate to work in real software: documents, spreadsheets, a database, a presentation, image editing and web authoring. Schools provide that software and the examination centre provides the examination environment, so there is no exam-day cost. Home practice is where the gap appears, and it is specific. Most of the task areas can be practised in a free office suite with no cost at all. Database work is the exception, because the package Dubai schools most often teach does not run on macOS, and a household with only a Mac has a practice problem rather than a money problem.

The second thing that quietly changes a 4IT1 bill is the confusion between ICT and Computer Science. The two sit in the same option column in many Dubai schools and are routinely described as versions of one subject. They are not. ICT is assessed on applied competence in software; Computer Science requires writing programs. Families who hire a programming tutor for an ICT candidate pay for hours that cannot help, and the mismatch is usually discovered only after a mock.

Dubai gives this some scale. The emirate has 227 private schools serving 387,441 pupils across 17 curricula, with 37 per cent of those pupils on a UK curriculum, and KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year. ICT groups are generally larger than Computer Science groups, which means classroom provision is usually solid and the useful tutoring is narrower: practical technique, evidence discipline and written precision rather than content from scratch.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-ict-4it1-tutor.programmesIntro: ICT at 16 is chosen, examined and then either dropped or carried forward, and each of those three points has its own cost. The stages below are where a 4IT1 decision gets made in a Dubai school.

programmes.name: Choosing ICT rather than Computer Science
programmes.description: The decision that prevents the most wasted money later. ICT is about applying software to real tasks and is assessed on what a candidate can produce. Computer Science is about how computation works and requires programming. A pupil who is quick and confident with software but dislikes writing code is well served by ICT and badly served by the other, and the reverse holds just as firmly.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools frequently run both in one option column, which forces a choice and often supplies little guidance. Ask the department two questions before the form goes back: which specification code is entered, and which software packages the practical component is taught in. The second answer tells you whether the laptop at home can support practice, which is a planning matter worth knowing in Year 9 rather than in Year 11.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE ICT
programmes.description: A written component covering ICT systems, networks and online services, data handling, the uses of ICT in organisations, and the legal, ethical, security and health implications of it. Alongside it sits a practical component in which candidates complete tasks in real software and produce the evidence of having done so. There is no coursework, so nothing accumulates across the two years outside examination conditions.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools enter 4IT1 through their own Pearson centre number and the entry is made by the exams officer. Confirm the code in writing, because Cambridge also offers an ICT qualification and the practical requirements are not identical. Ask as well which packages and which versions are installed in the room where the practical component is sat, since an unfamiliar menu layout costs minutes in a timed paper.

programmes.name: Where 4IT1 leads after Year 11
programmes.description: ICT at 16 leads most naturally into applied and vocational computing: BTEC qualifications in IT or business, A Level courses in applied or information technology where a school offers them, and business-facing routes where software competence is directly useful. It is weaker preparation for A Level Computer Science, which assumes programming the ICT course does not teach.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's post-16 provision is broadening quickly, with the 2026-27 intake adding seven new private schools and 16,846 places. Not every campus offers a vocational computing route at 16 to 18, so a family whose child is suited to the applied path should check sixth-form provision before committing to a school rather than afterwards. Asking which post-16 computing courses actually ran last year is the useful version of that question.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-ict-4it1-tutor.subjectsIntro: 4IT1 divides into a theory half and a practical half, and the marks are lost in quite different ways in each. The areas below name what the paper credits, which is usually more specific than a revision guide implies.

subjects.name: ICT systems, input and output devices
subjects.description: Hardware and peripherals, and the match between a device and a purpose. The paper asks why a given device suits a stated situation, so answers that describe the device without connecting it to the scenario score poorly even when they are accurate.

subjects.name: Storage, backup and file management
subjects.description: Storage types and capacities, backup strategies, and sensible file naming and folder structure. File management also carries marks in the practical component, where badly named files make a candidate's evidence hard to credit.

subjects.name: Networks, the internet and online services
subjects.description: Network types, connectivity, cloud services and the trade-offs between them. Marks go to candidates who can state a specific advantage and a specific drawback for the organisation in the question rather than in general terms.

subjects.name: Databases, queries and reports
subjects.description: Building a table structure, running queries against stated criteria, and producing a readable report. This is the task area most Dubai candidates practise least, often because the software at home cannot run it, and it shows in practical marks.

subjects.name: Spreadsheet modelling and formulae
subjects.description: Formulae, functions, conditional logic, charts and presentation of results. The highest-value practical area, because the tasks are prescriptive and the marks are recoverable through practice rather than through understanding.

subjects.name: Word processing and document layout
subjects.description: Mail merge, styles, headers, tables and layout to a stated brief. Candidates lose marks by producing something that looks acceptable but does not match the brief's specific instructions, which is what is actually being marked.

subjects.name: Graphics, image editing and presentation
subjects.description: Editing images to a specification and building a presentation to a brief. Marks attach to following the instructions precisely, including sizes, formats and placement, rather than to design quality as a matter of taste.

subjects.name: Security, privacy and data protection
subjects.description: Threats, safeguards and the obligations organisations carry over personal data. Answers need the threat and the matching safeguard linked together, which is the connection the mark scheme tests and the one candidates most often skip.

subjects.name: Health, safety and ergonomics
subjects.description: Workstation risks and the measures that reduce them. Low-tariff, reliable marks that candidates lose only by being vague, which makes this a sensible early win for someone rebuilding confidence.

subjects.name: Legal, ethical and environmental implications
subjects.description: The consequences of ICT use for individuals, organisations and the environment. The paper wants a consequence stated and attributed to a cause, not a list of concerns, and practising that shape transfers across the whole written component.

sections.heading: What 4IT1 is, and why it is not Computer Science
paragraphs: The most expensive mistake available in this subject is hiring the wrong teacher, and it starts with an option-evening conversation in which ICT and Computer Science are described as two versions of the same thing. They are not related in the way the names suggest. Pearson Edexcel 4IT1 assesses whether a candidate can use software to accomplish stated tasks and explain the role of ICT in organisations. Pearson Edexcel 4CP0 assesses whether a candidate can write and debug programs and reason about how computation works.

The practical consequence is that practice material, teachers and post-16 routes all diverge. A programming specialist hired for a 4IT1 candidate will teach beautifully and irrelevantly, because the practical paper does not involve writing code. Equally, a general ICT tutor is not the right choice for a 4CP0 candidate who cannot start a program. Families discover the mismatch after a mock, by which point a term of fees has been spent on hours that could not help.

Neither subject is the harder one in the abstract, which is the framing that causes the trouble. They test different capabilities. A pupil who is quick with software, reads instructions carefully and likes producing finished work is well suited to ICT. A pupil who enjoys puzzles and tolerates repeated failure while debugging is suited to Computer Science instead. The table below sets the two qualifications out side by side on the measures that actually matter when choosing a teacher and planning a budget for either one.

sections.heading: The practical paper, and the software question nobody prices
paragraphs: The 4IT1 practical component asks a candidate to work in genuine software and produce evidence of what they did. Schools install the packages, and the examination centre supplies and configures the environment for the paper itself, so there is no exam-day software cost to a family. The question that does cost something is home practice, and it is more specific than most providers admit. Practical marks come from doing, not from reading, and a candidate who cannot practise between lessons will not build speed.

For most task areas the answer is reassuring. Word processing, spreadsheets, presentation, image editing and web authoring can all be practised adequately in free software. Function names and menu positions differ slightly between suites, which is a small nuisance rather than a real obstacle, and it is worth confirming with the department which package and version the school uses so the differences are known rather than discovered. Nothing here requires a purchase.

Databases are the exception and it is a hard one. The database package Dubai schools most commonly teach runs on Windows and is not available for macOS, so a household whose only machine is a Mac has no straightforward way to practise that task area at home. The honest options are a Windows machine, access to a school computer room, or accepting that database practice happens in lesson time. Any provider who tells a Mac household that this is not a problem has not checked. The table lists each task area with its real home-practice position.

sections.heading: What 4IT1 support costs in Dubai, by what you are buying
paragraphs: Dubai providers price by the hour, by the month and by the group, and comparing across those three units is where families lose track. The figures below are published market rates, described by what is being bought rather than by brand, each with the month it was checked. Three of the six pages currently ranking for searches like this one publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars, which is a currency no Dubai family pays a tutor in.

Divide before you judge. A monthly online block advertised at AED 799 for eight sessions works out near AED 100 an hour, which sits below the qualified-teacher band and tells you something useful about who is likely to be teaching. A monthly in-home block at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits is roughly AED 200 to 225 an hour with travel inside it. Neither figure is dishonest; they are simply not comparable until they are reduced to the same unit.

IB Gram does not publish an ICT rate card here. The hours a candidate needs depend on which component is weak, and for 4IT1 that question has an unusually wide answer: a practical-only problem can be short work, while a candidate weak on both components is a longer block. A figure follows a free trial lesson, one per family, booked without any card details. The table below is what any quote should be measured against, including the one we give you.

sections.heading: What moves the number on an ICT quote in this emirate
paragraphs: Which component is weak is the first and largest driver, and it is specific to ICT. A candidate losing marks only on the practical paper often needs a short block, because practical marks respond to drilling a brief rather than to building understanding. A candidate whose written answers are vague needs a different and usually longer kind of work, because answer shape changes slowly. A provider who quotes before establishing which of those applies is quoting a package, not a plan.

Classroom provision is the second. ICT cohorts in Dubai are generally larger than Computer Science cohorts, which means the subject is usually taught by someone who teaches it regularly rather than by a stretched specialist covering four year groups. Teaching quality is therefore less often the gap. What a large group cannot do is notice that one candidate consistently ignores part of a brief, and that is the fault most private sessions are actually bought to fix.

The remaining drivers are the familiar ones, and they are worth asking about directly. Weeks remaining before the series, because availability tightens and specialists book out first. Delivery format, because a visiting tutor's drive sits inside the rate whatever the invoice says. Session length, since ninety minutes often carries a slightly lower hourly figure than sixty. Commitment length, because pre-paid blocks are usually discounted. And whether a sibling is taking the same subject at the same point, which occasionally supports a shared rate.

sections.heading: Where the written 4IT1 paper loses marks
paragraphs: The theory half of 4IT1 looks easy and marks badly. Candidates read about storage, networks, security and the uses of ICT in organisations, find all of it comprehensible, then score well below what they know. The cause is almost always answer shape rather than knowledge. Questions are set in a scenario, and the mark scheme credits answers that connect to that scenario specifically. A correct general statement about cloud storage earns little when the question asked about a particular organisation's problem.

Three failure patterns account for most of the loss. The first is describing a device or a service instead of saying why it suits the stated situation. The second is naming a safeguard without linking it to the threat in the question, which is the connection being tested. The third is listing concerns under the legal, ethical and environmental topics rather than stating a consequence and attributing it to a cause. All three are habits, and habits respond to marking and rewriting rather than to further reading.

The remedy is unglamorous and reliable. Write one answer, mark it against the published criteria, identify the required element that is missing, rewrite it, then do the same thing on a different topic. Three cycles changes how a candidate writes everywhere, because the fix is structural rather than topical. It is also the cheapest work in the subject: written technique needs no software, no device and no environment matching, which makes it the one part of 4IT1 support that is genuinely easy to buy.

sections.heading: 4IT1 costs in context for a Dubai household
paragraphs: Tutoring sits alongside fees, transport and everything else, and the useful comparison is annual rather than hourly. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. For a household whose school line is fixed, the tutoring decision is the discretionary one, which is exactly why it deserves honest arithmetic rather than a monthly figure with the hours hidden.

Examination entry fees are a separate line and are never inside a tutor's rate. Where a school enters a candidate, the fee is set by the school as the Pearson centre and appears on the school invoice. Where a family enters a private candidate, the centre bills them directly and the amount varies, so collect written quotes. For 4IT1 there is an extra constraint: the centre must be able to run the practical component, which is a narrower requirement than for a written-only subject and worth confirming before anything else is arranged.

The device question belongs in this table too, because it is the one real equipment cost in the subject and it only applies to some households. A family with a Windows machine already has what database practice needs. A family with only a Mac is choosing between buying a machine, using a school computer room, or accepting that database work happens in lessons. Stating that plainly is more useful than pretending the subject costs nothing to practise.

sections.heading: Permits, centres and who is allowed to charge you in Dubai
paragraphs: A parent comparing ICT tutors on price should also compare them on legality, and in the UAE that is a single question with a documented answer. An individual giving paid private lessons requires a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the MoHRE service listing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time through the ministry's smart app, website or e-services system.

Since it costs nothing and takes two working days, a tutor without one has no price-based excuse, and anyone offering private tutoring without the permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. What the permit does not tell you is anything about teaching quality. Eligible applicants run from teachers registered in government or private schools through to unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Treat the permit as a legality check and ask about subject experience separately.

Centres are regulated differently again, which matters for 4IT1 because the practical component needs one. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute: initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. No provider should describe itself as approved by KHDA unless it holds that permit. And a centre accepting a private candidate for the practical paper must be able to supply the examination environment, which is a question to ask before paying any entry fee.

sections.heading: Teaching a practical subject over live video
paragraphs: Every 4IT1 session for a Dubai family runs online, one-to-one, over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and home visiting is a service offered only in India. For a practical subject that deserves a proper explanation rather than an assertion, because the obvious objection is that software work needs someone sitting beside the candidate.

In practice the opposite holds. The candidate shares their screen and works in their own installation, with their own file structure and their own menu layout, which is exactly the environment their practice will happen in. The teacher sees every click at full size and can stop the candidate at the point where the brief was misread rather than after the task is finished and the evidence is wrong. Two people at one laptop see less, not more, and the teacher ends up taking the mouse, which teaches nothing.

The format also decides who is available. A Dubai family hiring locally chooses from people who can be in their community on a weekday afternoon. Online, they choose from ICT specialists across time zones that overlap with Gulf Standard Time evenings. Where no specialist is free at the level required, we say so before a payment rather than substituting a generalist you would notice three weeks in. For the database task area we will also say plainly whether a Mac household can practise at home, because that answer changes what the sessions should cover.

process.title: Tell us which component is weak
process.description: Send a marked written paper and, if there is one, a practical task the candidate produced. The two halves of 4IT1 fail differently and cost different amounts to fix, so this is the single most useful thing you can provide before anyone quotes a figure.

process.title: Check the software position
process.description: Tell us which packages and versions the school uses and what the household runs at home, including whether there is a Windows machine. That determines whether database practice between lessons is possible and therefore what the sessions should prioritise.

process.title: Free trial lesson, one per family
process.description: A full session with a teacher who has seen the work, booked without card details and carrying no obligation. The candidate works in the software during it rather than watching. A written note follows the same day with what the teaching found and how many sessions it suggests.

process.title: A quote with the hours shown
process.description: The figure arrives as hours multiplied by a rate, with the hour count justified by the component split rather than by a package length. The market bands on this page are the comparison. If the hours look wrong to you, that is a conversation to have before paying.

process.title: Review before the entry deadline
process.description: Six to eight weeks ahead of the series, read the notes and the component marks and decide whether to continue, change the split or stop. Families told clearly what to practise often finish the last weeks themselves, and should be told so plainly.

whyPoints.title: The software question gets a straight answer
whyPoints.description: Most 4IT1 task areas can be practised in free software. Database work usually cannot on a Mac, because the package Dubai schools teach has no macOS version. Saying that costs us nothing and saves a family from buying hours that assume practice which is not actually possible.

whyPoints.title: ICT and Computer Science kept separate
whyPoints.description: The two are routinely described as versions of one subject and they are not. A programming specialist hired for a 4IT1 candidate teaches well and irrelevantly. Teachers matched here work on ICT, and we will tell you if the entry code you quote points the other way.

whyPoints.title: Rates published, with the month on them
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is a published market rate described by what is being bought rather than by brand, each carrying the month it was checked. Half this search's ranking pages publish no price at all and two quote in a currency Dubai parents do not transact in.

whyPoints.title: Hours justified by the component split
whyPoints.description: A practical-only problem is short work. A vague written style is slower. A quote states which applies and why, so you can argue with the hours instead of only with the rate. A package length chosen in advance of seeing the work is not a plan.

whyPoints.title: Teaching and feedback, never produced work
whyPoints.description: A tutor explains, questions, reviews and gives feedback on tasks the candidate completed. No practical output is produced for a student to submit, at this level or on the vocational courses that follow, where assessed units are the student's own work.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated in the body copy
whyPoints.description: Lessons for Dubai families run online over live video. IB Gram makes no home visits in the UAE and operates no office, centre or branch here. The search phrase is targeted because parents type it, and then answered rather than quietly redefined later.

faqs.question: What does an Edexcel IGCSE ICT 4IT1 tutor cost per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates in October 2026 put qualified one-to-one teaching online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and subject specialists in international qualifications at AED 200 to 450 and above. Budget platforms advertise from the mid-forties and a premium tier marketed on examiner background reaches AED 650. Visiting in-home tutors are advertised at roughly AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the rate. Those are market figures rather than an IB Gram price list. Our figure follows a free trial lesson, because the hours needed depend on which component is actually weak.

faqs.question: Is Pearson 4IT1 ICT the same subject as 4CP0 Computer Science?
faqs.answer: No, and treating them as versions of one subject is the most expensive misunderstanding available here. 4IT1 assesses whether a candidate can use software to accomplish stated tasks and explain the role of ICT in organisations. 4CP0 assesses whether they can write and debug programs. The practical halves have nothing in common, so a programming specialist hired for an ICT candidate will teach well and irrelevantly. Confirm the entry code in writing with your school's exams officer before booking anyone, because the code determines which kind of teacher is useful.

faqs.question: Do we need to buy software for 4IT1 practice at home?
faqs.answer: Mostly no. Word processing, spreadsheets, presentation, image editing and web authoring can all be practised in free office and media software, with only small differences in function names and menu positions. The exception is database work. The package Dubai schools most commonly teach runs on Windows and has no macOS version, so a Mac-only household cannot practise that task area at home without a Windows machine or access to a school computer room. Any provider who says that is not an issue has not checked it.

faqs.question: What happens in the 4IT1 practical examination, and who provides the software?
faqs.answer: The examination centre provides and configures the environment, so there is nothing for a family to buy or install for the paper itself. Candidates complete tasks in real software to a stated brief and produce the evidence of having done so. Two things are worth confirming with the school well in advance: which packages and which versions are installed in the room where the paper is sat, and whether the practice setup at home resembles them. An unfamiliar menu layout costs minutes in a timed practical paper.

faqs.question: Why does my child understand ICT theory and still lose marks on the written paper?
faqs.answer: Because the written component is marked on answer shape rather than general understanding. Questions are set in a scenario and the mark scheme credits answers that connect to that scenario specifically. Describing a device instead of saying why it suits the stated situation earns little. Naming a safeguard without linking it to the threat in the question earns less. Listing concerns instead of stating a consequence and its cause earns least. The fix is to write an answer, mark it against the published criteria, find the missing element and rewrite it.

faqs.question: Which 4IT1 practical task area do Dubai candidates practise least?
faqs.answer: Databases, and the reason is usually access rather than attitude. The package schools teach is Windows-only in most cases, so households with Mac or tablet devices have no easy way to practise between lessons. The effect shows directly in practical marks, since database tasks reward familiarity with building a table structure, running queries against stated criteria and producing a readable report. Where home practice is genuinely impossible, the session plan should allocate more time to that area and the family should know that is why.

faqs.question: How many hours of 4IT1 support does a Dubai candidate usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends almost entirely on which component is weak, and the spread is wide. A candidate losing marks only on practical tasks often needs six to eight sessions, because practical marks respond to drilling a brief rather than to building understanding. A candidate whose written answers are consistently vague needs longer, since answer shape changes slowly. One weak on both usually needs a twelve-week block. Any provider quoting an hour count before seeing a marked paper and a practical task is quoting a package rather than a plan.

faqs.question: Is a monthly ICT package better value than paying per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Reduce both to an hourly figure before deciding. A monthly online block advertised at AED 799 for eight sessions is near AED 100 an hour, below the qualified-teacher band, which tells you something about who is likely to be teaching. A monthly in-home block at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits is roughly AED 200 to 225 an hour with travel inside it. Neither is dishonest, but they are not comparable until expressed in the same unit, and most comparisons in this market never do that step.

faqs.question: Can a private candidate sit the 4IT1 practical paper in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Only at a centre able to run the practical component, which is a narrower requirement than for a written-only subject. Confirm that capability before paying any entry fee, because a centre that accepts external candidates for written papers may not be equipped for the practical one. Entry fees for private candidates are set by the centre and vary, so collect two or three written quotes. The family also carries the deadlines, the identity documents and the timetable, since no school is chasing them on your behalf.

faqs.question: Does ICT at 16 close off A Level Computer Science?
faqs.answer: It makes it a harder step rather than an impossible one. A Level Computer Science assumes programming that the ICT course does not teach, including a substantial programmed project, so a candidate arriving from ICT starts behind. The natural routes from 4IT1 are vocational and applied: BTEC qualifications in IT or business, applied information technology courses where a school offers them, and business-facing paths where software competence is directly useful. Check which post-16 computing courses actually ran at the school last year rather than which appear in the prospectus.

faqs.question: What should I ask the school before hiring an ICT tutor?
faqs.answer: Four things, all free. The specification code and the series your child is entered for, confirmed in writing by the exams officer. The component marks from the most recent mock rather than the overall grade, because the breakdown identifies the fix. Which software packages and versions the practical component is taught and examined in. And whether the department thinks the gap is practical technique or written answers. With those four answers a quote becomes arithmetic instead of a guess.

faqs.question: Are 4IT1 lessons for Dubai families taught online or at a Dubai address?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram makes no home visits in the UAE, and home visiting is a service offered only in India. For a practical subject this works better than it sounds. The candidate shares their own screen and works in their own installation, which is where their practice will happen anyway, and the teacher sees every click at full size. Two people at one laptop see less, and the adult usually ends up taking the mouse, which teaches nothing at all.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Dubai need a permit before teaching ICT for money?
faqs.answer: Yes. An individual giving paid private lessons requires a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. The MoHRE service listing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Note what it does not tell you: eligible applicants include university students and school students aged 15 to 18, so it confirms legality rather than teaching quality.

faqs.question: Can a tutor produce the practical work for my child to submit?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody here will. A tutor explains, questions, reviews and gives feedback on tasks the candidate completed themselves. 4IT1 carries no coursework and the practical component is sat under examination conditions, so the exposure at this level is low. It rises on the vocational courses that follow, where assessed units are produced over time and must be the student's own work. Any provider offering to supply finished output for submission is offering malpractice, and the consequence of that falls on the student rather than on them.

faqs.question: How does the Dubai school fee freeze affect a tutoring budget?
faqs.answer: It fixes the largest education line for the year, which changes how the discretionary one should be judged. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not increase for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. For a household whose fees are flat, a short practical-only block at the qualified band, which is roughly AED 900 to 2,400 for six to eight sessions, is a smaller decision than it looks in isolation. The arithmetic is worth doing annually rather than monthly.

intro.heading: Pricing 4MA1 support honestly: the hour, the hours, and what each one gives back
paragraphs: Published market rates in Dubai, read in October 2026, put a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, a tutor travelling to the family at roughly AED 180 to AED 500, and an IGCSE or A Level specialist at roughly AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Budget online provision starts far lower: EdFlik lists from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. At the top, BartyED publishes AED 650. Those belong to the providers named. None of them is an IB Gram price.

A rate on its own decides nothing, because the question a family is really asking is what the total will be. Twelve hours at AED 300 is cheaper than forty hours at AED 150, and which of those a candidate needs depends entirely on why marks are being lost. This is why the first number worth producing is not a rate but a marked script. A candidate surrendering marks to unstated working and premature rounding can be fixed in a handful of hours. A candidate with real gaps across algebra and the Higher block is looking at a term.

The useful unit, then, is dirhams per mark recovered, and it varies enormously between causes. Written method and calculator discipline are the cheapest repairs available in 4MA1 because they recover marks the candidate has already earned mathematically and then failed to collect. Topic gaps cost more per mark because the content has to be taught and then practised to fluency. Timing is usually free, in the sense that it resolves once the first two are fixed. A tutor who sells hours without ranking them this way is selling volume.

Timing matters as much as ranking. The same budget spent fortnightly across two years buys algebraic fluency, brings the hardest Higher content forward so the school teaches it a second time for nothing, and allows the tier question to be settled before the centre's entry deadline. The identical sum spent as a block in the last six weeks buys paper discipline and damage limitation. Both are legitimate purchases. They are not the same purchase, and a provider should say which one you are making.

There is a third cost almost no page in this market mentions, and it is the largest of all: the tier. A capable candidate entered for Foundation cannot be awarded a top grade whatever they do, and the knock-on effect on sixth-form maths options and then on university routes is worth more than the entire tutoring budget. Changing that entry costs nothing at all, provided somebody notices before the centre's deadline. Noticing is the single highest-return thing a diagnostic paper does.

Lessons for Dubai families are delivered one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with slots moved to post-Iftar timing through Ramadan. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; that service runs only in India. On a written, calculator-permitted subject with no practical component, the shared workspace is what matters, and the saving on travel is real rather than rhetorical. The sections below put numbers on all of it.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-maths-a-4ma1-home-tu.programmesIntro: Where a candidate sits on the Pearson maths route changes both the hourly figure a family will be quoted and the number of hours that figure has to be multiplied by. These are the four stages, costed rather than described.

programmes.name: Lower secondary maths, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: The cheapest hours in the whole route, because the work is building fluency rather than repairing a grade under deadline. Algebraic manipulation practised to automaticity at thirteen removes most of what a Year 11 family would otherwise pay to fix. Market rates at this level sit at the lower end of every band, and sessions can be fortnightly without losing momentum.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools set maths from Year 7 or 8 in most centres, and set movement is where families first get a signal. A candidate in a middle set for two years running is usually on a Foundation trajectory that nobody has stated out loud. Asking the department what tier a set is heading for, at thirteen rather than at fifteen, is a free question with a large financial consequence.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1)
programmes.description: Two equally weighted written papers, calculator permitted in both, no coursework, tiered into Foundation and Higher. This is where almost all tutoring spend in the route concentrates, and where it is most often spent in the wrong order: families buy content coverage when the script shows method losses. Confirm the specification detail on qualifications.pearson.com for your centre's version.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai centres enter 4MA1 in the May/June series or in November, and a few use both. The entry deadline, not the exam date, is the financially significant date in the year, because it fixes the tier. Ask the maths department in writing for the tier, the code and the internal deadline for changing it, and treat the answer as a budgeting document.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Further Pure Mathematics (4PM1)
programmes.description: An additional qualification rather than an alternative, reaching into calculus, series and coordinate geometry. Financially it is a poor purchase for a candidate working hard for a 7, because the hours it consumes come straight out of 4MA1 preparation and the likely outcome is two mediocre grades instead of one strong one. For a candidate already finishing Higher papers early, it is a good use of the same money.
programmes.countryNote: Only a minority of Dubai schools teach 4PM1, usually those with large maths cohorts and an International A Level sixth form. Where it is not taught, paying a tutor to deliver it from scratch is an expensive way to buy a signal that a grade 9 on 4MA1 would send more cheaply and more reliably.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International A Level Mathematics
programmes.description: Where the cost of a weak IGCSE foundation finally lands. A candidate who obtained a grade 8 through procedural recall rather than algebraic fluency typically needs paid support through the first pure unit, at sixth-form rates, which are higher. Money spent securing genuine fluency at sixteen is the cheapest insurance available against that bill.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai sixth forms run either the modular International A Level or the linear UK specification, and the two have different assessment rhythms and therefore different points at which a family discovers a problem. Ask which one the school teaches before Year 12 begins; the modular route surfaces a gap earlier, which is cheaper even though it feels worse.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-maths-a-4ma1-home-tu.subjectsIntro: 4MA1 strands differ sharply in what they cost to repair. These are ranked roughly by marks recovered per hour of paid work, which is a more useful ordering for a budget than the specification's own.

subjects.name: Written method and layout
subjects.description: Recovers marks the candidate already earned mathematically and then failed to collect. The work is habit formation through repeated marking of their own scripts with method marks itemised, so it needs several short cycles rather than one long session. Typically the highest return per dirham of anything on this list.

subjects.name: Rounding and stored-value discipline
subjects.levels: One session plus two marked papers
subjects.description: Premature approximation puts a correct answer outside the accepted range, repeatedly, in both papers. One hour on calculator habits and two marked papers to confirm the change has stuck is usually the whole intervention. Very cheap, and almost never diagnosed without a marked script.

subjects.name: Geometry reasoning vocabulary
subjects.description: Reasoning marks are awarded for the written justification, not the number. A candidate with the right angles and no named theorems is losing one mark per question across the paper. A short fixed vocabulary per theorem, written even when the answer feels obvious, closes it quickly.

subjects.name: Upper and lower bounds
subjects.description: A predictable Higher loss with a characteristic wrong answer: the rounded value used where the bound belongs. The fix is a written framework the candidate reproduces each time rather than a remembered rule, then marked practice until the framework is automatic.

subjects.name: Area and volume scale factors
subjects.description: Candidates apply the length factor to an area or a volume and lose the whole question. Cheap to fix and expensive to leave, because it appears across mensuration and similarity questions on both papers rather than in one place.

subjects.name: Histograms with unequal class widths
subjects.description: Frequency density treated as frequency. A single session with marked practice afterwards generally settles it. Worth buying early, because the same misunderstanding quietly damages cumulative frequency interpretation as well.

subjects.name: Sine and cosine rules, including the ambiguous case
subjects.description: Losses here almost always trace back to no diagram having been drawn. Making the diagram the first non-negotiable line of the method costs an hour; the ambiguous case and three-dimensional problems need two or three more with marked practice between them.

subjects.name: Factorising and algebraic fractions
subjects.levels: Six to eight weeks of short daily work
subjects.description: The load-bearing strand, and the most expensive to repair because fluency cannot be taught in a session. It needs short daily practice over weeks. It is also the strand that determines whether Higher tier is the right entry, so the money spent here changes the tier conversation.

subjects.name: Differentiation and turning points
subjects.levels: A term if started late, half that if started early
subjects.description: Usually taught in the spring of Year 11 and practised too little, which is why it behaves like unlearned material under pressure. Meeting it with a tutor in the autumn costs fewer hours than meeting it in April, because the school teaches it a second time for free.

subjects.name: Vector geometry and proof
subjects.description: Column vector arithmetic is accessible; proof is not, and candidates lose whole questions for an answer with no route through the diagram. Expressing a path as a sum of named vectors before any algebra converts the hardest marks on the paper into bookkeeping.

subjects.name: Functions, composite and inverse
subjects.description: Notation errors and transformation direction account for most of the loss. Worth buying as a pair with the calculus work, since both appear in the same part of the Higher content and the same candidates miss both.

subjects.name: Paper timing and question order
subjects.description: Usually resolves on its own once method and rounding are fixed, because a candidate who writes method does not have to re-derive under pressure. Paying for timing drills before fixing the other two is the commonest way to waste money on 4MA1.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges for 4MA1 help, and what the number buys
paragraphs: The published spread in Dubai covers more than an order of magnitude, and the bands are not interchangeable. At the bottom, budget online provision starts from AED 45 to AED 65 on EdFlik's own listing and from AED 33 to AED 52 on Tutopiya's. A qualified subject tutor runs about AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist IGCSE and A Level provision sits at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, TutorChase publishing AED 270, and BartyED publishing AED 650 at the examiner tier. All read in October 2026.

What separates those bands for a maths candidate specifically is marking. A cheap hour is live help with whatever question is in front of the candidate, which has genuine value when the problem is that they are stuck on tonight's homework. It has close to no value when the problem is that they lose four of five marks on every multi-step question, because diagnosing that requires somebody to mark a full script against the published scheme and then itemise the losses. Nobody does that work inside an AED 50 hour.

In-home provision adds a journey to the bill. The published band of roughly AED 180 to AED 500 contains forty to eighty minutes of Dubai driving whether or not it appears as a line item, and on Palm Jumeirah or out at Studio City it contains more. It also narrows the pool to tutors willing to make that trip weekly for two years, which on Higher-tier calculus and vector proof is a meaningful constraint rather than a theoretical one.

IB Gram does not publish a price list on this page and will not quote one before a script has been marked. The first hour is free, no card details are taken, and a rate and an honest number of hours follow the diagnosis. A figure offered before anybody has seen how the candidate loses marks is not a price; it is a bet on volume, and the bet is placed in the seller's favour.

sections.heading: Cost per mark: ranking the 4MA1 repairs by what they give back
paragraphs: Hours are not interchangeable, and the difference between them is large enough to change a family's total spend by a factor of three. The cheapest marks in 4MA1 are the ones the candidate has already earned mathematically and then failed to collect: working that does not show the step the mark scheme rewards, and intermediate values rounded before the end. Both recover marks across every multi-step question on both papers, and both are fixed in a handful of hours because the underlying mathematics is already there.

The next tier up is the predictable topic losses, each with a characteristic wrong answer: bounds, area and volume scale factors, histograms with unequal class widths, the ambiguous case in the sine rule, and geometric vector proof. These cost more because the content has to be taught and then practised, but they are bounded. One to three hours each plus marked practice, and they close. A family with a limited budget should buy these in the order the marked script ranks them, not in the order a textbook presents them.

The most expensive repair is algebraic fluency, because fluency is not teachable in a session. Factorising and algebraic fractions need short daily work over six to eight weeks, and no amount of paid explanation substitutes for that practice. The money spent here is worth it, because the same fluency gates most Higher marks and determines whether Higher is the right tier at all, but a family should know they are buying a programme rather than a fix.

Timing comes last deliberately. A candidate who writes proper method does not have to re-derive their way through hard questions under pressure, and one who keeps full precision does not redo failed calculations. Fixing those two usually returns several minutes across a paper with no work on speed at all. Paying for timing drills first is the single commonest misallocation of a 4MA1 budget in this market.

sections.heading: The most expensive mistake in 4MA1 costs nothing to avoid
paragraphs: An avoidable Foundation entry is the largest financial event in a 4MA1 year, and it does not appear on any invoice. A Foundation entry caps the grade at the lower part of the scale. A candidate capable of a 7 who is entered for Foundation receives a grade that closes doors in a sixth-form maths conversation, and then in a university one, and no amount of later tutoring reopens them at the same price. The correction, made in time, costs a family nothing at all.

The reason it happens is structural rather than negligent. Set placement in Dubai schools is often made at thirteen on evidence from twelve, tiers follow sets, and nobody in the chain is required to tell a parent what tier their child is on. Families then receive report grades that look reassuring because they are reported against the tier the candidate is in. A steady run of strong marks in a middle set can mean a candidate is comfortably at the top of a ceiling they should not be under.

The window to act is set by the centre's Pearson entry deadline, which sits months ahead of the papers and, for a summer series, often before the Christmas break. Two emails settle it: one asking the maths department which tier the candidate is entered for, the other asking the internal deadline for changing it. Neither costs anything. The evidence that answers the question is one timed paper at each tier, marked against the published scheme, which is a two-week exercise.

The same logic runs in the other direction and is equally expensive. A candidate who is not secure on factorising, who draws no diagrams and loses the geometry reasoning marks will often score fewer raw marks on Higher than they would have on Foundation, because the accessible marks are thinner. Pushing a struggling candidate up a tier to signal ambition costs them a grade. Both errors come from the same reluctance to look at a marked script and say what it shows.

sections.heading: What the school already provides, and what you should not pay twice for
paragraphs: Dubai schools run more free maths intervention than most families use. Departmental catch-up clinics, lunchtime sessions, after-school revision in the term before a series, sixth-form peer tutoring, and in many centres a full mock programme with marked scripts returned. Before a family buys anything, the useful exercise is to find out exactly what the school offers, when it runs, and whether the candidate is attending. A paid hour that duplicates a free session the candidate skipped is pure waste.

Mock marking is the clearest case. If the department marks full mock papers against the published scheme and returns them, a family already has the diagnostic document that a tutor would otherwise charge to produce. Bring it to the first lesson. A tutor reading an existing marked mock can go straight to the plan rather than spending an hour establishing what is already known, which is a genuine saving rather than a notional one.

What the school cannot realistically provide is the thing worth paying for: sustained one-to-one marking of a single candidate's working, week after week, with the method marks itemised line by line. A teacher with twenty-five candidates and two other year groups marks holistically out of necessity. That is not a criticism of the teaching; it is an arithmetic fact about class size. One-to-one time is the only place the method-mark habit reliably transfers.

The second thing a school rarely does well is bring hard content forward. A scheme of work covers calculus in the spring of Year 11 because that is where it fits for everybody, and a candidate who needs to meet it twice has to find the first encounter elsewhere. That is a defensible use of paid hours in the autumn, and it is substantially cheaper than paid hours in April when the same material is competing with nine other subjects.

sections.heading: Group sets, small groups and one-to-one, priced per useful minute
paragraphs: Group tuition in Dubai is cheaper per hour and the arithmetic looks compelling until you divide by attention. In a group of four, a candidate gets roughly a quarter of the tutor's attention for a quarter of the price, so per minute of individual attention nothing has been saved. What a group genuinely buys is a taught explanation delivered once to several people, which is efficient when the whole group shares the same gap and worthless when they do not.

For 4MA1 the split is reasonably clear. A group works well for teaching a topic nobody in the room has met: bounds, histograms, the sine rule. It works poorly for everything else, because the remaining losses are script-specific. Four candidates in a room lose marks for four different reasons, and a tutor marking four scripts properly in one hour is not marking any of them properly. The method-mark work, which is where most recoverable marks sit, is irreducibly individual.

Tuition centres in Dubai towers frequently sell a monthly figure rather than an hourly one, and the published monthly patterns in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-range, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Those are the market's figures, not ours.

The sensible use of a mixed budget is deliberate rather than accidental. Buy group hours where a topic needs teaching to a cohort, and individual hours where a script needs marking. Families who make that split on purpose get more from the same total than families who pick one format for everything, and any tutor should be willing to tell you which of the two jobs a given hour is doing.

sections.heading: Resit economics: November entries, retakes and the private candidate route
paragraphs: Pearson makes International GCSE available in May/June and in November, which means a Dubai candidate has two chances in one academic year rather than one. The published reference points are worth knowing: the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Confirm any date against the live official timetable on qualifications.pearson.com.

Financially, the November route changes the whole risk profile. A January result leaves a full term to decide on a May retake, with the candidate now knowing exactly how they perform under real conditions, which is information no mock reliably provides. A family paying for support in that configuration is buying targeted hours against a known weakness. A family with a May-only entry and a disappointing August result is buying a full year's course again, usually at a worse moment.

Entry fees are set by the centre, not by Pearson's list price alone, and a school will add administration costs for a private or late entry. No figure is published here because no reliable sourced number exists for Dubai centres, and an invented one would be worse than silence. Ask the examinations officer directly what an additional subject entry and a private candidate entry each cost at that centre, before building a retake into a budget.

The private candidate route is also narrower than families expect. Not every Dubai school accepts external candidates, and those that do set their own conditions and deadlines. For a written subject with no practical component, 4MA1 is one of the more straightforward qualifications to sit externally, but availability still has to be confirmed centre by centre and well ahead of the entry deadline rather than after a disappointing result.

sections.heading: Two years or one term: when the same money works hardest
paragraphs: Timing changes the value of a tutoring dirham more than the hourly rate does. The same AED 6,000 spent across two academic years as fortnightly hours buys fluency, brings hard content forward so the school teaches it twice, and allows a tier conversation to happen before the entry deadline. Spent as a block in the final six weeks, it buys paper practice and a plan for damage limitation. Both are legitimate purchases; they are not the same purchase.

The strongest case for early spend is the compounding effect on algebra. Factorising and algebraic fractions gate most of the Higher content, so a candidate who becomes fluent in Year 10 needs fewer hours on everything that follows. The strongest case for late spend is simply that families do not always have the choice: a problem surfaces in February and the money has to work with what is left. A tutor should say plainly which of those two situations a family is in.

There is a third pattern that is more common than either and worse than both: weekly hours booked in September and cancelled half the time through the year. A fortnightly slot kept every time delivers more than a weekly slot kept every other week, because the work between sessions is what produces the progress and a cancelled session leaves nothing to mark. Families who are honest about their calendar at the start spend less and get more.

A fourth consideration is the number of subjects. A Dubai candidate sitting nine or ten subjects cannot be tutored in all of them, and trying produces a timetable with no time left to work. The useful conversation is which three subjects decide the sixth-form offer the candidate wants, and funding those properly instead of funding everything thinly. Maths is almost always one of the three, which is an argument for depth rather than for breadth.
