sections.heading: Invoices, VAT, cancellations and the questions to settle before paying
paragraphs: Most disputes in this market are not about teaching quality. They are about terms nobody wrote down. Before any money changes hands, five things should be settled in writing: whether the quoted figure is the figure you pay, whether an invoice will be issued, what happens to a session cancelled with a day's notice, whether marking a full paper is billed as tutoring time, and how the arrangement ends. All five are reasonable questions and a reluctance to answer any of them is itself an answer.

On tax, this page states only what can be stated. The UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees is not asserted here because no Federal Tax Authority citation has been read for it, and a page this widely read should not guess at a tax position. What a parent can insist on is clarity about the final number: inclusive or exclusive, invoiced or not, and with a tax registration number shown if the provider holds one. Ask, and keep the reply.

Marking is the term most often left vague and the one that matters most for maths. A full 4MA1 paper marked properly against the published scheme, with method marks itemised, takes real time. Some providers include it, some bill it, and some simply do not do it and say they do. Ask specifically whether full papers are marked, by whom, and whether that time appears on the invoice. The answer tells you which product you are actually buying.

Permit status belongs in the same conversation. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services with a stated two working day completion time. Individuals tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts has been published. Since the permit is free and quick, an evasive answer is informative in itself.

sections.heading: Why the search says home tutor and the lesson runs over live video
paragraphs: The phrase in this page's address is what Dubai parents type, and targeting it honestly is better than targeting it quietly. What families mean by a home tutor is one-to-one attention on their own child's work, at a time that survives the school run, without a group. All of that is deliverable over video. What is not deliverable is somebody arriving at the door, and IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service it runs only in India.

For maths this costs a family less than it would for a practical subject, because what matters is the shared workspace rather than the room. The candidate writes and the tutor watches the working appear line by line, so a correction lands at the step where the error happened instead of after the answer is already wrong. Scripts are uploaded between sessions and come back with method marks itemised. Very little of 4MA1 depends on physical proximity.

What the format buys in return is specificity. Higher-tier calculus, geometric vector proof and bounds are not general maths teaching, and selecting a tutor by driving distance from Palm Jumeirah or Studio City is a poor way to find somebody who marks those questions every week. Removing the journey also removes the travel premium that sits inside the published in-home band, which on a two-year arrangement is a real sum rather than a rhetorical one.

The limits are worth naming too. A tutor in the room can sit next to a reluctant fifteen-year-old and simply be present until they begin working, and some candidates genuinely need that more than they need a specialist. A family whose binding problem is motivation rather than marks should weigh it honestly. What this page offers instead is a free first hour with a marked script on the table, after which both sides know whether the arrangement is worth paying for.

process.title: Ask the school three free questions
process.description: The specification code, the tier the candidate is entered for, and the internal deadline for changing it. Then ask what free intervention the department runs and whether your child attends. Four answers, no cost, and they determine whether any paid hour is needed at all and what it should be spent on.

process.title: Find a marked mock before paying for one
process.description: If the department marks full mock papers against the published scheme and returns them, you already hold the diagnostic document. Bring it. A tutor reading an existing marked script goes straight to the plan instead of charging an hour to establish what the school has already established.

process.title: Take the free first hour with the script
process.description: One hour, no card details, with the paper and the marking in front of both of you. The tutor classifies the losses into method, rounding, content and timing and says roughly what each costs per paper. By the end you have a ranked list and an honest hour count, not a package.

process.title: Buy the cheapest repairs first
process.description: Method and rounding before topics, topics in the order the script ranks them, algebra as a programme rather than a session, timing last. Spending in that order routinely costs a family a third of what spending in the reverse order costs for the same grade movement.

process.title: Settle the terms in writing
process.description: Whether the quoted figure is the figure you pay, whether an invoice is issued, what a cancelled session costs, whether full-paper marking is billed, and how the arrangement ends. Five questions, asked once, before any money moves. A reluctance to answer any of them is itself useful information.

process.title: Review against the next marked paper
process.description: Progress is judged on a script, not on a feeling. If the second marked paper shows the method and rounding losses have gone, the work stops there and nobody sells you more. If it does not, the plan was wrong and changing it is our problem rather than yours.

whyPoints.title: No quote before a marked script
whyPoints.description: A rate and an hour count are proposed only after a full paper has been marked against the published scheme and the losses classified. A figure offered before that is a bet on volume rather than a price, and the bet is placed in the seller's favour. The diagnostic hour costs nothing.

whyPoints.title: Repairs ranked by what they give back
whyPoints.description: Written method and rounding discipline are bought before topic gaps, topic gaps in the order the script ranks them, and timing drills last. That ordering is the difference between a handful of hours and a term of them for the same grade movement, and it is rarely what a package sells.

whyPoints.description: An avoidable Foundation entry costs more than any tutoring budget and nothing to correct, provided somebody notices before the centre's deadline. The first thing a diagnostic paper is used for is that conversation, and the second is telling a family when their school's free intervention already covers the problem.

faqs.question: What does 4MA1 tutoring cost per hour for a Dubai family?
faqs.answer: Published market figures read in October 2026 put a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. Budget online provision starts lower, EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. Specialist IGCSE and A Level tutors sit at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, TutorChase publishing AED 270, and BartyED publishing AED 650. Those belong to the providers named. Our own first hour is free and a rate follows a marked script.

faqs.question: Which 4MA1 repair gives back the most marks per dirham?
faqs.answer: Written method, followed by rounding discipline. Both recover marks the candidate has already earned mathematically and then failed to collect, so no new content has to be taught. A candidate who reaches the right answer with three lines of calculator arithmetic loses most of the marks on every multi-step question, twice over across two papers. Three or four short cycles of marking their own scripts with method marks itemised typically closes it. Topic gaps cost more per mark, and timing drills are usually free once the first two are fixed.

faqs.question: What does an avoidable Foundation tier entry cost a family later?
faqs.answer: More than the whole tutoring budget, and it appears on no invoice. Foundation caps the grade at the lower part of the scale, so a candidate capable of a 7 receives a grade that limits sixth-form maths options and then university routes, and no later spending reopens them at the same price. Correcting the entry before the centre's Pearson deadline costs nothing at all. For a summer series that deadline often falls before Christmas, which is why the tier question belongs in September, not in March.

faqs.question: Is my child's school already providing maths help I would be paying for twice?
faqs.answer: Very possibly. Dubai schools run catch-up clinics, lunchtime sessions, after-school revision before a series and, in many centres, a full mock programme with marked scripts returned. A paid hour that duplicates a free session your child skipped is pure waste. Find out exactly what the department offers, when it runs and whether your child attends, before buying anything. If the school marks full mocks against the published scheme, you already hold the diagnostic document a tutor would otherwise charge to produce.

faqs.question: How does a small group of four compare with one-to-one on price for 4MA1?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per hour, no cheaper per minute of individual attention. In a group of four a candidate gets roughly a quarter of the tutor's time for roughly a quarter of the price. What a group genuinely buys is one explanation delivered to several people, which works when they all share the same unmet topic and fails when they do not. Four candidates lose marks for four different reasons, and the method-mark work where most recoverable marks sit is irreducibly individual.

faqs.question: What does it cost to enter 4MA1 as a private candidate in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The centre sets it, and it includes the school's own administration charge on top of the entry, so no figure is published here; no reliable sourced number exists for Dubai centres and an invented one would be worse than silence. Ask the examinations officer directly what an additional subject entry and a private candidate entry each cost at that centre. Also confirm that the school accepts external candidates at all, because many do not, and ask before the entry deadline rather than after a disappointing result.

faqs.question: Is a November entry plus a possible May retake more expensive than one summer attempt?
faqs.answer: In entry fees, yes. In total cost, usually not. Pearson offers International GCSE in May/June and November, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so a November candidate has a real result and a full term to decide. That means buying targeted hours against an evidenced weakness. A May-only candidate with a disappointing August result is buying a year's course again, at a worse moment, with less information. Confirm all dates on the live official timetable at qualifications.pearson.com.

faqs.question: Does starting 4MA1 support in Year 10 cost less overall than a Year 11 rescue?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, because of what the early money compounds into. Factorising and algebraic fractions gate most of the Higher content, so fluency bought in Year 10 reduces the hours needed on everything that follows. Early spend also lets the hardest content be met in the autumn and then taught again by the school in the spring at no cost, and it puts the tier conversation before the entry deadline. Late spend buys paper discipline and damage limitation, which is a legitimate purchase but a different one.

faqs.question: What should a 4MA1 tutoring invoice actually show?
faqs.answer: The hours delivered, the rate, whether the figure is the one you pay, and a tax registration number if the provider holds one. This page does not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition because no Federal Tax Authority citation has been read for it, and a page like this one should not guess at a tax position. What you can insist on is clarity about the final number before paying, and a written reply you keep. Vagueness about the total is worth treating as a warning sign.

faqs.question: Do we pay for a session the candidate misses?
faqs.answer: With us, a session cancelled with notice is not charged, and that is written down rather than implied. It is worth settling this with any provider before money moves, because it is one of the five terms that cause most disputes in this market, along with whether the quoted figure is the final figure, whether an invoice is issued, whether full-paper marking is billed, and how the arrangement ends. Ask all five once, at the start. A reluctance to answer any of them is informative.

faqs.question: Is marking a full 4MA1 paper billed as tutoring time?
faqs.answer: Ask, because providers differ and this is the term most often left vague. Marking a full paper properly against the published scheme, with method marks itemised line by line, takes real time. Some include it in the rate, some bill it separately, and some do not do it at all while implying they do. Ask specifically whether full papers are marked, by whom, and whether that time appears on the invoice. The answer tells you which product you are buying more clearly than any rate does.

faqs.question: My child sits ten subjects. How many should we actually fund tutoring for?
faqs.answer: Three at most, and usually fewer. A candidate tutored in everything has no time left to do the work that tutoring generates, which is where the progress actually comes from. The productive conversation is which three subjects decide the sixth-form offer your child wants, then funding those properly rather than funding ten thinly. Maths is almost always one of the three because it gates so many post-sixteen routes, which is an argument for depth in it rather than for breadth across the timetable.

faqs.question: Does a higher hourly rate buy a better 4MA1 tutor?
faqs.answer: It buys a different product rather than reliably a better person. The main thing the upper bands include is marking: full scripts assessed against the published scheme with the losses classified, plus preparation between sessions. That work does not happen inside an AED 50 hour, and for a candidate losing marks to unstated method it is the only work that matters. For a candidate who simply needs tonight's homework unblocked, the cheaper hour is genuinely sufficient and paying more is waste.

faqs.question: If we could only afford four hours, what should they be spent on?
faqs.answer: One timed paper marked against the published scheme, one session on written method and layout, one on stored-value working and rounding, and one more marked paper to confirm the change held. That sequence recovers marks the candidate has already earned mathematically and then failed to collect, which is the cheapest grade movement available in 4MA1. It also produces evidence for the tier conversation. Four hours spent on topic coverage instead, chosen without a script, is the commonest way this budget is wasted.

faqs.question: Our search said home tutor, so where does a 4MA1 lesson actually happen?
faqs.answer: Over live video, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time, with slots moved to post-Iftar timing through Ramadan. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; that service runs only in India. The candidate writes and the tutor watches the working appear line by line, so corrections land at the step where the error happened. Removing the journey also removes the travel premium inside the published in-home band of roughly AED 180 to AED 500, which over two years is a real saving.

faqs.question: Does a 4MA1 tutor in Dubai need a permit, and does it cost us anything?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and it costs the family nothing. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services under the service name Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two working day completion time. Individuals tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts has been published, so none is quoted.

A rate and an hour count follow that conversation rather than preceding it. Lessons run one-to-one over live video; no tutor is sent to a UAE address.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-maths-a-4ma1-tutor.tutorsIntro: These tutors work specifically on Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1) with Dubai candidates: tier decisions, topic-to-paper mapping, method-mark discipline, and timed paper practice through the May and November series.

intro.heading: What 4MA1 asks of a candidate, and what a tutor can actually change
paragraphs: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A, specification code 4MA1, is assessed by two written papers. Both allow a calculator, both carry equal weight, and there is no coursework component. The qualification is tiered: a Foundation entry sits papers 1F and 2F, a Higher entry sits 1H and 2H, and the tier decides the range of grades available before the candidate writes a single line. Confirm the current paper durations, mark totals and grade ranges against the specification on qualifications.pearson.com, because those are set by the version your Dubai school is teaching.

That structure has a specific consequence for tutoring. Because there is no coursework and no non-calculator paper, every mark in 4MA1 is won in a timed written environment with a machine on the desk. A candidate who is strong on content and weak on written method will underperform their ability by a grade or more, consistently, in both papers. That failure is not fixed by covering more topics. It is fixed by changing how working is laid out, which is a habit, and habits take weeks of marked practice rather than one explanation.

The second thing a diagnosis has to establish is the tier. Foundation and Higher are not easy and hard versions of the same paper; they are different papers with different content and a different grade ceiling. A capable candidate parked on Foundation cannot reach the top grades however well they perform, and a struggling candidate pushed onto Higher often scores lower than they would have on Foundation because the accessible marks are thinner on the ground. Getting that call right is worth more than any amount of revision.

What a 4MA1 session can realistically change, in order of return, is: written method and the marks awarded for it; the three or four topics where the candidate is reliably losing whole questions; calculator discipline, particularly rounding and premature approximation; and timing across a full paper. What it cannot change is the entry the school has already submitted, so the first job in any Dubai household is to find out in writing which tier and which series the centre has entered the candidate for.

There is also a Dubai-specific wrinkle worth naming at the start. Pearson makes International GCSE available in May/June and in November, and a number of Dubai centres use both. A candidate entered in November gets a result in January and four months to decide whether to retake in the summer, armed with real evidence of how they perform under pressure. A candidate entered only in May has a single attempt. Which pattern a school follows changes the whole shape of a tutoring plan, and most families never think to ask.

The rest of this page works through the content: both papers and what sits on them, the tier decision and the window in which it can still be moved, where marks actually go missing topic by topic, the Higher-only material that decides a top grade, calculator and formulae-sheet discipline, how 4MA1 compares with Mathematics B and when Further Pure Maths 4PM1 becomes relevant, the Pearson calendar counted backwards, and how the lessons themselves run for Dubai families.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-maths-a-4ma1-tutor.programmesIntro: 4MA1 sits on a route, and which rung a candidate is on changes what a session should spend its hour doing. These are the four stages Dubai families ask about around Pearson maths.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1)
programmes.description: The mainstream Pearson maths qualification in international schools, assessed by two equally weighted written papers with a calculator permitted in both and no coursework. Tiered into Foundation and Higher, with the tier fixed at entry by the centre. The content splits into number, algebra, geometry and trigonometry, and statistics and probability, with a substantial block of Higher-only material.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai centres enter 4MA1 in the May/June series or in November. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the only dates worth working to are the ones the school's examinations officer confirms against the live official timetable. A Dubai parent cannot establish the tier from a report card either; it has to be asked for directly, in writing, from the maths department.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Further Pure Mathematics (4PM1)
programmes.description: A separate qualification taken in addition to 4MA1 by candidates heading for maths-heavy A Levels. It extends into calculus, series, coordinate geometry, trigonometric identities and proof at a level 4MA1 only touches. It is not a substitute for 4MA1 and is not tiered in the same way, and it demands genuine algebraic fluency rather than enthusiasm.
programmes.countryNote: A minority of Dubai schools offer 4PM1, usually the ones with large maths cohorts and a sixth form running International A Level Mathematics. Where it is not offered, a candidate aiming at engineering or economics is better served by securing a grade 9 on 4MA1 Higher and reading ahead into A Level content than by trying to self-enter for a qualification with no teaching behind it.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International A Level Mathematics
programmes.description: The common destination for a strong 4MA1 candidate in a British-curriculum Dubai sixth form. Pure maths units build directly on the Higher algebra, trigonometry and calculus introduced at IGCSE, and the step is felt most by candidates who got their IGCSE grade through procedural recall rather than algebraic fluency.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai sixth forms vary in whether they run the modular International A Level or the linear UK specification, and the two have different assessment rhythms. Ask which one the school teaches before Year 12 begins, because it changes when the first external assessment lands and therefore when a candidate first discovers whether their IGCSE algebra was solid.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation
programmes.description: The alternative at sixteen in Dubai's International Baccalaureate schools. Analysis and Approaches is the proof-and-calculus route; Applications and Interpretation leans on modelling, statistics and technology. A 4MA1 Higher candidate with strong algebra is well prepared for Analysis and Approaches; one who relied on a calculator to do the thinking usually is not.
programmes.countryNote: International Baccalaureate students are about seven per cent of Dubai's private-school enrolment and three further IB schools open for 2026-27. Families choosing between the two maths routes should check the entry requirements of the specific universities they have in mind rather than relying on general advice, since expectations differ markedly between institutions and faculties.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-maths-a-4ma1-tutor.subjectsIntro: 4MA1 is best diagnosed by content strand rather than by grade, because a candidate rarely loses marks evenly. These are the twelve strands a tutor works through, with where each one typically fails in a Dubai cohort.

subjects.name: Number, bounds and standard form
subjects.description: Upper and lower bounds are the single most reliably dropped Higher topic in this strand, because candidates calculate with the rounded figure rather than the bound. Work here is on recognising a bounds question from its wording and on choosing which bound goes in the numerator and which in the denominator.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation and algebraic fractions
subjects.description: The load-bearing strand for the whole qualification. Candidates who cannot factorise confidently lose marks in geometry, trigonometry and calculus questions that were never about algebra. Sessions drill factorising, simplifying compound fractions and rearranging formulae until the step is automatic rather than reasoned out each time.

subjects.name: Equations, inequalities and simultaneous equations
subjects.description: Linear work is usually secure; the losses come from quadratic simultaneous equations and from inequality notation, where candidates solve correctly and then write the answer in a form that cannot be awarded. Practice is on the final line as much as on the method.

subjects.name: Sequences, series and the nth term
subjects.description: Linear nth term is well taught almost everywhere. Quadratic sequences and the recognition of a geometric pattern are not, and they appear often enough to matter. The fix is pattern-recognition practice rather than a formula, since a candidate who reaches for the wrong family loses the whole question.

subjects.name: Functions, graphs and transformations
subjects.description: Function notation, composite and inverse functions, and the transformations of a curve. Candidates confuse the direction of a horizontal shift with monotonous regularity. Sessions use the candidate's own sketch rather than a memorised rule, because the rule is what they will misremember under pressure.

subjects.name: Geometry, angle reasoning and circle theorems
subjects.description: The marks here are awarded for the written reason, not the number. A candidate who writes the correct angle without naming the theorem loses the reasoning mark every time. Work is on a short, repeatable vocabulary for each theorem and on the habit of writing it down even when the answer feels obvious.

subjects.name: Trigonometry in two and three dimensions
subjects.description: Right-angled work is usually fine. The sine and cosine rules, the ambiguous case and three-dimensional problems are where scripts break down, almost always because no diagram was drawn. Sessions make the diagram non-negotiable before any calculation and treat it as part of the method.

subjects.name: Mensuration, similarity and scale factors
subjects.description: Area and volume scale factors are a predictable loss: candidates apply the length factor to an area or a volume. The remedy is a single worked framework the candidate writes out each time rather than a remembered result, and a habit of stating which factor is being used.

subjects.name: Vectors
subjects.description: Column vector arithmetic is accessible and geometric vector proof is not. Candidates lose marks for an answer with no route through the diagram. Work centres on expressing a path as a sum of named vectors before any algebra, which converts a hard proof into bookkeeping.

subjects.name: Probability and set notation
subjects.description: Tree diagrams and conditional probability, plus Venn and set notation where the specification includes it. The frequent error is treating a without-replacement problem as independent. Sessions use the candidate's own tree rather than a formula, so the denominator change is visible on the page.

subjects.name: Statistics: histograms and cumulative frequency
subjects.description: Histograms with unequal class widths are the recurring loss, because frequency density is treated as frequency. Interpretation marks on cumulative frequency graphs are also routinely missed through imprecise reading. Both are correctable in a single session with marked practice afterwards.

subjects.name: Differentiation, turning points and kinematics
subjects.description: The Higher calculus block: differentiating polynomials, finding and classifying turning points, and applying rates of change to motion. This is the material that most often separates a grade 7 from a grade 9, and it is also the content a Dubai candidate is most likely to have met briefly and never practised to fluency.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-maths-a-4ma1-tutor.regionsTitle: Dubai communities, school mix and when a 4MA1 session can realistically start
dubai/edexcel-igcse-maths-a-4ma1-tutor.regionsIntro: 4MA1 candidates in Dubai sit in schools with very different maths cohorts, and the practical question for a family is what time a session can actually begin after the commute and the homework. These are the communities we are asked about most.

regions.name: Al Qusais and Al Nahda
regions.note: A dense school corridor on the Sharjah side of Dubai with large cohorts and a curriculum mix that includes both British and Indian systems. Sessions here usually start after half past six, because the cross-emirate commute at the end of the school day is unpredictable.

regions.name: Oud Metha and Karama
regions.note: Older established communities close to several long-standing schools, with short commutes and a high proportion of candidates taking nine or ten subjects. Maths tends to be the subject families protect, so an early evening slot holds well here.

regions.name: International City and Warsan
regions.note: A large residential community whose candidates travel to schools across the city. Families here are often weighing a group class against one-to-one, and the honest comparison depends on whether the candidate's problem is content coverage or written method.

regions.name: Motor City and Dubai Sports City
regions.note: Villa and mid-rise communities with schools on the doorstep and a short school run, so a five o'clock start is realistic. Candidates here frequently sit 4MA1 alongside three sciences, which concentrates the revision load into the same fortnight.

regions.name: Town Square and Remraam
regions.note: Newer communities further out along the Al Qudra corridor, where the drive to school is long in both directions. This is exactly the profile where a tutor's travel time would have dominated the arrangement, and where a video slot after seven is the practical answer.

regions.name: Jebel Ali and Green Community
regions.note: A cluster with long-established schools and a self-contained feel, so after-school activities finish earlier and sessions can start sooner. Candidates here often have quiet study space, which makes timed full-paper practice at home genuinely workable.

regions.name: Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: A newer villa community with strong school provision nearby and a short commute, but a crowded extracurricular timetable. Families here do better with one protected weekly slot than with two that keep moving, particularly in the term before a series.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Established eastern communities with a mixed school set and a long run across town to the newer centres. Candidates often travel a considerable distance to school, so a later start and a shorter, sharper session works better than a long one.

schoolClusters.city: Deira, Garhoud and Festival City
schoolClusters.note: Students we support attend long-established schools in this corridor, several with large maths departments and setted classes from Year 9. A candidate in a lower set is often following the same specification as the top set with a different pace and a different tier intention, so the first question is always which tier the department has in mind.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha South and Jumeirah Village
schoolClusters.note: A fast-growing cluster of newer schools with mixed cohorts and, in several cases, maths sets that move between years. Candidates here sometimes change set between Year 10 and Year 11, which can change the tier assumption without anybody telling the family.

schoolClusters.city: Mirdif, Al Warqa and Silicon Oasis
schoolClusters.note: A curriculum-mixed cluster on the eastern side of Dubai. Several centres here enter both the summer and the November series, which gives a candidate a genuine second attempt but also means the entry decision arrives earlier in the year than families expect.

Almost every later decision follows from that single document.

sections.heading: Two papers, a calculator in both, and what sits on each
paragraphs: 4MA1 is assessed by two written papers of equal weight, with a calculator permitted in both and no coursework anywhere in the qualification. That is simpler than many families expect and it removes a whole category of anxiety: there is no controlled assessment to chase, no portfolio, and no practical component. It also means there is nowhere to hide. Every mark the candidate earns is earned in a timed written environment, twice, on the same body of content.

Pearson does not divide the content into a Paper 1 syllabus and a Paper 2 syllabus. Both papers draw on the whole specification, which is why a candidate who revises by paper rather than by strand ends up with gaps. The useful mental model is that the specification is one body of content assessed twice, with the second paper statistically likely to include anything the first one left out. A tutor who tells you Paper 2 is the hard one is guessing.

What does differ between the two sittings is the candidate's state. Paper 2 is written after Paper 1 has already gone well or badly, and a candidate who came out of the first paper convinced they had failed frequently underperforms on the second. That is a coachable problem, and the coaching is specific: a rule against post-mortem discussion between papers, and a rehearsed plan for the first ten minutes of Paper 2 that does not depend on how the candidate feels.

Verify the current paper durations, mark totals and tier grade ranges against the 4MA1 specification on qualifications.pearson.com, because they are set by the specification version the centre is teaching and Pearson is the only authoritative source. The table below sets out the structure as it is commonly taught in Dubai schools, with that verification note attached rather than buried.

sections.heading: Foundation or Higher: the ceiling, the floor and the window to change it
paragraphs: The tier decision is the highest-leverage choice in the whole qualification and the one families have least visibility of. A Foundation entry caps the grade available at the lower part of the scale, so a candidate who is genuinely capable of a 7 cannot be awarded one, no matter how well they write. A Higher entry opens the top grades but thins out the accessible marks, and a candidate who is not secure on algebra can score fewer raw marks on 1H and 2H than they would have on 1F and 2F.

The honest signals are not hard to read. A candidate who factorises quadratics without hesitating, handles algebraic fractions and can differentiate a polynomial belongs on Higher. A candidate who still reaches for a calculator to multiply out brackets, draws no diagram for a trigonometry question and loses most of the geometry reasoning marks will do better on Foundation, and will come out with a better grade from it. A capable candidate on Foundation and a struggling one on Higher are both being failed by the same reluctance to have the conversation.

The window to change the decision is set by the centre's entry deadline, not by the exam date. Pearson's deadlines sit months ahead of the papers, and once the entry has gone the tier is fixed. This is the single most important date in a 4MA1 year, and almost no Dubai family knows what it is. Ask the maths department, in writing, which tier the candidate is entered for and what the internal deadline is for changing it. The answer is often earlier than Christmas for a summer series.

A tutor's contribution here is evidence rather than opinion. One marked paper at each tier, under timed conditions, settles the argument faster than a term of discussion: the raw marks, the pattern of losses and the candidate's own reaction to the two papers tell you which entry they belong in. That is a two-week exercise, and it should happen well before the department's deadline rather than in the week it falls.

sections.heading: Where 4MA1 marks actually go missing in a Dubai cohort
paragraphs: Marked scripts fail in patterns, and the patterns repeat across schools. The largest single category is not a content gap at all: it is method marks lost because the working does not show the step the mark scheme is looking for. A candidate who reaches the right answer with three lines of calculator arithmetic and no stated method earns the answer mark and nothing else. On a multi-step question worth five marks, that is four marks surrendered for a correct piece of mathematics.

The second category is calculator-driven. Because 4MA1 allows a calculator in both papers, candidates round intermediate values and then carry the rounded figure forward, which puts the final answer outside the accepted range. Premature approximation of this kind is almost invisible to the candidate, who is confident the method was right, and it is only diagnosable from a marked script. It is also one of the fastest things to fix once it has been named.

The third is topic-specific and predictable. Upper and lower bounds, area and volume scale factors, histograms with unequal class widths, the ambiguous case in the sine rule, and geometric vector proof account for a disproportionate share of lost Higher marks. Each of these has a characteristic wrong answer that a tutor recognises instantly, which is why a marked paper is worth more than a conversation about what the candidate finds hard.

The fourth is timing, and it is usually a consequence of the first three rather than a separate problem. A candidate who writes no method has to re-derive their way through hard questions under pressure; a candidate who rounds early redoes calculations that did not work. Fixing method and calculator discipline typically returns several minutes across a paper without any work on speed at all, which is why timing drills are the last intervention rather than the first.

sections.heading: The Higher-only content that decides a grade 8 or 9
paragraphs: Higher tier 4MA1 contains a block of material a Foundation candidate never meets, and the top grades are decided inside it. Differentiation of polynomials, turning points and their classification, and rates of change applied to motion sit at the centre of it. So do function notation with composite and inverse functions, vector geometry and proof, upper and lower bounds, the harder circle theorems, histograms with unequal class widths and three-dimensional trigonometry.

The characteristic Dubai problem with this block is not that it is untaught. It is that it is taught late and practised little. A scheme of work that covers number and algebra thoroughly in Year 10 often arrives at calculus in the spring of Year 11, where it competes with revision for nine other subjects. A candidate meets differentiation, follows it in class, and never reaches the point of fluency where a turning-point question is routine. Under exam pressure, partially learned material behaves like unlearned material.

The remedy is unglamorous and reliable: bring the hardest block forward. A candidate who meets differentiation in the autumn of Year 11 with a tutor, and then meets it again in class in the spring, is seeing it for the second time at exactly the point their peers are seeing it for the first. The same applies to vector proof and to bounds. This is one of the few places where tutoring that runs ahead of the school rather than behind it is clearly the right call.

There is a secondary benefit for anybody continuing into International A Level Mathematics or into IB Diploma Analysis and Approaches. The calculus and function work in Higher 4MA1 is the direct foundation for the first pure unit of either, and a candidate who leaves IGCSE genuinely fluent in it begins Year 12 with a real advantage. A candidate who scraped those marks through pattern recognition discovers the gap in the first term, which is a far more expensive place to discover it.

sections.heading: Calculator discipline, and the formulae the sheet does not give you
paragraphs: A calculator in both papers sounds like a simplification and behaves like a trap. The most common marked-script error in 4MA1 is not an arithmetic slip; it is a candidate writing down an intermediate value to three significant figures, clearing the screen, and typing the rounded number back in. The method is correct, the reasoning is correct, and the final answer falls outside the accepted range. Mark schemes are not generous about this because the examiner cannot distinguish it from a genuine error.

The fix is mechanical and should be drilled rather than explained. Intermediate values stay in the calculator's memory or on the answer line, the candidate works with stored values, and rounding happens once, at the end, to the degree of accuracy the question asks for. Alongside that sits a short list of machine habits worth establishing early: knowing how the specific model handles order of operations, checking the angle mode before any trigonometry, and recognising that a displayed fraction is exact while a decimal may not be.

The formulae sheet is the other half of this. Pearson supplies a sheet with the 4MA1 papers, and candidates routinely assume it contains more than it does. What it does not generally supply is exactly what gets forgotten: the circle theorems as statements, the area of a triangle in its various forms, the quadratic formula in some specification versions, compound interest, and the relationships between length, area and volume scale factors. Check the current sheet for the specification version your centre teaches, from Pearson, and build the memorisation list from what is missing rather than from a generic revision guide.

Both of these are cheap interventions with a measurable return, which is unusual. A single session on stored-value working and angle mode, followed by two marked papers, typically removes a recurring loss of several marks per paper. No amount of additional topic coverage achieves that, which is why a tutor who starts with content before looking at a marked script is starting in the wrong place.

sections.heading: Mathematics A against Mathematics B, and when 4PM1 belongs in the conversation
paragraphs: Pearson offers more than one International GCSE maths route, and Dubai families are sometimes told their child is doing Edexcel maths without being told which. Mathematics A, code 4MA1, is the tiered two-paper qualification most international schools enter. Mathematics B, code 4MB1, is a different specification with a different paper structure and a different content emphasis, and it is untiered. A tutor working from the wrong specification will teach material that is not examined and skip material that is.

Further Pure Mathematics, code 4PM1, is a third and separate thing: an additional qualification taken alongside 4MA1 rather than instead of it, extending into calculus, series, coordinate geometry and trigonometric identities at a level well beyond Higher tier. It suits a candidate who finds Higher 4MA1 comfortable rather than challenging and who is heading for a maths-heavy A Level. It is a poor idea for a candidate using it to signal ambition they have not yet earned on 4MA1.

The practical test for 4PM1 is simple and worth applying honestly. If a candidate is sitting mock papers at Higher tier, finishing with time spare and scoring in the top band without drama, the extra qualification is a reasonable use of their year. If they are working hard for a 7, adding 4PM1 will cost them the 7 and deliver a mediocre grade in the additional subject. Two strong grades beat one strong and one weak, in every admissions conversation anybody has ever had.

The first thing to establish, before any of this is debated, is which code the centre has actually entered. A Dubai parent cannot infer it from a report card or a textbook cover, and schools occasionally run more than one route across different sets. Ask the maths department for the specification code in writing. It takes one email and it determines everything a tutor should spend an hour on.

sections.heading: The Pearson calendar for a Dubai candidate, counted backwards
paragraphs: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year, which gives a Dubai candidate two genuine opportunities in a single academic year rather than one. The published reference points are useful for planning: the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including for International GCSE in future Novembers, and explicitly treats them as subject to revision. The operational consequence is that no family and no tutor should work to a date taken from a search result or a forum. The live official timetable on qualifications.pearson.com is the reference, and the school's examinations officer is the person who confirms which papers the candidate is entered for and when they fall.

Counting backwards from a series is what turns a vague intention into a plan. If the papers sit in late May, then the full-paper discipline block belongs in March and April, the topic-fix work belongs between October and February, the diagnostic paper belongs in September, and the tier conversation belongs before the centre's entry deadline, which in most Dubai schools falls months before anybody sits anything. Working in that order is also substantially cheaper than working in reverse.

The November series deserves more attention than it gets from Dubai families, because it changes the risk profile of the whole year. A candidate entered in November has results in January and the option of a May retake with four months of knowledge of exactly how they underperform under pressure. A candidate entered only in May has one attempt and a summer of waiting. Which pattern a school uses is a legitimate question to ask at the start of Year 11.

sections.heading: What a 4MA1 session actually fixes, and how these lessons run
paragraphs: A session that begins with a question about what the candidate finds hard has already wasted its first ten minutes, because candidates are poor witnesses to their own errors. A session that begins with a marked script starts from evidence. The first hour in every case produces a written error log that divides lost marks into content gaps, method losses, calculator errors and timing, and that document is what the next ten sessions work down. Progress is visible because the log shrinks.

After that the work is narrow and repetitive by design. One strand per session, taught from the candidate's own wrong answers rather than from a textbook running order, with a short marked set between sessions on that strand alone. The candidate sees the mark scheme applied to their own work rather than to a model answer, which is the only way the method-mark habit transfers. Six weeks before the series the format changes to full timed papers and the content work stops.

Lessons for Dubai families are delivered one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, and shifted to post-Iftar slots through Ramadan. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service it runs only in India. For maths this matters less than it does for a practical subject, because the medium that counts is the shared workspace: the candidate writes, the tutor sees the working appear line by line, and the correction lands at the step where the error happened rather than at the end.

What the format does buy is the right specialist. 4MA1 Higher calculus, vector proof and bounds are not general maths teaching, and selecting a tutor by how far they live from Town Square or Al Qusais is a poor way to find somebody who marks those questions regularly. The first lesson is free, with no card details, and the sensible way to use it is to bring a recent marked paper and let the tutor talk through what the script shows.

process.title: Get the specification code and the tier in writing
process.description: Email the maths department and ask for three things: the specification code, the tier the candidate is entered for, and the internal deadline for changing it. A parent cannot infer any of them from a report card. Everything a tutor should do with the first ten hours depends on those answers.

process.title: Sit one full paper under timed conditions
process.description: Not a selection of questions and not an untimed attempt. One recent paper, start to finish, at the tier the candidate is entered for. It is uncomfortable and it is the most informative ninety minutes available, because it produces a script that can be marked against the published scheme.

process.title: Take the free first lesson with the marked script
process.description: One hour, no card details, with the paper and the marking in front of both of you. The tutor talks through what the script shows rather than asking what the candidate finds difficult. By the end you have a ranked list of causes and an honest view of how many hours the work needs.

process.title: Work the error log, not the textbook
process.description: One strand per session in the order the log ranks them, with a short marked set in between on that strand alone. The log is updated every week, so a family can see what has actually closed. Topics the candidate already has are not revisited to fill time.

process.title: Switch to full papers six weeks out
process.description: Content work stops and paper discipline begins: timed papers in rotation, method marks itemised in the marking, and a question-order strategy built from the candidate's own mark pattern. New content in the final fortnight does more harm than good and is declined.

process.title: Decide the series question early
process.description: If the school enters November as well as May, that changes the plan. A November entry gives a January result and a full term to decide on a retake. That conversation belongs at the start of Year 11, with the department, not in the week the entry deadline falls.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis from a marked script, not a conversation
whyPoints.description: Every engagement opens with a timed paper marked against the published scheme and a written error log separating content gaps from method losses, calculator errors and timing. Candidates are poor witnesses to their own mistakes, and the log is what makes progress visible rather than asserted.

whyPoints.title: Method marks taught as a subject in their own right
whyPoints.description: The largest category of lost marks in 4MA1 is not a content gap; it is working that does not show the step the mark scheme rewards. That is a habit, and it changes only through repeated marking of the candidate's own scripts with the method marks itemised line by line.

whyPoints.title: Specification-specific, down to the code
whyPoints.description: Mathematics A 4MA1, Mathematics B 4MB1 and Further Pure 4PM1 are different qualifications with different content. Sessions are planned against the code the centre actually entered, confirmed in writing, rather than against a generic IGCSE maths scheme of work.

whyPoints.title: The tier decision treated as evidence, not opinion
whyPoints.description: One timed paper at each tier settles in two weeks what a term of discussion will not: raw marks, loss patterns and the candidate's own reaction. That exercise is scheduled before the department's entry deadline, because afterwards the ceiling is fixed whatever anybody concludes.

whyPoints.title: Higher-tier calculus brought forward, not left to spring
whyPoints.description: Differentiation, turning points, vector proof and bounds are usually taught late in Year 11 and practised too little. Meeting them with a tutor in the autumn means the candidate sees them a second time when their classmates see them first, which is where fluency comes from.

whyPoints.title: No guarantees, and every date attributable
whyPoints.description: No grade is promised here and no statistic appears without a source. The Pearson dates on this page come from Pearson's published pages and must be confirmed against the live official timetable. IB Gram is independent, holds no regulator or board approval, and operates no UAE office.

faqs.question: What is the structure of Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1?
faqs.answer: Two written papers of equal weight, with a calculator permitted in both and no coursework in the qualification at all. Entry is tiered: Foundation candidates sit papers 1F and 2F, Higher candidates sit 1H and 2H, and the tier is chosen and submitted by the centre. Both papers draw on the whole specification rather than splitting it between them, which is why revising by paper creates gaps. Confirm the current durations, mark totals and grade ranges against the 4MA1 specification on qualifications.pearson.com for the version your Dubai school teaches.

faqs.question: Why do Dubai candidates still lose marks when a calculator is allowed in both papers?
faqs.answer: Because the calculator introduces its own failure mode. The commonest marked-script error in 4MA1 is a candidate writing an intermediate value to three significant figures, then typing that rounded number back in and carrying it forward. The method is right and the final answer falls outside the accepted range. Examiners cannot distinguish that from a real error. The fix is mechanical: keep intermediate values in the calculator, work from stored values, and round once at the end to the accuracy the question asks for.

faqs.question: Which 4MA1 topics appear on Paper 1 and which on Paper 2?
faqs.answer: Neither paper has its own topic list. Pearson assesses the whole 4MA1 specification across both papers, so any strand can appear on either, and a strand absent from the first paper is statistically more likely to appear on the second. This is why revision organised by paper produces gaps and revision organised by content strand does not. A tutor who tells you Paper 2 is the hard one or the statistics one is guessing. Plan by strand, and treat the second paper as covering everything.

faqs.question: What grade can my child actually get on 4MA1 Foundation tier?
faqs.answer: Only the lower part of the grade scale. The Higher tier covers the upper grades, with one grade below the tier floor normally available as a safety net. The practical effect is that the tier sets a ceiling before the candidate writes anything, so a capable candidate entered for Foundation cannot be awarded a top grade however well they perform. Confirm the exact grade ranges for your specification version on qualifications.pearson.com, and ask the maths department which tier the entry has been made for.

faqs.question: How late can a 4MA1 entry be moved from Foundation to Higher?
faqs.answer: Until the centre's entry deadline, which sits months ahead of the papers and is set by Pearson rather than by the school's own calendar. For a summer series that deadline often falls before the Christmas break. Once the entry has gone, the tier is fixed. Ask the maths department in writing for two things: which tier the candidate is entered for and the internal deadline for changing it. Then sit one timed paper at each tier and compare raw marks, well before that date arrives.

faqs.question: Which Higher-tier 4MA1 topics separate a grade 7 from a grade 9?
faqs.answer: Mostly the Higher-only block: differentiation of polynomials with turning points and classification, rates of change applied to motion, function notation with composite and inverse functions, vector geometry and proof, upper and lower bounds, three-dimensional trigonometry, and histograms with unequal class widths. The Dubai problem is rarely that these are untaught. It is that they are taught in the spring of Year 11 and never practised to fluency, so under pressure they behave like unlearned material. Meeting them earlier with a tutor is the reliable remedy.

faqs.question: What does the 4MA1 formulae sheet give, and what has to be memorised?
faqs.answer: Pearson supplies a formulae sheet with the papers, and candidates consistently assume it contains more than it does. What is typically missing is exactly what gets forgotten: the circle theorems as statements, the various forms for the area of a triangle, compound interest, and the relationships between length, area and volume scale factors. Download the current sheet for your specification version from Pearson and build the memorisation list from what is actually absent, rather than from a generic revision guide written for a different qualification.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Edexcel Mathematics A 4MA1 and Mathematics B 4MB1?
faqs.answer: They are different qualifications. Mathematics A, 4MA1, is the tiered two-paper specification most international schools enter. Mathematics B, 4MB1, is untiered and has a different paper structure and content emphasis. A tutor working from the wrong one teaches material that is not examined and omits material that is. Dubai families are often told their child does Edexcel maths without being told which code, and a school may run different routes across different sets, so ask the department for the code in writing.

faqs.question: Should my child take Further Pure Maths 4PM1 alongside 4MA1?
faqs.answer: Only if Higher 4MA1 is comfortable rather than demanding. The honest test is mock performance: a candidate finishing Higher papers with time spare and scoring in the top band without drama can use the year well on 4PM1. A candidate working hard for a 7 will lose the 7 and gain a mediocre second grade. 4PM1 is an additional qualification extending into calculus, series and coordinate geometry, not a replacement for 4MA1 and not compensation for a weak grade in it.

faqs.question: Which Pearson results dates are already published for International GCSE?
faqs.answer: Pearson's published positions include a November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reaching centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also issues provisional timetables ahead of each series and treats them as subject to revision. Work only from the live official timetable on qualifications.pearson.com, and have the examinations officer at your Dubai school confirm which papers the candidate is entered for.

faqs.question: How many hours does it take to move a 4MA1 candidate from a grade 5 to a grade 7?
faqs.answer: Nobody can answer that honestly before marking a script, and a provider who quotes a number without one is selling rather than advising. What the marked paper establishes is whether the shortfall is content, method, calculator discipline or timing. A candidate losing marks mainly to unstated working and premature rounding can move quickly, because the content is already there. A candidate with genuine gaps across algebra and the Higher block is looking at a term of weekly work, not a half-term.

faqs.question: Does 4MA1 count towards the subjects the UAE Ministry of Education requires for equivalency?
faqs.answer: For the British track the Ministry requires five subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one subject at Advanced Level at E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five. Mathematics counts as one of the five. Verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority before relying on it. IB Gram does not perform equivalency, and tutoring is not a requirement for the process.

faqs.question: Do Dubai schools enter 4MA1 in November as well as the summer?
faqs.answer: Some do, and it changes the risk profile of the whole year. Pearson makes International GCSE available in May/June and November, so a November entry produces a January result and leaves a full term to decide on a May retake with real knowledge of how the candidate performs under pressure. A May-only entry gives one attempt and a summer of waiting. Which pattern your centre uses is a reasonable question to ask the maths department at the start of Year 11 rather than later.

faqs.question: How does an online tutor see my child's 4MA1 working?
faqs.answer: Through a shared workspace, which for maths is the part that matters. The candidate writes and the tutor watches the working appear line by line, so a correction lands at the step where the error happened rather than after the answer is wrong. Scripts and marked papers are uploaded between sessions, and the marking comes back with method marks itemised. For a written, calculator-permitted subject with no practical component, very little is lost by not being in the same room.

faqs.question: Our search was for a tutor in Dubai, so does somebody come to the house?
faqs.answer: No. Lessons for Dubai families are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with slots moved to post-Iftar timing through Ramadan. IB Gram does not send tutors to any UAE address; home visits are a service it runs only in India. The gain is the specialist rather than the nearest available teacher: Higher-tier calculus, vector proof and bounds are not general maths teaching, and driving distance from Al Qusais or Town Square is a poor filter for finding somebody who marks those questions regularly.

faqs.question: Does a maths tutor charging a Dubai family need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services under the service name Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two working day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents and university students. Tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts has been published.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: Every tutor below teaches to a Pearson specification rather than to a general maths or science syllabus. You see the subject, the tier and the papers they work on before you book, and the trial lesson is where you check whether your child will talk to them for sixty minutes.

intro.heading: What an Edexcel International GCSE tutor costs in Dubai, and what moves the number
paragraphs: Three of the six highest-ranking tutoring pages for this search publish no price at all. The two that do quote US dollars, a currency no Dubai family pays tuition in. So the first thing this page does is put numbers on the table: across the emirate, online one-to-one teaching for Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sits at roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour at the university-student end, AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject teacher, and AED 200 to AED 450 or more for a specialist who marks to the board's mark scheme. Those figures come from published provider rate cards and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring rate table, not from us.

The spread is wide because the word tutor covers at least five different jobs. At the bottom of the range you are buying supervision: someone sitting with your child while they do the homework the school set. In the middle you are buying teaching, which means a scheme of work, worked examples your child has not seen before, and a reason for each topic order. At the top you are buying marking: a tutor who sits with a Pearson mark scheme and tells your child why a correct answer earned four marks out of six. Those three products are not interchangeable, and a family paying specialist rates for supervision is the most common way money gets wasted in this market.

Dubai adds its own variables. A tutor who drives to a villa in Arabian Ranches prices the drive, and in practice that is forty to ninety minutes of unpaid time across Al Khail Road at the wrong hour. Bestimate's in-home band runs AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to AED 500; the gap between that and an online rate is mostly fuel, traffic and the tutor's lost second booking. IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE: tutoring here is delivered online, one to one, over live video, and home visiting is a service we run only in India. That is a limit, and it is also why a family in Dubai South can work with a 4PM1 specialist rather than whoever is willing to drive out that far.

The exam calendar moves the price as well, and almost no competitor page mentions it. Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and again in November, so a Dubai student has two live windows a year and a genuine resit route that does not cost a school year. Demand for specialists concentrates in the eight weeks before each window, which is when rates firm up and availability thins. Booking in September for a May/June series costs less and gets a better match than booking in April. The same logic applies to Cambridge candidates in Dubai schools that use the March series, where final entries close on 27 November 2026 for exams that start on 3 February 2027.

What follows is the detail behind all of that: a rate table by provider model with the source of each figure, a Pearson-against-Cambridge code comparison for the same subject, the session calendar counted backwards from results day, where 4MA1 and 4PH1 marks actually go missing, what a private candidate pays to sit a paper in Dubai, and the permit rule that decides whether a tutor may legally charge you in the first place. Every figure carries the date it was read and the party that published it. Nothing on this page is a price list of ours.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Dubai families searching for an Edexcel tutor are usually somewhere on a three-step route: a middle-years programme, then International GCSE at 16, then a post-16 qualification that the first two have to feed. The notes below describe where Pearson sits in that route for a Dubai school.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: A two-year linear qualification examined at the end of Year 11, reported on the 9-1 scale. Most subjects are assessed entirely by written paper, with practical skills in the sciences tested inside those papers rather than in a separate laboratory component. Mathematics A is tiered: Foundation reaches grade 5, Higher reaches grade 9. Entry codes such as 4MA1, 4PH1 and 4EA1 identify the exact specification your child sits.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson is the second board in Dubai after Cambridge, and plenty of British-curriculum schools here run a mixed basket: Cambridge for sciences, Pearson for maths or English, chosen department by department. That matters for tutoring because a tutor who knows 0580 inside out is not automatically fluent in 4MA1's two-paper structure. Ask the school's exams officer for the specification code before you book anything.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The other International GCSE route in Dubai, split into Core and Extended for many subjects, with a separate practical or alternative-to-practical paper in the sciences. Cambridge runs a June series, a November series and a March series used by a number of schools in this region, and every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones with its own version of the timetable.
programmes.countryNote: If your child's school uses the March series, the planning calendar is unusual: for March 2027, final entries fall on 27 November 2026 and the exam period runs 3 February to 4 March 2027. A Dubai family who starts tutoring in January for a March series has already missed the point at which the tier decision was locked. Cambridge states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who sit the wrong zone's timetable, so check which zone the centre is in.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International A Level
programmes.description: The post-16 route most Dubai British-curriculum students take after International GCSE, examined in units across May/June and October/November series. Grades A* to E are awarded, and the Ministry of Education's equivalency route for British-curriculum students requires at least one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level.
programmes.countryNote: The reason International GCSE tier choice matters in Dubai is what comes next. A student who takes Foundation tier 4MA1 and scores a 5 has a legitimate certificate but an uncomfortable start in International A Level Mathematics, where the first term assumes fluent algebraic manipulation. Where a tutor earns their rate is in the eight weeks between results and the first A Level lesson, not in the panic of October.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The alternative post-16 route, taken by students in the Dubai schools that run IB. Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus an extended essay, theory of knowledge and CAS. Internal assessment is worth a fifth of most subject grades, and the diploma is scored out of 45 points.
programmes.countryNote: Around one in fourteen Dubai private-school places sits on an International Baccalaureate programme, against 37 per cent on a UK curriculum, on KHDA's 2024-25 figures. That makes the Pearson-to-Diploma crossover a real Dubai problem: a student arriving in DP1 from 4MA1 Higher has met quadratics and trigonometry but not the mathematical writing that Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches expects in an exploration. Two terms of structured support closes it.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the Pearson specifications Dubai families ask for most often, with the code the school enters and the place marks usually leak. Ask the school which code appears on the entry, because two schools in the same community can run different specifications for the same subject.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (4MA1)
subjects.description: Two papers of two hours, 100 marks each, weighted 50-50, with a calculator allowed in both. Higher tier reaches grade 9; Foundation caps at 5. Marks disappear in algebraic fractions, vectors, histograms with unequal class widths, and the last two parts of a structured problem where students stop showing method.

subjects.name: Further Pure Mathematics (4PM1)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 4MA1 by students heading for International A Level Mathematics or Higher Level IB maths. Content overlaps early AS pure: series, logarithms, differentiation, trigonometric identities. The common failure is not the content but the volume of accurate manipulation required under time pressure.

subjects.name: Physics (4PH1)
subjects.description: Assessed entirely by written paper, with practical skills examined inside those papers rather than in a separate test. Dubai students lose most in units and prefixes, moments questions with awkward pivots, and the six-mark explanation items where the mark scheme wants a chain of cause and effect, not a definition.

subjects.name: Chemistry (4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations, electrolysis half-equations, rates graphs and organic reaction pathways carry the grade. The cheapest marks recovered in tutoring are in writing balanced ionic equations and in reading titration data correctly: both are procedural, and both are taught rather than revised.

subjects.name: Biology (4BI1)
subjects.description: Content-heavy, with the practical skills questions and data analysis separating a 7 from a 9. Students who revise by rereading notes plateau here. Marks come back through command-term drill, labelled diagrams and practice at describing a graph trend before explaining it.

subjects.name: English Language A (4EA1)
subjects.description: Paper 1 tests non-fiction reading and transactional writing; the second component is poetry and prose or, where the school chooses it, coursework. The reading marks go missing when students summarise rather than analyse method, and the writing marks go when the register does not match the audience named in the task.

subjects.name: English Literature (4ET1)
subjects.description: Closed-book or open-text depending on the route the school enters. The highest-value tutoring here is quotation economy: short embedded quotations with a comment on method, rather than long extracts narrating the plot back to the examiner.

subjects.name: Economics (4EC1)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the whole game. A correctly labelled and correctly shifted diagram earns marks that no amount of written explanation recovers. Dubai students with strong general knowledge often lose marks by answering with examples instead of with the model the question names.

subjects.name: Business (4BS1)
subjects.description: Application to the case material is where grades are made. Students who have learned definitions score in the lower bands; those who quote a figure from the stimulus and use it in a judgement score in the upper ones. That habit takes four or five marked attempts to build.

subjects.name: Information and Communication Technology (4IT1)
subjects.description: A written paper plus a practical component done at a computer. The practical rewards process discipline: file naming, evidence capture, following the task sheet exactly. Tutoring works best as timed practice with the evidence document checked line by line against the task.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-online-tutor.regionsIntro: What changes between Dubai communities is not the syllabus but the clock and the travel premium. The notes below are about scheduling and cost rather than about any tutor being physically present, because every IB Gram session here runs over video.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JBR
regions.note: Apartment living, short school runs to Emirates International and the British curriculum schools along Al Sufouh. A 4pm start is realistic on most days, which is the cheapest slot to book because it competes with nobody's commute.

regions.name: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Dense with British-curriculum schools, so local in-home tutors are plentiful and priced accordingly, often at the AED 250-400 end. The online case here is about subject match rather than access: 4PM1 and 4EC1 specialists are scarce at any address.

regions.name: Arabian Ranches and Dubai Hills Estate
regions.note: Villa communities where a visiting tutor prices the Al Khail Road drive into the hour. Families here see the widest gap between quoted in-home and online rates, usually AED 80-150 an hour for the same level of teaching.

regions.name: Mirdif and Al Warqa
regions.note: Mixed British and Indian-curriculum catchment with long bus runs. Students often get home after 4pm, so 6pm and 7.30pm slots dominate, and those are the hours when specialist availability is tightest across the emirate.

regions.name: Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City
regions.note: Younger families, a cluster of schools on site, and a lot of Year 10 and 11 students taking Pearson maths with Cambridge sciences. Checking which code sits on each entry matters more here than anywhere else in Dubai.

regions.name: Business Bay and Downtown
regions.note: Working parents, late dinners and students who revise after 8pm. Short, frequent sessions work better here than a single long weekend block, and the rate is identical because no one is driving anywhere.

regions.name: Dubai South and Jebel Ali
regions.note: Far enough out that in-home coverage thins and quoted rates rise to cover the distance. This is the clearest case in Dubai for buying the specialist online instead of buying whoever is prepared to make the drive.

schoolClusters.city: Beachside and New Dubai
schoolClusters.note: British-curriculum schools along the Al Sufouh and Umm Suqeim corridor feed most of the Marina, JBR and Palm Jumeirah Pearson entries. Students here typically sit a mixed basket of Cambridge and Pearson codes, which is why the exams officer rather than the class teacher is the right person to ask.

schoolClusters.city: Inland villa communities
schoolClusters.note: Ranches, Dubai Hills, Motor City and Sports City draw on schools where Year 11 cohorts are large and setting is tight. A student in the middle set with a target of grade 7 is the classic case for one weekly online hour plus marked papers rather than a group class.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.city: Eastern and central Dubai
schoolClusters.note: Mirdif, Al Warqa, Al Qusais and Garhoud run some of the largest British-curriculum cohorts in the emirate alongside strong Indian-curriculum provision. Session times here are dictated by bus routes, not by the school bell.

dubai/edexcel-igcse-online-tutor.modesIntro: Three shapes of booking cover almost every Pearson request from Dubai. All three run over live video with a shared screen, and all three are priced by the hour rather than by the term.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through the course
modes.description: One hour a week from September, tracking the school's scheme of work about a fortnight behind so the tutor is consolidating rather than pre-teaching. This is the cheapest route to a grade change because it never has to buy back lost ground. It also gives nine months of marked work, which is what makes the final eight weeks of revision targeted rather than general.

Suited to a student who understands the content but converts it badly under exam conditions. Availability for this block tightens sharply in the last month, which is the single most common reason a Dubai family ends up with a second-choice tutor.
