sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges, by provider model
paragraphs: An Edexcel IGCSE online tutor in Dubai costs between roughly AED 45 and AED 650 an hour depending entirely on which of five different products you are buying. The table below lists each provider model with the rate band and the party that published it, read in October 2026. None of these are IB Gram prices; our own model is a free first lesson and a rate agreed per match, because a 4PM1 specialist and a Year 10 English tutor are not the same commodity.

Read the table by what the hour contains rather than by the number. A university-student tutor at AED 60 is good value for supervised homework and poor value for exam technique, because marking a Pearson paper accurately requires having marked a few hundred of them. A specialist at AED 300 who gives you an annotated script every fortnight is often cheaper per grade than a mid-band tutor at AED 180 who only teaches. The variable that actually predicts cost per grade is how much marked evidence the hour generates.

Two cautions about the top band. First, a provider advertising AED 650 an hour is selling scarcity, and scarcity is real in the eight weeks before a series and much less real in October. Second, examiner status is used as a price justification all over this market, and almost nobody evidences it. IB Gram does not label a tutor an examiner, because current examiner status is confidential and changes series by series, and because no examiner has access to unreleased papers or boundaries to pass on. If a quote rests on that claim, ask what it changes about the lesson.

The last row is the one Dubai parents most often misread. A tuition centre group class at AED 120 per student looks cheaper than one-to-one at AED 250, and for a student who is behind on content it frequently is. For a student sitting at grade 6 and aiming at 8, a group of eight moving at the scheme-of-work pace adds very little, because what that student needs is their own work marked. The decision is about diagnosis, not about the headline rate.

sections.heading: Pearson is not Cambridge: the codes that change the lesson
paragraphs: Parents in Dubai routinely book an IGCSE tutor without knowing which board the school entered, and the two are not interchangeable at the level a tutor works. The table below sets the common Pearson codes against their Cambridge counterparts and names what actually differs for the student sitting the paper. A tutor who has taught 0625 for a decade can teach 4PH1 well, but only after reading the specification, because the assessment of practical skills sits in a different place.

The sciences are the sharpest example. Cambridge assesses practical work through a separate component, either a laboratory paper or its alternative-to-practical equivalent, which rewards a particular style of answer about apparatus, variables and sources of error. Pearson examines the same skills inside the main written papers, mixed into questions about content. A student who revises Cambridge-style practical answers for a Pearson paper has prepared for a component that does not exist on their timetable.

In mathematics the difference is tiering and paper structure. Pearson Mathematics A runs two papers of two hours each at 50 per cent apiece, both with a calculator, Foundation capped at grade 5 and Higher reaching 9. Cambridge splits Core and Extended across different papers with their own grade ceilings. The practical consequence for a Dubai family is the entry decision, which is made months before the exam and is very hard to reverse once the centre has lodged it.

One last trap: grade scales. Pearson reports International GCSE on the 9-1 scale throughout. Cambridge reports some subjects on 9-1 and others on A* to G depending on the syllabus and the region, so a single Dubai student can finish Year 11 holding certificates on two different scales. Universities and the Ministry of Education equivalency route both handle this, but a parent comparing one child's grades with another's needs to know which scale each sits on.

sections.heading: The session calendar, counted backwards from results day
paragraphs: No competitor page in this cluster names a single exam session, which is remarkable given that the whole point of tutoring is to arrive ready on a date somebody else chose. Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November. Cambridge runs June and November series plus a March series used by a number of centres in this region. Every one of those windows has an entry deadline months earlier, and the entry deadline is where tier and specification decisions get locked.

The dates in the table are from the boards' own timetable and key-dates pages, read in October 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so treat the live PDF on the Pearson qualifications site as the authority and never a date restated on a tutoring page, including this one. Cambridge adds a further wrinkle specific to international centres: every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after the wrong zone's timetable was used.

Work the table from the bottom up and the planning becomes obvious. If results reach Dubai students on a date in August, and a re-entry decision has to be made within days, then the November window is a live option for one subject rather than a repeated year. If Cambridge March entries close on 27 November for a February exam period, then October is when tutoring has to start, not January. Deliberately absent from this table: any IB exam or results date. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no IB date is published here. Ask your school's diploma coordinator and use what they give you.

For a Dubai family the practical rule is eight weeks. Eight weeks before a window, specialist availability thins across the whole emirate and quoted rates stiffen. Eight weeks after results, the next cohort has already booked. A booking made in September for a May/June series costs less and gets a closer subject match than the same booking made in March.

sections.heading: What one hour actually buys at each price point
paragraphs: Rate bands are only useful if you know what the hour contains, so here is the same money described as a product. At AED 45 to AED 150 online you are buying attention: a competent graduate who can answer questions on homework and keep a thirteen-year-old working for sixty minutes. For a Year 9 student who is disorganised rather than confused, that is the correct purchase and anything more expensive is waste.

At AED 150 to AED 300 you are buying teaching from someone who has taught the specification. The hour has a plan, the examples escalate, and the tutor can tell you by week three which three topics are costing your child the most marks. This band is where most Dubai International GCSE work belongs, and it is where the market is deepest, which means you can be fussy about subject match and about whether your child actually talks during the lesson.

At AED 300 and above you should be buying marking as well as teaching. The test is simple: ask what you will receive between sessions. A tutor at this level should be returning annotated work keyed to mark-scheme language, not a WhatsApp message saying the session went well. If the answer is vague, the extra AED 100 an hour is buying reputation rather than output, and reputation has never converted a 6 into an 8.

Hidden costs catch families out at every band. Travel time billed as teaching time on in-home bookings. Minimum four-session packages. Cancellation windows of 24 hours that fall over a weekend. Materials fees for photocopied past papers that both boards publish free to centres. Ask for the cancellation rule, the notice period and the paper source in writing before the first lesson, whoever you book with.
bullets: Under AED 150: supervision and homework support, no marked papers
AED 150-300: specification teaching, a plan, diagnosis by week three
Above AED 300: marked work keyed to the board's mark scheme, or you are overpaying
Always ask: cancellation notice, package minimum, who supplies past papers

sections.heading: Where 4MA1 and 4PH1 marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Grades in International GCSE maths and physics are lost in a small number of predictable places, and a tutor who starts with a diagnostic rather than with chapter one finds them in the first fortnight. In 4MA1 the recurring losses are algebraic fractions, vectors, histograms with unequal class widths, upper and lower bounds, and the final parts of multi-step problems where a student who knows the method stops writing it down. Method marks are awarded for working that is present on the page and nowhere else.

The calculator is a second source of loss specific to Pearson's structure. Both 4MA1 papers allow one, which tempts students to abandon exact form. A question that asks for an answer in terms of pi, or in surd form, awards nothing for a decimal. Teaching the habit of reading what form the answer must take recovers marks across every topic at once, which is why it is often the first thing a tutor fixes.

In 4PH1 the pattern is different. Unit and prefix errors cost marks on questions the student understood perfectly. Moments questions with pivots that are not at the centre of mass defeat students who learned a single worked example. And the extended-response items want a causal chain: current increases, so the magnetic field strengthens, so the force on the conductor rises. Students who write three true facts about electromagnetism earn one mark of six, because the mark scheme rewards connection rather than recall.

Practical-skills questions in Pearson sciences sit inside the written papers, which makes them easy to under-prepare. The questions reward precise language about variables, repeats and anomalies. None of that requires a laboratory to learn: a screen-shared data table and a well-chosen set of past-paper questions teaches the answer style directly, which is how it is taught in an online lesson.
bullets: 4MA1: algebraic fractions, vectors, unequal-width histograms, bounds, lost method marks
4MA1: exact form ignored because a calculator was available in both papers
4PH1: units and prefixes, awkward-pivot moments, unlinked extended answers
Both: practical and data questions answered with content rather than with method language

sections.heading: Sitting Pearson papers as a private candidate in Dubai
paragraphs: Some Dubai families need an exam seat rather than a school place: a child who has moved mid-year, a student adding a subject their school does not offer, or someone retaking a single paper in November. That means entering as a private candidate through a centre in the emirate that is registered with the board to accept external entries, and it is a part of the process no competitor page explains.

The mechanics matter more than the fee. Entries are made by the centre, not by the family, and they close on the board's published deadline rather than when the centre feels ready. The centre sets its own charge per subject per series, because neither Pearson nor Cambridge publishes a candidate-facing price list. Expect the centre to require proof of identity, the correct specification code, and a decision on tier where the subject is tiered, all of which has to be right before the deadline rather than after it.

There are components a private candidate cannot always complete. Where a specification includes coursework, a centre may decline to accept external coursework or may require it to be supervised on site. In sciences the Pearson structure helps here, because practical skills are examined inside the written papers rather than through a separate laboratory component. A family planning a private entry should confirm the component list with the centre before booking any tutoring around it.

Tutoring for a private candidate looks different from tutoring alongside a school. There is no school scheme of work to follow and no teacher setting deadlines, so the tutor owns the calendar: topic order, interim test dates, and the point at which revision replaces teaching. That is a heavier job than one weekly consolidation hour, and it is usually two sessions a week over two terms rather than one over three.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally allowed to charge you?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and the rule is clearer than most parents expect. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and it is granted free of charge for two years. The ministry's own service is listed as issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days.

The eligibility list is broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. People offering private tutoring without a permit from the ministry are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any page quoting you a specific dirham figure for the penalty is inventing it; one widely circulated number could not be verified against any ministry source.

There is a separate rule parents should know about before asking a favour of their child's own teacher. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also addresses serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. That is press-reported rather than quoted here from the policy document, so check the current rule with the school. The practical point stands either way: the convenient option can be the non-compliant one.

A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor. A training institute needs an educational services permit from KHDA, obtained in stages with an initial approval first and renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit and makes no regulatory claim: we are an online matching platform with no premises in the UAE, and no regulator or examination board has approved, endorsed or accredited us.

Free of charge, valid two years, stated two working days to issue

sections.heading: Two years of International GCSE, costed in context
paragraphs: Tutoring is a line in a household budget that already contains school fees, transport and uniform, so the useful question is not what an hour costs but what the two years cost against everything else. Dubai gives one helpful fixed point: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Fees are flat; tutoring is the variable.

The table uses published market estimates rather than our prices. Bestimate's monthly figures for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Advertised Dubai packages seen in October 2026 included AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, which is the clearest single illustration of what travel adds.

Two patterns in that data are worth planning around. The first is that one hour a week sustained across Year 10 and Year 11 costs roughly the same as an eight-week intensive before the exam, and buys far more, because it generates marked evidence the whole way through. The second is that the in-home premium is not a quality premium. The same tutor, teaching the same specification, costs AED 80 to AED 150 more an hour once the drive from one community to another is priced in.

Dubai's school market is also expanding, which affects supply. KHDA reported seven new private schools for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent. More Year 10 cohorts each year means more demand on the same pool of specialist tutors in the eight weeks before each series. Booking early is a price strategy, not just an organisational one.

process.title: Tell us the code, not just the subject
process.description: The first message we need is the specification code on the entry: 4MA1, 4PH1, 4EA1 or whichever applies, plus the tier where the subject is tiered. The school's exams officer has it. With the code we can match a tutor who already teaches that paper structure rather than one who will learn it on your time.

process.title: A free first lesson, with no card details
process.description: The trial is one full lesson with the proposed tutor, free, with no payment method taken in advance. It exists to test two things a profile cannot show: whether your child speaks during the hour, and whether the tutor can explain a topic a second way when the first way does not land.

process.title: A diagnostic rather than a syllabus restart
process.description: In the first two paid sessions the tutor works through mixed past-paper questions to find where marks are leaking, then returns a short ranked list: the three topics costing the most marks, and whether the problem is content, method or timing. That list, not the textbook order, sets what happens next.

process.title: Weekly work, marked, with a written note
process.description: Each session is followed by a question set of roughly thirty minutes and a short written note naming what the last hour fixed and what it did not. Across a term this becomes a record you can read, which is what makes a conversation with the school specific instead of general.

process.title: A review before each series
process.description: Eight to ten weeks out from a Pearson or Cambridge window, the plan switches from teaching to timed papers and the booking shape usually changes with it. We review the match at that point and say plainly if a different tutor, or fewer hours, is the better call.

whyPoints.title: Prices on the page, in dirhams
whyPoints.description: Most pages ranking for this search publish no rate at all, and the two that do quote dollars. Every band on this page carries the party that published it and the month it was read, so you can argue with the number instead of guessing at it.

whyPoints.title: Specification-level matching
whyPoints.description: We match on the code your child is entered for, not on the word maths. A tutor fluent in 4MA1's two-paper structure and exact-form conventions is a different purchase from a general GCSE tutor, and the difference shows up in the first marked paper.

whyPoints.title: Marked work, not progress reports
whyPoints.description: The output of a session is annotated work keyed to mark-scheme wording plus a short written note. That is the evidence a parent can read and a school can respond to, and it is the main thing separating the middle rate band from the top one.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the limits
whyPoints.description: Lessons are online, one to one, over live video. We do not send tutors to homes in the UAE, we hold no regulator or board accreditation, we do not label tutors as examiners, and we do not promise a grade. If a specialist is not free for your subject and tier, we say so rather than substituting.

whyPoints.title: Timed to the Dubai week
whyPoints.description: Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time around the school run and the working day, with the 6pm and 7.30pm slots that eastern Dubai bus routes make necessary. During Ramadan, slots shift to post-Iftar timings on request rather than being cancelled.

whyPoints.title: Academic honesty taken seriously
whyPoints.description: Coursework and controlled assessment must be the student's own work. A tutor here teaches method, models technique on separate material and gives feedback on a draft the student wrote. Anyone selling finished assessed work is selling an outcome that gets students disqualified.

faqs.question: What does an Edexcel International GCSE tutor charge per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published rates across the emirate in October 2026 run from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour for a university-student tutor online, AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject teacher, and AED 200 to AED 450 or more for a board specialist. In-home visiting sits higher, at AED 180 to AED 500, because the drive is priced into the hour. Those figures come from provider rate cards and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table, not from us. IB Gram agrees a rate per match after a free first lesson, because a further pure maths specialist and a Year 10 English tutor are not the same purchase.

faqs.question: Is Pearson Edexcel International GCSE harder than Cambridge IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Neither is harder as a qualification; they assess differently. Pearson Mathematics A sits two two-hour papers weighted equally with a calculator allowed throughout, while Cambridge splits Core and Extended across different papers. In the sciences Cambridge adds a separate practical or alternative-to-practical component, and Pearson examines the same skills inside the written papers. A student who prepares in the Cambridge style for a Pearson paper has revised for a component that is not on their timetable. The one that is harder is the one your child has not been taught to answer, which is why the specification code matters more than the brand.

faqs.question: How do I find out which exam board and specification my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's examinations officer, not the class teacher, and ask for the code rather than the board name. You want a string like 4MA1, 4PH1 or 0580, plus the tier where the subject is tiered. Dubai schools frequently run a mixed basket, entering Cambridge for sciences and Pearson for maths or English, chosen department by department, so one child can hold codes from both boards in the same summer. Entry codes appear on the statement of entry the centre issues before each series. Bring that document to a first tutoring conversation and the match gets considerably more accurate.

faqs.question: What does modular mean in Pearson International GCSE compared with Cambridge?
faqs.answer: Pearson's International GCSE suite is linear in most subjects: your child sits the full set of papers at the end of the course in one series rather than banking units along the way. What Pearson does offer is two full series a year, May/June and November, so a single subject can be resat a few months later instead of a year later. Cambridge also runs June and November series plus a March series used by a number of centres in this region. Ask the centre which series it enters for, because the entry deadline, not the exam date, is the decision point.

faqs.question: How are Pearson science practicals assessed if the lessons are online?
faqs.answer: Pearson International GCSE sciences examine practical skills inside the written papers rather than through a separate laboratory component, so there is nothing a student has to perform under observation. The questions test precise language about variables, repeats, anomalies and sources of error, plus reading and interpreting data tables and graphs. All of that is taught well over a shared screen with real past-paper data in front of both people. Your child still does school practicals in the school laboratory; the tutoring job is turning that experience into the answer style the mark scheme rewards.

faqs.question: When do Pearson International GCSE results reach students in Dubai?
faqs.answer: On the dates Pearson published and we read in October 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson revises provisional timetables, so use the live timetable PDF on the Pearson qualifications site as the authority rather than a date restated on any tutoring page. Plan the re-entry conversation for the week of results, because the next entry deadline arrives faster than most families expect.

faqs.question: Can my child resit just one International GCSE subject in the November series?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the most useful features of the Pearson suite for Dubai families. Because the qualification is sat in full at the end of the course and offered twice a year, a single subject can be retaken a few months after a disappointing summer without repeating the school year. The entry goes through a centre, which may be the school or an external centre accepting private candidates, and it closes on the board's deadline. The tutoring shape for a single-subject resit is usually two hours a week for eight to ten weeks, built almost entirely on timed papers.

faqs.question: How many International GCSE subjects does the UAE Ministry of Education count for equivalency?
faqs.answer: For the British track the ministry requires five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE level with a grade no lower than E or grade 3, together with either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One page currently ranking for these searches states six subjects, which does not match the published requirement. Verify your own case on the ministry's channels, because equivalency is a regulatory process run by the authorities and not something a tutoring platform performs, guarantees or expedites for you.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education count towards those five equivalency subjects?
faqs.answer: No. The published clarification states that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. They remain mandatory subjects in Dubai private schools under KHDA requirements regardless of the licensed curriculum, so your child studies them either way, but they sit outside the five that the equivalency calculation uses. That means a student planning for equivalency needs five other accredited subjects at the stated grade. Check the current rule through the ministry or the emirate's attestation channel before making subject-choice decisions on it.

faqs.question: Does a Dubai tutor's hourly rate include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask, in writing, before the first lesson. UAE tax treatment of education services is not something a tutoring page should assert as fact without a Federal Tax Authority citation, and this one will not. What you can reasonably require from any provider is a plain statement of whether the quoted dirham figure is the amount you will be charged, whether a tax registration number applies, and whether package prices differ from single-session prices. A provider that cannot answer that in one sentence is a provider whose invoices will surprise you later.

faqs.question: Which permit does a paid Edexcel tutor in Dubai have to hold?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. Ask your tutor directly for their permit position, and treat reluctance to answer as the answer.

faqs.question: How many hours does a Higher tier 4MA1 student usually need before the exam?
faqs.answer: The honest answer depends on the gap between current and target grade, not on the subject. A student sitting at grade 6 aiming at 8 typically works one hour a week from September with a marked question set between sessions, roughly thirty hours across the year. A student who is two grades short usually needs two hours a week for at least two terms, because content has to be rebuilt before technique can be drilled. An eight-week intensive before the series suits a student who understands the material but converts it badly under timed conditions. The diagnostic in the first fortnight is what tells you which case you are in.

faqs.question: My child is entered for Foundation tier maths. Can that be changed to Higher?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but it is the centre's decision and it closes with the entry deadline, which falls months before the exam. Foundation tier 4MA1 caps at grade 5; Higher reaches grade 9 and is the sensible route for anyone intending to study mathematics or the sciences after 16. If you think the tier is wrong, raise it with the head of department immediately rather than after a mock, and bring evidence: marked papers at Higher tier questions, not an opinion. A tutor can produce that evidence quickly, which is often the most valuable thing an autumn booking does.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help with coursework where the specification includes it?
faqs.answer: Within the rules, yes. Where a Pearson specification offers a coursework route, a tutor teaches the skills the task assesses, models technique on different material, and gives feedback on a draft the student has written themselves. What no legitimate tutor does is supply text, restructure a piece into its final form or hand over finished work, because that is malpractice and the consequences land on the student. If any provider offers to deliver a completed assessed piece for a fee, that is the clearest signal available that you are in the wrong place.

faqs.question: What happens in the free trial lesson, and what does it cost afterwards?
faqs.answer: The trial is one full lesson with the proposed tutor at no charge and with no card details taken beforehand. The tutor usually works a mixed set of past-paper questions to see where the marks are going, and you get a short note afterwards. Two things are being tested: whether your child actually talks during the hour, and whether the tutor can explain a topic a second way when the first way does not land. If either answer is no, we propose a different tutor. The rate is agreed per match after that lesson, and there is no package you have to commit to first.
